name: Kevin Barry
other clubs: Hastings United, Chelsea (0), Hastings Town and Rye United
bio:
Burly player born in Hastings who was known for his heading ability. Kevin first came to prominence in schoolboy football, captaining the Hastings Boys team that reached the sixth round of the English Schools Trophy in 1965. He was also captain of the Hastings & District side that won an international youth tournament in West Germany and played for the England Grammar Schools side in matches against Scotland and Wales.

Kevin began his senior career with Hastings United, appearing in their junior sides as early as the 1965/66 season. Kevin made his debut in the first team as a teenager during 1967/68 and played as a centre-back for Hastings during the first half of 1968/69 before being converted into a centre-forward in December 1968. He ended 1968/69 with 11 goals. During the 1969/70 campaign Kevin scored 24 Southern League goals and 36 in all competitions.

He kept up his good form during 1970/71 and during November 1970 Kevin trained with Second Division club Bristol City. In December 1970 they made an offer of £1,500 to Hastings but the club turned it down. Bristol City s manager Alan Dicks said Our scouts have watched Barry and have seen possibilities which could make him useful to us. But it is really a matter of how he develops. There is no guarantee that he will make the grade which is why we felt we were making a fair offer. Hastings player-manager Cyril Jeans, a former Margate player, commented If he plays up to his capabilities, I cannot see him missing out. He deserves League football and if he doesn t go off the boil, I feel sure he will be snapped up. Kevin was also being watched by Chelsea, Norwich and Tottenham at the time but he ended up staying with Hastings until the end of 1970/71, scoring 34 goals in all competitions during the season.

Kevin got his move into professional football in July 1971 aged 21 when First Division Chelsea signed him for a fee of £2,000. The deal included a clause whereby Hastings would receive a further sum if Kevin made a certain number of first team appearances and Chelsea also committed to playing a pre-season friendly at Hastings featuring their full senior side. Hastings player-manager Bobby Drake, son of the famous Ted Drake, told the Kentish Express I am naturally sorry to see him go, but the move will be beneficial to both parties. Kevin now has a wonderful chance to get on and the money we have received will certainly help our finances.

Kevin couldn t settle at Stamford Bridge and after playing in just 11 reserve team matches he was on the move again when Margate signed him for what was described as a "substantial fee" on 30.11.71. Margate's new manager Les Riggs said at the time "I regard him as an outstanding capture" and the local press referred to Kevin as being "free-scoring" and "an exceptional prospect".

He made his debut in a 0-0 draw at Poole in the Southern League Cup on 30.11.71 and went on to make a total of 34 appearances before the end of the 1971/72 season. Kevin scored 18 goals and the best of them was a 25 yard strike in a 3-2 defeat at Weymouth on 15.4.72. He also struck from the edge of the penalty area in a 2-1 defeat at Yeovil on 3.5.72, Margate's last game of the season, and Yeovil's player-manager Mike Hughes said of Kevin "he is a very good player and is obviously dangerous anywhere near goal."

The 1972/73 season was an excellent one for Kevin, he turned in many outstanding performances and scored 15 times in his 57 appearances (one as sub), including a hat-trick in a 5-1 win over Guildford at Hartsdown Park on 19.8.72. He was described as being a "will o' the wisp" by the local press and on 26.9.72 Kevin was sent off for disputing the referee s decision to dismiss Eddie Clayton during a 1-0 defeat at Gravesend & Northfleet in the Southern League Cup. Les Riggs explained to the East Kent Times Kevin Barry who protested that Eddie had a right as captain to ask a question was also ordered off. It was staggering.

On 4.11.72 he scored with a diving header in 2-0 home win over Sutton in the FA Cup and on 27.11.72 Kevin played as a makeshift right-back in a 2-0 win over visitors Hastings in the Kent Floodlight Cup. On 2.12.72 he came on as a substitute to play in goal for the last ten minutes of a 3-2 win at Guildford after Chic Brodie was carried off.

On 13.1.73 Kevin was in the Margate side that lost 6-0 to Tottenham at Hartsdown Park in the 3rd Round of the FA Cup, a game that was perhaps the biggest ever in the club s history. He scored two notable goals during the remaining months of the campaign, finding the net with a shrewd chip in a 2-2 draw with Worcester on 3.3.73 and then firing home an excellent volley as Margate beat visitors Dartford 3-1 on 9.4.73.

At the start of the 1973/74 season Kevin found it hard to gain a regular place in the side. He was often substitute and made only nine appearances (two as sub), scoring three times, before leaving the club at the end of September 1973. Kevin rejoined Hastings United for a fee of £1,400 and his departure came about due to him being promoted at work and having difficulty travelling from his Hastings home. Les Riggs hadn't wanted to lose Kevin and paid tribute to him, saying that he was "one of the easiest men to handle I have ever known." He scored ten goals for Hastings before the end of the 1973/74 campaign.

Kevin went on to become captain of the Hastings United side that won promotion to the Southern Premier during the 1976/77 campaign and by that time he had been converted into a centre-back. He stayed with United until being suspended and then sacked in November 1978 after a dispute that followed the reappointment of former Margate player Cyril Jeans as Hastings' manager.

Kevin later moved on to United's Sussex County League neighbours Hastings Town and had a spell as their manager before resigning during the 1984/85 season.

When Hastings United folded Hastings Town took over their ground and also their place in the Southern League and Kevin became manager of Town's reserve side for the 1989/90 season. His son Lee was a member of the team whilst Kevin himself also made a few appearances. Kevin continued in the role during 1990/91 and still played when required.

He later had a spell as player-manager of Rye United, taking Lee with him from Hastings, and Kevin finished his career playing local football in the Hastings area.

By the 1990's Kevin was a publican and owned a bar in Spain before returning to the UK where he was running a pub in the Worcester area in the early 2000's.

After another period of living in Spain Kevin returned to England and his native Sussex in September 2010. Shortly afterwards he was diagnosed with cancer. He sadly died at St.Michael's Hospice, Hastings on 11.5.11 aged 61 after a brave battle with the disease.

The Hastings & St.Leonards Observer described Kevin as being "one of Hastings United's most liked and well known players over the years" and in their article Kevin's former United team-mate Dave Nessling said "He was a wholehearted and very, very strong player, but a genuinely nice bloke. Everybody liked Kevin and the supporters really took to him at Hastings." Another former team-mate - Sidley manager John Lambert - told the paper "He taught me so much about defending, so much about football and how to conduct myself." Kevin's funeral was held in Hastings and there was a gathering afterwards at Hastings United's Pilot Field, a venue the paper described as being his "spiritual home".

Kevin was the uncle of Gareth Barry who made 653 Premier League appearances for Aston Villa, Manchester City, Everton and West Bromwich Albion as well as winning 53 caps for England.

name: Jock Basford
other clubs: Wolverhampton Wanderers (0), Gainsborough Trinity, Brush Sports, Portsmouth (0), Bournemouth & Boscombe Athletic (0), Bath City, Southampton (0), West Ham United (0), Birmingham City (0), Grantham Town, Gloucester City and Holbeach United
bio:
6' 0" tall defender coincidentally born in Basford, Nottinghamshire who was on the books of First Division club Wolverhampton Wanderers during the 1937/38 campaign. Jock featured in Wolves junior sides but never in the reserves or first team before being released at the end of the season.

He played for Nottinghamshire amateur club Annesley Welfare during the 1938/39 campaign and Jock also turned out for Midland General Omnibus Company in the Nottinghamshire Thursday League.

He had trials with Derby and Nottingham Forest before joining Gainsborough Trinity of the Midland and Yorkshire League ahead of the 1939/40 campaign.

During World War II he had a stint with Brush Sports as well as having spells at various Football League clubs as a guest player. The clubs concerned were Portsmouth, Bournemouth & Boscombe, Southampton, West Ham United and Birmingham City. Jock also appeared for Bath City during the conflict.

After the war, Jock played for Grantham Town before joining Southern League club Gloucester City in the summer of 1948.

In June 1949 Jock joined Margate, becoming the club's new player-manager on a one-year contract. He was a qualified FA coach and made his debut in a 2-1 win over Betteshanger at Hartsdown Park on 20.8.49 - the opening day of the 1949/50 season. Jock's performance at centre-back pleased the local press who praised his power in the air and distribution. His appearances were sporadic over the months that followed but on 29.10.49 Jock scored when playing as a makeshift striker in a 2-2 draw with Sittingbourne at Hartsdown. Shortly afterwards, he suffered a depressed fracture of his cheekbone that kept him on the sidelines for two months.

Towards the end of the season, Jock was informed that his contract as player-manager would not be renewed and in May 1950 he left the club having scored once in 14 appearances.

Jock joined Midland Counties League outfit Gainsborough Trinity as a player for the start of the 1950/51 campaign - his second spell with the club - and in November 1950 he was in the side that lost 3-0 at home to Plymouth in the First Round of the FA Cup.

Later in the 1950/51 season Jock became player-manager of United Counties League club Holbeach United.

He played for Gainsborough again during the 1953/54 campaign and by the end of that season Jock was 34.

After retiring as a player, Jock spent seven years as trainer-coach at Charlton before becoming assistant manager / trainer of Exeter.

In June 1966 he became Exeter s manager before leaving the club in April 1967.

In July 1967 Jock joined Mansfield as a coach and became their manager in July 1970. He was sacked in November 1971 but later returned to the club. He was working as Mansfield's youth team coach at the time of his death on 17.3.82. Jock was 62.

His full name was Walter David Basford.

name: John Batley
other clubs: Ramsgate Athletic, Ramsgate and Deal Town
bio:
Local player who started his career with Ramsgate Athletic where he made a one-off appearance for the first team during 1967/68. John then played for Margate A (Under-18's) under Terry Morris and progressed into Margate's reserves. He first featured for them during the 1968/69 season and on the last day of the 1970/71 campaign he made his first team debut, playing at left-back in a 3-1 defeat at Dover in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie on 5.5.71. John also won the Banks Cup awarded to the club's best young player for the season.

He continued playing for the reserves during the 1971/72 campaign and remained with the club for the following season too. John made three further first team appearances (one as sub) during 1972/73, the first of them in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie at Hastings on 15.11.72 that Margate lost 6-0.

He left the club at the end of the season and rejoined Ramsgate where he was a regular in the reserves during the 1973/74 campaign.

John then moved to Deal for the 1974/75 season before dropping into local football and in August 1976 he emigrated to Canada.

In 2003 John was back in the UK and living in Chislehurst, Kent. His sister was married to former Margate goalkeeper Paul Thomas.

name: Allen Batsford
other clubs: Arsenal (0), Folkestone Town, Ramsgate Athletic, Feltham United and Wembley
bio:
Hard working, thoughtful midfielder who began his career as a junior at Arsenal, joining them as an amateur in 1947. Allen then signed professional forms for the Gunners in July 1949 and stayed with the club until May 1955. During his eight years at Highbury Allen made over 200 appearances in Arsenal's youth, reserve and third teams and picked up London FA Challenge Cup, Eastern Counties League Championship and London Midweek Championship winners medals. However he never made a first team appearance.

After leaving Arsenal Allen spent three years with Folkestone.

In July 1958 he signed for Ramsgate and on 14.3.59 Allen scored as the Rams won 4-0 in a Kent League game at Margate. He found the net again as Ramsgate beat Margate 2-1 at Southwood in a Thames & Medway Combination game on 27.3.59.

In the summer of 1959, Allen joined Margate and made his debut in midfield in a 7-0 win over Dover at Hartsdown Park on 3.9.59. He went on to make a total of ten first team appearances during the early part of the 1959/60 season and scored once - the only goal in a 1-0 win over Folkestone at Hartsdown in a Kent Senior Shield tie on 21.10.59. However he wasn't able to establish himself and spent the majority of the campaign in the reserves before leaving Margate at the end of the season.

Allen then joined Surrey Senior League club Feltham United and also played for a Feltham side in the local Sunday League.

In November 1964, Allen was appointed as coach by Wembley aged 32, working alongside new manager Roy Dew who was only 31 himself. Allen carried on playing Sunday football and also made occasional appearances for Wembley as a player during 1964/65. Dew was sacked as manager by Wembley in September 1965 and Allen also lost his job.

He soon returned to Feltham and Allen was still playing for them during the 1966/67 campaign. By then he was also managing the team.

In the summer of 1967, Allen began what turned out to be a remarkable period of managerial success in the non-league game when he took charge of Walton & Hersham. Allen stayed with the club for seven years and during that time they won the Athenian League (1968/69) and the FA Amateur Cup at Wembley (1972/73). Walton also played Margate in the FA Cup during the 1972/73 season.

In May 1974, Allen took over at Wimbledon and guided the club to three Southern League titles. Wimbledon also enjoyed several famous FA Cup runs during his time in charge.

Allen then had short spells in charge of Dulwich and Hillingdon before enjoying further success with Wealdstone, winning the Southern League once more with them. However during his time there he had a triple heart by-pass operation and the Wealdstone job was Allen's last managerial post. He then worked as a scout for Sheffield United, Watford and Nottingham Forest, travelling all over England and Europe.

In later years he spent six years as Youth Development Manager at Millwall and in 2003 Allen was still working for the Lions, assessing future opponents and scouting.

During the 2004/05 season he was President of Walton & Hersham.

Allen died on 28.12.09 aged 77 having suffered a heart attack at Fulham Broadway underground station on the way home from watching a game between Chelsea and Fulham. Former Wimbledon keeper Dickie Guy told the Daily Mail "He was a nice man, a great friend and a good manager" whilst many Wimbledon and Wealdstone supporters posted messages on the internet saying that Allen was the best manager their clubs had ever had.

name: Darren Baxter
other clubs: Brighton & Hove Albion (0), Chelsea (0), Heart of Midlothian (Scotland) (0), Worthing, St Albans City, New York Freedoms (USA), Wealdstone, Toronto Lynx (Canada), Oakville Blue Devils (Canada) and Torquay United (0+1,0)
bio:
5' 7" tall left-sided midfielder born in Brighton who attended Hove Park School and played for Hove Park Colts as a youngster. Darren also had a spell on Brighton's books as a schoolboy.

He signed for Chelsea as a trainee ahead of the 1998/99 season and played in the club's youth sides until moving to Scotland to join Hearts towards the end of the 2000/01 campaign.

Darren was unable to play for Hearts' first team as the paperwork relating to his move was completed after the transfer deadline but he was a regular in the reserves before being released at the end of the 2000/01 season.

In the summer of 2001 Darren returned to his native Sussex and dropped into non-league football when he signed for Isthmian League Division 1 club Worthing. In October 2001 he made a one-off appearance for Isthmian League Premier Division side St Albans before going back to Worthing and Darren scored once in 22 league appearances (two as sub) for them before joining St Albans on a permanent basis in April 2002.

He made nine more appearances (four as sub) for St Albans without scoring in the closing weeks of the 2001/02 campaign and Darren then left the club at the end of the season.

He spent the rest of 2002 in the USA where he played for New York Freedoms in the Pro Select division of the United Soccer Leagues.

Darren briefly returned to England in January 2003 and made a one-off appearance for Wealdstone before heading back to the USA to resume his spell with New York Freedoms.

In the Spring of 2004 he had an unsuccessful trial spell with Major League Soccer (MLS) club MetroStars and Darren also had an extended trial with MLS side Montreal Impact before eventually signing for Toronto Lynx. They played in the A-League, the second tier of football in the USA, and Darren scored four goals from 24 outings during the 2004 season. He was chosen as the club's Best Offensive Player' for the campaign and was also selected in the league's Team of the Week' on two occasions during the season.

Darren moved to Oakville Blue Devils of the Canadian Premier Soccer League for the 2005 campaign and in July 2005 he played for the league's All-Stars' side in a match against Glasgow Rangers in Toronto.

In September 2005 Darren returned to the UK and in November he signed for Margate. He made his debut in midfield in an Isthmian League Premier Division game at Windsor & Eton on 19.11.05 but although Margate won 1-0 the Thanet Times said "a shocking pitch never really gave him a chance to show what he could do". It turned out to be Darren's only appearance and he left the club soon afterwards.

He rejoined Toronto Lynx for the 2006 season and made eight appearances for them during the campaign before making a permanent return to England in January 2007.

Darren was signed by League Two club Torquay and on 30.1.07 he made his Football League debut when he came on as a half-time substitute in a 5-0 defeat at Mansfield. It was his only first team outing for Torquay and in February 2007 he was released.

In the summer of 2007 Darren played in some friendlies for Eastbourne Borough but wasn't signed by the club and he was last heard of when he made a one-off appearance for Dorchester in a friendly against Torquay in October 2007.

name: Larry Baxter
other clubs: Northampton Town (17,2), Norwich City (5,0), Gillingham (68,7), Torquay United (181,22), Cheltenham Town, Deal Town, Loughborough United, Bourne Town, Newfoundpool WMC, Linwood Lane, Enderby Forest, GEC Leicester, Groby, Blaby Old Boys and St.Andrews
bio:
Skilful midfielder born in Leicester who played for the Leicestershire Schoolboys team that won the English Schools Trophy before starting his senior career with 3rd Division South club Northampton, joining them in March 1952. Larry made 17 first team appearances for the Cobblers during the 1952/53 and 1953/54 seasons before moving on to Norwich, also in the 3rd Division South, in November 1954.

He made a handful of appearances for the Canaries and then joined Gillingham in October 1955.

Larry went on to make 68 senior appearances for the Gills during 1955/56 and 1956/57, scoring seven goals.

His next move took him to Torquay in September 1957 and Larry clocked up 181 first team appearances there and scored 22 goals between 1957/58 and 1961/62 before moving to Cheltenham in July 1962.

Larry made 77 appearances for Cheltenham during the 1962/63 and 1963/64 seasons, scoring 19 goals and helping the club to win promotion to the Southern League Premier Division. He was also chosen to represent the Southern League during his time there.

He then moved to Deal and became their player-manager in March 1964, replacing former Margate player Billy Jowett as Deal boss. However a financial crisis at Deal led to the club's entire squad, including Larry, being transfer listed towards the end of 1965 and as a result Margate signed him in December of that year.

Larry made his debut for Margate on 18.12.65 and played well in a 0-0 draw at King's Lynn, impressing with his accurate passing and hard working style. However three days later Larry suffered the indignity of scoring an own goal against the club he'd just left as Margate won 5-2 at Deal in a Kent Floodlight Cup game. He stayed with Margate for the remainder of the 1965/66 season but was only a bit-part player and made just seven appearances, some at left-back, before being released at the end of the campaign.

Two months into the 1966/67 season Larry had already added two more clubs to his footballing CV - Loughborough United and Bourne Town.

He went on to have spells with Newfoundpool WMC, Linwood Lane (as player-manager), Enderby Forest, GEC Leicester, Groby (as player-manager), Blaby BC and then ended his career at St.Andrews.

In May 2000, the Torquay-based Herald Express reported that Larry was employed as a club singer in Leicester and in 2011 he was living in a village called Enderby, just outside Leicester, and still performing at the age of 80.

After a long illness, Larry died at home in Leicester on 24.11.16 - the day of his 85th birthday.

name: Peter Beadle
other clubs: Gillingham (46+30,16), Tottenham Hotspur (0), AFC Bournemouth (9,2), Southend United (8,1), Watford (13+11,1), Bristol Rovers (112+13,42), Port Vale (21+5,6), Notts County (15+11,3), Bristol City (64+42,19), Brentford (1,0), Barnet, Team Bath and Clevedon Town
bio:
6' 1" tall striker born in Camberwell who began his career with Lordswood Boys as a youth before joining Gillingham in 1988. Peter made his first team debut for the Gills in a home game against Cardiff City on 11.3.89 and he was only 16 at the time.

In March 1990 Peter joined Margate on loan and made his debut on 31.3.90 in a 2-1 defeat at the hands of Dunstable in a Southern League game at Hartsdown. He played up front with Karl Lloyd who scored his last goal for the club that day. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said that Peter "showed distinct promise" but it turned out to be his only appearance as Gillingham recalled him almost immediately, cutting short what was expected to be a loan spell lasting to the end of the 1989/90 season.

After returning to Priestfield Peter became a regular in the Gills' first team and in May 1990 he was given a professional contract. He went on to make a total of 76 appearances (30 as sub) in all competitions for the Gills and scored 16 goals.

In June 1992 Tottenham paid £300,000 for Peter's services - a club record fee for Gillingham at the time. However his dream move turned sour and Peter never made a first team appearance for Spurs. During his time at White Hart Lane he had loan spells at Bournemouth (March-April 1993) and Southend (March-April 1994) before being sold to Watford for just £5,000 in September 1994.

Peter struggled for form at Vicarage Road and in November 1995 he joined Bristol Rovers for a fee of £30,000. After scoring 43 goals from 127 games (13 as sub) in all competitions for the Pirates Peter moved to Port Vale for £300,000 in August 1998.

His next move took him to Notts County in February 1999 and the Meadow Lane outfit paid £250,000 for Peter's services. Eight months later he was transferred to Bristol City for £200,000, taking his total career transfer fees past £1,000,000.

Peter spent nearly four years at Ashton Gate and scored 19 goals in the 106 appearances (42 as sub) he made in all competitions before being released at the end of the 2002/03 season.

During the summer of 2003 Peter had trials with Cheltenham before signing for Brentford for the start of the 2003/04 season. However after making just one first team appearance he joined Conference outfit Barnet in September 2003. It was Peter's first taste of non-league football since his appearance for Margate over 13 years earlier.

After scoring five goals for Barnet Peter was on the move again in December 2003. He joined Team Bath as player-coach and in the summer of 2004 he linked up with Clevedon.

Peter went on to make nine appearances (seven as sub) without scoring for Clevedon during 2004/05 and he was Commercial Manager too.

In May 2005 Peter left Clevedon to become manager of Southern League Taunton Town and in October 2005 he took over the reigns at Newport County, by that time he had retired as a player.

Peter was still in charge at Newport during the 2006/07 season and in November 2006 he was involved in a much-publicised altercation with the fourth official during an FA Cup tie against Swansea. The incident led to the Football Association of Wales charging Peter with misconduct. He was sacked as Newport's manager at the end of the 2007/08 campaign.

After leaving Newport Peter did some scouting and coaching for West Bromwich Albion's academy before returning to management in March 2010 with Southern Premier League outfit Clevedon who he'd played for five years earlier. Peter left Clevedon again at the end of the 2009/10 season.

He then had an 18-month spell as manager of Cheltenham s Under-16 s team before taking a year out of football.

In the Spring of 2013 Peter became manager of Hereford s youth team and in March 2014 he took over as the Bulls caretaker first team manager following the departure of Martin Foyle. Peter s first match in charge saw Hereford lose 2-0 at Barnet in the Conference on 22.3.14.

In May 2014 he was appointed as Head Coach of Conference South club Sutton.

name: Sam Beale
other clubs: Tonbridge Angels, Brentford (0), Northwood, Lewes and Sittingbourne
bio:
Left-sided player born in Kent who was with Guru Nanak as youngster before moving to Tonbridge.

Sam featured in the Angels Under-18's side during 2010/11 and also played for Kent's Under-18's that season.

He then spent the 2011/12 and 2012/13 campaigns at Brentford as part of their development squad.

In December 2012 Sam started a loan spell with Northwood of the Southern Football League Division One Central and he made four appearances there (one as sub) without scoring before going back to Brentford in January 2013.

Sam was released by Brentford at the end of the 2012/13 season having been injured for much of the campaign. The Bees invited him to train with the club during the summer of 2013 but Sam didn't take up the offer.

During the early part of the 2013/14 campaign he had a short spell with Isthmian League Premier Division club Lewes and Sam scored in his only senior outing for them - a 2-1 home win over Corinthian Casuals in the Isthmian League Cup on 2.10.13.

Towards the end of October 2013 Sam joined Margate and spent some time in the Under-21's squad before making his first team debut at left-back in a 3-0 home defeat against Chesham in the FA Trophy on 16.11.13. He also wore the number three shirt in Margate's next game - a 1-0 win over Carshalton in the Isthmian League Premier Division at Hartsdown Park on 19.11.13 - but left the club soon afterwards.

In December 2013 Sam joined Sittingbourne of the Isthmian League Division 1 South and spent the remainder of 2013/14 there.

name: John Beales
other clubs: Tonbridge Angels, Dartford, Hastings United and Erith & Belvedere
bio:
Defender who progressed through Tonbridge s youth ranks before making his first team debut for the Angels aged 17 in a 2-1 home defeat against Welling in the Kent Senior Cup on 29.10.02.

Over the course of the next five seasons John played over 250 times for Tonbridge and in April 2008 he was linked with a move to Bristol Rovers before suffering a cruciate ligament injury.

John didn t play again for over a year but having finally regained fitness he signed for Dartford in July 2009 and made 38 Isthmian League Premier Division appearances (five as sub) without scoring during 2009/10 as the Darts won the title.

In the summer of 2010 John moved on to Hastings and scored three times in 23 outings before leaving the club in December 2010.

He then had a brief spell back at Dartford early in January 2011 but by the end of the month he d rejoined Tonbridge.

John made 13 Premier Division appearances for the Angels during the remainder of the 2010/11 campaign and scored twice but doubts about his fitness led to him being released by the club at the end of the season.

John trained with Margate during the summer of 2011 and after proving his fitness he formally signed for the club in October 2011, shortly after playing twice for Erith & Belvedere in the Kent League. Former Margate player Mike Azzopardi was in the Deres team when John made his debut for the club in a 3-1 home win over Deal on 1.10.11 and coincidentally Azzopardi had also been in the Tonbridge side when John made his debut for the Angels nine years earlier.

On 11.10.11 John made his debut for Margate at centre-back in a 2-1 home win over Cray in the Kent Senior Cup and the Isle of Thanet Gazette then said he looked the part" in a 3-1 win over visitors Kingstonian in the Isthmian League Cup on 18.10.11. John started the next four games wearing the number five shirt but on 5.11.11 he had to go off 20 minutes into a 1-1 draw with Wealdstone in an FA Trophy tie at Hartsdown Park. He collided with keeper Simon Overland and suffered a bad cut above his eye. John missed Margate s next four games as a result.

He returned to action in a 1-0 home win over Ramsgate in the Kent Senior Cup on 22.11.11 and from then on John was ever-present until the end of the season. In its report on a 4-1 win over visitors Hastings in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 2.1.12 the Isle of Thanet Gazette said John was forming a smashing understanding" with fellow centre-back Craig Cloke and the Thanet Times said he was excellent" in a 1-0 win over Concord Rangers at Hartsdown Park on 7.1.12.

The Times described John as being nice and solid" in its report on a 0-0 home draw with Leatherhead on 10.3.12 and at the end of March 2012 he became Margate s captain for a spell when Craig Cloke wasn t in the side. On 9.4.12 John got his first goal with a header in a 3-1 home defeat against Cray and he ended the campaign as Margate s Players Player of the Year' having made a total of 36 appearances.

John became Margate s permanent captain for the 2012/13 campaign and on 7.8.12 he scored in a 2-1 friendly win over Horsham at Hartsdown Park. He went on to be a fixture in the side at centre-back barring minor cup ties and after a 2-0 home win over Enfield Town in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 15.9.12 John told the Isle of Thanet Gazette We can hopefully stay there on the top of the league. The season is still early doors but we will be looking to stay there as long as possible."

On 10.11.12 he missed his first league game of the campaign as Margate won 2-0 at Harrow and on 8.12.12 John headed home his first goal of the season in a 2-0 win over visitors Wingate & Finchley. Margate s website said he was brilliant in defence" during a 3-0 home win over Bognor Regis on 9.3.13 and on 19.3.13 John scored with a header from a Matt Bodkin corner in a 1-1 draw at Whitehawk.

He finished the campaign having scored twice from 46 appearances and John won the Players Player of the Season award once again. He told Margate s website It s good to know that the boys respect you and think you re doing well." John also spoke about the difficulties of non-league football and said A lot of us have got full time jobs. You re up early in the morning; you do the Tuesday night away games - Bury, Lowestoft (for example) - getting home two o clock in the morning. You get up, work and then you re straight back training. Most of the time it s harder than full time football, but you just keep going."

In June 2013 John signed a contract to stay with Margate for the 2013/14 season and on 2.8.13 he made his first appearance of the campaign in a 2-2 draw at Ramsgate. As captain, John lifted the Thanet Challenge Cup after the game that had secured an aggregate win for Margate.

On 13.8.13 he headed home from a Matt Bodkin corner during a 2-1 defeat against AFC Hornchurch in the Premier Division at Hartsdown Park but on 3.9.13 John scored an own-goal in an 8-0 defeat at Dover in the Kent Senior Cup. Having been a regular in the number five shirt for the first few months of 2013/14 John had to go off with a knee injury during a 4-1 win over visitors Clevedon in an FA Trophy tie on 2.11.13 and joint-manager Simon Osborn told the Kentish Football website It s disappointing to lose John because he s a major part of us. He s our captain and he s played well again today so we ll just have to see how he settles down tomorrow.

John had damaged ligaments in his knee and the problem ended up keeping him out for over two months. During his spell on the sidelines John was Margate s caretaker manager for one match - a 2-1 home defeat against Billericay on 10.12.13 - before the appointment of Terry Brown.

After sitting out 13 games John made his comeback from injury in a 3-2 defeat against Hendon at Hartsdown Park on 11.1.14 and by then new signing Jamie Stuart had become Margate s captain. Shortly after his return to action John spoke to the Isle of Thanet Gazette about the captaincy and said I would have liked to have kept it but I've taken it on the chin. Terry spoke to me and told me his decision and I respect the gaffer wants Jamie as his captain. I need to get myself fit as there's going to be competitions for places all over the pitch.

During February 2014 John ended up captaining the side again for a few games when Stuart was out injured but in the eighth match of his comeback John picked up a hamstring injury and had to go off in the second half as Margate lost 2-1 at home to Kingstonian on 8.3.14.

After missing another 11 games John featured as a substitute in a 5-0 win over Cray at Hartsdown Park on 21.4.14 and he then started Margate s last game of the season - a 3-2 win over Hendon at Wembley FC on 26.4.14 to finish the campaign having scored once from 30 appearances (one as sub).

In May 2014 John signed another one-year contract and by the start of the 2014/15 season he was Margate s longest-serving player.

name: Simon Beard
other clubs: West Ham United (0), Peterborough United (0), Sittingbourne, Millwall (0), Hastings Town, Dover Athletic and Welling United
bio:
Bromley-born player who started his career as a trainee at West Ham where he played as a striker. In May 1991 Simon had a trial with Peterborough and turned out for their reserves in a game against Bury before being released by West Ham at the end of the 1990/91 season.

He joined Sittingbourne in the summer of 1991 aged 18 and initially played for the Brickies' reserve side. Simon made his first team debut in December 1991 and scored both goals in a 2-0 home win over Canterbury. Unfortunately there was a problem with his registration and as a result Sittingbourne were docked the three points Simon's brace had earned them. He went on to spend almost four years with the Brickies and scored 12 goals during 1993/94.

In January 1995 Simon was given a trial by Millwall at the same time as his teammate, and future Margate player, Tom Planck. On 30.1.95 he played for Millwall Reserves in a Football Combination game against Bristol Rovers at The New Den. Former England striker Clive Allen was also in the Millwall side, playing alongside Planck up front, and the Lions won 2-0. Nothing further came of Millwall s interest.

Simon had won Sittingbourne s 'Player of the Year' award twice by the time that he left the club in August 1995.

He was initially set to join Dover after a tribunal had agreed a fee for him but when Dover's manager John Ryan was sacked the deal was scrapped. As a result Simon signed for Hastings instead and became the club's captain. He stayed with Hastings until January 1999 when he finally linked up with Dover.

Simon made over 100 appearances for Dover and won the club's 'Player's Player of the Year' award for the 2000/01 campaign before signing for Margate in May 2001 when his contract expired. Margate manager Chris Kinnear had originally tried to sign him a few months earlier.

Shortly after Simon's capture was announced Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "Simon is a talented, experienced Conference player and is just the type we need to strengthen the squad." He made his debut in midfield on 11.8.01 as Margate took on Worcester at Hartsdown Park in the Southern League Championship Match. The match ended in a 1-1 draw and went to penalties. Simon slotted home the winning kick and his wild celebrations including kissing the badge on his shirt quickly endeared him to Margate supporters. On 18.8.01 Simon was part of the Margate side that famously won 1-0 at Boston in the club's first ever Conference match and he wore the number eight shirt in the next 12 games too. He got his first goal for the club in a 2-2 draw against visitors Hereford on 1.9.01 and on 11.9.01 Simon struck to earn Margate a 1-0 at Woking.

He was made captain in the absence of Graham Porter as Margate entertained Hayes on 2.10.01 but it turned out to be a bad evening for Simon. He was sent off in the second half after picking up two yellow cards and also suffered a facial injury that required stitches after the game which Margate won 1-0. Having served a one match suspension Simon struggled to regain his midfield place and only featured as a substitute in the next two games he was available for. He returned to the side on 27.10.01 as Margate lost 2-0 at Grays in an FA Cup tie and then played regularly again after that. On 10.11.01 Simon headed a dramatic equaliser seven minutes into stoppage time to earn Margate a 1-1 draw with Nuneaton at Hartsdown Park and in December he scored in consecutive matches. After being on target in a 2-2 draw at Leigh on 8.12.01 Simon cracked home a stunning 35-yard effort in a 4-1 defeat at Dagenham & Redbridge on 15.12.01 and that game saw him play as a centre-back for the first time. The Thanet Times said Simon "acquitted himself well".

He continued to be an automatic choice at the start of 2002, usually in midfield, and on 19.1.02 Simon was sent off again in a 3-0 defeat at Hereford after picking up two bookings. After a two game ban he returned to the side for a 1-0 defeat at Doncaster on 16.2.02 but Simon picked up a foot injury during the match that ruled him out for over two months. The problem mystified doctors and Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "We just can't get to the bottom of Beardy's injury." After a 3-1 defeat at Stevenage on 2.3.02 that Simon missed the home club's doctor looked at his foot and couldn't help. An x-ray also showed nothing and Chris Kinnear told the Thanet Times "No one knows what's wrong. It's weird. I've been in football a long time and I've never seen an injury like it. It's right on the bottom of the foot. Maybe it'll just heal up."

Simon eventually returned to action in a game at Barnet on 20.4.02. He came on as a substitute and scored with a brilliant 30-yard effort as Margate went down 4-1. The Thanet Times described it as a "first-time wonder strike" and a "worthy contender for any Margate goal of the season competition" as Simon fired a poor goal-kick straight back and into the net. He then started Margate's next game - a Kent Senior Cup tie against Ashford at Hartsdown Park on 23.4.02 - but Simon had to go off in the first half after his foot injury flared up again. Margate ran out 5-0 winners. He missed the last two matches of the season and ended the campaign having scored six goals in 32 appearances (three as sub).

Simon featured in Margate's friendlies ahead of the 2002/03 season but then suffered a recurrence of his foot injury which put him out of action for around two months. On 8.10.02 he made his first appearance of the campaign when he came on as a substitute in a 4-1 defeat at Farnborough and Simon then started Margate's next match - a 2-2 draw at Halifax on 12.10.02. On 26.10.02 he had an outing at centre-back in a 2-1 win at Gravesend & Northfleet in the FA Cup and the Thanet Times said Simon was "especially impressive" but his foot problem then flared up again and ruled him out of Margate's next six matches. He returned to the side as a substitute in a 3-0 defeat against Cardiff in the FA Cup at Margate's adopted home at Dover and Simon then enjoyed a good run in the team, starting nine of the next ten games. The Thanet Times described him as a "key player" in a 3-1 win at Stevenage on 14.12.02 and said Simon's "strength in midfield proved crucial". A week later he got his first goal of the season in a 1-1 draw with Nuneaton at Dover.

At the start of 2003 Simon embarked on a scoring spree that started with a goal in a 4-2 win over Gravesend & Northfleet at Hartsdown Park on New Year's Day. He was on target once more as Margate drew 4-4 with Northwich at Hartsdown on 18.1.03 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "produced one of his best performances in Gate colours as he controlled the midfield" during a 2-1 win at Gravesend & Northfleet on 21.1.03. Simon found the net again in a 4-1 defeat at Forest Green on 25.1.03 and a 2-0 win at Worcester in the FA Trophy on 1.2.03 to take his run to five goals in eight matches but his season was drawing to a close. After playing in a 2-0 defeat against Hereford at Dover on 11.2.03 Simon missed Margate's next game and when he came on as a substitute in a 2-0 defeat against Tamworth at Hartsdown on 22.2.03 it was his final outing of the campaign. Soon afterwards Simon discovered that he had a chipped bone in his ankle and he missed Margate's last 14 games. He'd made 16 appearances (three as sub) and scored five goals before injury intervened.

Simon was fit enough to take part in some of Margate's friendlies in the summer of 2003 but he was transfer-listed before the start of the 2003/04 season proper. Chris Kinnear said "Unfortunately because of wage budgeting, which is now strictly enforced by the Conference, we are going to have to let Simon go."

On 9.8.03 he made his first appearance for almost six months when he came on as a substitute as Margate drew 1-1 at Shrewsbury on the opening day of the new Conference campaign but Simon didn't feature in any of the next five matches. He returned to the side on 6.9.03 and went straight into the starting line-up as Margate took on Chester at Dover. Simon played in the heart of the defence and the Thanet Times said he gave a "fine performance at the back" as the visitors won 2-1. It turned out to be his last appearance for Margate and later in September Simon joined Welling on a free transfer. Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "His injuries were the main consideration - it's a lot of money to pay someone if they're not playing."

Simon's spell with Welling was blighted by injury and the Wings released him at the end of the 2003/04 season.

In the summer of 2004 he retired aged 31 after undergoing two foot operations.

During his time with Margate Simon worked for the HSBC bank at their branch in the Hempstead Valley shopping centre near Gillingham.

name: Dean Beckwith
other clubs: Gillingham (0+2,0), Tonbridge Angels, Dagenham & Redbridge, Hereford United (111+4,3), Northampton Town (80+4,3), Luton Town and Eastleigh
bio:
6' 3" tall defender born in Southwark, London who started his career with Gillingham. Dean progressed through the Gills' youth ranks and during the 2002/03 season he had a loan spell with Tonbridge where he made seven appearances without scoring.

In July 2003 Dean signed professional forms for Gillingham and at the start of October 2003 he was loaned out to Conference club Dagenham & Redbridge.

He scored once in five outings for the Daggers and featured in a 4-0 home win over Margate on 7.10.03.

Dean became captain of Gillingham's reserves for the start of the 2004/05 campaign and in September 2004 he joined Margate on a month's loan.

He made his debut at centre-back in a 1-0 defeat against Weymouth at Margate's adopted home in Ashford on 11.9.04 and the Thanet Times said Dean's performance was "one cause for Margate optimism". Assistant manager Kevin Raine told the paper "It's good for everybody concerned. We're glad to have him for the month, and maybe he'll stay a little bit longer." Dean also started Margate's next two Conference South games in the number five shirt but after a 4-2 win at Maidenhead on 18.9.04 injury forced him to miss a match.

Dean returned to the side for a trip to Redbridge on 25.9.04 but the Thanet Times said "just two minutes into the game Beckwith must have been wishing he had given it a miss" when he was robbed after dwelling on the ball just outside the penalty area and Redbridge scored. Dean later handballed to give the hosts a penalty which resulted in their second goal and Margate ended up losing the game 2-1. He sat out the next match - an FA Cup tie which Gillingham didn't want him to take part in - and Dean then lined up at right wing-back in a 1-1 draw with Newport at Ashford on 9.10.04. It was his last outing for Margate and he returned to Gillingham having played five times in all.

Shortly after returning to Priestfield Dean was sent off in consecutive reserve team matches and in one of them - a 2-1 win over Brighton reserves - the Gills' future Margate player Akwasi Edusei was also dismissed. On 8.1.05 Dean made his first team debut for Gillingham when he took to the field as an 89th minute substitute in a 1-0 defeat at Portsmouth in the FA Cup. Coincidentally future Margate player Matt Bodkin made his first appearance for the Gills that day whilst Barry Ashby and Paul Smith who were both later involved at Margate were also in the side. Dean made one further sub appearance for the Gills - coming on after 83 minutes of a 3-1 win at Rotherham in the Championship on 5.3.05 - before being released by the club in June 2005.

He joined Conference outfit Hereford ahead of the 2005/06 campaign and in his first season with the club Dean helped the Bulls to win promotion to the Football League via the play-offs. A crowd of over 15,000 saw Hereford beat Halifax 3-2 in the final at Leicester's Walkers Stadium.

Dean went on to make over 100 appearances for the Bulls after they entered the Football League and Hereford were promoted to League One for the 2008/09 campaign. He'd spent four years with the club when he signed for League Two side Northampton in June 2009.

Dean made 84 first team appearances (four as sub) for the Cobblers during the 2009/10 and 2010/11 seasons before being released by the club.

In June 2011 he signed for Conference outfit Luton and then in January 2013 Dean joined Eastleigh.

The Conference South club s manager Richard Hill told Eastleigh s website I have been chasing Dean s signature for around two months now and am delighted he has agreed to join us and in doing so, has turned down a number of approaches from well established Conference National teams. I am certain Dean will get a fantastic reception and become a firm fans favorite. Signing players of Dean s calibre will be very important if the club is to achieve its short, medium and long term goals."

name: Aaron Beech
other clubs: Watford (0), Ramsgate and Broadstairs
bio:
5' 11" tall midfielder born in Watford who was on his hometown club s books from the age of 11 and progressed through the Hornets youth ranks. By the 2006/07 season Aaron was featuring regularly in Watford s Under-18 and reserve teams, captaining both on occasions, but during 2007/08 he was troubled by leg problems.

Aaron had to undergo serious operations on both legs due to arteries being positioned in the wrong place which meant that when he ran no blood circulated through his calves. At the end of 2008 he was released by Watford as manager Brendan Rodgers hadn t seen him play enough and in 2011 Aaron told the This Is Kent website He told me I'd been unlucky but it hurt."

Having moved to Thanet where his parents lived Aaron contacted Margate manager Terry Yorath to ask for a trial in the summer of 2009 and he featured in a few pre-season friendlies. Yorath told the Thanet Times He had a bad injury 18 months ago so I m looking for him to get fitter and see what he can do at 100 per cent fitness." Aaron s younger brother Joe was also an unused substitute in some of Margate s friendlies.

On 28.7.09 Aaron made his competitive debut when he featured in a 1-0 win over Ramsgate at Hartsdown Park in the 1st Leg of a tie played for the Isle of Thanet Gazette Cup. He also came on as a substitute in the 2nd Leg at Ramsgate on 1.8.09 - a 1-1 draw. Aaron then spent the remainder of 2009/10 in the reserves where he sometimes played alongside Joe. Aaron s only other first team outing came when he wore the number four shirt in a 2-0 defeat at Welling in a Kent Senior Cup tie on 30.3.10.

In May 2010 Aaron signed for Ramsgate and their manager Jimmy Ward told the Isle of Thanet Gazette He played first team football at Watford before a bad injury, so he has league credentials, and Terry Yorath thought a lot of him. We re not in the habit of turning down players like that. It didn t work out at Margate but he fancies giving it a go here, so it could be our gain. He s a big, strong midfielder, so we ll see what happens."

Aaron went on to make 32 Isthmian League Division 1 South appearances (one as sub) for the Rams during 2010/11 and scored twice. He stayed with the club for the start of the 2011/12 season too but only featured in six league games (twice as sub) before leaving Southwood towards the end of October 2011.

By the end of 2011 Aaron was turning out for Generation Sports in the Thanet Sunday Football League and he also played once for Broadstairs in the Kent County League before rejoining Ramsgate in January 2012.

His second spell with the Rams was very brief and by March 2012 Aaron was back in local amateur football.

In the summer of 2012 he returned to Ramsgate once more and spent some of 2012/13 in their reserves but Aaron left the club again before the season ended without having featured in the Rams first team.

After another spell in local amateur football Aaron joined Ramsgate for a fourth spell early in March 2014.

name: Darren Behcet
other clubs: West Ham United (0), Cambridge United, Southend United (0), Yeovil Town (0), Dorchester Town, Bognor Regis Town, Fisher Athletic (London), Maldon Town, Sutton United, Grays Athletic, AFC Hornchurch, Maldon & Tiptree, Tooting & Mitcham United, East Thurrock United, Harlow Town and Cray Wanderers
bio:
6' 0" tall half Turkish keeper born in London who started his career as a trainee at West Ham where he was coached by Hammers legend Ludek Miklosko. During the 2003/04 season Darren played for the Irons Under-17 and Under-19 sides as well as featuring in the reserve team squad on occasions. He mainly turned out for the Under-18's during 2004/05 but Darren also made a few reserve team appearances.

At the start of the 2005/06 campaign he was loaned to Conference club Cambridge United and Darren played seven first team games before losing his place.

Towards the end of December 2005 he joined Southend on trial and by then Darren already knew that he'd be released by West Ham at the end of the season. He played in two reserve team games for the Shrimpers in January 2006 before moving to Margate on loan as a temporary replacement for Charlie Mitten who was struggling with injuries. Darren was recommended to the club by former Gate keeper Lee Turner who was Southend's goalkeeping coach at the time.

On 28.1.06 Darren made his debut aged 19 as Margate drew 0-0 with Harrow in an Isthmian League Premier Division match played at Hartsdown Park and then enjoyed a run in the side. An away game at AFC Wimbledon on 11.2.06 was Darren's fourth consecutive start and the Thanet Times praised a "flying save" he made but in the closing minutes of the match Darren made an error that led to stalwart sweeper Bill Edwards being sent off. Darren took a goal-kick that went straight to an unmarked Wimbledon striker and Edwards had little option but to bring the Dons player down to preserve Margate's 2-1 lead which they hung on to after his dismissal.

Darren then played in the next two games but in the second of them - a 4-0 win over Wealdstone at Northwood on 25.2.06 - he had to go off injured after an hour. He was due to start Margate's next match at Chelmsford on 3.3.06 but broke down in the pre-game warm-up and missed the match as well as Margate's next three fixtures. Darren returned to the side in a 4-1 defeat at Billericay on 25.3.06 and then made what the Thanet Times called "smart early saves" in a 2-1 home defeat against Heybridge on 1.4.06 before Charlie Mitten replaced him for Margate's next game. Darren then left the club.

A few weeks later Mitten got injured again and after his initial efforts to locate Darren failed new Margate player-manager Robin Trott finally tracked him down and Darren returned for the last two matches of the 2005/06 campaign. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he'd "impressively deputized" for Mitten in his initial spell with Margate. Darren made his comeback in a 2-0 win at Leyton on 22.4.06 and the Thanet Times said he "had little to do". He then featured in a 4-2 win over Hendon at Hartsdown Park on 29.4.06 to take his overall appearance tally for the season to ten games. Darren kept three clean sheets in those matches.

Having been released by West Ham Darren signed a two-year contract with League One club Yeovil in June 2006. He'd previously played twice for their reserves during the 2005/06 campaign. Darren became a regular in Yeovil's second string during the opening months of 2006/07 and on 28.11.06 he played in a Somerset Premier Cup tie at Minehead. The match was held up for a period after Darren had several coins thrown at him and the offenders were ejected from the ground. As the season progressed he sometimes featured on the substitutes bench for the first team but didn't make any senior appearances.

Darren joined Conference South club Dorchester on loan for the start of the 2007/08 campaign and their Director of Football Shaun Brooks said "He is a fantastic young keeper with a big future in the game, and a season playing regular first team football will be a huge help to his development". Darren played regularly for Dorchester until returning to Yeovil in January 2008.

He was released by the Glovers at the end of 2007/08 having never played for the first team and in August 2008 Darren joined Conference South outfit Bognor Regis on a week-to-week deal. He made four league appearances there before moving to Bognor's Conference South rivals Fisher in October 2008.

Darren's next move took him to Isthmian League Division 1 North club Maldon in the middle of November 2008 but he only played once there before switching to Isthmian League Premier Division side Sutton towards the end of the month.

Darren made his debut for Sutton in a 2-0 win at Croydon Athletic in the Isthmian League Cup on 2.12.08 and had four further outings deputizing for future Margate keeper Paul Nicholls in the weeks that followed.

In December 2008 Darren linked up with Conference outfit Grays Athletic - his fifth club of the 2008/09 season - as a non-contract player but didn't make any first team appearances and in January 2009 he signed for AFC Hornchurch of the Isthmian League Premier Division.

Darren went on to spend over two and a half years with Hornchurch and made around 100 league appearances before being released by the club in September 2011.

He joined Maldon & Tiptree of the Isthmian League Division 1 North immediately after leaving the Urchins but at the start of December 2011 the club signed former Margate keeper Scott Chalmers-Stevens to replace Darren and he moved on to Tooting & Mitcham having made six league starts for Maldon.

Darren was Tooting's regular keeper for the next few months and made 13 league appearances as they fought an unsuccessful battle against relegation from the Isthmian League Premier Division but in April 2012 he left the club shortly before the 2011/12 season ended.

In May 2012 Darren signed for Isthmian League Premier Division club Carshalton but before the start of the 2012/13 campaign proper he went back to Tooting. On 21.8.12 he was sent off as they lost 3-0 at home to Leatherhead in the Isthmian League Division 1 South and Darren made a total of 39 league appearances during 2012/13.

In July 2013 he linked up with Premier Division outfit East Thurrock and in October 2013 Darren moved on to Harlow of Division 1 North.

His next move took him to Premier Division strugglers Cray in January 2014.

name: Eddie Belchamber
other clubs: Ramsgate Athletic, Charlton Athletic (0), Deal Town and Dover
bio:
Wide player born in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire whose family originally came from Dartford. Eddie played for Kent Boys as a youngster and started his senior career with Ramsgate during the 1947/48 season.

On 28.2.48 he played in a trial match for Charlton and Eddie did so well that he was signed as an amateur at half-time during the game.

He moved on to Deal of the Kent League for the 1948/49 season and Eddie won a call-up to the England youth team squad, which also included future Margate player Vince Wright, but didn't win a cap.

In the summer of 1949 Eddie joined Margate and became a regular in the reserves. He also made a one-off appearance for the first team on 28.1.50, scoring in a 2-1 defeat at his old club Deal in the Kent League. Eddie impressed but then suffered an ankle injury that ruled him out of the rest of the 1949/50 campaign. He left the club at the end of the season.

Eddie joined Dover for 1950/51 and after starting the campaign in their senior side, he generally played for their reserves before leaving the club.

He also played rugby for Betteshanger and was still turning out for them during the 1952/53 campaign.

Eddie got married in 1955 whilst living in the Thanet area and later emigrated to Australia with his wife.

His real name was actually Elwin Belchamber but he was known as Eddie.

name: Jimmy Belcher
other clubs: Leyton Orient (0), Snowdown Colliery Welfare, West Ham United (0), Crystal Palace (137,22), Ipswich Town (29,0) and Brentford (36,1)
bio:
Midfielder born in Stepney, London who began his career as a junior at Leyton Orient in 1949 and signed professional forms for the O's in March 1950. During his time with Orient Jimmy had a loan spell with Kent League club Snowdown Colliery Welfare.

In August 1952 he was transferred to West Ham but didn't make the Hammers' first team and in June 1954 Jimmy moved onto Crystal Palace.

He went on to make over 130 first team appearances for the Eagles spanning the 1954/55 to 1957/58 seasons and was a member of the Palace team that won 3-2 at Margate in the FA Cup 1st Round on 16.11.57.

In May 1958 he moved to Ipswich and over the course of the next three seasons Jimmy made 29 first team appearances for the Suffolk club.

In July 1961 he linked up with Brentford and Jimmy played 36 first team games during 1961/62 before signing for Margate in the summer of 1962.

With his Football League pedigree Jimmy was felt to be a major capture for the club but things didn't work out for him at Hartsdown Park. He struggled for fitness initially and as a result Jimmy didn't make his first team debut until 7.11.62 when he wore the number ten shirt in 1-0 win at Romford in a Southern League Cup tie. He also featured in a 2-1 win at Ashford in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie on 28.11.62 but Jimmy didn't make any further senior appearances during 1962/63. He spent the rest of the campaign in the reserves and made a total of 29 appearances for them before being released at the end of the season.

During his time with Margate Jimmy lived in Rainham, Essex and during the 2002/03 season he was a regular visitor to Selhurst Park for Crystal Palace matches.

name: Derek Bellotti
other clubs: Queens Park Rangers (0), Bedford Town, Gillingham (43,0), Southend United (83,0), Charlton Athletic (16,0), Fulham (0), Swansea City (Wales) (22,0), Maidstone United, Cambridge City, St.Blazey, Torquay United (0), Falmouth Town, Saltash United, Bideford, Barnstaple Town, Stoke Gabriel, Newquay, Bovey Tracey, Torrington, Exeter City (0), Teignmouth, Galmpton United and Ilfracombe Town
bio:
6' 1" tall keeper born in West Ham, London. Derek started his career with Queens Park Rangers, becoming an apprentice in September 1963.

He was loaned to Southern League Bedford Town for two seasons - 1964/65 and 1965/66 - and Derek was Bedford's regular first-choice keeper until being injured in November 1965. He made a total of 73 appearances for the club.

In July 1966 he was signed by Gillingham and went on to spend four years at Priestfield, making 43 first team appearances for the Gills.

In October 1970 Charlton paid £5,000 for him and shortly before that, Derek had had a loan spell at Southend. He made 16 senior appearances for Charlton and had a loan spell at Fulham before being transferred in December 1971.

Derek rejoined Southend on a permanent basis and stayed there until the end of the 1973/74 campaign.

In May 1974 Derek moved to Swansea and spent 1974/75 there.

He linked up with Maidstone for the 1975/76 season having been offered a deal that included a job with The Kent Messenger newspaper. Derek went on to make 66 appearances for the Stones during 1975/76 and was in the side that beat Canterbury to win the Kent Senior Cup. He made another 65 appearances during 1976/77. Derek stayed with Maidstone for 1977/78 but faced strong competition from Barry Watling for a first team place.

In January 1978 Derek joined Margate on loan from Maidstone and made his debut in a 3-0 win over Taunton at Hartsdown Park on 14.1.78. He went on to make ten appearances filling in for the injured Steve Bowtell and was "an excellent replacement" according to the Thanet Times. He pulled off a string of great saves in a 2-0 win over Folkestone & Shepway on 18.2.78.

Derek returned to Maidstone in March 1978 and was immediately loaned to Cambridge City. He left Maidstone during the 1978/79 season and moved to Devon.

Derek joined South Western League club St.Blazey for 1979/80 and played for Devon during his time there.

He returned to the Football League for the 1980/81 season when he was signed by 4th Division Torquay as cover for their first-choice goalkeeper. Derek never featured in the senior side but was a regular in the reserves. He became player-manager of Torquay s reserve team for the 1981/82 campaign but left the club in the summer of 1982 after the reserves were disbanded as a cost-cutting measure.

After leaving Torquay, Derek joined Western League club Falmouth for the 1982/83 season. He then had spells with Saltash and Bideford.

He started 1983/84 with Western League outfit Barnstaple before leaving the club due to work commitments.

In January 1984 Derek signed for Stoke Gabriel of the South Devon League and on 28.4.84 he scored from the penalty spot in a 6-0 win over Windsor United.

He joined Newquay of the South Western League for 1984/85 and spent three seasons there before leaving the club at the end of 1986/87.

In November 1987 he signed for South Devon League club Bovey Tracey and spent the remainder of 1987/88 there.

During 1988/89 Derek was player-assistant manager of South Western League club Torrington and in December 1988 the Kent Messenger newspaper ran an article about his longevity as a footballer. He was 42 at the time and said I m still enjoying my football as much as I ever did. If I didn t enjoy it, I wouldn t be playing on.

In April 1989 Derek made a one-off appearance for Exeter City s A team in a Devon and Exeter League game against Chelston.

He later had a spell with Teignmouth of the South Devon League that included the 1990/91 and 1991/92 campaigns.

During 1994/95 he was playing for Galmpton United - another South Devon League club.

Derek s son Ross, also a goalkeeper, made two Football League appearances for Exeter during the 1994/95 season and during the 1997/98 campaign he was with Ilfracombe. In November 1997 Ross was injured immediately prior to a Western League game at Pewsey Vale and as a result Derek took his place, just a few weeks before his 51st birthday. Ross later played for other clubs including Newton Abbot Spurs where he eventually became manager and chairman.

By 2014 Derek had been the owner of Kingfisher Print & Design for well over 25 years and the company had a multi-million pound turnover. It was based in Totnes, Devon and Derek s son Ross was Managing Director.

Derek s grandson Jack - son of Ross - became a scholar / trainee with Exeter in 2025.

Derek died aged 79 on 10.3.26 after a short battle with cancer.

name: Peter Benevides
other clubs: Rhode Island Stingrays (USA)
bio:
Hard-working 5' 10" tall American player who was born in Newport, Rhode Island in the state of New England. Peter attended Mount Hope High School in Bristol, Rhode Island and captained the school's football team, winning numerous representative honours.

In 1998 Peter started a course at the University Of Rhode Island and enjoyed great personal success playing for their football team - the Rhode Island Stingrays - in the seven seasons up to and including 2004. Throughout that time he was also part of the Olympic Development Program - a scheme intended to eventually provide players for the USA's national team.

Rhode Island played in the Atlantic 10 Conference and later the Premier Development League and Peter was a fixture in their side throughout his time at the university with the exception of the 1999 campaign which he missed due to injury. He was chosen for the honorary All-New England select side for the 2002 season after scoring nine goals during the campaign and had trials to play in America's A-League.

Having earned both Bachelor's and Master's degrees in accounting Peter moved to England in the summer of 2004 along with his Rhode Island football team-mate Ross Smith. Peter joined Margate on trial and the Thanet Times said he was "particularly impressive" in a 3-1 defeat at Ramsgate in a friendly played on 25.7.04. Peter then scored twice in a 3-1 friendly win over Erith & Belvedere at Welling on 7.8.04 and Margate manager Chris Kinnear decided to sign him for the 2004/05 campaign.

Peter missed the first Conference South match of the season as his international clearance hadn't come through so made his debut in midfield as Margate won 1-0 at Carshalton on 16.8.04. He kept his place for a trip to Dorchester on 21.8.04 but the Thanet Times said his "talents on the ball were little help against a physical home side who managed to force him off the ball too easily" as Margate lost 2-0. Peter then played in a 6-0 defeat against Grays at Margate's adopted home in Ashford on 24.8.04 before being left out of the side for the next two matches.

He returned to the team for a game against Hayes at Ashford on 4.9.04 and Peter scored his first goal for Margate in a 3-1 win. He wore the number two shirt in that match and then lined up in the number three jersey for a 1-0 defeat against Weymouth at Ashford on 11.9.04 as Peter started a spell where he sometimes played as a wing-back. On 14.9.04 he was sent off for handball as Margate were thrashed 7-3 at Lewes. Peter punched a goal-bound effort away but there was a dispute about whether or not the shot had already crossed the line when he intervened. The referee decided that it hadn't, dismissed Peter and awarded a penalty.

After coming on as a sub in a 4-2 win at Maidenhead on 18.9.04 Peter was back in the starting line-up for a game against Thurrock at Ashford on 21.9.04 and his strike after 72 minutes was enough to give Margate a 2-1 win. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said it was "fitting" that Peter got the winner as he was "outstanding despite playing in the unfamiliar role of left wing-back". It was an excellent solo goal as he picked the ball up in midfield, charged down the left and cut inside two defenders before slotting home. Peter played once more before serving a one match ban and in his first outing after his suspension he scored with another solo effort as Margate drew 1-1 with Newport at Ashford on 9.10.04.

For the next two months Peter often had to play as a wing-back on either the right or left-hand flank due to Margate's lack of players and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he was "a particular threat on the right-hand side" in a 2-0 win at Welling in the Conference Cup on 2.11.04. The Thanet Times felt Peter "was a threat when linking up with the attack" from his wing-back position in a 1-0 defeat against Hornchurch at Ashford on 4.12.04 and as 2004 came to an end he enjoyed a spell in his favoured midfield role.

After a run of 16 matches wearing the number eight shirt and mostly playing in midfield Peter reverted to a right wing-back role as Margate lost 2-0 to Cambridge City at Ashford on 28.3.05. He then played at either right or left wing-back in seven of the final eight games of the season as Margate were relegated from the Conference South. Peter's last outing was on 2.5.05 when he was part of the side that beat Dover 2-1 at Folkestone to win the Kent Senior Cup and in all he played 46 times (once as sub) and scored three goals. After the 2004/05 campaign ended Peter returned to the USA.

By 2012 he was Director of Finance and Marketing Planning at Sony Music Entertainment and Peter was living in New York at that time.

name: Ty Benjamin
other clubs: Colchester United (0), Rushden & Diamonds (0), Southend United (0), Chelmsford City, Great Wakering Rovers and Southend Manor
bio:
Gritty midfielder born in Southend who played for Southend-based Regis Boys during his schooldays. Ty then had a spell at Colchester where he played in the youth and reserve teams.

He later had short stints with Rushden & Diamonds and Southend United before joining Chelmsford as part of their PASE scheme that combined football with college study for young players.

During his time with Chelmsford Ty played for the reserves and was also an unused substitute for the first team when they took on Nuneaton in an FA Cup tie.

In December 2007 he joined Great Wakering who were managed by former Margate star Iain O Connell and Ty initially played in the Essex club s reserves before moving to Southend Manor on a dual-registration basis in February 2008.

He made his debut for the Essex Senior League club in a 3-0 home defeat at the hands of Eton Manor on 23.2.08 and stayed with them until April 2008, making nine appearances without scoring.

Ty returned to Great Wakering in time to feature in their last two matches of the 2007/08 season - his first senior outings for the club. He then played more regularly during 2008/09 and 2009/10 but Ty had injury problems which restricted his appearances to 46 in total. He scored five goals for Great Wakering in that time.

In March 2010 Ty joined Margate shortly after Iain O Connell had taken over as the club s manager and at that time he was working as a full-time football coach. He made his debut in midfield in a 1-1 draw with Carshalton in an Isthmian League Premier Division game played at Hartsdown Park on 20.3.10 and the Thanet Times said he certainly had a go". Ty also featured in Margate s next match - a 1-0 win at Dartford on 23.3.10 - but picked up a toe injury after that and drifted away from the club without playing again. In April 2010 Iain O Connell told the Isle of Thanet Gazette It s a bit sad, he s had his chance and he s not taken it. He did really well in the games he played but he hasn t rung me."

At the end of May 2010 Iain O Connell announced he d re-signed Ty for the 2010/11 campaign and told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "He's a nightmare ! He's had issues with his social life, too much boozing, but I'm hoping he sorts himself out. He captained Colchester s youth team and reserves and had a very good future but he lost his way a little bit. He s one of those you can t trust not to go out boozing on a Friday night ! I hope I can knock that out of him."

In the summer of 2010 it turned out that Ty hadn t rejoined Margate after all and he started 2010/11 back with Great Wakering but he only made five Isthmian League Division 1 North appearances for them (one as sub) during the season, scoring once. He then played for the club throughout the 2012/13 campaign.

name: Dave Bennett
other clubs: Sheffield United (0), Luton Town (0), Gillingham (0), Ramsgate, Canterbury City, Herne Bay and Whitstable Town
bio:
Ramsgate-born player who attended Holy Cross School in Broadstairs and had spells on the books of Sheffield United and Luton as a youngster before moving on to Gillingham. Dave featured in the Gills youth team before being released by the club.

After a spell in Thanet amateur football, Dave was signed by Ramsgate in November 1977 and made his first team debut in a 1-0 defeat at Ashford in the Kent Senior Cup on 15.11.77. He went on to win the Rams Young Player of the Year award for the 1977/78 season.

In the summer of 1978 he joined Margate and Dave played a few reserve team games before moving on to Canterbury shortly before the end of 1978.

He scored twice on his debut for City and went on to make 18 Southern League appearances during 1978/79, scoring four goals in the process.

In March 1979 Dave returned to Thanet and rejoined Ramsgate. He also started the 1979/80 season with the Rams.

In September 1979 Dave returned to Margate and made his first team debut in a 2-0 defeat at Dorchester on 8.9.79. He played in midfield but later featured as a striker on a few occasions as he went on to make a total of 15 appearances, four of them as a substitute. On 13.11.79 Dave was sent off in a Kent Senior Cup tie against Ramsgate after clashing with Alan Draper.

In December 1979 Dave went back to Ramsgate and went on to spend several seasons there before linking up with Herne Bay for 1984/85.

In the summer of 1985 Dave returned to Hartsdown Park for the third time and became a regular in Thanet United's reserves during the 1985/86 campaign. He also made four first team appearances, two of them as a substitute. Dave's first senior start came in a 2-1 defeat at Chatham on 8.10.85 and he also played in midfield during a 2-1 win over Canterbury at Hartsdown Park on 22.10.85. Dave made his final senior appearance on 26.11.85 when he came on as sub during an Eastern Floodlight Cup tie against Sittingbourne at Hartsdown Park on 26.11.85. His cross from the left wing led to a debut goal for Clive Yeo. Dave then returned to the reserves for the rest of the season before leaving the club in the summer of 1986.

He went on to have two spells with Whitstable, the first including the 1987/88 and 1988/89 seasons and the second one starting during the 1989/90 campaign. In the period between his stints with the Oystermen Dave had been forced to give up football for some time due to a serious knee injury.

He later returned to Ramsgate once more and appeared for the Rams during the 1991/92, 1992/93 and 1993/94 seasons. In August 1993 Dave was sent off in a home game against Chatham.

In 2013 he was a company director and living in West Molesey, Surrey.

name: Ron Bennett
other clubs: Wolverhampton Wanderers (0), Portsmouth (8,1), Crystal Palace (27,5), Brighton & Hove Albion (3,0), Tonbridge, Folkestone Town, Chatham Town, Ashford Town, Deal Town and Hastings United
bio:
Much-travelled left winger born in Hinckley who began his senior career with 1st Division giants Wolves, joining them in January 1945. Ron made one first team appearance during the 1944/45 wartime season aged 17 and then spent the remainder of his time at Molineux in Wolves junior sides. He only made nine reserve team appearances, scoring once, before being released at the end of the 1947/48 campaign.

In July 1948 Ron was signed by Portsmouth and made eight senior appearances for Pompey during the 1949/50, 1950/51 and 1951/52 seasons, all of them in the 1st Division.

In January 1952 Ron was transferred to 3rd Division South club Crystal Palace and he went on to make 27 first team appearances for the Eagles during 1951/52 and 1952/53.

He was on the move again in July 1953, this time joining Brighton.

In the summer of 1954 Ron dropped into non-league football to join Tonbridge. He went on to make 93 appearances for the Angels and scored 22 goals during 1954/55 and 1955/56. His goal tally included the only goal of the game in an FA Cup replay at Margate on 14.10.54.

Ron signed for Margate in the summer of 1956 and made his debut in a 4-1 win over Whitstable in the Kent League at Hartsdown Park on 18.8.56. It was the opening day of the 1956/57 campaign. He went on to enjoy an excellent first season with the club, scoring 16 goals in 38 appearances, and proved himself to be a skilful wingman who was full of tricks. On 17.11.56 Ron scored as Margate beat Dunstable 3-1 at Hartsdown Park in the FA Cup 1st Round.

During the 1957/58 season he missed only a handful of matches and made 43 appearances. On 16.11.57 Ron played as Margate lost 3-2 to visitors Crystal Palace in the FA Cup 1st Round. He scored 11 goals during the campaign and two of them came from direct free-kicks - Ron was something of a dead ball specialist. He was also known for his powerful shooting and in a game at Snowdown on 11.1.58 managed a strike so powerful that it created a crack in the crossbar and rebounded all the way back to the halfway line. Snowdown had to purchase a new set of goal posts as a result.

With the arrival of Ken Tucker at Hartsdown Park, Ron found himself in the reserves at the start of the 1958/59 season but he got back into the first team when the former West Ham man was injured. Ron played four times during the first two months of the campaign and scored once, in a 2-1 Kent League Cup win over Ramsgate at Hartsdown on 4.9.58. However it proved to be his last goal for the club as in October 1958 Ron signed for Folkestone. A big factor in his departure was the fact that he'd recently been constantly barracked by Margate supporters, unfairly in the opinion of the local press.

In later years Ron went on to play for Chatham and Ashford and then spent the 1960/61 season with Deal.

He joined Hastings for the 1961/62 season and on 9.9.61 Ron was in their reserve side that lost 2-0 at Margate in a Seanglian Cup tie. The Thanet Times said that he tried hard to get the Hastings front line in motion, but his was a futile task. His ball control was as immaculate as ever, but with scant support he could work no miracles on his own. On 24.3.62 Ron scored the Hastings goal as they lost 2-1 at home to Margate Reserves.

After retiring, Ron settled in Tonbridge and was living and working there in 1975.

He died in 1997.

name: Ted Bensley
