name: Mark Brewer
other clubs: Tottenham Hotspur (0), Maidstone United (0), Heybridge Swifts, Enfield, Braintree Town, Billericay Town, Harlow Town, Staines Town and Cheshunt
bio:
Tenacious player who had a spell with Tottenham Hotspur as a schoolboy before moving to Maidstone for the 1989/90 season. Mark captained the Stones' youth team and also played for the senior side in the Kent Senior Cup Final against Gillingham in 1990.

In the summer of 1991 Mark signed for Margate aged 18 and made his debut on 17.8.91 as Margate went down 2-1 to Burnham at Hartsdown Park on the opening day of the 1991/92 campaign. He then played regularly for the rest of the season, usually in midfield but occasionally as a full-back. On 3.9.91 Mark scored his first goal in a 1-1 draw at Sittingbourne and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that he was "industrious". On 8.2.92 he was sent off for fighting in a 1-1 draw with Buckingham at Hartsdown and had to serve a three match ban. After missing five games through injury in April 1992 Mark returned to action at the end of the month and featured in the last two matches of 1991/92. On 5.5.92 he came on as a substitute as Margate lost 3-1 at home to Ramsgate in the annual Isle of Thanet Gazette Cup game and it turned out to be Mark's last appearance. He was released from his contract at the end of the season so that he could go and play in Hong Kong. Mark had made a total of 44 appearances (three as sub) and scored three goals for Margate.

After returning to the UK Mark joined Heybridge Swifts during 1992/93 and then started the 1993/94 campaign with Enfield.

In January 1994 he moved on to Braintree and Mark stayed there until early 1995.

His next move took him to Billericay and Mark made 18 appearances (two as sub) there before the end of 1994/95 and another 35 appearances (two as sub) during 1995/96. He spent around four years with Billericay before leaving the club to link up with Harlow towards the end of 1998.

He made 24 league appearances (ten as sub) and scored once for Harlow during 1998/99 and also played once for Staines during the season.

In the summer of 1999 Mark signed for Cheshunt and spent several years there. Injuries blighted the latter part of his time with the club and Mark missed the whole of 2002/03 and only played twice in 2003/04 before leaving Cheshunt during that season.

Having battled back to full fitness Mark returned to Cheshunt for the start of the 2004/05 campaign and took his total appearances for the club past the 100 mark before joining Enfield for a second spell in December 2004.

Mark made 12 Isthmian League appearances for Enfield before the end of the 2004/05 season and then retired.

name: Jeff Bridge
other clubs: Rochdale (0), Radcliffe Borough, Bromley, Gravesend & Northfleet, Adelaide Lion (Australia), Noarlunga United (Australia), Birkalla Rovers (Australia), Mitcham United (Australia) and Flinders University (Australia)
bio:
Defender born in Ashton-under-Lyne, Greater Manchester who started his career with 4th Division club Rochdale. Jeff joined the club in 1956 as a 16 year-old and played in the Dale's reserves for three years up to the end of the 1959/60 campaign.

In the summer of 1960 he joined Lancashire League outfit Radcliffe Borough and Jeff spent two seasons there before moving south to start a course at the University of London in 1962.

He played for the University's football team and after completing his studies Jeff signed for Isthmian League club Bromley in 1964.

He was in the Bromley side that lost 3-0 to Margate in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 24.2.65 and Jeff was still a Bromley player when he joined Margate on trial in December 1967 aged 27. Jeff made his debut at right-back in a 3-2 win over Erith & Belvedere in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 4.12.67 but it was his only first team appearance and he then returned to Hayes Lane.

In the summer of 1968 Jeff guested for Margate during a pre-season tour of West Germany.

At some point around 1970 he featured in several midweek matches for Gravesend & Northfleet under an assumed name but Jeff continued playing for Bromley in between and stayed with the club until 1972. He was a woodwork teacher at a school in Eltham, London for most of the eight years he was at Hayes Lane.

After leaving Bromley Jeff spent a couple of years playing for an amateur club called Catford Strollers and in 1974 he emigrated to Australia.

After arriving in Australia, he signed for Adelaide Lion who played in the South Australian Amateur Soccer League and were part of the Ukrainian Sports Club Lion organisation. Jeff spent two years there.

In 1976 he joined Adelaide-based Noarlunga of the South Australia 2nd Division and Jeff spent a season with the club before linking up with Birkalla in 1977.

Birkalla also played in the South Australia 2nd Division and were based in Adelaide. Jeff spent two years with them up to 1979 but then moved on to Mitcham.

He became the Victorian District League Division 2 club's player-coach and Jeff celebrated his 40th birthday in 1980 during his spell with Mitcham.

In 1982 he linked up with Flinders University of the South Australian Metropolitan League as player-coach and Jeff finished his career there in 1984.

He then moved away from Adelaide to take up a teaching appointment in a rural area - 'The bush' as it's called in Australia.

In 2012 Jeff was living in Stirling, South Australia and had retired from teaching.

name: Arthur Bridger
other clubs: Deal Town, Sittingbourne and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
Talented midfielder born in Blaydon, County Durham who relocated to London with his family aged ten and played for the City of Westminster boys team.

Arthur moved to Margate with his family as a teenager and joined Cliftonville in the Thanet League. At that time he worked for a local engineering firm but when he was 16 Arthur joined the Merchant Navy and spent two years travelling all round the world. He left the service in 1958 and returned to London to work as a porter at Paddington Station.

In January 1960 Arthur returned to the Thanet area and found work as an interior decorator. He signed for Margate and made his debut for the reserves in a 9-1 home win over Folkestone on 9.1.60. Arthur then played exclusively for the reserves up to the end of the 1959/60 season.

Arthur broke into the first team during the 1960/61 season, making his senior debut on 29.9.60 in a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Rugby in the Southern League. He went on to make a total of 11 appearances and impressed with his distribution and solid tackling. A Margate supporter's letter to the Isle of Thanet Gazette described him as "the best local find Margate has had for years". Arthur also played 31 reserve team games during the season and scored four goals for them.

In the summer of 1961, Arthur had his bicycle stolen from outside Hartsdown Park when he left it there whilst training and during the 1961/62 season he made a further 13 first team appearances and more than twice that amount for the reserves. Arthur scored once for the senior side during the campaign - in a 4-1 win over Burton at Hartsdown Park on 23.4.62 - and on 12.5.62 he played as Margate beat visitors Folkestone 4-0 to win the Kent Senior Shield. Arthur s performances towards the end of the season were described as "very encouraging" by the local press and his hard work was a particular feature of his game.

The 1962/63 season turned out to be Arthur's last at Margate and he only played seven times for the first team during the campaign, despite often impressing. He spent the majority of the season in the reserves and made a further 29 appearances for them, scoring four times. On 13.3.63 Arthur played 85 minutes in goal for the reserves after John Prodger was injured. In the summer of 1963 he was released and joined Deal.

Arthur then moved to Sittingbourne where he spent three seasons (1964/65-1966/67) and he scored against Margate in a 5-5 draw on 19.11.66. He then joined Ramsgate and spent the 1967/68 season there before retiring.

Arthur was still living locally in 2002.

name: Simon Briggs
bio:
Versatile Hammersmith-born player who spent his early years in Nottingham before moving to Margate with his parents in 1970. Simon first featured in junior football in the Thanet area during the 1976/77 season.

He was playing locally for Westcliff in the Thanet League and Lloyds Bank in the Thanet Works League when Thanet United's reserve team manager Peter Donnelly asked him to join the club for the 1981/82 campaign. Simon played exclusively for the reserves during the season and scored 15 goals for them. He also turned out for Sunday side Margate Athletic along with many other Thanet players.

Simon stayed with United for the 1982/83 campaign and made his first team debut in a Southern League game at Salisbury on 20.11.82. Although Thanet lost 6-1 Simon had the distinction of scoring the side's consolation goal. Thanet's manager Terry Morris resigned in the wake of the defeat. Simon went on to make 13 appearances (one as sub) during the remainder of the 1982/83 season and scored once more - in a 3-0 win at Andover on 18.12.82. He usually played as a striker but also featured in midfield and at right-back. Simon was described as being "tenacious" by the local press and was praised for his "strong front running" during a 5-0 defeat at Hillingdon on 1.1.83.

Simon stayed with United for the 1983/84 season but spent the entire campaign in the reserves before dropping back into local football.

In 1988 he left the Thanet area and moved to Heathfield in East Sussex. Simon carried on playing Saturday / Sunday football in local leagues there until retiring in 1995.

He was a prominent local cricketer in the Thanet area and after moving to East Sussex Simon carried on his cricket career with Heathfield Park. He also played for Sussex County Cricket Club's Over 50's side in the National Championship during the late 2000's.

In 2011 Simon was still living in Heathfield and his cricket career was still going strong. At that time he was in charge of a Crawley-based branch of the Swedish bank Handelsbanken and had worked in the banking industry for over 35 years by then.

Simon's sister was once married to Thanet United player Clive Haywood.

name: Richard Brinkworth
other clubs: Swindon Town (0), Gloucester City, Cheltenham Town and Fairford Town
bio:
Welsh midfielder who started his career with Swindon and played in their reserves during the 1975/76 season alongside his brother Trevor.

On his 18th birthday - 11.1.77 - Richard signed professional forms for Swindon but he was released at the end of the 1977/78 campaign.

In the summer of 1978 he joined Margate and made his debut in a Southern League Cup tie against Dartford at Hartsdown Park on 21.8.78. It turned out to be Richard's only appearance. He left the club soon afterwards and joined Gloucester.

Richard then moved to Cheltenham and made 19 appearances for them during the 1979/80 and 1980/81 seasons, scoring once.

He left Cheltenham to join Fairford Town.

Richard's brother Trevor played in the Southern League for Dorchester during the time that he was with Margate.

In 2007 Richard was living in Oxfordshire.

name: Jimmy Briscoe
other clubs: Sheffield Wednesday (5,3), Raith Rovers (Scotland) (0), Gainsborough Trinity and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
6' 0" tall, hard-working, burly centre-forward born in Swinton who started his career with Sheffield Wednesday and progressed through their junior ranks to the first team.

Before making his senior bow for Wednesday, Jimmy made wartime guest appearances for clubs including Raith Rovers and in October 1944 he scored a hat-trick for them in a 4-1 home win over Glasgow Rangers. That reputedly made Jimmy the first Englishman ever to have scored a treble against Rangers. He also turned out for various armed forces sides during the war and in 1946 Jimmy played for the Royal Navy against the Dutch national team at Ajax's stadium.

He finally made his first team debut for Sheffield Wednesday in a 2nd Division game at Manchester City on 12.10.46 and scored the Owls' goal in a 2-1 defeat watched by 36,413. Jimmy made four further senior appearances, the last of them in a 4-1 defeat at Plymouth on 4.1.47, and scored twice more before leaving the club at the end of the 1946/47 season.

In the summer of 1947, Jimmy was signed by Midland League club Gainsborough Trinity and he spent the first half of 1947/48 with them before his contract was cancelled by mutual consent in January 1948.

Jimmy then moved to Kent and found work as a miner at Betteshanger Colliery. In March 1948 he joined Ramsgate on trial and scored a hat-trick in his first outing for the club - a 6-0 win over 47th Coast Regiment in a friendly at Southwood on 13.3.48.

Jimmy went on to become a prolific marksman for the Rams and during the 1949/50 campaign he scored a remarkable 47 goals. His tally included two in matches against Margate - one in a 2-1 win at Hartsdown Park on 26.11.49 and the other in a 2-0 home win on 8.4.50. Jimmy also scored five times in a 6-1 win at Aylesford Paper Mills in the Kent League on 4.3.50. He played in every match the Rams took part in during the season, be it league, cup or friendly and Ramsgate won the Kent League title.

Jimmy spent three more seasons with the Rams and on 16.4.53 he scored twice in a 5-2 win at Margate.

Having been released by Ramsgate, Jimmy crossed Thanet to join Margate In June 1953 and made his debut in a 3-0 defeat at the hands of Dover at Hartsdown Park on 22.8.53. It was the opening day of the 1953/54 campaign. He went on to score six times in 13 first team appearances during the season but spent a lot of time in the reserves, finding the net 21 times for them. His second string tally included four goals in an 8-0 home win over Sheppey on 24.10.53 and an amazing six in an 11-0 home win over Beckenham on 9.1.54. Five of Jimmy s goals that day were scored with his head and he later said that Margate s manager Almer Hall asked him after the game "has thou got a problem with thee feet ?"

Jimmy stayed with the club for the 1954/55 season too but played exclusively for the reserves, scoring 34 times for them. His goal tally included four in a 6-1 home win over Betteshanger on 18.9.54 and five in a 7-0 win over visitors Deal on 13.11.54. Jimmy finished the campaign as top scorer but never got a chance in the first team.

He began the 1955/56 season in the reserves once more but with no sign of a first team opportunity on the horizon, Jimmy left the club before the end of 1955. He returned to make a one-off appearance for the reserves as they drew 1-1 with visitors Herne Bay on 21.1.56 but then retired from football aged 32.

Jimmy turned to cricket after his football career ended and in the summer of 1957 he turned out for Southwood Taverners. On 25.8.57 Jimmy took 5 for 12 in a game against Deal-based Petbows.

Jimmy continued to work as a miner and during January 1959 he suffered facial injuries in a pit explosion at Betteshanger.

During the early 1960's Jimmy returned to Ramsgate and became a member of the club's General Committee. In 1967 he left the Rams to become Commercial Manager at Stevenage Town but the club went bust at the end of 1967/68.

Jimmy then established a new club in the town - Stevenage Athletic - for the 1968/69 season and managed them until leaving the club in October 1970 to pursue interests outside of football.

When Stevenage Athletic went out of business in 1975 Jimmy was instrumental in forming Stevenage Borough who would eventually reach the Football League in 2010.

During the 2000/01 campaign Jimmy was President of Stevenage's Supporters Association and also helped out with matchday hospitality. His son Lloyd was also working behind the scenes at the club. When Margate played Borough in an FA Trophy tie on 3.2.01 Jimmy was interviewed for the matchday programme and remembered the local derbies between Ramsgate and Margate that he played in. "Having played with both sides, the build up to the derby game was exactly the same - it was one we must NEVER lose" he recalled. Jimmy added "both managers, Almer Hall and Jim Blair, would end up nervous wrecks !"

Jimmy also claimed that Margate once 'lost' a player during a home game with Dover. He told the interviewer "halfway through the second half Eric Worthington turned to me and said 'Jim, we've only got ten men on the field !' unbeknown to the rest of us, Almer Hall had taken Tommy Bing off and sold him to Spurs whilst we were playing the game !"

Another memory Jimmy shared related to a game where teams representing the towns of Margate and Ramsgate played on the Goodwin Sands - "there were ships passing by on either side of the pitch, which was between a couple of ship-wrecks" he recalled. Jimmy added "what we didn't realise though was that the timing was all wrong, the tide came in and we had to abandon the game at half-time !"

In his closing thoughts, Jimmy was quoted as saying "in my ten years with both clubs we played hard and fair but I cannot remember anyone being sent off. I must admit though, that if my generation had been playing today we would all be sent off within five minutes with those hard toe-caps !"

At the start of the 2006/07 season Jimmy was still busy with his dual role at Stevenage but sadly suffered a stroke in November 2006. However he made a welcome return to Broadhall Way in April 2007 when he watched Stevenage draw with Morecambe. At the time he was still in hospital and in May 2007 Jimmy was present at the new Wembley as Stevenage won the FA Trophy. Manager Mark Stimson told the club's website that his personal highlight of the day was Jimmy joining in with the celebrations down on the pitch. He said "Jim is the heart and soul of the football club and when he talks to you he makes a lot of sense and I enjoy listening to him."

Jimmy was still president of Stevenage's Supporters Association during the 2010/11 season and in 2011 he was living in a care home near Letchworth, Hertfordshire. His son Lloyd still took him to all Stevenage's home matches and Lloyd's godfather was Jimmy's old Margate team-mate Brian Moffatt.

Jimmy died on 27.8.14 at the age of 90 and his passing prompted a plethora of tributes to him for his lifelong service to football.

Stevenage Supporters Association issued a statement saying We are deeply saddened by the passing of Stevenage FC Supporters Association president, Jim Briscoe, who will be sorely missed by so many associated with the football club. Jim was passionate about Stevenage Football Club, was involved with football at Broadhall Way for almost 46 years and was a life member of the club. Most notably, he was a key member of the A Team - a group of enthusiasts who became the founding fathers of Stevenage Football Club. We wish to pass our deepest condolences to Jim s family and many, many friends.

Stevenage chairman Phil Wallace said Jim was a source of guidance and inspiration to me when I came to Stevenage 15 years ago, along with other members of the A Team that are sadly no longer with us. I never had anything but total support from Jim in our progress to the Football League. He wanted to see Stevenage FC in the Football League so badly that I felt I wanted to see that for Jim as much as myself. His dream drove me on and it was a real moment for me when promotion was secured. He was the first person I thought about when that whistle blew at Kidderminster. I valued the time I spent with him and his pals talking about the past and I valued the chats we had about football. Bringing Jim into the Boardroom to act as the club s ambassador was one of my proudest moments - he was a great character and helped change the way we were viewed by other clubs. I know he cherished that involvement and loved every minute he spent at the Club. I ve mentioned Jim s pals from the past a couple of times and I know he would want me to reinforce the fact that a lot of people did a lot of great work to get the Club where it is now - that was the type of person he was. He was the sole surviving member of the original A Team and those guys will never be forgotten. Our thoughts go out to Jim and his family and I personally look back with fond memories of many a laugh and joke with him. We will have a minute s silence on Tuesday night against Gillingham and a few of us will have a tear in our eye at the passing of a truly wonderful man.

Stevenage manager Graham Westley said It's a very sad day for a club like ours when we lose such a great supporter and such a great man. Jim was part of the infantry; he put one foot in-front of the other to get the Club to where it is. He loved his football and he was just a lovely guy. When I was here the first time he was at the ground every day and he didn t care if he was washing the cups up or cutting the grass - Jim would do anything. He was a special guy, he had a long history of football and he absolutely adored the game. He gave his heart and soul to this football club and I m sure everybody will be devastated.

Ramsgate s website described Jimmy as being A real gent who did a great many things for Ramsgate whether he was wearing his boots or not in his 20 years in the town, and who no doubt did as much if not more in the following 46 years in Stevenage.

name: Chic Brodie
other clubs: Partick Avondale (Scotland), Manchester City (0), Gillingham (22,0), Aldershot (106,0), Wolverhampton Wanderers (1,0), Northampton Town (97,0), Brentford (224,0), Wealdstone and Twickenham Villa
bio:
6' 0" tall goalkeeper born in Duntocher, Scotland who played for Scotland s schoolboy side aged 15. Chic was in the team that lost 1-0 to England - captained by Duncan Edwards - at Wembley on 5.4.52.

He began his senior career with Scottish junior club Partick Avondale and then joined Manchester City as a part-time player in June 1953. However he didn't make the first team at Maine Road and in July 1957 Chic moved on to Gillingham having been given a free transfer.

He made 22 appearances for the Gills during the 1957/58 season and was then transferred to Aldershot in the summer of 1958. Chic was undertaking his National Service at the time and was stationed at Aldershot. Chic went on to make over 100 senior appearances for the Shots, spanning the 1958/59-1960/61 seasons, before joining Wolves in February 1961.

In September 1961 he moved on again, having played just one 1st Division game for Wolves, and linked up with Northampton.

Chic's first game for the Cobblers completed an unusual run of three consecutive games where he played in the Football League for three different clubs in three different divisions. His last game for Aldershot was in Division 4, his only one for Wolves was in Division 1 and Northampton were in Division 3. Chic went on to become a first team regular for Northampton for just over two years.

On 20.11.63 Chic signed for Brentford for a fee of around 5,000 and on the same day the Bees played in an FA Cup replay at Margate but he wasn t in the squad. Chic went on to make over 200 first team appearances for Brentford before his professional career ended in bizarre fashion on 28.11.70 as Brentford visited Colchester in a 3rd Division match. Chic collided with a sheepdog that had run onto the pitch and was stretchered off having severely injured his knee and never played for Brentford again. Chic was later quoted as saying "the dog might have been a small one, but it just happened to be a solid one." The incident was captured on film by television cameras and became part of football folklore.

Around the time of the dog incident, the Evening Standard interviewed Chic, whose full name was Charles Thomas George Brodie, and he provided some interesting insights into his life and career. He told the reporter "All the other players call me Charlie but I don't like it. It puts me in mind of a big Irish navvy" and recalling his spell at Manchester City Chic said "I never managed to get into the first team. Whether I wasn't good enough I don't know, but they had Bert Trautmann then, who was such a personality and a great goalkeeper."

Chic also described his numerous superstitious rituals "I've always got to carry a ball out and I always carry my cap and gloves in the same hand. Then, as I go out of the dressing room into the tunnel, I always like to touch a piece of wood. I have to go out second, right after the captain. I'd knock the other players out of the way if they tried to get in front of me. It would upset me a bit if I didn't do these things, so I suppose I am a wee bit superstitious !"

The article concluded with some details of Chic's part-time job as a London taxi driver and he mentioned a collision he'd been involved in with a white Jaguar. Chic jumped out of his taxi and so did the Jaguar driver who turned out to be Geoff Hurst. "It was such a coincidence really, two footballers colliding, that he treated it as a joke and we had a good laugh together" Chic recalled.

By the summer of 1971, Chic had recovered sufficient fitness to play part-time football and in July 1971 he joined Margate. Player-manager Gerry Baker - who d been at Manchester City with Chic - told the Kentish Express He s the best goalkeeper I ever played with, and that includes Bert Trautman and Ronnie Simpson. An experienced goalkeeper is essential to a side that intends to play youngsters. While I was in Scotland I spoke to Jock Stein and he told me that the first thing he did on taking the Celtic manager s job was to sign a first-class keeper. In his case it was 36 year-old Ronnie Simpson.

Chic made his debut as Margate beat Telford 3-1 at Hartsdown Park on 14.8.71, the opening day of the 1971/72 season. His class and bravery became immediately apparent and the Thanet Times said that Chic "heartened all and sundry with his penalty box command and general poise". It was felt that Margate had finally found the solution to the goalkeeping problem that had hampered the club since the release of Brian Hughes at the end of the 1967/68 campaign. A kidney infection kept Chic out for around a month early in the season but he returned to put in some impressive performances, although he was also unfortunate enough to be in goal as Bournemouth & Boscombe famously beat Margate 11-0 in an FA Cup 1st Round tie on 20.11.71. Chic's display in an FA Trophy tie at Folkestone on 4.12.71 was described as "brilliant" by the local press and in the replay four days later he again pulled off some superb saves in a display the paper called "magnificent". However Chic's season came to a premature end when he suffered a hairline fracture of his ankle during a game at Romford on 26.2.72. He'd made 35 appearances before the injury ruled him out of the club's remaining games.

During the 1972/73 season Chic played in 56 of Margate's 64 matches and again impressed with what the local paper called his "general expertise". On 18.11.72 he was in the side that beat Swansea 1-0 in an FA Cup 1st Round tie at Hartsdown Park and on 2.12.72 Chic was carried off shortly before the end of a 3-2 win at Guildford having been kicked in the face. He recovered in time to play in Margate s 1-0 win at Walton & Hersham in the FA Cup 2nd Round on 9.12.72 and Chic then played in perhaps the club s biggest ever match - a 6-0 defeat against Tottenham at Hartsdown Park in the 3rd Round on 13.1.73.

Shortly before the Spurs tie, he was interviewed by John Sadler for The Sun and the article described Chic as "a walking mishap, a one-man casualty station, a multiple accident statistic". He was even five hours late for the interview because he'd been in hospital. As well as the infamous dog incident, Chic also mentioned two other memorable occurrences to Sadler. Playing against Millwall for Brentford on 6.11.65 a hand grenade was thrown into his goalmouth, luckily it turned out to be a fake. "I bloody scarpered" Chic told Sadler. Chic also recalled how the entire goal collapsed around him in a game at Lincoln and the feature was headlined "Unlucky Chic - The One-Man Natural Disaster".

Chic s best performance of the 1972/73 season came during a 4-0 defeat at home to Kettering on 12.2.73, he saved Margate from complete humiliation with a display described as "brilliant" by the Isle of Thanet Gazette and the paper said that he pulled off "a string of immaculate saves". At the end of the 1972/73 campaign, Chic was transfer-listed and in the summer of 1973 he left the club and joined Wealdstone for a small fee.

In the summer of 1974, Chic moved on to Maidstone but after playing in their pre-season friendlies he left the club without making a competitive appearance and retired from senior football.

Later in the 1974/75 season, Chic played for London-based Sunday League club Christon United and in March 1975 he was interviewed by the Acton Gazette. He told the paper that he was enjoying his football and said You see, there s no pressure on you. In the pro game you re worrying all the time about your place in the side, and you know that week after week you ve got to be at your very best. I was considering making a career for myself as a coach when my playing days were over, but I decided that it wasn t for me. The pro game is such a rat race.

Chic also looked back on his time at Manchester City and said I got into City s Central League side, and they wanted me to sign professional forms, but my father decided that I should have a trade behind me in case it didn t work out. So I completed my apprenticeship as an electrical engineer. That was a mistake. If I d signed as a full-time professional with them, the coaching and help I would have got from City s first team keeper - Bert Trautmann - would have proved invaluable.

Recalling his spell with Wolves, Chic said I just couldn t get on with their manager Stan Cullis. I was only there for seven months when I told him that I wanted away.

Chic also referred to his time with Margate and said The travelling I had to do was a killer. Twice a week sometimes from London to Margate. What with that in the evening and holding down a full time job as a taxi driver during the day as well, I was beginning to feel it. So I moved to another Southern League club a bit nearer home - Wealdstone.

The newspaper article also mentioned that Chic s 16 year-old son Gary played as a goalkeeper and had had a spell playing for Brentford s junior side.

Chic was still playing for Christon United during the 1976/77 season.

During the 1979/80 campaign, Chic played for Middlesex League club Twickenham Villa before finally retiring aged 43.

Tragically, in May 1980 Chic s 18 year-old son Grant was the victim of a stabbing and died in West Middlesex Hospital.

Chic sadly died on 24.4.00 aged only 63.

name: John Brooks
other clubs: Dover, Folkestone, Canterbury City, Dover Athletic, Herne Bay, Folkestone Town, Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Whitstable Town and Sheppey United
bio:
Striker born in West Ham who began his career at Dover and played in their reserves during 1979. John scored ten goals for Dover's first team during 1981/82 and then joined Folkestone for the start of the 1982/83 season.

Before the end of 1982 John moved on to Canterbury and he then rejoined Dover in March 1983. On 10.9.83 he scored as Dover drew 2-2 with Thanet United and he stayed with the club until the summer of 1985 when he went back to Canterbury.

John went on to spend five seasons with City and was their leading Southern League scorer during 1985/86 (15 goals) and 1987/88 (ten goals). He was voted 'Players' Player of the Year' for both 1986/87 and 1987/88. On 26.12.88 he scored in a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Thanet and also found the net in a 3-1 win at Thanet on 27.3.89. During 1989/90 John briefly left Canterbury to make a one-off appearance for Herne Bay before departing permanently at the end of the season having scored 45 goals in the 186 Southern League appearances he'd made in his two spells with the club.

In the summer of 1990 John joined Folkestone and in January 1991 he was on the move again, this time joining Margate.

He made his debut in a 1-0 defeat at Bury on 12.1.91 and kept his place for Margate's next three games, scoring with what the Thanet Times said was "a fine glancing header" in a 4-1 defeat at Buckingham on 26.1.91. John then found himself out of the side for several weeks and when he returned to make a substitute appearance in a 2-1 home win over Fareham on 2.3.91 it was his last game for Margate's first team. He then spent a few weeks in the reserves, scoring twice in seven appearances (one as sub) for them, before rejoining Canterbury for a third spell shortly before the end of 1990/91. He'd made five appearances (one as sub) for Margate and scored once.

John stayed at Canterbury until February 1992 when he signed for Kent County League side Snowdown Colliery Welfare.

In January 1993 he left Snowdown and linked up with Kent League Whitstable.

He was last heard of during 1996/97 when he made one appearance for Sheppey during the first half of the season.

name: Phil Brooman
other clubs: Gravesend & Northfleet, Canterbury City, Tonbridge, London City (Canada) and Ramsgate
bio:
London-born goalkeeper who moved to Thanet as a youngster and played for the East Kent Schoolboys team as an outfield player during the 1958/59 season aged 14. Phil also featured in goal for Thanet Senior Sunday League side Thanet United during the campaign.

Phil later appeared for Spartans in the Thanet League before joining Margate for the 1963/64 season. Phil made nine reserve team appearances during the campaign and also played twice for the senior side. He made his first team debut as an 18 year-old on 28.12.63 in a Southern League game against Rugby at Hartsdown Park and although Margate went down 2-1 Phil did well and kept his place for the home game with Cambridge United on 4.1.64. His performance in the 3-3 draw led to the local paper saying that he was "a good prospect" who deserved a run in the side. However it didn't happen and Phil returned to the reserves for the remainder of the campaign.

He spent the 1964/65 season playing for Northwood in the Thanet Premier Sunday League.

Phil then moved to Gravesend & Northfleet and spent the 1965/66 and 1966/67 seasons with them, making 73 appearances, before joining Canterbury for the 1967/68 campaign.

Phil made 31 Southern League appearances for City during 1967/68 and on 9.5.68 he played as a striker in a game at Dunstable. Canterbury won 6-1 and remarkably Phil scored a hat-trick.

In the summer of 1968 he moved on to Tonbridge and had the misfortune to be in goal as Margate thrashed the Angels 8-0 in a friendly at Hartsdown Park on 5.8.68. It was the day of Phil's 25th birthday. Phil later dropped back into junior football and often played as a striker in the local leagues for clubs such as Westgate and Lonsdale during the 1970's.

During the 1973/74 season he did some coaching in Canada. Phil also had a spell in Toronto, Canada in the summer of 1975 where he played for London City alongside the likes of Steve Breach, Barry Brown, Ray Flannigan, John Hold, Graham Sawyer and Paul Smith.

In December 1979 a goalkeeping crisis at Margate saw Phil return to the club to make a one-off appearance, almost 16 years after his last one. This constituted the longest gap between games of any player in the club's history. Regular keeper Bryan Parry was unavailable for an FA Trophy tie at Hastings on 1.12.79 and Phil was his emergency replacement, at the time he was playing in the Thanet League for Lonsdale. Although Margate lost the match 3-0 Phil "gave a typically fearless display" according to the Thanet Times.

During the 1980/81 season Phil made five further sporadic appearances, again helping out when the club's regular keepers were unavailable. He wore distinctive red goalkeeping gloves for his first appearance of the campaign - a 2-1 win over Crawley at Hartsdown on 30.9.80 - and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that Phil was "totally adequate and could easily become a regular in the side". He was also described as being "chirpy" and "evergreen" and Margate manager Terry Morris said "I knew Brooman would give a good account of himself and he did not let me down." During a 3-1 defeat at Dartford on 29.11.80 Phil "gave Margate's best goalkeeping display of the season" according to the Thanet Times and the local press also praised his bravery and agility during the campaign. In fact the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that Phil was "clearly Margate's most competent keeper".

The 1981/82 season saw Phil return to Hartsdown Park yet again and by then Margate had become Thanet United. As he d turned out for a local Sunday League outfit with the same name over 20 years earlier, Phil was the only player to have appeared for both clubs. He played a few games for Thanet's reserves during the campaign and also made three further first team appearances. Phil's first outing of the season was a 3-1 defeat at Gosport on 13.4.82 and he also deputised for Colin Page in the last two games of the campaign. During the 2-1 defeat at Hastings on 1.5.82 Phil "pulled off some exceptional saves" according to the Thanet Times and a 4-3 home defeat at the hands of Andover on 3.5.82 was his final appearance, over 18 years after his first.

He then helped out with coaching during the early part of the 1982/83 season before joining Ramsgate early in 1983, playing regularly for their first team. Phil then continued to play local football for several more seasons.

He played the last football of his career during the 1990's when he turned out for Thanet League club Margate Athletic Old Boys whose squad of veterans also included a host of other former Margate / Thanet players.

In 2012 Phil was still living in Thanet.

name: Harry Brophy
other clubs: Arsenal (0), Canterbury Waverley, Brighton & Hove Albion (0), Southampton (38,5), Clapton Orient (0) ,Folland Sports, Nuneaton Town, Corinthian Club (Australia)
bio:
6' 0" tall born in Leicester. 
 
Captained Islington Schools in 1931 as they won the English Schools Shield.
 
 Signed by Arsenal 1933 as trainee , been on their books as junior since he was 14
 
Played for Canterbury Waverley (loan from Arsenal) and Arsenal 33/34 
 
To us from nursery summer 1934. Also 1935/36 and on 18.1.36 played in Cant Wave 2 Margate Reserves 2   ITG reported constantly barracked by Cant fans (as ex player of theirs) and said  there was no  auld lang syne  spirit among the Canterbury supporters 
 
signed pro for Arsenal May 1936  and loaned to Brighton & Hove Albion 36/37 (1 first team - in Third Division Cup match against Crystal Palace in September 1936 ) broke a leg when playing in a reserve match for Brighton against Reading, 
 
back to Highbury. 
 
Released by Arsenal and joined Brighton again for  1937-38 but no first team appearances, played for reserves, 
 
He joined Southampton for the 1938-39 season, making 38 League appearances with 5 goals. 
 
made 1 wartime appearance for Clapton Orient in 1943-44. Other
than the O s he also guested for Bradford Park Avenue with 2 appearances in
1942-43, Huddersfield Town with 1 appearances in 1940-41, Fulham with 1
appearance in 1943-44 and Crystal Palace, where he made 2 appearances in
1942.
 
 
Also - after 1939 - Folland Sports (Hampshire League), Nuneaton Town (played in Birmingham Combination 1945/46   14 apps no goals, first was in October 1945 and last in January 1946) . 
During the War he joined the police before joining the Merchant Navy and
served on the Hospital ship St Andrew during the Dunkirk evacuation, 
Trained with Arsenal to keep fit 1948/49
On 29.4.49, he sailed from England to Queensland, Australia and at the start of June 1949 joined the Corinthian Club in Brisbane at the same time as England Amateur international forward Stan Eastham. Club organised accommodation and employment, getting Harry a job in an engineering workshop. Corinthian had put out an appeal for English players and Harry and Stan responded.
Immediately made captain of Corinthians and debut 11.6.49 in home game v Bundaberg, won 5-3 and Harry scored a penalty. The Brisbane Telegraph said he  gave a brilliant display of ball control .
10.9.49 switched to centre-forward for second half of a game against a Far North Coast representative side and scored hat-trick in 7-1 win.
Got involved in coaching and gave talks on tactics to local clubs
June 1950 captained Queensland in game v New South Wales, NSW won 2-0 at the Brisbane Cricket Ground. Queensland won a return game 3-0 shortly afterwards.
26.7.50 took part in long kicking contest against rugby and Aussie Rules players   came 4th with 44 yard effort
September 1950 captained an Australian X1 on tour of New Caledonia 
April 1951 transferred from Corinthian to Brisbane club Grange Thistle and debut for them 21.4.51, he was an Australian citizen by then.
Continued to play for Queensland state team
September 1951 left Brisbane area as work saw him transferred to Townsville   became executive at Coachcraft Ltd, Woolloongabba and retired from football as a player
June 1952 made a one-off appearance for a Brisbane side as they were short of players
March 1953 became coach of Queensland state team
August 1953 appointed as manager of the Australian National team. 
In 1957 he coached the Mauritius national team before returning to England to
gain his coaching badges at Lilleshall
Jan 1961 became manager of Sydney club Maccabi Hakoah 
Then had spell as manager of Sydney Prague
Jan 1963 became manager of Sydney Croatia
Good cricketer - played for Great Yarmouth and had spell on the ground staff at Sussex, also played for Leicestershire s second X1

name: Alan Brown
other clubs: Canterbury City, Gravesend & Northfleet, Deal Town, Bexley United, Whitstable Town and Herne Bay
bio:
Tall, prolific marksman born in Nottingham who also played cricket for both Kent and England.

Alan started his football career with Canterbury City during the 1953/54 season and spent over four years with City before joining Gravesend & Northfleet for the 1957/58 campaign.

Alan scored 58 goals for the Fleet's reserves during 1958/59 and another 32 for them during 1959/60 but only made a total of 26 first team appearances, scoring 15 goals, before joining Margate in June 1960.

Alan s Kent CCC commitments delayed his Margate debut, but after he d played in one reserve team game, Alan made his first senior appearance in a Southern League Cup tie at Dover on 7.9.60 and scored twice in a 3-3 draw. In his next outing - a Southern League game against Ashford at Hartsdown Park on 10.9.60 - Alan scored a hat-trick in a 4-1 win and then found the net in seven out of his next eight appearances, notching up nine goals in the process. After a couple of goalless outings, Alan was dropped to the reserves for a game against Tunbridge Wells Rangers Reserves at Hartsdown Park on 29.10.60 and promptly scored a hat-trick in a 4-3 defeat. He was immediately restored to first team duty. He got another hat-trick for the reserves as they thrashed Crystal Palace A 6-1 at Hartsdown Park on 17.12.60.

By the end of the 1960/61 campaign, Alan had managed a total of 28 goals from 35 appearances which made him Margate s leading goalscorer but despite those impressive statistics, he was also something of a controversial figure. Although he often displayed great pace and powerful shooting, Alan was sometimes criticised by the local press for his low work-rate. He was also felt to have a tendency to miss good goalscoring opportunities and Alan tended to be compared unfavourably with Margate legend Freddie Kearns who he d effectively replaced. Kearns was still with the club but playing principally for the reserves by that time. Alan was released by Margate at the end of the season.

He rejoined Canterbury in the summer of 1961 and during the 1961/62 campaign Alan scored five goals in 13 Southern League appearances for City. During 1962/63 he made a further seven league appearances, scoring once. He was also top scorer for City's reserves.

Alan joined Deal for the 1963/64 season and he was the club's leading goalscorer before moving on at the end of the campaign.

Alan played for Bexley during the 1965/66 season and he later returned to Canterbury once again where he made two Southern League appearances during the early part of 1967/68 without scoring.

He then rejoined Gravesend for a second spell and made 17 appearances during the remainder of the 1967/68 campaign. Alan scored seven goals to finish the season as the Fleet's top scorer but left the club in the summer of 1968.

He joined Whitstable early in the 1968/69 season and made his debut in a game at Sittingbourne on 7.9.68. Alan scored three times in a total of six games for the Oystermen before leaving the club in October 1968. He told Whitstable that he was retiring from the game.

Alan came out of retirement during the 1969/70 season when he returned to Deal for a second spell.

In the summer of 1970 he joined Herne Bay and they were Alan s last club before retiring.

Alan's cricket career was very distinguished, as a fast bowler he represented Kent from 1957 to 1970 and played in two Tests, against Pakistan and India, for England during 1961.

He worked as a salesman at New Northfleet Paper Mills during his time with Margate and later became a postman in the Gravesend area.

In 2010 Alan was a guest at a Kent County Cricket Club dinner at the St.Lawrence Ground in Canterbury that was held to celebrate the 40th anniversary of a County Championship win.

In 2013 he was still living in Gravesend.

name: Barry Brown
other clubs: North Deal United, Deal Town, Herne Bay, London City (Canada), Maidstone United, Dartford, Folkestone & Shepway and Woodnesborough
bio:
Energetic, opportunist goalscorer with a good turn of pace who was born in Deal and started his senior career with Kent Amateur League club North Deal United.

Barry joined Deal Town of the Greater London League for 1967/68 and was part of their side that won the Greater London League Cup for the season.

In March 1970 Barry was signed by Athenian League club Herne Bay and he scored regularly there before signing for Margate in November 1970, initially on trial, after impressing player-manager Gerry Baker during Margate's 1-0 FA Cup win at Herne Bay on 7.11.70. Baker described Barry as being "A player with plenty of dash."

He made his debut as Margate went down 4-0 at home to Folkestone in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie on 16.11.70 and was then in and out of the first team for the remainder of the 1970/71 campaign. Barry made a total of 20 appearances (one as sub) and scored four goals, the first of which came in a 5-4 win over Dartford at Hartsdown on 10.3.71. In April 1971 the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that he was "a much improved player". During the season the local press regularly commented on Barry's appearance and often referred to him as being "shaggy-maned". On 23.1.71 the report for Margate's 3-3 draw at Wimbledon expanded on this theme and reported that Barry's "Tiny Tim hairstyle was a dash of sheer vaudeville to the appreciative Wimbledon terraces".

Barry really established himself during the 1971/72 season and made 60 appearances. He was Margate s leading goalscorer with a total of 20 goals and he was a tireless worker for the side. Barry took to wearing distinctive white boots during the season and a haircut prompted the local press to comment that his "shorter hairstyle gives him a much more streamlined appearance". However he was still often referred to as "Mexican-moustached". Barry was also described as being "volatile" by the local paper and on 20.11.71 he featured in Margate s infamous 11-0 defeat at Bournemouth & Boscombe in the FA Cup 1st Round. He was watched by Football League scouts during the campaign and Barry s performances won him the club's first-ever 'Player of the Year' award.

He started the 1972/73 season in excellent form and his hat-trick in a 5-0 win at Dover on 16.8.72 was not only his first for the club but also the first that anybody had scored for Margate since March 1970. Barry was watched by Gillingham in September 1972 and scored regularly during the first half of the campaign. He was variously described as "elusive", "aggressive", "shock-haired" and "livewire" by the local press.

On 18.11.72 Barry was in the Margate side that beat Swansea 1-0 in an FA Cup 1st Round tie at Hartsdown Park and his performance in a 3-1 defeat at Yeovil on 25.11.72 led to the local press describing him as "razor-sharp". Barry scored from the edge of the penalty area with what the paper said was "a good goal from a good player". On 2.12.72 Barry notched a typical opportunist goal in a 3-2 win at Guildford after latching onto a loose ball, "pouncing like a ferret on a rabbit" according to the Thanet Times.

On 9.12.72 he got the vital goal as Margate won 1-0 at Walton & Hersham in the FA Cup 2nd Round to set up the famous January 1973 clash with Tottenham. Barry was interviewed by the Deal local paper just after the draw was made and said "this is the sort of draw every footballer dreams of but rarely gets. It is great, just fantastic." He went on to say "it's always been my ambition to play against a 1st Division side in the Cup. Now the chance is here I feel really nervous. We've got a chance of winning and we'll certainly give 100 per cent effort to try to win. Whatever happens, we'll enjoy it. We are all hoping the game is switched to White Hart Lane - it'll be fabulous playing there in front of such a massive crowd." In the end the match went ahead at Hartsdown Park on 13.1.73 and Spurs won 6-0.

Barry endured something of a barren spell during the early part of 1973 but regained his form towards the end of the season and scored another hat-trick described by the Thanet Times as "three killer opportunist goals" in a 5-0 win over Burton on 20.4.73. Barry again finished the campaign as Margate's top scorer, with 24 goals from 55 appearances (three as sub).

Although Barry struggled to find his best form for much of the 1973/74 season he still scored 19 times in 61 appearances (two as sub) to finish the campaign as the club's joint top scorer along with John Hold. His goals included a chip described by the local press as "surprising" in a 4-0 win over Chatham on 8.12.73 and a fluke effort as Margate won 2-1 at Telford on 23.3.74. A goal kick from the Telford keeper only went as far as Barry, lurking on the edge of the penalty area, and the ball cannoned off him and into the net. Barry also scored with a brilliant header in a 2-0 win at Maidstone in the Kent Senior Cup Final on 13.4.74 but at the end of the season he was transfer-listed.

Barry ended up staying with the club for the 1974/75 campaign and he made a further 57 appearances, four of them as a substitute. Barry, by then bearded, scored 21 goals and he was described as a "lightning striker" by the local press. On 30.11.74 he fired a hat-trick in a 4-1 win over Dulwich at Hartsdown Park and on 11.2.75 Barry scored with a crisp volley during a 2-1 win at Ramsgate. On 5.4.75 he was in the Margate side that lost 2-0 at home to Kettering in the first leg of the Southern League Cup Final. He also played in the second leg at Kettering on 12.4.75 as Margate secured a 1-1 draw that wasn t sufficient to claim the trophy. During a 2-1 home defeat against Chelmsford on 22.4.75 Barry was said to be "full of running and fire" and on 2.5.75 he scored twice after coming on as a half-time substitute in a 2-2 draw at Weymouth. One of his goals was a superb lofted shot.

During the summer of 1975 he had a spell in Toronto, Canada where he played for London City alongside the likes of Steve Breach, Phil Brooman, Ray Flannigan, John Hold, Graham Sawyer and Paul Smith.

At the start of the 1975/76 season Barry found it difficult to break into the side and he featured mainly as a substitute during the first two months of the campaign. In early October 1975 he was fined a weeks wages and transfer-listed after refusing to play for the reserves and manager Les Riggs told the East Kent Times It is now up to Barry to reconsider his decision. Naturally we do not want to lose him but on the other hand we do not wish to retain an unhappy or dissatisfied player.

Despite being made available for transfer, Barry still scored in three consecutive games during October. His goal in a 1-0 win at Burton on 11.10.75 was an excellent one as Barry beat two players before firing home. On 18.10.75 he was in the side that lost 2-0 at Canterbury in the FA Cup and that turned out to be Barry s final outing for Margate. On 25.10.75 he was asked to play for the reserves in a home game against Sittingbourne but Barry refused and was again fined a weeks wages. He was picked for the reserves once again for their next match and Les Riggs said I would think knocking in a few goals with the second team could only give him a confidence boost. As it turned out, Barry wasn t available for the second string game as during the first weekend of November he was sold to Maidstone for a fee of £800. Barry left Hartsdown Park just before completing five years service with Margate. He d made 11 appearances during 1975/76, four of them as a substitute, and scored three times.

He made a good start to his Maidstone career, scoring seven times in his first nine appearances before the end of 1975.

In September 1976 Barry was sold to Dartford for a small fee and scored five times in 21 appearances there, including two goals in a 4-3 win over Margate at Hartsdown Park on 16.10.76. Towards the end of the 1976/77 campaign he moved on to Folkestone & Shepway.

He then returned to Deal for the 1977/78 season and scored ten goals before retiring from senior football.

Barry then played for Kent Amateur League outfit Woodnesborough for many years.

In February 1984 he briefly returned to Kent League football when he made a one-off appearance for Deal in a game at Darenth. The club were in the midst of an injury crisis so Barry agreed to help them out. He was brought down for a penalty which Dick White - a former Margate player - scored to win the match 1-0.

Barry continued playing for Woodnesborough through to the early 2000's despite being over 50 by then.

In 2004 he was living in Deal and was part of Dover Harbour Board's works management team. Barry had originally been a carpenter for the company during his time with Margate.

He was still living in Deal in 2011.

name: Bill Brown
other clubs: Southampton (0), Charlton Athletic (0), Romford, Chelmsford City, Bedford Town, Gillingham (115+1,34), Portsmouth (9,2), Brentford (4,0), Dunstable Town and Ford United
bio:
Burly 6' 0" tall Croydon-born centre-forward who started his career at Southampton before being signed by Charlton as an 18 year-old in the summer of 1961.

Bill's next move took him to Southern League club Romford for the 1962/63 campaign and he was their top scorer during 1963/64, finishing the season with a total of 29 goals.

During the 1964/65 campaign Bill left Romford and signed for Chelmsford where he spent the remainder of the season before his next move took him to Bedford in August 1965.

Bill scored 17 goals from 42 games for Bedford, including one in a 6-0 home win over Margate on 11.9.65, before Gillingham's new manager Basil Hayward paid £2,000 for his services in February 1966. Hayward had just joined the club from Bedford.

A few days after signing for the Gills, Bill scored a hat-trick in a 4-2 friendly win over Ipswich and he then scored on his competitive debut in a 1-1 draw at Bournemouth. Bill went on to make 116 first team appearances for Gillingham, scoring 34 goals, before transferring to Portsmouth in June 1968.

After a year at Fratton Park he moved to Brentford in July 1969 but the transfer didn't work out and Bill joined Margate in October the same year. He decided to move back into part-time football as he had a haulage business that he wanted to devote more time to.

Bill made his Margate debut in a 2-0 defeat at Poole in the Southern League on 18.10.69 and he was described by the Thanet Times as being "a player of considerable ability". Bill was especially strong in the air and he scored his first goal for Margate on 8.11.69 during a 2-1 defeat at Hillingdon. It was a spectacular strike - a scissor kick that the local paper said "ripped into the roof of the net with such velocity that the netting required immediate repairs".

On 15.11.69 Bill was in the Margate side that were thrashed 7-2 by visitors Aldershot in the FA Cup 1st Round but he struggled for form after that and only played three more first team games, scoring in the last of them - a 3-1 defeat at Hillingdon on 20.12.69. Bill then had a spell in the reserves before leaving Margate in February 1970 having scored twice from nine appearances.

He spent the remainder of the 1969/70 season back at Bedford.

In August 1970 Bill joined Dunstable and he later played for Ford United.

In 2014 Bill was living in Essex.

name: Bob Brown
other clubs: Montrose (Scotland) (0), Raith Rovers (Scotland) (31,0), Fulham (0), Watford (0) and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
5' 11" tall Scottish keeper who was signed by Montrose in November 1945 before moving on to Raith in September 1946.

Bob went on to make 31 first team appearances for Raith in all competitions during 1946/47 and 1947/78 before his contract was cancelled in March 1948.

He had a brief spell with Fulham at the start of the 1948/49 season before joining Margate in September 1948.

Bob made his debut in a 2-0 Kent League defeat away to Gillingham Reserves on 22.9.48 and then enjoyed a run of games in the first team before losing his place to the newly-signed Ron Johnson. His final appearance was on 11.12.48 - a 2-2 draw at Royal Marines Chatham - and after that Bob played reserve team football before being released in May 1949. He'd made a total of eight appearances during 1948/49.

Bob spent the 1949/50 campaign at Watford but didn t feature in their senior side and in August 1950 he returned to Thanet to join Ramsgate.

He signed for Kent League club Chatham ahead of the 1951/52 season and Bob was their regular keeper until the end of January 1952 when he picked up a groin injury that required surgery.

name: Dennis Brown
other clubs: Chelsea (13,2), Swindon Town (106,45), Northampton Town (43+5,11), Aldershot (259+8,60), Barnet, Cheltenham Town and Wokingham Town
bio:
Reading-born player who began his career as a junior at 1st Division Chelsea and made 13 first team appearances for them during the 1963/64 and 1964/65 seasons.

In November 1964 Dennis was sold to Swindon for £15,000 and went on to score 45 goals from 106 senior appearances for the Wiltshire club.

In February 1967 Dennis moved on to Northampton. Shortly after his transfer, he was involved in a car crash and had to have a kneecap removed. Dennis was told that he wouldn t play again but 11 months later he returned to action and scored in his comeback match for the senior side, a 1-1 draw at Scunthorpe on 2.3.68. Dennis scored 11 goals in 48 first team games for Northampton before being given a free transfer at the end of the 1968/69 campaign.

In July 1969 he signed for 4th Division club Aldershot and Dennis went on to become a very popular player there. On 15.11.69 he scored a hat-trick in a 7-2 win at Margate in the FA Cup 1st Round and in the aftermath of the tie, the Daily Mirror asked Dennis about his knee problem. He told the paper I was really choked when a specialist said I was finished with football, but I worked hard at my remedial exercises and now my knee is fine. Aldershot player-manager Jimmy Melia said The way he played you wouldn t have thought there had ever been anything wrong with him. Dennis eventually made over 250 senior appearances for the Shots and scored 60 goals.

In the summer of 1975 Dennis joined Margate and in August 1975 the Thanet Times described him as being "the one man capable of replacing Eddie Clayton". He made his debut on 16.8.75 in a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Telford. Dennis played in midfield but later appeared on both wings, only occasionally featuring in his preferred role as a striker. On 6.9.75 he put in what the local press described as a "five star performance" in a 2-1 defeat at Wimbledon and on 27.9.75 Dennis scored direct from a corner during a 2-2 draw with Maidstone. He also found the net with a diving header in a 3-1 win at Stourbridge on 24.1.76 and Dennis made a total of 37 appearances (two as sub) during the 1975/76 season, scoring six goals. However he was released at the end of the campaign.

Dennis joined Barnet for the 1976/77 season and then scored 19 goals during the 1977/78 campaign before being transferred to Cheltenham for £1,000 in March 1978.

He scored 12 goals in 49 appearances there and then moved to Wokingham in July 1979, scoring five goals in 44 games during the 1979/80 season.

After retiring, Dennis kept fit by running every day and an Aldershot website (http://aldershotfc.has.it) said that he became a self-employed salesman, working in the Hampshire and Berkshire areas. In the early 2000's he was living in Wokingham, Berkshire.

name: George Brown
bio:
George Griffiths Brown     
Born Margate, Q2 1880
Diminutive 
Father George Frederick Brown was Mayor of Margate in 1897 and was mayor when lifeboat disaster happened, he opened fund to support wives and children of the men killed and  10,000 was raised. George (the Margate player) was one of 9 children - five of which had died by the time George senior passed away in November 1913
Attended Holy Trinity School in Margate and then Margate College
veterinary student in 1901   
Margate 00/01 and also played for Margate College that season, he was a master there   
Margate 01/02   
Left Thanet to study as a vet in London
Played for London Veterinary College 02/03, turned out for them in Fr v Margate October 1902     
Once qualified as a vet, moved to Inverness to assist a Major William Logan at his vet practice. They later entered into a business partnership. George became one of the best known vets in the Highlands.
Died in Inverness on 5.4.30 aged only 49

name: Jermaine Brown
other clubs: Arsenal (0), Bristol City (0), Colchester United (5+1,1), Crystal Palace (0), Boston United (3+2,0), Aldershot Town, Dulwich Hamlet, Ashford Town (Middlesex), Chelmsford City and Thamesmead Town
bio:
Lambeth-born attack-minded player who started his career as a trainee at Arsenal, joining the club as a nine year-old before graduating to the Gunners' academy in the summer of 1999 aged 16. Jermaine spent two years in the academy that was run by the legendary Liam Brady and was part of the side that won the FA Youth Cup in 2001, featuring as a substitute in both legs of the final against Blackburn.

In the summer of 2001 Jermaine was given a professional contract and he played regularly for Arsenal's reserves during the 2001/02 and 2002/03 seasons having made his debut for them during 2000/01. He'd made 36 reserve team appearances (11 as sub) and scored seven goals by the time he was released in June 2003. Jermaine had also previously made 53 appearances (13 as sub) in the Gunners' Under-17 and Under-19 sides and scored 20 goals.

In the summer of 2003 Jermaine had an extended trial with Bristol City where he played in the reserves but when City decided not to offer him a contract he moved on to 2nd Division (later League One) club Colchester in October 2003.

Jermaine made his debut for Colchester as a substitute in a Football League Trophy quarter final tie at Wycombe on 9.12.03. The match went to extra time and he came on two minutes from the end with the scores level at 2-2 before striking a dramatic last-minute winner. Jermaine went on to make five more starts for Colchester but he was released shortly after playing in a 1-0 defeat at Sheffield United on 15.2.04.

He then played in a reserve team game for Crystal Palace before signing for Division 3 (later League Two) outfit Boston towards the end of February 2004. Their manager Steve Evans said "Jermaine is lightning quick, has two good feet and is a good finisher." Jermaine made his debut for the Lincolnshire club in a 2-0 defeat at Torquay on 28.2.04 and had four more first team outings before being loaned to Southern League Eastern Division side King's Lynn in March 2004.

Immediately after joining King's Lynn Jermaine was granted compassionate leave after his father became ill and he never played for the club. He also didn't appear for Boston again and in July 2004 Jermaine signed for Conference South club Lewes.

Before the 2004/05 season proper began he parted company with Lewes and Jermaine then had a year out of football before joining Conference club Aldershot in August 2005.

After only two weeks with the Shots he signed for Margate and made his debut as a substitute in a Isthmian League Premier Division game at Staines on 23.8.05. Margate lost 2-1 but Jermaine got what the Isle of Thanet Gazette said was the "goal of the game", beating two defenders and dummying the Staines keeper before rolling the ball home. He made his first start in midfield in a 0-0 draw at Harrow on 27.8.05 and Jermaine then started six of the next seven matches.

The Thanet Times said he "did well" in midfield in a 0-0 draw with Redbridge at Hartsdown Park on 29.8.05 and on 10.9.05 Jermaine played as a right wing-back in an FA Cup tie against visitors Cowes. He got forward to score in a 4-0 win and the Thanet Times said he'd slotted into his new role "effortlessly". After a good run in the side Jermaine missed a 1-1 draw at Walton & Hersham on 1.10.05 before wearing the number two shirt in a 1-1 draw with Billericay at Hartsdown on 4.10.05. The Thanet Times said he was proving to be "a useful utility man" but he only played once more - in a 3-0 home defeat against Cray in an FA Cup tie on 8.10.05 - before being released having scored twice from 11 appearances (two as sub). Manager Chris Kinnear told the Thanet Times "Jermaine played in a couple of positions for us but has had one or two problems with work."

After leaving Margate he had a long spell out of football before resurfacing at Isthmian League Division 1 South outfit Dulwich at the start of the 2007/08 campaign. Jermaine left the club during the season and then had another lengthy spell away from the game.

In March 2011 he made a comeback aged 28 when he signed for Southern League Division 1 Central side Ashford (Middlesex) and Jermaine played for them until the end of the 2010/11 season.

In July 2011 he was signed by Conference South club Chelmsford and Jermaine made 13 appearances for the Clarets before being released in January 2012.

He played twice in the Isthmian League Division 1 for Thamesmead later in the 2011/12 campaign but then dropped out of senior football and during the first half of 2012/13 Jermaine turned out for Lambeth All Stars in the Morden & District League.

In January 2013 Jermaine rejoined Margate over seven years after his previous spell with the club and became new caretaker manager Craig Holloway s first signing. Jermaine was an unused substitute for five games before finally making his first appearance from the bench in a 2-1 win over Hampton & Richmond in an Isthmian League Premier Division match at Hartsdown Park on 23.2.13.

On 26.2.13 Jermaine started for the first time as Margate beat visitors Leiston 2-0 and the club s website said he put in an accomplished performance" in midfield. Caretaker assistant manager Simon Osborn said We brought Jermaine Brown in to play. First half he did exceptionally well. I thought he gave us a different option that we haven t had previously. He got a bit tired (in the second half) but that s to be expected because he hasn t had a lot of game time recently."

Jermaine played from the start in each of the next three matches and Margate s website said he was assured and controlled in midfield" during a 0-0 draw with Hendon at Wembley FC on 2.3.13. The site then said Jermaine was once again excellent at the heart of the midfield" in a 3-0 home win over Bognor Regis on 9.3.13 but on 16.3.13 he had to go off injured during the first half of a 3-0 win at Enfield Town and missed the next three games as a result.

Jermaine returned to action in a home game against Thurrock on 29.3.13 but picked up another injury and had to leave the field before half time. Margate went on to win 3-1. He only featured once as a substitute in the next four matches but on 13.4.13 Jermaine was back in the starting line-up as Margate lost 2-1 to Metropolitan Police at Hartsdown Park. He then started each of the last four games of the season to finish the campaign having made a total of 12 appearances (two as sub) without scoring. Jermaine left Margate at the end of the season.

name: Jimmy Brown
other clubs: Glasgow United (Scotland), Clydebank (Scotland) (0), Merthyr Tydfil (Wales), Tunbridge Wells, Tonbridge and Cray Wanderers
bio:
Scottish midfielder who started his career with Glasgow United before moving into league football with Clydebank. Jimmy was on the club's books during 1979/90 but never made a first team appearance. He later had a spell with Welsh club Merthyr before moving to England.

Jimmy played for Kent League outfit Tunbridge Wells before signing for Tonbridge.

In December 1988 Jimmy left the Angels to join Thanet United and made his debut on 17.12.88, ironically against Tonbridge. United won 2-0 at Hartsdown Park and the Adscene said that Jimmy had an "effective first match". The Isle of Thanet Gazette agreed, saying that he "often took the eye" but Jimmy then missed United's next five games due to a pre-arranged holiday in Scotland. He returned for a 4-0 home defeat at the hands of Andover on 21.1.89 and the Adscene felt he was "Thanet's most effective player". A week later United were thrashed 6-2 at Witney but the Thanet Times said that Jimmy was "outstanding" in midfield. He played once more, in a 2-0 defeat at home to Bury on 4.2.89, but Jimmy then left the club, telling player-manager Garry Aldous that he wasn't enjoying his football. He'd made four appearances before his departure.

After leaving Thanet Jimmy rejoined Tonbridge but after making eight appearances at the start of the 1989/90 season he moved on.

During the 1990/91 campaign he played for Cray.

name: Len Brown
other clubs: Tottenham Hotspur (0), Wingate, Wolverhampton Wanderers (0) and Birmingham City (0)
bio:
Brave keeper who began his career playing amateur football in the London area before being signed by Tottenham. After being released by Spurs, Len joined Wingate and impressed for them during the 1961/62 season as an 18 year-old. He had two trials with Wolves during the campaign, featuring in their youth team, and was also watched by scouts for the England Amateur team.

In May 1962 Len had a trial with Birmingham and played for them in the 2nd leg of the Lord Mayor s Charity Cup Final against Aston Villa at Villa Park on 7.5.62. He did well enough to be signed by The Blues ahead of the 1962/63 campaign. In May 1963 he was part of Birmingham s youth squad that travelled to Karlsruhe in Germany for a tournament and during the 1963/64 season he again featured in tour games for the club.

In March 1964 Len joined Margate on trial, the club had tried to sign him two years previously when he was still in amateur football. He made his debut on 27.3.64 in a Southern League game at Wellington and had what the local press described as "a day to remember" - pulling off several outstanding saves and displaying clean handling throughout the 1-1 draw. Len then kept his place for most of the campaign's remaining games, making nine appearances in total and keeping out the club's established first team keeper Brian Hughes. On 4.4.64 Len's performance in an away game at Cambridge City led to him being applauded off at half-time and the local press described him as being the best player on the field. He also produced a brilliant performance in a game at Weymouth on 21.4.64.

Len made a further nine appearances during the early part of the 1964/65 campaign, battling Hughes for the first team berth. However by early 1965 Hughes had firmly re-established himself as the club's first-choice keeper. As a result Len asked to be released and in February 1965 his contract was cancelled by mutual consent. Part of the problem was that Margate no longer had a reserve team so he often wasn't playing at all.

name: Shaun Brown
other clubs: Ramsgate, Herne Bay, Deal Town and Canterbury City
bio:
Margate-born striker who progressed through Margate's youth ranks and was playing for the Under-18's during the 1997/98 season. By 1999/00 Shaun was a regular in the reserves and he stayed with the club for the 2000/01 campaign too.

On 13.2.01 Shaun made a one-off appearance for the first team when he came on as a substitute in a 2-1 defeat at Dover in the Kent Senior Cup. The match went to extra time and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Shaun was "cruelly denied an equaliser by the Crabble pitch as a headed attempt stuck in the sandy goalmouth".

At the end of the season Margate's reserve team manager Steve Winch chose Shaun as his side's 'Player of the Year'.

Shaun joined Ramsgate for the 2001/02 campaign and then moved on to Herne Bay.

He returned to the Rams in October 2002 and his second spell with the club lasted until the summer of 2005 when he linked up with Herne Bay once more.

From 2006/07 to 2008/09 Shaun only played Sunday League football in the Thanet area but he signed for Kent League club Deal Town in the summer of 2009.

He left Deal at the end of the 2009/10 season and spent 2010/11 with Thanet Sunday Football League club Windsor D cor.

Shaun was still playing locally during 2011/12.

In the summer of 2013 he signed for Southern Counties East Football League outfit Canterbury and made his debut in a 2-0 defeat at Corinthian on 10.8.13.

name: Stan Brown
other clubs: Fulham (393+5,19), Brighton & Hove Albion (9,0), Colchester United (25,0), Wimbledon, Haywards Heath and Southwick
bio:
Intelligent, 5' 6" tall utility player born in Lewes, Sussex who began his career with Fulham and made almost 400 first team appearances for them spanning the 1960/61-1972/73 seasons. Stan was granted a testimonial during the 1970/71 season when Fulham entertained Chelsea on 12.10.70.

In October 1972 Stan joined Brighton on loan and in December 1972 he was transferred to Colchester. He made 25 senior appearances for the Essex club before dropping into non-league football to join Wimbledon for the start of the 1973/74 campaign.

Stan scored once in 27 games for Wimbledon between August and December 1973.

In January 1974 Stan was signed by Margate for a small fee and manager Les Riggs told the East Kent Times Stan Brown will be a decided acquisition for the club for he is a very experienced operator with the utility value of being able to perform with distinction in defence or attack.

Stan made his debut in a 0-0 draw with Chelmsford at Hartsdown Park on 5.1.74 and won praise from the local press for his "expert close control and intelligent passing" in a midfield role. He was also described as "a wily campaigner" and went on to make 14 appearances (two as sub) before the end of the 1973/74 season, usually playing in midfield but also appearing as a winger and as a striker. At the end of the campaign Stan was released.

He later played for Haywards Heath and Southwick (including the 1977/78, 1978/79 and 1979/80 seasons) before moving into coaching. Stan was on the staff at Sussex County League outfit Ringmer during the 1989/90 campaign.

In October 2008 he was a guest for Fulham's Premier League game against Sunderland at Craven Cottage and was introduced to the crowd on the pitch at half-time.

Stan had two brothers who also played in the Football League - Alan who played for Brighton and Irvin who was a Bournemouth player.

Stan died on 15.3.18 aged 76.

name: John Brunning
other clubs: West Ham United (0), Leyton Orient (0), Billericay Town, Fisher Athletic (London), Greenwich Borough and Erith & Belvedere
bio:
Attacking player who started his career in West Ham's youth set-up. During the 1991/92 season John played for the Hammers' South Eastern Counties League side and he also featured in the reserves.

He joined Leyton Orient as a trainee for the 1992/93 campaign and then moved on to Billericay but during his time with the Essex club John suffered a severe shoulder injury that kept him out of football for two years.

In the summer of 1996 John returned to football when he signed for Margate and he made his debut as a substitute in a 4-1 win over Yate at Hartsdown Park on 17.8.96 - the first game of Chris Kinnear's reign as manager. John also came on as a substitute in Margate's next game at Fisher Athletic on 20.8.96 and scored in a 3-2 win. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said his goal was "well-taken" - a low drive into the corner of the net. After five substitute appearances John made his first start in a 3-2 home defeat at the hands of Tonbridge Angels on 3.9.96 and he then started 12 of Margate's next 13 matches, usually playing in midfield. The Thanet Times said he was "impressive" in a 2-1 defeat at Forest Green on 7.9.96 whilst the Isle of Thanet Gazette said John's "aggressive runs gave Fisher the most cause for concern" during a 3-1 home defeat against the Londoners on 24.9.96. The paper also said he was "terrier-like" and John's committed display as Margate lost 2-1 at home to Aldershot in an FA Trophy tie on 19.10.96 led the Thanet Times to describe him as "a dogged little grafter".

He continued to earn praise from the local press as the weeks passed and the Gazette said John "battled like a beaver but lacked a shooting touch" in a 2-0 win over Erith & Belvedere at Hartsdown Park on 29.10.96. By then he was nearing the end of his spell with Margate and shortly after playing in a 1-0 home defeat at the hands of Bromley on 5.11.96 John was released. He'd scored once in 19 appearances (six as sub).

John joined Fisher immediately after leaving Hartsdown Park and his Margate team-mate John Embery also made the move. John scored on his debut in a 4-1 win at Dartford on 20.11.96 and went on to spend over two years with Fisher.

He joined Kent League club Greenwich Borough early in 1999 and spent the rest of the 1998/99 season there.

He linked up with Erith & Belvedere for the 1999/00 campaign and went on to score four goals in 17 appearances (two as sub) during two injury ravaged seasons with the Deres before retiring from senior football.
