name: Steve Cuggy
other clubs: Sunderland (0), Blyth Spartans, Maidstone United (3+13,1), Dover Athletic, Hastings Town, Gateshead, Folkestone Invicta, Tonbridge Angels, Bedlington Terriers, Whitley Bay and Chester-le-Street
bio:
Prolific goalscorer born in Wallsend on Tyneside who played for Blyth-based New Hartley Juniors as a schoolboy and scored 42 goals for them during 1987/88. In February 1988 Steve had trials with Sunderland and Northampton and in May 1988 he was signed by Sunderland on a two-year contract.

Steve featured in Sunderland s junior side and youth team before being released at the end of September 1989.

He immediately signed for Blyth Spartans and on 7.10.89 he came on as a substitute to score on his debut in a 2-1 defeat at Billingham Synthonia in the Northern League. Steve scored twice more for Blyth before the end of the season. He then rattled in 45 goals during 1990/91 and Steve s tally included three hat-tricks as well as four goals in a 7-0 home win over South Bank on 13.10.90.

In May 1991 4th Division Maidstone signed Steve for a fee of £2,000 and he made his first team debut for the Stones as a substitute in a League Cup tie Leicester on 21.8.91. On 7.9.91 Steve scored after coming on as a sub in a 2-0 win at Scunthorpe and he went on to make a total of 16 appearances (13 as sub) for Maidstone without scoring again before the end of the 1991/92 campaign, the Stones' last before folding.

In August 1992 Steve joined Dover and scored on his debut after coming on as a substitute in a 2-1 win at Cambridge City on 26.8.92. He also scored as a sub in a 3-1 home win over Margate on 20.10.92. On 1.12.92 Steve got five goals in a 7-1 win over Folkestone in an Eastern Floodlight Cup tie at Crabble and on 20.4.93 he came off the bench to score both Dover's goals as they beat Stourbridge 2-1 at home in the 2nd Leg of the Southern League Cup Final which the Midlands club won 3-2 on aggregate. Steve finished 1992/93 as Dover's leading scorer with 25 goals from 49 appearances (31 as sub). A remarkable 12 of his goals were scored as a substitute.

In the summer of 1993 Steve was transfer-listed by Dover manager Chris Kinnear and at the start of September Margate signed him for an undisclosed club record fee believed to be in the region of £5,000. Steve played his first game for Margate in a 1-0 win over Havant at Hartsdown Park on 4.9.93 and the Thanet Times said it was an "encouraging debut". He quickly struck up an understanding with fellow striker Joe Brayne and on 11.9.93 both he and Steve scored hat-tricks in a 6-0 home win over Pagham in an FA Cup tie. They were Steve's first goals for Margate and it was the first time that two Margate players had scored hat-tricks in the same match since January 1974. The Thanet Times said that Steve's "cultured and incisive play...showed what led the management to pay so much for his services" and his second goal was a tremendous rising drive that crashed into the top corner of the net. From then on he scored consistently and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Steve had "made a big difference to Margate's attacking options" the day before he got two goals in a 3-1 win at Bromley in the FA Cup on 25.9.93. On 26.10.93 Steve scored what the Gazette called an "absolute gem of a goal" after five minutes of a home game with Sudbury, firing home a lofted drive from fully 25 yards out that helped Margate to a 2-1 win. The paper said "his neat touches stamp him as a quality striker at this level" and called Steve "the master of the first touch". On 15.12.93 he had a weak penalty saved in a 4-1 defeat at Tonbridge but by the end of 1993 Steve had scored 11 goals.

He enjoyed an excellent run of form during January and February 1994 and when Steve scored in a 4-2 win at Tonbridge on 19.1.94 it was the first of five consecutive games in which he found the net. A full-length diving header in a 1-1 draw at Dunstable on 5.2.94 was the best of Steve's efforts during his purple patch and then on 1.3.94 he scored five for the reserves in a 7-1 win at Thamesmead in the Kent Midweek League. On 24.4.94 Steve scored twice in a 6-0 win over Braintree at Hartsdown and on 28.4.94 he bagged a hat-trick for the reserves in a 5-3 win at Faversham. On 2.5.94 he was part of the side that beat his old club Dover 2-1 at Gillingham's Priestfield Stadium to win the Kent Senior Cup for Margate and Steve finished the season having scored 24 times in 49 first team appearances (one as sub). His goal tally was one less than Brayne's and Steve also scored 15 times for the reserves.

Steve signalled his intentions for 1994/95 by scoring six times in Margate's pre-season friendlies and despite Brayne's departure he went on to enjoy an excellent campaign. On 20.8.94, the opening day of the season, Steve scored twice in a 3-1 win over Bashley at Hartsdown and he bagged another brace in a 3-1 home win over Tonbridge on 20.9.94. He then scored in Margate's next four matches and Steve's run included a hat-trick in 5-3 win at Peacehaven & Telscombe in an FA Cup replay on 27.9.94 and another treble in a 5-1 win at Fisher on 4.10.94 which took his tally to ten goals in five games. Steve then endured a barren run of seven matches without scoring despite playing well and the Thanet Times said he "had an outstanding game" as Margate lost 1-0 at home to Kingstonian in the FA Cup on 8.10.94. The paper wrote "he was full of running and his sharp close control (was) a revelation". Between 8.11.94 and 26.11.94 inclusive Steve was on target in four consecutive matches and was Margate's only scorer during those games. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said his rising drive in a 1-1 draw with Braintree at Hartsdown on 15.11.94 was a "stunning goal" whilst the Times described Steve's close range finish in a 1-0 home win over Yate on 19.11.94 as "a magic moment of opportunism". He also found the net in a 5-2 defeat at Salisbury on 3.12.94 to take his scoring run to five matches.

Steve enjoyed another five game scoring spell during December 1994 and January 1995, starting with a 2-0 win over Poole at Hartsdown on 17.12.94. On 2.1.95 he scored a hat-trick in a 7-3 win over visitors Tonbridge and also had a penalty saved. The Gazette said "he has the knack of being able to sense when a possible opportunity is about to come his way" and added "although slight of stature he is a terrier in the penalty area". Steve rounded off his spree with another hat-trick in Margate's next match - a 3-1 win over Clevedon at Hartsdown. He continued to score regularly after that but on 22.3.95 Steve was sent off for retaliating to a bad challenge after just 17 minutes of a 2-0 defeat at Havant. On 25.3.95 he scored both goals in a 2-0 win at Burnham and after serving a three match ban in April Steve returned to score twice in a 3-0 home win over Fisher on 17.4.95. He got two more goals in a 3-2 defeat against Weymouth at Hartsdown on 25.4.95 and on 2.5.95 Steve notched up his 40th goal of the season in a 2-0 win at Weston-Super-Mare. On 6.5.95 he played in a 4-0 home defeat against Baldock to finish the season with a record of 40 goals from 52 appearances.

Towards the end of May 1995 Margate turned down Gravesend & Northfleet's £7,000 offer for Steve and General Manager Cliff Egan told the Gazette "we don't want to lose him and anyway the offer was not a realistic one". However in August 1995 a bid from Southern League Premier Division Hastings was accepted and Steve left Margate before the start of the 1995/96 season having scored 64 goals in exactly 100 starts for the club. The transfer fee wasn't disclosed by Margate but was quickly revealed to be £13,000 by The Sun newspaper in an article that explained how Sussex-based lottery winner Mark Gardiner had paid the fee out of his own pocket. The report was headlined "£22m Mark Buys Local Side A Star" and Steve told the paper "It's flattering - £13,000 is a lot. A non-league transfer is usually about £500 or a set of new shirts." In an interview for the Thanet Times he said "I've really enjoyed my two seasons at Margate and I've many happy memories including winning the Kent Senior Cup last year. But it's a step up for me and although my chances of returning to the professional game are fading I want to play at the highest level possible." As various Margate fans voiced their dismay over Steve's sale in letters to the local papers chairman Gordon Wallis told the Thanet Times "If a club comes forward with an offer that would be financially the right option, you've got to bite the bullet" and in August 1995 Margate issued a press release saying that the £13,000 quoted was inaccurate.

He was Hastings' leading scorer with 24 goals during the 1995/96 season and Steve's tally included four in a 6-2 home win over Salisbury on 11.11.95. He top scored again during 1996/97 with 16 goals including a hat-trick in a 4-3 win over Sudbury on 25.3.97. During that season Steve had a spell on loan at Conference side Gateshead where he only started twice during February and March 1997 but scored a goal as a substitute in a 3-2 home win over Woking on 8.3.97.

In September 1997 Steve left Hastings to join Kent League club Folkestone and he scored over 30 goals during 1997/98 including two hat-tricks. Towards the end of 1998 Steve was loaned to Tonbridge where he scored twice in five appearances (one as sub) and he left Folkestone permanently to return to his native North East early in the 1999/00 season.

Steve initially joined Bedlington before moving on to Whitley Bay during the 1999/00 campaign.

He top scored for Whitley Bay with 25 goals during 2000/01 and in January 2001 Steve turned down the chance of rejoining Gateshead. On 11.5.02 he was part of the Whitley Bay side that won the FA Vase by beating Tiptree United 1-0 at Villa Park, coming on as a substitute to provide the cross that resulted in the winning goal.

In the summer of 2002 Steve joined Chester-le-Street before retiring at the end of 2003.

He rejoined Whitley Bay as a coach at the start of 2004 and during the 2004/05 season Steve made a comeback as a player for the club. In the summer of 2005 he retired again aged 34 and Steve said he'd given up "due to minor niggly injuries I keep picking up when I play. My body telling me something and I know my best years behind me." At that time he was a fireman living close to Whitley Bay's ground and Steve said that he still kept a look out for Margate's results.

He became Whitley Bay's assistant manager for the 2005/06 season and on 1.10.05 Steve was sent from the bench during a 4-2 defeat at Sunderland Nissan in an FA Vase 2nd Qualifying Round tie. During the summer of 2007 he briefly came out of retirement to play in some of the club's pre-season games and on 14.7.07 Steve scored the winner in a 3-2 home win over Thackley. In May 2009 Whitley Bay won the FA Vase with a 2-0 win over Glossop North End at Wembley and Steve was still the club's assistant manager / coach at the time.

During the 2009/10 season he made the long trip south to turn out for Dover's veterans team and scored twice in a 4-1 win over Bromley's veterans in February 2010.

In May 2010 Steve was back at Wembley as assistant manager of Whitley Bay. They hammered Wroxham 6-1 to retain the FA Vase.

Later in 2010 Steve featured in a television advert for sports channel ESPN that promoted their coverage of the FA Cup. The advertising campaign focused on "everyman" players who had scored goals in the FA Cup in the past and were now pursuing alternative careers - a fireman in Steve's case.

On 8.5.11 Steve had yet another day out at Wembley as Whitley Bay won the FA Vase for a third consecutive season but a couple of weeks later he left the club.

On 24.5.11 he was appointed as manager of Conference North outfit Blyth Spartans, returning to the club almost exactly 20 years after leaving. Steve told the Newcastle Evening Chronicle "I'm delighted, I've followed Blyth since I was a kid, played for the club and have a massive soft spot for it."

Unfortunately things didn't work out for Steve at Blyth and he left the club by mutual consent in December 2011 after a run of two wins in 20 matches had left the club bottom of the Conference North. He told local paper The Journal "I am very disappointed to be leaving Blyth. I had high hopes but things transpired against us. I know every club has injury problems but I don't feel like I had a break from the footballing gods. Everything that could go wrong did go wrong. You could not make up what has gone against us in the last six months."

In May 2012 Steve returned to football when he was appointed as assistant manager of Northern League Division 1 side Newcastle Benfield.

Steve's first name was actually Michael and before becoming a professional at Maidstone he worked as a croupier in a casino.

A relative of Steve's called Francis Cuggy made over 150 appearances for Sunderland between 1909 and 1921 and also won two caps for England. Steve s father also played non-league football and turned out for Northern Combination outfit High Pit during the 1978/79 season.

name: Neil Cugley
other clubs: Ashford Town, West Bromwich Albion (0), Folkestone & Shepway, Dartford, Dover, Folkestone, Maidstone United, Dover Athletic and Hythe Town
bio:
6' 1" tall, well-built player born in Folkestone who began his career with Ashford and broke into their first team as a teenager during the 1974/75 season. Neil made his senior debut in a 2-2 draw at Dover in the Kent Senior Cup on 9.12.74 and at that time he was principally a central defender but also played at left-back on occasions. During his time with the Nuts & Bolts, Neil had a two month trial spell with West Bromwich Albion and turned out for their reserves. He made 28 appearances for Ashford and scored once before moving on to Folkestone & Shepway for the 1975/76 campaign.

He made over 100 appearances for Folkestone before being transferred to Margate in March 1978 for a then club record fee of £3,000. Neil made his debut in a 1-1 draw with Salisbury at Hartsdown Park on 11.3.78 and the Thanet Times said that he "made a considerable impact with his aerial dominance and gritty tackling". He then became a regular in the centre of Margate's defence during the remainder of the 1977/78 season and made a total of eight appearances, scoring once as Margate won the Southern League 1st Division (South) title. Neil's goal came in a 3-1 win at Trowbridge on 15.4.78.

He continued to be a fixture at centre-back during the 1978/79 campaign and Neil's consistent performances led to Football League scouts watching him regularly. However in March 1979 he moved to Dartford. The fee was undisclosed but believed to be in the region of £1,750 and Neil had made 39 appearances, scoring twice, before his departure.

He went on to make over 70 appearances for the Darts and played for the Southern League before joining Dover for a £3,000 fee prior to the start of the 1980/81 campaign. Dover midfielder Billy Fogarty also joined Dartford as part of the deal.

Early in 1982 Dover decided to try Neil as a centre-forward and he scored 13 goals before the end of the 1981/82 season, including one in a 2-1 win against Thanet United at Hartsdown on 20.3.82.

In the summer of 1982 he rejoined Folkestone and played exclusively as a striker during the 1982/83 campaign. Neil scored a record 46 goals, six of them against Thanet. He got two in a 2-2 draw at Hartsdown on 23.10.82 and scored four as Folkestone thrashed United 8-0 on 27.10.82.

Neil continued to be a prolific scorer during the 1983/84 and 1984/85 campaigns and again fared well in matches against Thanet. He scored in a 4-1 win at Hartsdown on 10.1.84 and then found the net six times in games against United during the 1984/85 season. Neil bagged two in a 5-1 Southern League Cup win at Cheriton Road on 22.8.84 and scored two more in the return tie at Hartsdown on 25.9.84 as Folkestone won 3-1. He also scored one each in Folkestone's FA Trophy and Kent Senior Cup wins over Thanet at Cheriton - 6-2 on 20.10.84 and 2- 0 on 26.3.85 respectively. In total he scored 32 goals up to April 1985.

Neil was then signed by Gola League Maidstone and he made five appearances for the Stones before the end of the season, scoring once. At the start of the 1985/86 campaign he found it hard to gain a regular first team place and towards the end of September 1985 Neil joined Thanet on loan, shortly after making a one-off appearance on loan at Folkestone. United manager John Wickens said "once he settles I am sure he will score many goals for us" and added "at the moment he is suffering from lack of match practice because Maidstone have such a big squad".

Neil made his first appearance for Thanet in a 4-0 defeat at Salisbury on 28.9.85 and on 1.10.85 he made his home debut, scoring what the Isle of Thanet Gazette called a "streaky" goal as United lost 3-1 to Sheppey in a Southern League Cup tie. Neil's low 30 yard shot bounced in front of the Sheppey keeper who then fumbled it, allowing the ball to spin into the net. He scored once more, in a 2-1 defeat at Chatham on 8.10.85, before returning to Maidstone having made a total of six appearances.

In December 1985 Neil left Maidstone and rejoined Dover, by then known as Dover Athletic. He'd scored five goals in 13 games for the Stones up to that point of the season. He started his second spell at Dover in great style, scoring eight goals in his first six matches for the club and Neil scored in all six of those games. One of them was Dover's 3-1 win at Thanet on 26.12.85 and Neil also scored as Dover drew 2-2 with United at Crabble in an Eastern Floodlight Cup tie on 28.1.86.

In January 1987 Neil left Dover and joined Thanet on a permanent basis, following his striker partner Frank Ovard from Crabble in an expensive double swoop by United. He'd also played alongside Ovard at Folkestone and Maidstone. The first game of Neil's third spell at Hartsdown was a 0-0 draw with Chatham on 24.1.87 and the Thanet Times reported that he was "given few chances to shine". After a 3-1 home defeat at the hands of Hastings took Neil's goalless start to three games he was switched to central defence by John Wickens. The Thanet Times report for the Hastings game had said that Neil "made little impression" up front. His first game in defence was a 0-0 draw at Canterbury on 14.2.87 and Neil's next two appearances were also as a defender.

When Wickens was sacked in March 1987 Neil was immediately restored to the frontline by temporary player-manager Norman Fusco. Although Thanet's form improved Neil still couldn't find the net and his difficult spell continued when he was fined a week's wages by Fusco for turning out for Hythe, along with Ovard, in a Kent League match at Herne Bay on 28.3.87 without permission. Although not under contract with United the players failed to tell Fusco of their intentions, prompting him to say "what they did was morally wrong....they were out of order in simply going off to play for Hythe".

By the time Thanet entertained Canterbury in a Southern League game at Hartsdown on 7.4.87 Neil had made 12 appearances without scoring and before the evening game kicked off some supporters unfurled a banner reading "Cugley must go !". He answered his critics in the best possible way, finally breaking his duck with two goals in a 4-1 win, and Neil then embarked on a scoring spree. He scored six goals in Thanet's remaining four games, finding the net in each one, and rounded off the season by scoring twice in a 5-0 win over Poole at Hartsdown on 25.4.87. One of Neil's goals was a deft lob and his partner Ovard bagged a hat-trick. He finished the season with a record of eight goals from 17 appearances, an excellent return after such a slow start.

Neil carried his goalscoring form into the 1987/88 campaign, scoring both goals in United's 2-0 win at Hounslow on 22.8.87, the opening day of the season, and adding another in a 2-2 draw at Folkestone a few days later. He then took his tally to six goals in his first three games when he scored a hat-trick of headers in a 3-0 win over Canterbury in an FA Cup tie at Hartsdown on 29.8.87. It was Neil's first treble for the club. Norman Fusco said that his third goal was "magnificent" and the Thanet Times rightly said that he'd had "a superb start to the season". By then it had become clear that Frank Ovard had left the club and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that he "had not been missed" by Neil who the paper referred to as being Frank's "sparring partner". Fusco said "Neil has taken on more responsibility without Frank and it has done him good."

Neil carried on scoring throughout the early months of the campaign and the Gazette praised him for being "industrious". From 28.11.87 to 26.12.87 inclusive he found the net in seven consecutive matches, a run that brought him 12 goals. On 1.12.87 Neil scored four times in an 8-0 win over Chatham at Hartsdown, becoming the first Thanet player to score more than three goals in a game. The last Margate player to manage the feat had been John O'Mara way back in February 1978. Four days after the Chatham match United took on Poole in another home game and Neil bagged another hat-trick in a 4-2 win, lashing in a 25-yarder to complete his treble. It had been almost thirty years since a Margate / Thanet player had scored back-to-back hat-tricks, Freddie Kearns had been the last player to do so in October 1958. Later in December the Gazette ran an article headlined "Marksman Cugley United's rare gem" and Neil's full-length diving header in a 2-0 win at home to Bury on 19.12.87 was described as "a goal of stunning excellence" by the Thanet Times. On 13.2.88 Neil broke Vic Medus' Thanet record for goals in a season when he hit the target for the 25th time during a 2-1 win over Corinthian at Hartsdown. On 2.3.88 Neil took his tally to 27 in a 2-1 defeat at home to Waterlooville and the Gazette said it was "a typical opportunist strike" that "nearly blasted a hole in the net". It turned out to be his last goal for Thanet.

A few days after playing in a 0-0 draw at Corinthian on 8.3.88 Neil left the club in sensational circumstances. The Thanet Times ran a headline of "United sack Cugley for disloyalty" whilst the Adscene went with "Star played sacked". The Times article said that Neil had been "dramatically dismissed" after an emergency board meeting had been convened. United chairman Alan Edmonds explained "we expressed dissatisfaction at recent press reports linking Cugley with Hythe. It is understood that he has accepted the role of player-manager with them and due to his disloyalty to Thanet he has been dismissed." The Thanet board were upset because Hythe, Neil's hometown club, had not made a formal approach for him and negotiations had not involved United at all. The Isle of Thanet Gazette reported that Norman Fusco "fully endorsed the board's decision" and he told the paper "we released him from any ties with us because of his untimely connection with Hythe." Fusco went on to say "we feel he has shown no loyalty either to me or the club and United wish to make it clear we are not here to be used by Cugley or anyone else." Neil had been the highest-paid player on United's books and he had been ever-present up until his untimely departure, making 41 appearances to take his overall tally for the club past 100.

Neil began his new job at Hythe immediately after leaving Thanet and tasted instant success as the club, backed by millionaire Tony Walton, won the 1988/89 Kent League championship at a canter, gaining promotion to the Southern League. However in November 1989 Neil was sacked and he rejoined Folkestone, becoming their player-coach. On 26.1.89 he ironically scored for them in a 3-1 defeat at Hythe.

Early in 1990 Neil took over as Folkestone's player-manager and continued in the role until becoming Ashford's manager for the 1990/91 season. He combined the role with playing up until the end of the 1994/95 campaign and made 97 appearances (28 as sub), scoring seven goals. Neil s last appearance for Ashford was in a 5-2 win at Witney on 6.5.95 and he was 38 by then. He eventually took charge of 399 games as manager of the club.

In the summer of 1997 Neil went back to Folkestone as manager and it turned out to be the start of a very long spell at the helm. In October 2004 Folkestone entertained Gillingham in a joint testimonial match for Neil and former Margate manager Denis Hunt who was on Invicta's coaching staff at the time. The 2006/07 campaign was Neil's tenth season in charge at Folkestone and in December 2006 he reached the landmark of 500 competitive games as Invicta's manager. He was still in the hot seat at the start of the 2011/12 campaign and in November 2011 Neil took charge of his 750th game.

During the 2012/13 season he was heavily linked with the vacant manager s job at Margate following the departure of Chris Kinnear but Neil stayed at Folkestone and was still in charge there during 2013/14. In August 2013 he turned out for a Folkestone Legends team in a charity match to celebrate former Thanet player John Lineham s 50th birthday and a host of other former Margate / Thanet players were also involved in the game.

name: Brian Curtis
other clubs: Westgate Sports, Ramsgate, Deal Town and Herne Bay
bio:
Local keeper who started his career playing for Westgate in Thanet's junior leagues, appearing for them during the 1968/69 season.

Brian was turning out for Westgate Sports in the Kent Amateur League during the early part of the 1970/71 campaign and later in the season he had a spell with Ramsgate, playing a few games for their reserves.

During the 1975/76 campaign Brian had several outings for Margate Reserves.

He spent the 1977/78 season with Deal in the Kent League.

In the summer of 1978 Brian joined Margate as back-up keeper to Steve Bowtell and made his debut in an FA Cup 2nd Qualifying Round tie at Croydon on 7.10.78. Brian played against medical advice as he was recovering from three broken ribs. He then played in Margate's next two games but broke his elbow in October 1978.

Having recovered from his injury, Brian joined Ramsgate in December 1978 and became their first-choice keeper, making over 20 appearances before the end of the 1978/79 season. Brian stayed at Southwood for 1979/80 and made 43 appearances during the campaign. In an interview with the East Kent Times, Ramsgate s manager Bob Harrop said of Brian He s got to be one of the top six non-league goalkeepers in the country.

In the summer of 1980 Brian rejoined Deal and played alongside past / future Margate and Ramsgate players Marcus Newton and Vic Medus in their side that knocked Thanet United out of the FA Cup during the 1981/82 season.

Brian moved on to Herne Bay towards the end of the 1981/82 campaign.

He returned to Hartsdown Park in the summer of 1982 and was expected to become Thanet's first-choice keeper for the 1982/83 season. However Brian injured his back in a friendly at Deal in August 1982 and was out for a couple of months. By the time he'd recovered, youngster Craig Godden had established himself as first-choice and Brian left the club.

After his departure from Thanet, Brian rejoined Deal and was still there during the 1983/84 season. He made a total of 130 appearances for the club.

In the summer of 1989 Brian rejoined Ramsgate as cover for Bobby Miles and although he was firmly in the veteran category by that time, he made 29 appearances during 1989/90.

bio:

then player-coach at Chelmsford (joined Aug 1953) and made 102 appearances for City during 53/54 and 54/55
Sept 55 manager / coach England Youth 
then coached at Sunderland until became Brighton manager circa 1961 - on 23.9.61 Margate played Brighton Reserves in a friendly as a result of George's friendship with Almer Hall who he'd known in RAF during WWII. George was Brighton manager by then.. 
Qualified coach - managed Stevenage (from Aug 1963, straight after Brighton, to end of  66/67 - Stevenage played Margate a few times and Almer Hall was close freind) 
Hull coach after that, then Norway.  
Also coached Grays,  The Sudan and Norway (up to 1970's).. 
USA - managed San Diego Toros in North American Soccer League 1968 
Rosenborg head coach for parts of the club's first golden age - replaced Knut N ss as RBK's coach ahead of the 1969 season. His first meeting with the Rosenborg players is legendary: "This is a ball," Curtis stated whilst pointing to the round leather ball. "Don't go too fast, now!" Odd Iversen laughed. 
The 1969 debut season ended with a premiership title for RBK Curtis was allowed to continue for one more season. Despite placing second in the 1970 league, it was an anti-climax. Curtis went on home to England, but in 1972 he returned to Norway. This time to coach the national team He only got to lead Norway through 17 international matches before he was sacked.
Before the 1976 season, RBK needed a new coach. Club management decided to give George Curtis a second chance. Unfortunately, the Englishman was reduced following a car accident in which his Norwegian wife died, and Rosenborg quickly ended up struggling to avoid relagation. A 0-4 defeat against Division 3 side R ros in the 2nd round of the cup sealed his fate: Curtis was released from his contract.  
Later managed Qatari national team - in 1981, last coaching role. 
Died 17.11.04 aged 85.

name: Malcolm Dalrymple
other clubs: Luton Town (0), Cambridge United, Bristol Rovers (8,0), Watford (5,0), Hendon, Southport, Colne Dynamoes, Pendle Forest, Nelson, Accrington Stanley and Padiham Wanderers
bio:
6 1 tall, agile keeper born in Bedford who started his career with Luton, joining the club as an amateur in September 1968. During the 1969/70 season Malcolm won three caps for the England Youth team whilst on the Hatters books and in the summer of 1970 he was given a professional contract by Luton. Malcolm then almost immediately joined Margate on a 12 month loan. Luton felt a season of Southern League football would be good experience for him although Coventry were also interested in Malcolm.

He made his debut for Margate in the opening game of the 1970/71 campaign - a 3-0 win at Telford in the Southern League on 15.8.70. Malcolm went on to make a total of 46 appearances during the season. There were spells where he fell out of favour, most notably towards the end of the season when Allen Clarke joined the club on loan from Charlton, but generally Malcolm did well and displayed safe handling and bravery. He managed to save four penalties during the season, including a run of three in a row, and turned in a brilliant display in Margate's 1-0 win at Herne Bay in the FA Cup on 7.11.70. On 21.11.70 he played as Margate lost 2-0 at Dagenham in the FA Cup 1st Round.

At the end of the season Malcolm returned to Kenilworth Road and was then released by Luton.

He moved to Cambridge United on trial in August 1971 and then joined Bristol Rovers in October 1971, initially on trial.

Malcolm quickly earned himself a full-time deal with Rovers and made eight first team appearances before his contract was cancelled by mutual consent on 31.3.73. He didn t see eye-to-eye with manager Don Megson and was left without a club for several months. During that time Malcolm moved to Burnley where his fianc lived and he worked as a machine knitter in a factory. At the end of June 1973 he was interviewed by the Bristol Evening Post and said I earned myself a full contract with Rovers after joining them as a trialist and I can do the same elsewhere. I have confidence in myself but feel I suffered at Eastville because the manager didn t have much faith in me.

In July 1973 Malcolm returned to football when he was signed by Watford and he made five appearances for the Hornets during 1973/74 but they were the last Football League matches he played in.

During the 1975/76 and 1976/77 seasons, Malcolm was with Isthmian League club Hendon and by then he was working for a printing company in the town. In a November 1975 interview Malcolm said I don t want full-time football, I m enjoying my game more than I ever have. It s like a hobby now. All the pressures are gone - and I m a better player for it. Malcolm made a total of 105 appearances for Hendon.

He linked up with Southport for the 1978/79 campaign, their first in the Northern Premier League after relegation from the Football League. He made 15 appearances during the season.

Malcolm joined Lancashire Combination club Colne Dynamoes for the 1979/80 campaign and went on to spend several seasons with the club. On 13.2.82 Malcolm was sent off for comments made to the referee in a game against Caernarfon and moments earlier, he d saved a penalty. He was still with Colne during the 1983/84 campaign.

Malcolm later had short stints with Pendle Forest, Nelson and Accrington Stanley.

By the 1986/87 season he was playing for Padiham Wanderers in the North West Counties Football League and Malcolm finished his career with them, retiring at the end of the 1990/91 campaign aged 39.

In later years he worked as long distance lorry driver and continued to live in Lancashire.

His father, also named Malcolm, was a successful javelin thrower and competed for Great Britain in the 1948 Olympics. He also played football for clubs including Bedford Avenue. Malcolm s grandfather Jock Dalrymple had also been a javelin thrower and Olympian - competing in the 1924 Olympics.

name: Daniel Damoah
other clubs: Cove, Bedfont, Egham Town, Kingsbury Town, Redhill and Walton & Hersham
bio:
Tall defender born in Accra, Ghana who started his career with Combined Counties League club Cove during the 2003/04 season.

Daniel joined Bedfont, also of the Combined Counties League, for the start of the 2004/05 campaign and made five appearances there before signing for Southern League outfit Egham in September 2004.

He made his debut for Egham in a 5-2 defeat at Swindon Supermarine on 25.9.04 and in only his third outing for the club Daniel was sent off as Egham lost 4-0 at Mangotsfield. He made around 30 appearances during 2004/05.

Daniel started the 2005/06 season with Isthmian League Division 2 club Kingsbury and also turned out for amateur club Kennington who were a Ghanaian team based in the London Borough of Lambeth. In September 2005 Daniel captained them to victory in a gala tournament held in London for all the city's Ghanaian football teams.

In October 2005 he made a one-off appearance for Redhill as they lost 3-1 at Ash in a Surrey Senior Cup 1st Round tie but Daniel then returned to Kingsbury. He'd made 17 league appearances there (two as sub) before joining Margate in February 2006.

Daniel made his debut as a substitute in a 2-1 win at AFC Wimbledon in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 11.2.06 and also came on in a 4-0 win over Wealdstone at Northwood on 25.2.06 before leaving the club shortly afterwards.

After a spell out of the game Daniel resurfaced at Walton & Hersham in January 2007 and he had three Isthmian League Premier Division outings there before dropping out of senior football.

His date of birth may have been 6th December 1985.

name: Terry Dann
other clubs: Penzance, Plymouth Argyle (8,0), Sittingbourne, Torquay United (2,0) and Canterbury City
bio:
Attacking player born in Finsbury, London who was evacuated to Penzance in Cornwall aged five and started his senior football career with Penzance during the 1956/57 campaign. They won the South Western League that season. He featured alongside his brother Nat for Penzance and during his time with the club Terry played for Cornwall several times.

On 9.5.57, Terry made a guest appearance for Plymouth as they lost 6-3 at home to Exeter in a friendly match and in July 1959 the Second Division club signed him as a professional.

Terry went on to make eight first team appearances for Plymouth during 1959/60 but then dropped into non-league football and joined Sittingbourne in the summer of 1961. On 6.1.62 he scored a brilliant solo goal in a 5-3 home win over Margate, weaving past three defenders before firing home. He was also on target as the Brickies drew 1-1 at Margate on 27.1.62.

Terry returned to the Football League in July 1962 when he was signed by Torquay but only played twice for the senior side before joining Margate for a fee of £400 in February 1963 - a club record at the time. Corby had also been after Terry's services.

Margate manager Almer Hall told the local press We have made a jolly good capture after five weeks negotiation. We have the supporters club to thank for providing the bulk of the money and now we hope local fans will rally round and show practical appreciation of a progressive committee, who have scraped the bottom of our financial barrel to find the transfer fee. Terry was one of the best inside-forwards in the Southern League last season. Several clubs were after him but he elected to come to Margate because he likes the team style and the club s facilities. He is single and will live in Margate."

Terry made his debut for Margate in 2-2 draw at Burton on 2.3.63 and made a favourable impression with his deft ball control and passing ability. Terry was described as an "arch schemer" and a player of "great potential" by the local press. He went on to make a total of 31 appearances as an inside-forward during the remainder of the 1962/63 season as Margate won the Southern League Division One title, scoring nine times in the process. On 7.5.63 he played as Margate won 2-0 at Maidstone in the 1st Leg of the Kent Floodlight Cup Final and Terry also featured in the 2nd Leg at Hartsdown Park on 13.5.63 which Margate won 3-0 to claim the trophy. On 1.6.63 he was in the team that beat visitors Bexleyheath & Welling 1-0 in the Kent Senior Shield Final.

During the 1963/64 season Terry made a further 45 appearances, mostly as an inside-forward but sometimes as a winger, and scored six times. His goals included a 25 yard drive in a 3-3 draw at Hereford on 2.11.63. On 16.11.63 he played as Margate drew 2-2 at Brentford in the FA Cup 1st Round and then on 20.11.63 Terry featured in the replay at Hartsdown Park that the Bees won 2-0.

On 18.1.64 he scored with a brilliant solo effort in a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Chelmsford, beating three defenders before firing home. He gained praise for his hard work during the season but in his weekly Thanet Times column former Margate captain Davie Laing pointed out what he saw as a problem with Terry's style of play. Davie said that Terry had "an infuriating habit of running all over the place with the ball, instead of making the ball do the work".

Terry struggled to gain a regular place at the start of the 1964/65 season and in November 1964 he was sold to Canterbury. He'd made just nine appearances for Margate during the first three months of the campaign.

Terry went on to make 70 Southern League appearances for Canterbury during the 1964/65 and 1965/66 seasons. He scored 27 goals in those matches and Terry's tally included one in a 4-1 home win over Margate in a Kent Floodlight League game on 26.1.65. He also scored four goals in a 10-0 win over Deal on 30.1.65 - City's all-time record victory. He left Canterbury in the summer of 1966 and returned home to Cornwall.

Terry then spent two seasons as a player with his old club Penzance before having a spell as the club's manager. The Dann family had a long connection with Penzance and a stand at their ground was named after former club president Jimmy Dann whilst two of Terry s nephews also played for Penzance.

In 2012 Terry was living in Newlyn near Penzance.

name: Dave Danson
other clubs: West Ham United (0), AFC Bournemouth (0), Cardiff City (Wales) (0), Leytonstone-Ilford, Dagenham, Heybridge Swifts and Basildon United
bio:
Romford-born keeper who kept goal for Essex Schools whilst attending Moulsham Secondary Modern School in Chelmsford and won seven caps for the England Schoolboys team during the 1971/72 campaign. Dave's international team-mates included Ray Wilkins, Trevor Ross, Clive Walker and Wilf Rostron. Dave was also part of the Chelmsford Boys side coached by former Margate player Ron Smillie that won the English Schools Trophy in May 1972.

In August 1972 Dave joined West Ham as an apprentice and he played regularly in the Hammers' youth team during the 1972/73 and 1973/74 seasons. During 1974/75 he was a member of the side that lost to Ipswich in the FA Youth Cup Final and Dave also made four reserve team appearances during the campaign.

In November 1975 Dave joined Margate on a month's loan to cover for the injured Steve Bowtell and he also had a trial for the England Youth team during the month. He made his debut for Margate on 15.11.75 in a 3-0 win over Bromley in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park and went on to make a total of five appearances before returning to Upton Park. Dave saved a penalty in a 1-1 draw at Tonbridge on 29.11.75.

During the remainder of 1975/76, Dave continued to play in West Ham's youth team and towards the end of the season he made numerous appearances in the reserves. He stayed with the Hammers for the 1976/77 campaign and on 26.2.77 Dave made a return to Hartsdown Park when he kept goal for West Ham's reserve team in a friendly against Margate. In the summer of 1977 he was released having never made a first team appearance.

Dave later had spells with Bournemouth and Cardiff before dropping into non-league football.

He played for Leytonstone-Ilford during the 1979/80 and 1980/81 seasons and then joined Dagenham in August 1981. Dave left the Daggers at the end of the 1981/82 campaign.

He joined Heybridge Swifts for the 1982/83 season and Dave stayed with the club until the end of the 1984/85 campaign.

He later had a spell in charge of Basildon United that included the 1988/89 season. In September 1988 Dave came out of retirement, although he was only 31, to play for Basildon in an FA Cup tie at home to Barking and saved a penalty in a 3-2 defeat. Dave was sacked by Basildon at the start of December 1988.

name: Wayne Davey
bio:
Local player who turned out for Sunday side Margate Athletic before joining Thanet United for the 1987/88 season. Wayne became a regular in the reserves during the campaign.

He stayed with United for 1988/89 and made 11 appearances without scoring for the reserves during the season, sometimes playing alongside his brother Jason. Wayne also made a handful of first team appearances, making his senior debut on 12.11.88 when he came on as a substitute during Thanet's 6-2 defeat at Tonbridge. He played twice more as a sub in the weeks that followed and then made his first start in a 6-2 defeat at Witney on 28.1.89. Player-manager Garry Aldous said that Wayne's performance in midfield had been "quite pleasing". He then returned to the reserves for a lengthy spell before playing from the start as Thanet were thrashed 5-0 at Sheppey on 1.5.89. It was Wayne's last first team game and he left the club at the end of the season having made five appearances, three of them as a substitute. Wayne joined the Royal Navy towards the end of his time at Hartsdown and in 2005 he was living in Maidstone.

name: Norman Davidson
other clubs: 25th Old Boys (Scotland), Chelsea (0), Inverurie Locos (Scotland), Aberdeen (Scotland) (147,79), Heart of Midlothian (Scotland) (58,29), Dundee United (Scotland) (9,3), Partick Thistle (Scotland) (10,2),St.Mirren (Scotland) (1,0) and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
Much-travelled, 5' 7" tall Scottish centre-forward who was especially good in the air.

Norman began his career in Scottish amateur football with 25th Old Boys before being transferred to Chelsea in October 1951. After a short spell at Stamford Bridge he returned to Scotland and joined Highland League club Inverurie Locos.

In February 1955 Norman was signed by Aberdeen and he made his first team debut for the club during the 1955/56 season. He scored five goals from only nine appearances during the campaign. During the 1957/58 season Norman was picked for Scotland s Under-23 team for a match against the Netherlands at Tynecastle but had to withdraw due to injury. The game took place on 23.10.57.

He eventually played almost 150 games during a five year spell with Aberdeen and maintained a strike rate of better than a goal every other game. In 1959 he was a member of the Dons team beaten by St.Mirren in the Scottish Cup Final at Hampden Park.

In February 1961 Norman moved on to Hearts and although never quite establishing himself as a first team regular he kept up a good strike rate, scoring 29 goals in his 58 games for the club that spanned the 1960/61-1963/64 seasons. The highlight of Norman's time at Tynecastle came on 27.10.62 when he scored the goal that won the Scottish League Cup for Hearts as they beat Kilmarnock 1-0 at Hampden. The previous year, on 18.12.61, Norman had been part of the Hearts side that had lost 3-1 to Rangers in the Final and he had the distinction of scoring Hearts' goal.

Norman's successful spell in Edinburgh ended in November 1963 when he was transferred to Dundee United but he failed to settle there and after making just a handful of appearances he moved on once again.

In February 1964 he signed for Partick Thistle but Norman struggled to make an impact there and towards the end of the 1964/65 season he moved on once more. His next port of call was St.Mirren but Norman only made one senior appearance for the club before being released in April 1965.

After a few months out of the game, Norman joined Margate on a month's trial in September 1965. He was recommended to Margate by former Derby County player Jack Stamps whilst Margate s Laurie Thomson had also sung Norman s praises to Almer Hall, he knew Norman from his years playing in Scotland. Manager Almer Hall told the East Kent Times The Scottish FA have waived the transfer fee on Davidson who could add tremendous punch to Margate s forward line if he is as good as I have heard. I understand he is exceptionally good in the air.

Norman made his debut on 18.9.65 in a 1-1 draw with Hereford at Hartsdown Park and displayed deft ball control and accurate passing. However after making three further appearances without scoring he was released.

Norman immediately joined Ramsgate and on 30.10.65, in only his second outing, he scored both goals in a 2-0 win at Stevenage in the Southern League. Norman later scored for the Rams as they drew 2-2 with visitors Margate in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie on 1.2.66 and on 10.3.66 he was sent off in a 2-1 win at Erith & Belvedere in the Kent Senior Cup. He stayed with Ramsgate for the start of the 1966/67 season but left the club early in the campaign and returned to Scotland to play in the Highland League once more.

Whilst playing in Scotland, Norman ran a fish and chip shop and he was known as 'Norrie', rather than Norman, during his career north of the border.

He ended his playing career with a spell in South Africa and Norman later settled back in Edinburgh where he worked for Lothian Buses for many years.

He died on 20.11.22 aged 88 after a long battle with dementia.

name: Tom Davie
other clubs: Dagenham & Redbridge (0), Hendon, Harlow Town and Barkingside
bio:
5 10" tall product of Dagenham & Redbridge s academy system who progressed through the club s ranks to the fringes of the first team by the 2011/12 campaign. During that season Tom was loaned to Hendon where he made three appearances (two as sub) in the Isthmian League Premier Division without scoring.

In June 2012 he was given a professional contract by the Daggers who were in League Two at the time and in October 2012 Tom was sent out on loan once more.

He joined Isthmian League Division 1 North outfit Harlow and played regularly there before going back to Dagenham in January 2013.

In March 2013 Tom joined Margate on loan at the same time as his Daggers team-mate Andrew Burns and he made his debut as a substitute in a 2-2 draw with Canvey Island in an Isthmian League Premier Division game at Hartsdown Park on 23.3.13. Tom also featured as a sub in Margate s next two matches before starting for the first time in midfield in a 4-0 win over Cray at Bromley on 1.4.13. He kept his place for a 4-0 defeat at Carshalton on 6.4.13 but Tom then only appeared once as a substitute in Margate s next three games.

He returned to the starting line-up in a 2-1 home defeat against Kingstonian on 16.4.13 and Tom then started two of the next three matches. His last outing came in a 0-0 draw with Harrow at Hartsdown Park on 27.4.13 - the final day of the 2012/13 campaign - and Tom finished the season having made a total of nine appearances (four as sub) without scoring.

In May 2013 he was released by Dagenham & Redbridge having never featured in their senior side.

Early in September 2013 Tom joined Isthmian League Division 1 North club Barkingside.

name: Craig Davies
other clubs: Morecambe, Lancaster City, Gap Connah's Quay (Wales), Burscough, Vauxhall Motors, Newtown (Wales), Prescott Cables, Stalybridge Celtic, Warrington Town, St Albans City, Leatherhead, Horsham, Hampton & Richmond Borough and New Orleans Jesters (USA)
bio:
5' 10" tall attacker born in Whiston, Merseyside who started his career with Morecambe during the club s time in the Conference before moving on to Lancaster.

In July 2008 Craig joined Welsh Premier League outfit Gap Connah's Quay but picked up an injury in a pre-season friendly which hampered his spell with the club.

In November 2008 Craig had trials with AFC Bournemouth and then Welsh club The New Saints before linking up with Burscough of the Conference North.

He scored once from four league outings for Burscough and in December 2008 Craig got two goals in a 4-1 home win over Everton in the Liverpool Senior Cup.

In the summer of 2009 he played in some friendlies for Witton but Craig ended up starting the 2009/10 campaign with Vauxhall Motors where he made five appearances without scoring before leaving the club.

After a spell out of senior football Craig joined Newtown in August 2010 and he scored twice from 14 outings (seven as sub) for the Welsh Premier League club before being released in November 2010.

He then had a short spell with Northern League Division 1 North outfit Prescott Cable and in December 2010 Craig signed for Stalybridge.

He went on to make ten appearances (nine as sub) in all competitions for the Conference North club and scored once before being loaned to Warrington in March 2011.

Craig spent the last few weeks of 2010/11 with Warrington and at the end of the season he was released by Stalybridge.

In the summer of 2011 he joined Southern League Premier Division club St Albans after featuring in several friendlies for them but Craig only played twice (once as sub) before moving on to Leatherhead before the end of August 2011.

He scored twice from four Isthmian League Premier Division outings (one as sub) for Leatherhead and then in October 2011 Craig signed for Horsham.

He scored once from seven Premier Division appearances (two as sub) for the Sussex outfit and also got an FA Cup goal before moving on to Margate in December 2011.

Craig made his debut as a substitute in a 3-1 home defeat against Metropolitan Police in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 17.12.11 and after sitting out Margate s next match he came off the bench again in a 3-1 win at Aveley on 31.12.11. Craig also featured as a sub in a 4-1 win over Hastings at Hartsdown Park on 2.1.12 but that was his final appearance. Later in January 2012 he joined Conference South club Hampton & Richmond on a dual-registration basis but in early February 2012 Craig was released by Margate.

Not long after leaving Hartsdown Park Craig moved to America and in May 2012 he signed for New Orleans Jesters of the USL Premier Development League, the fourth tier of the American Soccer Pyramid. The club played in the Mid South Division of the Southern Conference and in one of his first outings Craig was sent off in a match against El Paso. He scored twice from eight appearances for the Jesters before leaving the club in July 2012.

By the start of 2013 Craig was back in England and working as a coach at Queens Park Rangers. He d previously coached at Bolton.

name: Ray Dawes
other clubs: Birchington
bio:
Thanet-born winger who played for Birchington in the Kent Amateur League and for Margate Athletic in the Thanet Premier Sunday League before joining Margate as a teenager during the 1972/73 season. Ray played regularly for the reserves and also made a one-off appearance for the first team, playing on the left wing as Margate went down 6-0 in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie at Hastings on 15.11.72. He was only 16 at the time of the match.

Ray continued to play locally for over 20 years and was turning out for Thanet Works League club Chauffeur Hire during the 1991/92 season. By 1993/94 he was playing for Thanet League side Ruby Lounge.

In 2014 Ray was living in Knebworth, Hertfordshire.

His older brother Eric was on Ramsgate's books during the early 1970's and made occasional appearances in their first team.

name: Alec Dawkins
other clubs: Guildford FC, Guildford City, Crystal Palace (0), Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Sittingbourne and Dartford
bio:
5' 7" tall forward born in Guildford who played for the Guildford Sea Cadet Corps as a teenager during the 1944/45 season, helping them to win the Southern Area Sea Cadets Football Challenge Cup.

Alec then turned out for amateur club Guildford FC during 1948/49, making his debut for their reserves at the end of November 1948. He made his first senior appearance for Guildford as they beat visitors Carshalton 3-1 in a Surrey League game on 18.12.48.

Alec joined Southern League club Guildford City in August 1949 and played in their reserves in the London League throughout the 1949/50 season. Alec stayed with City for the 1950/51 campaign and on 16.9.50 he scored twice as they lost 5-2 in a friendly at Margate.

In the summer of 1951, Alec was signed by Crystal Palace as an amateur and he made six reserve team appearances for the Eagles early in the 1951/52 campaign.

In December 1951, Alec signed for Margate and made his debut in a 6-1 win over Bowaters Lloyd at Hartsdown Park on 8.12.51. In his next outing on 15.12.51 he scored a hat-trick in an 8-0 win at Bexleyheath & Welling. Alec went on to make a total of 13 appearances before the end of the 1951/52 season and scored five times in all.

In the summer of 1952 Alec left the club and joined Snowdown.

At the start of December 1952, he moved on to Sittingbourne and Alec played for the Brickies until linking up with Dartford in February 1954.

In the summer of 1956, Alec rejoined Sittingbourne and his second spell with the club lasted until the end of the 1956/57 season.

In later years Alec worked for Seeboard and in June 2020 he was still living in Guildford aged around 90 and celebrated his 70th wedding anniversary. Alec was residing in a care home at that time.

name: Ray Dean
other clubs: Reading (57+5,0), Aldershot (282,9), Cheltenham Town and Wokingham Town
bio:
Towering defender born in Steventon who began his career with Reading and made 62 first team appearances for the Royals during the period 1966/67-1968/69.

In July 1969 Ray moved to Aldershot and he went on to make over 280 senior appearances there before joining Margate in the summer of 1975.

Ray made his debut in a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Telford on 16.8.75, the opening day of the 1975/76 season. He went on to become a fixture in the side and Ray's outstanding displays at centre-back prompted the local press to compare him to the legendary Bob Harrop. His tough tackling and powers of distribution were key features of his game. The Thanet Times described Ray as being a "pillar of consistency" and his performance during a 2-0 win over Dulwich in an FA Trophy tie at Hartsdown Park on 10.1.76 won him further acclaim from the paper. He was said to have "stood out like a Colossus...calm, cool, collected and twice as solid as that famous Gibraltar rock".

On 24.4.76 Ray featured in the 2nd Leg of the Kent Floodlight Trophy Final against Canterbury at Hartsdown Park which the visitors won 2-1 after extra time. The result meant Margate took the trophy with a 3-2 aggregate win. He d scored twice from 55 outings when he left the club at the end of the season. Ray departed as it was becoming too expensive for Margate to pay his rail fares from his Hampshire home and he was also having difficulty getting time off work to play football. Ray had actually changed jobs four times during 1975/76 in an effort to solve the problem and manager Les Riggs said "I am extremely sorry to lose him."

In July 1976 Ray joined Cheltenham and he won the club's 'Player of the Year' award for the 1976/77 season. He made a total of 149 appearances and scored four goals before moving to Wokingham in July 1979.

In the early 2000's an Aldershot website said that Ray was believed to be working as a plasterer in Fleet, Hampshire.

In September 2009 he was Aldershot's guest for their 2-2 draw with Hereford in League Two - part of an ongoing scheme where former players were invited to home games.

name: Willie Deans

Back to Scotland end of 34/35, lived in Paisley at that time and trained with St Mirren summer 1935 whilst looking for a new club. Then joined Cowdenbeath on month's trial in August 1935, signed permanently after that. Joined Dumbarton May 1937

name: Eric Deed
bio:
Margate-born player who attended Chatham House school in Ramsgate and then worked in the treasurer s department of Broadstairs Council before the outbreak of the Second World War.

In 1941, Eric joined The Royal Norfolk Regiment before being transferred to The East Surrey Regiment which then became The Royal West Kent Regiment - known as The Queen s Own . Eric rose to the rank of Lieutenant during his service.

After hostilities ceased, Eric joined Margate for the 1946/47 season and became a regular in the reserve team. He was still a serving solider in The Royal West Kent Regiment at the time. Eric also played a handful of first team games, making his debut up front as Margate thrashed Snowdown 5-1 in a Kent League match at Hartsdown Park on 16.11.46. Eric scored a solo goal to mark the occasion. He then made four further appearances without scoring before leaving the club due to his army unit being posted overseas.

Eric later returned to Hartsdown Park and played for the reserves during the first half of the 1950/51 season, mainly as a centre-back, before departing again in January 1951. His unit was posted to Malaya where British forces were fighting the Malayan National Liberation Army (MNLA) during a conflict that was known as the Malayan Emergency . A piece in the programme for Eric s last reserve match said "A better club man never put on football boots and a cleaner player never kicked a ball. The sports world has all too few such men".

During his time in Malaya, Eric rose to the rank of Captain in The Queen s Own and was acting Company Commander when he was killed on the New Caledonia Estate, Batu Arang on 22.10.51. Eric was 28 years-old and died instantly when the vehicle he was travelling in at the head of a convoy was ambushed by the MNLA. A further ten British soldiers were also killed at the scene, whilst another later died of his wounds. Eric was buried at Cheras Road Christian Cemetery in Kuala Lumpur.

On 27.10.51, a minute s silence was observed in Eric s honour as Margate took on Dover in a Kent League match at Hartsdown Park.

Although known as Eric, his first name was actually Edward. He was a keen chess player who played in tournaments as a youngster and kept a miniature chess set in his kit during his time in the Army.

name: Hasim Deen
other clubs: Gambia Ports Authority (Gambia), Bakau United (Gambia), Fisher Athletic (London), Dulwich Hamlet, Stevenage Borough, St Albans City, Ware, Curzon Ashton and Tooting & Mitcham United
bio:
Strong 5' 9" tall defensively-minded player born in Bakau, Gambia who started his career with Gambia Ports Authority as a youngster before joining Bakau United. Hasim played for Gambia's Under-17 and Under-21 sides before moving to England in 2004.

He had spells with Fisher and Dulwich during the 2004/05 season and in the summer of 2005 Hasim signed for Margate.

He made his debut in midfield in a 2-0 defeat at Ramsgate in a match played for the Kent Messenger Cup on 13.8.05 and became a fixture in the Margate side for the next few months. The Thanet Times said Hasim "shackled danger man (Steve) Hafner" as Margate beat Maldon 1-0 at Hartsdown Park in their first Isthmian League Premier Division game on 20.8.05 and in its report on a 0-0 home draw with Redbridge on 29.8.05 the paper said of Hasim "he tackles well, heads well and is not afraid to shoot".

On 6.9.05 he played as a centre-back for the first time as Margate drew 1-1 with Fisher at Hartsdown Park and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Hasim slotted "effortlessly" into the defence. The paper also wrote "few would dispute that Chris Kinnear has found a gem" and around that time the Margate manager compared Hasim to former star defender Sam Sodje.

In its report on a 2-2 draw with visitors Slough on 17.9.05 the Thanet Times said Hasim was "very clever at conceding fouls which won't get him booked" but on 29.10.05 he was sent off in a 1-0 defeat at Braintree after reacting badly to a dangerous tackle. After playing in a 3-2 home defeat against Bromley in the Isthmian League Cup on 8.11.05 Hasim had to serve a three match ban.

His suspension coincided with a call-up to the Gambian Under-23 squad for the 2005 Amilcar Cabral Cup held in Conakry, Guinea during November 2005. Hasim was one of five foreign-based players called up for the tournament for Western African nations and former Bakau United head coach Ebrima Jallow told the Daily Observer newspaper "Hasim played under me at Bakau United at a very tender age. He was a regular player in the team before his departure to the United Kingdom. Before joining Bakau United, Hasim was a trainee at Gambia Ports Authority." Jallow described him as "a young promising player, who has the potential to feature in big clubs in the near future." Unfortunately Gambia's Under-23's lost both their group matches - to Mali's full international side and Senegal's Under-23's - to finish bottom of the table.

After missing four games Hasim returned to the Margate side when he came on as a substitute in a match at East Thurrock on 3.12.05. He headed his first goal for the club from an Anthony Allman free-kick but Margate lost 3-1. Hasim was back in the starting line-up as Margate lost 2-0 at Heybridge on 6.12.05 and he then enjoyed another good run in the team, usually playing in midfield.

On 14.1.06 Margate took on Staines at Hartsdown Park and after 41 minutes debutant goalkeeper Billy McMahon was stretchered off with a knee injury. By then Margate were 3-0 down and with no sub keeper on the bench Hasim volunteered to take over in goal. He did well although Staines ended up winning 5-2 and the Thanet Times said Hasim "made a couple of decent saves and had his every touch cheered". He told the Kentish Football website "I really thought I could make a difference...I used to play as a goalkeeper when I was young but I got discouraged because of my height."

Hasim scored his second goal for Margate with a thumping header from a Greg Oates corner in a 2-1 home win over East Thurrock on 4.2.06 but he then missed the next two matches. He returned as a sub in a 1-1 draw with Braintree at Hartsdown Park on 18.2.06 and the Thanet Times said Hasim had "added real bite to the Margate midfield" after replacing Pat Gradley 20 minutes into the game. Hasim then featured in the next three matches, once as a sub, but after a 1-0 home defeat against AFC Wimbledon on 7.3.06 he sat out four games due to a groin injury.

Hasim made his comeback in a 1-1 draw with Windsor & Eton at Hartsdown Park on 4.4.06 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "looked strong on his return". He then wore the number five shirt in a match at Hampton & Richmond on 8.4.06 but had to go off due to injury as Margate won 1-0. That turned out to be Hasim's final outing for the club and he missed the last four games of the season. He'd scored twice from a total of 36 appearances (three as sub).

In July 2006 Hasim was transfer-listed at his own request and new player-manager Robin Trott told the Thanet Times "He's got a few things happening and decided he wants to go, so he's on the list. I was going to keep him but I don't want anyone who doesn't want to be at the club. How many times was he injured last year ? I think it's a blessing in disguise. I'm not bothered. I'm pleased he's going."

Towards the end of August 2006 Hasim joined Conference club Stevenage on trial before a formal loan deal was agreed in September, initially for a month. His loan spell was later extended to a second month and then a third and on 2.12.06 Hasim made his first start for Stevenage as they took on Oxford United at Broadhall Way. It was a memorable debut as he was sent off inside the first half hour following a mass brawl on the pitch. In January 2007 he finally joined Stevenage on a permanent basis after they paid Margate an undisclosed fee for his services but Hasim was released at the end of the 2006/07 campaign. He'd made a total of eight appearances for Stevenage but only one of them had been a start - the Oxford game he was sent off in.

In the summer of 2007 Hasim had trials at Leicester and Luton before signing for Conference South club St Albans in time for the start of the 2007/08 campaign. He went on to make 37 appearances (five as sub) and scored twice but left the club at the end of season as he couldn't train as often as the St Albans manager required him to.

After a few months out of football Hasim linked up with Isthmian League Division 1 North outfit Ware in December 2008. Their squad included former Margate players Tamba Ngongou and Osman Sesay but Hasim only made one sub appearance before leaving the club.

After another spell out of the game Hasim was reported as having signed for Sutton in June 2009 but the move fell through when he relocated to the north of England and he ended up joining Northern League Division 1 North side Curzon Ashton for the 2009/10 campaign.

In June 2010 Hasim returned to the Isthmian League Premier Division when he signed for Tooting & Mitcham and he captained them during 2010/11. Hasim scored once from 32 league outings before leaving the club at the end of the season and dropping out of senior football.

name: Terry Dempsey
other clubs: West Ham United (0), Brentwood Town, Southend United, Folkestone, Grays Athletic, Canterbury City, Wealdstone and Guildford City
bio:
Keeper who started his career with West Ham and played regularly in the Hammers' Southern Counties and Metropolitan League sides during the second half of the 1967/68 campaign. Terry also had a trial with Coventry during the season.

In April 1968 Terry joined Margate on a trial basis as a 19 year-old and played in a 6-0 win at Ashford in the Kent Floodlight League on 4.4.68. Although he did well it was his only first team appearance and he returned to Upton Park. Terry then had a loan spell with Brentwood before being released by West Ham at the end of the season.

He joined Southend on trial in the summer of 1969 and on 4.11.69 Terry played for Folkestone on trial as they beat visitors Deal 1-0 in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie. The Kentish Express report on the match said Dempsey, on this showing, did not impress with his kicking and is perhaps a little on the short side.

At the end of December 1969 Folkestone signed Terry on a permanent basis and he made a total of 13 appearances before finishing the 1969/70 campaign with Grays Athletic.

Terry returned to Folkestone for the start of the 1970/71 season and made 28 appearances before moving to Canterbury halfway through the campaign.

Terry went on to make 15 Southern League appearances for City before leaving the club in the summer of 1971.

He signed for Wealdstone ahead of the 1971/72 campaign and made his first team debut for them in a 5-1 home win over Southall on 16.11.71. In January 1972 Terry represented the Suburban League in a match against The Middlesex Border League. He was released by Wealdstone at the end of the 1971/72 season having made a handful of senior appearances.

Terry spent the 1972/73 campaign with Southern League club Guildford City and was in the side that lost 3-2 at Ramsgate on 7.4.73.

In the late 1980's Terry moved to Thailand where he was involved in coaching and in 2008 he assisted new Thailand manager Peter Reid, helping him to learn some of the language and also advising on players.

In October 2009 Terry was running a soccer school in Thailand and was no longer involved with the national team following Reid's return to England.

name: Alan Dennis
other clubs: Tottenham Hotspur (0), Cambridge City, Dover and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
5 9 tall, versatile, hard-working player born in Ashcot, Somerset who grew up in Bermondsey, South London and played for both London and Kent at schoolboy level. At the age of 14, Alan was spotted by a Tottenham scout and began training with Spurs twice at week whilst completing his education. One of the first players he met at Tottenham was future Margate player Eddie Clayton.

Alan was picked for the England Schoolboys team in 1960 and went on to captain the side on six occasions. His team-mates included future successful managers Barry Fry and David Pleat.

Alan was signed by Spurs after leaving school and spent five seasons in Spurs' junior and reserve sides but never made a senior appearance. He was released at the end of the 1964/65 campaign.

In the summer of 1965 Alan was signed by Southern League club Cambridge City and made 61 appearances for them during the 1965/66 campaign. He was also a regular in the City side during the 1966/67 season.

Alan's next move took him to Dover for the 1967/68 campaign and he spent two seasons there.

In the summer of 1969 Alan signed for Margate and made his debut in a 3-3 draw at Hereford on 9.8.69 - the opening day of the 1969/70 campaign. He initially struggled to win a regular first team place due to the form of Dai Yorath and Ray Flannigan in the full-back positions but really established himself after Christmas 1969. Alan was the team's regular left-back once Flannigan departed for Reading but he also featured in midfield and at right-back on occasions. In total he made 41 appearances and scored once, with a header in a 4-0 win at Ashford on 23.2.70, before being released at the end of the season.

After a short spell out of the game, Alan joined Ramsgate on a month s trial in October 1970. In November 1970 he was given a contract running to the end of 1970/71 but he was released towards the end of December 1970 having made a total of 11 appearances. Ramsgate s player-manager Les Riggs explained to the East Kent Times We parted on the best of terms. Alan s job as a rep in London involves a lot of travelling and he has felt recently that he is not as fit as he would like to be. Very often Alan had to rush straight back from work to play at Southwood and he quite rightly believed his game was suffering.

Alan retired from football after leaving Ramsgate, he d picked up a knee injury years before during his time with Cambridge City that had become progressively worse and required a cartilage operation. In later years Alan had to have the knee joint replace.

In 2018 he was interviewed for a Tottenham website aged 74 and at that time Alan was living in Kent. Looking back on his time at Spurs he said It was fantastic, I wouldn t have missed it for the world I loved every minute of it, everything about it. And now when I look back I can t believe it. I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Alan s cousin Dennis Burnett played over 400 games in the Football League for the likes of West Ham, Millwall and Hull during the 1960 s and 1970 s.

name: Peter Denton
other clubs: Gorleston Town, Coventry City (11,1), Luton Town (4+1,0), Canterbury City and Vauxhall Motors (Luton)
bio:
Diminutive, pacy winger born in Gorleston, Norfolk who played for Norfolk Boys during the 1960/61 season before starting his career with his hometown club in the Norfolk and Suffolk League. Peter played in Gorleston s first team aged only 15 during the 1961/62 season and in April 1962 he was signed as an apprentice by Coventry. Their manager at the time was Jimmy Hill.

Peter played for Coventry s A and reserve teams during 1962/63 and also featured as the Sky Blues youth side lost 5-0 at home to Port Vale in the 1st Round of the FA Youth Cup. In September 1963 Peter was one of five Coventry youngsters chosen to attend a two day England Youth trial at Lilleshall and he continued to feature in Coventry s junior ranks during the remainder of 1963/64. On 1.3.64 - his 18th birthday - Peter was given a professional contract.

He was a regular in Coventry s reserve team during 1964/65 and the opening months of 1965/66 and on 1.10.65 Peter had his first outing for the senior side aged 19 as Coventry took on 1st Division Stoke in a friendly at Highfield Road. City won 5-1 and Peter scored the fifth goal to cap an impressive showing. Shortly afterwards, Jimmy Hill spoke to the Coventry Evening Telegraph about him and said Peter has always had qualities of speed and skill with his passing and shooting. Some clubs make up their minds about players before they are 19. But I think in many ways it is often worth persevering with them after that age.

On 13.11.65 Peter finally made his full first team debut, playing in a 3-1 win over Ipswich at Highfield Road in the 2nd Division. He made a few more appearances before the end of 1965/66 and scored what turned out to be his only goal for Coventry in a 3-1 home win over Cardiff in March 1966. Peter made his final senior appearance, and his only one in the 1st Division, in August 1967 when Coventry lost 3-1 at home to Nottingham Forest.

In January 1968 Peter was signed by 4th Division Luton for a fee of £4,000 and he made his debut in a 1-1 draw with Newport County at Kenilworth Road on 20.1.68. He featured in three more matches before the end of the 1967/68 campaign as Luton won the league. Peter then played once in the 3rd Division during 1968/69 but spent the remainder of the season in Luton s reserve side before being released.

In July 1969 Peter joined Margate and made his debut as a substitute in a Southern League game at Hereford on 9.8.69, the opening day of the 1969/70 season. Much was expected of Peter but things didn't work out for him. In September 1969 he broke his nose during training and he was never able to gain a regular first team place. In fact he'd only made five appearances, two of them as a substitute, when he left the club to join Canterbury towards the end of October 1969.

Peter only made two Southern League appearances for City before leaving the club at the end of November 1969 to become a player-coach at Luton. Peter s role saw him take charge of Luton s youth team and ground staff.

He settled in the Luton area and worked for many years at Vauxhall Motors in the town. Peter also had a spell as player-coach of Vauxhall Motors FC in the 1970 s and stayed on as coach after retiring as a player. He was still involved with the club in the mid-1990 s. In the 2000 s he worked as a waiter at two restaurants in Hertfordshire and Peter also regularly visited his old clubs Coventry and Luton for matches and former player events.

He died in Luton on 21.10.16 aged 70 after suffering a stroke.

name: Les Devonshire
other clubs: Queens Park Rangers (0), Willesden, Brentford (0), Chester City (45,4), Crystal Palace (87,12) and Canterbury City
bio:
Pacy left-sided player born in Leytonstone who moved to Acton with his parents at the age of eight months in 1927. Les attended Acton Priory School and then worked in a local shopfitters once his studies were completed.

During the 1941/42 season, Les played for local amateur club Acton Sports aged 15 and he then turned out for Acton Sea Cadets during the 1943/44 campaign. He moved on to St. Cuthbert s of the Brentford and Chiswick League for the 1944/45 season.

In December 1944, Les joined the Royal Air Force aged 18 but he still played for St. Cuthbert s when his leave allowed him to before being posted to India in March 1945. Les service there extended beyond the end of World War II and he spent time in Cawnpore, Palam and Chittagong. By May 1947 Les was serving in Changi, Singapore and played football for the RAF s first X1 there.

Having returned to England, Les started his senior career with Queens Park Rangers, signing amateur forms for the club in the summer of 1947. He never appeared for QPR's first team and spent most of 1947/48 playing for Willesden in Division 1 (Western) of the Spartan League. In January 1948 Les scored all five goals as Willesden beat Wycombe Redfords 5-2 and Willesden finished the season as league champions.

On 5.5.48 Les was signed by Brentford but once again he couldn t break into the Bees senior side and spent two seasons in the reserves.

In June 1950, Les joined Chester and he was a fixture in their first team during the 1950/51 campaign.

In August 1951 Crystal Palace paid what was described as a substantial fee to Chester for Les services and he went on to make 87 first team appearances for the Eagles before dropping into non-league football to join Margate in July 1955.

Les made quite an impact at Hartsdown Park with his clever play and he scored twice on his debut - a 5-1 home win over Canterbury on 20.8.55. He also bagged four goals in a 5-3 home win over Dover on 3.9.55 and on 19.11.55 Les was in the Margate side that drew 2-2 with Walsall at Hartsdown Park in the FA Cup 1st Round. He also played in the replay at Walsall on 24.11.55 that the home side won 6-1.

Les was a fixture Margate s team until February 1956 when he was 'rested'. Manager Almer Hall felt that he was struggling on the heavy pitches at that time of the season and Les found himself in the reserves for the remainder of the campaign, Dave O'Callaghan replacing him in the first team. At the end of the 1955/56 season Les joined Canterbury City having scored 12 times in his 23 appearances for Margate.

He went on to spend four seasons with City and scored from the penalty spot as they beat visitors Margate 4-2 in a Thames & Medway Combination tie on 2.4.59. Les left Canterbury at the end of the 1959/60 campaign.

In the summer of 1968 Les became manager of Ealing-based amateur club Avenue Athletic.

He was the father of 1970's / 1980's West Ham and England player Alan Devonshire who was born during Les spell with Margate and the club gave him a christening spoon to mark the event.

In March 2002 Les was living in Greenford, Middlesex and had been married for 54 years. One of his 11 grand-children was part of Brentford's academy at the time.

In 2004 Les was invited to Brentford's Griffin Park as part of the club's centenary celebrations and he walked out on to the pitch to be introduced to the crowd.

Les died in Middlesex on 19.12.12 at the age of 86.
