name: Eric German
other clubs: Erith & Belvedere, Whitstable Town, Leyton Orient (0), Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Gravesend & Northfleet, Dartford and Dover
bio:
Birmingham-born forward sometimes referred to as Jerry or Gerry who started his career with Erith & Belvedere before joining Whitstable, signing for the club in the summer of 1950. Eric made his debut for Whitstable in a Kent League game at Ramsgate on 11.11.50 and went on to make 31 appearances before the end of the 1950/51 season, scoring six goals. He also had a trial at Leyton Orient during the campaign.

Eric scored six goals from a further 21 appearances for Whitstable during the first half of 1951/52 and in December 1951 he played for Kent in a game against London University at Bromley.

At the end of January 1952, he signed for Snowdown Colliery Welfare but Eric s stint there was very brief and in February 1952 he joined Margate. Eric played exclusively for Margate's reserves during the remainder of the 1951/52 campaign.

At the start of the 1952/53 season he enjoyed a short run in the first team, making his debut as Margate lost 4-1 at home to Gravesend & Northfleet in an FA Cup tie on 13.9.52. Eric kept his place for Margate's next game - a Kent Senior Shield tie against Dartford at Hartsdown Park on 18.9.52 - and scored in a 2-1 win. Two days later he played in a 1-0 defeat at Dover and then returned to the reserves having scored once in his three senior appearances.

Eric left the club before the end of 1952 and in January 1953 Margate s player-manager Almer Hall explained his departure to the East Kent Times. He told the paper At the end of one Hartsdown game Jerry asked, and received, permission to travel back with the visiting side. During the journey he was persuaded to sign for that club. Hall added that two days later, a First Division club - believed to be Portsmouth - approached Margate to sign Eric and said that they would pay a transfer fee as well as loaning him back to Margate for the rest of the 1952/53 season. Hall told the paper I wired to German, but he had signed for the other club. German was very upset, but the First Division club, which has built its reputation on team spirit, was no longer interested. They regarded German s conduct as a poor example of team spirit and esprit do corps. The club that Eric had signed for is unknown.

Eric later Gravesend & Northfleet for the 1954/55 campaign and scored twice from 11 appearances for the Fleet during the season.

Eric moved on to Dartford for the 1955/56 campaign.

He then returned to Whitstable and scored seven goals in 54 appearances there during the 1956/57 and 1957/58 seasons, his younger brother Tommy was on Whitstable s books during 1956/57.

Eric joined Dover for the 1958/59 campaign and although he was principally a reserve team player, Eric also scored three first team goals for Dover early in 1959.

He later returned to live in his native Birmingham and worked in the car industry. In December 1997, Eric, by then aged 64, tackled a burglar who d attempted to gain access to his property in Kingshurst, Birmingham. Having been threatened with a knife, Eric chased the intruder off his property with a walking stick and then, whilst dressed in pyjamas, pursued him before pinning him to the ground and disarming him.

name: Carl Gilbert
other clubs: Gillingham (28+2,11), Bristol Rovers (47+6,18), Rotherham United (91+17,44), Folkestone & Shepway, Folkestone Town, Canterbury City, Herne Bay and Folkestone
bio:
Stylish, 6' 2" tall, left-footed striker who was born in Folkestone. Carl joined the Army aged 15 and signed up for nine years service. He was stationed at Canterbury's Chaucer Barracks and enjoyed success as a cross-country runner, coming first in the England Junior Army Under-18 section and finishing third in Kent. Carl also played football for the army and his battalion received some coaching from Gillingham player Geoff Hudson. He recommended Carl to the Gills and, after impressing in their Youth team, Carl bought himself out of the Army to sign a professional contract with Gillingham in October 1965.

He was top scorer for the Gills reserves in each of his first two seasons - 1965/66 and 1966/67.

During the 1967/68 campaign Carl broke into the Gills' first team and marked his full debut with a goal in a 2-1 win over Mansfield at Priestfield on 27.4.68. He also finished as the reserves leading scorer for the third consecutive season, finding the target seven times in 25 appearances (two as sub).

Carl went on to make a total of 30 first team appearances for the Gills spanning the 1967/68 to 1969/70 seasons. He scored 11 times during that period.

On 1.12.69 Carl was signed by Bristol Rovers in an exchange deal that took Rovers' Ken Ronaldson to Gillingham. Carl went on to score 18 times in 53 senior appearances for Bristol Rovers during the 1969/70 and 1970/71 campaigns.

In March 1971 Rotherham paid Rovers £17,000 for Carl and he went on to make 108 first team appearances for the Yorkshire club. Carl scored 44 goals, including all four in a 4-0 home win over Swansea in September 1971.

In July 1974 Carl was signed by Margate for a club record fee of £2,000. Margate manager Les Riggs said it was "the best deal of the season" and that Carl was "strong" and had "tremendous potential". He also told the East Kent Times The club has done very well to raise the record transfer fee which I will consider well spent if Carl realises his potential and knocks in the goals for us. I am convinced that he will soon get on the goal trail.

Carl made his debut in a 2-1 win at Guildford & Dorking on 17.8.74, the opening day of the 1974/75 season and his aerial ability was immediately apparent. He was soon being referred to as Margate's "star striker" and a "veritable blonde bombshell" by the local press. Carl scored his first goals for the club when he struck twice in a 3-0 win at Wealdstone on 31.8.74 and on 5.10.74 he netted with a spectacular diving header to secure a 1-0 win over Kettering at Hartsdown Park. Carl also scored with a long range effort in a 2-2 draw at Stourbridge on 14.12.74 and found the net with another diving header in a 3-2 win at Nuneaton on 25.1.75.

In February 1975 Torquay made an approach for Carl s services and Les Riggs told the East Kent Times Torquay are very keen to secure Carl and have asked us to name a price. It is understandable that Carl would welcome a return to League football. But, so far as I am concerned, though we are in sore need of finance, the price would have to be high because I do not want to lose Carl and disturb the balance of the side at this stage. Gilbert has completely justified the faith I had in signing him and has been playing exceptionally well for weeks. Nothing came of Torquay s interest and Carl remained at Hartsdown Park.

On 1.3.75 he scored with a shot described by the Thanet Times as a "cannonball" to give Margate a 1-0 win over Cambridge City and on 5.4.75 Carl was in the Margate side that lost 2-0 at home to Kettering in the first leg of the Southern League Cup Final. He also played in the second leg at Kettering on 12.4.75 as Margate secured a 1-1 draw that wasn t sufficient to claim the trophy. By the end of the season Carl had scored 23 times from 65 appearances and finished the campaign as Margate's leading scorer.

He was made captain for the 1975/76 season but was hampered by injuries during the campaign. A slipped disc kept Carl out for over a month and various other niggling problems restricted him to 39 appearances (two as sub). He scored nine goals during the season. On 22.4.76 Carl featured as a substitute as Margate won 2-0 at Canterbury in the 1st Leg of the Kent Floodlight Trophy Final and he then started in the 2nd Leg at Hartsdown Park on 24.4.76 which the visitors won 2-1 after extra time. The result meant Margate took the trophy with a 3-2 aggregate win.

During the early months of the 1976/77 campaign Carl played regularly but struggled for goals. The local press felt that this was principally down to poor service from his team-mates and especially due to a lack crosses. He'd scored eight goals from 29 appearances (one as sub) when Folkestone & Shepway made a bid for him in January 1977 and after a fee in the region of £300 was agreed Carl left the club.

In the summer of 1978 he became Folkestone's player-coach and Carl went on to spend over five years at Cheriton Road before joining Canterbury early in 1982.

During the remainder of the 1981/82 season Carl scored six goals in 16 Southern League appearances (one as sub) for City but in the summer of 1982 he moved on to Herne Bay.

After a short spell as Herne Bay's player-manager Carl returned to Canterbury for the 1983/84 campaign and he scored six goals in 32 Southern League appearances (three as sub). His tally included one of the City goals in a 3-1 win over Thanet on 2.1.84. Carl only made two substitute appearances for Canterbury in the Southern League during the 1984/85 season and they were his last for the club.

In the summer of 1985 Carl took over from Alf Bentley as City's manager but he resigned during the 1986/87 season and returned to Folkestone as assistant manager / coach.

Carl later went on to manage Folkestone and he was in charge there during the 1988/89 season when he also made three substitute appearances aged 40. He was also in charge during the first half of the 1989/90 campaign but in February 1990 he resigned. However Carl then took over again early in the 1990/91 campaign, replacing Alf Bentley. He resigned once more in December 1990.

name: Matt Gilbert
bio:
Local keeper who joined Thanet United in September 1981 and made his debut for the reserves on 3.10.81. Matt also made two first team appearances during the 1981/82 season, deputising for Colin Page.

He made his debut in a home game against Crawley on 23.1.82 and kept a clean sheet in a 0-0 draw. The Thanet Times said that Matt gave "a competent display" and he was also described as being "promising". United manager Terry Morris said "young Matt did well. He kept us in the game several times with good saves." Matt also played in United's next match - a 3-0 defeat at Folkestone on 27.1.82.

He stayed with United for the 1982/83 season and played twice more for the first team. Matt's first appearance came in a 6-1 defeat at Fisher on 28.8.82 and the Thanet Times said that he was "out of touch". Three days later he played in a home game against Crawley that United lost 3-1 and then Matt returned to the reserves for the remainder of the campaign.

name: Phil Gilbert
other clubs: Ramsgate Athletic, Brighton & Hove Albion (6,3) and Salisbury City
bio:
5 10 tall player born in Minster who initially joined Margate in January 1960. Phil made his debut for the reserves on 9.1.60 aged only 15 and scored one of the goals as Margate hammered Folkestone Reserves 9-1 at Hartsdown Park.

Phil continued to feature in Margate s second string during the 1960/61 campaign but never made a first team appearance.

In the summer of 1961 he moved on to Ramsgate and Phil played in the Southern League for them as a 17 year-old during the early part of 1961/62 before being signed by Brighton in January 1962.

Phil usually played as a striker at that time and he went on to make four senior appearances for the Seagulls before the end of the 1961/62 season, scoring once. During 1962/63 Phil only featured once in Brighton s first team but managed to score twice as they beat visitors Bradford 3-1 on 27.4.63. He made one further senior appearance during the 1963/64 campaign and also scored five goals from 25 reserve team outings before leaving Brighton to join Salisbury in March 1964.

Phil went on to play over 300 games for Salisbury and featured in some famous FA Cup ties for the club before being released in 1972.

Phil then returned home to Thanet and dropped out of senior football to concentrate on work and family life but during the 1974/75 season he played for local Sunday League side Margate Athletic. On 27.10.74 Phil was sent off in a Thanet Premier Sunday League game against Northwood.

In March 1977 Phil was resigned by Margate as the club sought to bolster the first team squad with local players but he wasn t required to make a senior appearance. Margate didn t have a reserve team at the time.

During the summer of 1980 Phil returned to Margate once more and he played for the reserves as a 'father figure' during the first half of the 1980/81 campaign. In January 1981 he was unexpectedly pressed into first team duty due to a drastic player shortage following the departure of many senior players in a cost-cutting exercise. So on 31.1.81, just over 21 years since his first outing for Margate s reserve side, Phil made his senior debut aged 36 when he played at right-back in a 3-2 defeat at Tonbridge. The Thanet Times said that he "performed with utmost credit" on his home debut a week later - a 0-0 draw with Bognor Regis. Phil went on to play in each of the season s remaining games, making 20 appearances in all in the number two shirt, but when the campaign ended in May 1981 Phil left Hartsdown Park.

He moved to Ramsgate and took over as manager for the 1981/82 season, continuing to play in local amateur football but not for the Rams. Phil continued in that role until resigning in November 1982, he was replaced by Syd Jest.

During the 1983/84 season Phil became part of Thanet United's management committee.

In 2013 he was still living locally and made a rare visit to Hartsdown Park in October when he attended an evening featuring Terry Yorath as speaker.

On 12.4.14 Phil was one of the many former Margate players who attended the club s Legends Day at Hartsdown Park.

name: Kevin Gilchrist
other clubs: Dover, Ramsgate, Crockenhill, Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Dover Athletic, Deal Town and Woodnesborough
bio:
5' 10" tall keeper who began his career at Dover, his hometown club, as a 17 year-old during the 1975/76 season. Kevin then enjoyed a lengthy run in the first team during the 1976/77 campaign, taking over from future Margate assistant manager Kevin Raine. He also played as an outfield player in the youth team during the season, at the time their keeper was future Charlton star Bob Bolder.

Kevin stayed at Crabble for several more seasons and began the 1980/81 campaign as Dover's back-up keeper. At that time he was said to be attracting attention from Football League clubs.

In September 1980 he moved to Ramsgate and Kevin was working as a miner when he signed for the club. His spell at Southwood turned out to be eventful, he failed to turn up for the Rams' game with Chatham on 27.9.80, a situation described as "inexplicable" by the Thanet Times, and on 25.10.80 he was sent off for dissent in a game with Crockenhill. Kevin then walked out on the club, along with almost all the Rams' first team squad, as a protest at the sacking of manager Graham Sawyer (a former Margate player). He made a brief return to Southwood before joining Margate in November 1980.

Kevin made his debut for the club in a 3-2 win over Aylesbury at Hartsdown Park on 22.11.80 and his agile display led to him becoming Margate's first-choice keeper. On 27.12.80 Kevin had a great game during a 4-2 win at Ashford and the Thanet Times said that he made "a series of smart saves". However on 7.2.81 he failed to show up for the home game with Bognor Regis and as a result Kevin was sacked by the club. His unexplained absence had forced outfield player Mark Harrop to play the whole game in goal and Kevin had made 16 appearances before his sudden departure.

He later played for Crockenhill in the Kent League, featuring mainly as an outfield player for them, and went on to play as a midfielder for Snowdown. Kevin was with them during the 1986/87 season.

During the 1988/89 and 1989/90 campaigns Kevin played as an outfield player for Dover's reserves. He then played for Deal during 1990/91.

Kevin s career continued well into the 1990 s and he usually played as an outfield player. His last club was Woodnesborough of the Kent County League and Kevin made his final appearances for them during the 1998/99 season at the age of 40.

He was still living in the Dover area in 2017.

name: Peter Gillott
other clubs: Worsborough Bridge Miners Welfare, Barnsley (5,0) and Chelmsford City
bio:
6' 0" tall solid and dependable defender who was born in Barnsley and played eight times for England s Youth team.

Peter started his career with Worsborough Bridge Miners Welfare before moving on to 3rd Division club Barnsley. He spent six years there but found first team opportunities hard to come by.

In July 1959 he moved to Chelmsford and went on to spend seven years with the Essex club.

In May 1966 Peter joined Margate at the same time as his Chelmsford team-mates David Pye and Ron Smillie and before the month was out he was in the squad that travelled to West Germany for a three match tour.

Peter became Margate's club captain and made his competitive debut in a 5-2 win over Barry at Hartsdown Park on 20.8.66. It was the opening day of the 1966/67 season. Peter went on to make a total of 64 appearances without scoring as Margate won promotion from the Southern League Division One by finishing as runners-up. He usually played at right-back but also featured on the left-hand side on occasions. Peter s tough tackling and sound positional sense were his main assets.

He left Margate at the end of the season due to business commitments and returned to Chelmsford where he was something of a legend, becoming player-manager of their reserve team.

By the time Peter retired in 1969 he'd made 376 appearances for Chelmsford and he was still playing local football in the area when he was well into his fifties.

In later years a Sunday League in the Chelmsford area named one of their competitions 'The Peter Gillott Reserve Team Cup' in his honour.

In October 2008 Peter played for an ex-Chelmsford X1 in a charity match at the club's Melbourne Park ground and he was 73 at the time.

Peter died aged 85 on 23.1.21 after a battle with dementia.

name: Craig Godden
other clubs: Crawley Town, Peterborough United (0), Ashford Town, Bromsgrove Rovers and Whitstable Town
bio:
Brave, agile keeper born in Chatham whose older brother Wayne played for both Margate and Thanet United. Another older brother of Craig s - Tony - was a well-known Football League goalkeeper for the likes of West Bromwich Albion and Chelsea.

Craig initially joined Margate in January 1980 aged 16 and his brother Wayne was in the Margate side at that time. Prior to linking up with Margate, Craig had been playing amateur football in his native Ashford. After Margate s regular keeper Bryan Parry left the club, Craig was thrust into first team action and made his debut in a 1-1 draw with Hounslow at Hartsdown Park on 29.1.80. He immediately impressed the East Kent Times who wrote what a find this 16 year-old seems to be and added He showed all the confidence in the world, together with courage and determination in a testing debut. The Isle of Thanet Gazette noted that Craig "showed definite promise" but he only played once more for the senior side - in a 4-0 home defeat against Waterlooville on 2.2.80 - before Steve Pateman took over in goal for the remainder of the 1979/80 season.

Craig later had a spell with Crawley.

In the summer of 1982 he returned to Hartsdown Park and was expected to be Thanet United's back-up keeper for the 1982/83 campaign. However when Brian Curtis was injured during a pre-season friendly, Craig was given the opportunity of a run in the United side. He did so well that Curtis left the club once he'd recovered as Craig had firmly established himself as first-choice. He gained rave reviews for a string of fine performances. Craig had an excellent game in a 2-1 defeat at home to Tonbridge on 30.10.82, pulling off numerous saves, and on 13.11.82 he saved a penalty during a 4-0 home defeat at the hands of Ashford. The Thanet Times said that Craig "pounced on the penalty kick like a cat". The same paper then praised him for making "three top-class saves" in a 6-1 defeat at Salisbury on 20.11.82. In December 1982 United took the unprecedented step (for Thanet) of giving Craig a contract and caretaker manager Peter Donnelly said at the time "I think Craig is good enough for Football League clubs to take a good, hard look at him." The Isle of Thanet Gazette also felt that Craig could go a long way and said that he was "continually improving". His eye-catching displays continued and on 1.1.83 Craig played brilliantly in a 5-0 defeat at Hillingdon. He was still in sparkling form towards the end of the season and the Thanet Times was full of praise for Craig's performance in a 1-0 win over Woodford at Hartsdown Park on 2.4.83. The paper said that he "distinguished himself with some outstanding saves and his handling throughout was impeccable". Craig made 41 appearances in total, missing only three games, and kept 12 clean sheets. He was a worthy winner of United's 'Player of the Year' award. Peter Donnelly agreed and described him as being "a brave and agile keeper with a lot of class."

Craig was in fine form again at the start of the 1983/84 season and he was watched by Football League scouts on several occasions. The local press described him as being "fearless" and Craig gave a brilliant display in 1-0 defeat at Salisbury on 12.11.83, making what the Thanet Times said were "three stunning saves" to cap "a superb performance". The same paper later praised Craig for "goalkeeping heroics" during a 1-1 draw at Waterlooville on 17.12.83 but after a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Addlestone & Weybridge on 4.2.84 he was dropped by new Thanet boss John Wickens. Bobby Miles took over as United's first-choice keeper and kept his place for the remainder of the season. As a result, Craig left the club having made 31 appearances during the campaign.

During the early part of the 1984/85 season he played for Peterborough's reserves and Craig then joined Ashford, making his debut for them in an Eastern Floodlight Cup tie at home to Thanet on 11.12.84.

In later years Craig had a spell with Bromsgrove Rovers and featured for them during the 1987/88 season.

He also went on to have a spell with Whitstable, playing twice for their first team during the 1992/93 season as well as making numerous reserve team appearances.

Craig s younger brother Justin played for Whitstable's youth team and reserve teams during the early 1990's.

In 2003 Craig was living in the Medway area of Kent.

name: Wayne Godden
other clubs: Gillingham (0), Ashford Town, Canterbury City, Gravesend & Northfleet, Crawley Town, Tonbridge, Herne Bay, Chatham Town,Sittingbourne and Whitstable Town
bio:
5' 9" tall, hard-working full-back born in Gillingham who started his career in the Gills' youth team. Wayne then had a spell at Ashford where he made one first team appearance - in a 2-0 defeat at Ramsgate in the Kent Floodlight Trophy on 24.2.76.

Wayne joined Canterbury in the summer of 1977 and made 35 appearances (two as sub) for City in the Southern League during the 1977/78 season. He scored once - in a 6-3 defeat at home to Trowbridge on 3.12.77.

In August 1978 Wayne joined Margate and played for the reserves initially. He made his first team debut in a Southern League game at Yeovil on 11.11.78 and the Thanet Times said "he looks a natural left-back with a sound positional sense and strength in the tackle". He went on to make 30 appearances before the end of the 1978/79 campaign, occasionally playing at right-back but usually on his favoured left-hand side.

During the 1979/80 season Wayne made a further 42 appearances and played numerous games in midfield and a few at right-back. However left-back was still his primary position.

Wayne made his 100th appearance during the 1980/81 campaign, playing regularly once more and again featuring either at left-back or in midfield. However in February 1981 he left the club and joined Gravesend & Northfleet. This was due to Margate's desperate cost-cutting measures that saw several established players depart. Wayne had made 32 appearances during the season, three of them as a substitute.

After making nine appearances during a short stint with Crawley Wayne had a spell with Tonbridge before returning to Hartsdown Park to join Thanet United in October 1981. His first game back was a 4-0 defeat at Chelmsford on 19.10.81. Wayne went on to make 32 appearances before the end of the 1981/82 season and once again played at either left-back or in midfield. He managed to score three goals and Wayne s first for the club came in a 2-1 win over Salisbury on 24.4.82. The other two were both scored in a 4-3 defeat at home to Andover on 3.5.82 and one of Wayne's efforts was a shot from way outside the penalty area. Despite the last day victory United finished bottom of the Southern League Southern Division.

He stayed with Thanet for the 1982/83 campaign and missed only one match, adding another 43 appearances (one as sub) to his career tally and scoring once. Wayne began the campaign at left-back but later became a regular in midfield and even played as a striker on occasions. His barrage of shots in a 1-0 defeat against Salisbury on 5.3.83 prompted the Thanet Times to say that he had a "siege gun boot".

He was almost ever-present once again during the 1983/84 season, mostly playing in midfield, and his 47 appearances (one as sub) took him comfortably past 200 for the club. Wayne also managed to score three times during the campaign. On 28.4.84 he had an outstanding game in a sweeper role as Thanet won 3-1 at Woodford and Wayne also appeared at left-back and centre-back during the season.

During the 1984/85 campaign Wayne missed only one of Thanet's 62 games and he spent almost the whole season at left-back, apart from two early appearances in midfield. He scored once - from the penalty spot in a 2-0 home win over Dunstable at on 4.5.85. Wayne's performances earned him the club's 'Players Player of the Year' award and he was runner-up to Joe Radford for the 'Supporters Player of the Year' honour.

Wayne was as consistent as ever during the 1985/86 campaign, making 54 appearances (two as sub) to take his tally for the club past 300. He started the season at left-back but after a lengthy run there Wayne switched to right-back towards the end of 1985. He also played a few games in midfield towards the end of the season. Probably Wayne's best performance of an outstanding campaign came in a 1-0 win at Dover on 2.11.85. The Thanet Times said that he "gave absolutely nothing away". In February 1986 Thanet manager John Wickens said that Wayne had been "a solid and consistent performer for the club for five seasons" and added that he was "a smashing lad." On 4.2.86 Wayne scored his only goal of the season to earn Thanet a 1-0 win over Dover in an Eastern Floodlight Cup tie at Hartsdown and it turned out to be his last for the club. The last match of the season, a 2-0 win at Dunstable on 3.5.86, was Wayne's final game for United and his 237th as a Thanet player, a record for the club.

Before he left the club Wayne was granted a testimonial match at Hartsdown on 17.5.86. A Thanet / 1st Division X1 played a Maidstone United X1 and a bumper crowd was expected. The Thanet side included West Brom's goalkeeper Tony Godden - Wayne's brother - and internationals Derek Statham (England) and Terry Cochrane (Northern Ireland). Unfortunately for Wayne only 250 people paid for entry and at the same time the match was taking place evangelist Eric Delve was speaking to a capacity crowd in a large marquee directly adjacent to the ground. That may have influenced the attendance for Wayne's big game but he was philosophical about it, simply saying "it's a pity we couldn't have had a crowd like they've had next door".

The programme for his benefit match was full of praise for Wayne, Thanet's club president Bob Griffiths said Wayne was "always a trier and never a moaner" and that he had "proved to be a first class clubman, ever reliable". Local press legend Dave Cooper described Wayne as being a "chirpy, cheery character" and added "he would give 100% whether the game was at Wembley or John O'Groats". John Wickens had the final word - "players mainly get testimonials because of their character, friendliness and being liked by all, to me Wayne has all these qualities".

In the summer of 1986 Wayne joined Gravesend & Northfleet and he made 47 appearances (one as sub) without scoring for the Fleet during the 1986/87 season.

Just before the start of the 1987/88 campaign Wayne moved on to Herne Bay. His spell there was very brief and he only made one appearance before signing for Chatham.

Wayne left Chatham in December 1987 and joined Canterbury where he made 52 Southern League appearances (one as sub) without scoring before moving to Sittingbourne in March 1989.

Wayne stayed with the Brickies for two full seasons before leaving the club at the end of 1990/91.

In the summer of 1991 he featured in a couple of friendlies for Margate before opting to join Whitstable.

He made his debut for the Oystermen on 10.8.91 but later in August he had a short spell with Ashford where he made three appearances before returning to Belmont Road. It was the start of a long association with Whitstable. After two seasons as a player Wayne had a spell as the club's player-manager from 1993/94-1997/98 and made over 130 appearances, his last in the first team during 1996/97, before moving on.

Wayne became coach at Lordswood for the 1999/00 campaign and then took over as the Kent League club's manager during 2000/01. He was sacked in February 2002.

Wayne's younger brother Craig played in goal for Margate and Thanet United whilst Tony Godden's clubs also included Chelsea. Another younger brother called Justin played for Whitstable's youth and reserve teams during the early 1990's.

Wayne worked as an Advertising Sales Executive during his final spell at Hartsdown Park.

name: Paul Golden
other clubs: Dover Athletic, Charlton Athletic (0), Gillingham (0), Colchester United (0), Canterbury City, St.Margaret's and Snowdown Colliery Welfare
bio:
Left-sided player born in Canterbury who started his career at Dover where he played in the youth team before joining Charlton early in the 1989/90 season.

Paul played for the Addicks 'Colts' side and then signed for Gillingham as a trainee in August 1990. He scored 12 goals for the Gills' youth team during 1990/91. At the start of 1992 Paul had a loan spell at Colchester and shortly after returning to Priestfield in March 1992 he joined Margate on loan at the same time as his team-mate Nicky Forster.

Paul made his debut in midfield as Margate won 1-0 at Newport IOW on 28.3.92. He was 18 at the time and returned to Gillingham almost immediately without making another senior appearance for Margate.

At the end of the 1991/92 campaign Paul briefly returned to Hartsdown Park and played for the reserves in a 4-0 win over Tonbridge in the Kent Midweek League on 7.5.92.

He joined Margate on a permanent basis in the summer of 1992 having been released by Gillingham and the Thanet Times said that Paul "often took the eye with dogged tackling and intelligent overlapping" in a 4-1 win over Wealdstone at Watford on 22.8.92. He was a fixture in the side at left-back for the first few months of the season and on 26.9.92 Paul scored his first goal from the penalty spot in a 4-1 home defeat against Chertsey in the FA Cup. In mid-November 1992 he lost his place to loan signing Michael Harle and Paul sat out ten games before regaining the number three shirt at the start of January 1993. On 16.1.93 he scored in a 3-1 win at Burnham and in February 1993 Paul was switched to the left wing for four matches, the last of them being a 4-0 win over Burnham at Hartsdown on 6.3.93. A few days later he was released and joined Sheppey having scored twice in 33 appearances (one as sub).

In January 1994 Paul linked up with Canterbury and he stayed with City until the end of the 1993/94 campaign.

He played for Dover's reserves during the 1998/99 season and later dropped into the Kent County League. Paul had a spell with St.Margaret's before joining Snowdown Colliery Welfare for the 2003/04 season.

In 2012 he was living in Aylesham, Kent and working as a postman.

A relative of Paul's, probably his father, played for Snowdown during the 1970's.

name: Norman Golding
other clubs: Wimbledon, Tonbridge, Grays Athletic, Dartford, Crystal Palace (0), Queens Park Rangers (31,6), Kettering Town, Gravesend & Northfleet, Yiewsley and Cray Wanderers
bio:
London-born player who played for London Boys and South London Boys as a youth before starting his senior career with Wimbledon. Norman scored once in six appearances for the Dons during the early part of the 1954/55 season before leaving the club to start his National Service.

Whilst enlisted, Norman was on Tonbridge s books as an amateur during the 1955/56 campaign and scored four times from 12 outings for them during the season.

During 1956/57,he played for Royal Artillery Association Battersea in the London Sunday League and in October 1956 Norman featured in the league s representative X1 for a match against an Edmonton Sunday Football League side. Royal Artillery Association Battersea won the league and Premier League Cup during 1956/57.

Norman also played for Grays Athletic during the second half of 1956/57 and he scored a first half hat-trick for them in a 5-1 win over Hornchurch in the Essex Senior Cup semi-final in March 1957. Grays went on to win the trophy with a 3-1 win over Ilford and Norman was part of their final line-up.

In the summer of 1957 Norman was signed as a professional by Tonbridge and he spent the whole of 1957/58 there whilst doing his training at Millwall to save on travelling. He was released by Tonbridge at the end of the season having scored 12 times from 46 appearances during the campaign.

Norman was signed by Dartford in the summer of 1958 and stayed there until the end of the 1958/59 campaign. He also played Sunday football for Islington Queens during the season and helped them to win the Metropolitan Sunday Bart Bowl in April 1959.

In the summer of 1959, Norman spent a month on trial at Crystal Palace and played for the Eagles A team in the London Midweek League before being released.

At the start of September 1959, Norman was signed by 3rd Division club Queens Park Rangers on a month s trial and made his Football League debut in a 0-0 draw with York at Loftus Road on 14.9.59. He then scored five goals in his next four outings for the R s but Norman only added one further goal from a further 27 appearances for the club before being released at the end of the 1960/61 season.

Norman spent the 1961/62 campaign with Kettering and in the summer of 1962 he joined Gravesend & Northfleet.

Norman made 29 appearances for the Fleet during the first half of the 1962/63 season, scoring four goals, until linking up with Yiewsley in February 1963.

Norman scored four times in 19 appearances for Yiewsley before joining Margate in October 1963.

He made his debut in a 2-0 win over Hastings in a Southern League game at Hartsdown Park on 12.10.63 and went on to make 26 appearances during the remainder of the 1963/64 season. Norman scored four times but he was released at the end of the campaign.

Norman later played for Cray, joining them towards the end of the 1964/65 season. During 1965/66 he was a regular as the club won the Greater London League championship and League Cup.

Norman became Cray's player-manager during the 1966/67 campaign and guided the team to club record runs in the FA Cup (3rd Qualifying Round) and FA Amateur Cup (3rd Round - last sixteen). He stepped down from the job at the end of the 1969/70 season and retired from football to concentrate on the pub trade.

Norman worked for brewery firm Young's for over 35 years and ran the Duke's Head pub in Putney, London with his wife until retiring in the early 2000's. He'd worked at a printers during his time with Margate.

Norman died in 2014.

name: Antonio Gonnella
other clubs: Millwall (0), Fisher Athletic, Cambridge City, Hastings United, Carshalton Athletic, Maidstone United, Dulwich Hamlet, Greenwich Borough, Walton & Hersham, Folkestone Invicta, Kingstonian, Canvey Island, Thurrock, Concord Rangers, Bognor Regis Town, Faversham Town and Sittingbourne
bio:
Diminutive midfielder whose uncle was former Chelsea and Tottenham midfielder Gus Poyet. Antonio competed in the English Schools' Athletic Association National Cross Country Championships in 2003 and started his football career in Millwall s youth ranks.

Antonio then joined Fisher and progressed through the club s junior ranks to make a few Conference South appearances during 2006/07 before being released in May 2007 along with all the other members of Fisher s squad.

After trying unsuccessfully to find a club in Italy Antonio joined Cambridge City in July 2007 and made five substitute appearances for the Conference South outfit without scoring. He was released by City early in November 2007.

Antonio then signed for Hastings and made his debut as they lost 1-0 to visitors Leyton in an Isthmian League Premier Division game on 10.11.07. He got his only goal of 2007/08 when he struck the winner in a 2-1 win at Margate on 2.2.08 and Antonio finished the season having made a total of 19 Premier Division appearances (seven as sub). He went on to make 38 league appearances (five as sub) for Hastings during the 2008/09 campaign and scored seven times.

In July 2009 Antonio signed for Carshalton but the following month he was loaned to Maidstone ahead of the 2009/10 season proper.

On 18.8.09 he scored his first goal for the Stones after coming on as a substitute in a 2-1 win at Waltham Abbey and when his loan came to an end in September 2009 Antonio rejoined Hastings on a permanent basis having never played competitively for Carshalton.

He spent a few weeks back at Hastings and took his total record there to eight goals from 68 outings before moving on to Dulwich towards the end of October 2009.

His brother Gerry was on Dulwich s books at that time and Antonio made three Isthmian League Division 1 South appearances (two as sub) without scoring before signing for Margate in December 2009.

Antonio made his debut in midfield in a 3-3 draw at Bognor Regis in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 12.12.09 and the Thanet Times said he looked pretty handy when Margate got the ball on the floor". He also started Margate s next match - a 3-2 defeat at Sittingbourne in the Isthmian League Cup on 16.12.09 - but Antonio only featured twice as a substitute in the four games that followed.

On 26.1.10 he was back in the starting line-up for a 1-0 win over Chatham in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park and after that Antonio made two sub appearances in Margate s next five games. The last of them came in a 3-1 home defeat against Billericay on 16.2.10 and in March 2010 he was released after seven outings (four as sub) without scoring.

Antonio rejoined Maidstone for the remainder of the 2009/10 campaign and finished the season having scored three times in 19 Premier Division appearances (six as sub) for them in his two spells with the club.

At the start of the 2010/11 campaign Antonio was troubled by injuries and had only made eight league appearances (five as sub) without scoring for Maidstone when they allowed him to join Kent League club Greenwich on a dual-registration basis in November 2010.

In December 2010 Maidstone announced that Antonio had been released and he then joined Walton & Hersham but didn t feature in Division 1 South for them before swiftly moving on to Folkestone before the end of 2010.

He made four Premier Division appearances (two as sub) without scoring for Invicta and then left Folkestone to sign for Kingstonian in January 2011.

Antonio featured 12 times for the K s in the Premier Division before the end of 2010/11 but all bar one of his appearances were as a substitute.

Just after the start of the 2011/12 season he joined Canvey Island and Antonio made 11 Premier Division appearances there (seven as sub) without scoring before briefly linking up with Conference South outfit Thurrock on a dual-registration basis.

At the end of December 2011 he switched from Canvey Island to Concord Rangers where he made four sub appearances in the Premier Division without scoring.

Antonio s next move took him back to Folkestone in January 2012 but he only featured seven times for Invicta as a substitute in Division 1 South before making it six clubs for the season by signing for Bognor Regis in March 2012.

Antonio finished 2011/12 with the Sussex club and played five times (four as sub) for them in Division 1 South without scoring.

In June 2012 he joined Faversham and after scoring once from six substitute appearances in Division 1 South Antonio moved on to Sittingbourne in October 2012.

The Brickies were also in Division 1 South and he made four league appearances (three as sub) without scoring before moving on.

name: Dan Gonzalez-Bello
other clubs: Deal Town, Ramsgate and Canterbury City
bio:
Locally born striker who spent time as part of the AFC Margate youth setup before switching to Margate for the 2005/06 campaign. Dan played in the Under-15 s during that season and progressed through the junior ranks to Margate s reserves by the end of 2008/09.

On 8.8.09 he featured as a substitute as Margate lost 1-0 at Chatham in a friendly and Dan was a regular in the reserves throughout the 2009/10 campaign.

On 30.3.10 he made a one-off appearance for the first team in a 2-0 defeat at Welling in the Kent Senior Cup and at the end of the season Dan left the club.

He joined Kent League outfit Deal for the start of 2010/11 before dropping into local amateur football.

In the summer of 2011 Dan signed for Ramsgate and became a regular in their reserve team before making his senior debut as a substitute in a 5-1 defeat at East Thurrock in the Isthmian League Cup on 13.12.11. He also made one sub appearance for the Rams in the Isthmian League Division 1 South during 2011/12.

In September 2012 Dan rejoined Margate and became a fixture in the reserves for the remainder of the 2012/13 campaign.

During the opening months of the 2013/14 season Dan signed for Canterbury of the Southern Counties East League.

name: Matt Goodban
other clubs: Dover Athletic, Charlton Athetic (0), Portsmouth (0), Gillingham (0), St. Margaret s, Deal Town, Herne Bay, Folkestone Invicta, Ramsgate and Betteshanger Colliery Welfare
bio:
Attacking midfielder who played for Deal Minnows in the South-East Kent (Under-11) Youth League during the 1989/90 season and scored over 50 goals during the campaign. His father Mike was the team s manager. Matt also spent 1990/91 with the club and was picked for Kent Under-11 s during the season.

He played for Dover s Under-13 s side during 1991/92 and then played for Charlton Athletic Juniors during 1992/93, Matt also featured locally for Kingsdown Juniors at that time and he was a pupil at Walmer School.

In May 1994 he signed associate schoolboy forms for First Division club Wimbledon aged 14 and featured regularly in the Dons junior sides. Matt told the Deal, Walmer & Sandwich Mercury They really look after you and treat everyone the same, I want to be in the England side by the time I m 21. I know I could do this with Wimbledon but it s going to be a lot of hard work.

Matt later had a spell on the books at Portsmouth before spending a season in Gillingham s junior sides.

He joined Margate on trial in the summer of 1998 and scored in pre-season friendlies at Herne Bay and Deal. Matt then played in the opening game of the 1998/99 campaign as Margate lost on penalties at Forest Green in the Southern League Championship match but was released soon afterwards.

Immediately after leaving Hartsdown Park, Matt joined Dover where he played in the reserves.

In January 1999 he signed for Kent County League club St. Margaret s and spent the remainder of 1998/99 there.

Matt linked up with Deal for the 1999/00 season and scored eight goals in 13 reserve team games (one as sub) before leaving the club towards the end of 1999.

He then joined Herne Bay and finished 1999/00 there.

During the 2000/01 campaign Matt played for Folkestone's reserves and by 2002/03 he was back at Deal where he made a few first team appearances.

In March 2003 he signed for Ramsgate and scored twice in a 4-3 defeat at Thamesmead on 1.4.03 but Matt left the Rams at the end of the season and went back to Deal for a third spell.

In September 2003 he rejoined Ramsgate but left the club a few weeks later to link up with Kent County League outfit Betteshanger. Matt spent the 2004/05 and 2005/06 campaigns there too before injury forced him to retire.

He was appointed as manager of Canterbury's Under-21's side for the 2013/14 season.

name: Jackie Goodfellow
other clubs: Hamilton Academicals (Scotland) (0), Third Lanark (Scotland) (0), Burnbank Swifts (Scotland), Barry Town (Wales), Dartford, Dover and Yiewsley
bio:
Hard-shooting attacker born in Blantyre, Scotland who began his career with Scottish League club Third Lanark but never featured for their senior side before moving on to non-league outfit Burnbank Swifts.

In July 1954, Jackie signed for Welsh club Barry Town and Jackie scored over 20 goals in his first season there. He spent four years in Wales before signing for Dartford in the summer of 1958.

He went on to score 20 goals in 57 appearances for the Darts and Jackie s tally included a goal in a 5-3 home win over Margate in the Kent Senior Shield on 17.1.59.

In December 1959, Jackie was transferred to Margate and scored twice on his debut - a 4-0 win over Corby in the Southern League on 2.1.60 at Hartsdown Park. Jackie continued to find the net regularly during the remainder of the 1959/60 season and on 23.1.60 he scored a hat-trick in a 5-2 home win over Gloucester.

Jackie also caused Margate to be fined around £5 when he turned out in a Kent Senior Shield game against Sittingbourne on 9.3.60. Jackie scored in a 2-1 victory at Hartsdown Park but he'd already played for Dartford in the competition - against Sittingbourne - and was actually cup-tied. The match had to be replayed at Sittingbourne and Margate lost 3-1.

Jackie finished the campaign having scored 14 times from 21 outings but he was released at the end of the season.

He joined Dover for the 1960/61 campaign and spent two seasons at Crabble, during which he scored a total of nine goals.

In the summer of 1962, Jackie joined Yiewsley and on 27.2.63 he scored as they beat visitors Margate 3-2 in a Southern League Cup tie.

After two seasons out of football, Jackie had a trial with Ramsgate in the summer of 1965 but after featuring in a friendly against Gillingham he wasn t signed by the Rams.

name: Mark Goodfellow
other clubs: Chelsea (0), Leyton Orient (0), Purfleet, Thurrock, Welling United, Tonbridge Angels and AFC Hornchurch
bio:
London-born defender who started his career as a junior at Chelsea. Mark spent eight years there as a youngster before moving on to Leyton Orient.

He played alongside future Margate player Chris Wild in the O's reserves during the 2000/01 season and in March 2001 Mark dropped into non-league football to join Purfleet of the Isthmian League Premier Division.

He went on to spend over five years with the Essex club and former Margate legend Martin Buglione was one of Mark's team-mates during the early part of his stay at Ship Lane. Mark won both the Players' and Supporters' Player of the Year' awards at Purfleet for the 2002/03 campaign and in the summer of 2003 the club changed its name to Thurrock.

Mark fractured an ankle in March 2004 but recovered to play regularly again during the 2004/05 season, Thurrock's first in the Conference South. In October 2005 he was sent off in a 3-0 defeat at Woking in the 4th Qualifying Round of the FA Cup and Mark was so angry about his dismissal that he punched his way through a window in the changing room and ended up having to have stitches in his hand. He left Thurrock at the end of the 2005/06 campaign having made well over 200 appearances for the club in its two guises.

In July 2006 Mark signed for Conference South outfit Welling on a one-year contract and he played over 30 times for the Wings during 2006/07.

He moved on to Tonbridge of the Isthmian League Premier Division for the start of the 2007/08 season but Mark didn't make his debut for the Angels until 2.10.07 when he scored in a 3-0 win at Maldon in an FA Cup 2nd Qualifying Round replay. He'd been troubled with injuries until then and continued to struggle for fitness over the course of the next two months. Mark didn't play for Tonbridge again and at the start of January 2008 he signed for Margate.

Player-manager Robin Trott spoke to the Isle of Thanet Gazette in the wake of Mark's arrival and said "He's not played for a while but no one knows what his injury is. He's had a cortisone injection in his ankle but the experts can't find anything wrong with it. He's decent and will do a job in this league - a 100 per cent, no-nonsense centre-half."

Mark made his debut at centre-back in a 2-1 win over Ashford (Middlesex) in the Isthmian League Premier Division at Hartsdown Park on 5.1.08 and then scored in his next outing - a 4-2 home win over Carshalton on 19.1.08. He started each of the next five matches but after featuring in a 3-1 win over visitors Staines on 16.2.08 Mark missed five games due to injury.

He made a comeback as a substitute in a 3-3 draw with Wealdstone at Hartsdown Park on 22.3.08 but that turned out to be Mark's final appearance for Margate. He was released a few days later having scored once from eight outings (one as sub) and Robin Trott told the Thanet Times it was for budgetary reasons whilst adding "He wasn't playing to his full potential."

After a short spell out of football Mark linked up with AFC Hornchurch in June 2008 and he played regularly during the 2008/09 campaign, making 37 Isthmian League Premier Division appearances (two as sub) for the Urchins and scoring once. Mark's goal came in a 2-0 win over Margate at Hartsdown Park on 6.9.08. He then played 23 league games (three as sub) without scoring during the first half of the 2009/10 season before Hornchurch released him in February 2010. Mark then retired from football a few months before his 29th birthday.

In 2012 he was a partner in an accountancy firm based near Tonbridge.

name: Albert Goodman
other clubs: Tufnell Park, Crystal Palace, Maidstone United, Croydon Common, Clapton Orient (12,0), Tottenham Hotspur (16,1), Charlton Athletic (126,15), Gillingham (6,0) and Guildford City
bio:
5' 9" born in South Hackney, London. 
Captained London Fields School X1 and played for junior club Tottenham Thursday before starting senior career with Tufnell Park in 1911 
then spell with Southern League club Crystal Palace and there to Maidstone in 1913 - debut Nov 1913, 23, 4gls there. 
Then to Southern League  Croydon Common for 14/15 - 21,3 that season. They switched to London Combination for 15/16. He scored 5 goals in Croydon Common's penultimate match as a club and 43, 11 gls total there. 
Clapton Orient 16/17 and 17/18 in London Combination (wartime league) 6 apps 0 goals / 
back to Maidstone in March 1919 / 
to Spurs June 1919 - won Div 2 19/20 // - - 
Margate 20/21 -  - Margate to Charlton Jan 1921. 
Very versatile - Charlton's first genuine utility player - def, mid, att.  1st team debut 29.1.21 Ports 2 C 1 Southern League - 10 apps, 0 gls 20/21 (in addition to games for Margate) 
Despite Charlton debut 29.1.21 Albert played for Margate the following Sat - 5.2.21 - a 2-1 home defeat v Charlton (!) Reserves, at least 4 more apps for Margate over next few weeks then gap and back for last 2 of season.  Must have been loan / dual reg 
Played in Charlton's first ever League match (27.8.21 v Exeter (h)) 
Scored when Charlton won London Challenge Cup 4.12.22 C 2, Cpal 1.

name: Gareth Gore
other clubs: Charlton Athletic (0), Brighton & Hove Albion (0), Maidstone United, Erith & Belvedere, Aveley, Barking and Hornchurch
bio:
6' 4" tall defender born in Barking who had a spell at Charlton as a junior before joining Brighton. Gareth played for the Seagulls' youth team alongside future Margate player Roy Hales during the 1987/88 and 1988/89 seasons and then moved to Maidstone during 1989/90.

In the summer of 1990 Gareth signed for Margate and made his debut on the opening day of the 1990/91 season in a 2-2 draw at Witney. He missed Margate's next match but returned for a 2-2 draw with Burnham at Hartsdown Park on 25.8.90. Gareth then fell out of favour and in October 1990 he was loaned to Erith & Belvedere, playing for them as they drew 2-2 at home to Margate in a Southern League Cup tie on 16.10.90. He also played in the return leg at Hartsdown Park on 30.10.90 and incurred the wrath of the Isle of Thanet Gazette as the Deres went down 4-3. The paper said that Gareth was "hapless" and made "two woeful errors...(that) resulted in crucial goals". One of the mistakes was a weak headed back-pass that led to Margate's Paul Underwood finding the net. Gareth stayed with the Deres until December 1990 when he returned to Hartsdown Park after breaking his nose in the last game of his loan spell at Yate. He then made five appearances for Margate's reserves, scoring twice in the process, but never played for the first team again and left the club in February 1991.

Gareth spent 1991/92 with Aveley.

He joined Barking for the 1992/93 season and made nine appearances (one as sub) without scoring before leaving the club.

He moved to Hornchurch for the 1993/94 campaign.

In 2024 Gareth was living in Havering, Essex and working in London as a Global Account Director for a company called Colt Technology Services.

His older brother Shaun, also a centre-back, played professionally for Fulham and made 26 first team appearances for them in a six year spell with the club that began in 1985.

name: Jim Gorman
other clubs: Deal Town
bio:
Striker who played Sunday League football in the Thanet area for the likes of Saracens and Northwood in the late 1970 s. Jim was also picked for the Thanet Premier Sunday League s representative side.

He later moved into senior football with Kent League club Deal.

Jim joined Thanet United from Deal early in the 1981/82 season and made his debut in a 2-1 defeat against Tonbridge at Hartsdown Park on 29.8.81. After failing to score in his first five appearances for United, Jim was moved into midfield for two games but then returned to the forward line. He finally broke his scoring duck when he found the net in a 4-1 defeat at Poole on 3.10.81. It was Jim's only goal for the club and he departed in December 1981 having made 16 appearances.
