name: Leroy Griffiths
other clubs: Arsenal (0), Wimbledon (0), Sutton United, Banstead Athletic, Corinthian Casuals, Hampton & Richmond Borough, Queens Park Rangers (27+10,3), Farnborough Town, Grays Athletic, Fisher Athletic (London), Aldershot Town, Havant & Waterlooville, Lewes, Gillingham (4+21,2), Eastleigh, Staines Town, Athlitikos Omilos Ayias (Cyprus), Redhill, Thurrock, Harrow Borough and Leatherhead
bio:
Aggressive striker who started his career in Arsenal's junior ranks before moving on to Wimbledon. Leroy scored once in four Football Combination appearances (one as sub) for the Dons' reserves during 1994/95 and then dropped into non-league football.

He had spells with Sutton and Banstead before joining Corinthian Casuals in the summer of 1998.

Leroy scored 23 goals in 49 appearances for Casuals and then moved on to Hampton & Richmond in January 2000.

In his early days with Hampton & Richmond Leroy cut a distinctive figure with his silver boots and black gloves and he scored three goals before the end of the 1999/00 campaign. Leroy had a trial with Norwich in the summer of 2000 and then made a real name for himself during 2000/01. His 19 goals for Hampton & Richmond prompted Queens Park Rangers to pay £40,000 for him in June 2001.

Leroy made his debut for QPR as a substitute in a 1-0 win over Stoke at Loftus Road on 11.8.01 but picked up an injury and had to be replaced himself just ten minutes after taking to the field. He made his full debut in a 2-1 defeat at Brighton on 8.9.01 and opened his account for the R's when he got both goals in a 2-2 draw at Blackpool on 18.9.01. By the end of the 2001/02 campaign Leroy had made 31 senior appearances but only scored once more.

He was loaned out to Conference club Farnborough for the start of the 2002/03 season and Leroy made five appearances there (four as sub) without scoring before returning to QPR at the end of September 2002.

He then made one first team appearance for Rangers - as a substitute in a 0-0 draw at Port Vale on 2.11.02 - before joining Margate on loan a few days later.

Leroy made his debut in a 1-1 draw with Telford in a Conference game played at Margate's adopted home in Dover on 9.11.02 and the Nationwide football website said he "failed to make an impact". He was substituted after an hour but the Thanet Times said Leroy had "worked hard and showed some good touches". He then made substitute appearances in a 5-0 defeat at Chester on 23.11.02 and a 2-1 defeat at Yeovil on 30.11.02 before returning to QPR.

Leroy had five further first team outings for QPR during the second half of 2002/03 but at the end of the season he was released.

After leaving Loftus Road he had a trial with Staines before signing for Farnborough in August 2003. Leroy's second spell with the club was tarnished by reports of him biting an opponent in a Conference game and after scoring once in five appearances he moved on to Grays in September 2003, signing a full-time contract with the ambitious Essex outfit.

Leroy went on to score 14 goals from 43 appearances (four as sub) for Grays during 2003/04. His tally included two goals in a 3-3 home draw with Margate in an FA Cup tie on 25.10.03. Leroy then bagged 27 goals from 42 outings (six as sub) during the 2004/05 season before being released having fallen out with his manager.

He joined Fisher for the start of the 2005/06 season and on 24.10.06 Leroy scored in a 2-1 win over Margate at Dulwich. The Isle of Thanet Gazette's report said he should then have been sent off for "stamping on and punching Blues centre-back James Smith" but Leroy was only booked. Very shortly afterwards he was substituted.

In January 2006 Fisher loaned Leroy to Aldershot and he scored twice on his Conference debut for the Shots - a 3-1 home win over Halifax on 21.1.06. He ended up with seven goals from 17 appearances (one as sub) before going back to Fisher in May 2006.

Leroy's return to the Dockers saw him turn out for the club in the Conference South play-offs at the end of 2005/06 and he finished the season with 16 goals for Fisher. He stayed with the club for the start of the 2006/07 campaign but in February 2007 Leroy was loaned back to Grays. He scored twice in 13 appearances (seven as sub) before returning to Fisher at the end of the season.

In May 2007 Fisher released their entire squad so in July 2007 Leroy signed for Havant & Waterlooville. He found his opportunities limited with the Hampshire club, partly due to the form of former Margate striker Rocky Baptiste, and in mid-October 2007 Leroy returned to Corinthian Casuals over seven years after leaving the club.

He only played twice for Casuals but scored two goals before quickly moving on to Lewes towards the end of October 2007.

Leroy scored once for Lewes in a handful of outings for the club before landing a surprise move back into the Football League in November 2007. He was signed by League One club Gillingham who were managed by his former Grays boss Mark Stimson.

Leroy was given a short-term deal and said "I'm delighted to be here. I've endured a topsy-turvy season but the gaffer knows what type of player I am. He knows all about my game and gets the best out of me. I'm a player with pace, power and aggression. I'm also very direct and will give my all here at Gillingham. I'm only here initially for a month but if I come in and do what I know I can then hopefully that will be extended."

Leroy made his debut for the Gills in a 2-1 defeat at Yeovil on 18.11.07 and scored his first goal for the club after coming on as a substitute in a 3-0 win over Nottingham Forest at Priestfield on 29.12.07. In January 2008 he signed a contract to the end of the 2007/08 season and Leroy was used regularly as a substitute for the remainder of the campaign but only scored once more. He was released by Gillingham at the end of the season.

In the summer of 2008 Leroy joined Conference South club Eastleigh but only played once before linking up with Staines of the Isthmian Premier Division at the end of August 2008.

After a handful of games for Staines Leroy was on the move again as in September 2008 he joined Cypriot outfit Athlitikos Omilos Ayias who played in the second tier of football in Cyprus.

In January 2009 Leroy returned to Staines and finished 2008/09 having scored four goals from 21 Isthmian League appearances (two as sub) during the season as the club won promotion to the Conference South via the play-offs.

Leroy stayed at Staines until February 2011 when he joined Isthmian Premier Division club Sutton for a second spell after his stint there early in his career. He scored seven goals from 16 league outings as Sutton won the title.

Leroy stayed with the Surrey club for the 2011/12 season and on 1.10.11 he scored four goals as Sutton beat visitors Dulwich 5-1 in an FA Cup tie. He was released by Sutton in June 2012.

In the summer of 2012 Leroy linked up with Sussex County League outfit Redhill and scored twice on his debut in a 5-2 home win over Chichester on 4.8.12.

In September 2012 he moved on to Isthmian League Premier Division club Thurrock and on 8.9.12 Leroy was on target in his first outing for them - a 3-0 win at Basildon in the FA Cup. He scored twice more in FA Trophy ties but only featured three times in the league (once as sub) without getting on the scoresheet before leaving the club.

Leroy spent the remainder of 2012/13 back at Sutton where he scored once from 16 Conference South outings (11 as sub) to take his overall tally for the club to 22 goals from 88 appearances.

In July 2013 Leroy signed for Harrow of the Isthmian League Premier Division and by then he was 36.

In September 2013 he moved on to Isthmian League Division 1 South outfit Leatherhead and at the end of February 2014 Leroy went back to Premier Division Grays for a third spell with the club.

name: Mal Griffiths
other clubs: Merthyr Thursday (Wales), Arsenal (9,5), Leicester City (374,67) and Burton Albion
bio:
5' 7" Welsh right winger born in Merthyr who began his career playing in local football in his home town and then for Methyr 
Then Banbury Spencer in Birmingham Combination
before joining Arsenal as an amateur in September 1935. 
To Margate May 1936, back to Highbury end of Feb 37 and signed pro February 1937.  
11 reserve team games for Arsenal 36/37, 2 goals 
May / June 1937 part of Arsenal party that toured Sweden, Denmark and Holland.  
Regular reserve team winger and 9 first team end of 37/38.  Debut v Leicester on 2.2.38 19 gls in 38 reserve team apps // 8.1.38 - in Arsenal Reserves side that won 2-1 in friendly at Margate, one of 6 players in the team who d previously been at Margate  //
 2,0 for Arsenal s Southern League team (one step down from reserves) during 1938/39
then to Leicester September 1938 for  800 - 18 years there !  
Retired end of 55/56 and to Burton part time, became publican Queen s Head, Bull Head Street, Wigston, Leicester 1958-1969
Won 11 Welsh caps - became only 2nd Leicester player to appear in WC qual.  
Finished career with Burton. 
real first name William Died in 5 April 1969 aged 50.  
William Malwyn Griffiths

name: Micky Griffiths
other clubs: Crystal Palace (0), Dover, Crawley Town, Hastings United, Hillingdon Borough, Wealdstone and Tonbridge
bio:
Tenacious winger who began his career at Crystal Palace and scored eight times in 51 reserve team appearances for the Eagles spanning the 1961/62 to 1964/65 seasons before joining Dover in September 1964.

Micky scored 15 goals for Dover before the end of 1964/65 and top scored with 23 goals the following season. During 1966/67 he scored 16 times and during September and October 1965 Micky found the net in six consecutive matches. His tally included a hat-trick as Dover won 4-0 at Canterbury in a Kent Floodlight League tie on 15.11.66 and the goal that sealed a 1-0 win over Margate in the 2nd Leg of the Kent Senior Cup Final at Crabble on 6.4.67. Dover won 6-0 on aggregate.

The 1967/68 campaign saw Micky score 13 goals and on 15.4.68 he found the net in a 2-2 home draw with Margate. On 8.5.68 he was one of the marksmen as Dover beat Bexley 3-0 to win the Kent Senior Cup. Micky spent one more season at Dover, scoring once to take his overall goal tally for the club to 68, and then moved to Margate in the summer of 1969. Manager Almer Hall had initially tried to sign him when he'd left Crystal Palace.

Shortly after his arrival at Hartsdown Park, Micky suffered an elbow injury that kept him out of action for the first month of the 1969/70 season. He made his debut when he came on as a substitute in a 3-0 defeat at Barnet on 6.9.69 and his first full appearance came in a 2-2 draw with Chelmsford at Hartsdown Park on 13.9.69. Micky found it difficult to gain a regular place in the first team but showed flashes of ability, particularly with his accurate crossing, when he did feature.

On 25.10.69 Micky was the pick of the Margate attack in a 2-0 win over Kettering and he received a tremendous ovation from the Hartsdown Park crowd when he went off injured towards the end of the game. On 15.11.69 he was in the Margate side that were thrashed 7-2 by visitors Aldershot in the FA Cup 1st Round but Micky only made nine appearances (two as sub) before leaving the club in December 1969. He scored twice and one of the goals was with his first touch after coming on as a substitute in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie against Sheppey at Hartsdown Park on 8.9.69.

Micky joined Crawley after leaving Margate and on 18.3.70 he got their goal in a 2-1 home defeat against Margate. Micky went on to score 21 Southern League goals for Crawley during the 1970/71 season.

He later had a lengthy spell with Hastings which spanned the 1972/73 to 1975/76 campaigns.

In the summer of 1976 Micky joined Hillingdon and towards the end of the 1976/77 season he moved on to Wealdstone.

Micky stayed at Wealdstone until March 1978 when he signed for Tonbridge.

He made over 20 appearances for the Angels during the 1978/79 season, often playing as a left-back.

name: Peter Griffiths
bio:
Left winger born in Thanet who was principally a reserve team player but also played for the first team on occasions.

Peter made his debut in Margate's first game after World War II - a 1-1 draw at Gillingham Reserves on 31.8.46 and went on to make seven first team appearances during the 1946/47 season.

He also played three times for the senior side towards the end of the 1947/48 campaign and managed to score twice during those games, his first goal coming on 1.5.48 in a 7-3 home defeat at the hands of Maidstone.

Peter stayed with the club for the 1948/49 season but played exclusively for the reserves.

He continued playing for them during the 1949/50 campaign too but also made two first team appearances towards the end of the season.

Peter was still playing for the reserves during the 1951/52 season and scored 14 goals for them.

He was the younger brother of long-serving Margate / Thanet United official Bob Griffiths and Peter also played table tennis for Margate in the Kent League along with future Margate great Terry Joyce. In addition Peter played cricket locally for many years.

name: Sam Groombridge
other clubs: Gravesend & Northfleet, Sevenoaks Town, Thamesmead Town, Chatham Town, Tilbury, Slade Green, Croydon, Holmesdale, Bromley, Whitstable Town, Sittingbourne, Maidstone United, Erith & Belvedere and Corinthian
bio:
Sidcup-born player who started his career with Gravesend & Northfleet and progressed through the club s junior ranks into the first team squad during the 2004/05 campaign.

In November 2004 Sam was loaned to Kent League outfit Sevenoaks and after returning to the Fleet he made one substitute appearance in the Conference at the end of 2004/05 aged 17.

He captained the Fleet s youth team during the 2005/06 season but in September 2006 Sam left the club and joined Kent League side Thamesmead.

He usually played as a right-back for Thamesmead and Sam stayed with the club until January 2007 when he signed for Chatham.

He went on to make 17 Isthmian League Division 1 South appearances (three as sub) without scoring for Chatham before the end of the 2006/07 campaign. Sam stayed with the club for the start of 2007/08 and on 15.9.07 he was in the Chatham side that lost 3-0 at home to Margate in the FA Cup. Sam had made ten league appearances (one as sub) without scoring when he moved on to Tilbury in January 2008.

He spent the remainder of 2007/08 with the Isthmian League Division 1 North outfit and featured 16 times (twice as sub) in league matches without scoring before leaving the club at the end of the season.

Sam joined Slade Green of the Kent League in the summer of 2008 and became the club s captain aged just 20. However he only made 19 appearances during 2008/09 due to a knee ligament injury that kept him out of action for an extended period.

Sam started the 2009/10 campaign with Combined Counties League outfit Croydon but left them in September 2009 after scoring once from six outings.

His next move took him to Holmesdale and Sam scored twice as they beat Sporting Bengal 3-2 in the Kent League on 20.10.09.

In November 2009 he joined Conference South club Bromley and Sam played a few games for their reserves before signing for Margate at the start of December 2009.

He made his debut in a 2-2 draw with Harrow at Hartsdown Park in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 5.12.09 and from then on Sam was a regular in the side at centre-back. On 16.1.10 he scored his first goal for Margate when he knocked home a loose ball following an Aaron Lacy free-kick in a 1-1 draw with visitors Ashford (Middlesex) and Sam wore the number five shirt nine times up to and including a 3-2 home defeat against Hendon on 6.2.10. He then went out to the Middle East for an extended trial with a club there and missed seven Margate matches altogether.

Having returned to the UK Sam made his first appearance for four weeks when he came on as a substitute in a 2-1 win at Billericay on 13.3.10 and he then featured as a sub in three of the next four matches but after a 1-1 draw at Boreham Wood on 27.3.10 he sat out four games completely. He made his first start for over two months in a 1-0 defeat at Wealdstone on 7.4.10 but then missed Margate s last three matches as the club avoided relegation despite finishing in the drop zone. Sam had made a total of 14 appearances (four as sub) and scored once during 2009/10.

On the eve of the new season Margate manager Iain O Connell spoke about Sam to the Isle of Thanet Gazette and said Tough-tackling centre half but he s the worst 12-minute runner in the world. Even Bungle (keeper Jamie Turner) beat him !"

Sam didn t feature at all in the first five games of 2010/11 but on 11.9.10 he wore the number three shirt in a 3-0 win at Binfield in the FA Cup. He then sat out another seven matches before playing at centre-back in a 5-2 home defeat against Thamesmead in the Isthmian League Cup on 12.10.10. Sam s stop-start campaign continued with a sub outing in Margate s next game - a 5-1 win over Whitehawk in an FA Trophy tie at Hartsdown Park on 16.10.10 - and then a three match absence before he wore the number five shirt in a 2-0 home defeat against Bromley in the Kent Senior Cup on 2.11.10.

Later in November 2010 Sam was loaned to Isthmian League Division 1 South club Whitstable and he made four league appearances there before returning to Margate towards the end of December 2010.

On 27.12.10 Sam finally made his first Isthmian League Premier Division appearance of the season when he played at centre-back in a 2-0 home defeat against Cray and he then featured in three of Margate s next five games, once as a substitute.

He was moved into a defensive midfield position for a 1-1 draw with Hendon at Hartsdown Park on 25.1.11 and from then on Sam was a regular for the remainder of the campaign, almost always featuring in his holding role. However his last outing of the season was at centre-back in a 3-3 draw with visitors Kingstonian on 30.4.11 and that turned out to be Sam s final game for Margate. He d made 25 appearances (five as sub) without scoring during 2010/11 and then left the club shortly after the campaign ended.

In the summer of 2011 Sam joined Sittingbourne and he made 11 appearances (three as sub) without scoring for the Division 1 South outfit before moving on to Maidstone in December 2011.

Former Margate star Jay Saunders was the Stones player-manager at the time and Sam scored once from 17 Division 1 South outings up to the end of 2011/12.

In the summer of 2012 he featured in some friendlies for his old club Chatham but Sam ended up signing for Whitstable in August 2012.

By October 2012 he d left the Oystermen after only playing three times and Sam then spent some time playing for North Kent Sunday League side Valley Rovers. He was the subject of an approach from Hythe at the start of November 2012 - Whitstable still held Sam s registration - but the move didn t happen.

In January 2013 Sam s exile from senior football ended when he signed for Kent League outfit Erith & Belvedere.

In the summer of 2013 he moved on to Corinthian who played in the Southern Counties East Football League, formerly known as the Kent League.

Early in May 2014 Sam rejoined Erith & Belvedere, following Corinthian manager Matt Longhurst to the Southern Counties East Football League club. Sam became Longhurst s assistant as well as playing for the Deres.

His younger brother Ashley was briefly on Margate s books during the 2009/10 season and then joined the club again for 2011/12 but never featured in the first team. Ashley later had a spell with Ramsgate.

name: Bob Grover
other clubs: Gillingham (0), Maidstone United, Sheppey United, Gravesend & Northfleet, Chatham Town, Sittingbourne, Dover Athletic, Whitstable Town, Teynham & Lynsted and Borden Village
bio:
Much-travelled keeper born in Teynham, near Sittingbourne who started his career with Gillingham in 1978 and played for the club's youth and reserve teams before joining Maidstone in 1980.

Bob played for the Stones' reserve side prior to joining Sheppey in 1981 and becoming their first-choice keeper.

In 1983 Bob signed for Gravesend & Northfleet and made five first team appearances for the Fleet during the 1982/83 season.

Bob then played for Sheppey and Chatham during the 1983/84 season before linking up with Sittingbourne for the 1984/85 campaign. He also made two appearances for Dover early in the 1985/86 season.

Bob then returned to Sittingbourne once more and in November 1986 he joined Thanet United as a replacement for Glen Porter who was himself deputising for the injured Joe Radford. Bob made his debut in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Ashford on 11.11.86 and was kept busy as United went down 3-0. He kept his place for Thanet's next match, away to Poole on 15.11.86, and played a starring role in a 2-1 win. The Thanet Times' report for the game was headlined "Agile Grover defies Poole strike force" and went on to say that Bob was the "hero of the afternoon...who pulled off a string of fine saves". They included a full length diving stop to prevent what looked like a certain goal in the opening minutes. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said that Bob had "created a good impression" and showed "considerable potential". Thanet manager John Wickens said that Bob was "settling in well" but after he'd made five consecutive appearances, the last in a 3-2 defeat at Woodford on 26.11.86, Radford returned from injury to reclaim his first team place and Bob left the club.

He went back to Sittingbourne once more and then had a spell with Whitstable before joining Chatham for the 1987/88 season.

In October 1988 Bob rejoined Thanet on loan from Chatham, again as cover for the injured Radford, and his first game back was a 2-2 draw at Ruislip on 29.10.88. The Adscene said that Bob "saw plenty of action" in United's next match - a 2-1 home defeat against Trowbridge on 5.11.88 - but a few days later he had to miss a Southern League Cup tie against Dover due to being cup-tied. He returned to the side for a 6-2 thrashing at Tonbridge on 12.11.88 but then went back to Chatham as Radford was fit again.

In January 1989 Bob rejoined United for a third spell, this time because Radford was suspended for three matches. Bob made his second 'debut' of the 1988/89 season on 21.1.89 as Thanet lost 4-0 at home to Andover and it was a game of contrasting fortunes for him. After making a point-blank save early on Bob allowed an inswinging corner to float over his head and into the net and later made what the Thanet Times called "two daring saves" before being lobbed from 25 yards for Andover's fourth goal. A week later United lost 6-2 at Witney and the Adscene said that Bob was "constantly in action, making save after save". On 4.2.89 he made his sixth appearance of the season, and his last for the club, as Thanet entertained Bury at Hartsdown. The visitors won 2-0 and the Thanet Times blamed Bob for their first goal, saying it was "virtually a replica of one he gave to Andover a fortnight earlier". Again it was an inswinging corner that deceived Bob, the ball slipping through his hands to give a Bury player a tap-in.

After leaving Chatham in the summer of 1990 Bob joined Dover for the 1990/91 season and he later dropped into amateur football, playing for Teynham & Lynsted from 1991/92 to 1993/94 and turning out for Borden Village from 1994/95 to 1997/98.

Bob retired in 1998 and in 2004 he was working for a paper production company called the UPM-Kymmene Group. By 2006 he had moved on to Burgo, an Italian paper company.

name: Sid Gueran
other clubs: Arsenal (0), Southampton (3,0), Exeter City (0)
bio:
Born in Grays, Essex, before moving to Ramsgate as a child where he attended St George s Central School, their Junior Sports champion for 1930 having been runner-up in 1928
Represented Ramsgate Schools, first playing for them at unusually early age of 11 during 1927/28
1929/30 played 4 times for Kent
Ramsgate Schools 1929/30 aged 13 as captain   East Kent Times said he was  one of the most stylish players in the town eleven 
1930/31 was 4th seasons with Ramsgate Schools and played for Kent again that season. Also played in England Schoolboy trial match - 7.2.31 Southern trial East v West at Norwich. He played for the West as they lost 5-0 and was selected as reserve for South v North in Manchester on 7.3.31.
April 1931 toured Leicestershire with Kent, won all 3 games. One was 3-1 over Leicestershire Boys at Leicester FC. Captain for 1 of matches   a 3-0 win at Kettering.
2.5.31 played for Ramsgate v Dover at Crabble in Kent Schoolboys cup final   ended 2-2. Replay at Ramsgate (Southwood) on 9.5.31 watched by 7,000, won 1-0 after extra time
Joined Ramsgate Grenville (East Kent Amateur League) for 1932/33 aged 16 debut 27.8.32 as lost 2-1 to Betteshanger at Southwood, Thanet Advertiser wrote "although he did his best he could not cope with the pace"
Also played for local club Olbys
He joined Arsenal as an 18-year-old in May 1935 and was "farmed out" to play for Margate, Arsenal's nursery side. Signed as pro by Margate ahead of 36/37
Southampton 36/37   joined on loan from Arsenal in March 1937 and debut v Notts Forest at home on 1.5.37 - and 37/38, - still on loan from Arsenal that season
Described as "a thoughtful and constructive inside-forward",
Gueran spent most of his "Saints" career in the reserves, but was given a run-out in the first team in the last match of the 1936 37 season, when he replaced Wilf Mayer in a 3 0 defeat at home to Nottingham Forest.
Gueran made two further appearances in the opening matches of the next season, both defeats, before Arthur Holt took over at inside-right. Gueran then returned to reserve-team football, before being recalled by Arsenal in May 1938.
Exeter 38/39 (joined July 1938) 
Transferred permanently to Exeter City of the Third Division South, where he was describing by the Football Express as a scheming inside forward, but failed to break into the first-team.
The Football Express of Jan 28, 1939 reports that Sid was not retained by City in October 1938 and that he had joined his brother at Kent Senior League Canterbury Waverley.
With Cant Wav start of 39/40 too - played for them in friendly v Margate. On the outbreak of World War II, Gueran enlisted in the Royal Engineers as a sapper attached to the 1st Parachute Squadron 
November 1939 and December 1939 played at least twice for Ramsgate Grenville alongside older brother Stan - Stan featured in Margate's reserve team during 1937/38. He tragically died in January 1946 aged only 25 after a fortnight's illness.
2 years in Middle East plus Central Mediterranean and North Africa in Royal Engineers
End of 1943 volunteered for paratroop duties and back to England for training.
Killed on the second day of the Battle of Arnhem 18.9.44 aged 27 - 1st Parachute Squadron Royal Engineers, 1st Airborne Division. Landed, ran for cover in school building then 
Lance-Sergeant Harold Padfield was in charge of post overlooking bridge there - in Limburg Stirum school "I went to Sid Gueran and set him up on a desk so that he could comfortably sit and cover a vital area to the West through his porthole window. I was telling him the area I wanted him to cover and couldn't understand why I wasn't getting a response, when I turned towards him he was sat upright, and my first loss He had been shot through the mouth; it must have been a stray bullet because I certainly didn't hear anything. 
http://www.arnhemarchive.org/harold_padfield.htm // 
http://www.rogallo.co.uk/aea/rolls/1parasqn.htm Brother Stan killed in action too 
He is commemorated on the Groesbeek Memorial in the Groesbeek Canadian War Cemetery.
In May 1954 Sid s parents visited the Netherlands to see grave   Sid s unknown but one of 57 possibles   and the school where he died
There is a book published in 2019, on Arnhem and there is a chapter on the 1st Parachute Squadron Royal Engineers which includes Sid story. Sid was in B Troop & sadly has no known grave but is remembered on the Groesbeek Memorial. He made it to the bridge at Arnhem but was in the old school house when he was shot & killed. The school was then destroyed by enemy tanks & a fire.
His niece went to Arnhem for the book launch & to see where his medals have gone on display in the exhibition museum by the bridge.
There is a plaque in the clubs memorial garden at Exeter City Football Club, remembering Sid.
Also talented cricketer   played for Ramsgate Corinthians    https://www.saintsplayers.co.uk/player/sid-gueran/
For many years parents put annual memoriam notice in Thanet local papers, even as late as 1979. Parents Sid and Florence lived in Thanet and died there, Sid in 1983 aged 97 and Florence in 1988 aged 95.

name: George Guild
other clubs: Tamworth and Atherstone Town
bio:
Centre-forward born in Atherstone who attended Nethersole Boys School in Polesworth, Warwickshire and played for the school team in the Tamworth and District Schools Senior Shield during the 1937/38 season.

George later featured for Polesworth Boys Club in the Tamworth and Trent Valley League as a 16 year-old and on 9.9.44 he scored a hat-trick in 12-0 win over Home Guard of Polesworth.

George s senior career began when he joined Tamworth for the 1945/46 campaign aged 17. He made his debut on 29.9.45 as they lost 3-2 at home to City Transport in the Birmingham Combination. George went on to score 12 goals in 24 appearances during the remainder of the season.

He joined Atherstone of the Birmingham Combination in the summer of 1946 and spent the whole of the 1946/47 season there, mostly playing in the reserves.

George rejoined Tamworth for the 1947/48 campaign and scored six goals from 15 appearances before leaving the club again at the end of the season.

He spent 1948/49 playing for Wilnecote in the Tamworth and Trent Valley League and in December 1948 George was picked for the league s Representative X1 to play against an Oldbury and District Junior League side.

In August 1949 George signed for Margate and made his debut in a 4-1 defeat at Bowaters Lloyd on 7.9.49. It turned out to be his only first team outing and he quickly returned to the Midlands. In December 1949 George made a brief return to Margate and played twice for the reserves. After the second of those games - a 4-1 win over Aylesford Paper Mills Reserves at Hartsdown Park on 17.12.49 - he returned home permanently.

George rejoined Tamworth shortly afterwards and played once for their first team in January 1950.

During the 1950/51 campaign he was back playing local football for Polesworth Boys Club.

name: Steve Hafner
other clubs: Gillingham (0), Sittingbourne, Gravesend & Northfleet, Folkestone Invicta, Dover Athletic, Hastings United, Chatham Town, Dartford, Maldon Town, Erith & Belvedere, Hollands and Blair and Whitstable Town
bio:
Versatile Chatham-born player who started his career as a trainee with Gillingham. Steve spent a couple of years on the Gills' books before being released towards the end of the 2000/01 campaign.

Immediately after leaving Priestfield he had a brief spell with Sittingbourne before finishing the season at Gravesend & Northfleet. Steve played four times (one as sub) for the Fleet in the Isthmian League Premier Division.

In the summer of 2001 Steve signed for Margate ahead of the club's first-ever Conference campaign and after a few weeks on the bench he made his debut as a substitute in a 2-2 draw at Stalybridge on 22.9.01. On 9.10.01 Steve came on to good effect in the second half as Margate won 2-1 at Yeovil and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "impressed" in place of the injured Gary Blackford at right-back. Towards the end of the game Steve embarked on a 40-yard run that was only ended by a crude challenge which earned Lee Johnson (son of Yeovil manager Gary Johnson) a second yellow card. On 20.10.01 Steve made his first start when he wore the number two shirt as Margate lost 2-1 at home to Northwich and he kept his place for a disastrous 2-0 defeat at Grays in the FA Cup on 27.10.01. After that his appearances became very sporadic but on 13.11.01 Steve scored in a 3-1 win over Bromley in the Kent Senior Cup at Hartsdown Park. He played as a winger in that match. On 20.11.01 Steve got both goals as the reserves beat Ramsgate's second string 2-1 and on 1.12.01 he replaced Gary Blackford after 34 minutes of a home game against Boston. Steve's performance impressed the Thanet Times and the paper said he was "quickly earning himself a reputation as a talented right-sided player". The match finished 1-1.

Steve didn't feature at all in Margate's first four games of 2002 but on 2.2.02 he played at right-back in a 2-0 win over visitors Leigh in the FA Trophy, it was his first start since 24.11.01. Steve also wore the number two shirt in Margate's next match - a 0-0 draw with Chester at Hartsdown Park on 9.2.02 - before dropping out of the first team picture for a month. He scored twice for the reserves in a 6-3 home win over Folkestone Reserves early in March 2002 and Steve then played as a striker in a 2-1 win at Folkestone in the Kent Senior Cup on 19.3.02. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "showed flashes of skill throughout the match". He didn't feature in any of Margate's next five games but on 8.4.02 Steve replaced Nick Roddis during a 2-0 defeat at Telford and the Gazette said he was "one of Margate's better performers". In the closing weeks of the season Steve was a regular in the senior squad once more and he played in each of Margate's last four games. Although two of his appearances were as a substitute it was the only time during the campaign that Steve had featured in more than two consecutive matches. On 6.5.02 he lined up at right-back as Margate took on Gravesend & Northfleet in the Kent Senior Cup Final at Hartsdown Park and Steve was booked for what the Isle of Thanet Gazette called "an eye-watering late tackle" as Margate were thrashed 5-0. It was the last game of the season and Steve's final appearance for the club as he was released having scored once in a total of 17 outings (eight as sub).

Steve joined Folkestone for the start of the 2002/03 campaign and scored twice in 23 appearances (one as sub) there before being released in January 2003.

He then linked up with Sittingbourne but only spent a few weeks with the Brickies before signing for Dover in February 2003.

Steve's next move took him to Hastings in August 2003 and he went from there to Chatham in March 2004.

In the summer of 2004 he rejoined Hastings and made nine Isthmian League appearances (two as sub) without scoring before linking up with Dartford in December 2004.

Steve moved to Maldon in June 2005 and on 20.8.05 he was part of their side that took on Margate in the club's first game back at Hartsdown Park following three seasons of exile at Dover and then Ashford. Steve made six appearances (three as sub) for Maldon in the Isthmian Premier League and then went back to Dartford in September 2005.

He went on to make over 70 appearances for the Darts before being released at the end of the 2006/07 season.

In June 2007 Steve rejoined Sittingbourne and their manager Steve Lovell said "He's very energetic, got good pace, a good crosser and he can score goals." Steve scored twice in 23 Isthmian League appearances (five as sub) for the Brickies and then embarked on a second spell with Chatham in February 2008.

On 8.4.08 Steve bagged a hat-trick in a 6-1 win at Molesey and ended 2007/08 having scored six goals in ten Isthmian League appearances (two as sub) for Chatham. He stayed with the club for the start of the 2008/09 campaign and scored once in seven league appearances before dropping out of football for a while towards the end of 2008.

In March 2009 Steve joined Kent League outfit Erith & Belvedere but he only made one substitute appearance before leaving the club.

He went back to Chatham for the start of the 2009/10 season but after scoring once in four league appearances Steve left the club again before Christmas 2009.

Sadly in the summer of 2010 he was diagnosed with testicular cancer and Steve later endured months of chemotherapy that at one stage left him fighting for his life after his immune system collapsed. He spent six days in intensive care before recovering. He managed to play twice for Hollands and Blair in the Kent County League during 2010/11 before giving up football, for a while at least.

Happily by September 2011 Steve was in remission and on 18.9.11 he took part in the 'Run Together in Medway' race to raise money for Cancer Relief UK. At that time he was co-owner of a plumbing and heating business in the Medway area.

In March 2012 Steve resumed his football career when he rejoined Hollands and Blair who by then had graduated to the new Kent Invicta League. On 15.4.12 he was part of the side that won the Kent Senior Trophy by beating Sevenoaks 2-1 in the final played at Welling's Park View Road ground.

Steve also played for Hollands and Blair during the 2012/13 season.

In July 2013 he featured in some friendlies for Isthmian League Division 1 South club Whitstable and Steve was signed by the club ahead of the 2013/14 campaign.

name: Ivan Haines
other clubs: Gillingham (56+8,0) and Sittingbourne
bio:
Defender who played for Medway Colts as a schoolboy before joining Gillingham in August 1984. Ivan was virtually ever-present in the Gills' youth team for three seasons after making his debut aged 15 and in July 1987 he was signed as a professional. He made his first team debut during the 1987/88 campaign and in the summer of 1990 Ivan played for Gillingham in a friendly at Margate. After making 64 senior appearances (eight as sub) he was released by the Gills in the summer of 1991 along with future Margate players Michael Harle and Dave Jordan. All three players joined Sittingbourne for the 1991/92 season.

Ivan left the Brickies at the end of 1992/93 and in the summer of 1993 he appeared in friendlies for Dover before signing for Margate.

He made his debut in a 0-0 draw with Fareham at Hartsdown Park on 21.8.93, the opening day of the 1993/94 campaign, and the Thanet Times said he "proved a fine sweeper" behind centre-backs Billy Plews and player-manager Mark Weatherly. Ivan became a fixture in the Margate side from then on and was equally comfortable in either a sweeper or traditional centre-back role. The Thanet Times described him as "sturdy" in its report on a 2-0 home defeat against Baldock on 6.11.93 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Ivan was "outstanding" in a 2-0 win at Ashford on 16.11.93. In March 1994 the same paper said he had been "reliability personified" throughout the season but on 9.4.94 Ivan was sent off in a 4-1 defeat at Gravesend & Northfleet and missed three matches as a result of his suspension. He returned to the Margate side on 2.5.94 when he took over from Jason Fenton at left-back for the Kent Senior Cup Final against Dover at his old club Gillingham's Priestfield Stadium. It was a happy return as Margate took the trophy with a 2-1 victory. Ivan kept his place for the club's last two matches of 1993/94, wearing the number three shirt in each of them. He finished the season having made 49 appearances without scoring.

Ivan started the 1994/95 campaign in good form and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he was "especially dominant" as a sweeper in a 1-0 over Wealdstone at Yeading on 24.8.94. The paper said he was a "commanding figure" during a 1-1 draw with Braintree at Hartsdown on 15.11.94 and Ivan only missed three matches before the end of 1994. The Thanet Times described his performance in a 2-1 home win over Burnham on 14.2.95 as "inspirational" and Ivan continued to be an important part of Margate's defence until April 1995. After playing in a 3-1 defeat at Tonbridge on 15.4.95 he left the club with seven games of 1994/95 still to play. Ivan had made 45 appearances without scoring and retired from senior football after his departure from Hartsdown Park.

During the 1997/98 season he managed Medway-based Horsted Under-8 s and Ivan s son Matt was part of their squad. Ivan then played for a team called Borstal Bulldogs in a Medway 5-a-side league during 1998/99.

In the early 2000's Ivan was running his own car showroom in Luton near Chatham.

In 2009 his son Matt played for Great Britain and Ireland in golf's Walker Cup - the amateur equivalent of the Ryder Cup. Matt later turned professional and spent a few years on the European Tour and Challenge Tour circuit.

name: Roy Hales
other clubs: Brighton & Hove Albion (0) and Welling United
bio:
Tall centre-forward born in Rainham, Kent who came from a footballing family. Roy's father Bill and uncle Dick both played for Gillingham in the 1940's whilst his cousin Derek Hales (Dick's son) was a well-known Football League striker in the 1970's. He scored 168 goals in 368 games for Charlton and also played for West Ham and Derby as well as several other clubs.

Roy started his senior career with Brighton, joining the club in 1986. He progressed through Brighton's youth ranks and scored five goals in 20 appearances for the Seagulls' youth team during the 1987/88 campaign. Roy also made three appearances (one as sub) in the reserves before a knee injury finished his season in February 1988. He recovered sufficiently to play for Brighton's reserves throughout 1988/89.

Roy left Brighton to join Conference club Welling for the 1989/90 season and went on to score 11 goals in 40 appearances (13 as sub) for the Wings during the campaign. The club won the London Senior Cup by beating Boreham Wood 2-0 at Wimbledon.

In the summer of 1990 Roy moved on to Margate for a substantial fee at the same time as his Welling team-mate Martin Buglione and Margate also signed Gareth Gore around the same time, a defender who Roy had played alongside in Brighton's youth team. Roy made his debut on 18.8.90, the opening day of the 1990/91 campaign, as Margate drew 2-2 at Witney. He was a regular in the side for the opening months of the season and scored his first goal in a 2-2 draw with Burnham at Hartsdown Park on 25.8.90. On 13.10.90 Roy came on as a substitute during a 1-0 defeat at Peacehaven & Telscombe and the Adscene reported that he "immediately started to pose problems for the home defence". On 3.11.90 Roy again made an impact after coming off the bench, scoring the only goal of the game against Salisbury at Hartsdown with virtually his first touch. It was his third goal of the season and turned out to be his last. A week later Roy picked up a knee injury in a 3-0 defeat at Trowbridge and he didn't play again until coming on as a sub in a 2-2 at Burnham on 2.2.91. He made one more sub appearance during February 1991 but didn't start a game again until 29.3.91. After that match at Newport IOW Roy featured regularly again for the remainder of the campaign and ended the season having scored three times in 30 appearances (eight as sub).

In the summer of 1991 Roy underwent a cartilage operation and missed the first eight games of the 1991/92 campaign as a result. He returned to the Margate side for an FA Trophy tie against Abingdon at Hartsdown on 21.9.91. Manager Tommy Taylor told the Thanet Extra that Roy "did ever so well in his first match back after injury". The game finished 1-1 and during the second half Roy's wayward shot knocked out a Margate supporter on the terrace at the Hartsdown Road end. Roy scored the only goal of the game with a fine header in the replay at Abingdon on 24.9.91 but on 19.10.91 he was controversially sent off in another FA Trophy tie at Whyteleafe. Midfielder Ian Young threw a punch at an opponent and in the confusion that followed Roy was mistakenly identified as being the culprit and received his marching orders. The decision caused uproar on and off the pitch and Roy was outraged. When he eventually left the field and got back to the changing rooms, which were in full view of spectators, Roy found the doors locked and launched a furious assault on them.

In 2006 he recalled "Ian Young smacked one of their players and everyone started going in and I was just pulling a couple of people away and after it all quietened down the ref told me to go. I was gobsmacked and so was one of their players who I had played with at Brighton so to then get to the dressing room and find it locked - I was fuming. I'd just got sent off for nothing and then couldn't get in the dressing room. It's bad enough getting sent off but getting sent off for something you didn't do is even worse. I had to apologise to their directors and pay for the door and they were alright then. At least we got a result that day and I got my ban overturned by the league and Youngy got the suspension."

Roy was a fixture in the side after the Whyteleafe debacle and in Margate's next game on 26.10.91 he scored with two headers in a 4-4 draw with Witney at Hartsdown. On 2.11.91 he was on target once more in a 3-1 win at Erith & Belvedere and on 11.1.92 Roy was sent off again in a 0-0 draw at Witney, this time for dissent to a linesman. On 14.1.92 he played as Margate went down 2-0 at home to Sudbury and it turned out to be Roy's last game for the club. After serving his suspension he decided to retire due to constant problems with his knee and left Hartsdown Park in March 1992. Roy was only 21 at the time and had scored four goals in 23 appearances during 1991/92.

He never played again after his time at Margate and Roy eventually had nine operations on his knee.

He later emigrated to the USA and then in 2003 he moved to South Africa where he spent a year coaching. In 2006 Roy was living in Colorado where he worked in a casino and coached 11 to 15 year-olds in his spare time. He was also working towards his full coaching badge and played a lot of golf.

At that time Roy recalled his spell at Hartsdown Park Roy said "I enjoyed my time at Margate but I was gutted that I had to give up so early and not let the supporters see the fully-fit me." He added "I was playing with a knee injury for nearly a year and couldn't give a real account of what I was all about."

On a brighter note Roy said "I enjoyed playing with Paul Underwood, I think we complimented each other quite well with him getting on the end of my flick-ons." Roy also recalled some unorthodox training "Tommy Taylor had us in on a Saturday and Sunday and took us down to the beach on a cold Sunday morning and made us swim in the freezing sea which certainly woke us up."

On the subject of Mike Flanagan joining Margate having famously been sent off for fighting with Roy's cousin Derek whilst they were team-mates at Charlton Roy said "I thought it was going to be a bit awkward when he signed after what happened with Derek and him but it was fine."

Roy concluded by saying "it's good to see the 'Gate marching forward, I always look for the football teams I played for on the computer. I have to call it soccer over here which does my head in !"

By 2012 Roy was back in the UK and initially worked in a Brighton casino before becoming a plasterer. At that time he was helping out with coaching youngsters at Charlton.

name: Almer Hall
other clubs: Southwick, Brighton & Hove Albion (0), Tottenham Hotspur (21,3), Southend United (41,10), Bradford City (1,0), Norwich City (0) and West Ham United (56,14)
bio:
Clever, 5' 7" tall attacker born in Hove who began his career in Sussex with Southwick and won two Sussex Senior Cup winners' medals as a teenager during the 1929/30 and 1930/31 seasons before joining Brighton ahead of the 1931/32 campaign.

Although Almer didn't play for the Seagulls' first team during three years with the club he came to the attention of Tottenham who signed him in October 1934.

Almer went to make 21 first team appearances for Spurs spanning the 1934/35 and 1935/36 seasons and scored three goals before being released at the end of the 1936/37 campaign.

He then moved on to Southend where he scored ten goals from 41 senior outings during 1937/38 and 1938/39 and Almer then signed for Bradford City shortly before the outbreak of World War II.

Almer served in the RAF during the conflict and became good friends with former Margate player George Curtis who was in the same unit. During the 1939/40 wartime season, Almer guested for Norwich and on 16.3.40 he was sent off as they drew 0-0 at QPR.

During the remainder of the war, Almer played as a guest for West Ham and scored 23 goals in 34 wartime appearances for the Irons. In December 1945 he was officially transferred from Bradford to West Ham and went on to score 14 goals from 56 post-war first team appearances for the Hammers spanning the seasons from 1945/46 through to 1948/49.

In the summer of 1950 Almer joined Margate as player-manager and he also acted as the club's physiotherapist having qualified towards the end of his time at West Ham. Almer made his debut in a 3-0 defeat at Snowdown in the Kent League on 23.8.50 - the opening day of the 1950/51 campaign - and went on to score 24 times in 35 outings during the season. He also made a host of goals for other players with his incisive passing. Almer's goal tally included four in an amazing 11-2 win over Tunbridge Wells at Hartsdown Park on 26.12.50 and he also bagged a hat-trick in a 6-2 home win over Whitstable on 6.1.51.

Almer was troubled by injuries during the 1951/52 campaign but made a further 20 appearances and added another seven goals to his tally including a hat-trick in a 6-1 win over Canterbury at Hartsdown Park on 15.9.51.

Almer celebrated his 40th birthday during the 1952/53 season but still played when required. He made 12 appearances during the campaign, the first in November 1952, and his five goals proved that he was still a very useful player. After featuring in the side that drew 1-1 with visitors Folkestone on 9.5.53 to share the Kent Senior Shield, Almer retired from playing although he did feature in a Boxing Day friendly between the reserves and the first team in 1953.

In 1961 Almer was offered the chance to become West Ham s new manager following the departure of Ted Fenton but he opted to stay at Margate having been at the club for 11 years. Ron Greenwood got the West Ham job.

At Margate s annual meeting in July 1966, Almer announced that he would leave the club at the end of the 1966/67 season and at that time his salary was £1,000 per year. He also told the meeting that during his 16 years at Margate he d had six offers to manage other clubs.

Almer ended up staying at Hartsdown Park and eventually completed a remarkable 20 years as Margate's manager to cement his place as one of the club's legendary figures before stepping down by mutual consent at the end of the 1969/70 season aged 57. Margate s committee had decided that a player-manager was needed. Almer still had a year to run on his contract so he stayed on at Hartsdown Park for the 1970/71 campaign, acting as assistant to new player-manager Gerry Baker and he then became a scout for Luton.

Later in the 1970 s Almer did some scouting for Chelsea and in February 1980 the Whitstable Times reported that he d watched Whitstable s Kent League game against Faversham on behalf of the London club. Almer visited The Belmont to watch Whitstable midfielder Adrian Carter but hadn t realised Carter had already left the club, he d signed for Ashford the week before.

Almer died on 7.11.94, a few days before his 82nd birthday and curiously exactly sixty years since his first team debut for Spurs. Local press stalwart Dave Cooper paid tribute to Almer by saying "over a near 40-year period of working with sports personalities few are as dear to my heart as Almer Hall." He went on to say "he had that rare ability of establishing an immediate rapport with virtually everyone with whom he came into contact. Football may have been his career and, to a large extent, his life but he could discourse at a moment's notice on almost anything under the sun and leave a total stranger feeling that he had made a new friend."

Although his birth name was Almeric, he signed himself as Albert when writing notes for Margate programmes and press reports often referred to him as Albert rather than Almer .

name: Billy Hamilton
other clubs: Partick Thistle (Scotland) (0), St.Bernard's (Scotland) (0), Arsenal (0), Ramsgate Athletic, Canterbury City and Snowdown Colliery Welfare
bio:
5' 7" tall, talented, left-sided player born in Kingseat, Scotland who had two spells at Margate. Billy began his career in Scotland, playing for Partick Thistle and St.Bernard's, before representing Arsenal during the Second World War.

He then joined Ramsgate and spent the 1945/46 season at Southwood before moving to Margate for the 1946/47 season.

Billy made his debut in Margate's first game after World War II - a 1-1 draw at Gillingham Reserves on 31.8.46. His clever play and hard work made him one of the stars of the 1946/47 campaign and he was virtually ever-present. He made 37 appearances and scored ten times. Several of his goals were long-range efforts - something of a trademark for Billy. His tally included a hat-trick in a 5-0 win over Betteshanger at Hartsdown Park on 29.3.47 - all from distance. Billy also displayed his versatility during the season by filling in at left-back and playing as a striker on occasions as Margate won the Kent League title.

At the start of the 1947/48 season he struggled to win a regular place in the side and Billy rarely had the chance to feature in his favoured midfield position. He mostly played on the left wing and struggled to show his true ability. Although Billy managed to score four times in ten outings he wasn't happy with his lot at Margate and in November 1947 he asked to be released. Billy s request was granted and he soon joined Canterbury.

Within weeks he was playing for City against Margate and on 26.12.47 he had a penalty saved by Doug Read as his new side went down 2-1 at home. Billy stayed with Canterbury for the 1948/49 season too and was club captain.

After a spell at Snowdown Billy returned to Hartsdown Park in January 1951 and made 18 appearances for Margate, scoring once, before the end of the 1950/51 campaign.

He continued to be a regular during the 1951/52 season and made 35 appearances, scoring two goals.

The 1952/53 campaign saw Billy in and out of the side but he added a further 14 appearances to his tally and scored twice. One of his goals was a bizarre 40 yard effort in a game against Canterbury. The other came in a 1-1 draw against Folkestone at Hartsdown Park on 9.5.53 and it earned Margate a share of the Kent Senior Shield.

Billy played almost exclusively for the reserves during the 1953/54 season and only made one first team appearance, featuring as Margate beat Canterbury 5-0 at Hartsdown Park on 6.5.54 to win the Kent League Cup.

During 1954/55 he made two senior appearances and was a fixture in the reserves once again.

Billy continued to be a mainstay of the reserves during the 1955/56 season and he made just one first team appearance. That was in an FA Cup tie at Epsom on 22.10.55 and Billy scored with a 25 yard shot to show that he hadn't lost his touch.

Billy also made two first team appearances during the 1956/57 campaign, the first of them as a left-back in a 1-1 draw at Ashford on 30.3.57. He was also captain of the reserves and his experience helped them win the Kent League Division 2 and two cups.

After Vic Pilcher emigrated to South Africa in December 1957 Billy took over as reserve team player-manager although he only made a handful of appearances during the 1957/58 season and none for the first team.

Having retired from playing he continued to manage the reserves during the 1958/59 season and was still in charge of them in the 1960/61 campaign. Billy was still working at the club during 1962/63 and in 1967 he was landlord of The George And Dragon pub in Margate.

In August 1973 the 'Club Notes' section of Margate's programme reported that Billy was suffering with ill health and had been unable to work for two years. A collection was made for him and the total raised, including a donation from the Supporters Club, was £25.

Billy died in Thanet in the summer of 1980 aged 59.

His father played for Partick Thistle and an uncle of Billy's had a lengthy spell with Brentford.

name: Gary Hammond
other clubs: Ramsgate and Kent Police
bio:
Tall, burly, Dover-born centre-forward who began his senior career with Ramsgate. Gary joined the club in November 1980 when they were in the midst of a crisis following the mass departure of the first team squad and had to draft in numerous young local players. He made his debut in a 6-1 defeat at Kent Police in the Kent League on 29.11.80 and Gary had only celebrated his 15th birthday a few days earlier. He kept his place for a home game with Cray on 6.12.80 and scored as the Rams crashed to an 8-2 defeat. Gary s goal probably made him Ramsgate s youngest-ever goalscorer.

After leaving Ramsgate, Gary had a lengthy spell in local amateur football.

He joined Thanet United for the 1986/87 campaign and made a good impression in United's reserve side, scoring a hat-trick for them in a 5-1 win over Folkestone in September 1986. Gary had already scored nine goals for the second string when he made his first team debut in an FA Trophy tie against Dover at Hartsdown Park on 4.10.86. He came on as a substitute in a 1-1 draw.

Gary then returned to the reserves until being called up for Thanet's home game against Waterlooville on 22.11.86. He marked his full debut with a goal in a 2-1 victory, controlling the ball on his thigh before turning to fire home from close range. United manager John Wickens said that Gary was "a natural goal poacher with a good instinct and a deadly finish inside the box" and added "he looks very promising."

Gary scored again in a 1-1 draw with Dover in a Southern League Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 9.12.86 and he d made a total of seven appearances (two as sub) by the end of 1986, the last of them in a 2-1 defeat at Corinthian on 27.12.86.

Early in 1987 Gary rejoined Ramsgate and the Rams' manager Lester Smith said "I am sure he will be a good signing for the future."

Gary moved on to Kent Police of the Kent League for the 1987/88 campaign.

Towards the end of 1989/90 he made a brief return to Hartsdown Park, scoring twice in six games for Margate's reserves in March and April 1990.

Gary went back to Ramsgate again for the 1991/92 season and he was the Rams leading scorer for the 1991/92 campaign. He also spent 1992/93 at Southwood before leaving the club and moving to the Middle East.

Gary later lived in South America for a period and then spent nine years in Spain before returning to Thanet. Gary was living in Margate in 2012.

His uncle Dennis Hammond served on Dover s board for over 40 years and another relative of Gary s also played for Dover.

name: Wes Hammond
other clubs: Charlton Athletic (0), Gravesend & Northfleet, Ramsgate, Herne Bay, Deal Town, Faversham Town, Lordswood and Cray Valley (Paper Mills)
bio:
5' 10" tall Margate-born defender who played for the club's Under-14's side during the 1998/99 season and was then on Charlton and Gravesend & Northfleet's books as a schoolboy.

Wes returned to Margate for the 2001/02 campaign and he was a fixture in the reserves during the season. On 19.3.02 he made his first team debut aged 17 when he came on for the injured Iain O'Connell after 23 minutes of a Kent Senior Cup tie at Folkestone. The Thanet Extra said Wes "acquitted himself admirably" as Margate won 2-1 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "rarely looked out of place in the well-drilled Margate defence". Wes then returned to the reserves for the remainder of the season and won their 'Player of the Year' award.

He carried on playing for Margate's reserves during the early months of the 2002/03 campaign and Wes also turned out for Ramsgate's Under-18's side. On 28.1.03 he made his first senior appearance of the season for Margate as a substitute in a 3-1 win over Sittingbourne in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park. Wes took to the field as a replacement for Iain O'Connell with 12 minutes left. He made one more first team appearance - as a substitute in a 3-0 win at Erith & Belvedere on 1.4.03, also in the Kent Senior Cup - but at the end of the campaign Wes left the club.

He joined Herne Bay in the summer of 2003 and Wes was a regular in their first team throughout the 2003/04 season.

On 25.7.04 he made a one-off appearance for Margate in a friendly at Ramsgate and the Thanet Times said Wes "impressed at the back" but he spent the 2004/05 campaign proper with Herne Bay again.

He signed for Deal ahead of the 2005/06 season and after a year there Wes linked up with Faversham in July 2006, joining the club in time for their first season back in the Kent League.

He won Faversham's Supporters' and Managers' 'Player of the Year' awards for 2007/08 and in the summer of 2008 Wes played in two of Margate's pre-season friendlies. He went back to Faversham for the start of the 2008/09 campaign proper and in the summer of 2009 Wes moved on to Lordswood.

He stayed with the Medway club until December 2011 when he joined Lordswood's fellow Kent League club Cray Valley (Paper Mills). Wes had also been playing for Thanet Sunday Football League club Active Queens Head during 2011/12 and was working for Tesco at one of their Thanet stores. He'd been with the company for many years by then.

Wes left Cray Valley at the end of the 2011/12 season and started 2012/13 playing for Albys United in the Thanet Sunday Football League.

In March 2014 Wes rejoined Lordswood of the Southern Counties East Football League.

name: Tony Hampson
