Alan continued to play in the reserves throughout the 2007/08 campaign and in the summer of 2008 he featured in two first team friendlies but a few weeks into the 2008/09 season Alan left Margate and dropped back into local football.

During the 2011/12 campaign he was turning out for Bradstow Albion in the Thanet Sunday Football League and Alan was still playing locally during 2013/14.

He worked as a painter and decorator during his time with Margate.

name: Heath
bio: - Margate 08/09 reserves -

name: Gordon Heckley
other clubs: West Ham United (0), Canterbury City, Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Chislet Colliery Welfare and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
Skilful left winger born in Easington, County Durham who moved to Hersden near Canterbury in Kent as a youngster. Gordon s father was a miner who found work in the area and he played football for local amateur sides as well as featuring in Margate s reserve team from 1929/30 to 1932/33 inclusive. Gordon s uncle was also on Margate s books for some of that time.

Gordon was considered to be one of the Margate s brightest prospects as an 18 year-old during the 1946/47 season. He made his debut in Margate's first game after World War II - a 1-1 draw at Gillingham Reserves on 31.8.46. Gordon went on to make 35 appearances as Margate won the Kent League title and his tally of 11 goals included one direct from a corner and several excellent solo efforts. Player-manager Charlie Walker said of Gordon's strike in a 3-1 win over Shorts Sports at Hartsdown Park on 7.12.46 "I have not seen many better goals in first class football."

Gordon's talents came to the attention of West Ham during the season and in December 1946 they signed him on amateur forms. That was shortly after Margate s Jack Yeomanson had been signed by the Hammers. He went on to become a professional with the East London club but Gordon wasn't so lucky.

He ended up remaining with Margate for the 1947/48 season and unfortunately his performances didn't live up to the standards he'd set during the previous campaign. Gordon played only three times in the first two months of the season and in November 1947 he was released and signed for Canterbury.

Gordon then played for Snowdown Colliery Welfare in the Kent League and during 1949/50 he featured for them as well as turning out for Chislet Colliery Welfare in the Kent Amateur League. On 21.1.50 Gordon scored a hat-trick for them in a 4-2 win at Birchington.

He joined Ramsgate for the 1950/51 campaign and Gordon spent two seasons with the Rams.

He returned to Canterbury for the 1952/53 season and Gordon then spent 1953/54 with Chislet Colliery Welfare.

In the summer of 1954 he rejoined Margate having impressed manager Almer Hall who d watched him play three times during 1953/54. The Margate manager said "Heckley produces an attractive game and, with a little coaching, will prove a sound Kent League man." However Gordon left the club again a few weeks into 1954/55 without even featuring in the reserves.

He then returned to Chislet Colliery Welfare for a third spell, spending the remainder of 1954/55 with them. Gordon ended up stayng with Chislet until he retired aged 36 at the end of the 1963/64 season.

Gordon worked as a blacksmith's striker during his first spell at Hartsdown Park and died in the Canterbury area in January 1998.

name: Gavin Heeroo
other clubs: Chelsea, Crystal Palace (0+1,0), Leyton Orient (0), Billericay Town, Grays Athletic, Farnborough Town, Cambridge United, Chelmsford City, Fisher Athletic (London), Sutton United, Eastleigh and Ebbsfleet United
bio:
6' 0" tall midfielder born in Haringey, London to parents who hailed from Mauritius. Gavin was a trainee at Chelsea before joining Crystal Palace in the summer of 1999 having turned down an offer from Aston Villa.

He progressed through the Eagles' youth ranks and in 2002 he was chosen as Brent Council's Festival of Lights' Junior Sports Personality of the Year. Gavin played for Palace's reserves throughout the 2002/03 campaign and also won a full cap for Mauritius during the season in a match against Nigeria. He'd previously been an Under-21 international.

In November 2003 Mauritius wanted him to take part in the Indian Ocean Island Games but Gavin opted not to represent his country again as by then he was on the fringes of Palace's first team. He was an unused substitute for a few Division 1 games before making his senior debut as an 89th minute sub in a 1-1 draw with Preston at Selhurst Park on 8.11.03. Gavin didn't touch the ball but told the Croydon Guardian "to get on the pitch at Selhurst Park was like a dream come true."

He didn't feature in the Eagles' first team again and in April 2004 Gavin played for Leyton Orient's reserves in a 1-1 draw at Rushden & Diamonds during a trial spell with the club but had to go off injured after 50 minutes. By then he knew that he was going to be released by Palace at the end of the 2003/04 season.

After leaving Selhurst Park Gavin joined Isthmian League Premier Division club Billericay for the start of the 2004/05 campaign and made nine league appearances (one as sub) without scoring before linking up with Conference South outfit Grays in October 2004.

In March 2005 Gavin signed for Conference side Farnborough and spent a couple of months there before being released at the end of the season.

In the summer of 2005 he played in friendlies for Gravesend & Northfleet and Canvey Island before featuring in two of Margate's pre-season matches. On 13.8.05 Gavin made his competitive debut in a 2-0 defeat at Ramsgate in a match played for the Kent Messenger Cup but it was his only appearance for Margate.

After a short trial at Histon Gavin ended up going back to Farnborough early in the 2005/06 campaign and in November 2005 they loaned him to Cambridge United, also of the Conference. Injury delayed his debut for a month but Gavin eventually made his first appearance for the U's in a game at Stevenage on 26.12.05 and his loan spell lasted until the end of the 2005/06 season.

After leaving Farnborough once again Gavin linked up with Isthmian League Premier Division club Chelmsford in the summer of 2006 and made 19 league appearances (six as sub) without scoring before moving on to Fisher of the Conference South in January 2007.

The Londoners signed Gavin as a replacement for the recently departed Anton Robinson who was a former Margate player. Gavin stayed with Fisher until the end of the 2007/08 campaign.

In the summer of 2008 he joined Sutton of the Isthmian League Premier Division and went on to score once from 38 appearances (11 as sub) before being released in March 2009.

Gavin then signed for Conference South club Eastleigh where he spent the remainder of the 2008/09 season.

He joined Ebbsfleet United in the summer of 2009 and Gavin featured 33 times for them (four as sub) without scoring during the 2009/10 campaign before being released at the end of the season as the Fleet were relegated from the Conference. He then dropped out of senior football.

In 2012 Gavin was working as a personal trainer in the London area.

name: Kane Hemmings
other clubs: Deal Town, Ramsgate and Canterbury City
bio:
Locally-born son of 1980 s Thanet United and Margate player Richard Hemmings whose uncle Neville also had a spell with Thanet United.

Kane featured in Margate s Under-15 side during the 2005/06 season having recovered from a broken ankle and then played in the Under-18 s throughout the 2006/07 and 2007/08 campaigns before progressing to the reserves.

On 30.3.10 Kane made a one-off appearance for Margate s first team when he played at right-back in a 2-0 defeat at Welling in the Kent Senior Cup but he left the club at the end of the 2009/10 season.

In the summer of 2010 Kane joined Kent League outfit Deal and then dropped into local amateur football in the Thanet area.

At the start of the 2011/12 campaign he returned to Margate and became captain of the reserves but at the end of the season Kane left the club once more.

He joined Ramsgate in the summer of 2012 and played in their reserves but early in 2013 Kane started a third spell with Margate, again featuring regularly in the reserves. He left the club at the end of the 2012/13 campaign.

Early in the 2013/14 season Kane linked up with Canterbury of the Southern Counties East Football League.

name: Neville Hemmings
other clubs: Gillingham (0), Herne Bay and Ramsgate
bio:
Local defender who had a spell in Gillingham's youth team before joining Thanet United in September 1981. Neville made his reserve team debut on 3.10.81, shortly after his 17th birthday. He then progressed to the first team later in the 1981/82 season, playing alongside his older brother Richard.

Neville made his senior debut in a 6-0 defeat at Dorchester on 10.10.81, playing at right-back. He went on to make 24 appearances (two as sub) before the end of the campaign, all but one of them in the right-back position. The Thanet Times described him as "frequently catching the eye" during a 3-1 defeat at home to Welling on 28.12.81 and Neville won an award for being the best young player in the first team during the season although Thanet finished bottom of the Southern League Southern Division.

He stayed with United for the 1982/83 campaign and made 15 sporadic appearances (three as sub). Neville was in and out of the side all season and usually played in midfield, although initially he filled the right-back berth.

He made eight further appearances during the 1983/84 campaign, but all bar one of them was as a substitute. Neville's only start came in a 1-1 draw with Basingstoke at Hartsdown on 3.9.83 and his final appearance for Thanet was as a substitute in a 2-0 home defeat against Cambridge City on 7.1.84. He left the club in the summer of 1984.

Neville then joined Herne Bay for the 1984/85 campaign before linking up with Ramsgate in September 1985. He went on to spend several seasons in the Rams' first team, up to and including the 1988/89 campaign.

During 1990/91 Neville made the briefest of returns to Hartsdown Park, making one appearance for Margate's reserves. He also played for local amateur outfit Britannia during the season.

He played the last football of his career during the 1990's when he turned out for Thanet League club Margate Athletic Old Boys whose squad of veterans also included a host of other former Margate / Thanet players.

During the early 1990's Neville worked as a Civil Engineer and his nephew Kane was with Margate during the 2010's.

name: Richard Hemmings
other clubs: Ramsgate, Herne Bay, Sittingbourne and Faversham Town
bio:
Fast, versatile player who began his career in local amateur football during the 1977/78 season with Dreamland Colts. Richard then joined Ramsgate for the 1978/79 campaign and played in the reserves, winning their Player of the Year award for the season.

After a spell back in local football, Richard linked up with Margate for the 1980/81 campaign and played regularly for the reserves early on. He made his first team debut in a 2-1 win at Hastings on 9.12.80 aged 17 and had a good game in midfield. Richard then scored from long range in a 3-2 defeat at Basingstoke four days later and the local press described him as being "promising". On 20.12.80 he scored with a powerful drive from 20 yards as Margate beat Andover 4-1 and Richard went on to make a total of 19 appearances (one as sub), usually in midfield or attack, before the end of the season. He didn't add to his goal tally but turned in many impressive performances. In January 1981 manager Terry Morris said "Richard has a major part to play in the club's future plans" and the Thanet Times said that he "worked like a Trojan" in a 3-0 defeat at Dover on 14.2.81.

Richard also featured regularly in midfield for Thanet United during the 1981/82 season, making 25 appearances (one as sub) and he was joined in the first team by his younger brother Neville. Richard scored twice and both goals were memorable. On 13.10.81 he fired home a cannonball effort from 25 yards in a 3-1 home defeat against Addlestone & Weybridge, a strike described as "an absolute gem" by the Isle of Thanet Gazette. He also scored from distance in a 2-1 win over Chelmsford on 24.11.81 but Richard s season ended early after a broken glass was pushed into his face during a night out at the start of April 1982. He had to have 40 stitches in the wound and missed the last eight matches of the campaign as United finished bottom of the Southern League Southern Division.

By the start of the 1982/83 season Richard had recovered and he became a fixture in Thanet's side once more. Richard made 40 appearances and established himself in a new role as an attacking right-back. The Thanet Times praised him for his "telling runs" from defence in a 3-1 defeat at Crawley on 11.9.82 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that Richard was "outstanding with his darting runs down the right" in a 1-1 draw with Gravesend on 9.11.82. Later that month he escaped from a car crash with just a slight shoulder injury and Richard scored once before the end of the season.

He continued to be a regular in the United line-up during the 1983/84 campaign and spent most of the season playing in midfield, only playing twice at right-back. Richard also turned out as a striker on two occasions. He made 42 appearances (three as sub) to take his career tally for the club past 100. Richard scored three goals and each of them was spectacular. He fired home from 30 yards in a 4-3 win over Dover in an FA Trophy tie at Hartsdown Park on 13.9.83, a strike described by the Isle of Thanet Gazette as "a gem of a goal", and also scored from distance in a 2-2 draw at Chatham on 26.12.83. Richard then found the net with a scorching half-volley in a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Chatham on 23.4.84. The Gazette said it was a "brilliant" effort.

In the summer of 1984 Richard left the club, along with his brother Neville, and he joined Herne Bay for the 1984/85 season, scoring eight times during the campaign.

Richard then rejoined Thanet for 1985/86 and he was in great form as an attacking right-back during the early months of the season. The Thanet Times said that he was "outstanding" in his first game back - a 3-1 win over Chichester City in an FA Cup tie at Hartsdown on 24.8.85. Richard had a run of games in midfield, often wide on the right, during late October and early November 1985 and the Thanet Times said "his biggest asset is his speed off the mark". He then had a long spell in the reserves, only starting one first team game between mid-November and the end of January 1986. He returned to the senior side for an Eastern Floodlight Cup tie at Dover on 28.1.86 and then enjoyed a good run in the first team through to the end of March 1986. However on 29.3.86 Richard failed to arrive at Hartsdown to board the team coach for a trip to Cambridge City and after Thanet had lost the match 6-0 manager John Wickens released him. Wickens said "Richard let me down badly and I can tell him now that he will never play for Thanet United again while I am manager". He added "he let the club, the team, the supporters and most of all himself down badly and I cannot forgive him for being so unprofessional". Richard had made 32 appearances (three as sub) before leaving the club and his two goals included a superb strike in a 2-2 draw at Dorchester on 26.10.85. He cut in from an angle and crashed an unstoppable shot into the net.

After a spell in local amateur football, Richard joined Ramsgate in the summer of 1986 and went on to enjoy great success as a striker at Southwood. He scored 28 times for the Rams during the 1986/87 campaign and his tally included four goals in a 5-0 home win over Metropolitan Police in the Kent League on 20.9.86. However on 27.9.86 Richard was sent off in a 3-2 win at Beckenham. He added another 20 goals during 1987/88 and led the Rams scoring charts for the 1988/89 campaign too. During that season Richard was sent off as Ramsgate entertained Three Bridges in an FA Vase tie.

In the summer of 1989 Richard returned to Hartsdown Park to join Margate and his first game for the club was the annual Isle of Thanet Gazette Cup match against Ramsgate that Margate won 3-1 at Hartsdown Park. Richard came on as a substitute. His appearance made him the first person to have played during the last season of Margate's previous era (1980/81) and the first of the club's new dawn and no other player matched his achievement as the season progressed. Richard was a regular in the squad during the first month or so of 1989/90 and made a good impression after coming on as a substitute for David Fells an hour into a 0-0 home draw with Yate on 18.8.89. The Thanet Times said he "slotted in superbly to the right-back position and took the eye with some intelligent passes and the occasional sprint". The paper added that he was Margate's "best player by far." Richard played a few games in midfield in the weeks that followed but in the days leading up to a 1-0 home defeat at the hands of Hythe on 28.8.89 he was disciplined by manager Trevor Ford after missing a training session. Despite that Richard kept his place for the Hythe game and in the words of Ford "played a blinder" keeping a tight rein on the mercurial Frank Ovard. However Richard then had to endure what the Gazette called "a mind-bending" six week ban. The suspension related to an offence committed with his Sunday League side Brittania during 1988/89 - Richard was the club's player-manager. The Gazette said that he would be "hard to replace".

When he returned to the Margate side in October 1989 Richard settled at right-back for a couple of months and the Thanet Times said that he made "several timely interceptions" during a 3-1 win at Hastings on 28.10.89. Towards the end of the year he was given a run of games as a striker and Richard scored three goals in six games in the forward line during December 1989 and January 1990. The Thanet Times said he "gave his all" up front in a 1-0 home defeat against Witney on 30.12.89 and the Gazette praised his "darting runs". On 6.1.90 Richard was harshly sent off after 50 minutes of a 3-2 defeat at Trowbridge. He was chopped down when running through on goal and remonstrated with Marcus Bray, the Trowbridge player who'd committed the foul. Bray fell to the floor theatrically and Richard was dismissed. After serving a suspension for the red card Richard found himself becoming something of a utility player for the remainder of the season, playing at full-back, in midfield, as an out-and-out winger and up front once again.

After the 'double-header' weekend at Witney and Yate in April 1990 Richard was fined a weeks' wages for his part in an escapade that involved the team coach making an unscheduled evening trip to Bristol. Several other players were also disciplined. Carl Scriven and John Love were fined whilst Gary Moss and Alan Scotting were sacked over the incident.

On 1.5.90 Richard scored with a rising drive from just outside box in a 2-0 win over Corinthian at Hartsdown and the Gazette claimed that he "would be worth a small fortune, if only he could cross accurately after his speedy runs down the flank". Richard then played in a 2-1 defeat at Fareham on 5.5.90, a match that turned out to be his last competitive game for the club. After making 41 appearances (three as sub) and scoring five goals he left Margate in August 1990 shortly after playing in two friendlies prior to the start of 1990/91. In the second of them - a 4-2 defeat at the hands of Gillingham - Richard played 45 minutes in goal after keeper Martin Woodthorpe was carried off.

Richard ending up joining Sittingbourne for the 1990/91 campaign and enjoyed a successful spell with the Brickies, usually playing at right-back.

He rejoined Ramsgate for 1992/93 and in December 1992 Richard had to have 19 stitches in a head wound suffered during a racially-motivated assault outside the Ruby Lounge pub in Margate. He was attacked with a broken bottle and, when the case went to trial at Canterbury Crown Court in April 1994, it was revealed that Richard was lucky not to have been blinded or even killed. He d suffered his injury in what was described in court as a large scale street riot which involved between 15 to 20 men.

Richard ended his senior career at Faversham during the 1993/94 season.

fHe later dropped back into Thanet amateur football before hanging up his boots.

Richard worked as a carpenter and his son Kane later progressed through Margate's youth ranks up to the reserves. He made a one-off appearance for Margate s first team during 2009/10 and Kane was still playing for the reserves during the 2011/12 season.

name: Martin Henderson
other clubs: Leatherhead, Ramsgate, Deal Town and Nonington Old Boys
bio:
Tall defender who played for Leatherhead in the Isthmian League before his work as a PE teacher resulted in a move to the Thanet area.

Martin initially played locally for Minster in the Thanet League before stepping up to join Kent League club Ramsgate in the summer of 1980.

In September 1980 Martin moved on to Deal, also of the Kent League, and made his debut for them in an FA Vase tie at Horley on 27.9.80.

In March 1981 Ramsgate tried to re-sign Martin but the transfer was not allowed by the Kent League. That was due to a rule that stated players could only move once per season.

After his move fell through, Martin dropped back into amateur football and played for Nonington Old Boys in the Kent Amateur League.

He was still playing for Nonington when he agreed to help Thanet United out by playing in a Southern League game at Wealdstone on 15.9.81. United lost 6-1 but in October 1981 Martin joined the club on a permanent basis. He went on to make 17 appearances at centre-back before the end of the 1981/82 season.

Martin stayed with United for the 1982/83 campaign and made 27 appearances during an injury-hit season. He turned in several outstanding performances and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that Martin "reigned supreme in the heart of the defence" during a 0-0 draw at Woodford on 4.4.83.

Martin began the 1983/84 season free of injuries and he was a fixture in the side at centre-back until he failed to turn up for a Southern League match at Dover on 15.10.83. As a result he was released by United having made 13 appearances during the campaign and Martin then dropped out of senior football for a spell.

Immediately after leaving Thanet he rejoined Nonington Old Boys of the Kent Amateur League. Most of their side were PE teachers and former Ramsgate and Thanet player Brian Hassall was also part of their squad.

In the summer of 1984 Martin rejoined Thanet and he played in United's first three matches of the 1984/85 season before losing his place. He then had a stint in the reserves, usually playing as a striker for them. On 9.10.84 Martin was recalled to the senior side and played at centre-back in a 0-0 draw at Canterbury in the Southern League Cup but it was his last appearance in United's first team. After another spell in the reserves he left the club and once again returned to Nonington.

Martin was still playing local amateur football during the 1991/92 season.

name: Peter Heritage
other clubs: Albion United, Sidley United, Bexhill Town, Hastings United, Tonbridge, Hastings Town, Hythe Town, Gillingham (49+17,11), Hereford United (66+2,10), Doncaster Rovers (29+7,2), Woking, St.Leonards Stamcroft and Bexhill United
bio:
Burly player born in Bexhill who started his career as a centre-back with Albion United of the Sussex County League before moving on to Sidley.

In the late 1970's Peter had a spell with his hometown club Bexhill Town before linking up with Hastings United in the summer of 1979.

He joined Tonbridge for the start of the 1980/81 season and although Peter scored in a 3-1 win at Margate on 16.8.80 he was still a central defender at that time.

He rejoined Bexhill later in 1980/81 and during the 1981/82 campaign Peter started playing as a striker, top scoring with ten goals. During 1982/83 he again top scored with 32 goals and Peter then joined Hastings Town.

He got 20 goals for Hastings during the 1985/86 season and continued to score freely over the next few years. On 17.11.87 Peter was on target in a 5-2 home win over Thanet United and on 6.12.88 he scored in a 3-0 win against Thanet at Hartsdown Park. He stayed with Hastings until January 1989 when Hythe paid £4,000 for him and his team-mate Terry White.

At the start of August 1989 Gillingham signed Peter from Hythe for a fee in the region of £30,000, making him a Football League player for the first time a few weeks before his 29th birthday. Peter was nicknamed 'Hagar' by Gills supporters after The Sun newspaper's cartoon strip character and on 7.8.90 he scored a hat-trick in a 4-2 friendly win at Margate. He eventually scored 11 goals in 66 first team appearances (17 as sub) before being loaned to Hereford in January 1991. A fee of £20,000 made the transfer permanent in March 1991.

Peter scored ten goals in 68 first team appearances (two as sub) for Hereford during 1990/91 and 1991/92 and then in July 1992 he was signed by Doncaster.

In January 1993 he was loaned to Hastings and at the end of the 1992/93 campaign Peter was released having scored twice in 36 senior games (seven as sub) for Doncaster.

In August 1993 he rejoined Hastings on a permanent basis but a few weeks later Peter moved to Woking. He made three appearances there in September 1993 without scoring and then went back to Hastings.

In the summer of 1994 Peter joined Hastings' very near neighbours St.Leonards Stamcroft and made his Sussex County League debut for them in August 1994. He stayed with the club for the 1995/96 season and scored a hat-trick in a 5-0 win at Mile Oak on 13.12.95. A few days later Peter signed for Margate and the £1,500 transfer fee involved was a club record for St.Leonards at the time.

He made his debut in a 3-0 defeat at Bashley on 23.12.95 and the Thanet Times said Peter "did enough to show that he should prove a major asset and will considerably boost Margate's attacking potential". He played in Margate's next six games and on 6.1.96 Peter scored his first goals when he got two in a 6-0 win over Poole at Hartsdown Park. On 20.1.96 he was sent off after an off-the-ball incident in a 3-1 defeat at Forest Green and Peter's subsequent suspension meant that he missed three games in February 1996. After returning for a four match run in March 1996 Peter missed a 3-2 defeat at Witney on 30.3.96 after his car broke down en route to his pick-up point but on 6.4.96 he scored in a 2-2 home draw with Tonbridge to end a run of six games without a goal. He scored again in a 2-1 win at Poole on 13.4.96 but didn't find the net in any of Margate's remaining five games of the season, the last of which was a 2-1 defeat at Fareham on 4.5.96. That match was Peter's final one for the club and he was released in the summer of 1996 having scored four goals in 19 appearances.

He rejoined Sidley for the start of the 1996/97 campaign and top scored for them during the season. Peter managed ten goals during 1997/98 and towards the end of 2000/01 he became Sidley's joint manager as they won the Sussex County League championship. He scored 12 goals during the campaign.

Peter returned to Southern League football aged 41 during the 2001/02 season when he played a few games for St.Leonards under a dual registration deal with Sidley. He was still co-manager at Sidley during 2003/04 and played when required, marking a return to Thanet with a goal in an FA Vase tie at Ramsgate in September 2003. Peter finally left the club during the 2004/05 season and a profile of him on a Sussex football website said he had been a "hugely influential contributor to Sidley's incredible progress in recent years."

Peter later resumed his playing career with Bexhill United and during the 2007/08 campaign his son Aaron was the club's goalkeeper whilst Peter was a key player despite celebrating his 47th birthday before the end of 2007. In March 2008 he scored with a 25-yard free-kick as Bexhill won the Sussex County League Division 3 Challenge Cup by beating Haywards Heath 2-1 and on 19.4.08 Peter scored a crucial goal in a 3-2 home win over Forest that secured Bexhill's promotion to Division 2 of the Sussex County League. Later in April 2008 he was part of the side that won the Sussex County FA Intermediate Cup by beating Loxwood on penalties. Bexhill finished the season with a remarkable run of 17 victories.

In April 2009 Peter became joint caretaker player-manager at Bexhill for the last two games of the 2008/09 campaign and at the end of the season he was named as new manager Glyn White's assistant.

He continued as assistant manager at Bexhill during the 2009/10 season but only made one appearance as a player.

name: Gary Hewitt
other clubs: Gateway, Erith & Belvedere, Dulwich Hamlet, Hendon, Hornchurch, Gravesend & Northfleet, Bromley, Wimbledon (0) and Croydon Athletic
bio:
Skilful winger who started his career with Kent County League outfit Gateway before moving on to Erith & Belvedere for the 1982/83 campaign. Gary then switched to Dulwich during the season.

He stayed at Dulwich for 1983/84 and then joined Hendon in the summer of 1984.

Gary went on to make 60 appearances for Hendon, scoring three times, during the 1984/85 and 1985/86 seasons.

Gary's next move took him to Hornchurch for a brief spell towards the end of 1985 before he linked up with Gravesend & Northfleet for the 1985/86 season.

He went on to make 29 appearances (one as sub) for the Fleet, scoring once, and then moved to Bromley for 1986/87. During the season Gary had a short spell at Wimbledon before going back to Bromley.

During 1987/88 Gary scored for Bromley at Kingstonian and it was the last goal at their old Richmond Road ground. He then won Bromley's 'Supporters Player of the Year' and 'Players Player of the Year' awards for the 1988/89 campaign.

In the summer of 1989 Gary followed Bromley manager Trevor Ford to Margate and made his debut on 15.8.89 in a 3-1 win over Ramsgate at Hartsdown - the annual Isle of Thanet Gazette Cup game. He was a fixture in the side on the right wing after that and the Gazette said his "jinking runs often posed problems for the visiting defence" during a 1-0 defeat at home to Hythe on 28.8.89. On 9.9.89 Gary scored his first goal direct from a corner in a 2-1 defeat at Salisbury and he then starred as Margate beat Corinthian 1-0 in a Southern League Cup tie at Hartsdown on 12.9.89. The Gazette said that Gary "turned the Corinthian defence inside out" and the article also described him as being "talented". In its report on Margate's 1-1 draw with Ashford on 21.10.89 the Thanet Times described a typical piece of play from Gary, saying that he "bemused four men in a Stanley Matthews-type run down the left" and possessed "silky skills". The same paper said that Gary was "a constant menace" during a 3-1 win at Hastings on 28.10.89 and he scored an excellent goal with a free-kick from just outside the penalty area. Gary's form dipped as the season progressed and on 24.3.90 he played his last game for Margate in a 1-1 draw at Andover. It was his 46th appearance and he was released after the match. Gary scored five goals before departing.

Gary returned to Bromley after leaving Hartsdown Park and then went back to Erith & Belvedere in October 1990.

Later in the 1990/91 season he rejoined Dulwich and Gary went on to spend over ten years there. He was the club's 'Player of the Year' for both the 1993/94 and 1995/96 seasons and by the time he joined Croydon Athletic in August 2001 Gary had made over 400 appearances for Dulwich.

After making three Isthmian League appearances for Croydon during 2001/02 Gary retired aged 38.

During the 2005/06 campaign he was assistant manager of Bromley's reserve side but Gary left his post at the end of the season.

He later played for Runwell Hospital in the Essex Veterans Football League alongside former Margate defender Gary Blackford.

Gary lived in Strood and worked as a postman during his time with Margate.

name: Harry Hewitt
other clubs: Ramsgate Athletic, Leyland Motors, Fleetwood, Lancaster City, Nelson and Lytham Town
bio:
Clever forward born in Blackpool who played in army representative matches overseas during World War II.

In May 1946 Harry moved to Kent and had a short spell with Ramsgate where he played once - in a 2-0 home win over Gravesend in the Kent League on 4.5.46.

In the summer of 1946, Harry signed for Margate and made his debut in the club's first game after World War II - a 1-1 draw at Gillingham Reserves in the Kent League on 31.8.46. Harry was a regular in the Margate side for much of the 1946/47 campaign and scored 11 times in his 17 appearances, including a hat-trick in a 6-2 win over Gravesend & Northfleet at Hartsdown Park on 30.11.46. However in March 1947 he had to leave the club as he couldn't find anywhere to live in the Margate area.

After leaving Margate, Harry returned to the Blackpool area and initially signed for Leyland Motors of the Lancashire Combination 1st Division. He finished the 1946/47 season there.

Harry joined Fleetwood, another Lancashire Combination club, for 1947/48 where he generally played for the reserves.

He then had spells with Lancaster and Nelson in the same league.

In January 1949 Harry joined Lytham aged 30 and they were in Division 2 of the Lancashire Combination at the time. It was the start of a long association with the club. He became player-manager for the 1953/54 season and was still in that role during 1958/59, leading Lytham to promotion to Division 1 of the Lancashire Combination aged 40. Harry then retired as a player but continued as manager for 1959/60.

name: Micky Heynes
other clubs: Hythe Town, Folkestone, Herne Bay and Folkestone Invicta
bio:
5' 10" tall striker born in Lewisham who started his senior career with Hythe. Micky spent seven seasons there, interrupted by occasional spells at Folkestone, before joining Folkestone on a more permanent basis for 1985/86. During that campaign an article in Folkestone's programme revealed that Micky's ambition was to play a complete season for Folkestone and that he wanted to become an airline pilot. He returned to Hythe towards the end of 1985/86 but then rejoined Folkestone for the start of the 1986/87 season.

Micky made several more switches between the two clubs over the next couple of years and also had a spell at Herne Bay.

He started the 1988/89 season at Hythe and on 17.8.88 he scored a hat-trick for them in a 7-0 win at Ramsgate.

In November 1988 Micky joined Thanet and made his debut in a 6-1 home defeat at the hands of Poole on 19.11.88. He scored the United goal with what the Thanet Times called "a fine header" and kept his place for the two matches that followed. Micky then missed two games but marked his return to the side by scoring with a lob in a 4-1 defeat at Trowbridge on 10.12.88. He then enjoyed a run of four games in the first team and scored again in a 2-1 win at Canterbury on 26.12.88. It turned out to be his last goal for the club as after playing in a 1-0 defeat against Folkestone at Hartsdown on 2.1.89 Micky was hurt in an accident at work and left United a few weeks later. He'd scored three times in eight appearances for Thanet.

Micky soon rejoined Hythe and stayed there until moving to Kent County League outfit Folkestone Invicta for the 1990/91 season. At the time they were a separate club to Folkestone Town of the Southern League. Micky stayed with Invicta for the 1991/92 season, by which time they were the only senior club in Folkestone and were playing in the Kent League having taken over Cheriton Road following the demise of Folkestone Town.

He started 1992/93 at Folkestone but was sacked in January 1993 for a breach of the club's disciplinary code. Micky's former Thanet United colleagues Gary and Terry Collins were also axed at the same time.

Micky then had a further spell with Hythe before going back to Folkestone again in the summer of 1995.

name: Tom Hickman
other clubs: Ramsgate, Canterbury City, Dover Athletic, Herne Bay, Faversham Town, Whitstable Town and Hythe Town
bio:
Battling 5' 9" tall locally-born midfielder who progressed through Margate's youth ranks. During the 1996/97 campaign Tom played for the Under-15's and during 1997/98 he scored six goals as Margate's Under-16's beat Faversham 11-0. He finished that season as top scorer.

During the early part of the 1999/00 campaign Tom played regularly for Margate's reserves and he was their leading goalscorer before moving to Ramsgate at the start of 2000.

Tom returned to Margate for the 2000/01 term but left the club again towards the end of the season and joined Kent League club Canterbury.

In the summer of 2001 Tom signed for Dover and played regularly in their reserves throughout the 2001/02 campaign. On 29.1.02 he was sent off for a two-footed challenge just four minutes into his first team debut - a Kent Senior Cup tie at Ashford that Dover eventually lost 5-1. Tom also played once in the Conference during 2001/02, featuring as a late sub as Dover lost 1-0 at home to Hereford on 16.3.02.

He rejoined Ramsgate for the 2002/03 season and Tom then moved on to Herne Bay towards the end of 2003 before going back to Dover where he finished the 2003/04 campaign.

Tom was a regular in Dover's first team squad during the 2004/05 season and 24.8.04 he was sent off after picking up two bookings in a 2-1 home defeat against Worthing in the Isthmian League Premier Division. He ended the campaign having made 22 league appearances (five as sub) without scoring as Dover were relegated but Tom did find the net in a 2-1 home defeat against AFC Wimbledon in the Isthmian League Cup on 3.1.05. He stayed with Dover for the 2005/06 campaign but only made nine Division 1 appearances, all bar one of them as a substitute.

A few weeks into the 2006/07 season Tom rejoined Margate and became a regular in the reserves. On 8.11.06 he made his first team debut in a 1-0 defeat at VCD in the Kent Senior Cup and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "bossed midfield". Tom then returned to the reserves before being released in January 2007.

In February 2007 he started a third spell with Dover but during the remainder of the 2006/07 campaign Tom also helped out with coaching Margate's Under-18's team and he didn't play for Dover first team.

By the start of the 2007/08 season Tom was working as Director of Sport for Generation Sports who were a company that worked with Margate's Under-18's and reserves and also ran the new 5-a-side facility at Hartsdown Park. He was still on Dover's books at that time but after making one Isthmian League Division 1 South appearance during the early part of 2007/08 Tom joined Kent League outfit Faversham towards the end of 2007.

He scored five goals for Faversham in what remained of the season but in June 2008 Tom rejoined Margate - his third spell with the club.

After impressing new manager Barry Ashby in pre-season friendlies Tom was made captain for Margate's first Isthmian League Premier Division game at Carshalton on 16.8.08. He played in midfield in a 2-1 defeat but didn't feature at all in Margate's next match before coming on as a substitute in a 4-0 defeat against Canvey Island at Hartsdown Park on 23.8.08.

After making one more sub appearance Tom returned to the starting line-up when he played at right-back in a 2-1 home win over Heybridge on 30.8.08 and he kept his place in the number two shirt for the next two games before dropping out of the side following a 2-0 home defeat against AFC Hornchurch on 6.9.08. Tom then featured three times as a substitute in Margate's next four matches but his appearance from the bench in a 0-0 draw with Tonbridge at Hartsdown Park on 23.9.08 turned out to be his final outing for the club. In October 2008 Tom was loaned back to his old club Faversham having made nine appearances (five as sub) without scoring for Margate and his move soon became permanent.

He became Faversham's captain and Tom went on to lead them to the Kent League title during the 2009/10 campaign.

On 21.8.10 he scored the club's first-ever Isthmian League Division 1 South goal in a 2-2 draw at Whitehawk and Tom finished the 2010/11 season having found the net seven times in 37 league outings (one as sub).

He started 2011/12 with Faversham too and scored twice from 23 Division 1 South appearances before joining Ramsgate in January 2012 shortly after turning down an offer from Whitstable. Tom had played over 130 games for Faversham before starting his third spell with Ramsgate.

He made 11 Division 1 South appearances (one as sub) without scoring for the Rams during the remainder of 2011/12 and Tom stayed at Southwood for the start of the 2012/13 campaign but struggled to break into the first team initially. During the early part of the season he played alongside his brother Joe in Ramsgate's reserves and Joe had previously played for Margate's reserves during 2009/10 and 2010/11.

At the start of October 2012 Tom signed for Isthmian League Division 1 South outfit Whitstable and they were managed by his old Faversham boss Justin Lutchford at the time.

Tom only made two substitute appearances for Whitstable in the league and at the end of January 2013 he rejoined Ramsgate once again.

By the end of the 2012/13 campaign he d made nine league appearances (four as sub) for the Rams without scoring.

In July 2013 Tom signed for Hythe of Division 1 South but in October 2013 he returned to Faversham.

name: ? Higgins
bio:
Midfielder who made his only appearance for Margate when he wore the number seven shirt in the Kent Floodlight Cup Final Replay at Gravesend & Northfleet on 15.05.70. It was the last match of the 1969/70 campaign and Margate lost 2-1.

He may have been local player Cyril Higgins who was captain of the Bowkett s side that won the Thanet Works League title during the 1969/70 season. He d previously played for Herne United in the Canterbury & District League during 1967/68.

name: Arthur Higgins
other clubs: Whitstable Town and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
Thanet-born player who was a successful amateur boxer and was due to compete for Margate ABC in the Kent Senior Boxing Championships held at the Winter Gardens in Margate on 4.2.61. Unfortunately, Arthur was struck down by flu and couldn t take part in the event. He boxed in the featherweight division and, at the time of the competition, he d had 36 amateur fights and was working as an apprentice photographer.

Arthur started his senior football career with Margate as a teenager and made nine appearances for the reserves, scoring twice, during the 1962/63 season. He stayed with the club for the 1963/64 campaign and became a fixture in the reserve team. Arthur also made a one-off appearance for the senior side when he played at right-back as Margate went down 5-0 in a Southern League Cup tie at Bexley on 18.12.63. According to the local paper he had a "nightmare" match. He played in a total of 32 reserve team games during the campaign and scored five times for them. At the end of the season Arthur was released.

During the 1964/65 campaign Arthur played for Whitstable in the Aetolian League but continued to train at Hartsdown Park. He also turned out for Minnis Bay in the Thanet Premier Sunday League during the season and on 20.9.64 Arthur scored five times in an 8-3 win over a Margate Rangers side that featured former Margate star Freddie Kearns.

During the early weeks of the 1965/66 season Arthur made a one-off appearances for Ramsgate in the Southern League.

name: Ian Hilaire
other clubs: Dagenham & Redbridge, Leyton Pennant, Billericay Town, Enfield, Grays Athletic, Ford United, Boreham Wood, Waltham Forest, Tilbury, Redbridge, Leyton, Hendon, Erith & Belvedere, Heybridge Swifts, Tonbridge Angels, Chatham Town, Potters Bar Town, Ashford Town (Middlesex), Harrow Borough, Hitchin Town and Wealdstone
bio:
Extremely nomadic Newham-born striker who had a spell at Dagenham & Redbridge early in his career before moving on to Leyton Pennant.

In October 2000 Ian left Leyton Pennant to join Billericay where he played in the reserves for the remainder of the 2000/01 campaign.

Having left Billericay Ian played in two of Margate's pre-season friendlies in the summer of 2001 and was substituted having come on as a sub during a match at Erith & Belvedere after clashing with an opponent. In September 2001 Ian was officially signed by manager Chris Kinnear and made his debut as a substitute in a 2-1 win over Stevenage at Hartsdown Park on 18.9.01. The victory led to Margate briefly going top of the Conference. He made two more sub appearances during October and on 13.11.01 Ian wore the number nine shirt as Margate entertained Bromley in the Kent Senior Cup. He set up two of the goals in a 3-1 win but it was his only start and after coming on as a substitute in a 1-0 home defeat against Yeovil on 17.11.01 he left the club.

Ian spent the remainder of the 2001/02 season with Enfield where he made eight Isthmian League appearances (five as sub) without scoring and then joined Grays for the start of 2002/03.

After making just one appearance for Grays Ian moved on to Ford United but didn't play for their first team before joining Boreham Wood in March 2003.

He made three appearances as a substitute for Boreham Wood before the end of the 2002/03 campaign and then linked up with Waltham Forest in the summer of 2003.

At that time he was sometimes known as Ian Hilaire-Clarke and he made four appearances (three as sub) without scoring for Forest before rejoining Enfield in February 2004.

Ian played 14 games in the Isthmian League (one as sub) for Enfield without scoring and then left the club at the end of the 2003/04 season.

In the summer of 2004 he signed for Tilbury and in January 2005 Ian moved on to Redbridge. By then he was simply known as Ian Hilaire again but he only made one substitute appearance in the Conference South for Redbridge before the 2004/05 campaign ended.

On 19.7.05 Ian played for Margate in a friendly at Tonbridge and he also turned out in a pre-season game for Harrow at the start of August before deciding on a return to Hartsdown Park shortly afterwards. He made his first appearance of his second spell with Margate as a substitute in a 2-0 defeat at Ramsgate in a match played for the Kent Messenger Cup on 13.8.05 and Ian featured once more as a sub before wearing the number nine shirt in a 0-0 home draw with Redbridge in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 29.8.05. The Thanet Times said Ian had "a busy first start" and he kept his place for a 1-1 draw at Worthing on 3.9.05.

On 10.9.05 he scored his first goal for the club in a 4-0 win over Cowes in an FA Cup tie at Hartsdown Park and the Thanet Times said it was a "tidy finish" whilst noting that Ian "looked lively throughout". He made it back-to-back goals with a penalty in a 2-2 draw with visitors Slough on 17.9.05 and Ian made two more starts before dropping to the bench for a 1-1 draw at Walton & Hersham on 1.10.05. He was back in the starting line-up for a 3-0 home defeat against Cray in the FA Cup on 8.10.05 but after that Ian only featured three times as a substitute in Margate's next six matches.

On 12.11.05 he made his first start for over a month in a 1-0 defeat at the hands of Dartford in an FA Trophy tie at Hartsdown Park before dropping out of the side again. Ian made three sub appearances in Margate's next seven games and then came on again in a home game against Folkestone on 26.12.05. With six minutes remaining he scored to level the scores at 1-1 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Ian deserved his goal as he'd "dug in...and stuck around at the club while other strikers have come and gone".

After making one more sub appearance Ian was back in the number nine shirt for a trip to Maldon on 7.1.06 and scored his fourth goal of the season in a 1-1 draw. He then started each of the next 11 matches and on 18.3.06 Ian took his goal tally to five with a strike in a 4-2 defeat against Walton & Hersham at Hartsdown Park. It turned out to be his last appearance and a few days later Ian was released after 33 outings (13 as sub) during 2005/06.

Towards the end of March 2006 Ian joined Leyton and he made five Isthmian League Premier Division appearances there (three as sub) without scoring before the end of the season.

In the summer of 2006 he played in two friendlies for Carshalton but Ian wasn't signed by the Robins and a few weeks into the 2006/07 campaign he joined Hendon. Ian made his debut as a substitute in a 1-0 home defeat against Billericay in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 23.9.06 but only played six times (four as sub) without scoring before moving on to Kent League club Erith & Belvedere in October 2006.

On 17.10.06, a day after his last sub appearance for Hendon, Ian scored on his debut for the Deres as they lost 4-3 to Lordswood at Park View Road. He played twice more before linking up with Heybridge in November 2006.

Ian didn't play in the Isthmian League Premier Division for Heybridge but he did feature in an Essex Senior Cup tie at Hornchurch on 12.12.06 that the Urchins won 4-0.

Towards the end of December 2006 Ian was on the move again and he made on sub appearance for Tonbridge in the Isthmian League Premier Division before the Angels released him.

In January 2007 he signed for Chatham and Ian scored on his debut as they drew 2-2 at Croydon in an Isthmian League Division 1 South game on 13.1.07. It was his only goal for the club and after making three further appearances he made a switch to Redbridge of the Isthmian League Division 1 North at the start of February 2007.

Ian scored once in two outings for Redbridge (one as sub) before being released in March 2007. Their manager Allan Fenn told the club's official website "I unfortunately had to release Ian Hilaire after he made demands that we couldn't meet. Once again, another player was asked to leave because money came before wanting to play for the club. Ian is a very good player however we need players at this club with the right attitude and unfortunately in my opinion, Ian's let himself down at times. None the less, I'd like to take this opportunity to wish Ian every success in his future career."

After leaving Redbridge Ian finished the 2006/07 campaign with Potters Bar where he scored once in seven Isthmian League Division 1 North outings. Excluding the friendlies he'd featured in for Carshalton in the summer of 2006 Ian had played for seven different clubs during the season.

After a spell out of the game Ian joined Isthmian League Premier Division side Ashford (Middlesex) in December 2007 and made his debut for their reserves in a game at Whyteleafe on 15.12.07. Ian came on as a sub with 20 minutes left but was sent off only 11 minutes afterwards after picking up two rapid bookings for dissent. He made one appearance for Ashford's first team before leaving the club at the start of 2008.

At the start of the 2008/09 season Ian played for Harrow's reserves before signing for Southern League Premier Division outfit Hitchin in November 2008. He scored twice in seven appearances (three as sub) for the Hertfordshire side but left the club during December 2008.

In January 2009 Ian joined Wealdstone on trial and after scoring in his first reserve team outing the Isthmian League Premier Division club signed him. The Stones manager Gordon Bartlett said "He gives us something different in that he is strong and also good in the air. He certainly makes his presence felt." Ian went on to make four appearances (three as sub) without scoring before being released in March 2009. He then dropped out of senior football.

From 1999 to 2004 Ian featured in Sky One's Dream Team' programme as one of the players in the fictional Harchester United's squad.

name: Dean Hill
other clubs: Dover Athletic, Ashford Town, Sittingbourne, Ramsgate and Maidstone United
bio:
Tough-tackling defender who started his career in Dover s youth ranks and progressed to the reserves by the 2001/02 season.

Dean then joined Ashford for the 2002/03 campaign and stayed with the Nuts & Bolts until February 2004 when he signed for Southern League Division 1 East club Sittingbourne.

He spent the remainder of 2003/04 and the whole of the 2004/05 season with the Brickies before moving on to Ramsgate in June 2005.

Dean scored once from 18 league appearances (four as sub) as the Rams won the Isthmian League Division 1 title during 2005/06 and he then played 38 times (once as sub) in the Premier Division during the 2006/07 campaign, scoring three times.

In August 2007 Ramsgate s manager Jimmy Ward spoke to the Isle of Thanet Gazette about Dean and said "Tackles like a pit-bull terrier. He's one of them you don't want to play against because you know about it if he's marked you."

Dean went on to make 37 Premier League appearances and scored twice during 2007/08 as the Rams reached the play-offs. He was sent off in a 1-1 draw at Horsham in January 2008.

In May 2008 Dean rejoined Dover and he was a key part of their side that won the Premier Division during the 2008/09 season, scoring twice from 45 outings (one as sub) in all competitions. He then made 38 appearances (one as sub) and scored once in all competitions during 2009/10 as Dover consolidated in the Conference South.

Dean struggled for games at Dover during the first half of the 2010/11 campaign and in November 2010 he was loaned to Maidstone where he played three times before returning to Crabble in December 2010. Dean had only made six appearances for Dover (five as sub) during 2010/11 when he was released from his contract in February 2011 and signed for Margate.

He made his debut at centre-back in a 3-1 win at Carshalton in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 8.2.11 and Dean was then sent off in his next outing as Margate drew 1-1 with Horsham at Horsham YMCA. He was dismissed for picking up a second yellow card in the last few minutes of the game and had to serve a one-match ban.

Dean returned to Margate s defence in a 2-1 win over Carshalton at Hartsdown Park on 12.3.11 and then started four of the next five games at centre-back. On 26.3.11 he scored his first goal for the club in a 2-2 home draw with AFC Hornchurch and it was a great effort as Dean cut in from the left, beat two defenders and curled a low shot into the corner of the net. He then had to go off injured before half time of a 3-2 defeat against visitors Harrow on 2.4.11 and Dean missed two matches as a result.

He was back in the number six shirt at Margate lost 3-0 at home to Lowestoft on 23.4.11 and Dean then moved into midfield for a 2-0 defeat against Cray at Bromley on 25.4.11. He also featured in midfield as Margate took on Kingstonian at Hartsdown Park in the last game of the season on 30.4.11 and Dean capped a dramatic fight-back from 3-0 down by scoring with an acrobatic volley from 12 yards to level the scores at 3-3. He finished the campaign having scored twice from 10 outings.

At the start of July 2011 Dean was given a new one-year contract and a few days before the start of the 2011/12 season Margate manager Chris Kinnear spoke to the Isle of Thanet Gazette about him. Kinnear said Wasn t fit last year but looks in good shape now. Can play centre-half, left-back or centre-midfield. He s our Mr Consistency - you know what you re going to get out of him".

Dean made his first appearance of the new Isthmian League Premier Division campaign when he played at left-back in a 1-1 draw at Wealdstone on 20.8.11 and the Thanet Times said he impressed at the back". From then on he was ever-present in the number three shirt for the next three months and on 4.10.11 Dean scored his first goal of the season in a 6-1 win at Thamesmead in the FA Cup when a wayward shot struck him on the chest and cannoned into the net.

Dean had started each of Margate s first 27 matches when he suffered a knee injury in the first half of a 5-0 win over East Thurrock at Hartsdown Park on 29.11.11 and had to go off. He was diagnosed with ligament damage and missed the next 15 games as a result.

In February 2012 Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette Dean will definitely play again this season...it s just a case of getting him match-fit." and on 25.2.12 he played a full 90 minutes as Margate s reserves drew 1-1 at Deal.

Dean returned to first team action on 3.3.12 when he came on as an 80th minute substitute in a 2-2 draw at Wingate & Finchley and he then started at left-back in a 0-0 draw with visitors Leatherhead on 10.3.12. He was a fixture in the number three shirt for the remainder of the campaign and on 31.3.12 Dean headed the opening goal from a Dan Stubbs corner to set Margate on the way to a 2-1 home win over Horsham. Dean made his last appearance of 2011/12 in a 5-0 defeat at Canvey Island on 28.4.12 and it turned out to be his final outing for the club. He d played 39 times (once as sub) and scored twice during the season but in May 2012 Dean rejoined Ramsgate of the Isthmian League Division 1 South.

The Rams manager Tim Dixon told the Isle of Thanet Gazette This is a fantastic signing and is probably going to be our flagship signing of the summer. Dean is a winner and that is why I wanted him here." He added He was keen to come back to Ramsgate and I am delighted that we have signed such an experienced player with proven quality and ability."

Dean captained Ramsgate during the 2012/13 campaign and scored three times in 42 appearances in all competitions. He stayed with the Rams for the 2013/14 season too.

In February 2014 Dean became Ramsgate s player-caretaker manager following the departure of Tim Dixon. He was assisted by former Margate player Mark Weatherly. Dean took charge for six games before Justin Luchford was appointed as the Rams new boss in March 2014.

After only a handful of games in charge Luchford was sacked in May 2014 and two days after he d been confirmed as leaving Southwood Dean was announced as Ramsgate s new player-manager aged only 30. He told Ramsgate s website I m delighted to take the full time position as manager at Ramsgate FC. I feel passionate about the current squad of players and with a few additions, that are right for the club, we can really push on this year. Dean immediately brought in former Margate player Paul Murray as a coach.

name: H C J Hill
other clubs: Corinthians
bio:
Margate 31/32 -  H C J Hill / C H L Hill, described as both in reports. Had previously been a Corinthians player, was a school teacher in Westgate when played for MFC
Definitely not HCH Hill who was England Amateur international later in the 30 s   he was a goalkeeper and played for Dulwich

name: Henry Hill
other clubs: Fulham (0), Vancouver Royals (Canada), San Diego Toros (USA), Ipswich Town (0), Johannesburg Rangers (South Africa), Gillingham (2+2,0), Jewish Guild (South Africa), Dartford, Molesey, Woking, Hereford United (0+1,0) and Highlands Park (South Africa)
bio:
Lambeth-born player who began his career with Fulham, making his first appearances in their youth team during the 1963/64 campaign.

In 1968 Henry moved to Canada to join Vancouver Royals of the North American Soccer League (NASL) and made three appearances for the Royals before spending the remainder of the NASL season with San Diego Toros in the USA. He made 18 appearances for them during the 1968 campaign and scored three goals.

In March 1969 Henry joined Ipswich and he spent two years at Portman Road without making a first team appearance before leaving the club for a spell with Johannesburg Rangers in South Africa.

On his return to the UK in July 1971 he joined Gillingham. He made four first team appearances (two as a substitute) for the Gills early in the 1971/72 season but then left to play in South Africa once again. This time Henry linked up with Jewish Guild for a short spell.

When he returned to the UK in November 1971 Henry joined Margate on trial and made his debut on 24.11.71 in a 4-2 win at Ashford in the Kent Floodlight Cup. He turned in a good performance in midfield, impressing with his strength and passing ability. Henry went on to make a total of ten appearances but a nagging ankle injury hampered his performances and in January 1972 he was sent back to Gillingham who still held his registration. Margate manager Les Riggs said of Henry "I am sure if he had been fully fit he would have fitted the bill."

A month later Henry returned to South Africa once again and rejoined Johannesburg Rangers, he'd also featured twice for Dartford on loan from Gillingham during the 1971/72 season.

Over the next few years up to 1975 Henry divided his time between playing in South Africa and turning out for Isthmian League club Molesey.

During the 1976/77 season he had a short spell with Woking before returning to Molesey for 1977/78 and in 1978 Henry also made a one-off appearance as a substitute for Hereford in the Football League.

Henry later returned to South Africa and during 1982 he had a spell as acting coach of Highlands Park where he also played a few games. Later that same year he became coach at his old club Johannesburg Rangers and Henry stayed in that role until 1984.

In the summer of 1986 Henry returned to England and had a brief spell in charge at his old club Molesey at the start of the 1986/87 season.

In 2004 he was still believed to be living in South Africa.

name: Lee Hill
other clubs: Thamesmead Town and Crockenhill
bio:
Defender born in Bethnal Green, London who joined Thanet United from Thamesmead in March 1989 at the same time as his team-mates David Fells and Paul Domeney.

Lee made his debut on 18.3.89 as United lost 2-1 to Gravesend & Northfleet at Hartsdown and player-manager Garry Aldous said he was "a most able replacement" for the recently departed Ray Tumbridge. The Thanet Times agreed, saying that Lee "did a good job" at left-back. He also played in United's next game, a Southern League match at Folkestone on 25.3.89, and with three minutes to go Lee headed Thanet's equaliser in a 1-1 draw. He'd also given away the free-kick that had led to Folkestone's goal earlier on. Unfortunately Lee picked up a knee injury during the game and it turned out to be severe enough to end his season. He left the club in the summer of 1989 having played just twice.

Lee later rejoined Thamesmead and played for them during the 1991/92 campaign. He also had a spell at Crockenhill that included the 1993/94 season.

In 2011 Lee was manager of Seven Acre & Sidcup and also acted as the club's secretary. He was in charge as they took their place in the newly formed Kent Invicta League for the start of the 2011/12 season and lived in Erith at that time.

In the summer of 2012 Lee stepped down as Seven Acre's manager but stayed on as club secretary.

By April 2014 Lee was back in charge of Seven Acre and he was also the club s owner at that point, as well as acting as secretary.

name: Paul Hill
other clubs: Ramsgate, Herne Bay and Phoenix Rovers
bio:
Local forward who began his career with Ramsgate during the 1984/85 season, playing a few games for the reserves during the campaign. Paul stayed with the Rams until the summer of 1989 and then had a short spell with Herne Bay at the start of 1989/90.

In November 1989 he returned to Thanet to join Margate and although signed principally as a reserve team player he broke into the first team squad within weeks. Paul made his debut when he came on as a substitute as Margate were thrashed 6-1 at Dartford in a Southern League Cup tie on 12.12.89 and also featured as a sub in the next two first team games. He then returned to the reserves for the rest of the season and scored 11 goals in 18 games for them as they won the Kent League Division 2 title.

In the summer of 1990 Paul returned to Ramsgate and stayed at Southwood for a year before joining Kent County League side Phoenix Rovers for the start of the 1991/92 campaign.

Paul soon moved on to Herne Bay and in October 1991 he rejoined Ramsgate in a straight swap for John Munday. He spent almost three years with the Rams before returning to Margate in the summer of 1994.

Paul featured in most of Margate's friendlies ahead of the 1994/95 season and scored in a 4-3 defeat against Gillingham on 4.8.94. On 29.8.94 he came on as a substitute in a 1-0 defeat at Braintree but only made one other first team appearance - as a sub in a 4-1 win at Tonbridge on 7.9.94 - before going back to Ramsgate once more.

Paul dropped into Thanet amateur football for the 1997/98 season and carried on playing locally for several more years.

In the summer of 2011 he was playing cricket locally for Westgate's second team. His father Colin was a well-known figure in Thanet youth football and also served as trainer to Thanet United's reserve team during the 1981/82 campaign.
