name: Jimmy Hunt
other clubs: Herne Bay, Ashford Town, Birchington, Ramsgate Athletic and Paddock Wood
bio:
Rochester-born defender who moved to his father's home town of Margate when he was six years old. Jimmy watched Margate regularly as a youngster and even at an early age he harboured dreams of playing for the club.

During his time at senior school, Jimmy and his classmates received football coaching from Almer Hall and the Margate manager invited Jimmy to train with Margate once a week when he was around 13 years old.

At the age of 16 Jimmy joined Herne Bay and played for their reserves as an inside forward in the 2nd Division of the Kent League. A year or so later, he returned to Hartsdown Park and became a regular in Margate's reserve team at left-back. Jimmy was the only amateur in the side and at one stage The People newspaper said that he was going to be offered a trial by Ipswich. However nothing came of that and Jimmy himself was unaware of any interest.

During the 1960/61 season Jimmy played 26 games for the reserves and he also made two appearances for the first team. Jimmy's senior debut came on 11.1.61 when he played in midfield during a 3-1 defeat at Ashford in a Southern League Cup tie and he then played as a striker in a 1-0 defeat at Nuneaton in the Southern League on 22.4.61.

Jimmy made his home debut early in the 1961/62 campaign when he deputised for Terry Joyce at left-back in a Southern League Cup tie against Gravesend & Northfleet that Margate won 2-0. He went on to make a further seven first team appearances in the number three shirt during the season and Jimmy's performances led to Almer Hall offering him a professional contract in October 1961. At the time Jimmy was an apprentice Design Draughtsman and his father was dubious about him signing professional forms. He was worried it might affect Jimmy's apprenticeship and he also hoped that his son would play for Kent as an amateur but after Almer Hall had assured Jimmy and his father that being a professional wouldn't affect his training the contract was signed. A week later Jimmy was picked for Kent but he was no longer eligible to play for them.

Jimmy went on to make 17 first team appearances during the 1962/63 season and he again impressed when called upon. Having previously been in and out of the team he finished the campaign with a run in the side as Margate won the Southern League Division One title.

During the 1963/64 campaign Jimmy made ten more first team appearances, as well as 27 for the reserves, but at the end of the season he was released after the club decided to go full time and disband the reserve team to save money. Jimmy had been offered a match-by-match contract but with no prospect of playing regularly he decided to join Ashford for the 1964/65 campaign, turning down offers from Sittingbourne and Sheppey to do so.

Things didn't work out for Jimmy at Ashford and after making ten Southern League appearances he returned to Thanet in November 1964. He applied to the Football Association for a permit to play as an amateur again and turned out for Birchington in the Kent Amateur League as well as for Garlinge in the Thanet Premier Sunday League until the end of the 1965/66 season.

Jimmy then rejoined Margate for the 1966/67 campaign when the club became part time again and the reserves were reformed. He had offers of first team football from other clubs but preferred to return 'home' and Jimmy played regularly for the reserves during the season under new manager Ray John. He also made two first team appearances, featuring in both legs of the Kent Senior Cup Final against Dover during April 1967, and was as steady as ever.

Jimmy then spent the whole of the 1967/68 campaign in the successful reserve side and he also played Sunday football for Minnis Bay.

The local press described Jimmy as being the reserves "star player" during the 1968/69 season and he also made three first team appearances. The third of them came as Margate won 1-0 at Sheppey in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie on 12.5.69 and it turned out to be Jimmy's last for the senior side.

He stayed with the club for the 1969/70 campaign and played exclusively for the reserves. Jimmy also started 1970/71 in the reserves but shortly after the season started, he damaged his sciatic nerve in training and missed the rest of the campaign. Jimmy then left Hartsdown Park having played well over 150 times for the reserves.

After a spell out of senior football, Jimmy joined Ramsgate for the 1972/73 campaign having been asked to do so by player-manager Jack Smith, a former Margate player. After a season at Southwood Jimmy left Ramsgate, and the Thanet area, as he moved to a new house in Paddock Wood, near Tonbridge.

He went on to spend two seasons playing for Paddock Wood and during that time they lost to Hythe in the Kent Junior Cup Final at Ashford.

Jimmy then returned to Thanet where he played local amateur football for many years before a back injury finally forced him to retire aged 46 during the 1987/88 season. At the time he was playing for Margate Athletic.

In 2011 Jimmy was still living locally and his love for Margate was undiminished. He had many happy memories of his long association with the club and was working as a taxi driver.

On 12.4.14 he was one of the many former Margate players who attended the club s Legends Day at Hartsdown Park.

Jimmy's grandfather, also called Jimmy Hunt, played for Margate before the First World War.

Jimmy completed a questionnaire for this site which you can see here.

name: Kevin Hunt
other clubs: Queens Park Rangers (0), Gillingham (0+1,0), Gravesend & Northfleet, Faversham Town, Hong Kong Rangers (Hong Kong), Geylang United (Singapore) and Bohemian (Ireland)
bio:
5' 10" tall midfielder born in Chatham who had a spell with Queens Park Rangers as a schoolboy, joining the club in 1987, before moving on to Gillingham in 1989.

Kevin served his apprenticeship with the Gills and made one first team appearance during the 1992/93 season, coming on as a substitute for Glenn Roeder in an Autoglass Trophy tie at Leyton Orient on 1.12.92.

In March 1993 Gillingham loaned Kevin to Margate and he made his debut in midfield aged 17 in a 2-0 defeat against Baldock at Hartsdown Park on 27.3.93. It was his only appearance as he returned to Priestfield immediately afterwards.

Kevin was released by the Gills in the summer of 1993 and signed for Gravesend & Northfleet where he made 16 appearances (13 as sub) during the 1993/94 campaign.

He spent 1994/95 with Kent League Faversham and on 29.7.95 Kevin played for Margate in a friendly against Whitstable at Hartsdown shortly before moving to Hong Kong in the summer of 1995.

Kevin signed for Hong Kong Rangers and went on to spend three seasons with the club up to the end of the 1997/98 campaign, making 54 league appearances and scoring eight goals.

In May 1998 Kevin moved to Singapore to join Geylang United and made 15 appearances there before returning to England in November 1998.

After training with Barnet for a few weeks Kevin joined Irish club Bohemian in December 1998 and after making a good impression there he set up home in Ireland in March 1999.

Kevin went on to become a major star for the Bohs and after helping the club to avoid relegation during his first season he captained the Gypsies to their first ever Premier Division and Irish Cup double during 2000/01. The Bohs won the Premier Division title again during 2002/03 under his leadership and Kevin was chosen as the league's 'Player of the Year'.

By the end of the 2007 season Kevin had been with Bohemian for almost ten years and had made 352 appearances for the club, scoring 22 goals. He was still club captain.

Kevin retired in July 2008 aged 33 saying "I have had a good career but it is time to go...I don't feel like I am the player I once was and I don't want to turn up every week and collect my wages if I can't deliver, so I will finish playing now."

In October 2008 a testimonial game for Kevin saw his Bohemians X1 beat a Republic of Ireland X1 4-3 at Dalymount Park in Dublin.

After retiring as a player he started working for Manchester City as a scout.

name: Nej Hussein
other clubs: Southend United (0), Dulwich Hamlet, Fisher Athletic (London), Waltham Forest, Thurrock, Hamitkoy Spor Kulubu (Cyprus), Cheshunt, Hanwell Town and Bishop's Stortford
bio:
Turkish keeper who was born in the Istanbul area. Nej turned out for a few minor clubs in Turkey before moving to England and during the 2002/03 season he played for Southend's Under-19's team as well as being a regular in Dulwich's reserve side.

Nej spent the 2003/04 campaign with Fisher and after playing in two friendlies for Accrington in the summer of 2004 he signed for Margate.

He started the 2004/05 season as Margate's back-up keeper, initially to Scott Ward and then briefly to Ole Gottskalksson before the Icelandic international moved on. Nej then got his chance and made his debut aged 19 in a 3-1 win over Hayes in the Conference South at Margate's adopted home in Ashford on 4.9.04. The Thanet Times said he "had a nervy start" but Nej made two good stops after half-time and told the paper "I started off a bit edgy in the first half, but picked myself up and was pleased with the double save in the second half."

Nej kept his place as Margate lost 1-0 to Weymouth at Ashford on 11.9.04 and started his third consecutive game on 14.9.04 as Margate travelled to Lewes. It turned out to be a night to forget as the Sussex side won 7-3 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said an error by Nej gave a Lewes striker "a gift of a header" for the home sides sixth goal. Margate signed Peter Trego shortly afterwards and he took over as first-choice keeper.

With Trego firmly established as Margate's number one Nej found himself on the substitute's bench for almost two months before Trego was held up in traffic en route to a game against Havant & Waterlooville at Ashford on 13.11.04. He hadn't arrived at the ground by kick-off time so Nej started the game and played the first half before being replaced by Trego at half-time. Margate won the match 5-1.

Nej didn't feature again until 12.3.05 when he came on 66 minutes into a game at Hornchurch after Trego was sent off. Nej's first task was to face a penalty which the Urchins scored and the goal was enough to give the Essex club a 1-0 win. The Thanet Times praised Nej for making a "magnificent save" late on.

He made his last appearance on 28.3.05 when he played in a 2-0 defeat against Cambridge City at Ashford due to Trego serving his suspension and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Nej "could not be faulted for either of the goals and continues to look a solid shot-stopper on the rare occasions he gets to play". He spent the remainder of the campaign on the bench before leaving the club at the end of the season. In all Nej played six times (once as sub) during a campaign which saw Margate relegated to the Isthmian League Premier Division.

Shortly after leaving Margate Nej had a knee operation and towards the end of 2005 he joined Southern League Eastern Division outfit Waltham Forest. He played four times for them but left the club shortly after a 6-1 defeat at Boreham Wood on 28.1.06.

After undergoing two more knee operations Nej resumed his career when he signed for Conference South club Thurrock in the summer of 2007.

A few weeks into the 2007/08 season he moved on to Dulwich some five years after originally playing for the club and then towards the end of 2007 Nej linked up with Cypriot side Hamitkoy.

He spent a couple of months playing in Cyprus before returning to England in February 2008.

Nej spent the remainder of the 2007/08 campaign with Southern League Premier Division club Cheshunt before rejoining Thurrock in the summer of 2008.

On 23.12.08 Nej made a brief return to Margate when he played in a friendly against Kent County League side Canterbury City at Hartsdown Park and shortly afterwards he left Thurrock to join Spartan South Midlands League outfit Hanwell.

Nej made his debut for Hanwell in January 2009 and stayed there until the end of the 2008/09 campaign.

In the summer of 2009 Nej signed for Bishop's Stortford of the Conference South but left the club during the 2009/10 season and dropped out of senior football.

During the 2011/12 campaign he was turning out for Beckenham-based Cosmos 90 in the Metropolitan Sunday Football League.

At one point during his career Nej was part of the Harchester United squad in Sky television's 'Dream Team' programme about a fictional football club.

name: John Hutchins
other clubs: Sittingbourne, Queens Park Rangers (0) and Sheppey United
bio:
Winger born in Minster on the Isle Of Sheppey in Kent who attended the Sheerness Dockyard Technical School and started his career with Sittingbourne as a teenager. John made his first team debut for the club as they won 4-2 at Herne Bay in a Kent League game played on 28.4.58 and he scored one of the Brickies goals. At the time he was serving an apprenticeship as a shipwright. John made one further first team appearance before the end of the 1957/58 season.

He made a few more senior appearances for Sittingbourne during the first half of 1958/59 and then at the start of 1959 John was signed as a professional by Division Two club Queens Park Rangers aged 21. He made his debut for their reserves in a match against Crystal Palace Reserves at Loftus Road on 31.1.59. John s time with QPR was blighted by injuries and he broke his ankle a few weeks after joining the club. Later in 1959, John had to have an operation on his foot and then on 5.3.60 he suffered a compound fracture of his left leg eight minutes into a game between QPR Reserves and Reading Reserves at Loftus Road. John didn t resume training until December 1960 and he was eventually released in May 1961 having never made a first team appearance for QPR in over two years at the club.

Towards the end of March 1962, John joined Margate and after making one reserve team appearance he made his senior debut on the right wing as Margate lost 1-0 at Rugby on 20.4.62. John kept his place for a 1-0 win at Dover the following day but then returned to the reserves where he scored once in a total of three appearances before leaving the club at the end of the 1961/62 season.

John rejoined Sittingbourne for the start of the 1962/63 campaign and made a few Southern League appearances before being released at the end of the season.

In the summer of 1963 John signed for Sheppey and during 1964/65 he was part of their side that won the Greater London League Championship. Former Margate winger Peter Peters was also a member of the team. John was still on Sheppey s books during the 1967/68 campaign.

He worked as an insurance man during his time with Sheppey.

name: Keith Hymas
other clubs: Ipswich Town (0), Hastings United and Romford
bio:
Bustling centre-forward born in Southend who began his career with Ipswich. Keith played for the Suffolk club s youth team during the 1967/68 campaign and scored 14 goals from 24 appearances (one as sub) for them. He also scored twice from four outings for Ipswich s reserves before being released at the end of the season.

Keith signed for Hastings ahead of the 1968/69 campaign and during that season they loaned him to Romford. He stayed with Hastings for 1969/70 and the start of 1970/71 too and on 21.12.70 Keith scored the goal that gave them a 1-0 win in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie against Margate at Hartsdown Park.

In March 1971 Keith joined Margate and scored with a cheeky back-heel on his debut in a 2-1 home win over Telford on 24.3.71. He went on to make a total of 13 appearances before the end of the 1970/71 season and scored seven goals, including two in a 4-2 win over Hereford on 30.4.71.

Keith was in and out of the Margate side during the early part of the 1971/72 campaign, partly due to injury, but scored twice, including an excellent goal from the edge of the penalty area, in a 4-2 win at Ashford on 24.11.71. Keith won praise for his tireless displays but after finding the net three times in 11 appearances (one as sub) his contract was cancelled by mutual consent in December 1971.

Shortly after his departure from Margate, Keith emigrated to Australia.

name: Kezie Ibe
other clubs: Arsenal (0), AFC Bournemouth (0), Leatherhead, Hampton & Richmond Borough, Aylesbury United, Staines Town, Yeovil Town (0+3,0), Tiverton Town, Exeter City, Weymouth, St Albans City, Canvey Island, Chelmsford City, Ebbsfleet United, AFC Wimbledon, Farnborough, Sutton United, Eastbourne Borough, Basingstoke Town, Hendon and Harlow Town
bio:
Powerful 5 10 tall striker born in Camden who was on Arsenal s books from 1993 to 1997 before being released aged 15.

After leaving the Gunners Kezie had a short spell in Bournemouth s youth set up but then dropped out of football for two years.

He joined Isthmian League Division 2 club Leatherhead for the 2001/02 season aged 18 and Kezie scored his first goal in a 2-0 home win over Ashford (Middlesex) on 22.9.01. A few weeks later he had a trial with Sheffield Wednesday and shortly after returning to Leatherhead Kezie scored four times in an 8-0 win over visitors Metropolitan Police on 3.11.01.

At the end of November 2001 he stepped up to the Isthmian League Premier Division by signing for Hampton & Richmond Borough and Kezie went on to score twice from 18 league outings (seven as sub) before the end of the 2001/02 campaign. He also scored twice in cup ties.

In the summer of 2002 Kezie joined Premier Division club Aylesbury and he scored on his debut as they drew 2-2 at Basingstoke on 17.8.02. Kezie spent the whole of 2002/03 with the Ducks and scored nine goals from 53 appearances in all competitions.

He moved on to Staines ahead of the 2003/04 season and Kezie scored 27 goals during the campaign, 19 in the Isthmian League Division 1 South and eight in cup ties. His tally included all four goals in a 4-3 win at Bracknell on 30.3.04 and a month earlier Kezie had been involved in a controversial incident as Staines lost 3-2 at home to Halifax in an FA Trophy replay. The tie took place on 12.2.04 and after the final whistle Halifax manager Chris Wilder was punched and knocked out which led to criminal charges being brought against Kezie.

In June 2004 he was signed by League Two club Yeovil and Kezie made his debut as a late substitute in a 2-0 home win over Boston on 14.8.04. He featured once more as a sub before being loaned to Tiverton in October 2004.

Kezie s spell with the Southern League Premier Division outfit was a successful one and he scored seven times in 13 outings including a hat-trick in a 4-1 FA Cup Fourth Qualifying Round victory over Newport County before going back to Yeovil.

In December 2004 he was loaned to Conference club Exeter and Kezie made his debut as a substitute in a 4-0 home win over Hereford on 26.12.04. He started the Grecians next match on 28.12.04 and scored the opening goal as they won 2-1 at Tamworth. Kezie played twice more before returning to Yeovil in January 2005 and Exeter s manager Alex Inglethorpe said "Kezie has gone back, I was delighted with the way he played in the games he was available for us." Inglethorpe had previously briefly managed Kezie at Leatherhead in 2001.

At the end of January 2005, around the time his loan at Exeter ended, Kezie appeared at Guildford Crown Court accused of assault and causing actual bodily harm relating to the Staines v Halifax game a year earlier but the jury took only two hours to reject the charges brought against him after a week-long trial.

Having returned to Yeovil Kezie made one more substitute appearance in February 2005 before being loaned to Conference South outfit Weymouth before the end of the month.

At the end of March 2005 he joined St Albans on loan and Kezie made his debut on 2.4.05 as they lost 2-1 at home to Sutton in a Conference South game. On 5.4.05 he scored his first goal for the club in a 3-2 win over Margate at Ashford and in all Kezie managed four goals from eight outings before the end of the 2004/05 campaign.

Having been released by Yeovil he signed for Conference outfit Canvey Island on a one-year deal in August 2005 and Kezie went on to score six goals from 35 league appearances during 2005/06.

In July 2006 he moved on to Chelmsford of the Isthmian League Premier Division - following manager Jeff King from Canvey Island - and Kezie managed 19 goals from 40 league outings (four as sub) during the 2006/07 season. His tally included a hat-trick in a 7-3 home win over his old club Staines on 24.3.07 and Kezie also scored once in cup ties to take his overall tally for the campaign to 20 goals.

He stayed with Chelmsford for the 2007/08 season and scored 14 goals, nine of them in the Premier Division and five in cup ties including a hat-trick in a 5-1 home win over Dagenham & Redbridge in the Essex Senior Cup on 7.1.08.

Kezie joined Conference club Ebbsfleet in the summer of 2008 and he scored five goals from 26 league outings during 2008/09 before being loaned to AFC Wimbledon in March 2009.

He scored once from five Conference South outings (two as sub) for the Dons before the end of the season.

Kezie linked up with Southern League Premier Division club Farnborough for the 2009/10 campaign and scored 18 goals from 41 league appearances as they won promotion to the Conference South. He then played in 36 league games for Farnborough during 2010/11 and scored 13 goals.

In June 2011 Kezie rejoined Chelmsford and he scored seven goals from 37 Conference South appearances during 2011/12.

He signed for Sutton in the summer of 2012 but having failed to score in nine outings for the Conference South outfit Kezie was loaned to Eastbourne Borough in November 2012.

He initially joined Eastbourne for a month but Kezie s loan with the Conference South club was extended and then in January 2013 he signed a permanent deal. He scored once from 14 appearances before signing for Margate at the end of February 2013.

Kezie joined the club as player-coach and made his debut in a 0-0 draw with Hendon in an Isthmian League Premier Division game played at Wembley FC on 2.3.13. From then on he was a fixture in the Margate side and on 9.3.13 Kezie scored for the first time in a 3-0 win over Bognor Regis at Hartsdown Park. He then made it back-to-back goals by finding the net in a 3-0 win at Enfield Town on 16.3.13.

Kezie s good form continued and after scoring in a 4-2 home defeat against Wealdstone on 26.3.13 he bagged a brace in Margate s next match - a 3-1 win over visitors Thurrock on 29.3.13. Kezie s second effort was a low shot from an acute angle and joint manager Craig Holloway told Margate s website Kezie has done fantastic. He s scored two goals today and his hold up play was superb." Kezie then scored for the third game in a row when he struck twice from close-range in a 4-0 win over Cray at Bromley on 1.4.13.

He ended a run of three games without a goal by cleverly chipping the visiting keeper as Margate lost 2-1 at home to Metropolitan Police on 13.4.13 and on 23.4.13 Kezie scored for the ninth time in a 4-2 defeat against Ebbsfleet in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park. He made his last appearance in a 0-0 draw with visitors Harrow on 27.4.13 and Kezie ended the season having scored nine goals from 16 outings.

In June 2013 he returned to the Conference South by signing for Basingstoke and Kezie scored eight goals from 37 appearances (13 as sub) during 2013/14 before being released at the end of the campaign.

In July 2014 he signed for Isthmian League Premier Division club Hendon and Kezie went on to score 47 goals from 172 appearances before leaving for Harlow Town in December 2017.

name: Deren Ibrahim
other clubs: Dartford, Sittingbourne, St.Andrews (Malta), Maidstone United and Leatherhead
bio:
Keeper who started his career with Dartford where he played for the Under-18 s during the 2007/08 season and won both the Managers Player of the Year and Supporters Player of the Year for them.

Deren stayed with the Darts for the 2008/09 campaign and his display for the first team in a 3-2 home win over Hastings in the FA Cup 1st Qualifying Round on 13.9.08 earned him the accolade of Player of the Round . Deren was given a trophy by competition sponsors E.ON and also won a pair of tickets to the 2009 FA Cup Final.

He spent the 2009/10 season on loan at Isthmian League Division 1 South club Sittingbourne and Deren made 51 appearances for the Brickies in all competitions. He was part of the side that won 3-1 at Folkestone to claim the Kent Senior Cup on 4.5.10 and future Margate striker Tom Bradbrook was one of Sittingbourne s goalscorers that day. Deren also won the Brickies Young Player of the Year award.

In August 2010 Dartford loaned Deren to St.Andrews of the Maltese 1st Division (the second tier of football on the island) for three months and he scored with a drop-kick on his debut.

After a few months back at Dartford where he played twice in the Conference South Deren joined Margate in March 2011 on a dual-registration basis to cover for the injured Jamie Turner. He was caretaker manager Kevin Raine s first signing and Deren was 20 at the time.

On 26.3.11 he made his debut in a 2-2 draw with AFC Hornchurch in an Isthmian League Premier Division game at Hartsdown Park and in doing so Deren became the first post-World War II player with a surname beginning with the letter I to appear for Margate and only the second ever in the club s entire history.

He started each of the next four games and Deren also played in the Kent Senior Cup for Dartford during his spell with Margate as well as being on the subs bench for some Conference South matches. He made his last appearance for Margate in a 3-0 home defeat against Lowestoft on 23.4.11 before going back to Princes Park.

On 2.5.11 Deren was in goal as Dartford beat visitors Bromley 4-1 in the Kent Senior Cup Final and thus won a winners medal for the second season in succession having also triumphed with Sittingbourne during 2009/10.

He stayed with the Darts for the 2011/12 campaign as they won promotion to the Conference but Deren rarely played and at the end of the season he was released.

In June 2012 he signed for Isthmian League Division 1 South club Maidstone and on 14.7.12 Deren played in the Stones first ever game at their new stadium in James Whatman Way - a 5-0 defeat at the hands of Brighton. He then spent much of 2012/13 as Maidstone s first-choice custodian after former Margate keeper Charlie Mitten broke his arm. Deren made a total of 39 starts in all competitions as the Stones won promotion to the Premier Division via the play-offs but in May 2013 he was released. Player-manager Jay Saunders told Maidstone s website It s been a pleasure having Deren here and he was a big part of our promotion campaign. He has a great future in the game and everyone at the club wishes him every success in the future."

In the summer of 2013 Deren joined Division 1 South outfit Leatherhead on a dual-registration basis from Dartford and made his debut for them in a 1-0 win at Ramsgate on 10.8.13. He also worked as an academy coach for Dartford at that time.

name: George Ingmire
bio:
Born Dorking, Surrey Q2 1882   
Margate 10/11 - from reserves     
Partner (with brother Frederick) in F C Ingmire & Sons - Modern & Antique House Furnishers 125 High Street, Margate by 1948.  Been working in business for years before 
George Alma Ingmire, married Q2 1912, son also called George born 1912

name: Frank Jackett
other clubs: Glanrhyd (Wales), Pontardawe Athletic (Wales), Swansea Town (Wales) (0), Watford (14,0), Leyton Orient (4,0), Ramsgate Athletic and Adeyfield Athletic
bio:
Hard tackling Welsh player born in Ystalyfera, Glamorganshire who played for South Wales as a youth before starting his senior career with spells at Glanrhyd and then Pontardawe.

In 1948 Frank was signed by Swansea Town and played for their youth and reserve teams but he couldn't break into the Swans' senior side and in November 1949 he moved on to Watford.

Frank made 14 first team appearances for the Hornets, then in the 3rd Division (South), spanning the 1949/50 to 1952/53 campaigns.

In July 1953 he joined Leyton Orient and made four senior appearances for them during 1953/54.

In May 1954 Frank dropped into non-league football and signed for Ramsgate. He spent four seasons with the Rams before being released at his own request in September 1958.

Frank immediately moved across Thanet to join Margate and made his debut in a 4-1 win at Herne Bay on 13.9.58. On 15.11.58 he was in the side that lost 3-2 at Headington in the FA Cup 1st Round. Frank was a regular in midfield for a few months but towards the end of the season he often found himself in the reserves. On 18.4.59 he was sent off playing for them early in the second half of a game at Whitstable after committing a foul and then arguing with the referee. Frank made his last senior appearance for Margate in 4-3 home win over Tunbridge Wells on 25.4.59 and at the end of the 1958/59 campaign he was released having made a total of 24 appearances without scoring.

Frank later had a spell with Adeyfield Athletic, a Hertfordshire non-league club. Frank was player-coach there from January 1960 until 1962.

Frank died in the Watford area on 14.4.10 aged 82.

His son Kenny played for Watford and Wales during the 1980's and also managed clubs including Swansea City, Millwall and Wolves. Frank also had another son who was on Luton's books as an apprentice at one time.

name: Duane Jackman
other clubs: St Albans City, Bishop's Stortford, Aveley, Potters Bar Town, Cheshunt and AFC Hornchurch
bio:
Striker who was part of a PASE football scheme at Redbridge College when he made a one-off appearance for St Albans reserve team in the Essex and Herts Border League as an 18 year-old in November 2003.

Duane later joined Bishop s Stortford and scored on his senior debut - a 2-2 draw with visitors Cheshunt in the Herts Charity Cup on 10.8.04. He went on to make 27 Conference South appearances during 2004/05 and scored six times.

Duane again scored six times for the Bishops in the Conference South during 2005/06 and his goals came from a total of 34 league outings.

In September 2006 he signed for St Albans and Duane scored on his debut as they lost 4-2 at Exeter in the Conference on 19.9.06. He made a total of six league appearances (three as sub) but didn t score again before being released in October 2006.

Duane then joined Isthmian League Division 1 North outfit Aveley and scored once from ten league outings (two as sub) before the end of the 2006/07 season. He also got one goal in a cup tie.

He spent 2007/08 with Potters Bar and Duane made 26 appearances for them, scoring four times.

In the summer of 2008 he linked up with Cheshunt and Duane scored once from six outings before returning to Bishop s Stortford in November 2008.

His second spell with the Bishops saw him score nine times in 26 Conference South appearances during the remainder of 2008/09 and Duane also started the 2009/10 campaign with the club.

In October 2009 he signed for AFC Hornchurch and made 14 Isthmian League Premier Division appearances without scoring for the Urchins although Duane did manage three goals in cup ties.

In March 2010 he went back to Bishop s Stortford again and Duane s third stint with the club lasted until February 2011 when he rejoined AFC Hornchurch.

He scored once from five Premier Division outings for the Urchins but left the club before the end of the season and Duane finished the campaign playing for London-based Sunday League side Beckton Athletic.

After a spell out of senior football he returned to the Isthmian League Premier Division when he signed for Margate in November 2011. Duane made his debut in a 1-1 draw with visitors Wealdstone in an FA Trophy tie on 5.11.11 and the Thanet Times said he was in the mould of Rocky Baptiste". In addition to comparing him to the laid-back former Margate striker the paper said Duane looked to have something about him".

He then wore the number nine shirt in the next five games but Duane didn t score and a 1-0 win over Ramsgate in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 22.11.11 turned out to be his final appearance. Duane then missed two games due to work commitments and Margate s website said that "the ongoing situation with Duane will be assessed by the club." Although he was never officially announced as having left Duane didn t feature again and he then dropped out of senior football once more.

name: Alex Jackson
other clubs: Renton (Scotland), Dumbarton (Scotland), Bethlehem Steel (USA), Aberdeen (Scotland), Huddersfield Town, Chelsea, Ashton National, Sittingbourne, Nice (France) and Le Touquet (France)
bio:
Born Renton, nr Glasgow  5' 7" tall. speedy and skilful . 
Started with Renton - Dumbarton  signed him fron Renton for a transfer fee of 22 shillings 
One of British football s early superstars. 
Dumbarton - in first team by the age of 17.  Toured Norway with them.  
then Bethlehem in USA during the first attempt to establish a professional soccer league in the USA, the ambitious pro Pennsylvanian club Bethlehem Steel signed up Jackson  and his brother Walter, who played for Kilmarnock, in 1922 - Walter considered the 'star' at the time 
Bethlehem site - 23/24 28 games, 14 goals in American League (pro).  Over 20 goals in all games, around 40 apps. but his career was almost ended following one game in Fall River when he dived into a near empty swimming pool. 
Bethlehem - debut Oct 1923, last June 1924.  2 hat-tricks - 12.1.24 Beth 3 Bedford FC (Brooklyn, NY) 0 - all 3 in first 15 Another hat-trick in Beth 6 Newark 0 2.2.24, National Cup.. Brother Walter got the other 3.  Beth won American Cup, beat Fall River 1-0 in front of 3,000* 
Alex and Walter returned after a season to join Aberdeen for  1,000 (joint fee for A & W) for 24/25, winning the first three of his 17 Scottish caps. 
Bethlehem site "One of the greatest players in the game in the years between the wars"   
Aberdeen (first of 17 Scotland caps there) then to Huddersfield for club record  5,000.
 Toured Denmark and Sweden just after joined Hudd. A sensation when moved into English football aged 21 with Hudd for 25/26 -  Hudd boss Herbert Chapman. 
The Sports Post paper 1925 "Well, he's tall, straight as a cane; but with the resiliency of a young willow tree; when football breezes blow his way, Jackson bends to the work that is brought for him to do One moment he is tall, straight, subdued; the next he is a thing of grace, of action, of fire, of -- he's just alive with every mortal picture which shows activity .he is like a kitten on his toes ...His judgment of position play is immense  
At this time, Town were the most successful club in England. 
Having won two successive League titles, He promptly helped them clinch the celebrated hat-trick of championships in 1925-26. 
England 1 Scotland 5 - 31.3.28 at Wembley, Home International Championship.  Scored hat-trick, 1st with header in 3rd min  'The Wembley Wizards' - tallest of 5 in attack !!   One of 4 Huddersfield players in side -  first of 17 countries to defeat England at Wembley. "The Wee Blue Doubles" "The Wembley Wizards". Not since 1882 had England conceded five goals. Scotland paid  8 a man 
appeared in two Wembley FA Cup Finals for Town.  scored in 1928 FA Cup Final - Blackburn 3 Hudd 1 (weeks after Wembley Wizards)   //  1930 Arsenal 2 Hudd 0 - Jack Lambert one of the Arsenal goals, Preedy in goal. In all, he made 203 appearances for the club, scoring 89 goals. 
Last Scottish cap in May 1930 - Scottish record - played 17, won 15, drew 1, lost 1 - an 88% win rate 
4th highest ever British fee of  8,750 when he left Hudd for Chelsea in September 1930.  
An alleged drinking incident helped to end his pro career prematurely. Jackson who was said to be the ringleader of a boisterous session in a Manchester hotel the night before a match during the 1931-32 season. However there was a strong case that Jackson, a keen trade unionist, had upset the Chelsea board by demanding better pay and greater freedom of contract.   fell out with the club over his opposition to the maximum wage of  8 a week set by the Football League. He believed that players were performers and thus entitled to earn as much as anyone on the screen or in a boxing ring. 
Whatever the real reason, Chelsea caused a sensation by not re-engaging Jackson and putting him on the transfer list at  4,500 - more than any club was willing to pay. He became a pub landlord and was forced to play for non-League clubs.
At first joined Ashton National in August 1932 - they were funded by the National Gas Engine Company, a huge firm which once dominated the west end of Ashton. Jackson said: "I have got to live, so I have accepted this contract. I can't play for a Football League club until I have resolved my troubles with Chelsea but I shall travel to Ashton each week and give of my best." The Cheshire League was not bound by Football League rules and Jackson was paid  15 a week - almost double the maximum wage. His debut in a 2-0 defeat by Northwich at the old National Park, Katherine Street, was watched by 7,000, while an incredible 13,000 saw the visit of Hyde United. However, Jackson was injured on Christmas Eve, 1932, and his Cheshire League career came to an end after 19 appearances and 12 goals.  
 Then Margate  10 per week, Yeovil & Petters had also made an offer and thought Jackson was going to sign for them. Whilst with us we played at Ashford and prescence said to have led to one of largest gates ever seen there - despite counter attraction of Mr Lloyd George making by-election speech in Ash at same time ! 
LAST GAME FOR US   1.4.33 home to Ashford, twisted cartilage in right knee whilst shooting and had to go off
Definitely also played for Sittingbourne   straight after us ? 
August 1933 received big offer from French club Roubaix (seven miles from Lille). Told paper at time hard to leave England  Still, what can I do ? They won t let me play in England, and as I am a young man I am going to play somewhere.    could have played in England but only in FL if club paid Chelsea the fee which was  4,000, originally it was  5,000 but Alex applied to Football Leauge to have it reduced
Didn t join Roubaix and initially played for Nice then Le Touquet 
The war then took him to the Middle East, where his life - just like his football career - was to end all too early - died at the age of just 41 Sept 2005 - The Huddersfield Daily Examiner:  Edgerton woman Pauline Crowther (former nurse) told paper "During the Second World War and in the aftermath, I was a member of the Queen Alexandra's Royal Nursing Service in the Middle East," "One day in November, 1946, I was sent to a large hospital near the Bitter Lake at Fayed, near Cairo.  "The first person I ran into was the Army sports officer, who introduced himself as Alex Jackson. "He asked what part of the country I came from and I replied: `You've probably never heard of it, a northern town called Huddersfield.' "He laughed immediately and said he had played football for Huddersfield Town." "As sports officer, he was responsible for arranging a weekly football match at the main stadium in Cairo and that involved a lot of travelling On joining Margate "I shall continue to live in London and carry on my business, but I need some hard training due to excessive weight."  "Sadly, the next day I was asked to get the theatre ready to treat a severe head injury. It was Alex Jackson, who had been involved in a road accident on his way back from Suez. "He never got to the operating theatre, for he died as they were getting him out of the ambulance.  "The following Saturday there was a very emotional two minute's silence at the football ground. He had been a very popular officer."   
Known as "The Gay Cavalier" or Laughing Cavalier.  Said to be blessed with film star looks and to be at ease in any kind of company 
Died 15.11.46 actual name Alexander so Alex or Alec 
In 1995 a Housing Association development in Renton (hometown) was named Jackson Place in Alex's honour  
senior debut at centre-forward for Dumbarton in a 1-1 Second Division draw with Broxburn at Boghead on September 30th 1922. 28 apps, 2 goals 22/23 
Alex made his Dons debut alongside his brother Walter in a League match against Rangers at Pittodrie on August 23rd 1924. Aberdeen lost 1-0. 39 apps 8 goals 24/25 
May also have played for Nimes in France but think they made offer when he was with Chelsea and Chelsea wouldn't let him go - need to check up   
Daughter Grace Jackson did glamour modelling in 50's and 60's as Lee Southern // 
32/33 (with us) ended early as aggravated an existing knee injury by slipping on the lino at his home

name: Andy Jackson
other clubs: Ramsgate and Herne Bay
bio:
Local player who joined Margate in the summer of 1980 and played regularly for the reserves during the early part of the 1980/81 season. On 9.12.80 Andy made his first team debut when he played at left-back in a 2-1 win at Hastings in the Southern League and he went on to become a regular during the second half of the campaign, usually featuring as a central defender. Andy impressed with his aerial power, prompting the local press to describe him as "a promising pivot". He made a total of 19 appearances before the end of the season and in a 4-1 win over Addlestone & Weybridge on 10.1.81 Andy "tackled and covered with the utmost resolution" according to the Thanet Times. However the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that he was "repeatedly turned like a spinning-top" during a 3-2 defeat at home to Ashford on 27.1.81. Andy scored once during the season - in a 1-1 draw at Fareham on 8.4.81.

He stayed with the newly re-named Thanet United for the 1981/82 campaign and played regularly at centre-back early on, scoring an own goal in a 1-1 draw with Dunstable at Hartsdown Park on 15.8.81 - the club's first ever match. Andy then found himself out of the side for a lengthy period halfway through the season but returned to re-establish himself later on, finishing the campaign with a run of ten games. All in all he made 29 appearances (one as sub) and scored once as Thanet finished bottom of the Southern League Southern Division.

Andy began the 1982/83 season as a regular in the heart of United's defence before being moved into attack for an FA Cup tie at Hastings on 2.10.82. The switch proved to be a success as Andy scored in a 2-1 win. He continued in an attacking role for United's next three games before reverting back to his regular position in defence. After playing in midfield in a 3-1 home defeat against Crawley on 11.12.82 Andy found himself out of the team altogether for an extended period. He returned to the side for a 1-0 defeat at home to Salisbury on 5.3.83, playing up front once more, but then dropped back into the reserves for the remainder of the season. At the end of the campaign he left the club having made 19 appearances (two as sub) and scored three goals.

Andy joined Ramsgate for the 1983/84 season and then played for Herne Bay during 1984/85.

He later dropped into Thanet amateur football.

Andy worked as a prison officer.

name: Jimmy Jackson
other clubs: Charlton Athletic (0), Gravesend & Northfleet, Dagenham & Redbridge, Dover Athletic and Folkestone Invicta
bio:
Talented left-sided player born in Cobham, Kent who spent three seasons in Charlton's youth set-up from 1990/91 to 1992/93 inclusive before being released by the Addicks.

In the summer of 1994 Jimmy was signed by Gravesend & Northfleet and he went on to become a hugely popular figure at Stonebridge Road during an initial nine-year spell with the club. Jimmy's first manager at Gravesend was former Margate player-manager Garry Aldous. On 2.12.95 Jimmy was part of the Fleet side that lost 3-0 at Aston Villa in the FA Cup 3rd Round and his team-mates that day included future Margate players Paul Lamb, Mark Munday and Lee Turner. Jimmy also played a key role as Gravesend won the Isthmian League Premier Division title during the 2001/02 campaign and on 6.5.02 he scored in a 5-0 win at Margate in the Kent Senior Cup Final.

On 25.3.03 Jimmy won a cap for the England semi-professional team when he came on as a substitute in a 0-0 draw in Holland and in the summer of 2003 he signed for Conference club Dagenham & Redbridge.

Jimmy struggled with injuries during the 2003/04 season and in November 2003 the Daggers loaned him to Dover. He made seven appearances without scoring before going back to Dagenham in December 2003. Jimmy had difficulty combining his Daggers commitments with his work on his family's farm in Kent and after making 23 appearances (two as sub) during 2003/04 he rejoined Gravesend in May 2004. Jimmy had scored once for Dagenham - in a 3-3 draw at Margate one 6.3.04.

He went on to spend two more seasons with Gravesend and took his overall record to 520 appearances (26 as sub) for the club. Jimmy scored 92 goals, including numerous free-kicks and long-range strikes, before being released at the end of the 2005/06 campaign. He was one of numerous Fleet players who were unable to commit to the club's new full-time regime and a Gravesend website described Jimmy as being "undoubtedly one of the Fleet's all-time greats".

In May 2006 he signed a two-year contract with Margate, around the same time as several other former Gravesend players joined the club, and player-manager Robin Trott told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "Jimmy is one of the best signings we could have got - he's a great player. He's a different level and I'm absolutely over the moon because I worked hard to get him." Trott then told the KM Extra "Jimmy always gives 100 per cent and he is an absolute winner." Jimmy told the paper "I had some really good times at Gravesend and hopefully there will be a few more ahead with Margate."

In its report on a 1-1 draw with Millwall in a friendly at Hartsdown Park on 8.7.06 the Thanet Times said Jimmy's "sweet left foot will surely unlock a few defences this season" and on the eve of the new season Robin Trott spoke to the Isle of Thanet Gazette about Jimmy saying he "Never stops working and will never let his head get down. He's got a good left foot and will score goals. He's the same breed as Steve McKimm - a good professional."

Jimmy made his debut on the left of midfield in a 5-2 win at Worthing in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 19.8.06 and on 26.8.06 he scored his first goal with what the Thanet Times described as a "cracking effort from the edge of the box" in a 2-1 home win over Slough. Jimmy then made it back-to-back goals when he struck in a 5-1 win at Folkestone on 28.8.06.

On 12.9.06 he played a left-back for the first time as Margate lost 2-0 at Ramsgate in an Isthmian League Cup tie but Jimmy was soon back in midfield and the Thanet Times said he had "a field day down the left as he rained in crosses" during a 2-1 win at Whitstable in the FA Cup on 30.9.06. He'd started each of Margate's first 16 matches when he had to go off early in the second half during a 3-2 defeat at Billericay on 17.10.06. Jimmy then missed four games before resuming his duties in the number 11 shirt in a 2-0 win over Hampton & Richmond at Hartsdown Park on 11.11.06. He was ever-present from then on, almost always playing on the left-hand side of midfield.

Jimmy got his third goal of the season in a 4-0 win at Horsham on 9.12.06 and the Thanet Times said he "deliciously stroked the ball into the bottom right hand corner". He then opened the scoring in a 1-1 draw at Ramsgate on 26.12.06 with what the Isle of Thanet Gazette called an "outrageous" goal. The paper said "there looked to be little on when the ball dropped at Jackson's feet wide on the left and about 30 yards out. So he had a go on the volley and completely caught out Rams keeper Paul Wilkerson as the ball flew over his head and dropped in the far corner".

Jimmy continued to shine during the remainder of the campaign and on 17.2.07 he had another outing at left-back as Margate lost 2-1 at Carshalton. The Thanet Times picked him out as its man of the match' during a 1-0 home defeat against Heybridge on 24.3.07 and said Jimmy "wanted the ball more than anybody else". He finished the season having scored four goals from 46 appearances.

He scored three goals in Margate's friendlies ahead of the 2007/08 campaign and shortly before the new season began Robin Trott told the Isle of Thanet Gazette that Jimmy was an "Absolutely brilliant crosser of a ball." Trott added "Jimmy's a lovely lad who will always give 100 per cent. Takes up great positions."

He was a regular in midfield for the first three months of the campaign and on 23.10.07 Jimmy got his first goal of the season in a 3-1 win over Aylesbury in an FA Trophy tie at Hartsdown Park. On 17.11.07 he filled in at left-back in a 4-3 home defeat against Maidstone in the Isthmian League Premier Division and during December 2007 Jimmy wore the number three shirt for four consecutive matches. The last of them was a 4-1 win over visitors East Thurrock on 15.12.07 and after that he missed three games due to injury.

Jimmy returned to the side as a substitute in a 2-1 win over Ashford (Middlesex) at Hartsdown Park on 5.1.08 and from then on he was a fixture in midfield once more, usually playing on the left-hand side but sometimes filling a more central role. He got his second goal of the campaign in a 3-1 home win over Staines on 16.2.08 and Jimmy then scored twice in March 2008. He got the winner as Margate beat Billericay 1-0 at Hartsdown Park on 8.3.08 and he also found the net in a 3-3 home draw with Wealdstone on 22.3.08.

Jimmy took his goal tally to five with a deflected free-kick in a remarkable 5-4 win over visitors Heybridge on 5.4.08 and on 12.4.08 he made it back-to-back goals after beating two defenders and firing home from the edge of the penalty area in a 4-2 win at Leyton. On 26.4.08 Jimmy wore Margate's number 11 shirt for the last time in a 1-0 win at Harrow and after scoring six goals from 47 appearances (three as sub) during 2007/08 he left the club at the end of the season.

In May 2008 Jimmy signed for Isthmian League Division 1 South outfit Folkestone and scored on his home debut for them - a 2-1 win over Chipstead on 19.8.08. He went on to make 49 appearances and scored ten goals during 2008/09 and Jimmy won both the Players' and Supporter's Player of the Year' awards for the campaign.

He scored three goals from 44 appearances (one as sub) for Folkestone during the 2009/10 season as the club were promoted to the Isthmian League Premier Division via the play-offs and on 4.5.10 Jimmy found the net as Folkestone lost 3-1 to Sittingbourne in the Kent Senior Cup Final. That turned out to be the last game of his career as in June 2010 Jimmy announced his retirement aged 33 due to knee problems. He'd played in over 720 senior games by then and Folkestone's manager Neil Cugley said "We're very disappointed to be losing Jacko and I think he is equally disappointed at being forced to stop playing the game. It's a massive loss and I know he was hoping to play one more year in the Premier, where his experience would've been so important for us. He has been a great servant to the club over the last two seasons and a good person to have around."

name: Musa Jalloh
other clubs: Ajax Amsterdam (Holland), Feyenoord (Holland), Waltham Forest, Walton & Hersham and Basingstoke Town
bio:
Midfielder from Sierra Leone who was with Ajax Amsterdam as a youth and also had a spell on Feyenoord's books before injuries ruined his hopes of a professional career.

Musa later played in Sweden before moving to England and after a short period with Waltham Forest he joined Margate in November 2005.

Musa made his debut as a substitute in a 2-0 defeat at Heybridge in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 6.12.05 but didn't feature in the Margate side again until making another sub appearance in a 4-2 win over Hendon at Hartsdown Park on 29.4.06. It was the last day of the 2005/06 season and Musa then left the club.

After a spell out of football he joined Walton & Hersham in January 2007 and Musa made six appearances (three as sub) for the Isthmian League Premier Division outfit before the end of the 2006/07 campaign.

In the summer of 2007 he signed for Conference South side Basingstoke but Musa left the club a few weeks into the 2007/08 season and dropped out of senior football.

By 2010 he was working as a 'Football Consultant' in England and Musa was good friends with Chelsea's Salomon Kalou. They'd been at Feyenoord together as youngsters and in June 2010 Musa and Kalou visited Haiti, ten months after the devastating earthquake there. Musa contracted malaria whilst in Haiti and had to spend five days in hospital.

name: David Jarman
other clubs: Brett Sports, Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Herne Bay, Deal Town and Ramsgate
bio:
Locally-born, diminutive player blessed with great pace who attended St. John s School in Margate and played for the East Kent Schools side during the 1960/61 campaign aged 15. David also turned out for various Thanet junior clubs as a youngster.

During the 1961/62 season David played for Margate s youth team in an FA Youth Cup tie against Charlton at The Valley.

He first played for Margate's reserves as an amateur during the 1962/63 campaign, scoring twice in eight games for them.

David became a regular in the second X1 during 1963/64, making 24 appearances and scoring five times for them. He also turned out for Minnis Bay in the local Sunday league and on 24.11.63 David scored six goals in a 14-0 win over Bradstow United.

He made his first team debut for Margate as an amateur on 9.3.64 in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie at home to Dover that the visitors won 1-0. David performed well and the local press thought that he should have been given a run in the side but that didn't materialise, possibly because he was only 18 at the time, and David only made two further senior appearances before the end of 1963/64.

During the 1964/65 season David made a further 13 senior appearances and scored once, his first goal for the club, with a clever lob in a 6-1 win over Dartford at Hartsdown on 26.4.65. He enjoyed a run of games on the left wing towards the end of the season and compared favourably to the likes of Chick Hughes and David Hills who'd also played there during the campaign.

David was given a professional contract for the 1965/66 season and the campaign started well for him as he was selected for the opening game - a Southern League match at Guildford on 21.8.65. He scored in a 2-2 draw and put in a good display but soon found himself out of favour once more. David only made eight sporadic appearances during the season and scored twice.

In June 1966 he took part in Margate's tour of West Germany and David started the 1966/67 campaign with a hat-trick for the reserves as they won 5-1 at Ashford on 20.8.66. He was a fixture in the second string and didn t feature in the senior side until 10.10.66 when he wore the number seven shirt in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie against Deal at Hartsdown Park. David scored twice in a 6-0 win, one of his goals being an excellent volley, but didn t make another first team appearance until 18.1.67. From then on he was a regular in the side and David ended up making 36 appearances, scoring six goals. The local press said that he was "much improved and David turned in many impressive performances on the right wing as Margate won promotion from the Southern League Division One by finishing as runners-up.

During the 1967/68 season David made a further 48 appearances (two as a substitute) to take his total for the club past 100 and he scored 15 times. His accurate crosses also created many goals for team-mates. On 6.4.68 David featured in the 1st Leg of the Southern League Cup Final - a 1-1 draw with Ramsgate at Hartsdown Park - and he then took part in the 2nd Leg at Southwood on 13.4.68 which finished 0-0.

David was often used as a substitute during the 1968/69 campaign, mainly due to the form of Phil Amato on the right wing, but still scored 14 goals in a total of 36 appearances (eight as sub). David turned in many impressive displays and finished the season by scoring in both legs of the Kent Floodlight Cup Final against Maidstone. The first game was a 1-1 draw on 20.5.69 and in the second, on 24.5.69, two goals from David helped Margate win 3-1 at Hartsdown Park to claim the trophy.

He started the 1969/70 campaign by scoring a hat-trick as Margate Reserves beat Sheppey 5-1 on 9.8.69, the opening day of the season, and David continued to be a popular figure with Margate fans during the campaign but only made 14 first team appearances, four of them as a substitute. David scored five goals, including a hat-trick in a 3-0 win over King's Lynn at Hartsdown Park on 27.9.69. It was his first Southern League appearance of the season. On 15.11.69 David was in the Margate side that were thrashed 7-2 by visitors Aldershot in the FA Cup 1st Round.

He played more regularly during the 1970/71 campaign, making 33 appearances (three as sub) and scoring ten times. David played on the right wing early in the season but generally played on the left after the arrival of John Baber. He turned in some performances that the local paper described as "encouraging" and continued to display his usual trickery. During a 0-0 draw at Gloucester on 28.11.70 David was said to be "constantly menacing".

During 1971/72 David made 26 appearances, five of them as a substitute, to go past 200 for the club and scored twice. As ever, he was in and out of the side and played on both wings during the campaign. On 20.11.71 he featured in Margate s infamous 11-0 defeat at Bournemouth & Boscombe in the FA Cup 1st Round.

At the end of the 1971/72 season David was released after more than nine years with the club and the Isle of Thanet Gazette praised him for being "an exceptional clubman". The paper also said that David had "always been extremely popular with the terracers" and in recognition of his service to Margate a collection was organised for him during a home match in the 1972/73 season, a campaign that David spent with Brett Sports.

He joined Snowdown for the 1973/74 season before moving on to Herne Bay for 1974/75. David was still with the club during the 1975/76 campaign.

His next move took him to Deal where he played under Terry Morris during 1976/77 and David was known as 'Jinky Jarman' during his time there.

He later dropped into local amateur football and was still playing locally during the 1981/82 season.

David then made a surprise return to senior football during the 1982/83 campaign when he had a spell with Ramsgate aged 37.

He was still living in Margate in 2014 and at that time David s grandson Kyle was part of Margate FC s academy.

On 12.4.14 David was one of the many former Margate players who attended the club s Legends Day at Hartsdown Park.

name: Bernard Jarrold
other clubs: Bexleyheath & Welling, Arsenal (0), Bristol Rovers (0), Chippenham Town and Newton Abbot Spurs
bio:
Woolwich-born player who attended Erith Grammar School and began his career with Bexleyheath & Welling of the Kent League. Bernard played for the Heathens youth side during 1952/53 and scored 60 goals for them as a centre-forward. He progressed into the first team during the 1953/54 season and made his debut aged only 16 in a Kent League game against Ramsgate on 7.11.53. He played on the right wing and Bernard usually played as a winger from then on.

In April 1954 Bernard was part of the England Youth team squad that travelled to West Germany for a FIFA youth tournament. He scored on his debut in a 5-0 win over Northern Ireland in Bruhl on 10.4.54 and played in another five matches in the tournament. On 8.5.54 Bernard played alongside Bobby Charlton and future Manchester United boss Wilf McGuinness as England Youth drew 2-2 with Ireland Youth in a match played in Newtonards. It was Bernard s 7th and last international outing.

In the summer of 1954 Bernard was signed by Arsenal and played for their Colts side during the 1954/55 campaign before returning to Bexleyheath for 1955/56.

In November 1955 Bernard was included in the Wiltshire squad for a game against Sussex, he was undertaking his National Service in the Royal Army Pay Corps at the time. Bernard continued to turn out for Bexleyheath when he could during the season.

After playing regularly for Bexleyheath during the 1956/57 season, Bernard was signed by Bristol Rovers and played in their Colts side during 1957/58.

In July 1958 Bernard joined Margate and made his debut in a 6-3 win over Bexleyheath & Welling at Hartsdown Park on 23.8.58. He only made seven further first team appearances during the early part of the 1958/59 season and scored once in a 5-2 defeat at Betteshanger on 30.8.58. The local press said that Bernard "hared up and down the right wing like a greyhound" but also thought that his crossing let him down. Manager Almer Hall seemed to have similar thoughts and as a result Bernard spent most of his time at Margate in the reserves.

In January 1959 his contract was cancelled by mutual consent and Bernard returned to the West Country, joining Chippenham Town of the Western League. He stayed with Chippenham until the end of the 1961/62 season and then had a spell out of senior football.

In the summer of 1964 Bernard signed for Newton Abbot Spurs of the South Western League and almost immediately fractured his wrist in a pre-season friendly which kept him out for around two months. He recovered to play regularly during the remainder of the 1964/65 campaign and Bernard also played for the club during the 1965/66 season.

By 1970 Bernard was living in Surrey.

name: Peter Jarvis
other clubs: Sheppey United, Chatham Town, Ashford Town, Dover Athletic, Chelmsford City, Hythe Town, Tonbridge, Tonbridge Angels, Whitstable Town, Sittingbourne, Herne Bay and Bredhurst Juniors
bio:
Chirpy left-footed midfielder who started his career with Sheppey, making his first team debut as a teenager during the 1986/87 season. On 26.12.87 Peter scored for the Islanders in a 2-1 home defeat against Thanet United.

Towards the end of 1987/88 he moved on to Chatham and Peter then linked up with Ashford for the 1988/89 campaign.

He made 48 Southern League appearances for the Nuts & Bolts before leaving the club in March 1990 to play in Sweden.

Peter returned to England early in the 1990/91 season and had a short spell with Dover before linking up with Chelmsford.

In September 1991 he returned to Kent, joining Hythe. On 1.1.92 he showed his sense of humour when he ran out for Hythe's home game against Margate wearing a 'Max Wall' wig.

In February 1992 Peter signed for Margate and made his debut in midfield in a 5-1 defeat at Salisbury on 15.2.92. From then on he was a fixture in the side, always wearing the number seven shirt. The Thanet Times reported that Peter "often took the eye" in a 3-1 win at Andover on 22.2.92 and said he was "a dynamo in midfield" as Margate thrashed Erith & Belvedere 5-0 at Hartsdown Park on 29.2.92. He finished the 1991/92 season having made 13 appearances without scoring.

Peter started the 1992/93 campaign as an automatic choice in Margate's midfield, playing on both flanks as well as in a central role. The Thanet Times said that his "brave running often merited better reward" during a 4-1 home defeat against Chertsey in the FA Cup on 26.9.92 and on 24.10.92 Peter scored his first goal for Margate in a 5-2 defeat against Braintree at Hartsdown. It turned out to be his only goal for the club as after playing in a 2-1 home defeat against Wealdstone on 7.11.92 Peter left Margate and joined Tonbridge having made 20 appearances (two as sub) during the season.

He went on to make 26 appearances without scoring for Tonbridge during the remainder of 1992/93 and Peter stayed with the Angels until the end of 1995/96.

He started the 1996/97 season with Chatham before moving on to Whitstable in March 1997 and Peter then returned to his first club Sheppey in the summer of 1997.

His next move took him to Sittingbourne for the start of the 1998/99 campaign and Peter scored once in 14 appearances for the Brickies (eight as sub) before returning to Sheppey before the end of the season.

After a lengthy spell out of senior football Peter signed for Kent League club Herne Bay in December 2004 and stayed with the club until midway through the 2005/06 season when he retired from senior football.

During the 2009/10 campaign Peter played for Medway-based Kent County League club Bredhurst Juniors and after not featuring at all during 2010/11 he made a few appearances during the 2011/12 season. He was 43 by then.

name: Cyril Jeans
other clubs: Portsmouth (0), Ramsgate Athletic, Gravesend & Northfleet, Sittingbourne, Canterbury City, Deal Town, Hastings United and Sidley United
bio:
Pacy winger who started his career with his hometown club Portsmouth and toured the Netherlands with their junior side in May 1958. Cyril progressed to the reserves during the 1958/59 season and scored once from six outings for them. Cyril was transfer-listed by Pompey in October 1959.

On 24.10.59 he signed for Ramsgate and it was effectively a loan deal as Portsmouth retained his Football League registration initially. Cyril became a regular in the Rams side and on 6.4.60 he scored as they won 2-0 at Margate in a Southern League encounter. He ended 1959/60 having scored eight times from 33 appearances.

Cyril stayed with Ramsgate for the 1960/61 campaign and on 3.9.60 he scored a hat-trick in a 6-0 home win over Tunbridge Wells in the Southern League. On 1.10.60 he got the winner as Ramsgate beat Margate 3-2 in a league game at Southwood. Cyril was released by the Rams at the end of the 1960/61 season, he d been their leading scorer with 16 goals from 49 appearances.

In the summer of 1961, Cyril crossed Thanet to join Margate and made his debut in a 1-0 defeat against Wisbech in the Southern League on 19.8.61. He was in and out of the side during the remainder of 1961/62 and made a total of 30 appearances, scoring seven times. Cyril impressed with his work-rate and his goals included two in a 3-2 win at Hastings on 11.4.62. On 12.5.62 he played as Margate beat visitors Folkestone 4-0 to win the Kent Senior Shield and he also scored 12 goals in 17 appearances for the reserves.

The 1962/63 season saw Cyril establish himself and he made 40 first team appearances, scoring 12 goals. He was one of the stars of the Margate side that won the Southern League Division One title and was always willing to take on defenders as well as being a constant danger with his accurate shooting. On 3.11.62 he scored as Margate lost 3-1 at Millwall in the FA Cup 1st Round and Cyril s goals also included a superb solo effort in a 2-2 draw with King's Lynn at Hartsdown Park on 10.11.62. He beat four defenders before firing home a 20 yard shot. On 1.6.63 Cyril got the winning goal as Margate beat Bexleyheath & Welling 1-0 in the Final of the Kent Senior Shield at Hartsdown Park but that turned out to be his last outing for the club. He was released at the end of the season.

Cyril joined Sittingbourne for the start of the 1963/64 campaign but moved on to Gravesend & Northfleet later in the season.

He went on to make a total of 48 appearances for the Fleet during 1963/64 and 1964/65 and scored seven goals.

Cyril then moved to Canterbury for the 1965/66 season and went on to make 88 Southern League appearances (two as sub) for City up to and including the 1967/68 campaign. He scored 13 goals during that time.

After a short spell with Deal, Cyril joined Hastings United during the 1968/69 season and in the summer of 1969 he became the club's player-manager. He continued in that role until he was sacked at the end of the 1970/71 season. Hastings gave him the chance to stay on as a player but Cyril turned down the offer.

After turning down two approaches from Southern League clubs to join them as a player, Cyril joined Sussex County League Division 2 club Sidley United as player-coach in August 1971. His former Hastings teammate John Harris was Sidley s manager at the time. Speaking about his new role, Cyril told the Kentish Express After what happened at Hastings, I lost interest in the game and despite several offers I had firmly decided to hang my boots up. But after Sidley asked me to sign for them, I felt it would be silly to give up if I could help a few talented youngsters in the area to improve their football. If I can help some young players to better their game, I will be satisfied that I have done something worthwhile.

Cyril later became Sidley s player-manager and he was in charge there during the 1975/76 season.

In November 1978 Cyril left Sidley to rejoin Hastings as manager and vowed "I am going to get this club straightened out if it's the last thing I do" but he resigned in February 1979 after only a few months at the helm.

In later years Cyril managed Little Common as well as Shinewater and in August 2002 he was living in Bexhill-on-Sea, at that time he was assistant manager of Eastbourne United. He then had an eight week spell as the club's manager from December 2002 before departing.

Cyril died in East Sussex on 24.7.19 aged 79.

name: Paul Jefcoate
other clubs: Ramsgate
bio:
Attacking player born in Mtaifa, Malta whilst his father was in the Royal Navy who made his first reserve team appearances for Margate during the 1975/76 season. Paul also appeared for the reserves during the 1978/79 and 1980/81 campaigns.

He stayed at Hartsdown Park when Margate became Thanet United for the 1981/82 season and played exclusively for the reserves throughout the campaign, and during the 1982/83 season too.

The 1983/84 campaign saw Paul finally break into the first team and he made his debut in a 4-1 defeat at Poole on 24.3.84. He played as a striker and had a goal disallowed - a header from outside the 18-yard box. The local Adscene newspaper said that he had a "useful game". The Thanet Times also praised Paul's efforts, describing him as United's "danger man". He went on to make six further appearances before the end of the 1983/84 season, starting in all but one of those matches. In 2005 Paul recalled nutmegging former Southampton star Manny Andruszewski in the first couple of minutes of a 2-1 defeat at home to Waterlooville on 21.4.84. Paul said "I was foolish enough to call it" and still remembered Andruszewski's swift revenge - "I vaguely recall climbing from row 15 of the stand in the fifth minute, it was like being hit by a steam train."

Paul continued to be a regular in United's reserves during the 1984/85 campaign and he also made three further first team appearances. The first of them was as a substitute in a 4-2 win at Ashford on 11.12.84 - the match was an Eastern Floodlight Cup tie. On 7.3.85 Paul made his first senior start of the season and marked the occasion with a goal in a 2-1 defeat at Hastings United in another Floodlight Cup game. He later had a good game in a 1-1 draw at Basingstoke on 25.4.85 but it was his last appearance for Thanet. Paul left the club in the summer of 1985.

He went on to have a lengthy spell with Ramsgate and became the Rams' reserve team player-manager for a period that included the 1991/92-1994/95 seasons.

Paul made his last first team appearance for the Rams when he came on as a substitute in a game against Lordswood in April 2000 but he still turned out for the reserves occasionally as late as the 2002/03 season.

He also had a stint as the club's secretary that included the 1996/97-1999/00 campaigns and by the 2002/03 season Paul was Ramsgate's vice-chairman.

In 2005 Paul was still living locally and running his own business, as well as continuing in his role as vice-chairman of Ramsgate. At that time he was still turning out for Birchington USC in the Thanet Premier Sunday League and his team-mates included former Margate / Thanet legends Lennie Lee (who was the club's player-manager) and Joe Radford.

He was still playing locally in 2009 and was still Ramsgate's vice-chairman during the 2011/12 campaign. Paul's son Jamie was in Margate's reserve team that season.

At the end of June 2013 Paul became Ramsgate s chairman but he resigned from the role in February 2014.
