name: Adrian Jordan
bio:
Broadstairs-born reserve team player who went to Chatham House school and made a one-off appearance for Thanet United's first team during the 1983/84 season.

Adrian played in a 0-0 draw at Hillingdon on 14.4.84 although he was actually named as being fellow reserve team player Brian Phillips. He left United in the summer of 1984.

In 2012 Adrian was still living in Broadstairs.

name: Dave Jordan
other clubs: Gillingham (0+2,0), Croydon, Folkestone, Ashford Town, Fisher Athletic, Sittingbourne and Faversham Town
bio:
Distinctive blonde 6' 0" tall striker born in Gillingham who played for Twydall Boys Club, Kenilworth and Medway Boys as a youngster before joining Gillingham as a trainee aged 17 in February 1989. Dave became a regular in the Gills' youth team during 1989/90 and in June 1990 he was signed as a professional. In August 1990 Dave came on as a substitute for the Gills in a friendly at Margate and later that month he was loaned to Croydon.

Dave went on to have four other loan spells during 1990/91. He was with Folkestone from September 1990 until the club folded in January 1991 and then played for Ashford during January 1991, scoring in a 2-1 home win over Margate on 19.1.91. In February 1991 Dave was sent to Fisher and then in May 1991 he linked up with Sittingbourne. Despite spending most of the season at other clubs Dave managed to make two substitute appearances for Gillingham's first team and scored ten goals for the reserves but he was released in the summer of 1991.

He joined Sittingbourne on a permanent basis for the start of the 1991/92 campaign and scored over 18 goals during the season before moving on to Ashford in the summer of 1992.

After scoring around ten goals for Ashford during the early part of 1992/93, including one in a 4-0 win at Margate on 8.12.92, Dave joined Margate on a month's loan in January 1993. He made his debut in a 1-1 draw with Newport IOW at Hartsdown Park on 2.1.93 and the Thanet Times said "he has speed off the mark and adroit ball control". The paper also described Dave as being "nimble" and said that he "showed enough to prove that he will be a valuable asset...with flowing silver locks kept in check by a headband he cut a dashing cavalier-type figure".

Margate's next match was at Gravesend & Northfleet on 5.1.93 but Dave missed it having gone to Hartsdown by mistake, thinking it was a home game. He returned for a Southern League match against Witney at Hartsdown on 9.1.93 and scored his first Margate goal in a 2-1 defeat. In his next outing Dave found the net again with a spectacular diving header in a 3-1 win at Burnham on 16.1.93. The Isle of Thanet Gazette mentioned Dave's "shoulder-length flaxen hair and dashing demeanour" in its report for a 3-1 home defeat against Fisher on 19.1.93 and Dave then scored in Margate's next two matches. He was on target in both a 3-1 win over Poole at Hartsdown on 26.1.93 and a 5-3 home defeat against Salisbury on 2.2.93 to complete a run of four goals in five games but Dave then briefly returned to Ashford.

He missed one match before his transfer to Margate became permanent and the Gazette said he was "a bonny battler up front" during a 1-0 win over Buckingham at Hartsdown on 23.2.93. On 10.3.93 Dave bagged a hat-trick for the reserves in a 5-1 win at Herne Bay in the Kent Midweek League and on 13.3.93 he scored what the Thanet Times called "a classic goal" in a 2-0 home win over Gravesend & Northfleet. Dave dummied a defender before firing low into the corner of the net and he scored once more before the end of the season to take his overall tally to six goals in 20 appearances. He also scored 11 goals in ten reserve team games.

Dave made his first appearance of the 1993/94 campaign in a 3-0 defeat at Sudbury on 24.8.93 and after that he came on as a substitute in eight consecutive matches as the form of new strike pairing Joe Brayne and Steve Cuggy kept him out of the side. Dave earned himself a possibly unwanted 'super sub' reputation by scoring three times when coming off the bench, getting his first goal in a 3-2 win over his old club Ashford on 30.8.93 and then finding the net in a 3-2 win at Erith & Belvedere on 7.9.93 and a 3-0 win at Bromley in the FA Cup on 25.9.93. On 5.10.93 he made a rare start in a 0-0 home draw with Fisher in the Southern League Cup and Dave then made three more sub appearances before being given the number ten shirt for a Kent Senior Cup tie at Fisher on 9.11.93. Margate won 1-0 and it was Dave's last game for the club as he rejoined Ashford later in November 1993. He'd scored three times in 14 appearances (11 as sub).

In December 1993 Ashford loaned Dave to Faversham and he spent the rest of the season with the Kent League outfit. He was always amongst the goals and on 26.4.94 Dave scored in a 10-1 win over Margate's reserves in the Kent Midweek League.

Dave's move to Faversham became permanent in the summer of 1994 but at the end of the 1994/95 campaign he left the club and took an extended break from senior football.

He resurfaced at Sittingbourne during the 1998/99 season and played for the Brickies during 1999/00 too before retiring aged only 28.

name: Derek Jordan
bio:
Local forward who played regularly for the reserves during the 1946/47 season and also made a one-off appearance for the senior side in the last match of the campaign. Derek played as Margate won 3-1 at Royal Marines Chatham on 31.5.47 and scored the third goal to help seal the Kent League title.

He carried on playing for the reserves during the 1947/48 and 1948/49 seasons before leaving the club.

Derek died on 25.10.86 aged only 59.

name: Gerry Jordan
other clubs: Ramsgate, Deal Town, Folkestone & Shepway, Faversham Town, Herne Bay, Canterbury City and Sheppey United
bio:
Battling striker who started his career with Ramsgate as an 18 year-old during the 1973/74 season. At the time Gerry was described as being "quick and brave in the box" by the Rams' manager Jack Smith and he added that Gerry showed "genuine promise."

He moved on to Deal for the 1974/75 campaign but rejoined Ramsgate in January 1976, Gerry had scored 33 goals in his last 18 games for Deal at the time. On 24.1.76 he was sent off for the Rams in a 0-0 draw against visitors Bognor Regis and on 16.3.76 Gerry scored four goals in a 5-4 win at Hastings.

In November 1976 he moved to Folkestone & Shepway but returned to the Rams again in February 1977.

Gerry then spent the early part of the 1977/78 campaign with Faversham but left them in October 1977 having been sent off twice in quick succession. He then joined Herne Bay later in the season.

He spent the 1978/79 campaign there too and also played once for Canterbury during the season but in March 1980 Gerry returned to Ramsgate once again.

He then played for Sheppey during 1980/81 and Gerry was selected in the Kent League's representative side during the campaign before moving on to Deal for the 1981/82 season.

In November 1982 Gerry joined Thanet United on loan from Deal and made his debut in 1-0 defeat at Basingstoke on 6.11.82. Three days later he made his home debut, scoring with a volley from ten yards in a 1-1 draw with Gravesend & Northfleet.

Gerry then returned to Deal and took his career tally of goals for them to 40 in 119 appearances but in January 1983 he signed for United on a permanent basis. Although he struggled for goals early on the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that he "considerably gingered up the strike force". In February 1983 Gerry had to serve a two week ban for being sent off in a Sunday League game for his club Margate Athletic but he began to find his scoring touch when he returned to action. On 19.3.83 what the Thanet Times called "one magic moment of memorable opportunism" from Gerry gave United a 1-0 win at Dover. He beat two defenders and unleashed a shot from just outside area that screamed into the bottom corner past Joe Radford. He scored three times more before the end of the 1982/83 campaign to finish the season with a record of 17 appearances and five goals. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said that Gerry had "repeatedly impressed with his willingness to take a man on and become involved in the box".

He stayed with United for the 1983/84 season but Gerry was plagued by injuries. The worst of them was an ankle injury sustained in a game at Salisbury on 12.11.83 that kept him out of action until February 1984. As a result Gerry only made 28 appearances (two of them as a substitute) and scored just two goals during the season. The first was a memorable effort, Gerry beat two defenders before firing home from a narrow angle in a 4-1 defeat at Tonbridge on 25.2.84. He left United in the summer of 1984 and joined Herne Bay for the 1984/85 campaign.

Gerry rejoined Ramsgate towards the end of the 1985/86 season but only played a handful of matches before breaking his leg. He had another spell with the Rams during the 1990/91 campaign, scoring once in two first team appearances and also finding the net three times in 14 games for the reserves.

He played the last football of his career during the 1990's when he turned out for Thanet League club Margate Athletic Old Boys whose squad of veterans also included a host of other former Margate / Thanet players.

In 2011 Gerry was living in Margate.

name: Hugh Jordan
other clubs: Falkirk (Scotland), Norwich City (18,3)
bio:
Hugh McNaughton Jordan. Born Musselburgh, Lothian
Started his football career with Scottish League Falkirk in 1929, before moving south to join Third Division (South) Norwich City in 1930. He made his Football League debut against Notts County in September 1930, and scored 3 goals in 20 appearances during the 1930-31 season before joining non league Margate in 1931.
But he is best known for his time in France, which during the 1930 s was a very popular place for British players to play professionally, where he achieved significant success with the likes of Stade de Riems, Olympique Dunkerque, and Racing Club de Paris.

bio:

The Jordan in 30/31(2) as player looks like 46/47 reserve trainer Jordan..   
 3.1.31 scored 6 for reserves in 13-0 home win over Deal in Folkestone & District League. // Scored 5 in trial match ahead of 31/32

name: Anthony Joseph
other clubs: Chertsey Town, Ashford Town (Middlesex), Bromley, Kingstonian, Sutton United, Carshalton Athletic, Chipstead and Tooting & Mitcham United
bio:
Pacy London-born attacker who started his career with Isthmian League Division 2 club Chertsey where he scored seven times in 36 league outings (six as sub) during the 2003/04 season.

In September 2004 Anthony joined Ashford (Middlesex) who were in Division 1 West of the Southern League at that time and he was still with the club during the 2006/07 campaign - Ashford s first in the Isthmian League Premier Division. Anthony only featured in seven league matches (twice as sub) without scoring during an injury-hit season but he played more regularly during 2007/08. The Thanet Times report on Ashford s 0-0 draw with visitors Margate on 6.10.07 said that Anthony was the game s best player" and the paper also noted that he gave Margate full-back Louis Smith a going over". Anthony scored four times in 31 Premier Division appearances (11 as sub) during 2007/08 and also managed two goals in cup ties.

In July 2008 he signed for Bromley and after a few months there Anthony moved on to Kingstonian in December 2008.

He made three Isthmian League Division 1 South appearances for the K s without scoring before going back to Ashford in February 2009.

Anthony finished the 2008/09 season there and scored three times in 14 Premier League outings (two as sub).

In the summer of 2009 he linked up with Sutton and in November 2009 Anthony was loaned to Margate in what was intended to be a three month deal.

He made his debut as a substitute in a 3-2 defeat against Cray at Bromley in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 29.11.09 and on 5.12.09 Anthony made his first start for Margate. He marked the occasion by scoring with what the Thanet Times called a wonderful shot" into the far corner from just outside penalty area having beaten two defenders on a probing run. The match ended in a 2-2 draw and when the Thanet Times asked manager Mark Butler for a comment on Anthony s goal he remarked a bit special, that."

Anthony started seven of Margate s next eight games and in its report on a 1-0 win over Maidstone at Ashford on 26.12.09 the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he gave the hosts a right going-over". Margate lost the return match against Maidstone 1-0 at Hartsdown Park on 2.1.10 and the Thanet Times said Anthony looked a threat with his pace". He made his last appearance in a 2-0 defeat at Kingstonian on 31.1.10 and the Thanet Times said Anthony was kicked out of the game" by big home defender Francis Duku. In all Anthony had scored once from nine outings (one as sub) before his loan was cut short.

After returning to Sutton he featured in a few games before the end of the season and Anthony finished 2009/10 having scored four goals from 18 Premier League appearances (eight as sub) for the Surrey club.

Having been released by Sutton Anthony featured in a friendly for Tonbridge in the summer of 2010 before signing for Carshalton ahead of the 2010/11 campaign proper. Their manager at the time was former Margate boss Mark Butler.

Anthony made 27 Premier League appearances (ten as sub) for Carshalton during 2010/11 and although he didn t score in the league he did manage two goals in cup ties. Anthony then made a further 16 league appearances (12 as sub) for the Robins during the 2011/12 season and his only goal of the campaign came in a cup tie. He was released in May 2012.

After leaving Carshalton Anthony had a few months out of football before signing for Division 1 South outfit Chipstead in September 2012. He made four league appearances (one as sub) there without scoring.

In October 2012 he moved on to Tooting & Mitcham, also of Division 1 South, and at that time former Margate player Jamie Lawrence was also in the Terrors squad. Anthony finished the 2012/13 season there and scored three times from 29 league outings (seven as sub).

name: Ricardo Joseph
other clubs: Sutton United, Rushden & Diamonds (1,0), Rugby Town, Worthing United, Harrow Borough, Ashford Town (Middlesex), Carshalton Athletic and Metropolitan Police
bio:
5' 11" tall Jamaican full-back who started his career in Sutton's youth ranks before being signed by Football League club Rushden & Diamonds in 2003 aged 16.

Ricardo progressed through Rushden's junior sides and for some of his time at the club future Margate goalkeeper Scott Chalmers-Stevens was also part of the squad.

On 7.1.06 Ricardo made his first team debut at left-back as Rushden lost 2-0 at Peterborough in a League Two game but although he was named as a substitute for two more matches later in the 2005/06 campaign he didn't make another senior appearance.

In March 2006 Ricardo briefly joined Southern League Premier Division club Rugby on loan but he only played once before returning to Nene Park.

At the end of the 2005/06 season Rushden were relegated from the Football League and Ricardo was released.

In the summer of 2006 he signed for Isthmian League Premier Division club Worthing and Ricardo made six league appearances there without scoring before being released in November 2006. He didn't play anywhere else during the remainder of the 2006/07 campaign.

Ricardo returned to football a few weeks into the 2007/08 season when he joined Harrow and he made five Isthmian League Premier Division appearances for them before signing for Margate in December 2007. His old Rushden team-mate Scott Chalmers-Stevens had recommended him to the club.

Ricardo made his debut at left-back in a 1-1 draw with Ramsgate in an Isthmian League Premier Division game at Hartsdown Park on Boxing Day 2007 and he also started Margate's next two matches in the number three shirt. On 19.1.08 he was due to play in a home game against Carshalton but Ricardo was delayed in traffic en route to the match and only arrived in time to feature as a second half substitute.

After returning to the starting line-up at right-back in a 2-1 win over visitors Chatham in a Kent Senior Cup tie on 22.1.08 Ricardo then enjoyed a lengthy run in the side at left-back and only missed two of Margate's remaining 17 games. The Thanet Times described him as "outstanding" in a 1-0 home win over Billericay on 8.3.08 and said Ricardo was "nice and solid in defence and bombing on to join the attack". On 26.4.08 he made what turned out to be his final appearance for Margate in a 1-0 win at Harrow and Ricardo left the club at the end of the season after playing 20 times (once as sub) without scoring.

In June 2008 he signed for Isthmian League Premier Division Ashford (Middlesex) and Ricardo went on to make 82 appearances (five as sub) there without scoring before moving on to Carshalton in March 2010.

He played nine times (three as sub) for the Robins without scoring before the end of the 2009/10 campaign and then scored once from 16 Isthmian League Premier Division outings during 2010/11. Ricardo stayed with Carshalton for the 2011/12 season and made 26 league appearances (four as sub) without scoring. He was still with the club during 2012/13 and featured 35 times in Premier Division games (once as sub) without breaking his goal duck.

At the start of July 2013 Ricardo signed for Premier Division club Metropolitan Police.

name: Billy Jowett
other clubs: Wickersley, Eastwood United, Beighton Miners Welfare, Hull City (0), Weymouth, Deal Town, Betteshanger Colliery Welfare and Sittingbourne
bio:
Skilful, energetic, inside-left born in Rotherham who started his career with Wickersley, helping them to win the Rotherham Intermediate League during 1945/46.

Billy then spent the 1946/47 season with Eastwood before moving to Beighton Miners Welfare in the summer of 1947. During his time there, the club were runners-up in both the Sheffield Association League and the Sheffield Senior Cup.

In October 1948 Billy was signed by Hull following a successful trial spell with the club. He spent around 18 months with the Tigers but never broke into the first team and at the end of the 1949/50 campaign he was released.

Billy spent 1950/51 with Southern League outfit Weymouth before moving to Kent in the summer of 1951.

He signed for Deal and made his debut for them in a Kent League game against Dover at the Charles Ground on 18.8.51, scoring in a 2-2 draw that was watched by a crowd of 4,200. Dover s goals were scored by future Margate players Len Dolding and Eric Worthington. Billy went on to become a very popular player at Deal and was known for his accurate crosses.

In November 1952 Billy joined Margate for a fee of £100 and he made his debut on 29.11.52, coincidentally in a Kent League game against Deal at Hartsdown Park. The match finished 2-2 and Billy went on to make 28 appearances during the remainder of the 1952/53 season, scoring five times. His tricky performance in a 1-0 win at Canterbury on 28.3.53 prompted the East Kent Times to headline their match report for the game "Super Salesman" with a sub-headline of "Cheeky Billy's Bluffs". The report went on to say that "diminutive Billy Jowett reached the super salesman class at Canterbury on Saturday. He sold the bewildered City defenders so many dummies that they must have left the field convinced the will-o'-the-wisp Margate inside forward could have found a breed buyer for a mongrel pup at Crufts". Billy finished the campaign by playing as Margate drew 1-1 with visitors Folkestone on 9.5.53 to share the Kent Senior Shield.

He stayed with Margate for the 1953/54 season and on 3.9.53 Billy inadvertently started something of a riot in a derby game at Ramsgate. He clashed with the Rams player-manager Jimmy Blair, causing him an injury that saw him leave the field on a stretcher, and a large amount of spectators rushed onto the pitch. It was sometime before order was restored and after the match ended with Margate winning 3-2, some 500 Ramsgate supporters besieged Margate's dressing room for around 90 minutes. They broke down the door and the police had to be called to restore order and ensure the Margate team's safety.

Billy was a fixture in the number ten shirt for the remainder of the 1953/54 campaign, making a total of 38 appearances and scoring eight times. His tricky skills often earned him praise from the local press. Billy finished the season by scoring as Margate beat Canterbury 5-0 at Hartsdown Park on 6.5.54 to win the Kent League Cup after a replay, he d also featured in the first match.

The 1954/55 season wasn't such a good one for Billy and he made only nine sporadic first team appearances, spending the rest of the campaign in the reserves. However his 17 goals for the second string made him their second top scorer behind Jimmy Briscoe.

Billy found himself in the reserves for practically the whole of the 1955/56 season too and on 31.8.55 he bizarrely had to play in his socks for the last twenty minutes of a reserve team game against Ashford. He was sent off to have a boot repaired, returned with only one boot, was sent off again and finally returned without any boots. He made 12 further first team appearances during the season but they turned out to be his last for the club. Billy's final match was the Kent League Cup Final against Gillingham Reserves at Hartsdown on 10.5.56, a game which Margate lost 2-1.

In the summer of 1956, Billy joined Betteshanger as they offered him and his new wife a house, the club's ground was at the bottom of his garden. On 22.3.58 Billy scored from the penalty spot as Betteshanger drew 1-1 with visitors Margate and on 30.8.58 he missed a penalty in a home match against Margate but Betteshanger still ran out 5-2 winners. Billy stayed with the colliery outfit until he retired in 1961.

Billy later played Sunday football for Deal Wanderers and then had a short spell as manager of Deal. He was in charge there at the start of the 1963/64 season and made one appearance for the reserves - in a 2-1 home defeat against eventual Metropolitan League champions Gillingham Reserves on 18.1.64. It was Billy s only outing as a player and in March 1964 he was replaced as Deal s manager by future Margate player Larry Baxter.

At the start of the 1965/66 campaign, Billy accepted the offer of a position on Deal's Executive Committee aged 37 and in October 1965 he was persuaded to become player-coach of Deal's reserve side. They were known as Deal Town 'A' and played in both the Kent Amateur League and the Thames & Medway Combination. In the programme for Deal's first team game against Hinckley on 30.10.65 it was noted "now Bill Jowitt (sic) is able to turn out for the lads his experience and coaxing will certainly be an advantage to the team and already he is holding the defence together and making it a defence that won't give many goals away this season".

On 5.3.66 Billy added a new name to his list of clubs when he turned out for Sittingbourne as they were a man short for their Thames & Medway Combination match against Deal 'A'. Although Sittingbourne lost 3-1 Billy scored their goal with a well-judged lob and his guest appearance for the Brickies was mentioned in the programme for Deal's first team game against Kettering the following Saturday. That was ill-advised as if word had got out about Billy helping Sittingbourne out Deal could have been fined by the Kent County Football Association.

In April 2002 Billy was still living in the house that Betteshanger had provided for him and the East Kent Mercury ran a story in which Billy recalled the Deal v Betteshanger local derbies he d played in.

Billy died on 31.5.05 aged 76 and an article in the East Kent Mercury described him as being "one of the finest local footballers of the past 50 years". Former Deal groundsman Gilham Thompsett said "he was a great footballer and a lovely man he loved his cricket as well, and he was always going to watch Kent play." Betteshanger chairman Roy Barlow described Billy as "a legend in local football." He went on to say "anyone you talk to who saw him play always says what a great player he was he was a really smashing guy."

Billy's son Micky played for clubs including Dover, Folkestone and Ashford during the late 1970's and early 1980's.

name: Terry Joyce
other clubs: Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
Tough-tackling, Margate-born full-back who started his career with Ramsgate. Terry joined the club for the 1947/48 campaign after the Rams had spotted him playing in junior football and he started the season in the reserves. On 17.1.48 Terry made his first team debut for Ramsgate as they beat Snowdown Colliery Welfare 4-2 in a Kent League game at Southwood.

He was part of the Rams side that won the Kent League Cup during 1948/49 and the Kent League title during 1949/50. Terry played many games for Kent as an amateur during four seasons with Ramsgate and also represented the county at table tennis.

In May 1951 Terry joined Margate and made his debut in a 0-0 draw with Whitstable in the Kent League at Hartsdown Park on 18.8.51. He quickly formed a notable full-back partnership with Jack Yeomanson but contracted pleurisy in November 1951 and missed several games. Unluckily for Terry, the illness first developed on the way to his honeymoon. He made a total of 32 appearances without scoring during the 1951/52 campaign.

Terry continued to be the club's first-choice left-back during 1952/53 and added another 33 appearances but still didn't find the net. On 9.5.53 he was part of the side that drew 1-1 with visitors Folkestone on 9.5.53 to share the Kent Senior Shield and the Isle of Thanet Gazette's end of season round-up said that Terry "went through many successive matches without an opponent passing him".

Despite being troubled by a knee injury Terry made 35 appearances during 1953/54 and interested Football League clubs. He featured as Margate beat Canterbury 5-0 at Hartsdown Park to win the Kent League Cup on 6.5.54.

Terry notched up a further 42 appearances during the 1954/55 season to take his total for club comfortably past 100. He also finally broke his scoring duck when he got a late goal in a 3-2 defeat against Tunbridge Wells in the Kent League Cup Final at Hartsdown Park on 30.4.55.

During 1955/56 Terry made 35 more appearances but he missed about six weeks of the campaign due to an ankle injury. On 19.11.55 he was in the Margate side that drew 2-2 with Walsall at Hartsdown Park in the FA Cup 1st Round and Terry also played in the replay at Walsall on 24.11.55 that the home side won 6-1. At the end of the season Margate manager Almer Hall paid tribute to him saying "if we had 11 Terry Joyce's what a cracking side it would be." He added "We could have sold him over and over again. He is the finest left-back in the Kent League, bar none."

Terry made 42 appearances during the 1956/57 campaign and Derek Wells became his regular full-back partner due to Jack Yeomanson having injury problems. On 17.11.56 Terry was part of the Margate side that beat Dunstable 3-1 at Hartsdown Park in the FA Cup 1st Round and he also played in a 4-0 defeat at Millwall in the 2nd Round on 8.12.56. Terry scored twice during the season to triple his career tally for the club and his first goal came in a 3-1 win over Chatham at Hartsdown Park on 16.3.57. His second followed just a fortnight later in a 3-1 win at Ashford on 30.3.57. Terry actually played as a forward during that match but was quickly restored to his customary position of left-back.

Early in the 1957/58 season Terry made his 200th appearance for Margate and in total he played 39 times during the campaign although another ankle problem forced him to miss a few games. On 16.11.57 he played as Margate lost 3-2 to visitors Crystal Palace in the FA Cup 1st Round.

Terry managed to steer clear of injuries during the 1958/59 season and notched up 49 appearances, scoring twice more. The second of his strikes came in an 8-0 win over Sheppey on 2.5.59 and was Margate s 100th Kent League goal of the season. Earlier in the campaign - on 15.11.58 - Terry had been in the side that lost 3-2 at Headington in the FA Cup 1st Round.

The 1959/60 campaign saw Terry pass 300 appearances for the club and he played 48 games without scoring despite missing almost two months of the season through injury. On 14.11.59 he played in a 1-1 draw at Kettering in the FA Cup 1st Round and Terry also featured in the replay at Hartsdown Park on 19.11.59 that Margate won 3-2. He was then in the side that drew 0-0 with visitors Crystal Palace in the 2nd Round on 5.12.59 and took part in the replay at Selhurst Park on 9.12.59 that the Eagles won 3-0. At the end of the campaign Margate manager Almer Hall paid tribute to Terry at the club's annual meeting and said "I think he is an extremely good full-back, also, he mends my wireless set from time to time."

During the 1960/61 season Terry continued to be the club's first-choice left-back and he made a further 34 appearances. However he missed a portion of the season due to suffering a wrenched thigh.

The 1961/62 campaign saw Terry make 54 appearances to pass 400 for the club. He was as good as ever and the local paper described him as "evergreen" and "reliability personified". However on 16.9.61 Terry was sent off in a 1-1 draw at Canterbury after a clash with future Margate player Johnny Ray and he received a seven day ban. Remarkably Terry had never even been booked before. He also suffered head injuries in four consecutive games during November 1961 and in a famous FA Cup 1st Round tie at Bournemouth & Boscombe on 4.11.61 Terry was knocked out after 35 minutes but carried on despite having a minor concussion and helped Margate to win 3-0. He also featured in the 2nd Round tie against Notts County at Hartsdown Park on 25.11.61 which ended in a 1-1 draw and in the replay at Notts County on 30.11.61 which the home side won 3-1. On 12.5.62 Terry was part of the Margate side that beat visitors Folkestone 4-0 to win the Kent Senior Shield.

During the 1962/63 season he made a further 43 appearances and managed two goals, his first since the 1958/59 campaign. Terry was as steady and sound as usual as Margate won the Southern League Division One title and on 3.11.62 he was in the side that lost 3-1 at Millwall in the FA Cup 1st Round. On 7.5.63 Terry played as Margate won 2-0 at Maidstone in the 1st Leg of the Kent Floodlight Cup Final and he also featured in the 2nd Leg at Hartsdown Park on 13.5.63 which Margate won 3-0 to claim the trophy. On 1.6.63 he was in the team that beat visitors Bexleyheath & Welling 1-0 in the Kent Senior Shield Final.

Knee problems restricted his appearances during the 1963/64 campaign but Terry still played 41 times to take his appearance tally for the club past 500 - the first player ever to reach that landmark. On 21.9.63 he played as a left winger in a game against Wisbech and he was often outstanding during the season. On 16.11.63 Terry played as Margate drew 2-2 at Brentford in the FA Cup 1st Round and then on 20.11.63 he featured in the replay at Hartsdown Park that the Bees won 2-0.

In recognition of his superb service Terry was granted a testimonial - a Kent Floodlight Cup game against Folkestone at Hartsdown Park on 2.12.63. He was presented with a gold watch before the match which Margate unfortunately lost 3-1. The attendance was 1,523 and helped earn Terry the sum of £275, a figure which also included donations from the club and well-wishers.

On 30.4.64 Terry was booked for arguing in a 4-4 draw at Bexley and the match turned out to be his last for the club. In May 1964 he was controversially released, partly because his right knee was believed to be a major problem. However Terry refuted that and in fact only found out he'd been released when he read the local paper - a sad way to finish. The story made the front page of the Isle of Thanet Gazette under the headline "They Might Have Told Me - Says Axed Soccer Man".

Terry found himself out of football altogether at the start of the 1964/65 season but in October 1964 he rejoined Ramsgate, over 14 years since he'd left Southwood. A month earlier Terry had turned down an offer to play for Sittingbourne. He made a handful of appearances for the Rams during the remainder of the season.

Terry made his last appearance for the Rams first team during the 1965/66 season and by then he was running a hotel in Margate. He went on to manage Ramsgate s youth and reserve sides and still played for the reserves during the 1966/67 and 1967/68 seasons.

He left Ramsgate by mutual consent in the summer of 1972.

In 1973, prior to the Margate v Tottenham FA Cup tie, a piece about Terry appeared in The Sun newspaper. It was headed " Margate Miss The 'Tank' " and was full of memories about his playing style.

Terry was described as "a classically built full-back...short back and sides...a bull neck...barrel chest, massive legs and toe-capped boots". The article went on to describe what the author called "a Hartsdown Park ritual" - Terry's "specials." They were his crunching tackles - "The crowd would cheer him every ground-shaking inch of the way. He would run full tilt at a winger to a point about a dozen yards from the disaster area and there was a sort of excited wail from the terraces. Then a great oak of a leg would snap out and the turf would be scarred as he slid towards his victim. The sounds from the terraces were now akin to a four-ale bar at chucking-out time. Finally the crunch - just a blur of distorted limbs. The crowd, hoarse with excitement, would take a few minutes to simmer down into muttered appreciation of a job well done. That he always got the ball, never the man, was, I feel, the result of truly sensible discretion on the part of opponents".

In the summer of 1981 Terry became manager of a local youth side called Northwood.

He worked as a radio mechanic early in his football career and later worked for Standfast as a Technical Manager for many years.

In 2007 Terry was still living in the Margate area, not far from Hartsdown Park.

By March 2014 he was living in care home in Thanet and unfortunately suffering from dementia.

Terry died aged 89 on Christmas Day 2016.

name: Ishmail Kamara
other clubs: Issia Wazi (Ivory Coast), Virginia Beach Mariners (USA), Thai Honda (Thailand) Willem II (Netherlands), Palm Harbor University of Tampa Bay (USA), Real Maryland Monarchs (USA), Motala AIF (Sweden), Brighton & Hove Albion (0), Maidenhead United, Dulwich Hamlet, Barnet (0+1,0), Dartford and VCD Athletic
bio:
Unorthodox 6 1" tall striker born in Freetown, Sierra Leone who started his career with Issia Wazi of the Ivory Coast where he scored seven goals from 16 outings during the 2004/05 season.

Ishmail then played for Virginia Beach Mariners in the USA during the 2005 campaign before moving to Thailand.

He joined Thai Honda for 2006/07 and Ishmail also spent the 2007/08 season there.

On 17.10.07 he made his international debut for Sierra Leone when he played the full 90 minutes of a 1-0 home win over Guine-Bissau and Ishmail went on to win another four caps as a substitute between November 2007 and June 2008.

At the end of 2007/08 he left Thai Honda having scored 13 times in 23 career appearances there and during his time with the club Ishmail had also had a trial with Dutch outfit Willem II.

He then studied in the USA and during the 2008 season there Ishmail scored 20 goals for Palm Harbor University of Tampa Bay. He was also selected for the All-Pinellas County team.

Ishmail spent the 2009 campaign with Real Maryland Monarchs and when the USA season finished he joined Swedish club Motala AIF towards the end of 2009.

He scored twice from seven appearances for Motala during 2009/10 and in November 2009 Ishmail scored for Sierra Leone in a friendly against Willem II where he d trialed two years earlier.

By March 2010 Ishmail had arrived in England and after a short trial with Wycombe he played in one reserve team game for Brighton before the end of the 2009/10 campaign.

In the summer of 2010 Ishmail had a trial with Leeds before appearing in friendlies for Margate and scoring five goals in pre-season at a time when his identity was seemingly unknown to anybody. He was signed on for 2010/11 and on the eve of the new campaign manager Iain O Connell spoke about Ishmail to the Isle of Thanet Gazette and said Still got no idea what his other name is ! He s one of the best athletes in the side and he has an eye for goal. From Sierra Leone but seems to have picked up English and he s lucky to have me and John Keister as his personal chauffeurs. We have to take him everywhere !"

Ishmail missed the first game of the season as Margate were awaiting international clearance for him due to his last club being Motala in Sweden but on 28.8.10 he made his debut in a 2-1 defeat at Lowestoft in the Isthmian League Premier Division. Ishmail then came on as a substitute in Margate s next three matches.

In the third of those games - a match against Aveley at Hartsdown Park on 7.9.10 - he was due to start but a London Underground strike delayed Ishmail s arrival at the ground and he was introduced as a half-time sub instead. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he was the star man" as Margate scored twice in the second half to win 2-0 and scared the Aveley defence half to death". The paper said the visitors didn t have a clue what to do about a player with pace, strength and skill who was happy to run at them all night long".

Iain O Connell told the Gazette He s got an agent and has already had a two-day trial at Leeds. He s similar to Akpo Sodje. It wouldn t surprise me at all if he got a league club but I hope he s here for a while yet. He would have started against Aveley but the train strike meant he only got to the ground five minutes before kick-off. We were awful first half so I put him on for the second half and he completely changed the game." When asked how he d have dealt with Ishmail during his playing days O Connell said I d have kicked him as hard as I could ! Having said that, I d have to try and catch him first ! He s got that awkward running style but he s even quicker than he looks. He s also strong and has amazing feet."

Ishmail started Margate s next game - an FA Cup tie at Binfield on 11.9.10 - and scored his first goal for the club in a 3-0 win. He then kept his place for the following match on 18.9.10 and Ishmail took what the Thanet Times called one of the worst penalties you ll see" as Margate beat Wealdstone 1-0 at Hartsdown Park. He blazed a first half spot-kick over the top and the paper said don t know what it is about gangly players standing over a penalty but you never fancy them". The Times continued sure enough, Kamara lifted the ball miles over the bar and out of the ground".

Despite his penalty embarrassment Ishmail started again as Margate travelled to Folkestone on 21.9.10 but he limped off with a calf problem after just six minutes. Margate went on to win 2-1 and Ishmail missed the next game due to his injury. He was back in the side as Margate lost on penalties in an FA Cup tie at Kingstonian on 27.9.10 after the match finished 1-1 after extra time but Ishmail then missed another two matches due to injury.

After returning to action in a 6-1 home win over Horsham on 9.10.10 he missed two more games and Ishmail then wore the number nine shirt in a 0-0 draw at Billericay on 23.10.10. It was his last outing for Margate and he was released a few days later. Iain O Connell said Ishmail certainly has something about him, but I m just not getting enough minutes on the pitch from him so reluctantly I have had to release him. I would like to thank him for his efforts, and wish him the best of luck at his next club." Ishmail had scored once from a total of ten appearances (three as sub) before his departure.

He didn t play elsewhere during the remainder of the 2010/11 season but in the summer of 2011 Ishmail featured in three friendlies for Conference club Forest Green, scoring once in a 3-0 home win over Hereford on 30.7.11. However he wasn t signed by the Gloucestershire outfit and started the 2011/12 campaign as a free agent.

In September 2011 Ishmail signed for Conference South club Maidenhead and he spent a few weeks there before linking up with Dulwich of the Isthmian League Division 1 South in November 2011.

Ishmail spent the remainder of 2011/12 there and scored 14 times in 25 league outings (two as sub). He also got one goal in cup ties before leaving the club at the end of the season.

In May 2012 media reports suggested that Ishmail was likely to move into the Football League with AFC Bournemouth and Stevenage being mentioned as interested parties but in the end he started the 2012/13 campaign without a club.

A few weeks into the new season Ishmail started training with League Two outfit Barnet and at the end of September 2012 the Bees gave him a two-year contract. He told the club s website "I'm so happy that I've signed, everyone has made me feel so welcome and I'd like to thank the technical team for giving me this opportunity."

Barnet s head coach Mark Robson said of the signing "Ishmail is an extremely hungry lad that's desperate to do well and he really impressed us whilst training. Ishmail stands at 6ft 1in, he's strong and very quick which will help compliment our team."

He made his debut for the Bees as an 80th minute substitute in a 2-1 defeat at Fleetwood on 29.9.12 but Ishmail dislocated his shoulder soon after coming on and didn t feature again in Barnet s first team before the end of the 2012/13 campaign which saw them relegated to the Conference. In May 2013 he was released.

In December 2013 Ishmail resurfaced when he signed for Conference club Dartford and he made his debut for the Darts as a substitute in a 2-1 defeat at Alfreton on 21.12.13.

At the end of January 2014 Dartford loaned Ishmail to Isthmian League Division 1 North club VCD and he made his debut in a 2-0 home win over Thurrock on 4.2.14. VCD s manager Tony Russell told the Kentish Football website We lacked a little spark up front and when Tony (Burman, the Dartford manager) said he wanted to get him out to get some games we jumped at the chance He done his work well, bits and pieces, hold up play, lay-off play. He had two one-on-one s and the goalie s not made a save ! It s not good enough and that s him saying that as well for a man that s played at that level. We should be scoring them really but he was neat and tidy.

name: Peter Kavanagh
other clubs: Dagenham, Fulham (0), Romford, Everton (6,0), Brentford (0), Gravesend & Northfleet, Buffalo White Eagles (Canada), Brentford (0), Stevenage Town and Brentwood Town
bio:
5' 10" tall, speedy left winger born in Romford who played for Dagenham Schoolboys as a youth alongside the great Jimmy Greaves.

Peter started his senior career with Dagenham before moving to Fulham in October 1956. Peter didn't make the first team at Craven Cottage and in the summer of 1959 he dropped back into non-league football to play for his hometown club Romford.

Peter made his debut for Romford in a game against Guildford on 22.8.59 and went on to score 17 goals from 69 appearances before 1st Division club Everton paid 1550 for his services in February 1961.

Peter made his first team debut for the Toffees in a 1-1 draw with Chelsea at Goodison Park on 18.2.61 and the match was watched by a crowd of 34,449. His former Dagenham Schoolboys colleague Jimmy Greaves was in the Chelsea side along with the likes of Terry Venables and Peter Bonetti . Peter made five further senior appearances for Everton in their next six matches but in the last of them - a 3-0 defeat at West Bromwich on 25.3.61 - he suffered a broken leg. The injury ended his professional career and Peter was released at the end of the 1960/61 season.

Peter then returned to the non-league game once more and joined Gravesend & Northfleet in the summer of 1961.

He made 31 appearances for the Fleet during the first half of the 1961/62 season, scoring twice, before joining Margate in March 1962. Margate manager Almer Hall said Kavanagh, whom I rate very highly, is a good ball player and has a tremendous shot. He will help out with the many league matches we still have to play. He is not eligible for cup games.

Peter scored twice on his debut for Margate s reserves in a 4-2 home win over Sittingbourne on 21.3.62 and then made his senior debut in a 2-1 defeat at Dartford on 31.3.62. He only played twice more for the first team before leaving the club in April 1962.

In May 1962 Peter signed for Canadian club Buffalo White Eagles who played in the Eastern Canada Professional Soccer League.

He was back in England by September 1962 and Peter spent a month on trial with Brentford at that time but wasn t signed by the club.

He later played for Stevenage, joining the Southern League outfit for the 1963/64 season, and scored four times from 21 appearances for them before leaving the club early in 1964.

Peter also had a spell with Brentwood Town as his career drew to a close.

name: Freddie Kearns
other clubs: Shamrock Rovers (Ireland), West Ham United (45,15), Norwich City (30,14), Tonbridge and Deal Town
bio:
Whole-hearted, 5' 11" tall striker born in Cork, Ireland who only started playing football aged 16, concentrating on hurling prior to that. Freddie began his career with Irish side Shamrock Rovers before joining West Ham in May 1948.

He went on to make 45 appearances for the Hammers and scored 15 times in all competitions during a six year stay at Upton Park. During the 1953/54 season, Freddie gained an international cap for Ireland when he played in a World Cup Qualifier against Luxembourg.

In June 1954 he joined Norwich for the handsome fee of £9,000. Freddie went on to play 30 games for the Canaries and scored 14 times before dropping into non-league football to join Tonbridge at the end of the 1955/56 campaign.

He scored 12 goals from 54 appearances for the Angels during 1956/57 and usually played as an inside left with future Aston Villa manager Ron Saunders wearing Tonbridge's number nine shirt. Freddie worked as a window cleaner at the time.

In the summer of 1957, he joined Margate and Freddie made an immediate impact by scoring a hat-trick on his debut - a 5-0 win at Ashford in the Kent League on 24.8.57. He also bagged three goals in a 6-1 home win over Sheppey on 26.12.57 and in total scored 30 times during the 1957/58 season. One of his goals came in Margate's 3-2 home defeat at the hands of Crystal Palace in an FA Cup 1st Round tie on 16.11.57.

During 1958/59 Freddie notched up 27 goals in 48 games and he was joint top scorer with Tony Spink. He managed three hat-tricks including back-to-back trebles in a 9-5 home win over Chatham on 4.10.58 and a 5-1 win at Ramsgate on 11.10.58. It would be almost 30 years before another player would emulate the feat and Freddie might have scored more goals but for the fact that he played numerous games at full-back and in midfield. Freddie also had a few games on the right wing during which the local press said that he "cantered around like an exultant stag". Early in the season he d suffered concussion during a match against Ramsgate on 4.9.58 and Freddie played the entire second half with the problem. Afterwards he couldn't remember anything about those 45 minutes and didn't even know that Margate had won the game 2-1. However Freddie played again just two days later. He was also part of the Margate side that lost 3-2 at Headington in the FA Cup 1st Round on 15.11.58.

The 1959/60 season was a superb one for Freddie as he scored 41 times in his 52 first team appearances. On 14.11.59 he got the Margate goal in a 1-1 draw at Kettering in the FA Cup 1st Round and Freddie then got all three in the replay at Hartsdown Park on 19.11.59 that Margate won 3-2. He was in the side that drew 0-0 with visitors Crystal Palace in the 2nd Round on 5.12.59 and also played in the replay at Selhurst Park on 9.12.59 that the Eagles won 3-0.

Freddie scored four other hat-tricks, hit all four goals in a 4-1 win over Bexleyheath & Welling on 24.10.59 and bagged five goals in a 6-1 Southern League win over Trowbridge at Hartsdown Park on 30.1.60. He was described as "having the biggest heart in the world" by the local press and in its end of season review the East Kent Times wrote "Without a doubt, if Margate had not had such a stalwart player as Freddie Kearns they would have been in a sorry state. After Christmas, when outside-left (Ken) Tucker was rarely 100 per cent fit, it was generally Kearns - and Kearns alone - who ever looked like scoring".

Freddie never managed to gain a regular first team place during the 1960/61 season despite his scoring exploits and he spent the majority of the campaign in the reserves. That was mainly due to the signing of Alan Brown but the local press felt that Freddie should still have been Margate's first-choice centre-forward. As it was he only made 15 first team appearances and many of them were at left-back. Freddie scored just once during the season - in a 3-3 draw with Kettering at Hartsdown on 27.8.60 - and in the summer of 1961 he was released. During his time at Hartsdown he'd been known as a real character in the dressing room.

After leaving Margate Freddie was offered terms by Canterbury but turned them down. Later in the 1961/62 season he joined Deal and played for them during the 1962/63 campaign too before retiring from senior football.

During the 1964/65 season Freddie sometimes turned out for Margate Rangers in the Thanet Premier Sunday League.

He later had spells coaching Margate County Youth Club FC and then Sunday League side Quarterdeck in the early 1970's.

Freddie made a brief return to senior football when he became assistant manager of Ramsgate in July 1980. He was former Margate player Graham Sawyer's right-hand man until October 1980 when Sawyer was sacked.

In October 1985 the Thanet Times mentioned that Freddie had paid a rare visit to Hartsdown Park to watch Thanet United beat Dorchester 5-0. He was quoted as saying "there is so little atmosphere in the ground nowadays" - the attendance was just 142 - and was described as being "one of the most popular players ever to wear a Margate shirt".

Freddie was a radio mechanic for many years and finished his working life at RAF Manston.

His son John had a spell with Margate during the 1970/71 and 1971/72 seasons.

Freddie sadly died suddenly on 7.1.87, the day before his 60th birthday. He'd been living in Margate at the time. The Isle of Thanet Gazette's Dave Cooper paid tribute to him, saying that Freddie was "as brave a centre-forward as any East Kent soccer fan has ever seen." He went on to say that Freddie "never admitted defeat on the field until the final whistle had gone and many of his goals came from what appeared to be hopeless situations."

name: John Kearns
other clubs: Brighton & Hove Albion (0), Coventry City (0), Epping Town
bio:
Well-built centre-forward who was the son of legendary Margate striker Freddie Kearns.

John played for the Thanet Primary Schools side during the 1963/64 season alongside future Margate player Ricky Fusco.

John started his senior career with a spell on the books of Brighton & Hove Albion before joining Margate as an amateur in the summer of 1970, shortly before his 18th birthday. John quickly impressed in the reserves early in the 1970/71 season and in September 1970 he started a month's trial at Coventry. John played for City's 'A' team during his spell at Highfield Road.

Having returned to Hartsdown Park, John made his first team debut in a 3-0 win at Weymouth in the Southern League on 14.11.70 and had a good game, resulting in him signing professional forms soon after the match. The local paper described him as having "bags of heart" and player-manager Gerry Baker said I was very impressed with his showing against Weymouth and the obvious improvement he has made during his short experience away. He is one of the enthusiastic talented youngsters of great promise whom I want with Margate.

John s performance in Margate's 2-0 defeat at Dagenham in the FA Cup 1st Round on 21.11.70 prompted the Thanet Times to say that he had "latent potential" and he eventually made a total of 11 appearances for the first team (one as sub) during the season. John scored three times and his first goal for the club came in a 1-1 draw with Bexley at Hartsdown Park on 18.1.71.

During the summer of 1971 John had contact lenses fitted and although he continued to be a regular in the reserves he only made 12 first team appearances during the 1971/72 season. He scored twice, with both goals coming in a 4-0 win over Poole at Hartsdown Park on 9.10.71. The first of them was described by the Thanet Times as "a thunderous drive". On 20.11.71 John featured in Margate s infamous 11-0 defeat at Bournemouth & Boscombe in the FA Cup 1st Round. At the end of the season he was released.

He later had a spell with Epping Town that included the 1977/78 campaign.

In later years John returned to Thanet and played for local Sunday League side Westgate USC during the 1978/79 season. He also played locally for Dalby during 1981/82 and in 1987 he was still playing local football for Orb Strollers. Sometime after that he moved to the USA but by 2008 he was living in Thanet once more.

In 2023, John was living in Bexley, Kent aged 70 and by then he d had two hip replacements and a knee replacement.

name: Kery Kedze
other clubs: West Ham United (0), Croydon Athletic, Barnet (0), Erith & Belvedere, Hampton & Richmond Borough, Feltham, Walton & Hersham, Charlton Athletic (0), Thamesmead Town, Horsham, Waltham Forest, Bromley and Eastbourne Town
bio:
5 11" tall attacker born in Cameroon who was on West Ham s books from the age of 11, joining the club in 2003. Kery spent four years as part of the Hammers Development Centre before being released in May 2007 aged 15.

He then spent 2007/08 in Croydon Athletic s Academy before switching to Barnet s Academy for the 2008/09 campaign. Kery was released by Barnet in January 2010.

He then signed for Kent League club Erith & Belvedere and Kery spent the remainder of the 2009/10 season there.

In the summer of 2010 he joined Hampton & Richmond and in October 2010 they loaned Kery to Feltham.

He made four appearances for the Combined Counties League Division 1 outfit and scored once in a 5-1 home defeat against Bedfont Sports on 23.10.10 before going back to Hampton & Richmond.

Kery was then loaned out again almost immediately and joined Walton & Hersham. He didn t play in the Isthmian League Division 1 South for the Swans but did feature in the FA Trophy.

He left Hampton & Richmond towards the end of 2010 having only ever played twice as a substitute for their reserves and Kery then had a short spell in Charlton s Academy. He also took part in Samsung s nationwide Win a Pro Contract competition in an effort to gain a contract with Swindon and Kery reached the last three before bowing out.

In February 2011 he joined Thamesmead of the Isthmian League Division 1 North having been recommended to the club by Charlton and Kery made four substitute appearances without scoring in the league. He also had a trial at Notts County before the end of the 2010/11 campaign.

Kery started 2011/12 with Croydon Athletic and on 29.8.11 he scored twice as they lost 3-2 in an Isthmian League Division 1 South game at Faversham. He left the club a few weeks later.

In November 2011 Kery again took part in Samsung s Win a Pro Contract competition to win a contract with Swindon and he reached the final.

At the start of December 2011 he signed for Isthmian League Premier Division outfit Horsham and Kery went on to score twice from 20 league outings (four as sub) during the remainder of the 2011/12 season. One of his goals came in a 2-1 defeat at Margate on 3.3.12 and on 2.5.12 Kery scored the winner in the 120th minute as Horsham beat Worthing 3-2 in the Brighton Charity Cup Final. He stayed with Horsham until October 2012 when he asked to be released. Kery had scored once in an FA Cup tie during the early weeks of 2012/13 but had only featured three times in the league for Horsham, twice as a substitute.

Kery then joined Margate on trial and made his debut in a 4-0 defeat against Metropolitan Police in an Isthmian League Cup tie played at Hartsdown Park on 16.10.12. He didn t feature in the first team again, not even as an unused substitute, and in November 2012 Kery left the club.

He then linked up with Waltham Forest of the Isthmian League Division 1 North where he made five league appearances (one as sub) and scored once - in a 2-1 defeat at Thamesmead on 24.11.12.

Towards the end of the 2012/13 season Kery joined Conference South club Bromley and he played for their reserves during the remainder of the campaign. He was still turning out for them at the start of 2013/14.

In September 2013 Kery rejoined Horsham of the Isthmian League Division 1 South but after a few weeks there he signed for Eastbourne Town.

Kery made his debut for Eastbourne as they lost 2-1 at home to Chipstead in Division 1 South on 26.10.13 and he found himself in the same side as veteran former Margate striker Rocky Baptiste.

Kery was the nephew of Wolverhampton Wanderers defender George Elokobi.

name: W Keen
other clubs: Ashford Railway Works
bio:
In from Tunbridge Wells summer 1925. Our player was definitely captain of Ashford Railway Works - could be related to other ARW KeenE's      
Ashford RW had two KeenE (extra E) players in early part of 20th century so could be related   
Percy Keene played LW for Crystal Palace and he was with Tunbridge Wells Rangers 22/23 at same time as a W KeenE. W Keene of TWR was a right winger
Probably William G Keen, born Margate 1896*   
An E J Keene captained Ashford United 1892/93   he was Percy Keene s father
 Signed by Margate on month's trial for 25/26 but released after month up

name: Frank Keetley
other clubs: Victoria Ironworks, Derby County (76,8), Doncaster Rovers (110,28), Bradford City (28,8), Lincoln City (45,27), Hull City (0), Worcester City
bio:
5' 9" born Derby
Victoria Ironworks to Derby Feb 1921
Derby 21/22 to 25/26  - debut on 1 October 1921 in a 3-0 defeat away at Nottingham Forest. In total he turned out 82 times for Derby, scoring 8 goals.
Doncaster (joined June 1926) 26/27 to 29/30  - when signed by Doncaster he was replacement for Jack Lambert who d just joined Arsenal. Frank s brothers Tom and Harold were on Doncasters books when he signed for them and he was fourth brother in total to join the club.
Bradford (joined November 1929) 29/30 to 30/31  
Lincoln (joined May 1931) 31/32 and 32/33 
31/32 - scored six goals in 21 mins for Lincoln in 9-1 win over Halifax 16.1.32.  First Lincoln player to score double hat-trick
Had five brothers who all played league football - four of them for Doncaster 
One of eleven brothers and one sister, he was born in Derby and came from a footballing family with several other brothers who played professionally including Arthur, Harry, Tom, Joe and Charlie.
