name: Ebenezer Masade
other clubs: Fulham (0), Erith & Belvedere, Yeovil Town, Gravesend & Northfleet, Slade Green, Thamesmead Town, Thurrock, Dartford, Harrow Borough, Horsham, Sutton United, Tonbridge Angels, Fleet Town, Aveley, Leyton, Romford, Cray Wanderers, Seven Acre & Sidcup and Whitstable Town
bio:
Pacy 5' 5" tall winger born in London to Nigerian parents who was on Fulham's books as a schoolboy before being let go by the Cottagers. Ebenezer later recalled "They released me saying it was because of my height and nothing to do with my football ability."

After leaving Fulham he spent some time in Erith & Belvedere's youth team at the start of the 2005/06 season and Ebenezer also wrote to over 200 clubs across Europe to try and get a deal but nothing came of his efforts initially.

In November 2005 he was signed by League One club Yeovil on a scholar's contract and Ebenezer made his debut for their Under-18's in a 3-2 home defeat against Swindon on 26.11.05. He featured in a few more youth and reserve team games before moving on to Conference club Gravesend & Northfleet.

Ebenezer spent around six months playing for the Fleet's youth and reserve sides before linking up with Kent League club Slade Green towards the end of 2006.

At the start of 2007 he travelled to the USA and had an unsuccessful trial with Major League Soccer (MLS) outfit LA Galaxy before taking part in a series of trials for Chivas USA, another MLS club from the Los Angeles region. Ebenezer started out as one of 2000 hopefuls and eventually progressed to the final 24 before being let go. The trials formed part of a reality television show broadcast in the Los Angeles area.

Having returned to England Ebenezer joined Kent League club Thamesmead in the summer of 2007 and in November 2007 he returned to Slade Green.

He made 20 appearances (six as sub) without scoring for Slade Green during the remainder of the 2007/08 campaign.

Ebenezer started the 2008/09 season with Conference South outfit Thurrock and on 23.8.08 he scored on his debut as they lost 2-1 at home to Welling but he only played once more.

Early in September 2008 he went back to Slade Green again but Ebenezer's third spell there was very brief and before the end of the month he joined Margate.

He played in some reserve team matches for Margate over the next few weeks before leaving the club in October 2008 to link up with Dartford.

In November 2008 Ebenezer rejoined Margate having played a few games in Dartford's Under-21's team and on 15.11.08 he made his debut as a substitute in a 3-2 defeat against Harrow in an Isthmian League Premier Division match at Hartsdown Park. Ebenezer then wore the number seven shirt in a 2-1 win at Hendon on 22.11.08 and also started as Margate lost 2-1 to Maidstone in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Sittingbourne on 25.11.08.

He came on as a sub in a 2-1 home defeat against Staines on 29.11.08 and Ebenezer then missed four games altogether before having a final outing from the bench in a 2-0 defeat against Dover at Hartsdown Park on 3.1.09. He was released shortly afterwards having made a total of five appearances (three as sub) without scoring.

Ebenezer joined Harrow after leaving Margate and made his debut for them in a Middlesex Senior Cup tie against visitors Hendon on 21.1.09. Hendon won on penalties after a 1-1 draw. He also played once as a substitute in the Isthmian League Premier Division before moving on to Horsham, also of the Premier Division, in February 2009.

Ebenezer linked up with former Margate striker Reggie Savage at Horsham and made four first team appearances (two as sub) without scoring during the remainder of the 2008/09 season.

He started the 2009/10 campaign in Sutton's reserves and Ebenezer scored twice from seven outings for them before being signed by Tonbridge in September 2009.

He made his debut for the Angels as a late substitute in a 2-0 home win over Bognor Regis in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 23.9.09 but didn't feature in the league again before joining Fleet at the start of December 2009.

Ebenezer went on to make a total of five appearances (two as sub) for the Division 1 South club without scoring but left the club at the end of 2009.

He finished the 2009/10 campaign at Premier Division Aveley but didn't play for the first team there.

In the summer of 2010 Ebenezer featured in friendlies for Cray but he ended up linking up with Leyton of Division 1 North for the start of 2010/11 proper.

In September 2010 he moved on to Romford, also of Division 1 North, and Ebenezer played twice as a substitute for them before being signed by Cray in October 2010.

He made seven sporadic substitute appearances for Cray in the Isthmian League Premier Division during the remainder of the 2010/11 season and in July 2011 Ebenezer won four medals at a community athletics event at the Mile End Stadium in London which included gold for the 100 metres.

He stayed with Cray for the start of 2011/12 but a few weeks into the new campaign Ebenezer left the club and dropped out of senior football to concentrate on his work as a personal trainer.

He spent some time with Kent Invicta League club Seven Acre & Sidcup early in the 2012/13 season and then in January 2013 Ebenezer signed for Whitstable of the Isthmian League Division 1 South. He only made one substitute appearance there.

In July 2013 he featured as a substitute in Margate s first two pre-season friendlies but Ebenezer wasn t signed by the club again.

name: Lee Maskell
other clubs: Charlton Athletic (0), Gravesend & Northfleet, Ebbsfleet United, Sutton United, Wivenhoe Town, Ramsgate, Chatham Town, VCD Athletic and Lordswood
bio:
Bexley-born midfielder who was on Charlton's books for four years as a schoolboy before joining Gravesend & Northfleet's PASE scheme aged 16 in 2005. Lee played in the Fleet's youth sides during 2005/06 and 2006/07 and in May 2007 he was part of the Kent Youth League Under-18 Representative side that took part in a game against Charlton's Under-18's.

Gravesend & Northfleet became Ebbsfleet ahead of the 2007/08 season and on 3.11.07 Lee made his first team debut as a late substitute in a 2-0 home defeat against Forest Green in the Conference.

In December 2007 he was loaned to Isthmian League Premier Division club Sutton and Lee made six appearances there (one as sub) without scoring before returning to Stonebridge Road early in February 2008.

Before the end of February 2008 Lee was loaned to Isthmian League Division 1 North outfit Wivenhoe at the same time as future Margate player Dan Stubbs and he played three times during his spell there.

At the end of the 2007/08 campaign Lee was released by the Fleet having made two sub appearances for the first team.

In June 2008 he signed for Ramsgate of the Isthmian League Premier Division and the Rams assistant manager Danny Ward told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "I think Maskell could be the next legend of Ramsgate Football Club, he looks like he could be one of those players. Other clubs offered him more money but we won him over." Things didn't work out for Lee and he was released by the Rams at the end of August 2008 without making a single competitive appearance for the first team.

After leaving Southwood he immediately joined Margate and Lee made his debut as a half-time substitute for Paul Smith in a 1-1 draw at Harlow in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 2.9.08. He then started in midfield as Margate lost 2-0 to AFC Hornchurch at Hartsdown Park on 6.9.08 before making another sub appearance in a 2-1 defeat at Tooting & Mitcham on 9.9.08. Lee was an unused substitute for two more games in September before being released.

He signed for Chatham before the end of September 2008 and Lee went on to score once from nine Isthmian League Division 1 North outings (one as sub) for the Medway club before moving on to VCD in January 2009.

Lee helped VCD to win the Kent League title and then scored three times in 26 appearances (eight as sub) for the club in the Isthmian League Division 1 North during the 2009/10 season.

In June 2010 he rejoined Chatham as part of a mass exodus of VCD players who followed manager Paul Foley to the club and Lee also had a groin operation before the start of the 2010/11 campaign. He made 11 Isthmian League Division 1 South appearances (seven as sub) without scoring for Chatham before being released at the end of November 2010.

Lee then linked up with Kent League outfit Lordswood and he was still playing for the club at the start of the 2012/13 season.

name: Ron Matthews
other clubs: Herne Bay, Chelsea (0), Snowdown Colliery Welfare and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
6' 4" tall, skilful attacker born in Barnet who moved to the Thanet area as a youngster and attended Hereson School in Ramsgate before leaving in 1956.

Ron started his senior football career with Kent League outfit Herne Bay and he was on their books during the 1958/59 campaign. He also played twice as a trialist for Chelsea's youth team that season.

Ron started 1959/60 with Snowdown in the Kent League before returning to Thanet to play for Ramsgate's reserves.

He then had a spell in local amateur football and Ron was turning out for Margate Athletic when he was signed by Margate in January 1962 aged 20.

He made 13 appearances for Margate's reserves during the remainder of the 1961/62 season, scoring once, and Ron also made a one-off appearance for the first team when he wore the number eight shirt in a 2-0 win over Gravesend & Northfleet in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 14.2.62 before departing.

Ron later had another spell with Ramsgate and he was a regular in their reserves during the 1963/64 campaign.

Ron continued to play locally for almost 20 years and his clubs included Northwood and Monkton. He was in the Monkton side that lost 4-2 to Eastcliffe in the Thanet Premier Sunday League Division One Cup Final at Ramsgate s Southwood ground on 4.5.80 and Ron was 38 by then.

In 2025 he was still living in Ramsgate.

name: Josh Mattless
other clubs: Ramsgate and Deal Town
bio:
Keeper born in Lambeth, London who was in Margate s Under-14 s side during the 2008/09 season. In the summer of 2009 Josh had a two day intensive training course with West Ham s goalkeeping coach and in August 2009 Margate Under-15 s manager Kevin Powell told the Thanet Times The coach said he had very good hands but highlighted some areas for Josh to work on."

As well as playing for Margate s Under-15 s during 2009/10 Josh featured in the Thanet District Schools side but in the summer of 2010 he moved to Ramsgate.

He was part of the Rams Under-16 s team that won the Kent League Under-16 s South title for 2010/11 and Josh was chosen as the side s Players Player of the Year .

He also started the 2011/12 campaign with Ramsgate and after featuring in their Under-18 s and reserve teams Josh returned to Margate before the end of the season and played regularly in the reserves.

He featured in several of Margate s first team friendlies ahead of the 2012/13 campaign and Josh was an unused substitute six times during the opening weeks of the season proper. On 9.10.12 he made his senior debut as a replacement for the injured Craig Holloway as Margate took on Concord Rangers in an Isthmian League Premier Division game at Hartsdown Park and Josh was only 17 at the time. The visitors won 2-0. His next appearance was in a 4-0 home defeat against Metropolitan Police in the Isthmian League Cup on 16.10.12 and Josh then returned to the reserves for a lengthy spell.

On 6.4.13 Josh was back in first team action as he took over in goal after Craig Holloway was sent off 64 minutes into a match at Carshalton and his first task was to face a penalty which was scored. The home side eventually won 4-0. Josh then played in a 2-2 draw at Bury on 20.4.13 when Holloway was suspended and kept his place as Margate lost 4-2 to visitors Ebbsfleet in the Kent Senior Cup on 23.4.13. That was his last senior outing and Josh finished the campaign having made five appearances (one as sub). He also won Margate s Young Player of the Year award for the season.

In July 2013 he featured in one of Margate s friendlies, playing the second half of a 5-2 win at Hythe on 13.7.13, but on 20.7.13 Josh turned out for Kent League outfit Deal as they drew 2-2 with visitors Ramsgate in a friendly and joined the club for the 2013/14 campaign.

name: David Maughan
other clubs: Ramsgate
bio:
Locally-born product of Dane Court School who was prominent in schools football and rugby before joining Margate during the 1974/75 season. David made his debut for Margate Reserves in a 2-1 home win over Whitstable on 2.11.74, less than a month after his 15th birthday, and featured regularly in the second string after that.

He stayed with Margate for the 1975/76 campaign and again played for the reserves, usually as a goalkeeper but occasionally as an outfield player. David also featured for Margate Colts in the Thanet Premier Sunday League and played for Kent Schools Under-19 side during the season. On 8.4.76 he made a one-off appearance for Margate s first team, playing in goal in a Kent Messenger Trophy tie at Ramsgate on 8.4.76. Although Margate lost 1-0, he gave a "thoroughly competent display" according to the Thanet Times and David was probably the youngest keeper ever fielded in a first team game as he was still only 15 at the time. Margate's reserve team was disbanded for financial reasons at the end of the season.

David carried on playing for Margate's youth side during the 1976/77 campaign and won the Banks Cup awarded to the club's best young player.

He then played for the reserves once more when they were reinstated for the 1977/78 season. In January 1978 David fractured his knee-cap during an England Schoolboys trial in London but he recovered to play for Margate's youth and reserve sides once more during the 1978/79 campaign.

He later played many seasons of local amateur football and won the Thanet and District League's 'Player of the Year' award for 1982/83. He also had a spell with Ramsgate during the 1984/85 campaign. David was the Rams' regular keeper during the season.

He later became a referee in local football and was working as a bank manager in 2003.

name: Wes Maughan
other clubs: Cowes, Southampton (8,1), Reading (18,3), Chelmsford City, Cambridge United, Brentwood Town, Bexley United, Fleet Town, Basingstoke Town, Walton & Hersham and Staines Town
bio:
5 9 tall striker born in Sholing, Southampton who moved to Cowes on the Isle of Wight as a youngster when his parents took on a corner shop in the town. Wes was brought up in a very Christian Salvation Army family and played trombone in the Salvation Army brass band.

Having been a prolific scorer for Cowes Secondary Modern School, Wes started work at local firm J S White and played for their football team. He scored over 100 goals in a season and then started his senior career with Hampshire League club Cowes as a teenager. Wes was selected for the Isle of Wight FA Youth team whilst on their books in 1956 and scored four times as the Isle of Wight FA Youth side beat the Southampton FA Youth team 6-1 in a Hampshire Youth Inter-Association Cup semi-final. Fortunately for Wes, Ted Bates - the manager of Third Division club Southampton - watched the match and signed Wes as an amateur. He was offered a full-time contract, but turned it down as he was training to be an accountant and wanted to complete his studies.

Wes started out playing for Southampton s A side in the Hampshire League and also played in the Saints youth team during the 1956/57 season. He scored a hat-trick for them in a 6-0 win over Tottenham in the FA Youth Cup and on 8.4.57 Wes was in the side that travelled to Old Trafford to take on Manchester United s youth team in the 2nd Leg of the FA Youth Cup semi-final. He got two goals in a 3-2 win watched by a crowd of 17,000 at Old Trafford but Southampton lost 7-5 on aggregate. It was the first defeat United had suffered in 43 FA Youth Cup matches.

In May 1957 Wes signed a professional contract with the Saints and progressed into the reserve team during the early part of the 1957/58 season. On 21.2.59 he made his first team debut in a 4-1 defeat at Reading but Wes found senior opportunities hard to come by as Southampton had a settled forward line comprising Terry Paine, George O Brien, Derek Reeves, Tommy Mulgrew and John Sydenham. His best run in the first team consisted of three consecutive appearances in February 1960 when O Brien was suspended and on 15.4.61 Wes got the only senior goal of his Southampton career in a 2-1 defeat at Sheffield United. In total he made eight first team appearances for the Saints and also played 101 times for the reserves, scoring 47 goals for them.

In March 1962 Wes was transferred to Reading for a fee of £4,000 and in his first appearance at Elm Park he scored a hat-trick in a friendly win over a West Ham side featuring Bobby Moore. Wes made 18 senior appearances for the Royals and scored three times before a severe groin injury put him on the sidelines for six months. During that time, Reading tried to get Southampton to repay some of the transfer fee they d paid for Wes. The club claimed they hadn t been told about Wes being short-sighted - he wore glasses for driving - when signing him. Reading were unsuccessful in their efforts.

In the summer of 1963 Wes dropped into Southern League football when he signed for Chelmsford as a full-time professional. He scored 30 times in 42 appearances for City during 1963/64 and two of his goals came in a 4-1 home win over Margate on 14.9.63. During the 1964/65 campaign he scored 15 times in 41 games, including a goal in a 5-2 home win over Margate on 21.11.64.

In the summer of 1965 Wes joined Cambridge United, again as a full-time player, and spent two seasons there. He scored 37 goals from a total of 98 appearances, four of which were as a substitute. On 20.8.66 he became the first sub ever used by United.

Wes joined Brentwood for the start of the 1967/68 campaign and in January 1968 they loaned him to Margate.

Wes made his debut on 17.1.68 as Margate went down 4-2 at Erith & Belvedere in a Kent Floodlight Cup game and was described as "a useful ball player" by the local press but only played once more before being going back to Brentwood.

In the summer of 1968 Wes returned to Chelmsford but after making 13 appearances for them in the early part of the 1968/69 campaign he moved on to Bexley.

Wes spent four seasons at Bexley and later had short spells with Fleet, Basingstoke (during 1972/73), Walton & Hersham and Staines.

In 1974 he returned to Bexley as reserve team coach.

In later years, Wes was employed in the accounts department of American company Du Pont and travelled the world whilst with them. He spent four years living and working in Italy and then returned to England, becoming a Southampton season ticket holder. In 1997 he got married at the age of 58 having previously been a lifelong bachelor and in 2000 Wes was living near Sunbury-on-Thames. At that time he was still doing some IT consultancy work despite being officially retired.

Between 2008 and 2012 Wes coached a Salvation Army football team, SA Stainash, who played in the East Berkshire Football League.

Wes was a lifelong member of the Salvation Army and in an interview for a Cambridge United website in the 2010 s he said It would be easier today for a Salvationist to play professional football than when I was playing. When I signed pro in 1957, it was quite frowned upon to be associated with professional football with its gambling (in the form of pools) and drinking at the grounds. Times have changed and along with them the Salvation Army. I could write a book on it - that s an idea ! I am chairman of the trustees board for the Kenya Trust and am still heavily involved with it. The Trust s aims are to assist in improving conditions and facilities at the Salvation Army s schools, hostels and community centres in Kenya and to promote and support the development of music within the Salvation Army in the country. I am on the social support side - we raise money for projects that introduce water facilities into drought areas and also specialise in providing better conditions for deprived children (orphans and those with some disability) in homes and schools.

In 2019, Wes autobiography Soccer, Saints and Salvation was published and in June 2020 he was interviewed by the Isle of Wight County Press. Looking back at his early days with Southampton, Wes told the paper I was always concerned about the timing of going fully professional, if I had gone earlier, would I have done more at a higher level ? To me it was important that I achieved my accountancy qualifications. Wes also recalled his spell at Reading and said Jackie Milburn had been my schoolboy hero and I had his pictures all around my bedroom walls. He was the coach at Reading and I learned a lot from him, especially about movement.

name: Bernie Maxted
other clubs: West Ham United (0), Ramsgate Athletic, Southampton (0), Ashford Town, Hastings United, Maidstone United and Kent Police
bio:
Ramsgate-born player educated at Chatham House School who played for Manston Youth Club during the 1957/58 season and helped them to win the Thanet League Division 2 Cup, scoring the only goal as they beat Thanet Electric Reserves 1-0 in the final.

Bernie turned out for Ramsgate Sporting Youth Club, whose manager was former Margate centre-forward Jimmy Briscoe, during the early part of the 1958/59 campaign and on 11.10.58 he made his debut for the Kent Youth team aged 15, scoring twice in a 3-0 victory over St. Edmund s at Canterbury.

Shortly after his debut for Kent, Bernie was signed as an amateur by First Division club West Ham and played for the Hammers' South Eastern Counties League team for the remainder of the 1958/59 season. In May 1959 he toured Switzerland with West Ham s youth side.

In the summer of 1959, Bernie was on the ground staff at Essex County Cricket Club and played for their Essex Club and Ground X1.

Bernie stayed with West Ham for the 1959/60 campaign and featured in both their South Eastern Counties League and Metropolitan League sides. He also played some games for Ramsgate s reserve side. At the end of the 1959/60 season, Bernie was released by West Ham.

In June 1960, he was in the Kent Association of Boys Clubs squad that played in a tournament at Langen, near Frankfurt in West Germany.

Bernie joined Ramsgate for the 1960/61 campaign and had a trial with Southampton just before the start of the season. The Saints were impressed and Bernie turned out for their youth team, between matches for Ramsgate (mostly reserve team games), during 1960/61. On 7.1.61 he scored four times as Ramsgate s reserves beat visitors Gravesend & Northfleet Reserves 5-1 in a Seanglian League game at Southwood.

On 17.1.61 Bernie was given a first team opportunity as Ramsgate took on Snowdown Colliery Welfare in a Thames And Medway Combination tie at Southwood. It was a debut to remember as he scored all three goals in a 3-0 win and the East Kent Times said that Bernie was full of menace . On 4.2.61 he bagged another hat-trick for the reserves in a 5-1 win over Betteshanger. Those goals took his tally to ten from only six reserve team outings.

On 20.4.61 Bernie crossed Thanet and signed for Margate. He made his debut wearing the number nine shirt in a 1-0 defeat at Nuneaton on 22.4.61 and played twice more as an inside forward before the end of the campaign. Bernie left the club in the summer of 1961.

He joined Ashford for 1961/62 but only played one Southern League game for the Nuts & Bolts during the season.

Bernie then had a spell at Hastings early in the 1962/63 season before joining Maidstone United. He also began training as a policeman at that time.

Bernie later returned to Ramsgate and played a few games for their reserves during the 1963/64 season.

By the start of the 1965/66 campaign Bernie was a serving police officer and was playing football for Kent Police of the Kent Amateur League. He was still turning out for them during 1972/73 and by then the club were in the Kent League.

Bernie had left the police by 1976 and in that year he was working as head of security for GKN Kent Alloys in Strood.

During the late 1990's and early 2000's Bernie worked at Sittingbourne's Central Park stadium as the greyhound track manager.

In 2009 Bernie was living in the Maidstone area.

name: Dick Maxted
other clubs: Folkestone, Folkestone & Shepway, Ramsgate, Hythe Town, Folkestone and Biggleswade Town
bio:
Defender who began his senior career with Folkestone, first playing for their reserves during the 1973/74 season. Dick stayed with the club as it s name changed to Folkestone & Shepway for 1974/75.

In January 1976 Dick joined Ramsgate and spent the remainder of the 1975/76 campaign there. He scored seven goals, five of which came from the penalty spot.

Dick returned to Folkestone & Shepway for the 1976/77 season and mostly played in the reserves there.

In the summer of 1977 he joined Margate and made his debut in a 1-0 win over Ramsgate in a Kent Senior Shield tie at Hartsdown Park on 6.8.77. On 20.8.77 he scored an own goal from 20 yards in a 3-1 home defeat against Maidstone. His attempted back-pass "went tragically wrong" according to the Thanet Times and floated over goalkeeper Steve Bowtell. Dick went on to make 26 appearances (one as sub) during the 1977/78 season, usually playing at left-back but sometimes switching flanks. He scored once - in a 2-1 defeat at Romford on 2.1.78.

Dick was in and out of the side throughout the campaign and on 7.1.78 he was punched by a spectator during a 2-1 win at Aylesbury having ended up in the crowd after making a tackle. The incident led to the game being held up for ten minutes while order was restored. Margate went on to win the Southern League 1st Division (South) title.

Dick featured in some pre-season games in the summer of 1978 but he then left Margate and moved to London to work as an engineer.

Having returned to Kent, Dick joined Hythe for the 1979/80 campaign and stayed with them for the rest of the season.

In the summer of 1980 he rejoined Ramsgate who were managed by former Margate player Graham Sawyer at the time.

Dick started a second spell with Hythe early in 1981 and was still with them during the 1981/82 campaign.

He later had a short stint back at Folkestone during the 1984/85 season.

Later in the 1980 s, Dick featured for South Midlands League club Biggleswade where he played alongside his former Margate team-mate Vic Pain.

name: Ryan Maxwell
other clubs: Tottenham Hotspur (0), Crystal Palace (0), Reading (0), Grays Athletic, Purfleet, Hamilton Academicals (Scotland) (2+1,0), Raith Rovers (Scotland) (2+3,0), Dagenham & Redbridge, Redbridge, Gravesend & Northfleet, Basingstoke Town, Bishop's Stortford, Llanelli (Wales), Tonbridge Angels, Braintree Town, Billericay Town, Welling United, Wivenhoe Town, Boreham Wood, Stansted, St Albans City, Harlow Town, Waltham Abbey, Whyteleafe, Heybridge Swifts and AFC Sudbury
bio:
Much-travelled 5' 9" tall left-sided player born in Larne, Northern Ireland who represented his country from Under-16 up to Under-21 level. Ryan started his career at Tottenham and played for Spurs' Under-17's side during the 1998/99 season alongside future Margate player Andrew Burke.

Ryan later had a spell on Crystal Palace's books and then joined Reading in February 2001. He played for the Royals' Under-18's and Under-19's before being released at the end of the 2001/02 campaign.

Ryan linked up with Isthmian League Premier Division club Grays in the summer of 2002 and made ten league appearances (one as sub) without scoring there before being released in March 2003.

He immediately moved on to Purfleet and made nine Isthmian League Premier Division appearances (four as sub) without scoring for them before the end of the 2002/03 season.

In the summer of 2003 Ryan was signed by Scottish Division 2 club Hamilton and made his debut for them as a substitute in a 3-2 home defeat against St.Johnstone in the Scottish League Cup on 2.8.03. He played twice more before falling out of favour.

In January 2004 Ryan signed for Division 1 club Raith but although he was sometimes on the bench for the senior side he didn't feature in the first team during what remained of the 2003/04 campaign. Ryan finally made his debut for Rovers as a substitute in a 1-0 defeat at St.Johnstone on 28.8.04 and he went on to make a total of five appearances (three as sub) before being released in January 2005.

Ryan then returned to England and joined Conference club Dagenham & Redbridge. He played in their 3-1 defeat against Margate in a Conference Cup tie at Ashford on 25.1.05 but in April 2005 Ryan was released by the Daggers.

He finished the 2004/05 season at Redbridge and then joined Conference club Gravesend & Northfleet in the summer of 2005.

Ryan dislocated his shoulder 30 seconds into a friendly at Folkestone in July 2005 and in August 2005 the Fleet loaned him to Basingstoke. He made two Conference South appearances for the Hampshire club before quickly returning to Stonebridge Road. Ryan played a few games for Gravesend's reserves before joining Margate in October 2005.

He made his debut at left-back in a 1-0 win over Wealdstone in the Isthmian League Premier Division at Hartsdown Park on 22.10.05 but Ryan then missed the next two matches. He returned to the side when he wore the number three shirt in a 1-0 home defeat against Chelmsford on 5.11.05 and Ryan then played in midfield as Margate lost 3-2 to Bromley in an Isthmian League Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 8.11.05. He made one more appearance - as a substitute in a 1-0 home defeat against Dartford in the FA Trophy on 12.11.05 - before being released shortly afterwards.

Later in November 2005 Ryan signed for Conference South club Bishop's Stortford and he spent the remainder of the 2005/06 campaign there.

In July 2006 Ryan joined Welsh Premier League side Llanelli and on 13.7.06 he came on as a 90th minute substitute as they won 2-1 at Swedish club Gefle in a UEFA Cup tie. He then started the home leg against Gefle on 27.7.06 and Llanelli progressed after a 0-0 draw. Ryan didn't play again for the Welsh club and in October 2006 he returned to the Isthmian League Premier Division when he signed for Tonbridge.

Ryan went on to make 18 league appearances (four as sub) for the Angels and scored once - in a 3-2 win at AFC Wimbledon on 18.11.06 - before being released in February 2007.

He finished the 2006/07 season with Braintree where he played three times in the Conference South.

In the summer of 2007 Ryan played in some friendlies for Heybridge but he ended up starting the 2007/08 campaign back at Braintree. Within weeks of the new season starting he moved on to Billericay but Ryan only played twice for them in the Isthmian League Premier Division before being released in November 2007.

His next move took him to Welling and Ryan featured regularly for them in the Conference South up to March 2008 when he joined Isthmian League Division 1 North outfit Wivenhoe.

After making only two appearances for Wivenhoe Ryan moved on to Boreham Wood before the end of March 2008.

The Wood were his fifth club of the season and Ryan made six Isthmian League Premier Division appearances for them before the 2007/08 campaign ended.

After a spell out of football Ryan linked up with Essex Senior League club Stansted in February 2009 and he spent the remainder of 2008/09 with them.

In September 2009 he moved on to Conference South side St Albans and Ryan made his debut for them as a substitute in a 1-0 defeat against Heybridge in the FA Cup on 26.9.09. He made one further sub appearance for the first team before leaving the club in November 2009 following a spell in the reserves.

Ryan then rejoined Stansted and in January 2010 he linked up with Harlow of the Isthmian League Division 1 North. He made ten league appearances for them without scoring before the end of the 2009/10 campaign.

In the summer of 2010 Ryan played in some of Harlow's friendlies before signing for Waltham Abbey in time for the start of the 2010/11 season proper. He went on to score once from 22 appearances in the Isthmian League Division 1 North and Ryan stayed with Abbey for the start of the 2011/12 campaign too.

In October 2011 he rejoined Harlow and Ryan made 17 league appearances (four as sub) for the Hawks without scoring before being released in July 2012. Harlow issued a statement saying "We would like to thank Ryan for all his efforts while at the club, and wish him all the best for the future."

After leaving Harlow Ryan played in some friendlies for Grays but he then signed for Kent League newcomers Whyteleafe in time for the first match of the 2012/13 season.

In the summer of 2013 Ryan joined Grays of the Isthmian League Premier Division but only made three appearances there before moving on to Heybridge of Division 1 North early in March 2014.

In the summer of 2014 Ryan became player-coach at Division 1 North club AFC Sudbury and said "I think maybe in the past Sudbury had players with the technical ability to get there or thereabouts, but lacked a bit of a determined streak. I will not let that happen again, and certainly on the mental side, we will be digging in. I have taken a few sessions already and am pushing them more than they have been pushed before and I am only getting my teeth into them now. It is demanding, but I am hoping what does not kill them makes them stronger."

name: Cyril May
other clubs: Queens Park Rangers (0), Wealdstone and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
6 1 tall defender born in Hammersmith, London who grew up on the White City Estate and was widely known as 'Ticker'. Cyril started his career as an amateur with Queens Park Rangers, the club he d supported as a child. He first appeared in QPR s A team during the 1952/53 season and during the 1953/54 campaign he made seven reserve team appearances.

Cyril left the R s to join Athenian League club Wealdstone on loan for the 1954/55 season but on 5.1.55 he was recalled to Loftus Road and given a professional contract by QPR. Cyril went on to make 21 reserve team appearances during the remainder of 1954/55 but never featured in QPR's first team. At the end of the season he was given a free transfer.

Cyril joined Ramsgate in the summer of 1955 and went on to spend four successful seasons with the Rams, helping them to win the Kent League twice and playing in their FA Cup tie at Watford during 1955/56.

Cyril left Southwood to join Margate for the 1959/60 campaign and made his debut at centre-back in the first match of the season - a 3-2 win over Cambridge United at Hartsdown Park on 22.8.59. It was Margate's first post-war game in the Southern League. Cyril then found himself in the reserves for almost all of what remained of 1959, playing only once more for the first team before Christmas. In January 1960 he got back into the senior side when an injury to left-back Terry Joyce led to regular centre-back Ray Chatham moving to the number three shirt temporarily. Cyril made three appearances, the last of them in a 3-0 defeat at Merthyr Tydfil on 16.1.60, before returning to the reserves for the rest of the season.

He was released in May 1960.

Cyril was often referred to as Charlie in local press reports.

name: Jon Mayall
other clubs: Herne Bay, Ramsgate, Canterbury City, Folkestone Invicta, Tonbridge Angels, Maidstone United, Tunbridge Wells, Cray Wanderers, Thamesmead Town, Hythe Town and Slade Green
bio:
Athletic, left-sided player who was born in Birkenhead but moved to Thanet as a youngster. Jon began his career in Ramsgate's youth setup as part of the Westgate Sports club that played at Southwood. He then played for Thanet United's Under-14 side during the 1982/83 season.

Jon progressed to United's reserves and made his debut for them in a 2-2 draw with Folkestone on 23.11.85. He became a regular in the side for the remainder of the 1985/86 campaign. Jon stayed at Thanet for the 1986/87 season and on 21.2.87 he made his first team debut in a 3-2 defeat at Trowbridge. He played on the left wing and after one further appearance in midfield Jon was switched to left-back for the home game against Erith & Belvedere on 14.3.87. The Thanet Times reported that he "gave a thoroughly promising account of himself". The paper went on to describe Jon as "a strong lad with genuine bite in the tackle" and added "he also demonstrated his prowess with the long throw-in - a rare asset which gives him an extra string to his bow". Jon kept his place in the number three shirt for the remainder of the season and turned in what the Isle of Thanet Gazette said were "some exceptional displays", particularly impressing with his willingness to get forward.

In March 1987 the Gazette ran a story about him under the headline "Young Mayall looks a lad with promise" and said that Jon was "an outstanding prospect", describing him as "well-built and clearly extremely fit". New player-manager Norman Fusco told the paper "I have been very impressed with him in training and believed he merited his chance...he took it well and I feel he is a player of considerable potential." In April 1987 Jon and goalkeeper Joe Radford were given contracts, making them the club's only contracted players. Norman Fusco explained the move, saying "Joe and Jon are our most outstanding players and we expect league sides to show a great interest in them in the coming months." He went on to say "the club and I felt it was in Thanet United's best interests to have them under contract. This way the club will at least get some financial return if they move on to another team." This was a huge compliment to Jon as at the end of the season he had made just 11 appearances for United's first team.

In the summer of 1987 Jon had trials at Colchester and Brentford but nothing came of them and he stayed with Thanet for the 1987/88 campaign. He was a fixture in the side, making 54 appearances without scoring, and played at left-back throughout the season, apart from four games where he was used in a midfield role. Jon only missed two matches. It took him a while to find his best form but towards the end of 1987 Jon's performances began to match his impressive displays of the previous campaign. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said that he was "outstanding" in a 2-1 win at Sheppey on 26.12.87 and Jon consistently won praise from the local press during the second half of the season. The Thanet Times reported that he "took the eye with some decisive work plus a magnificent 40-yard diagonal pass" in a 1-0 home win over Ruislip on 20.2.88 and said that Jon was "often prominent...with his powerful over-lapping runs down the left flank" in a 1-1 draw at Chatham on 9.4.88.

The 1988/89 season wasn't such a good one for Jon and although he was mostly used at left-back he sometimes found himself playing out of position at right-back during the early months of the campaign. He made four appearances in the number two shirt and also played a couple of games on the left wing before losing his first team place altogether after playing in a 3-0 home defeat at the hands of Hastings on 6.12.88. Jon had made 21 appearances without scoring before being demoted to the reserves and he went on to play eight games for them, scoring twice, before leaving the club towards the end of the season.

Jon joined Herne Bay for the 1989/90 campaign and then returned to Thanet to play for Ramsgate at the start of 1991.

At the start of the 1991/92 season Jon concentrated on playing rugby for Thanet Wanderers and at that time he was serving in the Royal Marines.

In December 1991 he returned to Hartsdown Park when he signed for Margate. Jon made his first appearance as a substitute in a 1-0 defeat at Burnham on 21.12.91 and the Thanet Times said he "gave a good account of himself". The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he had "slotted into the left-back position as if he had never been away" and was "clearly a talented all-round sportsman". Jon became a fixture in the number three shirt from then on, featuring in Margate's next ten matches as a replacement for the injured Bill Roffey. His energetic display in a 0-0 home draw with Havant prompted the Thanet Times to say that he was "the fittest of the fit". The same paper said that Jon was "outstanding" in a 3-1 defeat against Braintree at Hartsdown on 4.1.92 but the Gazette reported that he "had a match he will wish to forget" as Margate lost 5-1 at Salisbury on 15.2.92. A few days later the paper said Jon was "lion-hearted, strong in the tackle, equally effective with either foot" and added "Margate need more men of his calibre" but he lost his place when Roffey returned. After coming on as a sub in 5-0 win over Erith & Belvedere at Hartsdown on 29.2.92 Jon left Margate having made 12 appearances (two as sub) without scoring during 1991/92.

He started the 1992/93 season with Canterbury and played regularly there before rejoining Ramsgate at the end of 1992.

Jon left Ramsgate in the summer of 1993 but went back to the club again in December 1993 and became a fixture in the Rams' side for the next 18 months. In April 1995 the Thanet Times described Jon as being a "man-mountain" and reported that he turned in an "inspirational display" as the Rams beat Dartford 3-0 to win the Kent League Cup. Jon had a hand in all three goals.

In the summer of 1995 he moved on to Folkestone and Jon spent two seasons there before returning to Ramsgate for the 1996/97 season. His fourth spell at Southwood lasted until the end of the 1998/99 campaign and Jon then linked up with Tonbridge.

He made a total of 86 appearances (15 as sub) without scoring for the Angels during 1999/00 and 2000/01 before signing for Maidstone in the summer of 2001.

After a season with the Stones Jon joined Tunbridge Wells where he played regularly during the 2002/03 campaign before leaving the club to join Cray early in 2003/04.

A few weeks into the 2004/05 campaign Jon left Cray and linked up with Thamesmead. On 5.3.05 he scored from the penalty spot in a 5-4 win over his old club Ramsgate and Jon was then sent off in Thamesmead's last Kent League game of the season at Beckenham.

Jon's next move took him to Hythe early in the 2005/06 campaign but he was released in March 2006.

In the summer of 2006 he signed for Slade Green and became the club's captain for the 2006/07 term before retiring at the end of the season.

Jon worked as a fireman during the latter part of his football career and in 2011 he was living and working in Iraq.

name: Jack Mayo
other clubs: Dover
bio:
Jack Owen Mayo
Born Wolverhampton Q2 1912
Played for the army against the French Army.
Played for the Lincolnshire Regiment in Folkestone & District League when they were based in Dover. 1930/31 was first season with them. Was actually in the 1st South Staffordshire Regiment and in May 1931 he was stationed at Whittington Barracks, Lichfield, Staffs. Home address in Willenhall. Pleaded guilty to breaking into a Willenhall bakers shop with another soldier and stealing fancy cakes worth 6d   both were AWOL at the time. Policeman at court suggested they committed the offence as a way to get out of the army. Asked for earlier theft of cigarette machine to be taken into consideration. Jack was discharged into hands of the army whilst his accomplice was sent to borstal for 3 years.
Also played hockey for his regiment
Still playing for Lincolnshire Regiment 1931/32 and 1932/33
Regiment relocated to Staffordshire and Jack played for them 1933/34 in that region
Joined River United of Dover & District League for 35/36
Dover United 36/37, 37/38, 38/39), 18.4.38 played in Northfleet United 2 Dover 1 KSC Final at Maidstone, 9168 attendance
Margate 39/40 as part-time professional after three seasons with Dover. 
Kent & Sussex Courier - Friday 01 December 1939 report on TW v Margate  blond-bombshell   kept goal for the visitors in a singularly spectacular and effective fashion   If Mayo ever needs to change his vocation the Royal and Ancient Guild of Acrobats would certainly welcome him into their fold 
Served in South Staffordshire Regiment during WWII and was Staff Serjeant
Injured by a shell splinter early in 1941 and hospitalised
Killed in Burma 17.4.44 aged 31. Commerated on Willenhall war memorial.
Son of Enoch and Elizabeth Mayo; husband of Dorothy May Mayo, of Willenhall, Staffordshire

name: Jason McAree
other clubs: Ramsgate
bio:
Locally-born player who progressed through Ramsgate's youth ranks and played for the club's Under-15's during the 2003/04 season before moving up to the Under-16's for 2004/05.

After a couple of years out of football Jason joined Margate for the 2007/08 campaign and started the season in the reserves. A few weeks later he damaged his thigh in an accident with a saw at work - he was a self-employed carpenter - and Jason was out of action for some time as a result of his injury.

By the start of 2008 he was playing again and on 26.3.08 Jason made his first team debut when he wore the number four shirt as Margate lost 4-1 to Ebbsfleet in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park. It was his only senior outing.

Jason stayed with the club for the 2008/09 campaign but he again struggled with injuries which restricted his reserve team appearances and he left Margate at the end of the season.

Jason then dropped into local amateur football and was playing for Generation Sports in the Thanet Sunday Football League during the 2011/12 campaign. He was still playing locally during 2013/14.

name: Warren McBean
other clubs: Barnet, Waltham Forest, Farnborough Town, Braintree Town, St Albans City, Sutton United, Eastleigh, Bromley, Chelmsford City, Havant & Waterlooville, Welling United, Cray Wanderers and Canvey Island
bio:
London-born striker who started his career in Conference club Barnet s youth academy at a time when he was also studying music at Southgate College. Warren made his first team debut for Barnet during 2003/04 and at the end of that season he played for Southgate College as they won the English Schools Football Association Colleges Trophy by beating Middlesbrough at Doncaster.

During the 2004/05 campaign Warren featured five times in Barnet s senior side (three times as sub) without scoring as the club won promotion to the Football League and he also spent a month on loan at Waltham Forest towards the end of the season, making three appearances (two as sub) without scoring there.

In July 2005 Warren signed for Farnborough and scored 19 goals from 48 outings during 2005/06.

He moved on to Braintree for the start of the 2006/07 campaign but in October 2006 Warren linked up with Conference club St Albans City.

He scored on his debut in a 4-2 home win over York on 14.10.06 but Warren only played once more before joining Conference South outfit Sutton before the end of October 2006.

He went on to score ten league goals during the remainder of 2006/07 and Warren then scored six times for Sutton in the Conference South during the 2007/08 season before being loaned to Eastleigh in February 2008.

He managed four goals for the Hampshire club in the Conference South before going back to Sutton in April 2008. Warren was then released.

In the summer of 2008 he signed for Bromley and Warren scored 21 Conference South goals during 2008/09. In August 2009 he got four goals as Bromley beat Grays 5-1 in a pre-season friendly and Warren went on to score 17 times in the league during the 2009/10 campaign before being loaned to Chelmsford in March 2010.

He got four goals from eight outings for Chelmsford and then went back to Bromley.

By the end of the 2010/11 season Warren had scored in excess of 50 goals from over 100 appearances for Bromley but in July 2011 he left the club and joined Isthmian League Premier Division outfit Lewes.

His stay in Sussex was very brief and in August 2011 Warren moved on to Havant & Waterlooville ahead of the start of the 2011/12 campaign proper.

He made five appearances (three as sub) without scoring for the Conference South club before returning to Bromley.

On 15.10.11 Warren was on the substitutes bench as Bromley visited Margate for an FA Cup tie and he was introduced at half-time with his side 2-0 down. He scored twice in the space of two second half minutes to level the game at 2-2 and Bromley then went on to snatch a 3-2 win.

In December 2011 Warren joined Margate and manager Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette Twice he s finished second-top scorer in Conference South and he s still only 25 so it s a decent signing for us. He s all about pace and finishing, similar to Kwesi (Appiah), and I d like to think the two of them will cause plenty of problems."

Warren made his first appearance as Margate entertained Metropolitan Police in an Isthmian League Premier Division game at Hartsdown Park on 17.12.11 but the Thanet Times said he had a debut to forget" as the visitors won 3-1 and the paper s report was headlined McBean and gone as new signing pulls up". Warren went off just before the hour mark and the Times said he d barely had a kick before pulling up injured". Warren didn t play again and he was released less than two weeks after signing for Margate.

At the start of January 2012 he joined Conference South outfit Welling but Warren only made two substitute appearances for the Wings that month before injury ruled him out for the rest of the season.

In the summer of 2012 he featured in some of Bromley s friendlies and on 17.7.12 Warren scored twice in a 5-1 win at Beckenham. Bromley s coach Neil Smith told the Kentish Football website "We want to get the best out of Warren and he's got to get the best out of himself as well so at the moment he's looking very good. He's looking very sharp. He's looked after himself in the close season and we'll just keep plugging away and see where we are on August 18th."

Unfortunately Warren ruptured his Achilles tendon before the 2012/13 campaign began and he ended up missing the entire season but in June 2013 he was resigned by Bromley having regained his fitness.

Early in October 2013 Warren joined Isthmian League Premier Division club Cray on a dual-registration basis and before the end of that month he signed for Canvey Island, also of the Premier Division, in a permanent deal.

Warren was released by Canvey in December 2013 having scored once from ten outings (three as sub).

name: Jimmy McBennett
other clubs: Belfast Celtic (Northern Ireland), Cardiff City (Wales) (4,2), Tranmere Rovers (13,1) and Chelmsford City
bio:
Forward born in Newcastle, Northern Ireland who started his career with Belfast Celtic before being signed by Cardiff in September 1947.

Jimmy made four first team appearances for the Bluebirds during 1947/48 and then moved to Tranmere in November 1948.

He made a total of 13 senior appearances for Rovers during 1948/49 and 1949/50.

In February 1951 Jimmy dropped into non-league football and joined Margate. He made his debut in 2-2 draw with Betteshanger at Hartsdown Park on 17.2.51. Jimmy went on to make a total of six appearances and scored once during the remainder of the 1950/51 season but never really established himself and left the club to join Chelmsford in the summer of 1951.

Although his first name was James he was known as 'Seamus' during his league career but called Jimmy at Margate. In addition his surname was sometimes listed as being 'MacBennett'.

He died in Lambeth, London on 23.2.95 aged 69.

name: Tom McCann
other clubs: Celtic
bio:
5' 8". 
Thomas McCann was an inside left who played for Auchinstarry Port Vale, a Juvenile club near Kilsyth.  He attracted the attention of St Johnstone but they decided he was not quite ready for Senior football.  He then signed for Junior club Saltcoats Victoria in November 1928.  They played in the Scottish Junior League that season.  Saltcoats were fined  1 for playing him without permission from his former club and then had to pay compensation for his transfer.  He had no sooner signed than he was invited to go on a month s trial to Burnley.  However, Celtic stepped in and provisionally signed him meaning that he would stay at Saltcoats Vics until Celtic called him up.  This interest from Senior clubs resulted in Auchinstarry holding out for more compensation from the Saltcoats clubs.  
He represented Glasgow in the Scottish Counties Cup against Perthshire on 1 January 1929.  Glasgow lost 6-8 but Tom McCann scored two goals.  
Played for Celtic in a 2nd XI Cup tie on 23 February 1929 Home v Airdrie 3-5 but did not score. 
Called up by Celtic at the start of the 1929-30 season along with Peter Scarff and Charlie Napier, both of Maryhill Hibernian, who, along with Tom, had all played in that Glasgow team on 1.1.29
Celtic s first team inside left position was won by Charlie Napier who went on to play for Scotland.  Tom McCann was released at the end of the season.
Took part in the Celtic pre-season Trial Matches (1st team v 2nd team) on 2 and 9 August  1929 with McCann scoring in the second trial.
In that season Celtic did not have their reserve team in the Scottish Alliance, unlike most other clubs, and played friendly matches although they did enter the Scottish Second XI Cup and played three ties.
Thomas McCann played in the following ties:
8 February 1930  Home v St Mirren 0-0
22 February 1930 Away  v St Mirren  2-1 - did not score
 
Margate 30/31 - came from Celtic
Sent off 4.10.30 in Folkestone Res 0 Margate 2 - last first team game for the club. Dismissal felt to be very harsh and even Folkestone players pleaded with ref not to send him off. KCFA dismissed case when it went before them in November 1930 - no ban.. 
Scored 3 for reserves 11.10.30 as they won 6-1 at Shorncliffe v Manchester Regiment in the Folkestone and District League.
Left us  November 1930 by mutual agreement - paid him  30 - then  joined Folkestone on a month's trial and stayed till end of 1930/31  "smart little Scot" . Known as 'Mac'

name: Vic McCartney
bio:
Left-sided Margate-born player who attended St. John s School in Margate and played for amateur club Margate Thursday before World War II.

During the conflict, Vic served in the Royal Navy and spent three years in the Mediterranean before returning home to Thanet in March 1944.

Vic joined Margate for the 1946/47 season and became a regular in the reserves. He also made a single first team appearance, wearing the number 11 shirt in a 3-2 defeat at the hands of Lloyds Paper Mills at Hartsdown Park on 14.9.46.

He later played for local amateur club Thanet Press and turned out for their veterans side in a charity match at The Royal School for the Deaf in Margate in March 1959.

name: Dean McDonald
other clubs: Crystal Palace (0), Arsenal (0), Ipswich Town (5+10,1), Hartlepool United (5+1,1), Gillingham (20+10,6), Inverness Caledonian Thistle (Scotland) (0+7,0), Rushden & Diamonds, Grays Athletic, Northwich Victoria, Tooting & Mitcham United, Farnborough, Carshalton Athletic, Billericay Town, Macclesfield Town and Sutton United
bio:
5  8  tall, born Lambeth
Schoolboy at Crystal Palace
Started as youth player at Arsenal in 2002
2003/04 two sub apps for reserves who include likes of Fabregas and Bentley as well as Craig Holloway 
Released end of 2003/04
Trials at Boston, Farnborough Town and Wycombe Wanderers during early part of 2004/05 
December 2004 started trial with signed by Championship club Ipswich and signed by them in Feb 2005 on short-term deal to end of 2004/05
Six goals in 16 reserve team appearances
Then given one-year contract by Joe Royle in the summer of 2005 and said "I managed to do enough in the three months I was here for him to give me this chance and I want to show what I can do. I hope to be a part of the first team squad on a regular basis and hopefully I can make my first team debut. I'm looking to make as big an impact as possible."
Ipswich debut 20.8.95 in 2-1 home win over Sheffield Wednesday. 7 more apps then loaned to League One Hartlepool in November 1995
Hartlepool debut as sub in 1-0 defeat at Gillingham on 19.11.95. Five more there   all starts   and scored in 2-1 home win over AFC Bournemouth on 10.12.95
Back to Ipswich later in December 1995 and seven more senior outings before end of season. Scored winner after coming on as sub as the Tractor Boys won 2-1 at Crewe on 14.2.06. Last appearance was as first half sub in 1-1 draw with Hull at Portman Road on 25.3.06. Also two goals from 12 reserve team apps during 2005/06
Trial at Watford April 2006 once knew Ipswich contract not going to be renewed
May 2006 signed by League One Gillingham on two-year deal. Debut 5.8.06 in home game against Huddersfield and scored in a 2-1 win. Went on to make total of 30 appearances (ten as sub) during remainder of 2006/07 and scored six goals in all, last of them secured 1-0 win over Bristol City at Priestfield on 9.4.07
Released from contract (year to run) in July 2007 and signed for Scottish Premier Division outfit Inverness Caledonian Thistle
Debut as sub in 3-0 home defeat against Rangers on 4.8.07. Then six more sporadic sub appearances, last in January 2008
July 2008 released and signed for Conference club Rushden & Diamonds. Debut 9.8.08 in 1-0 win at Eastbourne Borough. Only two more apps, both starts, and goal in second of them   2-1 defeat at Kidderminster on 30.8.08. Released start of November 2008.
Later in November 2008 he signed for Conference outfit Grays
No league apps for Grays but did score in a Conference Shield tie against Chelmsford.
Joined Conference club Northwich in January 2009   scored winner as they won 2-1 at Kidderminster on 15.2.09 but left later that month after only two apps
Left Northwich (manager Steve King) Feb 2009 and joined Tooting for remainder of 2008/09
Six goals from nine Isthmian League Premier outings for Tooting before end of season, played with future Margate team-mates Joe and  Paul Vines
To Southern League Premier Division club Farnborough summer 2009   Steve King now there. Scored on debut 15.8.09   3-1 home win over Leamington and Kezie Ibe also scored.
Prolific early on and October 2009 Celtic reportedly interested and News of The World ran story.
Farnborough manager Steve King said: "We received a fax from Celtic asking for tickets to be left for our last home game. When someone spoke to their scout he confirmed that it was Dean they were watching. It's a great honour to have a club like Celtic watching one of our players and Dean should certainly be playing way above the level we're at. There are often reasons why young players don't make it at bigger clubs. Sometimes bosses simply don't have the man-management skills to deal with certain players and some footballers are just late developers. I have known Dean since he was 12 years old and he's really taken the bull by the horns since he came down here. He's on fire right now. Apart from the competitive matches, he also scored seven goals in our pre-season games against the likes of Chelsea, Reading, Southampton and Brentford. We are a non-league club so that means we are not affected by the transfer windows. I would be very surprised if Dean was still with us come the New Year."
26.12.09 scored hat-trick in 4-0 win at Bashley
25.1.10 scored five in 7-1 home win over Bagshot in Aldershot Senior Cup
20.3.10 another hat-trick in 4-0 win at Rugby
Ended 2009/10 with 35 goals from 53+3 as won promotion to Conference South
July 2010 trial with Swansea (Championship) and played 90 minutes in friendly v Neath   Swansea won 2-0. BBC Sport report said Dean  impressed on his Swans debut . He later said offered a deal but Farnborough and Swansea couldn t agree fee
2010/11   23+11, 10 goals
Spent 2011/12 with Carshalton   five goals from 21 Isthmian League Premier Division appearances (13 as sub) including one on his debut 20.8.11, a 2-1 win at Canvey Island. Released end of season
Summer 2012 trial with Conference club Macclesfield  - friendlies but not signed and no club first half of 2012/13
Early January 2013 joined Conf South Billericay   only there a couple of weeks 
Before end of January 2013 joined Macclesfield and told Cheshire Today site "I was up at the club on trial earlier in the season, but we couldn't get things worked out and unfortunately I got a hand injury so was out for a couple of months. But I've been spending the time in the gym and working hard to keep fit. The gaffer has been very honest with me and now it's down to me to keep working, get match fit and prove myself worthy of a chance in the side. I know a bit about the club from being here on trial, and I've worked with the manager before, and played with CBB. I've also played against a few of these lads, so I know there's a lot of quality here. I'm not an out and out striker like say, Barnsey [Matthew Barnes-Homer], but I can get forward, create a few chances and I've got a good eye for goal." 
Debut as sub 26.1.13 as Macclesfield lost 1-0 at home to Premier League club Wigan in the FA Cup 4th Round. Wigan eventually won trophy
Released by Macclesfield April 2013 after 3+8, 0 goals in all
20.7.13 played as Ebbsfleet lost 3-0 at Maidstone in a friendly
Then trial with Dover   scored in a 3-1 friendly win at Whitstable on 23.7.13, beat three players before rifling shot past Lamprell. Only outing for Dover
then joined Sutton in August 2013 and featured regularly (CHECK SUTTON ARCHIVE), although often as sub, before signing for us
After joining us days after Terry Brown and his assistant Stuart Cash appointed Dean told the This Is Kent website "I knew about Terry and Stuart as they are well-known in non-league football and Sutton needed to release a couple of players from their budget and I was interested in the whole project here. With the takeover and the club's plans, the chance to join the gaffer, who has managed at a higher level, means I know the training will be of a good standard which is important to me as a player."
Asked if had been guaranteed starts "It's not something I've ever asked for at any club I've been at. Non-league football is honest, it doesn't matter who you are, if you play well, you keep the shirt. I'm as fit as I've ever been and feel very good. I can get through 80 or 90 minutes no problem. I've had injuries in the past but this year, I've stayed injury-free so far. My best role is as an attacking midfielder behind one or two strikers but I am happy to play wherever the manager thinks I can help the team."
Brown described him as "an absolute diamond" and "one of the most gifted players in non-league football".
The most prolific spell of his career was at Farnborough where he notched 35 goals in the 2009-10 season which attracted the attention of Brendan Rodgers' Swansea City who offered him a deal before the clubs failed to agree a fee. The Swans won promotion to the Premier League that season but McDonald shrugs off thoughts of what might have been.
The former Ipswich and Gillingham player said: "I try not to think too much about it as mentally it is going to play games with you. I just need to keep working and see what happens. I love playing non-league as you can see what the game means to the fans as they love the club."

name: Paul McDonald
other clubs: Gillingham (0), Tonbridge and Faversham Town
bio:
Defender who began his career with Gillingham and became a regular in their reserves during the 1975/76 season, winning the 'Young Player of the Year' award for the Gills.

In the summer of 1976 Paul joined Margate and made his debut on 24.8.76 when he came on as a substitute in a 2-0 defeat at Hastings. However he was hampered by an ankle injury and only featured in three more games (once as a sub) before being released.

In November 1976 Paul joined Tonbridge and impressed enough to earn a contract.

Paul later played for Faversham and was with them during the 1978/79 campaign.

name: Sean McFadden
other clubs: Chelsea (0), Charlton Athletic (0), Erith & Belvedere and Hamilton (New Zealand)
bio:
Versatile player born in Hackney, London who joined Chelsea as a non-contract player on 27.8.82 aged only 15. Sean then joined Charlton and signed apprentice forms there on 3.8.83.

He played for the Addicks' Colts and Football Combination sides during 1983/84 and 1984/85 which led to Sean becoming a non-contract senior player in April 1985. A back injury ended Sean's hope's of a professional career with Charlton and in December 1985 he left the club to join Erith & Belvedere.

Sean spent the summer of 1986 playing for Auckland-based club Hamilton in New Zealand and their manager at the time was Tommy Taylor. Sean won the club's 'Player of the Year' award before returning to Erith.

He was the Deres 'Player of the Year' for 1987/88 and went on to make over 150 appearances for the club before signing for Margate in February 1991. His former Hamilton boss Taylor had recently taken charge at Hartsdown Park.

Sean made his debut for Margate on 16.2.91 when he played in midfield during a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Dunstable. The Isle of Thanet Gazette described him as being "uncompromising". He then featured in Margate's next nine games and divided his time between midfield and the left-back slot. After missing three matches in April 1991 Sean returned to wear the number three shirt in a 1-0 win at Gosport on 20.4.91 but it was his last game for Margate. He'd made 11 appearances without scoring during 1990/91.

Sean featured in a couple of Margate's pre-season friendlies in the summer of 1991 but left the club before the 1991/92 campaign proper started and returned to Erith & Belvedere.

He stayed with the Deres until the end of the 1993/94 season and made a total of 153 appearances for the club, scoring 24 goals.

Sean's family had strong ties with Erith & Belvedere and in 2005 his father John was the Deres chairman whilst his mother ran the club bar and his sister ran the matchday refreshment hut.

name: Dave McFall
other clubs: Crusaders (Northern Ireland), Sittingbourne, Aldershot (3,0), Ashford Town, Ramsgate Athletic, Deal Town and Whitstable Town
bio:
5' 8" tall Northern Irish player born in Ballymena who began his career with Crusaders in his native Northern Ireland.

Dave moved to England in the summer of 1957 and signed for Kent League side Sittingbourne. He spent just over a year with the Brickies before joining Aldershot in October 1958.

Having made three Football League appearances during the 1958/59 season, Dave left Aldershot in the summer of 1959 and signed for Margate. The club had previously tried to sign him during his time with Sittingbourne but Dave chose to try his luck with Aldershot instead.

He made his debut on 22.8.59 as Margate took on Cambridge United at Hartsdown Park. It was the club s first Southern League game since the end of the 1936/37 season. Dave sensationally scored with a header from a Ken Tucker cross after only 15 seconds and added another goal barely a minute later to put Margate 2-0 up on the way to a 3-2 win. Despite his amazing start to the campaign, Dave spent most of 1959/60 in the reserves and only played eight times for the first team, scoring four goals. He was released at the end of season.

After leaving Hartsdown Park, Dave had a short spell in Thanet local football before moving on to Ashford in October 1960.

He made 23 Southern League appearances for Ashford during the remainder of 1960/61 and scored four goals.

Dave then joined Ramsgate for the 1961/62 season but returned to Margate in the summer of 1962 having been released.

The 1962/63 campaign wasn't a good one for Dave, he spent most of his time in Margate s reserves, making 34 appearances for them, and only played seven times for the first team, scoring twice. In October 1962 he was quite depressed about the direction his football career had taken and was said to be thinking about giving the game up altogether. He decided against that course of action but at the end of the season Dave was released.

He linked up with Deal for the 1963/64 campaign but left the club at the end of the season.

Dave joined Whitstable for the 1965/66 campaign and spent three seasons there, scoring 15 goals in 55 appearances up to and including his last game at Brett Sports on 3.2.68.

After retiring as a player, he had a three year spell as Whitstable s club secretary that included the 1976/77 season and then became the club s assistant manager for a time. During 1982/83 he was reserve team manager.

Dave then moved on to Herne Bay where he coached and acted as assistant manager.

He spent the 1985/86 campaign as manager of Faversham s reserve team and in March 1986 it was announced that Dave would become first team manager in May 1986. He told the Faversham News I m very pleased to be having my first shot at management with Faversham. I shall continue the policy of using homegrown players and fully backing Town s progressive youth policy. Every club in Kent could take a leaf out of Faversham s book. Unfortunately for Dave things didn t work out and at the end of November 1986 he resigned with Faversham bottom of the Kent League. He was replaced as manager by former Margate player Andy Woolford.

Dave then went back to Whitstable where he held various backroom roles and he was still involved with the club during the 2001/02 season when he was reserve team manager once again.

In 2010 Dave was living in Whitstable but he was no longer involved with the club at that time, although he was still a regular spectator at Belmont Road.

Shortly before his 77th birthday in 2012 Dave moved to Derbyshire to be closer to his family for health reasons.

He died in Burton-on-Trent on 14.12.14 aged 79.
