name: Andrew Miller
other clubs: Dover Athletic, Folkestone Invicta, Deal Town and Ramsgate
bio:
Striker who started his career in Dover s youth ranks. Andrew played for the club s Under-16 s side during the 2008/09 campaign and then progressed to the reserves during 2009/10. He also featured three times as a substitute for Dover s first team that season.

In April 2010 Andrew scored the only goal of the game as Kent beat Sheffield & Hallamshire in the Final of the FA County Youth Cup and it was the first time that Kent had ever won the trophy.

In the summer of 2010 he featured in some friendlies for Faversham but Andrew ended up staying with Dover for the start of 2010/11 and scored 11 goals from ten outings for the youth team before featuring in the senior side as they lost 3-1 in a Kent Senior Cup tie against Cray at Bromley in January 2011. Andrew also played for Kent s Under-18 s during that month.

In February 2011 he had a short trial with Gillingham and Andrew scored as a Gills side won 5-1 in a friendly at Deal.

In March 2011 he signed for Margate and made his debut as a substitute in a 2-1 home win over Carshalton in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 12.3.11. Andrew then featured once more as a sub in Margate s next four games before starting for the first time in a 2-2 draw with visitors AFC Hornchurch in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 26.3.11. He came off the bench again in Margate s next match and then wore the number eight shirt in a 3-0 defeat at Hastings on 9.4.11.

Andrew featured three more times as a substitute and his last outing came in a 2-0 defeat against Cray at Bromley on 25.4.11. At the end of the season he left Margate having made a total of eight appearances (six as sub) without scoring.

In the summer of 2011 Andrew featured in some of Ramsgate s friendlies but he signed for Folkestone ahead of the 2011/12 season proper.

He went on to make seven sub appearances for Invicta without scoring in the Isthmian League Division 1 South before moving on to Kent League club Deal by the end of 2011.

Andrew was still with Deal during the 2012/13 campaign but in the summer of 2013 he signed for Ramsgate.

At the end of January 2014 Andrew went back to Deal having scored four times from 27 outings (18 as sub) for Ramsgate during the first half of 2013/14.

name: Gary Miller
other clubs: Dover, Dover Athletic, Canterbury City, Deal Town, Ramsgate, Folkestone Invicta, Whitstable Town Hythe United and Hythe Town
bio:
Canterbury-born player who started his career with Dover, playing for their youth team during the 1978/79 campaign. Gary stayed with the club for over five years and played for Dover's first team during the 1982/83, 1983/84 and 1984/85 seasons.

Towards the end of 1984 Gary moved on to Canterbury but played just once before linking up with Deal for the 1985/86 campaign.

Gary stayed with Deal until December 1986 when he signed for Thanet United. He made his debut on 9.12.86 in a 1-1 draw with Dover in a Southern League Cup tie at Hartsdown Park and had a solid game in the heart of the United defence. He went on to make a total of 18 appearances (two as sub) before the end of the 1986/87 season and played as a striker in two of those games. Gary scored his only goal in a 4-0 win over Ramsgate in the inaugural Isle of Thanet Gazette Cup match at Hartsdown on 13.4.87.

During the early months of the 1987/88 campaign Gary was mostly used as a striker and on 12.9.87 he scored with two headers in a 3-1 win at Merstham in the FA Cup. He also scored twice as Thanet beat Chatham 8-0 at Hartsdown on 1.12.87 and by that time Gary had moved into midfield. Towards the end of 1987 he was in and out of the side and after a 1-0 defeat at Baldock on 16.1.88 Gary spent almost three months out of the first team picture altogether. This was mainly due to a foot injury although there were times when he was fit but only chosen for the reserves. On 6.4.88 Gary finally returned to the senior side when he played up front in a 1-1 draw at Burnham but he only featured twice more as a substitute before the end of the season. When he came on in a 3-1 defeat at Hastings on 2.5.88 it was Gary's last game in a Thanet shirt. He was released in the summer of 1988 having scored six goals in 31 appearances (four as sub). He'd also made eight appearances in the reserves, scoring once, and their manager Mick Busby praised Gary's attitude although it was later suggested that he'd failed to turn up for some games towards the end of the 1987/88 campaign.

Gary joined Canterbury for 1988/89 and made 58 Southern League appearances, scoring four goals, before moving to Ramsgate in September 1990. In November 1990 he was sent off in the Rams' 4-1 win at Crockenhill.

Gary moved to Folkestone Invicta in the summer of 1991 and spent four years there before rejoining Deal for 1995/96.

By the time he left Deal to return to Canterbury in the summer of 1997 Gary had taken his total career appearances for the club to 115.

After spending the 1997/98 season with Canterbury Gary joined Whitstable for 1998/99. He made his debut for the Oystermen on 15.8.98 and was sent off in his fourth game for club, a 2-1 home win over Herne Bay on 31.8.98. Towards the end of the campaign he moved on to Hythe United.

Gary went on to stay at Hythe for over five years and during the 2002/03 season, by which time they were known as Hythe Town, he had a spell as the club's player-manager before reverting to a purely playing role for 2003/04.

In September 2004 he went back to Deal once again, around the time of his 42nd birthday. By the start of 2007/08 Gary was approaching 150 first team appearances for Deal and during the 2007/08 campaign he made 28 appearances (two as sub) for the reserves aged 45.

He was player-manager of Deal's reserve side during 2008/09 and in October 2008 Gary was sent off for them in a game against Dover Reserves. He was 46 by then.

During the 2009/10 season Gary was assistant manager of Deal's reserves and still playing for them. He also turned out for a Dover veterans side during the campaign.

Gary was still player-manager of Deal's reserve side at the start of 2011/12 and by then his son Jordan was playing for Deal's first team. At that time Gary was living in Newington near Folkestone and running his own company 'Gary Miller Gas Services Limited'.

Early in 2012 Gary became Canterbury City's assistant manager and Jordan followed him to the club. City's manager at the time was former Margate player Paul Murray.

In April 2012 Gary left City after a brief spell as caretaker manager following Murray's departure.

name: Johnny Miller
other clubs: Tufnell Park, Dulwich Hamlet, Islington Corinthians, Fulham (4,0), St Albans City and Ayr United (Scotland)
bio:
5' 7" tall fast, two-footed left winger nicknamed 'Dusty' who was born in Leyton, London and began his career with Tufnell Park before joining Dulwich Hamlet.

Johnny played for Dulwich in an FA Cup tie at Margate on 14.11.36 and helped Hamlet win the Surrey Senior Cup during that 1936/37 campaign. The club also won the FA Amateur Cup at Wembley but Johnny didn't play in the final.

The following season was a remarkable one for Johnny as he was part of the Islington Corinthians amateur team that embarked on an ambitious and ground-breaking world tour. The side played a remarkable 95 games in eight months from October 1937 to May 1938 and won 68 of them, losing just eight. The tour took the Corinthians and Johnny to Holland, Switzerland, Egypt, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Hong Kong, the Philippines, Vietnam, occupied China, Japan, Hawaii, the United States and Canada. In 2008 the story of the 40,000 mile trip was documented in a book fittingly called 'Around The World In 95 Games' which included tales of the team being taken on an opium den raid by the Hong Kong Police, being arrested in Shanghai, visiting film sets in Hollywood and meeting famous stars of the silver screen including David Niven and Pat O'Brien.

After returning to the UK following his epic trip Johnny signed for Fulham and made four first team appearances for the Cottagers during the 1938/39 campaign before World War II began.

Johnny remained on the Cottagers' books throughout the conflict and guested for various clubs whilst serving in the forces. Towards the end of the war he featured regularly for St Albans and during the early part of the 1945/46 season Johnny turned out for Ayr United whilst he was stationed in Scotland.

Later in 1945/46 he returned to St Albans and Johnny made a career total of 55 appearances there and scored seven goals. He finished the campaign back at Fulham but left the club at the end of the season.

In November 1947 Johnny joined Margate and made an instant impression by scoring on his debut - a 4-0 win away to Lloyds in the Kent League on 22.11.47. His goal came from a corner kick that went straight in. Johnny went on to make a total of 18 appearances during the 1947/48 season and scored 11 times but missed the last part of the campaign after pulling a leg muscle. Margate finished the season as Kent League champions.

During 1948/49 Johnny made a further 25 appearances and scored eight goals, several from the penalty spot. His elusiveness was praised in the local press.

In the summer of 1949 Johnny announced that he was planning to wind down his career and would only play when absolutely necessary but he ended up featuring regularly again during the 1949/50 season. He played 30 times and scored nine goals, fitting in his appearances around his work in the newsreel business. However the campaign did prove to be Johnny's last as a first team regular and although he stayed with the club for the 1950/51 season he only played twice for the first team.

He then retired from the game at the age of 38.

Johnny died in Hillingdon during March 1990 aged 77.

name: Kien Millington
other clubs: AFC Wimbledon, Sutton United and Ashford Town (Middlesex)
bio:
5' 10" tall midfielder born in Wandsworth, London who played his first football whilst attending The Archbishop Lanfranc School in Croydon. During the 2007/08 season Kien took part in a scheme to get young people involved in football known as the Kickz Programme and that was a joint venture between Charlton and Carshalton.

Kien played for AFC Wimbledon's Under-18's side during 2008/09 and he also had a trial at Bolton that was organised through a website called Football Showcase.

By the start of the 2009/10 campaign he was part of the Jamie Lawrence Football Academy run by the former Premier League player and at that time Jamie was playing in non-league football. When Jamie signed for Margate in August 2009 Kien also joined the club.

On 31.8.09, just two days after his 17th birthday, he made his debut for Margate in a 1-0 defeat against Cray in an Isthmian League Premier Division game at Hartsdown Park and Jamie Lawrence also made his Margate bow in the match. Manager Terry Yorath spoke to the Isle of Thanet Gazette about Kien and said I thought he looked good, then he fell down with the rest of the players. But I still think he could have a future with the club."

Kien then featured in midfield in Margate s next two games but after a 2-2 home draw with Sutton in the FA Cup on 12.9.09 he left the club. Jamie Lawrence also moved on at around the same time.

In November 2009 Kien joined Sutton where he spent the remainder of the 2009/10 season playing in their youth and reserve teams.

In the summer of 2010 he signed for Ashford (Middlesex) whose player-manager was Jamie Lawrence and Kien stayed there until the end 2010. He then moved to the USA for a while where he lived in Miami Beach, Florida.

Around that time he put out a mixtape having been writing and recording songs since the age of 12. He also launched a clothing line.

name: A C Mills

name: Peter Mills
other clubs: Ashford Town and Ramsgate
bio:
Ashford-born attacker who played local football in the Ashford area before signing for Margate in the summer of 1979.

Manager Terry Morris had high hopes for Peter and said "he is very quick with a good shot and all he needs is a shade more confidence." Peter scored with a header on his debut in a 3-2 home defeat at the hands of Crawley on 18.8.79 and the Thanet Times described it as "a classic goal". The paper also said that Peter was "the brightest part of Margate's overall display and "a fleet-footed striker with the deadly finishing touch who could well prove to be Margate's best bargain discovery for many a moon". Peter scored in each of his next two appearances to make it three goals from three starts and his goal in a 2-1 home win over Dunstable on 25.8.79 was described as "magnificent" by the local press. He got his fourth goal of the campaign in a 4-1 win over visitors Bromley in the FA Cup on 15.9.79.

The day before Margate were due to entertain Dulwich Hamlet in an FA Cup tie on 6.10.79, Peter collapsed at work. He missed the Dulwich game and medical tests revealed that he had a slight heart murmur which he d most likely been born with. Peter was soon cleared to play again and after missing two more matches he was back in the Margate team for a 1-0 win at Chatham in the FA Cup on 20.10.79.

He continued to be a regular in Margate s attack until February 1980 but only scored once more - in a 5-1 win at Basingstoke on 26.1.80. On 13.2.80 Peter came on as a substitute in a 1-0 win at Folkestone & Shepway but suffered an injury to his right leg that led to him being carried off on a stretcher. He didn t play for the first team again and Peter was released at the end of the 1979/80 season having scored five times from 31 appearances (two as sub).

He joined Ashford Town in the summer of 1980 but didn t feature in their first team.

In January 1981 Peter returned to Thanet and signed for Ramsgate.

He later spent several more years playing locally in the Ashford area and during 1984/85 he featured for Ashford Borough.

Peter rejoined Ashford Town ahead of the 1985/86 campaign and made his debut for the senior side in a 5-1 home win over Faversham in the FA Cup on 24.8.85. He made three further first team appearances before dropping back into amateur football later in the season.

name: Charlie Mitten
other clubs: Thamesmead Town, Dover Athletic, Gillingham (1,0), Gravesend & Northfleet, Welling United, Folkestone Invicta, Hastings United, Faversham Town, Thurrock, Cray Wanderers, Croydon Athletic, Maidstone United and Leatherhead
bio:
6' 2" tall laid-back keeper born in Woolwich who started his senior career with Thamesmead. Charlie made his first team debut for the London club on 6.9.94 aged 19 and played around 50 games before being signed by Dover in March 1996. The transfer involved the first fee that Thamesmead had ever received.

Charlie made his debut for Dover in a 2-1 home win over Welling in the Conference on 26.3.96 and made a total of five appearances before the end of the 1995/96 campaign. He couldn't break into Dover's side at the start of 1996/97 and in September 1996 Charlie joined Margate on loan.

Manager Chris Kinnear brought him in to replace Kevin Hudson and Charlie had an eventful debut on 28.9.96 as Margate made the long trek to the Isle of Wight to take on Newport. After 15 minutes he committed a foul that resulted in a penalty for the home side but Charlie instantly redeemed himself by saving the spot kick. The game ended in a 1-1 draw. He went on to play in 10 of Margate's next 12 matches, sitting out two cup ties, before briefly being recalled by Dover at the start of December 1996. Charlie only missed one Margate game and his reappearance in a 3-2 defeat at St.Leonards Stamcroft on 11.12.96 started a run of four more matches in Margate's number one shirt. The last of them was a home game against St.Leonards on 26.12.96 and Charlie was carried off after 55 minutes with a twisted ankle. He then returned to Dover having made 15 appearances in all in which he kept seven clean sheets. The Thanet Times said he'd "certainly stabilized the defence and played a key role" during his time at Hartsdown Park.

Charlie didn't make any first team appearances for Dover during 1996/97 but the 1997/98 season saw him play seven times although only twice in the Conference. He really established himself at Crabble during the 1998/99 campaign and made 41 Conference appearances, only missing one game. After making two more appearances for Dover at the start of the 1999/00 season Charlie was signed by Gillingham for a five-figure fee in October 1999.

On 7.12.99 he made his debut as the Gills lost 3-0 to Torquay in a Full Members Cup tie at Priestfield but it turned out to be Charlie's only first team appearance during an 18 month spell with the club. A fractured spine suffered in a car crash meant that he was unavailable for much of this time with the Gills and he was released at the end of the 2000/01 season.

In the summer of 2001 Charlie returned to Margate and Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "He's a very good keeper, and at 26 he's still young for the job. We want Lee Turner to stay because we want two quality goalkeepers to choose from. I've got no preconceptions about who will be first-choice and they've both got something to fight for." On 11.8.01 Charlie started the opening match of the 2001/02 campaign as Margate beat visitors Worcester on penalties to win the Southern League Championship Match after a 1-1 draw. It was his first appearance for the club since 26.12.96. On 18.8.01 he played in Margate's first-ever Conference game - a 1-0 win at Boston - and the Thanet Extra praised Charlie for an "excellent injury time save" that preserved Margate's lead. He then started each of the next 13 matches with Lee Turner having to settle for a place on the subs bench.

The Isle of Thanet Gazette said Charlie "had to be in top form on a number of occasions to keep the visitors at bay" as Margate drew 1-1 with Dagenham & Redbridge at Hartsdown Park on 21.8.01 and the Nationwide football website said he made "a number of excellent stops" during a 1-0 win at Woking on 11.9.01. The site noted that one save in particular stood out as Charlie somehow got down to hold a venomous close-range effort "when a goal looked certain" and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said it had been a "simply heroic effort" from him. In its report on a 2-1 home win over Stevenage on 18.9.01 the Gazette said that he made a "great save" to push a firm header round the post but on 29.9.01 Charlie had to go off with a groin injury during the second half of a 1-0 defeat against Barnet at Hartsdown Park. Lee Turner replaced him and Charlie missed Margate's next three games due to his injury. He was fit again by mid-October but by then Turner had reestablished himself as Margate's first-choice keeper and Charlie found himself amongst the substitutes for five matches.

He returned to action on 13.11.01 when he played in a 3-1 win over visitors Bromley in the Kent Senior Cup but Turner took over again for Margate's next match and on 20.11.01 Charlie suffered a recurrence of his groin problem during a reserve team game against Ramsgate. Chris Kinnear told the Thanet Times "Something will have to be done about it. We're not sure when he's going to be fit." and Charlie didn't play for the first team again until 5.1.02 when he featured in a 2-1 win over Farnborough at Hartsdown Park. Charlie then played in Margate's next nine matches and the Thanet Times said he was "in good form" in a 3-0 defeat at Hereford on 19.1.02 and "produced a great pointblank save". The paper said that Charlie "made the save of the match when he extended his right arm to take a one-handed hold" during a 2-0 home win over Leigh in the FA Trophy on 2.2.02 and in a 3-1 defeat at Stevenage on 2.3.02 Charlie pulled off a great stop to deny future Margate striker Jean-Michel Sigere a goal.

Charlie's run of games ended on 5.3.02 when he was sent off in injury time as Margate won 2-1 at Braintree in the FA Trophy. His dismissal followed a brawl in the immediate aftermath of the home side pulling a goal back and trying to retrieve the ball quickly. Charlie missed one match due to suspension and then sat out another due to a hip problem before taking over from Lee Turner for an FA Trophy quarter final tie against Morecambe at Hartsdown Park on 16.3.02. Unfortunately Charlie's hip injury flared up again and he had to go off at half-time as Margate went down 2-1. The injury, sometimes reported as a thigh problem, finished Charlie's season and he missed Margate's last 12 games of the campaign. He'd made 25 appearances and in its end of season round-up the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Charlie had been "pretty much faultless...but his struggle to recover from a thigh injury may be a concern for the Margate management".

In the summer of 2002 Charlie was released as he was due to move to Sheffield and start a new job so new signing Phil Smith started the 2002/03 campaign in goal. But a couple of weeks into the new season Charlie rejoined the club after his relocation fell through and he immediately took over from Smith as Margate's first-choice keeper. He made his first appearance in a 2-2 draw with Barnet at Margate's adopted home in Dover on 3.9.02 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Charlie was "pretty much faultless". He was a fixture in the side for the next few months and started 25 consecutive games.

In its report on a 2-1 win at Gravesend & Northfleet in the 4th Qualifying Round of the FA Cup on 26.10.02 the Thanet Times said Charlie "commanded his area well" and the KM Extra newspaper said he was "equal to everything thrown at him" in a 1-1 draw with Telford at Dover on 9.11.02. On 16.11.02 Charlie played as Margate drew 1-1 at Leyton Orient in the 1st Round Proper of the FA Cup and he also featured in the replay at Dover on 26.11.02 that Margate won 1-0.

The BBC's 'Match of the Day' cameras were at Dover to record highlights of Margate's FA Cup 2nd Round tie with Cardiff on 7.12.02 and just before half-time Charlie came out of his goal to clear a back-pass, swung at the ball and completely missed it. The ball rolled just past the post and when the BBC replayed the moment that night the memorable caption was "Mitten has kittens". Margate lost 3-0 but the KM Extra said Charlie's "handling and shot-stopping were impeccable".

On 14.12.02 Margate won 3-1 at Stevenage in the Conference and the Thanet Times said Charlie "bounced back with a confident and assured display" after his lapse against Cardiff. The paper said he "probably didn't have the video recorder set to tape the Cardiff highlights". Charlie's run in the side continued into 2003 and the KM Extra said he made an "excellent reflex stop" to prevent an early goal as Margate won 2-0 at Dulwich in an FA Trophy tie on 11.1.03. Seven days later things turned sour for Charlie when he inexplicably fumbled a speculative 35 yard shot from player-manager Jimmy Quinn into the net as Margate entertained Northwich at Hartsdown Park. The game ended in a 4-4 draw and Charlie was dropped afterwards.

He sat out Margate's next 15 games as Phil Smith became first-choice keeper and in February 2003 Charlie twisted his ankle after falling down a flight of stairs. His only other first team outing came in a 3-0 win at Erith & Belvedere in the Kent Senior Cup semi-final on 1.4.03 but Smith then took over again and Charlie finished the season having played 26 times - exactly half of Margate's fixtures.

He featured in some of Margate's friendlies ahead of the 2003/04 campaign but with Phil Smith firmly established Charlie became a permanent fixture on the subs bench as Margate's final Conference season unfolded. On 29.11.03 he finally made his first appearance when he came on as a substitute for the injured Smith after 70 minutes of a game at Chester and the Thanet Times said Charlie made "some good saves" although Margate lost 3-0. It was his only first team outing and in February 2004 Charlie joined Gravesend & Northfleet. He hadn't been under contract at Margate and joined the club's Conference rivals after they'd made a seven day approach for his services. Margate's assistant manager Kevin Raine said "Charlie's not had an opportunity, but he's stood by us and been there when we've needed him. He's done well for us, both when we were trying to get in the Conference and in it. He's been good for us and there's no animosity between us and Charlie."

He became Gravesend's back-up keeper and Charlie stayed with the club until November 2004 when he moved on to Welling. He'd only played seven first team games in his nine months with the Fleet.

Charlie was released by Welling in May 2005 and in July 2005 he rejoined Margate.

Charlie was the club's first signing after a transfer embargo was lifted and he put pen to paper on a two-year contract. Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "He had other offers but he's been with us before and a signing like this helps fill everyone with confidence that our problems are behind us, because there has been a little bit of doubt. Charlie's still only 30, could do a job in the Conference and I wouldn't think there will be many better than him in the Ryman League." Kinnear also said "He's got all the experience we need really, he's a top notch goalkeeper. Charlie's more than good enough to play a couple of leagues higher."

He made the first appearance of his fourth spell with Margate in a 2-0 defeat at Ramsgate in a match played for the Kent Messenger Cup on 13.8.05 and Charlie then played in a 1-0 win over Maldon in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 20.8.05. It was Margate's first game back at the temporary version of Hartsdown Park after three seasons of groundsharing at Dover and Ashford. The Thanet Times said Charlie "came into his own in the latter stages and pulled off a great diving stop" as Margate drew 0-0 at Harrow on 27.8.05 and the paper said he "caught everything" in a 0-0 draw with visitors Redbridge on 29.8.05.

Charlie's good form continued and the Thanet Times praised a "superb late save" in a 1-1 draw at Worthing on 3.9.05 whilst the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he turned in "the complete performance" during a 1-1 draw with Fisher at Hartsdown Park on 6.9.05. In its report on a 1-0 home win over Carshalton in the FA Cup on 24.9.05 the Thanet Times said Charlie was "by no means 100 per cent fit following a thigh strain" and as the weeks passed it became clear that he was being hampered by injury although it didn't directly affect Charlie's form.

At the start of October 2005 he had a spell as captain following the departure of Mark Green and Charlie's first game as skipper was a home match against Billericay on 4.10.05. The Thanet Times said he made "a brilliant save at full stretch" to claw away a header from Ricay's soon to be Margate striker Danny Hockton early in game and the paper also praised Charlie's "immaculate handling". On 22.10.05 he denied the prolific Richard Jolly with what the Thanet Times said was "a superb diving save" as Margate beat Wealdstone 1-0 at Hartsdown Park and on 12.11.05 Charlie headed over the bar from an injury time corner in a 1-0 home defeat against Dartford in the FA Trophy. The Thanet Times said he "proved the hero" after making a "brilliant save" to push a late free-kick over as Margate won 1-0 at Windsor & Eton on 19.11.05 and the paper praised Charlie for "two top saves" in a 3-2 win over Hampton & Richmond at Hartsdown Park on 26.11.05.

Throughout the first half of the season Charlie had been troubled with niggling injuries but only missed one of Margate's first 30 matches and at the end of 2005 he was diagnosed with having a problem with the nerves in his back which had been causing other symptoms. After finding out about Charlie's damaged nerves Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "I'm not surprised playing behind our defence !"

After playing in a 3-1 defeat at Redbridge on 2.1.06 Charlie was rested to aid his recovery and he sat out the next eight games before having to come on as a substitute 60 minutes into a 4-0 win over Wealdstone at Northwood on 25.2.06 when his loanee replacement Darren Behcet was injured. Behcet then suffered a recurrence of his injury in the warm-up for Margate's next game at Chelmsford on 3.3.06 so Charlie had to play and he made a blunder which led to the only goal of the game. He allowed a tame shot to squeeze between him and the post and Chris Kinnear told the Thanet Times "I saw the shot, thought Oh, he's got that covered', then I looked back and saw it in the net."

Despite not being fully fit Charlie started the next three matches too but after a 1-0 defeat at Gravesend & Northfleet in the Kent Senior Cup on 21.3.06 he was able to have another break and missed two games before returning in a 1-1 draw with Windsor & Eton at Hartsdown Park on 4.4.06. That match turned out to be Chris Kinnear's last in charge. Charlie kept his place for the next three games and the Thanet Times said he made "two excellent saves" in a 0-0 draw with visitors Worthing on 15.4.06. He then played in a 1-1 draw at Folkestone on 17.4.06 but in the last minute Charlie had to be stretchered off after injuring himself whilst clearing the ball. He missed the last two matches of the season and ended the campaign having made 38 appearances (one as sub), keeping ten clean sheets.

Charlie featured in some of Margate's pre-season friendlies in the summer of 2006 as he gradually regained his fitness but in July 2006 trialist keeper Paul Nicholls impressed new player-manager Robin Trott who declared his intention to sign the former Chelsea player. Trott told the Thanet Times "I'm not knocking Charlie Mitten because he's a decent keeper. He's just been unfortunate in that he's had a couple of injuries." Nicholls ended up going elsewhere but Margate did sign young keeper Scott Chalmers-Stevens and at the start of August Robin Trott told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "To be quite honest I don't know if I've seen any progress in Charlie's injury. He's not had a good rehab and the injury has remained stagnant. Hopefully it will improve because he's a decent keeper."

On the eve of the new season Trott again spoke to the Gazette about Charlie and described him as being "very quiet" but "a big presence" as well as a "good shot-stopper who comes and collects crosses." He was fit for the start of the 2006/07 campaign but Scott Chalmers-Stevens started the season as first-choice and Charlie didn't feature until 14.10.06 when he came on as a substitute three minutes from the end of a 2-1 home defeat against Potters Bar in the FA Cup after Chalmers-Stevens was sent off.

With Chalmers-Stevens suspended Charlie made his first start of the campaign in a 4-0 win at Leyton in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 28.10.06 and before the game Robin Trott had told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "Scotty's out and if Charlie does well he can keep his place - that's the way it is." Charlie made what the Thanet Times called a "magnificent save" in the first half and he then started six of Margate's next seven matches, only missing a Kent Senior Cup tie at VCD on 8.11.06 which didn't involve any regular first team players.

His run in the side ended after a 4-2 home defeat against Staines on 28.11.06 and Chalmers-Stevens then took over as first-choice once again. Charlie sat out six games before being recalled for a 3-0 win at East Thurrock on 23.1.07 and played in the next two matches before being dropped after a 4-4 draw at Harrow on 3.2.07.

After missing five games Charlie again took over from Chalmers-Stevens as Margate lost 1-0 at Staines on 17.3.07 and he then started each of the next eight matches. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he made "three brilliant saves" in a 1-1 draw with Horsham at Hartsdown Park on 27.3.07 and the Thanet Times praised him for an "outstanding save" from a free-kick in the first half of a 3-0 home win over Walton & Hersham on 31.3.07.

Charlie's good form continued and the Isle of Thanet Gazette's report on a 0-0 draw with visitors Billericay on 3.4.07 was headlined "So how did Charlie manage that save ?". The paper said he'd made a "wonder-save" by somehow keeping out what it described as a "bullet header" after changing direction in mid-air to tip the ball over. The Times said it was the "save of the season without any doubt" and added that Charlie later "followed up his heroics with another smashing stop in a one-on-one". On 14.4.07 Charlie made what turned out to be his last-ever appearance for Margate in a game at Chelmsford. He went off injured after 37 minutes to be replaced by Chalmers-Stevens and Margate won 3-1. Charlie missed the last two matches of the campaign and finished the season having played 20 times (once as sub). He kept six clean sheets.

In May 2007 Charlie was released and Robin Trott told the Thanet Times "It's been difficult because I've had two very good goalkeepers here. Scott Chalmers-Stevens made an excellent start coming down from full-time football and adjusting to our level. Charlie took his time then was absolutely excellent for us. Goalkeepers have longer careers than outfield players and Charlie's got a long way to go. But Scott's only 20, has ambition to go full-time and he's the one with the price-tag around his neck."

In the summer of 2007 Charlie signed for Isthmian League Premier Division club Folkestone but was hampered by injuries throughout 2007/08. In March 2008 he broke two bones in his hand after falling down some stairs and missed the rest of the campaign as Folkestone were relegated. At that time manager Neil Cugley told the Kentish Football website "He's an all round excellent goalkeeper and he's been there and done it and he doesn't feel any pressure and he's the sort of experience that we need in this team. People don't realise just what a quality keeper he is and he is certainly one of the best I have had in my time as a manager." Charlie had managed to make 24 appearances before injury cut his season short.

He started the 2008/09 campaign with Folkestone too and Neil Cugley told Kentish Football "You will struggle to find a better keeper than Charlie in non-league football." He made 21 Division 1 South appearances before being released in January 2009 as Folkestone trimmed their squad due to financial cut-backs. Cugley told Kentish Football "He has been excellent and has such a calming influence and he has been great to have around the club."

Charlie linked up with Welling for a second spell shortly after leaving Folkestone and soon became the Conference South outfit's first-choice keeper. He went on to win the Wings' Player of the Year' award for the 2009/10 season and stayed with Welling until September 2010 when he was released due to budget issues. By then Charlie had made 56 first team appearances for the club.

Later in September 2010 he joined Isthmian League Premier Division side Hastings and at that time Charlie's former Margate rival Scott Chalmers-Stevens was also on the books of the Sussex club. Charlie only made one appearance for Hastings before moving on to Faversham towards the end of October 2010.

His spell with the Isthmian League Division 1 South club was very brief and after making his debut in a 3-0 home win over Corinthian Casuals on 26.10.10 Charlie didn't play again.

At the start of November 2010 he signed for Thurrock where he played in the Conference South before linking up with Cray on a short-term deal later in the month.

Charlie joined the Isthmian League Premier Division outfit as their regular keeper was injured and he went on to make four appearances for Cray including one in a 2-0 win at Margate on 27.12.10.

At the start of January 2011 Charlie joined his sixth club of the 2010/11 season when he signed for Croydon Athletic and on 8.1.11 he played as they won 2-0 at Margate. It was Margate's first home game since the 2-0 defeat against Cray so that meant Charlie had been in goal for two different opponents in two consecutive Margate matches at Hartsdown Park.

In February 2011 Maidstone made a seven-day approach for Charlie's services but he turned the Stones down and spent the remainder of the 2010/11 campaign with Croydon as they were relegated. Charlie made 20 appearances for the club and was chosen as Player of the Year'.

In June 2011 Charlie did sign for Maidstone and the Isthmian League Division 1 South club's player-manager at the time was former Margate star Jay Saunders. Charlie was the Stones' first-choice keeper for the first few months of 2011/12 but in November 2011 he picked up a hip injury which ruled him out for the rest of the season having made 13 league starts.

Charlie stayed with the Stones for the start of the 2012/13 campaign and on 14.7.12 he was an unused substitute as Maidstone lost 5-0 to Brighton & Hove Albion in the club's first-ever match at their new stadium in James Whatman Way. In August 2012 the Stones announced that Charlie had been appointed as the clubs player-goalkeeping coach and he was their first choice keeper for the opening months of the season before breaking his arm in a 1-0 home win over Leatherhead on 8.12.12. He was back in the Maidstone side by the end of the campaign and played as they beat Faversham 3-0 in the Division 1 South Play-Off Final on 4.5.13 to win promotion to the Premier Division. In all Charlie made 11 league appearances during the season and he stayed with the Stones for 2013/14, celebrating his 39th birthday during the early part of the campaign.

At the end of March 2014 Charlie left Maidstone to join Division 1 South club Leatherhead.

name: Bob Moffat
other clubs: Portsmouth (0), Gillingham (23+1,1), Chelmsford City, Dallas Tornado (USA), Club America (Mexico), Yeovil Town, Weymouth and Waterlooville
bio:
Lean and wiry Portsmouth-born player who started his career with his hometown club aged 15 in 1961 and spent four years with Pompey before joining Gillingham in May 1965.

Bob made 24 first team appearances for the Gills, scoring once, between 1965/66 and 1967/68. He then moved to Margate in July 1968.

Bob made his debut on 10.8.68, the opening day of the 1968/69 season, and scored as Margate drew 2-2 with Weymouth in a Southern League game at Hartsdown Park. He went on to make a total of 30 appearances in the months that followed and scored 13 goals. Bob generally played as a striker, although he was essentially a midfielder, and impressed with his intelligent style and what the local press referred to as his "gliding movement". Between 19.8.68 and 14.9.68 (inclusive) Bob scored in eight consecutive games. However on 2.11.68 he was sent off for kicking an opponent during an FA Cup 4th Qualifying Round tie against visitors Walton & Hersham and the local press said it was totally out of character for Bob. On 16.11.68 he was in the side that lost 3-1 at Northampton in the FA Cup 1st Round.

In December 1968 Bob was sold to Chelmsford for a fee of approximately £800 and he spent most of the 1969/70 season there too before signing for Dallas Tornado in the USA. He d scored 29 times from 61 outings for Chelmsford.

Bob went on to spend almost eight years with Dallas up to 1977 although he returned home to England and had loan spells with several Southern League sides during the early 1970's. That was possible because the National American Soccer League campaign in the USA lasted from March to August / September each year. He also had a short stint with Mexican outfit Club America between NASL seasons.

Bob was part of the Yeovil side that won the Southern League during 1970/71 and the club also reached the semi finals of the FA Trophy that season with Bob scoring in every round up to that stage. In addition Yeovil beat Bournemouth in the FA Cup and lost 3-0 to Arsenal in the 3rd Round but Bob missed the big game because Yeovil couldn't get clearance from the US Soccer Federation for him to play.

During 1971/72 Bob played for Weymouth and he then spent the 1972/73 campaign with Waterlooville, his last season in England.

Bob's spell with Dallas was extremely successful and coincided with the 'boom' period for football in the USA. During his time with the club the North American Soccer League (NASL) expanded from eight to 24 teams as the game went 'big time'. In 1971 Dallas won the NASL title and a year later Bob played in a game against Moscow Dynamo at the Texas Stadium that was watched by over 25,000 fans. It was a challenge match between the champions of the USA and the USSR. In 1975 Bob played against Pele when the Brazilian legend made his NASL debut for New York Cosmos. The match was broadcast live on national television and was also shown in 23 other countries. By the time Bob retired in 1977 he'd made 123 appearances for Dallas, many as a defender, and scored 12 goals. During his time with the club Dallas' average attendance had risen from around 2,000 in 1970 to a figure in the region of 16,500.

From the end of 1975 to 1978 Bob worked in Dallas' front office and during that time he was the publication director and editor of "Surge", a free football magazine for the Dallas area with a circulation of 50,000 per month.

Bob had previously hosted a television programme about football called "Soccer Locker" which was broadcast to the North Texas region during 1973 and 1974. He also wrote and directed the show.

Bob was also a successful author and his 1973 book called "Basic Soccer Guide" sold 50,000 copies whilst his 1982 publication "Intermediate Soccer" achieved sales of 10,000. In 1994 he produced "Soccer Pouch" which was a coaching system including a booklet, skills card and a small magnetic field with players on it.

As a qualified coach with a Football Association preliminary badge and an American "A" badge license Bob began a coaching school after he retired as a player. By 2005 that had expanded into a business attracting between 2,300 and 3,200 youngsters to coaching camps each year. At that time Bob was also running a company offering football tours and had taken over 6,000 Americans to Europe since 1979. Another branch of his company, Moffat Enterprises Inc., was "Rent-a-Coach" and Bob's business had a website located at http://www.soccermoffat.com He'd also found time to coach Flame Soccer Club at some stage.

Moffat Enterprises was still going strong in Dallas in 2011.

Bob's grandfather Billy Moffat made 130 Football League appearances for Portsmouth during the 1920's.

name: Brian Moffatt
other clubs: Wycombe Wanderers, Epsom, Ramsgate Athletic, Ashford Town, Folkestone Town, Walthamstow Avenue and Bexleyheath & Welling
bio:
Commanding defender born in Doncaster who started his career with Wycombe but never played for their first team before moving on to Epsom.

In November 1949, Brian joined Margate as an amateur for the first of two spells with the club and after a lengthy stint in the reserves, he made his first team debut on 18.3.50 in a 2-0 home win over Chatham in the Kent League. He put in an impressive performance and kept his place for the remaining matches of the 1949/50 season, making a total of seven appearances before the end of the campaign.

In June 1950 Brian moved across Thanet to join Ramsgate. He spent the 1950/51 season at Southwood and then joined Ashford, making 58 appearances for them during the 1951/52 & 1952/53 campaigns.

Next, Brian had a brief spell with Folkestone and he then joined Walthamstow Avenue before returning to Margate in September 1953.

Brian was signed as a professional and initially rejoined the club to replace broken ankle victim Len Revell. He quickly established himself in the number five shirt and was watched by a Football League scout from a London club as Margate lost 2-1 at Kingstonian in the FA Cup on 10.10.53. Brian was a target for abuse from the crowd during the game and the East Kent Times reported that the scout s notes on Brian were Best work in the game with the crowd yelling at him continually. He might have been a seasoned veteran. The newspaper said of Brian Many a youngster would have wilted beneath the sustained vociferous criticism but Moffatt did not apparently turn a hair. He tackled strongly, distributed to advantage, and wrote Moffatt on every ball in the air.

Brian was a fixture in the Margate side for the rest of the 1953/54 season and made a total of 33 appearances. He scored one goal during the campaign - a late equaliser in a 1-1 draw with Deal at Hartsdown Park on 24.4.54. The rest of the team joked about him 'finally' scoring and Brian's response was "You forwards were in the goalmouth for 80 minutes, I went up there for half a minute and scored." He finished the campaign by playing as Margate beat Canterbury 5-0 at Hartsdown Park to win the Kent League Cup on 6.5.54.

Brian was then a regular in the side during the 1954/55 campaign until first thigh and then knee ligament injuries curtailed his season. He made a total of 34 appearances but didn't add to his goal tally.

He went on to be ever-present during the 1955/56 season, making 45 appearances and once again playing a pivotal role. On 19.11.55 Brian was in the Margate side that drew 2-2 with Walsall at Hartsdown Park in the FA Cup 1st Round and he also played in the replay at Walsall on 24.11.55 that the home side won 6-1.

The 1956/57 campaign was another good one for Brian. Although he suffered several bouts of blood poisoning during the season he still managed 37 appearances and his aggressive display in a 4-2 FA Cup win at Wycombe on 3.11.56 was described as "magnificent" and "brilliant" by the local press. On 17.11.56, Brian played as Margate beat Dunstable 3-1 at Hartsdown Park in the FA Cup 1st Round and he also featured in a 4-0 defeat at Millwall in the 2nd Round on 8.12.56.

Brian missed the first two games of the 1957/58 season due to being on holiday and when he returned he was unable to regain his first team place as Jimmy Bonds had played well whilst deputising in the heart of the Margate defence. So Brian found himself in the reserves but cracked a bone in his foot in his first match for them and was out of action until November 1957. On 7.12.57 he finally returned to first team action for a match against Gillingham Reserves at Priestfield. Margate won 2-1 and Brian was outstanding - it was "a magnificent return" according to the local press report. The same article also described him as "an iron man" and said that he "covered himself in mud and glory". Brian kept his place for the remainder of the season and his 25 appearances took him past 150 for the club, still with just one goal to his credit.

He started the 1958/59 season in the first team and made six appearances during the first two months of the campaign before sustaining a knee injury. Brian then had a spell in the reserves but returned to the first team on 27.12.58. Margate went down 5-1 in a Kent League game at Bexleyheath & Welling and the match turned out to be Brian's last for the club. He left Hartsdown Park in January 1959.

Immediately after his departure from Margate, Brian signed for Bexleyheath & Welling and spent the remainder of the 1958/59 season there.

On 1.4.61 he watched Margate s home game against Tunbridge Wells from the trainers bench and by then Brian had retired from football.

In November 1963 he was living in Brentford and paid a visit to Margate's dressing room prior to their FA Cup game against Brentford. He also did some scouting for Margate at that time.

In 2011 Brian was living just outside Falmouth, Cornwall and he was the godfather of his former Margate team-mate Jimmy Briscoe's son Lloyd.

Brian died at the Royal Cornwall Hospital in Truro on 22.2.15 aged 86.

name: Nicky Moir
other clubs: Ilford and Faversham Town
bio:
Pacy striker born in the Barking area of Essex who was on the books of Isthmian League Division 1 North club Ilford during the 2006/07 season but didn't play any first team games there.

Nicky joined Margate as a non-contract player in the summer of 2007 aged 17 and on 31.7.07 he scored in his first friendly appearance as Margate drew 1-1 at Chatham. Player-manager Robin Trott told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "Nick Moir impressed me. He's only 17 and has been on trial here. I sent him training with the reserves and he'd played a couple of practice matches but this was the first time I've had a proper chance to look at him. He shone - and took his goal very well."

On the eve of the 2007/08 campaign Robin Trott again spoke to the Isle of Thanet Gazette about Nicky and said he had "...the fastest feet you'll ever see on the pitch" whilst adding "He's got a good touch and I've been impressed with him in pre-season."

Nicky made his debut as a substitute in a 3-0 win at Chatham in the FA Cup on 15.9.07 and then scored in his next outing, again as a sub, as Margate lost 3-2 to East Thurrock in an Isthmian League Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 2.10.07. He didn't feature in the next four games but on 21.10.07 Nicky made his third sub appearance in a 0-0 draw with Aylesbury at Chesham in the FA Trophy.

Before the end of October 2007 he was given a contract and after two more outings from the bench Nicky made his first start for Margate in a 1-1 draw at Folkestone in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 29.10.07. He then featured three times as a substitute in the next eight matches before wearing the number nine shirt as Margate entertained Welling in a Kent Senior Cup tie on 11.12.07. Nicky scored from the penalty spot in a 2-1 win but when he came on as a sub in Margate's next game - a 4-1 home win over East Thurrock on 15.12.07 - it turned out to be his last first team outing for over four months.

After a lengthy spell in the reserves Nicky returned to the senior side when he played up front as Margate lost 4-1 at home to Ebbsfleet in a Kent Senior Cup tie on 26.3.08. He didn't feature in the next four games but on 26.4.08 Nicky wore then number eight shirt as Margate travelled to Harrow for their last Isthmian League Premier Division match of the season. He scored the only goal of the game to finish the campaign with a record of three goals from 13 appearances (nine as sub).

In the summer of 2008 Nicky featured in a first team friendly at Thamesmead but a few weeks into the 2008/09 season he left Margate having failed to break into the senior side.

After his departure from Hartsdown Park Nicky dropped into local amateur football in Essex and he started the 2011/12 campaign with Dagenham club Thamesview who played on Sundays in the Romford & District Football League.

In December 2011 Nicky returned to senior football when he signed for Isthmian League Division 1 South outfit Faversham having been recommended to the club by their former Margate striker Danny Hockton. Nicky spent the remainder of the 2011/12 season with Faversham but only made three substitute appearances in the league without scoring.

name: Jon Monteath
other clubs: Queens Park Rangers (0),Sittingbourne, Sheppey United, Chelmsford City, Canterbury City, Lewes, Gravesend & Northfleet, St.Leonards, Fisher Athletic (London) and Langney Sports
bio:
Crowborough-born midfielder who played for Kent Schools as a youngster alongside future Margate player Paul Sykes. Jon started his career with Queens Park Rangers during 1993/94 and was a member of the youth team that won the South Eastern Counties League and Cup. He also played four times for the R's reserves in the Football Combination during the 1994/95 season.

After completing his apprenticeship at QPR Jon joined Sittingbourne during the 1995/96 campaign and played in their Southern League Cup winning side that season.

He moved on to Sheppey in the summer of 1996 and in December 1996 Jon signed for Margate.

He made his debut in midfield in a 3-2 defeat at St.Leonards Stamcroft on 11.12.96 but apart from one further substitute appearance Jon didn't feature in the first team again until 15.2.97 when he played in a 2-1 defeat at Witney. He started Margate's next two games as well and scored in a 5-3 defeat at Bashley on 22.2.97. During the closing weeks of the 1996/97 campaign Jon made three more sporadic appearances and the last of them was as a substitute in a 1-1 draw at Clevedon on 3.5.97. He was released at the end of the season having scored once in eight appearances (three as sub).

Jon joined Chelmsford for the start of the 1997/98 campaign before linking up with Canterbury a couple of months into the season.

He finished 1997/98 with Lewes where he made 13 appearances in the Isthmian League Division 3 without scoring.

Jon joined Isthmian Premier League outfit Gravesend & Northfleet in the summer of 1998 and made four league appearances (two as sub) without scoring before signing for St.Leonards in December 1998.

He moved on to Fisher Athletic (London) early in 1999 but rejoined St.Leonards in the summer of 1999.

Jon stayed with the Sussex club until the end of the 2001/02 season and then had a spell with Langney Sports before retiring.

name: Gary Moore
other clubs: Southwark Sports, Erith & Belvedere, Alma Swanley, Sangley Sports, Maidstone United (0+5,1), Dover Athletic, Furness, Greenwich Borough, Bromley, Ramsgate and Herne Bay
bio:
Powerful Greenwich-born striker who started his career with spells at Southwark Sports and Erith & Belvedere.

Gary later joined Alma Swanley before moving on to London Spartan League club Sangley Sports during the 1990/91 season.

In March 1991 Maidstone signed him and on 12.3.91 Gary scored in his first game for the Stones - a 1-1 draw in a friendly at Margate. He went on to make five substitute appearances in the Football League before the end of the 1990/91 season and scored once in a game at Halifax before rejoining Alma Swanley in the summer of 1991.

At the end of August 1991 Gary signed for Margate as a replacement for the recently departed Paul Underwood and made his debut in a 3-1 win over Newport IOW at Hartsdown Park on 31.8.91. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "struggled to make an impact". Shortly after he'd come on as a substitute in a 1-0 home defeat against Gosport on 7.9.91 the same paper said he had "not settled down" and Gary left the club soon afterwards having made only two appearances without scoring.

He rejoined Alma Swanley initially but in January 1992 Gary had a trial at Dover and scored for them in a 4-2 win over Hythe in the Eastern Floodlight Cup before going back to Alma again.

Gary later played for Furness where he spent the 1996/97 campaign before linking up with Greenwich for 1997/98.

He joined Bromley early in 1998/99 and made four sub appearances there before returning to Thanet to join Ramsgate later in the season.

Gary left the Rams to join Greenwich a few weeks into the 1999/00 campaign and then moved to Herne Bay later that season.

name: Glenn Moore
bio:
6' 0" tall defender born in Margate who went to Hartsdown School and progressed through Margate's youth ranks. Glenn was in the Under-11's during the 1991/92 season and by the 2001/02 campaign he was playing regularly for the reserves having been on Margate's books for ten years.

Glenn continued to turn out for the reserves during 2002/03 and in March 2003 his fiance entered him into a 'Dreamboys' modeling competition without his knowledge. Glenn won and told the Thanet Times "I've always fancied myself as a bit of a model and had to do a dance at the audition. I like dancing, but usually after a few drinks. To get up there sober was a bit of a challenge." He then gave up his job as a self-employed carpenter to travel the world doing photo shoots for a few months.

After a spell in local amateur football Glenn returned to Margate for the 2007/08 season and became a regular in the reserves once more. On 2.10.07 he made his first team debut at centre-back in a 3-2 defeat against East Thurrock in an Isthmian League Cup tie at Hartsdown Park but it was Glenn's only senior outing. He spent the remainder of the campaign back in the reserves before leaving Margate at the end of the season.

Glenn then resumed his Sunday League career and was still playing locally at the start of the 2012/13 campaign before suffering a broken leg In October 2012. He recovered to play again during the 2013/14 season.

name: Howard Moore
other clubs: Maidstone United, Ashford Town, Coventry City (0), Gillingham (19,0), Southend United (6+1,0), Port Vale (0), Canterbury City and Dartford
bio:
5' 10" tall, fast, skilful winger born in Harbledown, near Canterbury in Kent who started his career with Maidstone before moving on to Ashford in November 1965.

Howard made 17 Southern League appearances for the Nuts & Bolts before being signed by Coventry in March 1966.

He spent around 16 months with the Sky Blues but moved on to Gillingham in July 1967 having never played for Coventry's first team.

Howard spent the first half of the 1967/68 season with the Gills and made 19 first team appearances without scoring before moving on again in January 1968.

He signed for Southend but never established himself at Roots Hall and made only seven senior appearances before joining Port Vale in July 1968.

After a year in which he never made a first team appearance, Howard left the Valiants and joined Margate during September 1969.

He made his debut in a 5-2 defeat at Yeovil on 20.9.69 and impressed with his intelligent play and mazy dribbling. However Howard never gained a regular place and he became the club's perennial substitute during the 1969/70 campaign. He was only actually brought on once and at the end of the season Howard was released having made 14 appearances (one as sub) without scoring.

Howard joined Canterbury for the 1970/71 season and made 34 Southern League appearances (one as sub) for City, scoring four goals.

He moved on to Dartford for the 1971/72 campaign but only made five first team appearances, spending most of the season in the reserves. On 1.1.72 Howard scored as Dartford Reserves lost 2-1 at home to Margate Reserves. He left the Darts at the end of 1971/72 and dropped out of senior football aged only 25.

He died in Southend on 9.10.12 aged 65.

name: Jason Moore
other clubs: West Ham United (0), Dover Athletic, Ramsgate, Folkestone Invicta, Deal Town, Tilbury and Hythe Town
bio:
5' 8" tall attacking full-back who started his career with West Ham. In 1996 Jason played in both legs of the FA Youth Cup Final as the Hammers lost 4-1 on aggregate to a Liverpool side that included Michael Owen and Jamie Carragher. Future England internationals Rio Ferdinand and Frank Lampard were in the West Ham line-up as well as Manny Omoyinmi who later played for Margate. Jason went on play more than 70 reserve team games for the Hammers but in May 1998 he was released.

He joined Dover for the start of the 1998/99 season and early in 1999 he had a loan spell with Ramsgate before signing for Margate in February 1999.

When the local press asked manager Chris Kinnear about Jason he said "He's got lots of qualities, is very quick and a good acquisition for the club". Jason made his debut at right-back in a 2-0 win over Brackley at Hartsdown Park on 27.2.99 and the Thanet Times said he "looked a good addition". Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "He was ok. He hasn't played since November". Jason started Margate's next two matches in midfield and on 23.3.99 he came on as a substitute in a 3-2 home defeat against Welling. It turned out to be his last appearance for the club and he moved on shortly after missing the team bus for a trip to Witney on 17.4.99.

After leaving Hartsdown Park Jason had a spell with Folkestone and in the summer of 2000 he rejoined Dover.

Jason made five substitute appearances for Dover (four in the Conference) in the early months of the 2000/01 campaign before linking up with Ramsgate at the start of 2001.

He went back to Dover for a third spell in the summer of 2001 but joined Deal a few weeks into the 2001/02 season.

Jason returned to Ramsgate for the start of 2002/03 and after his third stint with the Rams ended he had a lengthy spell out of senior football.

He played for Tilbury during the 2004/05 campaign but then dropped out of semi-professional football again.

Jason resurfaced in the summer of 2008 when he played in three pre-season friendlies for Dover who'd just signed his younger brother Sammy. Jason left the club before the start of the league season.

In March 2010 he materialised at Hythe and Jason made four appearances (one as sub) there before leaving the club.

name: Micky Moore
other clubs: Bromley, Tooting & Mitcham United, Wimbledon, Hendon, Sittingbourne, Canterbury City and Gravesend & Northfleet
bio:
Diminutive forward who started his career with Bromley, first appearing for them during the 1956/57 season. Micky stayed with the club until the end of 1959/60 and at that time he was still doing his National Service in the army.

Micky joined Tooting & Mitcham in the summer of 1960 and he went on to make 25 appearances for them during the 1960/61 campaign, scoring ten goals.

He then moved to Wimbledon and made 159 appearances there, scoring 32 goals, in a spell that spanned the 1961/62-1965/66 seasons.

Micky left London to join Sittingbourne in October 1966 before coming to Margate towards the end of April 1967 on a short-term contract.

He made one first team appearance, in a 4-2 Southern League win over Banbury at Hartsdown on 29.4.67, but was released at the end of the 1966/67 season.

Micky then moved to Canterbury for the 1967/68 season and made 34 Southern League appearances (six as sub) during the campaign. He scored three goals in those games.

In the summer of 1968 Micky joined Gravesend & Northfleet and he made 31 appearances (two as sub) without scoring for the Fleet during the 1968/69 season before leaving the club.

name: Andrew Morgan
other clubs: Brechin City (Scotland) (0), Cuper Thistle (Scotland), Dundee (Scotland) (0), Raith Rovers (Scotland) (0), Markinch Victoria Rangers (Scotland), Chelsea (0), Fulham (0), Guildford City and Croydon Rovers
bio:
5' 10" tall centre-forward born in Freuchie, Fife who began his senior career with Brechin City, signing for them in March 1939.

Andrew then moved on to Cuper Thistle, a Scottish junior club, in May 1939.

In April 1940 he was signed by Dundee and by that time World War II was in progress. Andrew became a Spitfire pilot in the RAF and in December 1943 he was shot down over Lille and captured. He then spent the remainder of the war in a prison camp based in East Germany.

After his liberation in April 1945, Andrew returned to Britain and joined Raith Rovers but he only played a few games for them during the 1945/46 season and soon moved on to Markinch Victoria Rangers, another Scottish junior side.

In October 1947 Andrew's job as a salesman led him to move South and he joined Chelsea for a short spell before linking up with Fulham as a part-time professional in January 1948. At that time Margate were one of several clubs trying to sign him.

Whilst with Fulham, Andrew played exclusively for the reserves, mainly due to work commitments limiting his availability, and he scored a hat-trick on his debut for them. He did receive one first team call-up but was injured and couldn't play.

In July 1948 Andrew joined Guildford City having been transfer listed by Fulham. Due to a shortage of football boots, he initially had to play in ordinary work boots but still managed to score twice on his debut for City. He went on to score 14 goals in 34 appearances during the 1948/49 season but missed a month of the campaign due to a knee injury that required an operation. At the end of the season Andrew was released.

During the early part of 1949/50 he had a spell with Croydon Rovers.

In February 1950 Andrew signed for Margate and made his debut in a 4-0 win over Royal Marines Chatham in a Kent League game at Hartsdown Park on 18.2.50. The following Saturday Andrew scored the only goal as Margate won 1-0 at Snowdown and he went on to score twice more before the end of the 1949/50 campaign. At the end of the season Andrew was released having made just nine appearances for Margate.

After his stint at Hartsdown Park, Andrew retired from football as he felt that he was no longer fit enough to play. He then concentrated on coaching in schools football and managed Onslow Boys for a spell.

In 2007 Andrew was 86 and living in Onslow, near Guildford with his wife having been married for over 50 years. Sadly he was almost blind as a result of macular degeneration but was otherwise in good health.

His brother Jimmy played for Hearts and Dundee.

name: Dennis Morgan
other clubs: Seven Sisters AFC (Wales), Britton Ferry (Wales), Cardiff City (Wales) (0), Norwich City (250,3) and Merthyr Tydfil (Wales)
bio:
Defender born in Seven Sisters, Glamorgan who captained Seven Sisters Boys Club as a youth. Dennis then started his senior career with spells at Seven Sisters AFC and Britton Ferry.

In January 1945, Dennis had a trial with Cardiff City and scored a hat-trick for their reserves in his first outing for them on 6.1.45.

In the summer of 1946, Dennis signed for Norwich and went on to make exactly 250 first team appearances for them. He was in the side that pulled off a famous FA Cup shock by winning 2-1 at First Division Arsenal on 30.1.54, Norwich were in the Third Division South at the time.

On 17.8.56, Dennis left Carrow Road after a decade with Norwich and joined Southern League club Merthyr Tydfil. He was still on Norwich s books whilst playing for Merthyr and was transfer listed with a price of 4,000. The fee would only have been payable if Dennis joined another English team.

At the end of January 1958, Dennis joined Margate after around three months of protracted negotiations. Margate originally signed him in October 1957 after Dennis former Norwich team-mate Albert Foan, a Margate player at the time, alerted manager Almer Hall to the fact that Dennis had moved to Aylesham in Kent. The Welsh Football Association then blocked the deal because Merthyr still held Dennis registration and at that point Margate also found out that they d need to pay the 4,000 transfer fee set by Norwich. Almer Hall told the Thanet Times It s a stalemate because we can t afford a fee. But it s rough on Dennis, who lives near here with his parents - hundreds of miles from Merthyr. Merthyr eventually agreed to release him and Norwich waived the transfer fee.

Dennis mainly played for Margate s reserves during the remainder of the 1957/58 season but also made five first team appearances. He made his debut on 8.3.58 as Margate went down 3-1 to Ramsgate in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park but was unable to break into the side on a regular basis due to the form of the established Terry Joyce.

Dennis was made captain of the reserves for the 1958/59 season and only made one first team appearance during the campaign. That was in a 3-3 Kent League draw at Tunbridge Wells on 22.4.59 and it proved to be his last first team game for the club as Dennis was released in the summer of 1959. The Thanet Times said he was perhaps a little unfortunate to be leaving the club and added that Dennis had been a pillar of consistency at left-back for the reserves. In total, he d made around 40 appearances in the second string.

Dennis died in 1980 after developing gangrene in his right leg.

In 2003 Dennis was voted into Norwich City s Hall Of Fame after a vote by the clubs supporters.

name: Jack Morrell
bio:
Local player who played for Margate s reserves during the 2008/09 campaign and stayed with the club for 2009/10 too.

Jack was a regular in the reserves once more during the season and on 30.3.10 he made a one-off appearance for the first team when he came on as a substitute in a 2-0 defeat at Welling in the Kent Senior Cup.

He dropped into local Sunday football for the 2010/11 campaign but Jack then returned to Margate for 2011/12 and played for the reserves once again. He left Hartsdown Park once more at the end of the season and returned to local football.

name: John Morris
other clubs: Chislet Colliery Welfare and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
Striker who joined Margate from Chislet Colliery Welfare in December 1948 and played exclusively for the reserves during the remainder of the 1948/49 season.

John then went on to play six first team games during the 1949/50 campaign, first appearing in a 5-1 Kent League win over Snowdown at Hartsdown Park on 24.8.49. He left the club and rejoined Chislet before the end of the season.

In the summer of 1950, John signed for Ramsgate but he soon returned to Chislet for a third spell.

At the start of October 1951, John left Chislet once more to begin a second stint with Margate. He made his first appearance for the reserves as they thrashed Bowaters-Lloyd Reserves 6-0 at Hartsdown Park on 6.10.51. John didn t feature in the senior side before leaving the club again.

name: Kieran Morris
other clubs: Ramsgate, Whitstable Town and East Kent College
bio:
Battling locally-born player who started out in Margate's youth ranks and played for the club's Under-11's side during the 1997/98 season.

Kieran later moved across Thanet to Ramsgate and captained their Under-16's team during 2002/03 and then the Under-18's during the 2003/04 campaign. He made his first team debut in the Kent League during 2004/05 as a 17 year-old and by then his brother Liam was an established first team player for the Rams too. Kieran finished that season having made three senior appearances. He had to wait until the 2006/07 campaign for his next taste of first team football and Kieran made one sub appearance in the Isthmian League Premier Division before rejoining Margate in October 2006.

He was a regular in Margate's reserves for the remainder of 2006/07 and Kieran was also an unused substitute for the last two first team matches of the season.

In the summer of 2007 he played in two of Margate's friendlies and on the eve of the new campaign player-manager Robin Trott spoke to the Isle of Thanet Gazette about Kieran and described him as "Another player who gives 100 per cent...he's very young, but he's good on the ball and hopefully will develop."

Kieran made his first team debut as a substitute in a 2-0 win over Horsham in an Isthmian League Premier Division game at Hartsdown Park on 27.8.07 and he then came off the bench in two of Margate's next four games. On 22.9.07 he made his first start in midfield in a 2-0 home defeat against Hendon and Robin Trott told the Thanet Times "Kieran Morris did well". It was the start of a good run in the side for him and Kieran started six of the next seven matches. On 6.10.07 he wore the number two shirt in a 0-0 draw at Ashford (Middlesex) and the Thanet Times said Kieran could "be proud of his efforts as a makeshift right-back" but after he'd played in midfield in a 2-1 home win over Leyton on 16.10.07 Kieran lost his place and only made one start in Margate's next eight games although he did feature as a substitute on four occasions.

At the end of October 2007 Kieran drove his car into a ditch when he was carrying his team-mates Paul Axon, Matt Bowles and Louis Smith as passengers and Robin Trott told the Thanet Times "It's not a nice thing to happen - it shook them all up."

On 24.11.07 Kieran made his first start for almost a month as Margate won 1-0 at Billericay and the Thanet Times said he was "excellent" in midfield. He then enjoyed another good run and started nine of the next 11 matches, featuring as a substitute in the other two. His latest spell as a regular ended after a 2-1 win over Chatham in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 22.1.08 and after that Kieran only made five sub appearances in the next 11 games.

Towards the end of February 2008 Robin Trott spoke to the Thanet Times about Kieran and told the paper "He's done well and I like him. He'll be a very good player when he's older but you have to take things slowly."

On 26.3.08 Kieran made his first start for over two months as Margate entertained Ebbsfleet in the Kent Senior Cup and he scored in a 4-1 defeat to open his account for the club. He featured in four more matches during the closing weeks of the 2007/08 campaign, making three starts and one sub appearance, and after a remarkable 5-4 win over visitors Heybridge on 5.4.08 Robin Trott told the Thanet Times that Kieran had done well and added "He concentrated on what he's good at - winning tackles and headers." Kieran finished the season having scored once from 38 appearances (16 as sub).

He was a regular in the Margate side during the early part of the 2008/09 campaign and after wearing the number 11 shirt in a 2-1 defeat at Carshalton on 16.8.08 - the opening day of the new Isthmian League Premier Division season - Kieran started the next eight games in midfield before losing his place after a 5-1 defeat at Worthing in the FA Cup on 13.9.08. He only featured twice as a sub in the next five matches.

On 25.10.08 Kieran made his first start for over a month in a 1-0 defeat against Wealdstone at Hartsdown Park and he then came on as a substitute in each of the next three games. He returned to the starting line-up in a 2-1 win at Boreham Wood on 11.11.08 and on 25.11.08 Kieran was switched to right-back for a Kent Senior Cup tie against Maidstone at Sittingbourne. Margate lost 2-1 but he started four of the next five matches in the number two shirt before reverting to a midfield role in a 2-0 home defeat against Dover on 3.1.09. Kieran kept his place in midfield for Margate's next four games too but on 31.1.09 he had to go off after 15 minutes of a 1-0 defeat at Tonbridge having dislocated his shoulder.

Kieran's injury kept him out of the next seven matches and when he returned to the side for a league game against Maidstone at Sittingbourne on 21.3.09 he lined up as a centre-back. The Thanet Times said he was "the pick of the defence" in a 1-1 draw and in its report on a 3-1 home win over Billericay on 28.3.09 the paper asked "could Kieran Morris have finally found a home at centre-half ?" whilst adding he'd "probably found his best form". Manager Terry Yorath told Margate's official website "I don't know whether I should say this or not but Kieran's improved a hell of a lot since the beginning of the season. The good thing about Kieran is he's a 100 per center, he can play in a few positions and he's vital for the club at the moment."

On 4.4.09 Kieran was sent off in a 3-2 defeat at Harrow after bringing down an opponent who was through on goal having already been booked earlier. The Thanet Times said he "took one for the team" and after two outings at right-back Kieran missed a match due to his suspension. He made his last appearance of the season in the number two shirt as Margate lost 4-1 at Staines on 25.4.09 to finish in the Isthmian League Premier Division relegation zone and Kieran had played 35 times in all (seven as sub) without scoring during 2008/09.

He was given a contract ahead of the 2009/10 campaign and on the eve of new season Terry Yorath spoke to the Isle of Thanet Gazette about Kieran, saying Absolutely fantastic for us last year. I admire him for what he tries to do. If all the others were like him I d be happy. He s such an honest player and that s all I want."

Kieran made his first appearance of the new campaign when he featured in a 1-0 home win over Ramsgate in the first leg of a tie played for the Isle of Thanet Gazette Cup. He played in midfield and then started Margate s next three matches but after wearing the number two shirt in a 4-0 home defeat against Dartford in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 18.8.09 a broken toe ruled him out for several weeks.

Kieran returned to action when he came on as a substitute in a 2-0 defeat at Canvey Island on 10.10.09 and after one more outing from the bench he lined up in midfield as Margate won 1-0 at VCD in a Kent Senior Cup tie on 10.11.09. It was his first start for almost three months.

Shortly afterwards Kieran joined Division 1 South club Whitstable on loan and he made six appearances there without scoring before returning to Hartsdown Park in February 2010.

On 16.2.10 he came on as a sub in a 3-1 defeat against visitors Billericay but Kieran then missed the next ten games completely before playing in midfield in a 2-0 defeat at Welling in the Kent Senior Cup on 30.3.10. It turned out to be his last outing for Margate and at the end of April 2010 Kieran was released having made a total of nine appearances (three as sub) without scoring during 2009/10.

He signed for Whitstable on a permanent basis in July 2010 and Kieran made 17 appearances there (four as sub) without scoring during the 2010/11 campaign before leaving the club at the end of the season.

He dropped into local amateur football for 2011/12 and Kieran was still playing in the Thanet Sunday Football League during the 2012/13 campaign.

In July 2013 he signed for Kent County League Division Two East newcomers East Kent College.
