name: Johnny Ray
other clubs: Cuckfield Town, APV Athletic, Lewes, Chelsea (0), Canterbury City, Dover, Guildford City, Romford and Bexley United
bio:
6' 0" tall opportunist goalscorer born in Falmer who played for Sussex as a youth whilst attending Cuckfield County Secondary School.

Johnny made his first foray into senior football with Cuckfield in the Sussex County League, a club that his father Cecil had previously played for, and then moved on to Crawley-based APV Athletic, also of the Sussex County League.

In March 1958 Johnny signed for Lewes, another Sussex County League outfit, and he was still only 16 at the time. He was once again following in the footsteps of his father Cecil who d been a prolific striker for the club in the 1930 s. He d scored a remarkable 175 goals in just three seasons with Lewes before being signed by Aldershot in 1935. Cecil then found the net 39 times in 92 Football League outings for the Shots.

Johnny scored his first goal for Lewes as they lost 2-1 to Southwick at the Dripping Pan on 22.3.58, it was his third appearance for the club. In his fourth outing he scored twice and Johnny ended the 1957/58 season with a total of six goals. In May 1958 the Sussex Agricultural Express said that Johnny was top of the class for his constructive ball manoeuvres .

In July 1958 Johnny had a trial with Chelsea and then returned to Lewes, playing for them in a public trial match on 16.8.58. On 25.8.58 he went back to Chelsea for a two week trial and the First Division club then signed him as an amateur.

Whilst at Stamford Bridge he played in Chelsea's youth and 'A' teams alongside the likes of Peter Bonetti, Bobby Tambling, Terry Venables and future Margate full-back Dennis Butler. In April 1959 Johnny played in the London Minor Cup Final against QPR at Loftus Road and on 11.6.59 he was given a professional contract. A highlight of Johnny s time with Chelsea came when he scored a hat-trick as they beat Cannes 6-0 in a floodlit friendly played at the French club's stadium but he was released at the end of the 1959/60 season. In January 1960, Southern League club Boston had tried to signed him.

Johnny joined Southern League club Canterbury for the 1960/61 campaign and became a prolific scorer for City. On 17.9.60 he scored in a 4-2 home defeat against Margate. In six seasons with the club he was top scorer on five occasions and Johnny managed a total of 80 league goals in 192 league appearances for City. During the 1961/62 season he was sent off after a clash with Terry Joyce in a Canterbury v Margate match and he was also sent off for City during the 1962/63 campaign.

In August 1966 Johnny moved to Dover and he scored 70 goals during three seasons at Crabble. His tally included 41 during 1966/67 and on 3.4.67 he scored a hat-trick as Dover won 5-0 at Margate in the 1st Leg of the Kent Senior Cup Final.

In the summer of 1969 Johnny moved to Margate and made his debut in a 1-0 win over Brentwood at Hartsdown Park on 11.8.69. He backed up his reputation as being one of the Southern League's best goal-poachers by scoring 31 goals from 58 appearances during the 1969/70 season. Johnny was referred to as Margate's "star forward" and "sharpshooter-in-chief" by the local paper during the campaign and he was especially effective in the air. He scored in a 7-2 defeat at home to Aldershot in the FA Cup 1st Round on 15.11.69 and also found the net with several solo efforts during the season. The best of them saw Johnny beat two players before firing home in a 3-1 win over Dover on 27.12.69.

On 2.2.70 he was sent off for kicking Ramsgate's player-manager Les Riggs as Margate beat the Rams 5-1 in a Kent Senior Shield match at Hartsdown Park and the three week ban Johnny was given in April 1970 brought his season to a premature end.

Johnny began the 1970/71 season by scoring in an opening day win at Telford on 15.8.70 and he'd scored a total of three goals when he broke his wrist in a 1-1 draw with Hillingdon at Hartsdown Park on 17.10.70. The injury kept him out until January 1971. Johnny scored three further goals after his return but he soon fell out of favour. Player-manager Gerry Baker thought that Johnny didn't make enough effort but the local press said that he was "much under-rated".

In March 1971 Johnny's contract was cancelled by mutual consent and he'd scored six times in 22 appearances (one as sub) during the season.

In April 1971 Johnny signed for Guildford City of the Southern League First Division and helped them to secure promotion.

In the summer of 1971 Johnny signed for Romford and stayed there until the end of the 1971/72 campaign.

In May 1972 he joined Bexley and they were Johnny s last club before he retired.

After his football career finished, Johnny changed direction completely and began working in agriculture / horticulture.

In 2002 Johnny was working for a private estate in West Sussex and kept himself trim - he was the same weight he'd been during his football career.

In November 2013 Johnny was retired and still living in West Sussex. He sadly died on 10.3.14 at the age of 72.

Johnny completed a questionnaire for this site which you can see here.

name: Derrek Razzell
other clubs: Tooting & Mitcham United, RAF St Mawgan, Croydon Amateurs, Carshalton Athletic, Queens Park Rangers (0), Kettering Town, Dartford, Hastings United, Crawley Town and Cray Wanderers
bio:
Bustling, two-footed centre-forward born in Wandsworth, London who started his career with Tooting & Mitcham. Derrek then played for RAF St Mawgan in the Cornwall Senior League during 1956/57 whilst serving in the forces.

After returning to London Derrek signed for Surrey League club Croydon Amateurs and played for them during the 1957/58 season.

In August 1958 Derrek had trials with Chelsea and Wimbledon and at that time he living in Balham and working as an engineer. When nothing came of the trials, Derrek continued to play for Croydon Amateurs and on 7.3.59 he scored five times in a 9-1 win at Whyteleafe.

Derrek signed for Athenian League club Carshalton in August 1959 and by the end of January 1960 he d scored over 20 goals for them.

In the summer of 1960 Derrek was signed as an amateur by Queens Park Rangers and before the end of August 1960 he was given a professional contract having already impressed in reserve team outings. He went on to score 58 goals for QPR's youth, A and reserve teams during 1960/61, including one in a 2-1 win at Margate Reserves on 12.4.61, but he never made a first team appearance and was released at the end of the season.

Derrek joined Margate in the summer of 1961 and made his debut in a 1-0 defeat against Wisbech at Hartsdown Park on 19.8.61. He only made four more appearances during the early part of the 1961/62 season and scored just once - in a 3-0 Southern League Cup win at Gravesend & Northfleet on 30.8.61. However he did score four times in only two games for the reserves - all of the goals coming in a 7-1 win over Ramsgate Reserves on 2.9.61.

In October 1961 Derrek was transferred to Kettering of the Southern League Premier Division and he later played five times for Dartford during the 1962/63 season, scoring three goals.

He spent the 1963/64 campaign with Hastings before signing for Crawley in the summer of 1964.

Derrek later played for Cray and his stint with the club included the 1965/66 season.

name: Charlie Read
other clubs: Millwall (0), Ebbsfleet United, Bromley, Aveley and Redbridge
bio:
Defender who started his career at Millwall and played for the Lions youth team during the 2006/07 campaign. Charlie then featured regularly for the reserves during the 2007/08 and 2008/09 seasons.

In August 2009 he signed for Conference club Ebbsfleet but during the early part of 2009/10 Charlie still occasionally featured in Millwall s reserve team.

In October 2009 Ebbsfleet loaned him to Conference South outfit Bromley and shortly after Charlie returned to Stonebridge Road he was sent out on loan to Margate for a month.

He made his debut at centre-back on 5.12.09 as Margate drew 2-2 with Harrow in an Isthmian League Premier Division match at Hartsdown Park and Charlie then started three of the next four games. He made his last appearance in a 1-0 home defeat against Maidstone on 2.1.10 and then went back to Ebbsfleet.

Charlie didn t feature at all in the Fleet s first team during the remainder of 2009/10 and at the end of the season he left the club.

He joined Aveley of the Isthmian League Premier Division for the start of the 2010/11 campaign but in November 2010 Charlie moved on to Redbridge.

He featured in four Isthmian League Division 1 North games for Redbridge and then rejoined Aveley in December 2010.

Charlie ended 2010/11 having made a total of 19 league appearances (one as sub) for the Millers without scoring during his two spells with the club and stayed at Aveley for the start of 2011/12 too. He played eight times (twice as sub) in league matches before leaving the club towards the end of 2011 and dropping out of senior football.

name: Doug Read
other clubs: Stoneycroft, Chester City (0), Bath City, Oldham Athletic (0), Canterbury City and Ramsgate Athletic
bio:
Heavily built, 5' 11" tall keeper with an eccentric streak born in West Derby, Liverpool. Doug started his career with Liverpool-based junior club Stoneycroft who played in the curiously named I Zingari League - an amateur competition for local clubs. He made his first appearances for them during the 1936/37 season aged 19 and was a fixture in their side during 1937/38.
At the start of March 1938, Division 3 (North) club Chester offered Doug a trial and on 2.3.38 he played for their reserves in a 3-1 win over Winsford United. After he d played in another reserve team game against Buxton on 5.3.38, Doug was signed as a professional by Chester and played in their second string for the remainder of the 1937/38 campaign. A Cheshire Observer journalist described Doug as being "one of the best young goalkeepers I have seen for years". 
In July 1938 he was signed by Southern League club Bath having turned down an offer to stay at Chester. Doug had been named on their retained list but opted to move. Bath s new manager Alex Raisbeck had joined the club from Chester where he d signed Doug a few months earlier and the Bath Chronicle and Weekly Gazette described Doug as being "a player of great promise". He went on to make 48 appearances for Bath during the 1938/39 campaign.
In July 1939 Doug was signed by Oldham Athletic of Division 3 (North) and he played in their reserves before World War II interrupted his career.
At the start of the 1946/47 season Doug had a trial with Chelsea and in October 1946 he joined Margate. Doug made his debut on 12.10.46 in a 2-2 draw with Shorts Sports at Hartsdown Park, it was a Kent Senior Shield tie and he was already Margate's fourth keeper of the season. Doug went on to make the position his own during the remainder of the 1946/47 campaign. He made 31 appearances and impressed with his anticipation and consistency.  However in April 1947 his Margate career seemed over when he returned home to Liverpool to assist with his family's business. Doug initially said that he wouldn't be able to play for the club anymore but quickly changed his mind and returned after missing only one match. Margate finished the season as Kent League champions. 
Just before the start of the 1947/48 campaign, Doug had the misfortune to dislocate his shoulder and as a result he missed the first two months of the season.  That led to an amusing quote from player-manager Charlie Walker. Peter Hughes, one of Doug's temporary replacements in the Margate goal, had a poor game against Ramsgate on 25.10.47 and Walker said "Doug Read will be playing in goal next Saturday even if he has one arm in a sling." Sure enough, Doug did take to the field for Margate's next game at Hartsdown Park (against Chatham on 1.11.47) but he ran out with his arm still in a sling, much to the concern of the crowd.  However shortly before kick-off Doug removed it - it had been practical joke.
Doug went on to turn in some brilliant displays during the rest of the season, despite suffering a broken finger and a fractured rib, and he showed his sense of humour again in a home match against Maidstone on 1.5.48. Margate had already won the Kent League title so he frequently ran up field to join in with attacks during the match, playing as an extra centre-forward.  However Maidstone had the last laugh, running out 7-3 winners. In total Doug made 33 appearances during the season, keeping 13 clean sheets, and he was part of the side that beat visitors Ramsgate 2-1 to win the Kent League Cup Final on 6.5.48. Doug also featured as Margate won 4-1 at Gravesend & Northfleet on 8.5.48 to claim the Kent Senior Shield and complete a three trophy haul for the season.
His injury jinx continued during the 1948/49 campaign and on the opening day of the season - 21.8.48 - Doug was carried off before half-time of a home game against Gillingham Reserves after being knocked out. Later in the campaign he sustained another dislocated shoulder, fractured another rib, suffered concussion, cut his head and also had recurring leg problems.  His multiple ailments meant that Doug was rarely fit to play and he only appeared six times in total during the season. His final game for Margate was a Kent Senior Cup tie against Gillingham at Hartsdown Park on 5.2.49 which the Gills won 5-1. By then Ron Johnson had established himself as the first team keeper (he was cup-tied for the Kent Senior Cup) and in May 1949 Doug left the club and joined Canterbury. 
In the summer of 1950 he returned to Thanet to join Ramsgate. Doug made his debut on 31.8.50 as the Rams beat visitors Bowaters Lloyd 4-0 in a Kent League game at Southwood. He made a total of 14 appearances for Ramsgate before leaving the club at the end of the 1950/51 season. 
After his stint with Ramsgate, Doug lived in the Hemel Hempstead area and in 1957 he emigrated to Northern Rhodesia (now the Republic of Zambia). He lived in Ndola and played for the town football team. Doug also turned out for Ndola s cricket team, opening the batting and keeping wicket for them.
In 1972 he moved to Cape Town in South Africa along with his wife Alice (known as  Bunny ) who was from Margate, they d been married in Margate in 1948. Doug s son Chris (born in Margate in 1951) lived in Cape Town at the time.
In later years Doug lived near Perth in Australia and whilst recovering from a heart attack he wrote his autobiography which was published under the title  Get On With It . Doug died in Australia on 29.3.04 aged 86.

name: William Read
bio:
Born in Thorne, Yorkshire
Educated at Thorne Grammar School in Doncaster and University College, Durham. Gained a  blue  for football at university and also rowed and played cricket there. 
Had a keen interest in athletics throughout his life.
Moved to Margate in 1896 to become an assistant master at Stanley House School. Played football for Thanet Wanderers and then for Margate during 1896/97 and 1897/98. Also played cricket locally. Knee injury ended football career although he continued to play for Stanley House until 1916.
Later became joint headmaster at Stanley House alongside Mr Albert Cozens who was one of original Margate FC committee members in 1896. Took over as sole head when Mr Cozens retired in 1912.
Member of the standing committee of the Chamber of Commerce in Margate for many years and served as chairman and president at various times. Also part of the committee that organised annual Margate exhibitions and was a keen member of the Rotary Club, serving as vice-president for a spell than ended in 1933 due to pressure of work. Also a member of St. Paul s Church Council for many years.
 Still playing cricket for Stanley House in 1933
Son Rex Read took over as principal of Stanley House after his father s death. Rex was a well-known hockey player who played for Middlesex.
Died in Thanet 28.1.34 aged 59 after suffering a severe stroke from which he never regained consciousness. Funeral held at St. Paul s Church and former Margate player Reverend David Railton was one of the clergy that officiated, he was an old boy of Stanley House School.

name: Kevin Readings
other clubs: Dover Athletic, Canterbury City, Deal Town, Folkestone Invicta, Hythe Town, Sidmouth Town, Tiverton Town, Faversham Town and Whitstable Town
bio:
Dover-born keeper who started his career with his hometown club, joining them in the summer of 1996 shortly after leaving school. Kevin spent two seasons with Dover as a back-up player before signing for Margate in July 1997.

He made his debut in the opening match of the 1997/98 campaign as Margate beat Ramsgate 3-1 at Hartsdown Park to claim the Link Music Cup. Kevin played because first-choice keeper Lee Turner was unavailable. Kevin made one other senior appearance - in a 1-0 home win over Fisher on 25.11.97 and then spent the rest of the season in the reserves.

With Lee Turner in commanding form Kevin only managed one first team appearance during the 1998/99 campaign. He played in a 2-1 win over St.Leonards at Hartsdown Park on 27.3.99 and the Thanet Times said he had "nothing to do apart from take a couple of goal kicks". However the paper also noted that Kevin "looked nervous on the few occasions the ball came in his direction". At the end of the season he left the club.

Kevin joined Canterbury for the start of the 1999/00 campaign but moved to Deal a few weeks into the season and made two first team appearances there.

He spent 2000/01 with Folkestone and again played twice in the first team before returning to Dover for 2001/02.

Over the course of the next few years Kevin had several stints with Dover but as a Royal Marine his work commitments took priority over football.

During the 2004/05 campaign he managed six league appearances for Dover and towards the end of the season he moved on to Hythe. Kevin started 2005/06 with Hythe too but in February 2006 he signed for Dover once again and made four league appearances before the end of the 2005/06 campaign.

Kevin's next senior club was Sidmouth and in December 2006 he left them to join Southern Premier League outfit Tiverton.

In February 2007 he was stretchered off with a broken wrist as Tiverton lost 5-3 at Chippenham and the game was held up for eight minutes due to Kevin's injury. He stayed with the club until the end of the 2006/07 campaign.

In June 2008 Kevin returned to Kent when he joined Faversham but he left the club towards the end of the 2008/09 season and dropped out of senior football.

By 2012 he was working for Kent Police and in May of that year Kevin played for their football team as they lost 4-1 to Police Service of Northern Ireland in the Police Service UK Cup Final at Dartford's Prince's Park stadium.

In the early weeks of the 2012/13 campaign Kevin signed for Isthmian League Division 1 South club Whitstable.

He won many honours playing for the Royal Marines and Royal Navy.

name: Harry Reay
other clubs: Sunderland (0), Preston North End (1,0), Grimsby Town (1,0)
bio:

name: Martin Redpath
other clubs: Westgate Sports, Whitstable Town, Hungarian FC (Australia), Ukrainian Kiev (Australia), Azzuri (Australia), Kwinana United (Australia), Sittingbourne and Ramsgate
bio:
Thanet-born player who attended King Ethelbert School in Birchington and played for King Ethelbert Old Boys in the Thanet League during the 1958/59 season as a teenager.

Martin then played for Westgate Sports in the Kent Amateur League before joining Margate in February 1960. He scored on his debut for the reserves as they drew 1-1 at Bexleyheath & Welling on 13.2.60 and made a few more reserve team appearances before the end of the 1959/60 season.

Martin stayed with Margate for 1960/61 and made nine appearances for the reserves, scoring once, before emigrating to Australia with his parents and younger brother Michael on 11.1.61. The family moved as Martin s father had taken a job with Shell I.C.I. in Melbourne and Martin was quoted as saying I have enjoyed coming to Hartsdown and will miss it and the lads. I hope to keep playing when we get to Melbourne.

After arriving in Australia, Martin initially played for Melbourne-based Hungarian FC in the Victoria State League and he was selected for the Victoria State team. Martin then moved some 2,500 miles to Perth in Western Australia and continued his football career with Ukrainian Kiev in the Western Australia League. Martin was then signed by Azzuri for the substantial fee of £300 and whilst playing for them, he was chosen for the West Australia state side. Martin toured Victoria and South Australia with them.

In the summer of 1965 he returned to the UK and had a spell with Sittingbourne at the start of the 1965/66 campaign.

In the summer of 1966, Martin returned to Margate and after impressing in the reserves he made his first team debut on 14.1.67, playing in midfield in a 4-1 Southern League win at Wisbech. The local press said that he "came through...with flying colours". However Martin was really a centre-back and later featured in that position, making a total of six first team appearances before the end of the 1966/67 season. He was said to be one of the most enthusiastic trainers at the club. He left Margate once again in the summer of 1967.

Martin spent the 1967/68 campaign with Whitstable and stayed with them for the whole of the 1968/69 season too.

In the summer of 1969 Martin returned to Australia after completing a keyboard apprenticeship at Thanet Press and by 1972 he was captain of Kwinana United in the Western Australia League. Martin was awarded the Rothmans Gold Medal for being voted the best and fairest player in the state for 1972 and the Sunday Times of Perth referred to him as a "smiling colossus" and "soccer's no. 1 stalwart".

Martin later returned to the UK and played for Ramsgate Reserves during the 1977/78 season.

name: Matt Reed
other clubs: West Ham United (0), Barnet (4,0), Bristol City (0), Walton Casuals, Tonbridge Angels, Sittingbourne, Carshalton Athletic, Dartford, Metropolitan Police and Leatherhead
bio:
6' 1" tall keeper who was on West Ham s books from the age of ten and completed a scholarship with the club during the 2005/06 campaign. Matt featured in the Hammers reserves during the first half of that season and vied with future Margate keepers Darren Behcet and David Blackmore for a place in the side.

In January 2006 Matt was loaned to League Two club Barnet for the remainder of the 2005/06 campaign and on 25.2.06 he made his Football League debut in a 2-1 home defeat against Carlisle. He then started the Bees next three matches before dropping to the subs bench for the rest of the season.

At the end of 2005/06 Matt was released by West Ham at the same time as Darren Behcet.

In July 2006 Matt was signed by League One outfit Bristol City and during the opening weeks of the 2006/07 campaign he was an unused substitute for some first team matches but he left the club at the start of September 2006.

Matt then dropped into non-league football and joined Isthmian League Division 1 South club Walton Casuals. He made 38 league appearances for them during the remainder of the 2006/07 season.

In the summer of 2007 Matt had a trial with Conference outfit Crawley but he ended up signing for Tonbridge ahead of the 2007/08 campaign proper and made 58 appearances for the Isthmian League Premier Division club during the season.

After trials with Dartford and Bognor Regis in the summer of 2008 Matt joined Sittingbourne of the Isthmian League Division 1 South in September 2008 and made 43 appearances in all competitions for them during 2008/09.

He started the 2009/10 campaign with Premier Division Carshalton and Matt featured in the Robins first nine matches of the season before being released at the start of November 2009.

He then signed for Margate and on 7.11.09 Matt made his debut in a 2-1 defeat at Hastings in the Isthmian League Premier Division. In doing so he equaled an all-time club record by becoming Margate s sixth different keeper in six consecutive games. The Thanet Times said Matt made an excellent save" as an attacker bore down on goal in the second half and also praised him for a fingertip stop" from a close-range header.

Matt started 11 of the next 12 games and on 26.12.09 he saved a penalty from former Margate striker James Pinnock in a match against Maidstone at Ashford. Margate were 1-0 up at the time and Matt s save ensured the scoreline remained the same until the final whistle. He made his 12th and final appearance in a 2-0 defeat at Kingstonian on 31.1.10 and shortly afterwards Matt was injured whilst training with Barnet without Margate s permission. He was then released.

In February 2010 Matt joined Dartford as back-up for their first choice custodian Andrew Young but he didn t feature in the Darts first team during the remainder of 2009/10 as they won the Isthmian League Premier Division.

In the summer of 2010 Matt played in some friendlies for his old club Carshalton but he rejoined Sittingbourne in time for the start of the 2010/11 campaign.

He made 40 appearances (one as sub) for the Brickies in Division 1 South during the season before moving on to Metropolitan Police in July 2011.

Matt spent a few weeks with the Met but in September 2011 he returned to Sittingbourne once more. By the end of 2011/12 he d made a career total of 113 appearances for the club.

In the summer of 2012 Matt moved on to Leatherhead of Division 1 South and he made 12 league appearances there during the 2012/13 campaign.

name: Stuart Reed
other clubs: Folkestone Invicta, Folkestone, Canterbury City, Whitstable Town, Snowdown Colliery Welfare, St.Margaret's, Betteshanger Colliery Welfare, Dover Athletic and Sittingbourne
bio:
Folkestone-born defender who began his senior career with Folkestone Invicta at a time when they played in the Kent Amateur League.

Stuart later dropped into local football in the Folkestone area and was playing for a team called Nailbox when Folkestone FC (as opposed to Folkestone Invicta) signed him in March 1989.

He made his home debut in a 1-1 draw with Thanet United on 25.3.89 and stayed at Folkestone until the club went out of business in January 1991.

Stuart joined Margate after Folkestone's collapse and went on to make 11 reserve team appearances without scoring before the end of the 1990/91 campaign.

At the start of the 1991/92 season Stuart broke into Margate's first team, making his debut as a substitute in a 4-0 defeat at Hastings on 20.8.91. On 24.8.91 he made his full debut at centre-back in a 2-1 defeat at Baldock and Stuart then became a fixture in the heart of Margate's defence, usually partnering the experienced Mark Weatherly. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said Stuart was "outstanding" in a 0-0 draw with Dunstable at Hartsdown Park on 9.11.91 whilst the Thanet Times reported he was "in typically sound form" in a 0-0 home draw with Havant on 28.12.91. On 1.1.92 Stuart turned in what the Gazette called a "commanding" performance in a 1-0 win at Hythe and on 29.2.92 he scored his first goal for the club in a 5-0 thrashing of Erith & Belvedere at Hartsdown. He continued his good form as the season drew to a close and the Times said "he gave nothing away in the middle" in a 1-0 win at Newport IOW on 28.3.92. Stuart ended 1991/92 having made 48 appearances (one as sub), scoring once.

He struggled to gain a first team place during the opening weeks of the 1992/93 campaign and Stuart didn't appear until the sixth game of the season when he came on as a substitute in a 0-0 home draw with Corinthian in an FA Cup tie on 12.9.92. He then had a run in the side at right-back and scored with a low shot from well outside the penalty area as Margate beat Corinthian 4-0 in the replay on 21.9.92. After another spell on the sidelines Stuart broke back into the side in October 1992 and played five consecutive games in his favoured centre-back position in the absence of Billy Plews and Mark Weatherly who'd become Margate's first-choice centre-backs. When the experienced pair returned Stuart again found first team opportunities hard to come by and when he lined up for a home game against Bury on 19.12.92 it'd been eight matches since his last start. Unfortunately for Stuart he was sent off for a 'professional' foul before the end of the first half and after he'd played as a makeshift striker in a 5-1 defeat at Canterbury on 26.12.92 he had to serve a three match ban. After completing his suspension Stuart started featuring more regularly, although often as a substitute, and after playing at right-back in a 3-1 win at Burnham on 16.1.93 he appeared in 14 of Margate's last 18 games of the campaign. He usually wore the number two shirt but also played at left-back and in midfield. On 1.5.93 Stuart played his last game for Margate in a 1-1 draw at Dunstable and left the club at the end of the season having scored twice in 33 first team appearances (11 as sub). He also played 12 games for the reserves in the Kent Midweek League.

He joined Canterbury for the 1993/94 campaign and in October 1993 took over in goal when former Margate keeper Joe Radford went off injured during a 3-2 home defeat against Fisher. Stuart made over 30 appearances for City before moving to Whitstable in the summer of 1994.

He went on to make 65 appearances for Whitstable before leaving the club to rejoin his first club Folkestone Invicta in February 1996.

At the end of the 1996/97 season Stuart dropped into Kent County League football and had spells with Snowdown, St.Margaret's and Betteshanger before going back to Whitstable for the 1999/00 campaign.

In the summer of 2000 he joined Dover where he played exclusively for the reserves during 2000/01 and Stuart then joined Sittingbourne for the 2001/02 campaign, again only featuring in the reserves.

He later dropped into Sunday football and in 2007 Stuart was playing for a pub side in Dover aged 40.

name: Jim Regan
other clubs: Ramsgate
bio:
Well-built Thanet-born defender who attended Holy Cross School in Broadstairs and played for the Thanet Under-14 Schools team during 1977/78.

Jim began his career in local football during the 1978/79 season and had a trial at Nottingham Forest in the summer of 1980.

Jim then joined Ramsgate for the 1980/81 campaign and won the club's award for the best young player of the season. He also spent the 1981/82 & 1982/83 campaigns with the Rams.

Jim joined Thanet United for the 1984/85 season and played regularly for the reserves. He also made five first team appearances, making his debut in a Southern League Cup tie at home to Dover on 16.10.84 that United won 1-0. Jim impressed during his outings for the senior side and his display in a 1-1 draw at Addlestone & Weybridge on 15.12.84 prompted the Thanet Times to say that he was an "admirable deputy" for the injured Carl Scriven. Jim's aerial strength had particularly impressed the paper and he was referred to as being "an exceptional prospect in the making". He was later said to have "created an excellent impression" during a 5-3 home win over Addlestone & Weybridge on 9.2.85. That match turned out to be Jim's last senior appearance of the season and he then returned to the reserves. He was sent off playing for them in a game at Hastings on 16.3.85.

Jim started the 1985/86 campaign in United's first team and played in the first five matches of the season. The Isle of Thanet Gazette described him as being "redoubtable" and said that Jim was "outstanding" in a 2-0 home defeat at the hands of Welling on 3.9.85. A few days later, on 7.9.85, Thanet entertained Bromley in an FA Cup 1st Qualifying Round tie and the 2-2 draw turned out to be Jim's final game for the club. He left the Thanet area shortly afterwards.

Jim was back in Thanet by 1987 and during the 1987/88 campaign he played for local amateur club Margate Athletic.

During the 1990/91 season he returned to Hartsdown Park and made nine appearances for Margate's reserves.

name: Jamie Reilly
other clubs: Maidstone United (0), Ashford Town, Purfleet, Sudbury Town, Cambridge City, Chelmsford City, Canvey Island, East Thurrock United, Grays Athletic, Romford, Leyton Pennant and Aveley
bio:
Talented attacking player born in Corringham who started his career as a trainee at Maidstone when they were a Football League club.

In March 1991 Jamie was released by the Stones and joined Margate. He made his debut on the left wing in a 0-0 draw at Newport IOW on 29.3.91 and the Thanet Times said that he was "promising". Margate boss Tommy Taylor said he "did well...at 17 he looks set for a great future in the game." Jamie was then virtually ever-present up to the end of 1990/91, usually playing on the left wing but also featuring as a striker and right winger. On 27.4.91 he scored his first goal in a 3-2 win over Sudbury at Hartsdown Park with what the Thanet Times called "a splendid volley" and Jamie finished the season having made nine appearances, scoring once.

He performed well in Margate's friendlies ahead of the 1991/92 campaign, scoring three goals, and Jamie featured in nine of the first ten games of the new season although often as a substitute. When he started matches he usually played on the left wing. On 26.8.91 he scored his first goal of the campaign in a 2-2 draw with Ashford at Hartsdown but in October Jamie suffered an injury that kept him on the sidelines for around two months. Apart from a brief substitute appearance in a 2-0 defeat at Erith & Belvedere on 5.11.91 Jamie didn't feature in the first team for 14 matches played between 19.10.91 and 26.12.91. He returned to action when he wore the number seven shirt in a 0-0 home draw with Havant on 28.12.91 and the Thanet Times report on the game said that he "often flattered to deceive". Jamie kept his place on the right wing for Margate's next five matches and according to the Isle of Thanet Gazette he turned in "a five-star performance" in a 1-0 win at Hythe on 1.1.92. The paper described him as being "fleet-footed". On 4.1.92 Jamie scored what the Times said was "a fine goal" in a 3-1 defeat against Braintree at Hartsdown. The paper said his "fearsome left-footed volley fairly whistled into the far corner of the net". It was his second and last goal of the season. When he came on as a substitute in a 1-1 home draw with Buckingham on 8.2.92 it was Jamie's 19th appearance (six as sub) of 1991/92 and it turned out to be his final one for Margate. In March 1992 he was loaned to Ashford and Jamie played well for them in a 1-1 draw at home to Margate on 17.3.92. The Gazette said he was "often prominent" and shortly afterwards Jamie's transfer became permanent.

He was a thorn in Margate's side during 1992/93, scoring the only goal of the game as Ashford beat Margate 1-0 in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Homelands on 3.11.92 and finding the net again in a 4-0 win at Hartsdown Park on 8.12.92.

Jamie later had a loan spell at Purfleet before joining Sudbury in March 1994 for a fee of £4,000.

He went on to make over 100 appearances for Sudbury and also had another loan spell at Purfleet during 1995/96 and one at Cambridge City towards the end of 1996/97 before moving to Chelmsford for the 1997/98 season.

Jamie scored 16 goals in 42 appearances for Chelmsford during the 1997/98 campaign and his tally included the winner as City beat Margate 2-1 at home on 1.11.97. The Thanet Times report on the match said Jamie earnt the game's "star rating" for his "solo runs down the left".

He moved on to Canvey Island in the summer of 1998 and scored five goals before linking up with East Thurrock in February 1999.

Jamie scored ten goals in 15 league games for East Thurrock before the end of 1998/99.

His next move took him to Grays in the summer of 1999 and Jamie scored nine goals in 35 league appearances (18 as sub) during 1999/00 including all four in a 4-1 home win over Whyteleafe on 4.12.99. He also scored four cup goals. He started the 2000/01 campaign at Grays but after failing to score in six league appearances (three as sub) Jamie moved on to Romford in September 2000.

He scored once in six league appearances before signing for Leyton Pennant in October 2000 - his third Isthmian League club of the season in a third different division. Grays were in the Premier Division, Romford were in Division 1 and Leyton Pennant were in Division 2.

Jamie scored three goals in 23 league appearances (two as sub) for Pennant before the end of the 2000/01 campaign and then moved to Aveley in the summer of 2001.

During the 2001/02 season he scored nine goals for Aveley in 25 league appearances (three as sub) before a cruciate ligament injury ended his career in senior football at the age of 29.

Jamie later played some Sunday League football for Ockendon Motor Spares in the Circus Tavern Sunday League and in 2011 he was running his own electricians business and living in South Ockendon, Essex.

name: Ellis Remy
other clubs: Wimbledon (0), Hastings United, Lincoln City (0+2,0), Kettering Town, Grays Athletic, Redbridge, Braintree Town, East Thurrock United, Bromley, Staines Town, Harrow Borough, Folkestone Invicta, Welling United, Heybridge Swifts, Enfield Town, Bishop's Stortford, Potters Bar Town, Brentwood Town, Maldon & Tiptree, Aveley, Hemel Hempstead Town and Eastbourne Borough
bio:
6' 2" tall striker born in Hackney who started his career in Wimbledon's junior ranks before being released by the Dons at the end of the 2001/02 season.

Ellis joined Southern League Premier Division club Hastings United in the summer of 2002 aged 18 and scored five goals during the 2002/03 campaign.

In the summer of 2003 he played in some friendlies for Division 3 side Lincoln City and at the start of August 2003 Ellis was given a three-month contract by the Imps. He made his first team debut as a substitute in a 1-0 home defeat against Oxford United on 9.8.03 and Ellis also featured as a sub in a 1-0 defeat against Stockport in a League Cup tie at Sincil Bank on 12.8.03.

In September 2003 he was loaned to Kettering and played twice in the Isthmian League Premier Division for them, scoring in a 1-1 draw at Grays on 23.9.03.

After briefly returning to Lincoln Ellis was sold to Grays for a fee of £5,000 in October 2003 and the Imps manager Keith Alexander told Lincoln's official website "Ellis has signed for Grays and we'll be keeping an eye on his progress between now and the end of the season."

Ellis went on to score three goals for Grays during the remainder of the 2003/04 campaign but he was generally used as a substitute and left the club at the end of the season.

He started the 2004/05 campaign with Conference South outfit Redbridge and towards the end of 2004 Ellis signed for Braintree.

He scored nine goals from 25 Isthmian League Premier Division outings (11 as sub) for the Iron before the end of the 2004/05 before moving on again at the end of the season.

In August 2005 Ellis linked up with East Thurrock, also of the Premier Division, and the Rocks were asked to pay compensation to Braintree. East Thurrock's co-manager Lee Patterson told the club's website "The way Braintree have gone about this silly as they told Ellis he wasn't wanted yet want him to pay for his own release. I spoke to their Chairman and tried to come to a compromise, but got nowhere. The unfortunate one in all this is Ellis as being only 21 it meant he could not play anywhere until a club agree to settle with Braintree. The figure quoted to me was embarrassing so the FA can sort it now. Whatever happens now Ellis will at least have got away from there and can play again." He ended up only making three appearances (one as sub) without scoring for East Thurrock and in September 2005 Ellis signed for Margate. Manager Chris Kinnear said "He's still only 21, so he's got a little way to go, but we hope he's got goals in him."

Ellis made his debut in an Isthmian League Premier Division game against Fisher at Hartsdown Park on 6.9.05 and scored Margate's goal in a 1-1 draw. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "did really well" to lift the ball over the onrushing Fisher keeper and Ellis then started each of the next seven matches. He was on target again in a 4-0 home win over Cowes in the FA Cup on 10.9.05 and Ellis then made it back-to-back goals with a strike in a 2-2 draw with Slough at Hartsdown Park on 17.9.05.

He got his fourth goal for Margate to secure a 1-0 win over visitors Carshalton on 24.9.05 but after playing in a 3-0 home defeat against Cray in the FA Cup on 8.10.05 Ellis fell out of favour. He only featured as a substitute in the next three games but scored after coming on in a 2-1 defeat against Fisher at Dulwich on 24.10.05. Ellis then started Margate's next match - a 1-0 defeat against Braintree at Hartsdown Park on 29.10.05 - and kept his place for the three games that followed that before dropping back to the subs bench after a 1-0 home defeat against Dartford in the FA Trophy on 12.11.05.

Ellis made four substitute appearances in Margate's next six matches but after coming on in a 1-0 home defeat against Leyton on 10.12.05 he was released. Ellis had scored five goals from 19 outings (seven as sub) and Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "Unfortunately, things didn't click for Ellis, so it's probably best he finds another club."

Immediately after leaving Margate Ellis trained with Dagenham & Redbridge and in January 2006 he joined Isthmian League Premier Division club Bromley. Ellis made his debut in a 2-1 home defeat against Fisher on 17.1.06 and Bromley's joint manager Billy Smith told the Kentish Football website "I thought the boy Ellis done okay tonight, without looking as though he was going to score but he held the ball up well." Ellis scored four goals from ten appearances (one as sub) before moving on again in March 2006.

He looked set to rejoin East Thurrock after they made a seven-day approach to Bromley but at the last minute Staines stepped in and Ellis signed for them. He made seven Isthmian League Premier Division appearances (three as sub) for Staines without scoring before the end of the 2005/06 season.

On 12.8.06 Ellis played for Margate in a friendly at Dover but he was replaced at half-time and ended up linking up with Harrow for the start of the 2006/07 campaign proper. He made one sub appearance for them in a 1-0 win at Folkestone in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 19.8.06 and then joined Folkestone before the end of August 2006.

Ellis moved to Invicta as a non-contract player and Folkestone's manager Neil Cugley said "If he puts in positive performances when he gets the chance and scores some goals then he will create competition and I will make funds available to sign him". Ellis scored seven goals in 13 games for Folkestone, including a hat-trick in a 4-3 home win over Walton & Hersham on 7.10.06, but at the start of November 2006 he was released along with former Margate player Samuel Okikiolu as Folkestone couldn't afford to keep him.

Ellis and Okikiolu both joined East Thurrock and Ellis marked the first appearance of his second spell with the Rocks with a goal in a 4-1 home win over his old club Staines on 18.11.06. He played three more games without scoring before going back to Folkestone early in December 2006, barely a month after leaving the club, and Okikiolu also rejoined Invicta.

By the end of the 2006/07 campaign Ellis had scored 13 goals in all competitions for Folkestone and in the summer of 2007 he trained with Montserrat's international squad with a view to playing in their forthcoming World Cup qualifying campaign but nothing came of that at the time.

Ellis eventually left Folkestone in December 2007 after scoring six goals from 25 outings (12 as sub) during the early part of the 2007/08 season and he then linked up with Conference South club Welling.

Ellis spent the rest of campaign with the Wings and then left the club at the end of the season.

After featuring in some of Braintree's friendlies ahead of the 2008/09 campaign Ellis joined Heybridge for the start of the new season and made four Isthmian League Premier Division appearances without scoring before moving on to Enfield Town of the Isthmian League Division 1 North at the end of August 2008.

Ellis was on target on his debut for Enfield as they lost 3-1 in an FA Cup tie at Hillingdon on 30.8.08 and he went to score 13 goals from 29 appearances in all competitions before the end of 2008/09.

In the summer of 2009 Ellis linked up with Conference South club Bishop's Stortford and in September 2009 they loaned him to Potters Bar of the Isthmian League Division 1 North.

Ellis scored 13 goals from 22 outings for Potters Bar before returning to Bishop's Stortford in January 2010.

He signed for Isthmian League Division 1 North outfit Brentwood in the summer of 2010 and on 7.10.10 Ellis made his international debut for Montserrat in a Caribbean Cup Group B match against Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. Montserrat lost 7-0 and Ellis was sent off in the 68th minute after picking up two yellow cards. He didn't make another appearance in the tournament.

Ellis had scored 11 goals for Brentwood when he moved on to Maldon & Tiptree in February 2011 and the Isthmian League Division 1 North club's squad included several former Margate players including Dean Standen and Jack Haverson. Ellis scored twice from 11 league outings (one as sub) before the end of the 2010/11 campaign.

In the summer of 2011 he signed for Aveley of the Isthmian League Premier Division and they became the 20th different club Ellis had played for.

In January 2012 he moved on to Southern League Premier Division outfit Hemel Hempstead and in February 2012 Ellis joined Conference South side Eastbourne Borough where he finished the 2011/12 season before leaving the club.

In September 2012 Ellis played in all three of Montserrat s Caribbean Cup Group 3 matches in Martinique and on 9.9.12 he scored twice in a 7-0 win over the British Virgin Islands after coming on as a substitute with 20 minutes to go.

At the start of October 2012 Ellis returned to Eastbourne Borough and came off the bench to score in his comeback match - a 2-1 home defeat against Tonbridge on 2.10.12.

name: Mike Renshaw
other clubs: Blackpool (0), Dallas Tornado (USA) and Rhyl (Wales)
bio:
Manchester-born player who was on the books of Blackpool as a youngster, signing for them in 1963, and played for the club's youth team before dropping into amateur football.

In September 1967 Mike went to the USA having answered a newspaper advertisement for "top class young players to play professionally in the United States" and played for Dallas Tornado under former Margate player Keith 'Spud' Spurgeon.

Towards the end of 1968 the National American Soccer League (NASL) folded, temporarily as it turned out, and in December 1968 Mike returned to the UK. He joined Margate on trial along with his Dallas team-mate Brian Harvey who was the brother of Everton player (and later manager) Colin Harvey. The move was arranged by Keith Spurgeon. After scoring on his debut for the reserves, Mike made his senior bow on the right wing in a Southern League Cup tie against Ashford at Hartsdown Park on 23.12.68 but it was his only appearance for Margate and he was released the very next day, along with Harvey. Mike then returned home to Manchester. The local newspapers reported that was due to the club being unable to find him a job locally but in 2004 Mike himself said that he "had an absolutely terrible game" in the 1-0 defeat.

After leaving Margate Mike joined Rhyl in the Welsh League, again along with Harvey, and stayed with them until the end of the 1968/69 season. By that time the NASL had restarted and Mike returned to the USA, rejoining Dallas where he played until 1975.

In 1970 Mike was chosen for the NASL 'All-Star' second team after making 23 appearances for Dallas, scoring five goals and being credited with five assists. In 1971 and 1972 he gained an 'honourable mention' when the all-star selections were made. His record for 1971 was 23 appearances, three goals and eight assists as Tornado won the NASL championship. Former Margate player Bob Moffat was also in the Tornado side. During the 1972 season Mike made 14 appearances, scored five goals and made three assists.

Mike also played six games for the USA national team before FIFA discovered that he was actually ineligible due to being a British citizen. He won two full caps against Poland and Bermuda in March 1973 and also played in four other matches that didn't count as 'full' internationals. They included a game against Lazio in Rome and matches against Germany and Poland Under-23's.

Knee problems forced Mike to retire in 1976 after he'd made over 120 appearances for Dallas but in 1977 he returned to the club as assistant to head coach (manager) Al Miller. Mike replaced Miller as the Tornado's head coach for the 1981 NASL campaign but he was sacked during the season in the midst of a 16 match losing streak.

He was still living in Dallas in 2004, a year in which Manchester United signed young American striker Kenny Cooper after Mike had recommended him. At that time Mike was in the antique furniture business, sourcing fine English furniture in North Texas for a London-based dealer.

In August 2005 Mike provided some more information about his unusual international career on the 'Big Soccer Board' website. He wrote "a bit disappointing that I'm only officially credited with two caps as I actually played six times (missed the game in Belgium due to a turned ankle) but as the other four were against Poland U23's (in Warsaw), Germany U23's (in Duisburg), Lazio (in Rome) and some Italian Serie B team the USSFA (as it was then) didn't count them as "full" internationals. Funny as hell though that I was selected, I guess they never bothered to check if I was eligible. It was only when the paperwork caught up with FIFA that the USSFA found out, although they might have started to get a clue when, upon returning to the States, resplendent in my USSFA blazer and having represented the USA, the INS detained me for three hours.....as my visa had expired."

Asked if he realised he wasn't actually eligible for the USA Mike said "of course I knew, I just figured 'what the hell, I guess they know what they're doing'. I LOVED playing for the USA."

Mike died in Dallas on 17.2.01 aged 72

name: Len Revell
other clubs: Luton Town (0) and Ashford Town
bio:
Long-serving player who grew up in Thanet and first appeared for Margate during the 1946/47 season, the club's first after re-forming following World War II. Len spent the majority of the campaign in the reserves but also made two first team appearances. He made his debut on 16.11.46 when Margate beat Snowdown 5-1 in a Kent League game at Hartsdown Park but had to wait until 10.5.47 for his other first team opportunity.

Len featured more regularly during the 1947/48 campaign, making nine first team appearances. He had to wait until 26.12.47 for his chance but finished the season with a run of six matches to establish himself.

On 21.8.48, Len played at centre-back as Margate opened the 1948/49 campaign with a 1-1 draw against Gillingham Reserves at Hartsdown Park. Shortly afterwards, he was signed by 2nd Division Luton as an amateur and he played for their Colts side before returning to Margate in November 1948.

Len made his comeback in the number five shirt as Margate lost 3-2 at Lloyds Paper Mills on 27.11.48 and by the end of the season he d made a total of 18 appearances at centre-back or left-back. Len scored one goal during the campaign, a remarkable lob from just inside his own half in a 5-3 win over Canterbury at Hartsdown Park on 4.12.48 - the City keeper was future Margate star Peter Peters. Len also came to the attention of several Football League clubs during the season and played trial games for Leyton Orient. He also represented Kent.

In the summer of 1949, Len signed for Ashford and he stayed there until December 1951 when he rejoined Margate.

Len made his first appearance as Margate drew 2-2 at Betteshanger on 12.1.52 and he was ever-present at centre-back until the end of the 1951/52 season, making a total of 15 appearances without scoring.

Len was a fixture in the side during the 1952/53 season, making 40 appearances without scoring, and on 9.5.53 he was part of the side that drew 1-1 with visitors Folkestone to share the Kent Senior Shield.

The 1953/54 season was a nightmare for Len as he broke his ankle in a game against Betteshanger at Hartsdown Park in September 1953. Len didn't make another first team appearance during the season although he played a few times for the reserves towards the end of the campaign.

Len also spent almost the entire 1954/55 season in the reserves, only getting a first team chance in April 1955 when regular centre-back Brian Moffatt was injured. Len then went on to play in most of the season's remaining games and finished up with 11 first team appearances to his credit.

However he found himself back in the reserves for the whole of the 1955/56 season.

The 1956/57 campaign was another in which Len failed to make a single first team appearance and he only played twice for the reserves during the season. That was due to him suffering from a serious chest complaint which saw him hospitalised several times.

However he eventually recovered his health and spent the 1957/58 season in the reserves, making just one first team appearance.

The 1958/59 season turned out to be Len's last at Margate and once again he spent most of it in the reserves. However on 17.1.59 he made a rare appearance for the senior side when he played in 5-3 defeat at Dartford. It was a Kent Senior Shield tie and Len also made one more first team appearance during the season. His final match for the club was on 22.4.59, a 3-3 Kent League draw at Tunbridge Wells - 13 and a half years after his first. At the end of the campaign Len was released.

He continued to play local football and during the 1960/61 season Len turned out for Old Centrals.

He also played cricket locally and in June 1968 Len took nine for 20 when bowling for St. Andrew s in an away game against Kingsnorth. He was still playing cricket for Westgate in the summer of 1973 aged 45.

Len later became a well-known local bowls player.

His son Keith played for Margate s reserve side during the 1977/78 season.

Len died on 16.7.01 aged 73 and had still been living locally at the time. His ashes were scattered on the pitch at Hartsdown Park. An article in the Isle of Thanet Gazette marking Len's passing described him as "a multi-talented sportsman" and a "key player" for Margate in the years after the Second World War. Len's widow June told the paper "He was very modest and didn't talk much about what he'd achieved apart from to people who he'd actually played with. They were all happy days, and he always played just for the love of sport."

name: Alex Rhodes
other clubs: Newmarket Town, Norwich City (0), Yeovil Town (0), Ipswich Town (0), Brentford (22+43,6), Swindon Town (0+4,0), Grays Athletic, Bradford City (11+19,3), Rotherham United (23+4,3), Woking, Oxford United, Braintree Town and Canvey Island
bio:
5 9" tall left-sided attacker born in Cambridge who started his career with Eastern Counties League outfit Newmarket where he was known as Tiger . Alex progressed through the club s junior ranks and made his first team debut during the 1999/00 season.

During the 2002/03 campaign Alex scored 30 goals from just 34 outings for Newmarket and his tally included four goals in a 7-1 win over Ely in the Cambridgeshire Invitation Cup in January 2003.

At the start of the 2003/04 season Alex scored hat-tricks in three successive games which brought him to attention of Football League clubs.

In September 2003 he had a trial with Norwich and played for the reserves as they lost 2-1 at home to Northampton on 24.9.03.

In October 2003 Alex had further trials at Yeovil - where he scored for the reserves in a 9-0 win over Frome - and Ipswich where he featured in a reserve team match against Derby.

His next trial was at Brentford and Alex then played for Yeovil s reserves again in a game against Plymouth. He was widely expected to join Yeovil but in November 2003 it was Brentford who secured Alex s services for a fee of £7,500. A few days before his transfer was confirmed Alex scored a hat-trick in his last match for Newmarket as they beat visitors Great Yarmouth 4-3.

He had some injury problems during his early weeks at Brentford but on 26.12.03 Alex made his first team debut as an 85th minute substitute in a Division 2 (later League One) game against Bristol City at Griffin Park. The visitors won 2-1. He featured twice more as a sub during the remainder of the 2003/04 season and in the second of those outings on 8.5.04 Alex scored the only goal of the game as Brentford beat visitors AFC Bournemouth. It was a crucial strike as it ensured the Bees avoided relegation.

In the summer of 2004 Alex scored a hat-trick in a friendly at his old club Newmarket that had been arranged as part of his transfer deal and on 7.8.04 - the opening day of the 2004/05 campaign - he scored after coming on as a substitute for Brentford in a 3-1 defeat at Chesterfield. Alex finally made his full debut for the Bees in a 2-0 defeat at Ipswich in the League Cup on 24.8.04 and future Margate player Ryan Peters also made his full debut for Brentford in the tie. Alex finished 2004/05 having scored four times in 28 senior outings, many of them as a substitute.

He scored once from 18 first team appearances for the Bees during 2005/06 and at the start of the 2006/07 season Alex featured in 12 matches before being loaned to Swindon in October 2006.

He made his debut as a substitute for Swindon as they beat visitors Grimsby 3-0 in a League One game on 14.10.06 and Alex then played three more times as a sub before going back to Brentford in November 2006.

After returning to Griffin Park he made three further senior appearances but after coming on as a substitute in a 1-0 defeat at Port Vale on 16.12.06 Alex fell out of favour and didn t feature again in Brentford s first team before being loaned to Conference outfit Grays in March 2007.

He made his debut for the Essex club as a substitute in a 1-0 home defeat against Stevenage in the FA Trophy on 10.3.07 and Alex went on to score twice from a total of 14 outings (seven as sub) up to the end of April 2007.

On 5.5.07 he made his final appearance for Brentford when he came on as a substitute in a 3-1 defeat at Tranmere and after rejecting a new contract Alex was released at the end of the 2006/07 season.

In the summer of 2007 he signed for Bradford City and Alex made his debut in a 1-1 draw with visitors Macclesfield in League Two on 11.8.07. He scored his first goal for the Bantams in a 2-1 home win over Chester on 6.11.07 and by the end of the 2007/08 campaign Alex had scored three times in 30 appearances (19 as sub). He was released by Bradford at the end of the season.

In June 2008 Alex linked up with League Two club Rotherham and made his debut in a 1-0 win over visitors Lincoln on 9.8.08. In his next outing on 12.8.08 he scored the opening goal of the game in a 2-2 draw at Sheffield Wednesday in the League Cup that Rotherham won 5-3 on penalties. Alex featured regularly for the next few months but after he d played in a 2-0 home win over Macclesfield on 31.1.09 he dropped out of the first team picture.

In March 2009 Alex was loaned to Conference club Woking and made his debut for the Cards in a 1-1 draw with visitors Wrexham on 14.3.09. He played twice more (once as a substitute) and on 11.4.09 Alex scored in a 2-0 win at Forest Green which was his last outing for Woking.

At the end of the 2008/09 campaign he was released by Rotherham having scored three times in 27 appearances (four as sub) in all competitions.

In July 2009 Alex signed for Oxford United and his first outing for them was as a substitute in a 2-1 home win over York in the Conference on 8.8.09. He played twice more as a sub before being released at the end of October 2009.

At the start of November 2009 Alex joined Conference South outfit Braintree and in January 2010 he was on the move again, going back to Grays for a second spell there.

He spent the remainder of the 2009/10 season with Grays and made 15 Conference appearances (three as sub) without scoring there before being released.

In July 2010 Alex trained with AFC Sudbury and then had a trial with Hereford but shortly after the start of the 2010/11 campaign he signed for Isthmian League Premier Division club Canvey Island.

Alex went on to score 22 goals from 91 appearances (eight as sub) in all competitions for Canvey during 2010/11 and 2011/12 before joining Margate in July 2012.

He signed a one-year contract and Margate s Chief Executive Officer Cliff Egan said Alex is a player that our manager Chris Kinnear has had his eye on for a while. We re highly delighted to have signed him. He has plenty of experience in the Ryman League and above and as a goal-scoring left-winger, with a good goal to games ratio, I m sure our supporters will be excited about his signing."

Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette Alex is a quality player and has been on my radar for a while. He performed really well against us for Canvey last season and I was keen to get him in."

Alex scored in a 4-0 friendly win over Erith & Belvedere at Welling on 21.7.12 and then made his competitive debut on the left wing as Margate beat Hendon 2-0 at Hartsdown Park in the opening Isthmian League Premier Division game of the season on 18.8.12. He also started the following game - a 2-2 draw at Hastings on 21.8.12 - but Alex was then an unused substitute for Margate s next two matches.

He was back in the side for a 2-0 win at Bognor Regis on 1.9.12 but after that Alex only featured twice as a sub in the next five games. On 22.9.12 he came off the bench to score his first goal in an FA Cup tie at Aveley that Margate won 4-1.

His next outing came on 2.10.12 as Margate entertained Sittingbourne in a Kent Senior Cup tie and the match marked Alex s first start for over a month. He scored a hat-trick in a 6-1 win and afterwards Alex told Margate s website It was a good game; not just for myself, but for all the other boys that haven t been involved (in previous matches). It was a nice chance for everyone just to express themselves and show the manager and everyone else that they want to enjoy their football, and play at a high intensity and I think a lot of the boys were happy when they came off."

Alex also said he d been frustrated about not starting matches and explained It s hard when you feel you re not contributing a lot, because you want to be on the pitch. Unfortunately for a few of us, because the team are playing so well, we ve had to wait for our chance."

For the next few months Alex was a fixture in Margate s matchday squad but he was mostly used as a substitute. On 8.12.12 he scored his fifth goal of the season in a 2-0 home win over Wingate & Finchley after coming off the bench but there was an element of fortune about Alex s effort as his free-kick from way out on the right wing drifted into the net.

He came on early in the second half of Margate s next game - a home match against Carshalton on 11.12.12 - and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Alex made a huge impact from the bench" by setting up two second half goals in a 3-1 win. The paper said he did brilliantly down the right" in the build-up to Margate s second goal - a 25-yard effort from Mark Corneille - and Alex then put in a low cross that Matt Bodkin backheeled into the net.

He made another big impression as a substitute on 9.2.13 as Margate took on high-flying Whitehawk at Hartsdown Park. Alex came on a few minutes into the second half and proceeded to score both goals to give Margate a 2-1 win. Both his strikes were impressive efforts from distance. Alex then started the following match - a 1-0 defeat at Lowestoft on 12.2.13 - but resumed his substitute duties for the next four games after that.

On 23.2.13 he again scored after coming on as a substitute as Margate beat visitors Hampton & Richmond 2-1 and that was the fifth goal Alex had managed after starting on the bench. Caretaker assistant manager Simon Osborn spoke to Margate s website about him and said He brings a goal threat for you and he s good in the air. He s a little frustrated, he wants to start and that s understandable; I d be disappointed if he wasn t but when he s come on he s made an impact which is vitally important as a squad player."

On 26.2.13 Alex featured once again as a substitute in a 2-0 home win over Leiston but that turned out to be his final appearance for Margate. He then drifted away from the club citing work commitments having scored eight times in 26 outings (16 as sub).

name: Clive Richards
other clubs: Aberkenfig (Wales), Tondu Robins (Wales), Edgware Town, Wembley and Bridgend Town (Wales)
bio:
Welsh centre-forward born in the village of Tondu, Bridgend who attended Bridgend Grammar School and started his football career with local club Aberkenfig during the 1949/50 season. Clive was picked as reserve for the Welsh junior side around that time.

He was also a talented cricketer and in 1951 Clive captained Wales schoolboys side in a match against England at Old Trafford, scoring 63 in his innings. In the summer of 1952 he played cricket for Maesteg Celtic and scored a century for them in a match against Briton Ferry in May 1952.

During the 1952/53 and 1953/54 football seasons Clive played for Tondu Robins of the Llynfi and Garw Association League.

After his work as a teacher saw him relocate to the Wembley area, Clive joined Edgware Town of the Corinthian League during 1956/57 and started playing cricket for Wembley in the summer of 1957.

Clive spent the 1957/58 season with Edgware too before signing for Margate in April 1958.

He made his debut in a 3-1 win over Bexleyheath & Welling at Hartsdown Park on 21.4.58 but it was his only appearance. Clive s work as a school teacher in Hendon meant he found it difficult to get time off to travel to play football.

Clive rejoined Edgware for the 1958/59 campaign and in June 1959 he scored a century for Wembley in a match against Luton.

He spent the 1959/60 football season with Wembley too and they were in the Corinthian League at the time. Clive stayed with Wembley for 1960/61 but in August 1961 he returned home to Wales, shortly after completing 1000 runs for Wembley during the cricket season.

Clive signed for Welsh League club Bridgend ahead of the 1961/62 campaign and also played for them during 1962/63.

In later years Clive returned to England and in 1972 he was headmaster of the Heart of England High School, Balsall Common, Coventry.

name: Bob Ritchie
other clubs: Craigton Athletic (Scotland), Kirkintilloch Rob Roy (Scotland), Rickmansworth Town, Watford (1,0) and Leavesden Hospital
bio:
5' 10" tall Glasgow-born striker who played his first football as a pupil at North Kelvinside Secondary School in the city.

During World War II, Bob served in the 51st Highland Division of the Royal Army Ordnance Corps and played for his unit in the Western Desert. He also turned out for a divisional team in a game against Poland that took place in Germany. In the midst of the conflict, Bob featured in Scotland for Craigton Athletic before signing for Kirkintilloch Rob Roy in July 1943. They released him at the end of the 1942/43 season.

After the war ended, Bob moved to England and joined Hertfordshire non-league outfit Rickmansworth. He came to the attention of 3rd Division (South) club Watford who signed him in February 1948.

Bob was a part-time player for the Hornets and only made one first team appearance - in a 3-1 defeat at Port Vale on 8.1.49 - before being released by Watford at the end of the 1949/50 campaign having spent over two years with the club.

He joined Margate in August 1950 and at the time manager Almer Hall described him as being "a 100% team man who can't be a stooge." Bob made his debut in a 3-0 defeat at Snowdown on 23.8.50 - the opening day of the 1950/51 season and the first match of Hall's long reign as manager. Bob also played in Margate's next game - a 2-1 defeat against Ashford at Hartsdown Park on 2.9.50 - before leaving the club.

He later had a spell with Hertfordshire outfit Leavesden Hospital that started in September 1952 and in 1956 Bob was elected as captain of Rickmansworth Golf Club.

He died in 2017 at age of 97.

name: Arthur Roberts
other clubs: Walton & Hersham, Aldershot (0), Tonbridge, Ramsgate Athletic and Chertsey Town
bio:
Energetic player born in Aldershot who was universally known as 'Digger' although his given name was Arthur. He started his career with Walton & Hersham as an amateur before signing professional forms for Aldershot aged 17.

Digger s career there was halted by his National Service and he joined Tonbridge when he was demobbed. Digger spent two seasons with the Angels before joining Margate prior to the start of the 1959/60 campaign. He was working as a sheet metal worker at the time.

He made his debut for the club in a 7-0 Southern League Cup win over Dover at Hartsdown Park on 3.9.59 and went on to make 30 appearances as a winger or inside forward during a season in which he had several lengthy spells out of the first team. On 14.11.59 Digger played in a 1-1 draw at Kettering in the FA Cup 1st Round and he also featured in the replay at Hartsdown Park on 19.11.59 that Margate won 3-2. He was then part of the side that drew 0-0 with visitors Crystal Palace in the 2nd Round on 5.12.59 but didn t play in the replay at Selhurst Park.

On 30.3.60 Digger scored a hat-trick for Margate s reserves as they beat Betteshanger 4-3 at Hartsdown and he then enjoyed a good run in the senior side, featuring in each of the last 13 games of the season. On 23.4.60 he found the net with a brilliant 25 yard strike in a 1-1 draw at Dover in the Southern League. Digger ended the campaign having scored four first team goals and, looking back at the season, the East Kent Times said that "he proved a good utility player...and never gave a bad showing".

After a few early season domestic problems, Digger established himself during 1960/61 and made 34 appearances. He scored four goals including a stunning solo effort in a 3-2 win over Poole at Hartsdown on 15.4.61. Digger set off on a mazy run from the halfway line and beat two players before lashing home. However it turned out to be his last goal for Margate as he was released at the end of the season. He'd been constantly barracked by supporters during home matches and had struggled on the left wing for much of the season, mainly due to being right-footed.

After a few months out of the game, Digger joined Ramsgate in October 1961. He was a regular scorer for the Rams during 1961/62 and found the net in a 2-1 defeat at Margate in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie on 6.11.61. He was also sent off 15 minutes from the end of a 0-0 draw at Trowbridge on 13.1.62 after kicking out at an opponent.

Digger left Ramsgate in the summer of 1962 and underwent a cartilage operation before returning to Aldershot, playing almost exclusively for their reserves during the early part of the 1962/63 season. In January 1963 he returned to Margate on trial, hoping to come back on a permanent basis.

Digger made his first appearance on 9.2.63 as Margate beat Nuneaton 3-1 at Hartsdown Park but he only played once more before being released.

During the 1963/64 season he was playing for Metropolitan League club Chertsey and scored twice in their 5-2 home win over Margate Reserves on 8.2.64. He was still at Chertsey during 1965/66.

Digger s son Kieron later played non-league football for various sides that included his father s old club Chertsey.

name: Jack Roberts
other clubs: Tottenham Hotspur (0), Northfleet Amateurs, Northfleet United, Chelmsford City, Canterbury Waverley, Ashford Town, 12th I.T.C. (Canterbury), Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Ramsgate Athletic, Sittingbourne, Canterbury City and Betteshanger Colliery Welfare
bio:
Hard tackling, 5' 11" tall defender born near Hersden in the Canterbury area who played for Sturry School and the Canterbury district's school side before joining the groundstaff at Tottenham in August 1933 aged 14.

Jack performed various chores around White Hart Lane as well as playing for the club's youth sides and Spurs sent him to their junior 'nursery' club Northfleet Amateurs for the 1935/36 campaign.

At the start of the 1936/37 season Jack made four appearances for Spurs' reserves before joining the club's senior nursery side Northfleet United for the bulk of the 1936/37 campaign. Northfleet won the Kent League and Kent League Cup and at the end of the season Jack made another appearance for Spurs' reserve side, helping them to win the London Challenge Cup by beating Arsenal Reserves 1-0 on 3.5.37.

Jack went back to Northfleet for 1937/38 and the club won the Kent Senior Cup as well as retaining the Kent League Cup.

In the summer of 1938 Ipswich tried to sign him ahead of their first season in the Football League but Northfleet held Jack's registration by that time and refused the offer. They gave him a professional contract for the 1938/39 campaign but after an injury-ravaged season he moved on to Chelmsford in May 1939.

Jack's spell with the Essex club was very brief and he joined Canterbury Waverley for the start of 1939/40 but when World War II broke out a few weeks later he signed up for the army. He saw service in Africa and Burma during the conflict and Jack was seriously wounded but happily recovered. He played football for various regimental teams as well as making appearances in wartime games for Ashford (during 1940/41 and 1941/42), 12th I.T.C. (Canterbury) and Snowdown Colliery Welfare (during 1944/45).

Jack joined Ramsgate of the Kent League at the end of November 1945 and then rejoined Chelmsford in February 1946. He helped them secure the Southern League title and Southern League Cup before signing for Margate in March 1947.

Jack made his debut at right-back in a 3-0 win at Sittingbourne in the Kent League on 15.3.47 and became a fixture in the side during the remainder of the 1946/47 season as Margate won the Kent League title. He made 12 appearances and gained a reputation as a solid full-back who was hard for wingers to pass.

During the 1947/48 campaign Jack was virtually ever-present, always wearing the number two shirt, and made a further 43 appearances as Margate retained the Kent League title. He never grabbed the headlines but Jack was a rock in Margate's defence. On 6.5.48 he was part of the side that beat visitors Ramsgate 2-1 to win the Kent League Cup Final and on 8.5.48 Jack also featured as Margate won 4-1 at Gravesend & Northfleet to claim the Kent Senior Shield, completing a three trophy haul for the season.

Shortly after the end of the 1948/49 campaign he was approached by Sittingbourne to become their player-manager but Jack initially turned the offer down. However he soon changed his mind and left Hartsdown Park to take charge of the Brickies in the summer of 1948.

Jack resigned as Sittingbourne's manager in December 1948 and joined Canterbury City as a player, ironically making his debut in a 1-0 defeat at Margate on 25.12.48.

In February 1950 Jack rejoined Margate and played at left-back for the remainder of the 1949/50 season, making a total of 11 appearances.

He made a further 32 appearances during the 1950/51 campaign and at that time Jack worked as an ice cream man from his own van. He left the club at the end of the season and became player-coach at Betteshanger Colliery Welfare. Jack continued in that role until retiring in 1952.

After his career had ended Jack worked in the insurance business and also played various other sports to a good standard - darts, cricket, golf and bowls.

In 1999 he was interviewed for Tottenham's 'Spurs Monthly' magazine and at that time Jack was aged 80 and living in Leigh-on-Sea, Essex. Jack said that he still followed Spurs' fortunes with interest and he was still playing indoor bowls regularly.

He died in Leigh-on-Sea, Essex on 28.3.00 aged 81.

name: George Robertson
other clubs: Ashton National, Manchester City (14,0), Cambuslang Rangers (Scotland), Southend United (43,0), Chesterfield (2,0)
bio:
Born Failsworth, Manchester. 
Ashton then to Man City for 27/28, last there 32/33.  
Cambuslang Rangers next 
Joined Southend from Cambuslang Rangers in June 1933.  There 33/34 and 34/35 
Chesterfield 35/36 
then us for 36/37  Capt of 36/37 KSC winning side.  Also Margate's trainer during 37/38.
January 1939   joined Folkestone, not sure where playing before that
Returned - captain and player-coach - as one of two full-time pros signed by Bill Fogg for start of 39/40 and new MFC // served in National Fire Service during WWII //
Ramsgate Athletic (KL) captain and manager 45/46 and was still in NFS initially, awaiting release from service // Ramsgate player manager 46/47 (retired as player by end 1947) and 47/48. Manager 49/50 when Ramsgate Athletic won KL.
Still Rams boss 1950/51 and on 3.2.51 he made an emergency appearance   playing on the left wing in a 2-2 draw at Tunbridge Wells in the Kent League, he was 46 at the time. Played again in 0-0 at Sheppey on 19.4.51.
Replaced as manager by Charlie Walker on 12.5.51 but stayed on at Rams as trainer / coach / groundsman
Stayed with Rams right through until leaving in May 1961, manager by then Walter Rickett
Died March 1984 in Manchester
