name: Les Strowger
other clubs: Arsenal (0), Cheltenham Town, Windsor & Eton, Reading (0), Canterbury City, Tonbridge and Chatham Town
bio:
6' 0" tall defender born in Godstone, Surrey who played for local junior side Bandon Hill Old Boys during 1937/38. They were based in Wallington, Surrey.

Les started his senior career with Arsenal and was with the Gunners during the 1945/46 campaign. Towards the end of that season he played in a friendly at Cheltenham.

In the summer of 1946, Arsenal loaned Les to Cheltenham and he featured in their Southern League side during the first half of the 1946/47 campaign.

Having been released by Arsenal, Les signed for Windsor & Eton of the Corinthian League towards the end of 1946.

In the summer of 1947 he signed amateur forms for Reading and Les made his debut in their reserves as they beat Crystal Palace 3-0 at Elm Park on 1.10.47.

Later in the 1947/48 campaign Les moved on to Canterbury and he went on to spend around 18 months with City. On 4.9.48 he scored from the penalty spot as Canterbury lost 3-1 at Margate in an FA Cup tie.

In March 1949 Les linked up with Tonbridge and spent the remainder of 1948/49 there.

In August 1949 he signed for Margate and Les made his debut in a 2-1 win over Betteshanger at Hartsdown Park on 20.8.49 - the opening day of the 1949/50 Kent League campaign. He proved to be a defensively sound player and made a total of 16 appearances during the season. Les usually played at right-back but also wore the number three shirt a few times. He left the club in April 1950 having fallen out of favour in the later stages of the campaign.

In the summer of 1951 Les signed for Kent League club Chatham.

He died in 2009 at the age of 89.

name: Jamie Stuart
other clubs: Charlton Athletic (60+3,3), Millwall (50+3,0), Bury (64+7,2), Southend United (30+3,0), Hornchurch, Grays Athletic, Rushden & Diamonds, AFC Wimbledon (38+1,1) and Sutton United
bio:
5 10  tall, born Southwark
Up through youth ranks at Charlton, signed pro in January 1995 aged 18
Debut at left-back in 2-0 defeat at Huddersfield in the old First Division (later the Championship) on 17.8.96
1st goal in 5th appearance when opened scoring in 2-0 win over Southend at The Valley 10.9.96
20.9.96 sent off 55 minutes into a 2-1 defeat at Ipswich after picking up two yellow cards
Few more apps after that but injured early in second half of a 4-1 defeat at Liverpool in League Cup on 13.11.96 and only one more first team app before end of season   in April 1997
 500,000 bid from Palace when at Charlton
England Under-18 (two caps) and Under-21 (four caps)
Two more first team apps start of 1997/98 but sub outing in 1-1 home draw with Birmingham in Division 1 turned out to be last.
November 1997 sacked by Charlton after failing drugs test - testing positive for cocaine and cannabis. He denied the charge, claiming that a cigarette he smoked had been laced with the cocaine. Given six-month ban by Football Association.
Signed by Millwall in July 1998. Debut in 1-0 win at Wigan on 8.8.98   Division 2 (later League One)
By end of 1998/99 he d featured in 43 senior games without scoring and was sent off twice
1999/00 regular to for first few weeks but then fell out of favour and only nine first team, last in January 2000
2000/01 only one sub appearance   in 1-1 home draw with Bristol City on 17.10.00. Released end of 2000/01
Trial with Cambridge United early in 2001/02
To Bury (Division 2) in October 2001   debut in Football League Trophy tie at Hartlepool 16.10.01, won 1-0 after extra time
Sent off in third outing for Bury   a 5-1 defeat at Brentford on 23.10.01
First goal 22.12.01 in 1-1 draw with Blackpool at Gigg Lane
15.1.02 sent off again in 0-0 draw with visitors Huddersfield
By end of season had made 28 first team apps, scoring once. Bury relegated
2002/03 regular again as Bury played in Division 3 (later League Two)   43 apps, 1 goal and two red cards. Second was in 0-0 draw with Bournemouth at Gigg Lane on 10.5.03 and turned out to be his last appearance
Southend (Division 3) summer 2003 as wanted to be nearer to family in London and regular until slight fracture of pelvis end of February 2004. Back in side mid-April 2004 and finished 2003/04 with 30+3, 0 and no reds for Southend. Released May 2004
June 2004 Hornchurch of Conference South   17 appearances before financial crisis saw most players leave
Nov 2004 Grays when Hornchurch bust   Steve West also went Hornchurch to Grays.
2004/05 Grays won Conf South and FA Trophy   Grays beat Hucknall on penalties after 1-1 draw at Villa Park
2005/06 Grays lost in Conference play-offs but retained FA Trophy with 2-0 win over Woking at Upton Park. Two red cards that season including one for punching team-mate John Nutter during 2-1 defeat at Canvey Island on 2.1.06 (**If plays for us along with Ashikodi then two players fielded who d both been sent off for incidents involving own players**)
2006/07 regular again in Conference and managed Grays for an Essex Senior Cup tie in October 2006. Won players, supporters and manager s player of year. End of season called up for National Game squad.
2007/08   22.9.07 sent off in 2-0 home defeat against York in Conference after an incident that left York player Chris Beardsley with a jaw broken in two places. October 2007 Jamie arrested by Essex Police and in December 2007 he was charged with grievous bodily harm.
Regular for Grays for rest of season and captain before the end of it.
September 2008 case went to trial and acquitted when jury accepted clash with Beardsley an accident after Jamie trying to free himself from Beardsley s hold
Became Grays  assistant manager end of January 2009
Over 200 apps for Grays
June 2009 signed for Conference side Rushden & Diamonds who were managed by former Grays boss Justin Edinburgh. Captain for 2009/10 and regular throughout, supporters player of season and named in Conference National  team of the year 
After making around 70 appearances for R & D Jamie signed for AFC Wimbledon in January 2011. Manager Terry Brown
21 Conf apps, one goal as helped them gain promotion to Football League after beating Luton on penalties in the Play-Off Final at City of Manchester Stadium on 21.5.11
Captain for AFC s first ever league season and on 6.8.11 he scored the club s first-ever goal in the Football League as they lost 3-2 at home to Bristol Rovers. Regular throughout and made total of 39 apps without scoring again. Last app was 5.5.12 in 3-1 win over Shrewsbury at Kingsmeadow and was last for club.
Released later in May 2012 and joined Conference South club Sutton as captain
Regular for Sutton 2012/13 and early 2013/14 
Early November 2013 interviewed by The Non-League Paper and at that time Jamie was managing Welling s youth team as well as playing for Sutton and working. Told paper  I m trying to hold down three jobs at the minute and it s tough. You ve got to earn money somehow and as you get older, there s not so much there in football. I feel I can play past 40, the way things are going at the moment. 
Looking back on drugs thing at Charlton etc  You go through life and you make mistakes - it s how you come back from them. The best thing I ever did was move up north (to Bury). I hadn t appreciated football when I was young at Charlton. I was more interested in my so-called friends. I left them all behind and started again. The ban made me more determined to play football. It really changed my outlook on life and the game. I wanted to earn a living out of it and, after that, I was 100 per cent dedicated. 
 Maybe I do have regrets, but I ve got a lot to give back. No-one grafts more than me and when there s young lads in the side, I want them to look at me as an example. I m always honest and open if ever anyone wants to ask me about anything that s happened in my life. I m not ashamed or embarrassed. You do things, but you ve got to get on with it and learn by them. I ve got nothing to hide. 
  four goals from 82 appearances in all for Sutton
Released by Sutton so he could join us as player-coach in December 2013, teaming up with old AFC Wimbledon boss Terry Brown. First Margate signing for Brown
Manager Paul Doswell explained ''We had an enquiry from Terry and his assistant Stuart Cash about Jamie, and while we're sorry to see him leave it would have been wrong to deny him a great opportunity, as he will be involved in the coaching and it is logically the next step in his career. I'd like to thank him for being a great skipper for me and a good person, highly thought of among all the management and playing staff, and we wish him well. There aren't many of his ilk left, and he's someone I can still relate to.''

name: Dan Stubbs
other clubs: Ebbsfleet United, Whitstable Town, Wivenhoe Town, Maidstone United, KA Akureyri (Iceland), Thurrock and Hythe Town
bio:
Energetic Maidstone-born midfielder who started his career in Conference club Ebbsfleet s youth set-up. Dan was given a first team squad number for the 2007/08 campaign and in October 2007 he was loaned out to Whitstable.

Dan played alongside future Margate loanee John Akinde for the Oystermen and made ten appearances (three as sub) in the Isthmian League Division 1 South, scoring once in a 3-3 draw at Corinthian Casuals on 16.10.07.

In February 2008 Dan began a loan spell with Wivenhoe of the Isthmian League Division 1 North at the same time as future Margate player Lee Maskell was farmed out to the club by Ebbsfleet. Dan made eight appearances (four as sub) without scoring before returning to Stonebridge Road in March 2008.

After going back to Ebbsfleet he featured in some Kent Senior Cup ties which included a 4-1 win at Margate on 26.3.08. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said Dan was "excellent" and "the best player on the pitch".

In the summer of 2008 he signed for Margate after being released by Ebbsfleet and Dan played in most of Margate s pre-season matches, scoring what the Isle of Thanet Gazette described as a "cracker" from 25 yards in a 1-1 draw at Whitstable on 22.7.08. Manager Barry Ashby told the paper "It was a great strike, a half-volley on the left foot, but that s what he s capable of. I don t think we ve seen the best of him yet because he s tried to do too many people s jobs. If he sees someone out of position, he ll try and help out, where he s such an honest and nice lad. He needs to be a bit more selfish and think about his own position more."

Dan made his competitive debut aged 19 in a 2-1 defeat at Carshalton in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 16.8.08 - the opening day of the 2008/09 campaign - and the Thanet Times said he "worked his socks off in midfield". He was a fixture in the side for the next few months and on 4.10.08 Dan scored his first goal in a 3-2 defeat against Hastings United at Hartsdown Park. He thumped home a half-volley from 25 yards and the Thanet Times said it was "a hell of a strike".

Dan got his second goal of the season in a 3-2 defeat at Billericay on 1.11.08 and started each of Margate s first 18 matches in midfield up to and including a 2-0 defeat at Horsham on 8.11.08. After that he had a run of just three starts from 12 games although he was used as a substitute seven times in that period. He came off the bench to score with a left footed volley from the edge of the penalty area in a 2-1 home defeat against Staines on 29.11.08 and after wearing the number seven shirt in a 2-0 win over visitors Ashford (Middlesex) on 24.1.09 Dan was ever-present for the remainder of the campaign.

On 28.2.09 he played at left-back in a 2-0 defeat at Wealdstone and Dan made a few more appearances in that role during the closing months of the season. He was back in midfield on 13.4.09 as Margate beat rivals Ramsgate 1-0 at Hartsdown Park and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "showed plenty of energy". The Thanet Times then described Dan as "a proper terrier in midfield" in its report on a 2-0 home win over Sutton on 18.4.09 and he ended the campaign having scored three goals from 44 outings (seven as sub) as Margate finished in the relegation zone of the Isthmian League Premier Division.

Dan was included on Margate s retained list for the 2009/10 season but in July 2009 manager Terry Yorath told the Your Thanet newspaper "I offered him a contract and he has taken a decision not to sign so at the moment he is not in my thoughts. Some people over value themselves. People like Dan Stubbs and some others didn't have a club at the end of last season and after finishing in the relegation zone this year, I'm not going to reward people for that with more money." Yorath also spoke to the Thanet Times about Dan and said I offered him a new contract on the same wages as last season and he said no, so he s left the club."

Dan ended up joining his hometown club Maidstone later in the summer of 2009 and he made six Isthmian League Premier Division appearances (five as sub) during the early part of the 2009/10 campaign, scoring once in a 2-1 home defeat against Tooting & Mitcham on 29.8.09. At the start of October 2009 Dan was released by the Stones and rejoined Margate.

He made the first appearance of his second spell with the club as a substitute in a 2-0 defeat at Canvey Island in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 10.10.09 and the Thanet Times said Dan looked good on his Margate return". The paper also said he was just about the only player to have a go at Canvey in the 15 minutes or so he was on the park" and Dan then featured again as a sub in a 3-1 defeat at Wealdstone in the FA Trophy on 17.10.09. The Thanet Times said he again looked lively".

Dan made his first start in midfield in a 2-1 defeat at Hastings on 7.11.09 and he then wore the number 11 shirt in each of the next six matches. On 29.11.09 he scored his first goal with a low curling shot in a 3-2 defeat against Cray at Bromley and the Thanet Times described Dan s effort as being well-taken". On 16.12.09 he scored twice in the dying minutes of an Isthmian League Cup tie at Sittingbourne as Margate lost 3-2 having been 3-0 down but Dan then missed the next two games.

He returned to action as a substitute in a 1-1 draw with Ashford (Middlesex) at Hartsdown Park on 16.1.10 and in Margate s next match - against Horsham at Horsham YMCA on 23.1.10 - Dan played up front. The Thanet Times said he had his best game of the season, buzzing about all over the place" as the game finished 3-3 and from then on Dan was a fixture in the side, usually playing in midfield.

On 6.2.10 he got his fourth goal of the season in a 3-2 home defeat against Hendon and in its report on a 2-1 defeat against visitors Canvey Island on 20.2.10 the Thanet Times said Dan put in a fair old shift getting up and down the park".

On 9.3.10 he played at left wing-back as Margate beat Tooting & Mitcham 2-1 at Hartsdown Park and Dan set up Leroy Huggins headed winner. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he did a smashing job" and Iain O Connell told the paper I m so pleased for Stubbsy who s played two games out of position for me now. He took 10 minutes to get used to it on Tuesday but he started the move for our second goal and put the cross in for Leroy (Huggins). I ve not seen many players with his energy." Dan then started the next four games in the number three shirt.

After a three match spell back in midfield he resumed his wing-back duties in a 0-0 draw at Tonbridge on 5.4.10 and Dan continued in the role for the last five games of the season as Margate avoided relegation despite finishing in the Premier Division drop zone again. He won the Supporters Player of the Year award and in all Dan had made 33 appearances (four as sub), scoring four times.

At the start of May 2010 he decided to join Icelandic 2nd Division club KA Akureyri for the summer and Iain O Connell told the Isle of Thanet Gazette Dan Stubbs is one I want to keep but he s gone out to Iceland to play, so I won t have him back until mid-September. I believe he got a call from an old pal and I don t blame him for going out there. Apparently it s a Conference-standard league and he s only young, so it could do him good."

Dan made his debut for KA Akureyri in a 2-1 win at Trottur Reykjavik on 9.5.10 and set up the first goal with a cross. He then played regularly through to September 2010 and later said "It was a great experience and it was one of those things I'll never forget. Standard-wise it was like the Conference but a lot less physical."

Having returned to England Dan joined Conference South club Thurrock towards the end of October 2010 but early in November 2010 he rejoined Margate for a third spell.

He made his first appearance in midfield in a 1-0 home defeat against Bury in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 6.11.10 and in his next outing on 9.11.10 Dan scored in a 1-1 draw at Tonbridge, finding the net with a strike from just outside the penalty area.

From then on he was a fixture in the Margate side and in its report on a 3-2 win over Sutton at Hartsdown Park on 13.11.10 the Thanet Times said Dan s pace and energy down the left raised Margate to another level". The paper also described his display a immense".

On 10.1.11 Dan played as a left wing-back in a game at Wealdstone and scored the only goal of the game with a rasping rising shot from the edge of the box. It was the start of a run at left wing-back and on 25.1.11 Dan was sent off in a 1-1 draw with visitors Hendon. He made another three starts wearing the number three shirt but after a 1-0 home defeat against Billericay on 5.2.11 Dan began a suspension and at the start of March 2011 he went back to Maidstone without featuring for Margate again. He d scored twice from 16 appearances (one as sub) before his departure.

Dan s second spell with Maidstone saw him score three times in 11 Isthmian League Premier Division outings during the remainder of 2010/11 as they were relegated and the Stones player-manager at the time was former Margate star Jay Saunders.

In July 2011 Dan rejoined Margate to begin a fourth stint with the club and manager Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "Stubbsy works very hard and is an all-action player who gives everything. He just needs a little direction and it'd down to me and Jake Leberl to give him that. He's maybe been allowed to do his own thing too much in the past but that's not his fault." Dan told the paper "I've played under a few managers in the past so when I heard that Chris (Kinnear) was interested in getting me back I was delighted."

A few days before the start of the 2011/12 season Chris Kinnear spoke about him to the Gazette and said We ve brought Dan back for his energy, enthusiasm and workrate. He s a really mobile player".

Dan made his first appearance of the new campaign in a 1-1 draw at Wealdstone in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 20.8.11 but on 29.8.11 he was sent off for what was deemed to be a stamp on an opponent as Margate drew 2-2 at Hastings. Dan tried to hurdle a challenge but landed on the Hastings player and was harshly dismissed. As a result of his red card Dan had to serve a three-match ban following a 2-0 home defeat against Hendon on 10.9.11.

He returned to Margate s midfield in a 2-0 defeat against AFC Hornchurch at Hartsdown Park on 27.9.11 and then played once more in the number 11 shirt before dropping to the subs bench. Dan came on in three consecutive matches in the early part of October 2011 but after regaining his place for a 3-2 home defeat against Bromley in the FA Cup on 15.10.11 he was ever-present in midfield for the remainder of the season.

On 12.11.11 Dan got his first goal of the campaign in a 5-0 win over visitors Wingate & Finchley and he also created one of Kwesi Appiah s four goals with what the Thanet Times described as a perfect defence-splitting through ball". Dan scored for the second time in a 4-2 win over Cray at Bromley on 27.12.11 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he had one of his better games" whilst praising a hell of a ball from inside his own half" that created a goal for Kwesi Appiah.

On 21.1.12 Dan was on target again as Margate thrashed Lewes 5-1 at Hartsdown Park and it was a great strike from the corner of the penalty area. The Thanet Times said he looked up and bent an absolute beauty into the far top corner". His next goal came from the penalty spot in 2-2 draw at Wingate & Finchley on 3.3.12 and having been used as both a wide midfielder and more centrally Dan told the Isle of Thanet Gazette I don t mind where I play, it s up to the gaffer how he uses me."

In its report on a 0-0 draw with visitors Leatherhead on 10.3.12 the Thanet Times said Dan worked hard throughout, for little reward, down the Margate right" and on 9.4.12 he caused amusement in a 3-1 home defeat against Cray after a mix-up about a substitution. Dan saw the number 11 board held up and assumed he was coming off so headed towards the Margate dugout but it turned out to be Cray that were making the change and the Thanet Times said Stubbsy returned to his position with a big smile on his face and no doubt it ll take a while to live that little gem down".

On 21.4.12 Dan got his fifth and sixth goals of the season in a 2-2 draw with Billericay at Hartsdown Park, scoring from the penalty spot and then tucking away the rebound after a second penalty was saved later on. He ended the campaign having made a total of 51 appearances (four as sub).

Dan scored a last-minute winner as Margate won 1-0 at Whitstable in a pre-season friendly on 24.7.12 and he made his first competitive appearance of the 2012/13 campaign as a substitute in a 2-0 home win over Hendon in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 18.8.12. Dan then came off the bench to score from the penalty spot as Margate drew 2-2 at Hastings on 21.8.12 and he made his first start of the season in a 3-3 draw at Kingstonian on 25.8.12.

For the next two months Dan was a regular in Margate s midfield but after a 4-0 home defeat against Metropolitan Police in the Isthmian League Cup on 16.10.12 he only featured as a substitute in the next two games. In the second of them Dan scored with a superb volley from just outside the penalty area as Margate lost 3-1 at Canvey Island. He was then restored to the starting line-up for a home game against Hastings on 27.10.12 and Dan made it back-to-back goals with Margate s strike in a 1-1 draw. From then on he was a fixture in the side once again and on 6.11.12 Dan scored for the third match in a row - a penalty in a 2-1 win at Leiston.

He got his fifth goal of the season in 3-1 win over Bury at Hartsdown Park on 17.11.12 and Dan then made it five goals in six games with a strike in a 2-1 win at Hampton & Richmond on 1.12.12.

On 5.1.13 he put a penalty over the bar as Margate lost 2-1 at Concord Rangers and on 16.2.13 Dan scored in a 2-1 defeat at Wealdstone. After a long run in the side he was dropped to the bench for a home game against Bognor Regis on 9.3.13 and when Dan came on in a 3-0 win it turned out to be his final appearance for Margate. Shortly afterwards he left the club citing work commitments and by then Dan had scored seven goals (two penalties) from 35 outings (seven as sub) during 2012/13.

Shortly after his departure from Hartsdown Park Dan rejoined Maidstone again and he scored once from seven league outings as the Stones won promotion from the Isthmian League Division 1 South via the play-offs. Dan was released by the club in June 2013 after negotiations with manager Jay Saunders over a new deal broke down.

In July 2013 Dan featured in some friendlies for Conference South outfit Dover who were managed by former Margate boss Chris Kinnear at the time but he wasn t signed and started 2013/14 without a club.

At the start of March 2014 Dan signed for Isthmian League Division 1 South outfit Hythe and made his debut for them as a substitute in a 2-0 home defeat against Walton & Hersham on 4.3.14.

name: Ron Sturgess
other clubs: Whitstable Town and Herne Bay
bio:
Thanet-born centre-forward who joined Margate in the summer of 1949 and spent the majority of the 1949/50 season in the reserves, scoring 24 times for them. That made Ron their leading marksman. However Ron also featured in the first team on occasions and with no little effect. He made his debut on 15.10.49 and scored as Margate beat Aylesford Paper Mills 2-1 in a Kent League game at Hartsdown Park. Ron went on to make a total of ten appearances and scored six goals in all, including an overhead kick against Royal Marines Chatham on 11.3.50 - a strike described as a "wonder goal" by the local paper.

He stayed at Margate for the 1950/51 campaign and scored 16 times in as many matches but at the end of the season Ron left the club and joined Whitstable.

Ron made his debut for the Oystermen in a 0-0 draw against Margate at Hartsdown Park on 18.8.51 and he went on to score 32 goals in 39 appearances during the 1951/52 campaign. His tally included one in a 2-1 home win over Margate on 24.11.51 and it remained a club record until beaten by Lee Bosson during 1995/96. Ron also spent 1952/53 with Whitstable and scored eight times in 27 matches during the season. He made his final appearance on 1.5.53 and coincidentally the opposition at the Belmont was supplied by Margate. Whitstable won 4-0 and Ron scored twice.

Ron then joined Herne Bay for the 1953/54 campaign and also played for them during the 1954/55 and 1955/56 seasons.

He died in Thanet on 3.1.86 aged only 58.

name: Arthur Summers
bio: - Margate 99/00 - came from Southampton area Arthur Gregson Summers born in Romsey, near Southampton in q3 1869     . Some reports list him as H G Summers though

name: Percy Summers
other clubs: Chesterfield, Grimsby Town (34,0), Luton Town
bio:
5  9  tall
Born Derby as Philip French Somerville although usually listed as being born in Sheffield
The son of a  doctor and descended from Irish landed gentry, he took up work as a fitter at Townsend's, in Sheffield, but a career in engineering offered few attractions for the young man, and he joined the army in July 1908. A reference from his local clergyman reckoned him to be "Industrious and respectable," but he soon found that the army life wasn't for him. He deserted from the 3rd Dragoon Guards at Aldershot in April 1909. Desertion in peacetime wasn't the big deal that it became during the Great War, and the army forgot about him. Philip Somerville slipped back into civilian life and began using the name "Percy Summers."
as a junior, played in South Wales where he also worked as a mechanic in a Rhondda coal mine, somewhere near pit village between Beighton and Kiveton Park
Then joined Chesterfield Town for 1910/11 
Midland League debut on October 13th 1910 at Nottingham Forest Reserves
and became one of the most respected goalkeepers in the Midland League - 134 apps for Chesterfield in League / FA Cup
Chest to Grimsby start of May 1914, was 24 then - debut on 1 September 1914 in Grimsby 2 Preston 2 (Div 2). 
Grimsby press report on their Nov 1914 6-0 loss at Arsenal "Summers was never idle and saved several times". 
Whilst Grimsby player WWI broke out and joined 17th Battalion of the Duke of Cambridge's Middlesex Regiment in February 1915 along with many footballers, six went with Percy from Grimsby 
Carried on playing for Grimsby to end of 14/15 season - professional footballers in the battalion were given train tickets to return to their clubs every Saturday - army training in London during week. Total of 35 apps for Grimsby during 14/15
Also guested for both Reading and Sheffield Wednesday during 14/15 whilst training 
Played for 'The Footballers Battalion' team played around the country right up to embarkation in November 1915 and in January 1916 Percy played in a match for them  at the Front  v The Royal Engineers. Described as  Phil (better known as Percy)  in mention of that game
He suffered hand and stomach injuries from rifle grenade in Battle of the Somme 20th March, 1916 then transferred to a training battalion before discharged in July 1917 as unfit for action. Played for Sheffield Wednesday again after recovery
one more game for Grimsby   in 1919 against Notts County - before playing one season (19/20) for Luton Town 30.8.19
Football League kicked off again and Percy played in Luton Town v Swansea that day, let in early goal but ended 1-1 local reporter was very impressed by Luton's new goalie: "Summers was very clever in preventing further scoring."
- Margate 20/21 - Margate 21/22 (captain) 
He and his wife took up jobs at the Dreamland amusement park and Percy was tempted out of retirement when Margate Town was formed in the summer of 1924 to replace his old club, which had been disbanded by the Kent FA in 1923. 8.11.24 broke bone in his right thumb during Bostall Heath 5 Margate 2 and didn't play again.
June 1926 - advertised in Athletic News for post as player-coach or trainer, address 32 Ramsgate Road, Margate. 
Percy, his wife Jessie and his family remained in Margate, operating a lodging house at 32 Ramsgate Road. Court case in May 1927   Percy applied to have tenant evicted, won case.
 
before moving to Derby, his wife's home town, in the late 1920s. Percy worked for British Celanese at Spondon before retirement, and died in Derby aged 76 on 21.6.66, interestingly a death notice in a Derby paper used his original name Phillip French Somerville

name: Ray Summers
other clubs: Folkestone & Shepway, Folkestone Town and Ramsgate
bio:
Versatile, 5' 7" tall, Aldgate-born player who initially joined Margate in the summer of 1967 and made his first appearance for the reserves on 30.9.67 aged just 15.

Ray then became a fixture in the reserves during the remainder of the 1967/68 season and also made a one-off appearance for the first team. His debut came when he played at right-back in a 3-3 draw at Hastings in the Kent Floodlight Cup on 20.3.68. It was only a month after Ray's 16th birthday.

He continued to play regularly for the reserves during the 1968/69 campaign and played twice more for the first team too, first appearing on 25.3.69 in a 1-1 draw at Deal.

Ray signed professional forms in the summer of 1969 and he went on to make ten further first team appearances (one as sub) during the 1969/70 season. He usually played at left-back and impressed with his speed and solid tackling. His performance after coming on as a substitute in the Kent Floodlight Cup Final Replay at Gravesend & Northfleet on 15.5.70 was described as "outstanding" by the local press.

During the 1970/71 season Ray made 39 appearances, nine of them as a substitute, and scored three goals. The first of them - Ray's first for the club - came during a 3-1 win at Andover in the FA Trophy on 5.12.70. Throughout the season Ray impressed with his determined, energetic style of play and he usually played at either right-back or as a striker. In January 1971 he was given the captaincy for a spell and at the time Ray was only 18. He was referred to as a "blonde bombshell" by the local press during the season.

A back injury forced Ray to sit out the early part of the 1971/72 campaign and he often found himself on the subs bench once he'd recovered. However Ray still made a total of 43 appearances, 11 of them as a substitute, and in doing so took his overall tally for the club past 100. He spent most of the season playing at right-back but also featured at left-back on occasions. His enthusiastic over-lapping won him praise from the local press and Ray was said to play as if he was "bristling with fire".

On 2.10.71 he scored a great goal with a drive from the edge of the penalty area in a 4-3 win at Telford and on 20.11.71 Ray came on as a substitute as Margate infamously lost 11-0 at Bournemouth & Boscombe in the FA Cup 1st Round. He managed one other goal during the campaign and again it was a good one as Ray cut in from the right wing to fire home from distance in a 4-2 win at Ashford on 24.11.71. He was watched by Football League scouts during the season.

Ray spent the majority of the 1972/73 campaign playing at left-back, initially filling in for the injured Alan Butterfield but later being chosen in preference to him. He also played at right-back on occasions when Colin Clewlow switched to central defence. Ray's attacking full-back play again won him many plaudits and his hard tackling prompted the local press to describe him as "a resolute defender who replaces his lack of inches with anticipation". He made a total of 56 appearances (four as a substitute) during the season and scored twice. Ray s first goal came in a 3-1 win over Poole at Hartsdown Park on 7.10.72 and he found the net from fully 35 yards. The Thanet Times said the strike "would have won any goal of the month competition".

On 18.11.72 he was in the Margate side that beat Swansea 1-0 in an FA Cup 1st Round tie at Hartsdown Park and Ray also featured in a 1-0 win at Walton & Hersham in the 2nd Round on 9.12.72. He then played in perhaps Margate s biggest ever match - a 6-0 defeat against visitors Tottenham in the 3rd Round on 13.1.73. Ray s second goal of the campaign came in a 3-2 defeat at Canterbury on 23.1.73 when he hammered home a shot from the edge of the penalty area after a solo run.

During the 1973/74 season Ray was virtually ever-present, making 59 appearances to take his overall tally for the club past 200. He played at right-back throughout the campaign and was variously described as being "dashing", "a model of consistency" and "a redoubtable dreadnought" by the local press. Ray was a worthy winner of the club's 'Player of the Year' award.

He managed three goals during the season and the first of them came in a 4-1 home win over Maidstone on 26.12.73. Ray cracked home a shot described by the Isle of Thanet Gazette as "blistering" from out on the right wing and then on 27.1.74 he scored what the Thanet Times called a "truly memorable goal" as Margate beat Bognor Regis 5-1 at Hartsdown Park. Ray exchanged passes with Eddie Clayton before smashing home a shot from outside the penalty area. He also scored a superb solo goal in a 2-1 win over visitors Folkestone on 9.3.74, collecting the ball some 40 yards out and then surging forward. Ray beat several defenders in a diagonal run before lashing home with his weaker left foot. On 13.4.74 he was in the side that won the Kent Senior Cup with a 2-0 win at Maidstone.

Ray was suspended for the first two weeks of the 1974/75 season and took a while to regain his place in the side after his enforced absence. However by October 1974 he was back in the first team and found himself playing at left-back initially.

As the campaign wore on Ray played a few games at right-back and also appeared in central defence before moving up into midfield. He thrived in his new position and finished the season having made 50 appearances (three as sub), scoring four goals. The pick of them was a solo effort in a 3-2 win at Folkestone & Shepway on 10.12.74, Ray ran from his own penalty area before firing home. He also scored with a spectacular header in a 2-0 over Romford on 4.1.75. Ray's best performance of the season came in the first leg of the Southern League Cup Final against Kettering on 5.4.75. The Thanet Times said that he put on "a one man show...mopping up at the back, powering through midfield and linking with the attack" but Margate lost 2-0. Ray also played in the second leg at Kettering on 12.4.75 as Margate secured a 1-1 draw that wasn t sufficient to claim the trophy.

During the 1975/76 campaign Ray continued to revel in a midfield role and he was praised by the Thanet Times for giving "101% for 90 minutes". He made 58 appearances, taking his career tally past 300, and scored eight goals. Although he spent the majority of the season in midfield Ray also played as a right-back, centre-back and centre-forward on occasions during the campaign. On 22.4.76 he played as Margate won 2-0 at Canterbury in the 1st Leg of the Kent Floodlight Trophy Final and Ray also featured in the 2nd Leg at Hartsdown Park on 24.4.76 which the visitors won 2-1 after extra time. The result meant Margate took the trophy with a 3-2 aggregate win.

The 1976/77 season saw Ray once again being used as something of a 'utility man' and he played in midfield, up front, at left-back and at centre-back during the season. He made 55 appearances and although many of them were in defensive positions Ray was the club's leading marksman with 15 goals.

On 28.9.76 he scored a hat-trick in a 5-2 win over Hastings at Hartsdown Park and on 20.11.76 Ray scored a superb solo goal during a 3-1 home defeat against Bedford. He beat three defenders before scoring with a low swerving shot from 35 yards. His consistent performances in a range of positions were enough to win Ray the club's 'Player of the Year' award for the season, the second time he'd won the trophy, but unfortunately Margate were relegated from the Southern League Premier Division.

The 1977/78 campaign was a memorable one for Ray, as club captain he made 42 appearances to take his overall tally past the 400 mark and he scored a career-best 20 goals which made him the club's joint leading marksman along with Vic Pain. Margate won the Southern League 1st Division (South) title and it was also Ray's benefit season, in recognition of his ten years at the club. Events held to raise funds for him included a stag night and disco.

Ray spent most of the campaign playing as a striker and on 17.12.77 he scored five times in a 7-1 win over Trowbridge at Hartsdown Park including a remarkable spell of three goals in four minutes. Margate manager Denis Hunt told the Kentish Express Summers was so powerful and fast he almost frightened me ! On 28.2.78 Ray was sent off for throwing a punch at an opponent in a 5-0 home win over Crawley and as a result he somewhat bizarrely missed his own testimonial match - against 2nd Division Luton on 15.3.78 - due to suspension. Shortly before the Luton game, Ray had been offered to Folkestone & Shepway in part-exchange for Neil Cugley but he didn't want to move and the Cugley transfer went through as a straight cash deal instead.

Ray began the 1978/79 season playing up front and on 23.9.78 he took over in goal when Steve Bowtell was carried off before half-time in a 1-1 draw with visitors Nuneaton. Ray had scored four times in 14 appearances when he was sold to Folkestone & Shepway for £750 in November 1978. His 11 year spell at Hartsdown Park ended at the age of 26 and manager Denis Hunt said "We sold him because we need a few quality players quickly he has given outstanding service to Margate."

Ray went on to score 11 goals for Folkestone & Shepway before the end of the 1978/79 campaign.

In February 1980 Ray rejoined Margate in a straight swap for Alan Fagan and the first match of his second spell with the club was a 2-0 defeat at Andover on 9.2.80. Ray played in midfield and went on to make 15 appearances, all in that position, before the end of the 1979/80 campaign. He scored four goals and was praised for his "whole-hearted industry" by the Isle of Thanet Gazette.

On 5.8.80 Ray played an entire game in goal as Margate drew 3-3 with Deal in a pre-season friendly at Hartsdown Park and he continued to be a fixture in the side during the 1980/81 campaign, usually playing in midfield or as a striker. He also turned out at right-back, left-back and centre-back during the campaign. Ray s competitive instincts were as keen as ever and at one stage the Thanet Times said that he had "a frustrating tendency to be penalised for clumsy challenges". The paper also claimed that Ray was "as solo-minded as the Lone Ranger" in its report on a 5-0 home defeat against Dorchester in January 1981. However the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that Ray was "a constant source of inspiration" in a 3-2 defeat against visitors Ashford in the Kent Senior Cup on 27.1.81. Ray had made a total of 42 appearances and scored six goals during the season when his Margate career finally ended in February 1981. After playing in a 0-0 draw with Salisbury at Hartsdown Park on 21.2.81 he left the club and rejoined Folkestone. It was part of a drastic cost-cutting exercise by the club and Ray's final appearance for Margate had come just under 13 years since his first.

In the summer of 1981 he became area manager for the 'Goldliner' lottery and sales of the tickets helped clubs such as Thanet United.

Ray stayed with Folkestone until January 1982 when he returned to Thanet and joined Ramsgate.

He played for the Rams for the rest of the 1981/82 season but he also made a brief return to Hartsdown Park. Ramsgate allowed Ray to play at right-back for Thanet in a 3-2 defeat at home to Ashford on 16.2.82 but it was strictly a one game loan deal.

At the end of the 1981/82 campaign he was forced to give up playing for the Rams due to work commitments. Ray then dropped into amateur football and played for Margate Athletic for several seasons.

In December 1985 Ray scored a hat-trick in a veterans match at Hartsdown Park and his performance prompted Thanet manager John Wickens to sign him on for United. He played a few games for the reserves early in 1986 and then on 4.2.86 Ray wore the number 11 shirt for United's first team as they took on Dover in an Eastern Floodlight Cup tie at Hartsdown Park. It was almost 18 years since he'd made his Margate debut, also in a Floodlight Cup game, and the match was the last of Ray's senior career. He played as a striker as Thanet won 1-0 and had a header well saved by future Margate keeper Kevin Hudson during the first half. Early in the second period Ray hobbled off with a leg injury and he then dropped back into local amateur football, becoming player-manager of Oddfellows FC for the 1986/87 season.

During the early part of his Margate career Ray worked in chemical manufacturing but he later became a well-known pub landlord in the Thanet area. He ran the Ruby Lounge in Margate for a lengthy period and later took over The Belle Vue in Cliftonville. Ray was still landlord there in 2006.

His son Rob played for Margate during the 1990's and then spent several seasons with Herne Bay before moving to Ramsgate during the 2004/05 campaign. He later returned to Margate, playing for the club during 2007/08.

In 2013 Ray was Head Steward of The Birchington Club and on 12.4.14 he was one of the many former Margate players who attended the club s Legends Day at Hartsdown Park.

name: Rob Summers
other clubs: Wimbledon (0), Ramsgate, Folkestone Invicta, Herne Bay, Whitstable Town, Deal Town and Faversham Town
bio:
Locally born son of Margate legend Ray Summers who attended St. George s School in Broadstairs and captained their football team.

In November 1992 Rob signed schoolboy forms for Premier League club Wimbledon aged 14 and played for their youth team on three Saturdays out of every four. On the other week Rob turned out for Swale League club Elmcourt Celtic. At that time his father Ray told the Isle of Thanet Gazette He s a good lad in every way and now it s up to him.

Rob joined Margate for the 1993/94 season and played regularly for the club's Under-18's side as well as making a few reserve team appearances in the Kent Midweek League. On 13.2.94 Rob took over in goal after eight minutes of an Under-18's game at Dover when Gavin Wright was sent off and a week later he spent part of the first half in goal after Luke Hills was dismissed in a 5-4 win over Snowdown's Under 18's. Rob later scored with a 30-yarder.

On 24.4.94 he made his first team debut at left-back in a 6-0 win over Braintree at Hartsdown Park and it was just a few weeks after Rob's 16th birthday. He also wore the number three shirt in Margate's next match - a 2-0 win at Buckingham on 30.4.94 - but didn't feature again before the end of the season.

Rob made his first senior appearance of the 1994/95 campaign when he came on as a substitute in a 2-0 home win over Merstham in an FA Cup tie on 10.9.94 and then made eight further sporadic appearances as a sub over the course of the next few months. On 22.10.94 he scored his first goal for Margate after coming on during a 3-0 win at Erith & Belvedere but Rob didn't start a match until 25.3.95 when he lined up at left-back in a 2-0 win at Burnham. He kept his place for a 3-1 defeat against Ashford at Hartsdown on 28.3.95 and then missed three games before finishing the season by starting seven of Margate's last eight matches at left-back. In total Rob made 19 appearances (nine as sub) and scored once during 1994/95.

He stayed at Margate for the 1995/96 campaign and on 9.9.95 Rob made his first appearance of the season when he played at left-back in a 5-2 win at Corinthian Casuals in the FA Cup. He made his next start in a 2-2 draw at Walton & Hersham in the FA Cup on 23.9.95 and on 17.10.95 Rob played in midfield as Margate lost 2-1 to Bashley at Hartsdown. He then spent the next five months playing for the Under-18's and reserves. Rob didn't feature in the first team again until 16.3.96 when he came on as a substitute in a 1-0 home defeat against Braintree. He also came on as a sub in a 2-0 win over Fareham at Hartsdown on 21.4.96 and a 1-0 defeat at Newport IOW on 30.4.96 to take his total appearances for the season to six (three as sub).

Rob was still a Margate player during the 1996/97 campaign but he didn't feature in the first team and in the summer of 1997 he joined Ramsgate.

Rob returned to Margate for the start of 1998/99 and played exclusively for the reserves before leaving the club again at the end of the season.

He started the 1999/00 campaign at Folkestone but in January 2000 Rob rejoined Ramsgate.

His next move took him to Herne Bay in July 2000 and Rob went on to spend several seasons with the club. On 15.9.01 he scored an own goal after only 11 seconds of a 4-2 home win over Erith & Belvedere but he later made amends by slotting home a penalty.

In January 2005 Rob linked up with Ramsgate for the third time and stayed there until October 2005 when he moved on to Whitstable.

He rejoined Herne Bay in the summer of 2006 and then had a short spell with Deal at the start of the 2007/08 campaign before returning to Margate a few weeks into the season.

Rob was signed as a reserve team player but on 2.10.07 he played at left-back as the first team lost 3-2 to East Thurrock United in an Isthmian League Cup tie at Hartsdown Park. It was his first appearance in Margate's senior side since 30.4.96 - a gap of over 11 years - and his first start since 17.10.95. Rob also wore the number three shirt in a 4-1 home defeat against Ebbsfleet in the Kent Senior Cup on 26.3.08 and played in midfield as Margate won 1-0 at Harrow on 26.4.08, the last day of the 2007/08 campaign.

In the summer of 2008 he joined Faversham of the Kent League but later in the 2008/09 season Rob returned to Margate to act as assistant manager for Mark Weatherly's reserve team.

In May 2009 Rob left Hartsdown Park once more to become player-manager of Ramsgate's reserve team. He was only 31 at the time.

Rob left Ramsgate at the end of the 2009/10 season and after a brief spell back at Herne Bay in the summer of 2010 he retired from football before the start of the 2010/11 campaign to spend more time with his young son Albert.

Rob came out of retirement for the start of the 2011/12 campaign when he joined Thanet Sunday Football League side Eclipse Recovery Services.

name: D Sutherland
bio: In from Walsall Wood and Rushall of the Birmingham Combination. Margate Amateurs after us later in 1927/28 and with them 1928/29 too

name: Rod Sutton
bio:
Local player who first played for Margate s reserves during the 1962/63 season, making ten appearances and scoring six times.

Rod then started the 1963/64 campaign with a second half hat-trick as the reserves won 4-0 at Chingford on 24.8.63 and he went on to score 13 times in 27 reserve team outings during the remainder of the season.

Rod also made a one-off appearance for the first team when he wore the number nine shirt in a Kent Senior Shield tie at Dartford on 11.11.63 that Margate lost 2-0.

name: Sutton
bio: Ransgate - occasionally - 09/10, 10/11 and 11/12. Handful of games across those 3 season. Margate 12/13 - had also played for Canterbury previously, a 'Buff'

name: Mark Sutton-Foster
other clubs: Ramsgate and Deal Town
bio:
Diminutive Margate-born player who started his career with Ramsgate before joining Margate in October 1993. Mark played for the Under-18's throughout the remainder of the 1993/94 season.

On 30.4.94 he made his first team debut shortly after his 18th birthday when he came on as a substitute in a 2-0 win at Buckingham in the Southern League but it was Mark's only senior appearance. He left Margate at the end of 1993/94 and returned to Ramsgate.

Mark rejoined Margate for the start of the 1995/96 campaign and played exclusively for the reserves during the season, making over 20 appearances for them.

He was back at Ramsgate by the start of the 1999/00 campaign and Mark later had a spell with Deal that included the 2002/03 and 2003/04 seasons.

In the summer of 2004 Mark returned to Ramsgate yet again where he played for the reserves during 2004/05 before dropping into Sunday football.

During the 2006/07 and 2007/08 campaigns Mark played for Westbrook Social in the Thanet Sunday Football League and he was also assistant manager of Monkton Youth's Under-10's side during 2007/08.

Mark joined Thanet Sunday Football League side Social Westbrook Club for the start of the 2010/11 season but only played a handful of games before retiring.

name: Bill Swain
other clubs: Fulham (0), Dover and Bexley United
bio:
Powerful, 6' 4" tall centre-back born in Romford, Essex noted for his aerial ability.

Bill started his career in Fulham's juniors and, after initially being an amateur, he was given a professional contract at the start of the 1959/60 season. Bill progressed to the first team squad during the 1960/61 campaign but never featured in Fulham s senior side before being released at the end of that season.

In July 1961 Bill joined Dover and he went on to be a pivotal figure at the club over the course of the next eight seasons. He was club captain for most of his time at Crabble. On 18.5.63 Bill bagged a hat-trick in a 3-0 win at Canterbury and that was part of a run where he scored six goals in three games.

On 4.9.65 Bill was sent off in an FA Cup tie at Deal and was fined £5 as well as being banned for seven days. When he was dismissed again in a game at Hastings on 30.10.65 he was given a six week suspension and fined £5 and 5 shillings.

In March 1968 Bill was appointed as Dover s player-manager after the club s previous manager Jack Clover passed away. He continued in the role until tendering his resignation at the end of January 1969. Bill gave notice that he would be unable to continue as manager due to work commitments - he was about to become a manager for the North Thames Gas Board. Bill stayed on as manager until the end of March 1969 when Terry Adlington took over. Bill continued to play for Dover until the end of the 1968/69 season and made a total of 304 Southern League appearances for the club, scoring 19 goals.

In the summer of 1969 Bill joined Margate as a replacement for the recently departed Bob Harrop and a fee of around £500 was involved, Margate used the money they had just received from the sale of Phil Amato to fund the deal. Manager Almer Hall said at the time "I have always rated Swain as being one of the finest centre-halves in the Southern League and I am confident he will do well with us."

Bill became Margate's captain and made his debut in a 3-3 draw at Hereford on 9.8.69 - the opening day of the 1969/70 Southern League campaign. He went on to make 71 appearances during the season and was described as being "a tower of strength" by the local press. Bill was a model of consistency throughout the campaign and on 15.11.69 he was in the Margate side that were thrashed 7-2 by visitors Aldershot in the FA Cup 1st Round. He scored five goals including one in the 2nd Leg of the Kent Floodlight Cup Final at Gravesend & Northfleet on 7.5.70 and another in the 2nd Leg of the Kent Senior Cup Final at Dartford on 9.5.70.

Bill started the 1970/71 season in commanding style and continued to be a cool head in the heart of Margate's defence, as well as being a danger when going forward for set pieces. On 21.11.70 he played as Margate lost 2-0 at Dagenham in the FA Cup 1st Round. In December 1970 he was promoted to an executive position by North Thames Gas Board and as a result Bill left the club early in 1971. He felt that the travel involved with playing for Margate combined with his new work duties would be too much. Bill had made 23 appearances and scored three goals during the season.

In June 1971 he joined Bexley and as Bill was living in London at the time the travel involved was far less than during his time with Margate. During the 1971/72 season he played a key role as Bexley enjoyed an excellent run in the FA Trophy that took them from the 1st Qualifying Round through to the 3rd Round - six games in total - before losing 3-2 at Buxton. Bill was also a regular in Bexley s side at the start of the 1972/73 campaign but in December 1972 he retired aged only 29.

name: Paul Sykes
other clubs: Gillingham (0), Welling United, Folkestone Invicta, Herne Bay, Dover Athletic and Dartford
bio:
Effervescent whole-hearted striker widely known as 'Syko' who played for Kent Schools as a youth alongside future Margate player Jon Monteath before starting his senior career with Gillingham as a trainee.

Paul scored 15 goals for the Gills' youth team during the 1992/93 campaign before suffering a double fracture of an arm in March 1993 and his tally included five in a Kent Under-16's cup tie. He spent two more seasons with Gillingham and on 4.8.94 Paul scored twice as the Gills drew 3-3 in a friendly with Margate at Hartsdown Park. One goal was a 25-yarder and the other a 35-yard free-kick. He was released at the end of 1994/95 having never played for the first team.

Paul joined Welling for the start of the 1995/96 campaign and scored twice in seven appearances for the Wings during the season. He also had a loan spell with Folkestone where he scored once in four appearances. Paul was released by Welling in the summer of 1996.

He linked up with Margate ahead of the 1996/97 campaign and was one of new manager Chris Kinnear's first signings for the club. Paul made an early impression when he was sent off during a friendly at Ramsgate in July 1996 after a clash with former Thanet United player Chris Thomas. Paul had earlier scored in a game that finished 3-3.

He made his competitive debut in a 4-1 win over Yate at Hartsdown Park on 17.8.96 and scored what the Thanet Times called "a grand goal". His fellow striker Martin Buglione bagged a hat-trick and it was the start of a great partnership in which Paul's determination and aerial power perfectly complimented Buglione's pace and skill. Paul scored again in Margate's next match - a 3-2 win at Fisher on 20.8.96 - and then notched a brace in a 3-1 home win against Erith & Belvedere on 26.8.96 to take his tally to four goals in his first four games. The Isle of Thanet Gazette described him as being "a lanky livewire".

On 21.9.96 Paul was sent off for a second bookable offence just 52 minutes into a 4-0 home defeat at the hands of Witney and with a ban still pending for his pre-season dismissal the Thanet Times said he "needed another red card like a hole in the head". Paul was suspended for one match for the Witney incident and then sat out four games in October and November as a punishment for his red card at Ramsgate in July.

On 2.12.96 Paul appeared at Thanet Court charged with driving while under the influence of alcohol. On the way home after a game at Hartsdown Park in October he'd written-off his car after driving into a field near Ramsgate. Paul had waited for the police to arrive and admitted his guilt in court. He was banned from driving for 18 months and fined £300 with £50 costs. To add insult to injury the scrap value of his car was only £25. The local press reported that Paul was living on his Margate earnings of £70.80 per week at the time.

On 7.12.96 Paul quickly put his off-field troubles to one side in emphatic fashion by scoring both goals in a 2-1 win at league leaders Havant. The second was a stunning effort from fully 30 yards that the Thanet Times described as "a gem of a strike". On 21.12.96 he was on target in a 2-0 win over Forest Green at Hartsdown Park and celebrated his goal by sitting on Buglione's back and puffing on an imaginary cigar in front of the delighted Margate supporters. Paul was rapidly establishing himself as something of a cult hero for 'Gate fans. He continued to score regularly, often with his head, and on 15.4.97 Paul bagged a hat-trick in a 6-0 win at Fleet. Buglione also got three in a match that confirmed the quality of their striking partnership. Paul scored two more in a 3-1 home win over Cinderford on 19.4.97 and ended the season with an impressive record of 20 goals from 41 appearances (one as sub).

In an interview with the short-lived sports newspaper The Far Post ahead of the 1997/98 campaign Margate manager Chris Kinnear said Paul "had the heart of a lion" and added "Paul Sykes is only just twenty, and he's a good player. He looks a bit sharper this year. He makes a few mistakes, but he's only twenty - he's not twenty six, and he's so committed to Margate, and to football. He's a great player to have in the squad".

Paul's younger brother Peter joined Margate for 1997/98 and Paul started the new season in great form. On 16.8.97 he found the net with what the Thanet Times said was an "excellent strike" in a 1-1 draw with Trowbridge at Hartsdown Park - it was a low drive from just inside the penalty area. He scored in Margate's next two games as well and on 11.10.97 Paul was booked for what the Thanet Times called "a senseless foul" on the opposing goalkeeper during a 2-1 home win over Deal in the FA Cup. On 18.10.97 Paul scored twice in a 5-1 win at Whyteleafe with Martin Buglione getting the other three goals and in its report on a 3-1 win over Staines at Chertsey in an FA Cup tie on 24.10.97 the Thanet Times described Paul as being a "Hartsdown icon". He scored one of the goals and made another as Margate made it through to the 1st Round for the first time in 25 years. On 28.10.97 Paul scored twice in a 4-0 home win over Tonbridge and he marked his 21st birthday on 8.11.97 by being booked for what the Thanet Times said was a "needless foul" on Waterlooville's keeper as Margate beat the Hampshire side 3-2 at Hartsdown Park.

On 16.11.97 he played as Margate lost 2-1 to visitors Fulham in the FA Cup 1st Round. The match was shown live on Sky Sports and Paul unfortunately missed a good chance to level the tie in the closing minutes.

He kept up an impressive strike rate as the season progressed and on 8.12.97 Paul scored a hat-trick in a 5-1 home win over Corby in the FA Trophy. He scored his 19th and 20th goals of the campaign in a 4-0 win over visitors St.Leonards Stamcroft on 6.1.98 and notched up another double to earn Margate a 2-0 win over Weymouth at Hartsdown Park on 24.1.98. The Thanet Times said they were "two superbly headed goals". On 3.2.98 Paul scored twice in a 2-1 home win over Cambridge City and on 7.2.98 he scored with a brilliant 30-yard lob in a 2-0 win over visitors Havant before being carried off with a knee injury that kept him on the sidelines for five matches.

After regaining his fitness Paul scored in a 4-0 win at Cinderford on 28.3.98 and on 31.3.98 he notched up his 30th goal of the season to earn Margate a 1-0 home win over Gillingham in the semi-final of the Kent Senior Cup. On 7.4.98 he was on target as Margate beat Redditch 2-0 in the 1st Leg of the Southern League Cup Final at Hartsdown Park and Paul also played in the 2nd Leg on 21.4.98 which the home side won 1-0. That result meant that Margate claimed the trophy with a 2-1 aggregate victory.

He took his goal tally to 32 with a strike in a 3-1 home win over Clevedon on 25.4.98 and on 4.5.98 Paul featured as Margate beat Gravesend & Northfleet 1-0 at Stonebridge Road to win the Kent Senior Cup. He ended the campaign having made a total of 59 appearances (four as sub) and Paul s 32 goals meant that he edged out Martin Buglione by a single goal to finish the campaign as Margate's top scorer. Paul and Buglione had scored 110 times between them in two seasons together but his fellow striker left the club in the summer of 1998.

In May 1998 Paul signed a long-term contract and during the summer he had a minor knee operation. In August 1998 he played as a centre-back in a friendly at Deal and on 29.8.98 he scored his first goal of the 1998/99 campaign in a 2-2 draw at Raunds. By mid-October Paul had scored five goals and had a new strike partner in Phil Collins.

Collins struggled to win over the Margate fans initially and after he'd been the target of abuse in the first half of a 2-0 home defeat against Raunds on 24.10.98 Paul intervened as only he could. As the rest of the players left the field at half-time he ran over to the Hartsdown Road terrace where the majority of the Margate supporters were standing and launched into an astonishing impassioned defence of Collins, calling on people to get behind him. It was a remarkable show of support for his strike partner and the sight of Paul berating the Hartsdown Park faithful would live long in the memories of those that witnessed it.

In Margate's next match at Yate on 7.11.98 Paul played despite having a broken nose and scored in a 3-0 win. That started a run of four consecutive games in which he found the net and the sequence included two goals in a 3-2 win at Chelmsford on 14.11.98. In December 1998 Paul embarked on another four game scoring spree that started with a goal in a 3-1 win at Andover on 5.11.98. He then bagged a hat-trick in a 5-0 home win over Bashley on 12.12.98 before scoring twice in a 6-1 win at St.Leonards on 19.12.98. Paul ended the run with a brace in a 2-1 win over Sittingbourne at Hartsdown Park on 26.12.98 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette described him as a "Margate hero" as he scored the winner with an injury time penalty although he was suffering with 'flu. On 9.1.99 Paul got both goals in a 2-0 home win over Tonbridge. His first was a "25-yard screamer" according to the Thanet Times whilst his second was his 20th goal of the season.

Paul's form dipped in the second half of the campaign and the Thanet Times reported that he missed several chances and had a "sorry game" in a 2-2 draw with Dartford at Hartsdown Park on 23.01.99. He was booked for dissent after what the paper said was "an obvious dive in the box" and Paul clashed with a Dartford defender soon afterwards. The match report said Chris Kinnear then "brought him off before he was sent off" and described Paul's departure dramatically saying "Angry, he tore his shirt off and stomped down the tunnel". The paper said his "reaction smacked of petulance".

Paul bounced back by scoring twice in Margate's next four games but didn't find the net in the following four matches and found himself on the subs bench six times during March and April 1999. On 30.3.99 he came on to notch a last-minute goal that secured a 1-0 win at Newport IOW but although he regained the number nine shirt for the last seven matches of the season Paul didn't score again. The Isle of Thanet Gazette noted that he "unusually looked low on confidence" during a 2-1 home defeat against Fleet on 13.4.99 but on 1.5.99 Paul ended the campaign on a brighter note when he played in a 4-0 win at Brackley that sealed Margate's promotion to the Southern League Premier Division. He finished up as the club's top goalscorer once again having scored 23 times in his 49 appearances (seven as sub).

Paul started the 1999/00 season in great style by scoring twice in Margate's shock 3-1 win at Southern League Premier Division title favourites Worcester on 14.8.99. The Thanet Times said his first goal was a "sweet 20-yard strike" into the bottom corner. Paul then found the net in three consecutive matches later in August, starting with what the Thanet Times called a "30-yard belter" in a 3-0 win over Gloucester at Hartsdown Park on 21.8.99. Next came the only goal of the game that secured a 1-0 win at Weymouth on 24.8.99 and Paul's effort was described as being a "fabulous strike" by the Isle of Thanet Gazette. He cut inside two defenders before curling home a 25-yard effort and the paper said it was a "moment of brilliance". Paul ended the run with a goal in a 3-2 home win over Ilkeston on 28.8.99 and the Thanet Times said he was "in prime form up front". He'd scored six goals before picking up a hamstring injury in October that ruled him out for seven games. Paul returned to the Margate side for a 2-0 win at Sittingbourne on 16.11.99 and was a fixture in the number nine shirt after that but he didn't score again during 1999.

On 3.1.00 Paul was sent off before half-time as Margate beat Crawley 1-0 at Hartsdown Park but the general consensus was that his two bookings were harsh - one for dissent on 38 minutes and the other two minutes later for a foul on the Crawley keeper. Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "We couldn't believe that he was booked for dissent and Paul says he didn't touch the player when he was sent off".

On 22.1.00 Paul scored from the penalty spot to secure a 1-0 home win over King's Lynn and his effort ended a run of 15 appearances without a goal, a run that stretched back to September 1999. Chris Kinnear told the Thanet Times "It was good to see Paul score. Every striker has an iffy patch, but once he starts scoring again we'll be quite a force up front" and Paul repaid his manager's faith in him by finding the net in each of Margate's next three games. He was on target with a looping header in a 3-2 home defeat against Folkestone on 25.1.00 and then scored the only goal in a 1-0 win at Atherstone on 29.1.00 before finishing the run with two goals in a 5-2 win at Fleet on 1.2.00. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said that Paul "worked himself into the ground" during a 1-0 win over Burton at Hartsdown Park on 22.2.00 and "earned a terrific ovation" when he was substituted with three minutes left due to cramp. That match was one of a run of five without a goal for Paul but on 11.3.00 he bagged a brace in a 4-3 win at Merthyr. His second was a header that won the game for Margate and it was his 13th goal of the campaign.

Disaster struck for Paul in his next outing - a home game against Bath on 18.3.00. He threw himself into a slightly ill-advised challenge with typical gusto and was carried off in agony. He'd ruptured a knee ligament and the injury not only ended his season but effectively finished his Margate career. Paul had made 34 appearances (one as sub) before fate intervened.

On 16.9.00 Paul attempted a comeback when he played for the reserves in a 1-0 win over Whitstable Reserves at Hartsdown Park but he suffered a recurrence of his knee injury and had to go off after just ten minutes. He didn't play again during the 2000/01 campaign.

In June 2001 the Isle of Thanet Gazette reported that Paul was fit again and Chris Kinnear said "I am delighted that Paul has recovered so well and we look forward to seeing him back in contention at the start of the season." Despite that early optimism Paul didn't feature at all in Margate's friendlies ahead of the 2001/02 campaign - the club's first in the Conference - but after some home games early in the season he could be seen running laps round the Hartsdown Park pitch. Paul finally returned to action on 16.10.01 when he played the last 20 minutes of a friendly at Tonbridge that the home side won 5-2. He then managed a run of reserve team games and scored four goals in as many outings for them.

On 13.11.01 Paul made a hugely popular return to first team duties when he came on as a substitute with 20 minutes left of a Kent Senior Cup tie against Bromley at Hartsdown Park. His last senior appearance had been almost 20 months earlier. Paul was clearly delighted to be back and was up to some typical antics almost immediately - encouraging the crowd as only he could and cupping his hand to his ear when 'Syko' chants rang out. Margate won 3-1 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette's headline for its match report was "Sykes finally ends injury nightmare". Chris Kinnear said "Paul will still take a while to get fully ready, but he is keen to get back into the side. He was there at the beginning when we began to do well and has worked hard." The paper said "his appearance was one of an admittedly short list of highlights".

Just when it seemed that Paul's problems were behind him he went off injured in a reserve team game against Ramsgate on 20.11.01 and after recovering he picked up a hamstring injury in a 3-1 defeat against Deal Reserves on 5.12.01.

In February 2002 Paul was loaned to Kent League club Herne Bay and made his debut in a 2-1 home win over Greenwich on 9.2.02. Chris Kinnear told the Thanet Times "We'll see how Sykes gets on at Herne Bay, and he'll stay as long as it takes."

Paul scored three goals in seven appearances for Herne Bay but left the club before the end of the 2001/02 season. He didn't return to Margate and his cameo as a substitute in the Bromley game had been his only first team outing.

In August 2002 Paul signed for Dover who had just been relegated to the Southern League Premier Division and his first appearance for his new club was as a substitute in a 2-1 friendly win over Margate at Crabble on 3.8.02. He made his first competitive start in a 2-0 win at Moor Green on 17.8.02 and Paul scored his first goal for Dover on his home debut - a 2-1 win over Crawley on 19.8.02. He then struggled for goals but did score twice in a 3-2 home defeat against Sittingbourne in the Kent Senior Cup on 4.11.02.

Later in November 2002 Paul was loaned to Dartford and scored four goals in seven appearances there. He was also sent off for foul and abusive language in a game against Stamford on 17.12.02.

At the end of December 2002 he returned to Dover and on 25.1.03 Paul managed to get sent off before he'd even touched the ball just a minute after coming on as a substitute in a 1-0 defeat against Chippenham at Crabble. He chased down the visitors custodian who'd come out of the penalty area to clear and challenged for the ball but unfortunately Paul mistimed his tackle and caught the keeper. The general consensus was that there was no malice in his challenge and that a yellow card would have been a more fitting punishment. Paul eventually scored five goals from 26 appearances (19 as sub) for Dover before being released in May 2003.

He joined Dartford on a permanent basis in the summer of 2003 and Paul was reunited with his old Margate strike partner Martin Buglione there. Paul soon became a hugely popular player for the Darts. On 14.2.04 he played in went in goal only four minutes into a game at Erith & Belvedere and did well as the Darts lost 2-0. Paul also turned out in midfield and as a central defender during his time with the club. In November 2004 he left Dartford and manager Tommy Sampson explained "He has found it increasingly difficult with work commitments and a new addition to his family. He found it tough to juggle a life that consists of looking after his young son Thomas, spending time with wife Carly and making the 75-mile trip from his home between Dover and Hythe, working as a milkman, which involves getting up much earlier than most people, and playing for the Darts." Sampson added: "I don't want Paul to go and he doesn't want to really, but his life, family and health comes first. He will be a great addition to any club and it doesn't matter where he goes. He can play in the Southern, Ryman or Kent League but he has to train nearer to his home. He is a lovely lad who always did his best for us. Unfortunately he never had a real injury free run and it was my intention to turn him into a centre half."

Paul signed for Folkestone a few days after leaving the Darts and made his debut in a 4-3 home win over Cheshunt on 13.11.04. On 18.1.05 he was sent off in a Kent Senior Cup tie against his old club Dartford. He'd scored three goals in 23 appearances (three as sub) for Folkestone before lining up to play for them in the Kent Senior Cup semi-final against Margate at Cheriton Road on 12.4.05.

Paul typically exchanged some banter with Margate players and supporters before the kick-off but with Folkestone 1-0 down around 30 minutes into the game he collapsed in the Margate penalty area. Many people present initially thought that it was typical horseplay from Paul but it rapidly became apparent that something was seriously wrong. Margate's physio John Griffin and his Folkestone counterpart were quickly on the scene and tried to revive Paul along with other medical staff but after being taken to the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford Paul was tragically pronounced dead around 10.00 pm. He was only 28 and his passing was later found to be due to a form of Sudden Death Syndrome. There were tributes galore for Paul from players, supporters and managers all over Kent that proved beyond all doubt that he'd been one of the most popular football personalities in the county. An estimated 600 people attended his funeral with around 250 more outside the church in Buckland, Dover.

On the 15.4.05 the Isle of Thanet Gazette wrote "Kent football has been united by grief this week by the tragic death of Folkestone Invicta's former Margate striker Paul Sykes" and said he would "be remembered as much for his approachability and humour off the pitch as for his commitment and talent on it, always being the centre of clubhouse and dressing room attention". The article continued "His infectious sense of humour always seemed to penetrate the most difficult of times in football, and he often spoke of his genuine love for Margate - saying the club made him feel the town was as much a part of him as his hometown of Dover".

Chris Kinnear spoke to the Gazette and said "I knew Paul pretty much right through his career, and he played his best football under us. The sad thing was we were having a laugh and mucking about just before the game. He was a great fella. I told him that night that him and Phil Collins were the best strike pair we had. His death is such a shock and no one had any idea." Kinnear told the paper the Margate squad were struggling to cope and said "The players are not dealing with it very well, particularly Bill Edwards and Peter Trego, who were trying to help him and John Keister - who was the only player in our squad to play with Paul apart from Bill. The players were in a mess, and it will be difficult to get them in shape for the weekend." Kinnear added "They are all thinking what they could have done, but I don't think anyone could have done anything. When he went down everyone thought he was joking - but that was Sykesy."

In the wake of the tragedy Folkestone opted to allow Margate to progress to the Kent Senior Cup Final to play Dover and it was decided that all the proceeds of the game would go to Paul's family. In the programme for the match that took place on 2.5.05 Chris Kinnear and his assistant Kevin Raine wrote an article about Paul that described him as a "larger than life character" and "his own greatest critic". They recalled an away game at Newport County where Paul had been so disgusted with his own performance that he'd locked himself in the toilet at half-time and refused to go out for the second half. Over 2,000 people attended the final which Margate won 2-1.

In April 2006 a fund-raising match dubbed 'The Syko Challenge' was played at Hartsdown Park with the proceeds again going to Paul's family and around 500 people watched two teams mostly consisting of his former team-mates.

Towards the end of his life Paul had been joint manager of St.Margaret's Under-15's and Dartford later awarded the 'Paul Sykes Trophy' as a prize for outstanding young players.

name: Peter Sykes
other clubs: Dover Athletic
bio:
Dover-born younger brother of Paul Sykes who attended Archer's Court school in Dover and played for Dover's reserves during the 1995/96 season.

Peter joined Margate in the summer of 1997 and made his debut aged 18 on 29.7.97 when he wore the number eight shirt in a 3-1 win over Ramsgate at Hartsdown Park for the Link Music Cup. He made one more first team appearance as a substitute in a 2-0 home win over Baldock on 23.9.97, a game in which his brother Paul scored.

Peter then played for the reserves until breaking his leg in 4-0 defeat at Herne Bay on 4.11.97. The injury ended his senior football career.

Following his brother Paul's tragic death from a heart defect in 2005 Peter played in the Syko Challenge game at Hartsdown Park on 30.4.06 and later ran several London Marathons in aid of Cardiac Risk in the Young.

He was working as a postman in the Dover area in 2008.
