name: Don Wade
other clubs: Tottenham Hotspur (0), Wood Green Town, Edgware Town, West Ham United (40,7), Bedford Town, Gravesend & Northfleet and Ashford Town
bio:
Creative forward born in Tottenham - very close to the White Hart Lane stadium - who started his career in Spurs' junior sides.

Don joined Tottenham-based Spartan League club Wood Green Town for the 1943/44 campaign and played regularly in their first team as a teenager during the first half of the season.

During the early part of 1944 he moved on to Middlesex Senior League club Edgware Town and stayed with them until being called up to the Army in September 1944. Don scored a hat-trick in a 6-1 win over Southall in one of his last outings for Edgware. Just before he started his service, Don signed amateur forms for West Ham.

During the remainder of the Second World War, Don was prominent in army football and West Ham kept in touch with him.

After the conflict ended, he rejoined Edgware and played for them during 1945/46 and 1946/47.

At the start of December 1947, Don played in a reserve team game for West Ham - they d retained his amateur registration for over three years - and did so well that he was immediately signed as a professional. Without making another appearance for the reserves, Don made his first team debut for the Hammers aged 21 in a 3-0 home win over Fulham on 13.12.47, replacing future Margate winger Jackie Wood in the side. Don went on to score seven goals in 40 sporadic senior appearances spanning the 1947/48 to 1949/50 seasons. He was released by West Ham at the end of the 1951/52 campaign having not featured in the first team for over two years.

Don joined Bedford in the summer of 1952 and spent two seasons there without ever becoming a first team regular. He made a total of 35 appearances and scored 12 goals before being released at the end of the 1953/54 campaign.

He joined Gravesend & Northfleet in the summer of 1954 and spent the first half of 1954/55 there.

In January 1955 Don signed for Margate and made his debut on the left wing in a 2-1 defeat at home to Snowdown on 8.1.55. It turned out to be his only first team appearance and Don spent the rest of the 1954/55 season in the reserves.

In May 1955 Don joined Ashford and scored on his debut as they beat visitors Sheppey 2-1 in a Kent League game on 20.8.55. He made three more appearances and scored again in the last of them - a 5-2 home defeat at the hands of Ramsgate in the FA Cup on 24.9.55 - before leaving the club.

name: Steve Wadhams
other clubs: Sittingbourne, Whitstable Town, Ashford Town, Sheppey United, Chatham Town, Tonbridge and Lordswood
bio:
Energetic player who began his career with Sittingbourne and made his first senior appearances in 1974. Steve then joined Whitstable for the 1977/78 season before returning to Sittingbourne in the summer of 1980. He scored for the Brickies in their 4-3 defeat at the hands of Margate in an FA Cup tie on 16.9.80.

Steve had a loan spell with Ashford early in the 1981/82 season and scored three times in 12 Southern League appearances for the Nuts & Bolts before returning to the Bull Ground. He was Sittingbourne's top scorer with 21 goals during the 1982/83 campaign.

In August 1984 Steve signed for Sheppey and scored in a 2-0 win over Thanet United at Hartsdown Park on 12.1.85. He finished the 1984/85 season as Sheppey's leading marksman with 14 goals to his credit.

In the summer of 1985 Steve joined Thanet and made his debut on 24.8.85 as United beat Chichester City 3-1 in an FA Cup tie at Hartsdown. He had the distinction of scoring one of the goals. Steve continued his good start by scoring in a 3-1 win at Waterlooville two days later and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said that he "gave the home defence considerable problems". He was a regular in the side for the first two months of the season, playing as either an out-and-out striker or in midfield, but in November 1985 Steve was released and rejoined Sheppey. He'd scored four goals in 14 appearances (one as sub) but the local press had felt that he needed a target man to play alongside him in United's forward line and Steve had suffered from the lack of such a partner.

He stayed with Sheppey until early 1988 when he moved to Chatham. Steve scored for them in a 1-1 draw with Thanet at Maidstone Road on 9.4.88.

Steve then went back to Sittingbourne for the 1989/90 season and also had another spell with Sheppey during the campaign.

He returned to Sittingbourne for the 1990/91 season and then linked up with Tonbridge in October 1991.

Steve later finished his career with Kent League outfit Lordswood. He made a few appearances for the club during the 1996/97 season and played occasionally during 1997/98 aged 40 when he was also assistant manager.

In 2006 Steve was living in Harlow, Essex and ran his own plumbing and tiling business.

bio:
Dartford-born former Gillingham youth player who played for the Gills' junior sides from 1978/79 to 1980/81 before going on to have spells with Folkestone and Ashford later in the 1980/81 season.

Nigel joined Canterbury during the early part of the 1981/82 campaign and made seven Southern League appearances for City without scoring before joining Thanet United in March 1982.

Nigel made a one-off appearance for United in a 2-0 defeat against Hounslow at Hartsdown on 3.4.82 and left the club soon afterwards.

He later played for Gravesend & Northfleet, making one substitute appearance during 1982/83, and also had three separate spells with Darenth Heathside, starting with the 1984/85, 1985/86 (42 appearances, four goals) and 1986/87 seasons.

Nigel also had a stint in Australia with Bondi Marine and played for Hollisters in the North Kent Sunday League before returning to Darenth once more for the 1990/91 campaign.

He began his third spell with Darenth during the 1991/92 season and combined that with turning out for Hollisters. One of Nigel s team-mates for the Sunday club was former Margate player Bob Walter.

During the 2011/12 campaign Nigel was assistant manager of Gravesend-based Kent County League club Guru Nanak.

name: Bob Waldock
other clubs: Young Wolves
bio:
Midfielder who started his career with Barnsley-based outfit Young Wolves who played in the Yorkshire Intermediate League. Bob signed for them in the summer of 1957 aged 16 and the club was an unofficial feeder club for Wolverhampton Wanderers.

In the summer of 1962 Bob signed for Margate and local press reports said that he d been on the books of a London club during 1961/62. He was also said to have played for England s amateur side but records show that no player called Bob Waldock ever won a cap.

Having never even featured for the reserves, Bob made a one-off appearance as Margate beat Ramsgate 2-1 in a Southern League Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 5.9.62. A local press report said that he found the pace of the game rather too hot and added he also managed to put the ball over the bar from three yards with no one to beat close on the interval . Bob left the club shortly afterwards.

name: Ronnie Waldock
other clubs: Heanor Athletic, Coventry City (29,10), Sheffield United (56,10),  Scunthorpe United (103,46), Plymouth Argyle (19,6), Middlesbrough (35,7), Gillingham (71,15) and Selby Town
bio:
5' 8" tall player born in Heanor, Derbyshire who attended Loscoe Road School in Heanor and turned out for Modern Machine Tools as a youngster before moving on to Loscoe Youth Club.

Ronnie joined his hometown club Heanor Athletic ahead of the 1948/49 season, his late father Sydney had also played for them.

In January 1950 Ronnie was given a trial by Coventry and after featuring in two matches for their A team, scoring a hat-trick in one of them, he was given a professional contract early in February 1950. He went on to spend over four years at Highfield Road. Ronnie became a regular in the reserves but didn t make his senior debut until 27.9.52 as Coventry lost 2-0 at Millwall. He eventually made 29 first team appearances and scored ten goals.

In May 1954 he was transferred to 1st Division Sheffield United and made over 50 senior appearances for the Blades before moving to Scunthorpe in February 1957.

Ronnie averaged almost a goal every other game at Scunthorpe and then joined Plymouth in September 1959.

In January 1960, just four months after his last move, Ronnie was signed by Middlesbrough and played regularly for them.

In October 1961 Gillingham paid a then club record £6,000 fee for Ronnie. He spent three seasons at Priestfield and scored 15 times in 71 first team appearances before joining Margate in the summer of 1964.

Ronnie made his debut in a 2-0 win over Bath at Hartsdown Park on 22.8.64 and went on to become a fixture in the Margate side during the 1964/65 season, making 59 appearances and scoring twice. He was a solid, consistent performer in midfield although he also filled in at right-back on occasions. Hard work was a big part of Ronnie's game and the local press referred to his "sledgehammer tackles" as well as likening him to "a super-charged steam-roller".

Ronnie made 14 further appearances at the start of the 1965/66 season but in December 1965 he was released by the club for what were described as "reasons of a disciplinary nature".

After leaving Margate, he had a trial with Halifax and soon afterwards Ronnie joined Yorkshire League club Selby Town. After three seasons as a player with Selby, usually as captain, Ronnie was appointed as the club s player-manager in the summer of 1969.

In May 1988 he was one of numerous former Scunthorpe players introduced to the crowd before what was scheduled to be the club s final match at the Old Show Ground, a game against Exeter. Another ex-Margate player, Horace Cumner, was also part of the proceedings.

In 2010 Ronnie was living in Leeds and working locally as a caretaker at 'Football World' - a purpose built centre for 5-a-side football.

In 2013 he attended a Coventry City Legends Day and Ronnie was still living in Leeds in 2018 aged 86.

name: Bob Walker
other clubs: Gateshead, Brighton & Hove Albion (13,1), Ashford Town, Hartlepools United (0), Bournemouth & Boscombe Athletic (10,0), Colchester United (13+6,0), Dover, Bedford Town and Salisbury City
bio:
Defender born in Wallsend who started his career with Gateshead before being signed by Brighton in May 1962. Bob made 13 first team appearances for the Seagulls during 1962/63 and then dropped into non-league football to join Ashford in August 1963.

He made over 50 appearances for the Nuts & Bolts during the 1963/64 season and in August 1964 Bob returned to the Football League when he signed for Hartlepools.

Bob's stay there was very brief and in October 1964 he joined Margate on trial.

Bob made his debut on 19.10.64 in a 3-1 win over Deal at Hartsdown Park and went on to make a total of four appearances before leaving the club in November 1964.

In January 1965 he returned to league football when Bournemouth signed him.

He went on to spend a couple of years at Dean Court and then transferred to Colchester in July 1967. After making 19 senior appearances for them Bob dropped back into non-league football and played once for Bedford during 1968/69 before having a short spell at Dover during the 1969/70 season.

He later played for Salisbury.

name: Bruce Walker
other clubs: Hungerford Town, Swindon Town (36+3,7), Bradford City (28+1,1), Exeter City (24+3,2), Hereford United, Nuneaton Borough, Newbury Town and Kintbury Rangers
bio:
Pacy player with a powerful left foot shot born in the West Berkshire village of West Woodhay who began his career with Hungerford in the Hellenic League as a 15 year-old but was then picked up by Third Division club Swindon in 1963.

Bruce was in the Swindon side that reached the FA Youth Cup Final in 1964 and scored in the second leg of the tie against Manchester United at Old Trafford on 30.4.64. A crowd of 25,563 saw United run out 4-1 winners to take the trophy with a 5-2 aggregate score. George Best was in the United team and future England player David Sadler scored a hat-trick for them.

After playing in Swindon s youth and reserve sides for the next 18 months, Bruce finally made his first team debut in a 2-2 draw at Grimsby on 27.12.65 and he made one further senior appearance before the end of the 1965/66 campaign.

During 1966/67 he featured regularly in Swindon s first team and Bruce scored six times from a total of 29 appearances. His most significant goal was the equaliser that secured a 1-1 draw with First Division visitors Nottingham Forest in an FA Cup 5th Round replay on 14.3.67. Swindon lost the second replay 3-0 at neutral Villa Park.

Bruce fell out of favour during the 1967/68 season and only made eight first team appearances, three of them as a substitute. He scored once and the goal came in his last league outing - a match at Southport on 18.11.67. Bruce took to the field as a substitute in the 55th minute and two minutes later fired Swindon ahead. The match finished 1-1. His final appearance for Swindon came in an FA Cup tie against visitors Salisbury on 12.12.67.

In March 1968 Bruce was signed by Bradford City for a fee of 5,000 and he made a further 29 first team appearances for them during a 15 month stay in Yorkshire. He then moved to Exeter in June 1969.

Bruce played 27 senior games for Exeter during 1969/70 before joining Hereford.

He went on to make around 50 appearances for Hereford before September 1971 when he joined Nuneaton on loan. Bruce scored three times from six outings for the club before briefly returning to Hereford in November 1971.

In December 1971 he joined Margate, initially on a month's trial, and made his debut on 18.12.71 as Margate entertained Guildford at Hartsdown Park. Bruce played on the left wing and scored in a 2-1 win. The Thanet Times said that he "looked a good capture". His strong, incisive wing play ensured that his transfer became permanent in January 1972 and very early in his Margate career Bruce's shooting prowess led the local press to say that he had "a deadly left foot".

He scored nine goals in the 19 appearances he made before the end of the 1971/72 season and they included three penalties and a direct free-kick in a 2-2 draw with Dartford on 1.1.72. Bruce also scored with a cannonball shot from 25 yards as Margate crushed Ramsgate 5-1 on 17.4.72. That was shortly after he'd returned from a double fracture of the jaw suffered in a game against Merthyr on 4.3.72. The injury was expected to have ended Bruce's season but he surprised everybody by coming back after just over a month on the sidelines and featuring in the last few games of the campaign.

During the 1972/73 season Bruce really established himself on Margate's left wing and he made 56 appearances (one as sub). His powerful long-range shooting again came to the fore and was responsible for many of his 20 goals. The local press said that Bruce had "an explosive left foot" and described the shots it invariably delivered as his "redoubtable Long Toms", a phrase previously reserved for Margate legend Bryan Clifton.

On 9.12.72 Bruce featured in a 1-0 win at Walton & Hersham in the FA Cup 2nd Round and he then played in perhaps Margate s biggest ever match - a 6-0 defeat against visitors Tottenham in the 3rd Round on 13.1.73.

His best goal of the campaign was a dipping 25-yarder to clinch a 1-0 home win over Waterlooville on 27.1.73 and on 12.3.73 Bruce scored direct from a corner when his low in-swinger found the net in a 2-0 win over Hillingdon at Hartsdown Park. He also got what the local press called "a gem of a goal" from a position way out on the left wing during a 2-1 home defeat against Nuneaton on 17.3.73 and cracked home a stunning volley in a 4-0 win over visitors Canterbury in the Kent Floodlight Cup on 26.3.73. Bruce then scored twice in a 3-1 win at Hillingdon on 21.4.73 and one of his goals was another fine volley.

The 1973/74 season was another good one for Bruce, he began the campaign on the left wing as usual but also had spells playing at left-back. He performed admirably in that role but it was as an attacker that he made the most impact.

Bruce scored 18 goals in his 61 appearances and many of his strikes were memorable. On 29.9.73 he blasted home a shot in a 2-2 draw with Hillingdon having "steamed in like an express train" according to the Thanet Times and on 2.10.73 Bruce scored twice in a 4-2 defeat at the hands of Ashford at Hartsdown Park. One of his goals was a 25 yard effort and the other was a 30 yard free-kick, backing up Bruce's reputation as a dead ball expert. He fired in another direct free-kick in a 2-0 win over Dover on 12.1.74 and on 2.5.74 he scored both goals in a 2-0 win at Barnet, a game in which the Thanet Times said Bruce unleashed "a frightening barrage of shots". On 13.4.74 he was in the side that won the Kent Senior Cup with a 2-0 win at Maidstone.

During the summer of 1974 one of Bruce's vicious shots broke team-mate Dave Rouse's hand in training and the 1974/75 season saw him again divide his appearances between left-back and the left wing. He also helped with the coaching of the club's juniors. Bruce made 58 appearances and scored 13 goals, an impressive tally considering he spent much of the season in defence. Bruce scored twice from direct free-kicks during the campaign and found the net with a trademark 25-yarder in a 5-1 over Poole on 11.1.75. On 5.4.75 he was in the Margate side that lost 2-0 at home to Kettering in the first leg of the Southern League Cup Final. On 12.4.75 Bruce scored a brilliant solo goal - his 60th for the club - in the second leg at Kettering, beating three defenders before walking the ball into the net. It helped Margate to secure a 1-1 draw that wasn t sufficient to claim the trophy.

At the end of the season he was announced on Margate s retained list but at that time Bruce was about to move out of Thanet to work alongside his father in a rural pub near Newbury. Manager Les Riggs told the East Kent Times I will be chatting with Bruce because the distance of his new home from Margate presents travel and cost problems which must be investigated. Bruce ended up leaving the club and Riggs said "he was an excellent servant to the club and I am sorry to lose him."

After featuring in a pre-season friendly for his original club Hungerford, Bruce joined Newbury of the Hellenic League for the 1975/76 campaign and also played for them during the 1976/77 season.

In the summer of 1977 he was appointed as player-manager of North Berkshire League outfit Kintbury Rangers. Bruce went on to spend around ten years with the club and guided them to promotion to the Hellenic League. He made his last appearances for them during the 1986/87 season aged 40.

In 2003 Bruce was living in Hampshire and by 2011 he d moved to Wareham in Dorset.

name: Charlie Walker
bio: 3 years with Arsenal and regular in London Combination team. September 1939 returned to home in Margate at outbreak of WWII and offered to play for club if required, football had just been suspended.

name: Charlie Walker
other clubs: Arsenal (0), West Ham United (121,0) and Ashford Town
bio:
5' 10" tall, Nottingham-born defender raised in Sheffield who began his senior career with Lopham Street United Methodists. They played in both the Sheffield City League and the Sheffield Amateur League. Charlie made his first appearances for them during the 1930/31 season aged 19 and was part of the side that won the Sheffield Amateur League Cup by beating Thorpe Hesley Victoria 3-0 on 25.4.31. He was still with Lopham Street when Arsenal invited him for a trial in November 1932 and on 23.11.32 Charlie played for a Gunners side in a match at Oxford.

In January 1933 Arsenal signed Charlie and he played in their junior sides until being loaned to Margate early in 1935 as part of the 'nursery' arrangement the club had with the Gunners.

Charlie made his debut at left-back in a 1-1 draw with Dartford at Hartsdown Park on 16.2.35 and stayed at Margate until the end of the 1935/36 campaign making 66 appearances in all and scoring four times.

After briefly returning to Arsenal, Charlie was transferred to West Ham early in May 1936 and he went on to make 121 first team appearances there spanning the 1936/37-1939/40 seasons before World War II began. He also turned out for the Hammers during the conflict, making 65 appearances without scoring, and was a member of the side that beat Blackburn 1-0 to win the Football League War Cup Final at Wembley in 1940.

At the start of the war Charlie was initially enlisted into the police, along with many other footballers, but as some his friends had joined the armed forces he decided to sign up for the RAF. Whilst serving on the Burma border in India towards the end of the war Charlie played for an England side against a Scottish X1 in several services games that took place as part of an 'All India' tour.

When hostilities ended Charlie returned to Margate and became player-manager on a £7 per week contract when the club re-formed for the 1946/47 season. He was an influential player for the club as they won the Kent League title and he made a total of 34 appearances without scoring during the campaign as a left-back or centre-back. In his central role Charlie often marked his opposing centre-forward out of the game and he was particularly strong in the air.

During the 1947/48 season Charlie made a further 44 appearances without scoring in another Kent League title winning campaign and played as well as ever in Margate's defence. On 6.5.48 he was part of the side that beat visitors Ramsgate 2-1 to win the Kent League Cup Final and on 8.5.48 Charlie played at centre-back as Margate won 4-1 at Gravesend & Northfleet to claim the Kent Senior Shield, completing a three trophy haul for the season. It was his last outing for the club.

In June 1948 Charlie was sacked as Margate s player-manager, despite winning the Kent League two years running, as the club s management committee felt that a new business interest he had - a grocery shop in Canterbury Road, Westbrook - meant that he wouldn't be able to devote enough time to Margate. Charlie's dismissal was highly controversial and a special meeting of club members was convened to discuss the possibility of him being re-instated. However the decision to terminate his contract was upheld and as a result Charlie joined Ashford as their player-manager for the 1948/49 season.

He led the Nuts & Bolts to the Kent League title at the first attempt to complete a remarkable personal treble of three championships in his first three seasons as a manager. Charlie remained in charge of Ashford for the 1949/50 campaign and on 16.3.50 he spent most of a 5-1 defeat at Ramsgate playing in goal after keeper Donovan Moore had to go off injured. He continued as Ashford s player-manager until May 1951 when Ken Horrigan left Margate to take over, around the time of Charlie s 40th birthday.

He then had a spell as manager of Ramsgate, taking over from former Margate player George Robertson on 12.5.51, but the role was only part-time due to his business commitments.

In January 1953, Charlie was replaced as the Rams manager by Scottish international Jimmy Blair but he stayed on as Blair s assistant. Charlie eventually left Ramsgate in 1953 and in 1961 he emigrated to the USA aged 50.

Charlie initially lived in Plainfield, New Jersey and worked as a mechanical engineer there. He coached a local Irish side for two years during that time. He then moved to Florida where he coached the football team at the high school that his grand-daughter attended. The side had only just started playing when Charlie arrived but he led them to two local league titles.

On 16.8.75 he made a return to Hartsdown Park, watching Margate s first Southern League Premier Division game of the season against Telford. The visitors won 2-1 and the Thanet Times noted that Charlie must have been shocked by the meagre attendance of 515, in stark contrast to the crowds during his time with Margate.

In 1977 Charlie briefly returned to the UK and lived in Margate but after just a few months he went back to the USA.

Looking back on his career during another visit to the UK in September 1988, Charlie said "I was never a great player, but I was strong and reliable." With regard to his dismissal as Margate's manager he explained "it came as a complete surprise. I was never given a reason and to this day I do not know what I did wrong. I was not so much bitter as puzzled."

Charlie died on 7.5.90, a few days before his 79th birthday, and at the time he was based in Jacksonville, Florida.

name: Cyril Walker
other clubs: Hitchin Town, Leavesden Mental Hospital, Watford (0), Gillingham (11,4), Sheffield Wednesday (4,0), Chelmsford City, Shorts Sports, Norwich City (3,2), Chatham Town, Dartford, Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Sittingbourne and Gravesend & Northfleet
bio:
Newport Pagnell-born centre-forward who had spells with Hitchin Town and Leavesden Mental Hospital before being signed by Watford in November 1935. Cyril didn't make the first team there and in June 1937 he moved on to Gillingham.

Cyril scored four goals in 11 senior appearances for the Gills during the early part of the 1937/38 season.

In October 1937 Cyril left Gillingham after just four months there and joined Sheffield Wednesday where he made four first team appearances before the end of the campaign.

After leaving Hillsborough he dropped into non-league football, linking up with Chelmsford City for 1938/39 and then having a stint with Shorts Sports before World War II.

During the conflict Cyril served in the R.A.F. and featured in representative games for them. He also played in 34 wartime matches for Norwich, scoring a remarkable 37 goals.

After hostilities ceased Cyril officially signed for Norwich in August 1946 and marked his debut by scoring the winning goal with two minutes left as the Canaries beat Cardiff 2-1 in a Division Three South game. In the weeks that followed Cyril played twice more for the first team but after scoring in a 5-1 home defeat against Swindon he was dropped to the reserves despite a record of two goals from three outings. He never played in Norwich s senior side again and left Carrow Road in the summer of 1947.

In June 1947, Cyril dropped out of the professional game once again and signed for Chatham of the Kent League. He stayed there until the end of December 1948 when he was transferred to Dartford.

Cyril started the 1950/51 season with Snowdown Colliery Welfare but in March 1951 he moved to Margate, shortly after his 37th birthday.

Cyril scored on his debut for Margate - a 4-1 home defeat at the hands of Folkestone on 23.3.51. He also found the net in his next game - a 3-3 draw at Whitstable on 26.3.51. Cyril played twice more before the end of the season and took his goal tally to three in four appearances when he scored in a 2-1 defeat against his old club Snowdown at Hartsdown Park on 11.5.51.

Cyril stayed with Margate for the 1951/52 campaign but only made two first team appearances. However he scored 14 goals for the reserves. He was eventually released by the club in November 1952 without featuring in the senior side during 1952/53.

At the start of December 1952, Cyril signed for Sittingbourne at the same time as former Margate player Frank Johnson.

In November 1953, Cyril left Sittingbourne to join Gravesend & Northfleet and he then linked up with Chatham again in February 1954, around the time of his 40th birthday.

Cyril finished his playing career with Chatham and then became part of the club s backroom staff after retiring. He was manager of Chatham s reserve team during the 1957/58 season. On 9.4.60 he made an emergency appearance for Chatham aged 46 in a 1-0 win over Charlton A .

In later years Cyril had a spell as Beckenham's manager.

He died in the Medway area in July 2002 aged 88.

name: George Wallace
other clubs: Fraserburgh (Scotland), Herne Bay, Phoenix Rovers, Canterbury City and Whitstable Town
bio:
Glasgow-born defender who played for Highland League club Fraserburgh before moving to England in 1988.

George joined Thanet United for the start of the 1988/89 season and made his debut in a 2-2 draw at Buckingham on 27.8.88. The Thanet Times said that he "took the eye with some timely interceptions" at right-back. George then dropped back into the reserves and missed United's next five games before returning to the side for an FA Trophy tie against Hitchin at Hartsdown on 24.9.88. He played as a centre-back in a 1-0 win. He then wore the number five shirt in two of Thanet's next three games and the Thanet Times said that he "marshalled his backs in fine style" as United lost 3-1 at home to Fisher in an FA Cup tie on 1.10.88. After playing in a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Canterbury in a Southern League Cup tie on 11.10.88 George returned to the reserves and in November 1988 he left the club and joined Herne Bay. He'd made four first team appearances and played seven games for the reserves, scoring once for them. The Thanet Times said he had "looked a useful defender during his short stay".

George stayed at Herne Bay until moving on to Kent County League club Phoenix Rovers just after the start of the 1989/90 season. He was sent off for them in a match against Herne Bay early in 1990 and had to be escorted off by team-mates after initially refusing to leave the field.

George started the 1992/93 campaign at Canterbury City and in September 1992 he had to play an entire game in goal for City's reserves. They only had eight players and went down 11-0 to their Chatham counterparts.

George later linked up with Whitstable and played exclusively for their reserves during the early part of 1994/95 before dropping into local Thanet amateur football for a few more seasons.

In 2011 he was still living in Thanet and refereeing in local football.

name: Darren Walmsley
other clubs: New Romney, Hythe United, Ramsgate, Canterbury City, Tonbridge Angels, Folkestone Invicta, Tunbridge Wells and Hythe Town
bio:
Aldershot-born attacker who started his senior career with Kent County League club New Romney before joining Margate towards the end of the 1991/92 season, around the time of his 17th birthday.

Darren made a few appearances for Margate's Under-18's in the last couple of months of the campaign and stayed with the club for 1992/93.

On 20.10.92 he made his first team debut when he came on as a substitute in a Southern League Cup tie at Dover that Margate lost 3-1. Darren then made two more sub appearances before returning to the Under-18's at the end of October 1992.

He was a prolific scorer at Under-18 level and on 17.1.93 Darren bagged four goals in a 7-0 win at Faversham. In total he scored 24 goals in 29 Under 18 appearances.

On 6.3.93 Darren returned to first team action when he came on during a 4-0 win over Burnham at Hartsdown Park and he made his first start for Margate when he played on the left wing in a 1-0 win at Braintree on 3.4.93. Darren then featured in the last five matches of the campaign, three times as a substitute and twice on the left wing. The Thanet Times said that he showed "some silky skills" in a 1-0 home win over Canterbury on 10.4.93 and praised Darren's "numerous impressive contributions" in a 0-0 draw at Buckingham on 17.4.93. The paper also reported that he "gave a good account of himself" during a 2-1 win at Havant on 24.4.93 and Darren played his last game of the season in a 1-1 draw at Dunstable on 1.5.93. He'd made a total of 11 appearances (eight as a substitute) without scoring.

Darren featured in some of Margate's friendlies ahead of the 1993/94 campaign but after failing to make a first team appearance in the opening weeks of the season he was loaned to Hythe United in September 1993. In November 1993 he was sent on loan again, joining Ramsgate, and Margate then sent him back to Hythe once more in January 1994. Darren spent the rest of 1993/94 there and didn't make any first team appearances for Margate during the campaign.

In the summer of 1994 he scored twice in Margate's pre-season friendlies and Darren made his first competitive appearance of the 1994/95 campaign when he came on as a substitute in a 5-3 win at Peacehaven & Telscombe in an FA Cup tie on 27.9.94. He then featured in Margate's next 11 games, starting six of them. Darren played at left-back, as a left winger and up front and on 4.10.94 he scored his first goal for the club in a 5-1 win at Fisher. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "slotted in well at left-back and often took the eye with his keen overlapping" in a 2-2 home draw with Fisher on 18.10.94 and on 22.10.94 Darren scored again in a 3-0 win at Erith & Belvedere. After a 1-0 defeat against Bury on 29.10.94 the Thanet Times said of Darren "he grows in stature with every game" and after he'd had a spell on the sidelines the Gazette said Darren made "a welcome re-appearance" when he scored in a 2-2 draw at Fisher on 26.12.94. The paper reported that he "displayed astute close control" before firing home. After making two more sub appearances in January 1995 Darren was loaned to Canterbury at the start of February.

He scored twice on his debut for City and later bagged a ten minute hat-trick in a 6-0 win over Kent Police before returning to Hartsdown Park in April 1995.

On 22.4.95 Darren made his first Margate appearance since 14.1.95 when he came on as a sub in a 2-2 draw at Poole and he also came off the bench in a 3-2 home defeat against Weymouth on 25.4.95. On 29.4.95 Darren started in midfield as Margate drew 1-1 at Newport IOW but he didn't feature again and ended the season having scored three times in 19 appearances (11 as sub).

After playing in some of Margate's friendlies ahead of the 1995/96 campaign Darren returned to Canterbury for the start of the season proper and then joined Tonbridge in the summer of 1996.

Towards the end of 1997 he moved on to Folkestone and Darren later had a lengthy spell with Tunbridge Wells before linking up with Hythe.

His first season at Hythe was 2002/03 and Darren was still with the club during the 2007/08 campaign by which time he was assistant player-manager of the reserves and rarely played for the first team.

Darren was working as a sales representative for Sony in 2008.

name: Bob Walter
other clubs: Gillingham (0), Canterbury City, Dover and Crawley Town
bio:
5' 10" tall versatile, tough-tackling player born in Dartford who started his career at Gillingham as a junior, appearing in their youth team as early as the 1970/71 campaign.

Bob then moved to Canterbury during the 1971/72 season and he went on to make 160 Southern League appearances (seven as sub) for City, scoring 11 goals, during a six year spell at Kingsmead.

In the summer of 1977 Bob joined Margate in an exchange deal that took Greg Wood to Canterbury and he made his debut in a 3-3 draw with Ashford in a Kent Senior Shield tie at Hartsdown Park on 9.8.77. Bob went on to make 46 appearances during the 1977/78 campaign, playing as a centre-back or in midfield, and was a model of consistency as Margate won the Southern League 1st Division (South) title. He scored five goals during the season, including two in a 6-3 win at Tonbridge on 26.12.77.

During the 1978/79 campaign Bob made a further 53 appearances (three as a substitute), once again in midfield or defence, and scored eight goals. They included what the Thanet Times called a "magnificent running header" in 2-0 win at Hastings on 14.4.79. The local press described Bob as being "a tremendous battler" during the season. His efforts secured him the club's 'Player of the Year' award but just before the start of the 1979/80 campaign Bob left the club after being involved in a dispute. He then joined Dover.

Bob spent two and a half seasons at Crabble but found himself in Dover's reserves for most of the 1979/80 and 1980/81 campaigns. During 1980/81 he played ten games on loan at Crawley but scored twice for Dover in a 3-0 win over Margate on 14.2.81. Bob then became a regular in the Dover side during the 1981/82 season, up until he returned to Hartsdown Park in March 1982 to join Thanet United.

The first game of Bob's comeback was a 2-0 defeat at Ashford on 6.3.82 and he quickly showed that he was as uncompromising as ever. He went on to make 14 appearances before the end of the season as United finished bottom of the Southern League Southern Division and usually played as a centre-back.

Bob stayed with Thanet for the 1982/83 season and he was virtually ever-present, playing 40 times and scoring three goals. He usually played in midfield during the campaign but also turned out at centre-back and even had a few games as a striker. His best goal was a clever chip in a 2-1 win over Erith & Belvedere at Hartsdown Park on 26.3.83.

Bob began the 1983/84 season as a fixture in the side once more. The Thanet Times described him as being "a tower of strength" and a "midfield dynamo". On 21.9.83 Bob had to be carried off during an FA Cup replay against Pagham after he was kicked in the face and he lost several teeth as a result.

In October 1983 Bob fell off some scaffolding at work and injured his back. That forced him to miss two months of the season but Bob went on to turn in some outstanding performances, mostly in central defence, after his return to action in December 1983. He'd made 30 appearances (one as sub) when he failed to turn up for a game at Crawley on 7.4.84. That resulted in Bob being released by the club and manager John Wickens said "it is a sad blow to lose a player of his calibre."

Bob's period of exile lasted until November 1984 when he rejoined United and he made his first appearance of the 1984/85 campaign when he came on as a substitute in a 1-1 draw at Chatham on 20.11.84. Bob then became a fixture in the Thanet side for the remainder of the season, initially playing in midfield before settling down at centre-back once again. He was as dependable as ever and the Thanet Times said that Bob "reigned supreme in the middle" as Thanet beat Dunstable 2-0 at home in the club's last Southern League game of the campaign. During the season Bob made a total of 35 appearances (four as sub) and in doing so he took his career tally for the club past 200 matches.

Work commitments led to Bob leaving the club once more in the summer of 1985 but in January 1986 he rejoined United for his fourth spell at Hartsdown Park.

He made his first appearance of the 1985/86 season when he came on as a substitute in a 3-1 home win over Waterlooville on 11.1.86 and Bob then played regularly, although often as sub, during the remainder of the campaign. He usually featured in a midfield role and made a total of 18 appearances (five as sub) before leaving United in May 1986. Bob's final game had been a 2-1 defeat at the hands of Salisbury at Hartsdown on 24.4.86, more than eight years after he'd made his debut for Margate.

Bob later played in the North Kent Sunday League and was turning out for Hollisters during the 1988/89 campaign. He was still with the club during 1991/92 aged 38.

In a 1978/79 season Margate programme Bob revealed that his favourite player was Nobby Stiles and at that time he worked as a glazier.

name: Dale Walton
other clubs: Dover, Canterbury City, Ashford Town, Whitstable Town and Herne Bay
bio:
Ramsgate-born player who began his career in Thanet youth football and had trials at Coventry during the 1973/74 and 1975/76 seasons.

Dale then joined Dover and played for their reserves during the 1977/78 campaign. At the time his father Gordon, a former Margate full-back, was Dover's reserve team manager.

In the summer of 1978 Dale moved to Canterbury and he was the only ever-present in City's Southern League side during the 1978/79 season, making 40 appearances and scoring three goals.

Dale joined Ashford for the start of the 1979/80 campaign and made five Southern League appearances there before moving on to Margate in October 1979.

He made his debut in a 0-0 draw at Dartford on 9.10.79 and went on to make a total of 39 appearances during the remainder of 1979/80. Dale usually played in midfield but also featured as a centre-back and in an attacking role during the season. He scored twice, both goals coming in matches against Chelmsford. Dale scored the only goal in a 1-0 win at Hartsdown Park on 5.1.80 and was on target again as Margate won the return game 2-1 on 12.4.80.

In the summer of 1980 Dale left the club and joined Whitstable for the 1980/81 campaign. He stayed with the Oystermen for the 1981/82 season too.

He then joined Herne Bay for the 1982/83 campaign and went on to spend several years with the club during the 1980's before returning to Whitstable for a further spell that spanned the 1985/86-1991/92 seasons.

Dale's brother Grant also played for several Kent League clubs and Dale was still living locally in 2011. At that time he was working as a Building Surveyor for Thanet District Council.

name: Gordon Walton
other clubs: Boldon Colliery Welfare, Murton Colliery Welfare, Eppleton Colliery Welfare, South Shields, Lincoln City (0), Ramsgate Athletic, Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Deal Town, Canterbury City and Whitstable Town
bio:
5 9 tall, solid, reliable full-back born in Easington Lane who began his senior career with Boldon Colliery Welfare in his native North East. Gordon played for them during the 1952/53 campaign before switching to Murton Colliery Welfare part way through the season.

He stayed with Murton, who played in the Wearside League, until the end of the 1953/54 campaign.

Gordon signed for Eppleton Colliery Welfare ahead of 1954/55 and came to the attention of Charlton during the season.

In the summer of 1955 he linked up with South Shields and Gordon played in each of their North Eastern League matches during 1955/56.

In June 1956 he was signed by 2nd Division club Lincoln and Gordon went on to spend three years with the Imps without ever featuring in the first team.

In the summer of 1959 he joined Ramsgate and was in and out of the Rams senior side before signing for Margate in March 1960.

Gordon made his debut in a 3-0 win over Tunbridge Wells at Hartsdown Park on 19.3.60 and the local press said his "creditable display" was a "pleasing feature" of the match. He went on to make a total of nine appearances at right-back before the end of the 1959/60 season.

Gordon then really established himself during the 1960/61 season and made 49 appearances without scoring.

In the summer of 1961, Gordon suffered a severe thigh injury which kept him out of action for the first few weeks of the 1961/62 campaign. In the meantime, new signing Bill Parry impressed at right-back and as a result Gordon spent most of the season in the reserves. On 6.1.62 he scored a hat-trick in a 5-2 home win over Canterbury City Reserves when playing as a makeshift centre-forward. Gordon only featured seven times for the first team but scored in a 1-1 draw at Ramsgate in the Kent Floodlight Cup on 27.3.62, again when playing up front. He was released at the end of the 1961/62 season.

After a few months out of football, Gordon linked up with Snowdown in October 1962.

He then joined Deal and spent the 1963/64 campaign with them before moving to Whitstable for 1964/65. After two seasons with the Oystermen Gordon joined Canterbury in the summer of 1966.

Gordon went on to spend six seasons (1966/67-1971/72) with City, making 146 Southern League appearances without scoring. He became City's player-assistant manager during 1970/71 and eventually left the club in the summer of 1972.

Gordon then returned to Whitstable and stayed there until his retirement as a player.

In April 1974 Gordon became Coventry's south-east scout and in the summer of 1975 he was appointed as Ramsgate's youth team coach and assistant first team manager to Alf Bentley. Gordon combined those roles with his Coventry duties. However he was sacked by the Rams in January 1976, along with Bentley, during a financial crisis at Southwood.

During the 1976/77 season, Gordon was player-manager of local Sunday club Deccar Sports and he continued to manage them for several years, alongside his other roles in football.

Gordon was reserve team manager at Dover during 1977/78 and he was known for unearthing talented youngsters, including future Thanet United striker Gary Pugh. Gordon then returned to Canterbury and during the 1978/79 campaign he was assistant manager there.

Gordon s son Dale played for Margate during the 1979/80 season and another son, Grant, played for Ramsgate during the early 1980's.

Gordon was still living in Thanet in 2012.

name: Dave Ward
other clubs: Charlton Athletic (0), Bromley, Tonbridge, Alma Swanley, Chatham Town, Dulwich Hamlet, Gravesend & Northfleet, Fisher Athletic, Erith & Belvedere, Sittingbourne, Thamesmead Town, Fisher '93, Folkestone Invicta, VCD Athletic, Hythe Town, Leatherhead, Greenwich Borough, Ramsgate and Herne Bay
bio:
Much-travelled aggressive left-sided player who started his career with Charlton before joining Bromley for the 1983/84 season.

In February 1984 Dave moved on to Tonbridge and during the 1984/85 campaign he had a short spell with Alma Swanley before returning to the Angels.

Dave left Tonbridge to join Folkestone in the summer of 1986 and then signed for Chatham at the start of 1988 before joining Dulwich for the 1988/89 season.

He returned to Kent for the 1989/90 campaign and scored twice in 26 appearances (nine as sub) for Gravesend & Northfleet before briefly returning to Tonbridge towards the end of the season.

Dave's next move took him to Fisher for the start of the 1990/91 campaign and he then had a spell with Erith & Belvedere before signing for Sittingbourne in February 1992.

He was the Brickies' captain during the 1992/93 season and in September 1993 Dave joined Margate.

He made his debut as a substitute in a 3-2 win at Erith & Belvedere on 7.9.93 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Dave "showed some nice touches in midfield during the brief time he was on the pitch". On 18.9.93 he made his first start in midfield in a 2-0 defeat against Worthing at Hartsdown Park but shortly before the end of the game Dave was sent off for a second bookable offence. His second booking was for a foul that the Thanet Times said was "committed more in frustration than malice". After serving a three match ban Dave returned to the Margate side as a substitute in a 1-1 draw at Havant on 16.10.93 and the Thanet Times said he "proved outstanding at the back" after coming on early in the game. He then enjoyed a run in the side, featuring in midfield or at left-back, and on 23.10.93 Dave scored the only goal of the game to give Margate a 1-0 home win over Erith & Belvedere. On 9.11.93 he played in a 1-0 win at Fisher in the Kent Senior Cup but it was Dave's last start for Margate. He made three further substitute appearances but in the last of them, a 3-2 defeat at Poole on 27.11.93, Dave was sent off again after 82 minutes. He'd only been on the field for three minutes after coming on when a linesman spotted an off the ball incident and Dave was dismissed. He was released a few days later having scored once in 13 appearances (five as sub).

After leaving Margate Dave had a spell with Thamesmead before rejoining Sittingbourne for the start of the 1994/95 campaign. He went back to Fisher later in the season and then linked up with Folkestone Invicta in the summer of 1995.

Dave was released by Invicta before the end of 1995/96 and joined VCD as player-coach. Whilst playing for them he was sent off for an altercation with a spectator, an incident that led to a lengthy ban.

Dave moved on to Hythe for the start of the 1996/97 season and became captain and later assistant manager there before returning to Folkestone for 1997/98.

During the 1998/99 campaign he played for Leatherhead and then Greenwich Borough where he was also assistant manager.

In March 1999 Dave went back to Erith & Belvedere and stayed with the Deres until becoming Ramsgate's player-assistant manager towards the end of 1999.

In the summer of 2000 he became manager of Ashford's Under-14's side.

During 2002/03 Dave was manager of Ashford's Under-16's and he then became Greenwich's manager for the 2003/04 season.

During the 202005/06 campaign he was player-manager of Thamesmead's reserves and in September 2006 Dave joined Herne Bay as a player.

He made 19 appearances (ten as sub) during the remainder of the 2006/07 season and in the summer of 2007 he became the Bay's player-coach. Dave made five appearances as a sub for Herne Bay's first team during the opening weeks of the 2007/08 campaign but he was sacked by the club after being sent off in a 4-1 home defeat at the hands of Colliers Wood in the FA Vase on 22.9.07. He was booked for a bad tackle and then had 'words' with the referee which resulted in another yellow card followed by a red.

name: Scott Ward
other clubs: Luton Town (1,0), Boreham Wood, Chesham, Millwall (0), Dulwich Hamlet, Grays Athletic, Blackpool (0), Wycombe Wanderers (0), Lewes, Crawley Town, Plymouth Argyle (0) and London Colney
bio:
6' 2" keeper born in Brent, London who started his career with Luton and played 14 times for their youth team during the 1997/98 season. Scott kept nine clean sheets and featured in the South East Counties League Cup Final against West Ham.

In the summer of 1998 Luton gave Scott a YTS contract but in October 1998 the club decided to upgrade his deal to a three-year full-time contract as he reached the age of 17. He continued to be the Hatters' regular youth team keeper throughout the 1998/99 and 1999/00 campaigns and during the latter season Scott also made five reserve team appearances as well as being an unused substitute for the first team on 16 occasions.

He spent the majority of the 2000/01 campaign as Luton's third-choice but towards the end of the season Scott became second-choice and featured in nine reserve team matches.

On 3.5.01 he was on the subs bench as Luton's first team travelled to Brentford for a Division 2 match and after only two minutes Scott found himself making a surprise senior debut aged 19 when keeper Mark Ovendale was sent off. Scott's first task was to face the penalty conceded by Ovendale and remarkably he saved it. The game ended 2-2 and curiously Brentford's keeper was Ole Gottskalksson who would later take over from Scott as Margate's custodian. Future Margate player Gareth Graham also featured as a substitute for Brentford.

Scott stayed with Luton for the 2001/02 campaign but fell down the goalkeeping pecking order and in November 2001 he was loaned to Boreham Wood. Scott only played twice there before injury curtailed his loan and he returned to Kenilworth Road. He eventually played six reserve team games but at the end of the season Scott was released.

During the summer of 2002 he played in some friendlies for Gravesend & Northfleet but Scott ended up joining Chesham for the start of the 2002/03 campaign proper.

Before he'd played a competitive game for Chesham Scott was signed by Millwall on a non-contract basis and in October 2002 they loaned him to Dulwich.

Having returned to Millwall Scott was released before the end of 2002 and he made four appearances for Grays before rejoining Dulwich on a permanent basis in January 2003.

At the start of February 2003, shortly after he'd returned to Dulwich, Scott had a trial at Blackpool where he played for the reserves but he wasn't taken on by the club and saw out the remainder of the 2002/03 season with Dulwich. In total he made 25 Isthmian League appearances there in his two spells with the club.

In the summer of 2003 Scott had trials with both Gillingham and York but he ended up starting the 2003/04 campaign with Dulwich once again. In February 2004 he had a trial at Wycombe but after featuring in the reserves he returned to Dulwich and by the end of the season Scott had made 24 Isthmian League appearances for them.

After playing in some friendlies for Weymouth during the summer of 2004 Scott signed for Margate in August 2004 and made his debut on 14.8.04 in a 3-2 defeat against Bognor Regis in the Conference South. The match was played at Margate's adopted home in Ashford. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said Scott had a shaky night in his next outing - a 1-0 win at Carshalton on 16.8.04 - and wrote his "blushes were twice saved by his defenders making goal-line clearances".

On 24.8.04 Scott played his fourth consecutive game and had what the Gazette said was "another miserable night between the sticks" as Margate were thrashed 6-0 by Grays at Ashford. The paper said he "spilled" a cross for the second goal whilst Grays' fourth from future Welsh international Freddy Eastwood "seemed to run straight past" him. However the Gazette did add "Ward may have been at fault for several of the goals, but in truth he got little protection from his defence". It was Scott's last appearance and he was released after four outings. He was replaced in the Margate goal by Ole Gottskalksson.

After leaving Margate Scott joined Lewes and on 14.9.04 he was part of the side that beat visitors Margate 7-3. He'd made just three appearances before Crawley signed him in October 2004 but they immediately loaned Scott back to Lewes. He played regularly for them for the remainder of the 2004/05 season and on 7.12.04 he kept goal in a 1-1 draw with Margate at Ashford. The Isle of Thanet Gazette report said Scott was "in surprisingly good form" having "had a torrid spell" at Margate.

During the 2005/06 campaign Scott was understudy to former Margate keeper Phil Smith at Crawley but only made a handful of first team appearances for the Sussex club. In February 2006 he had a one week trial at Championship club Plymouth and played in the reserves before going back to Crawley.

Scott left Crawley at the end of 2005/06 and in the summer of 2006 he played in some friendlies for Gillingham where he'd been on trial three years earlier.

Scott ended up starting the 2006/07 season with London Colney of the Spartan South Midlands League and played for them throughout the campaign before retiring aged just 25.

In 2010 he was working as a tax consultant in the London area.

Scott's older brother Darren and younger sibling Elliott both enjoyed successful Football League careers as centre-backs and during the 2011/12 season Darren was with Championship club Millwall whilst Elliott was on the books of Premier League Norwich.

name: Mark Warlosz
other clubs: Canterbury City, New Romney, Folkestone, Folkestone Invicta and Whitstable Town
bio:
Versatile left-sided player born in Folkestone who began his career with Canterbury during the 1984/85 season but then dropped into the Kent County League. Mark spent several years with New Romney before joining Thanet United in November 1988.

He made his debut at left-back as United lost 2-0 at home to Fisher in a Kent Senior Cup tie on 22.11.88 and the Thanet Times then said he was "very impressive" in a 0-0 draw at Andover on 26.11.88. Mark made the number three shirt his own for the next few weeks, enjoying a run of 14 games at left-back. The Thanet Times said he "took the eye with some dogged work" in a 4-0 defeat at home to Andover on 21.1.89 but on 4.2.89 Mark damaged his knee ligaments as United lost 2-0 to Bury at Hartsdown Park. The injury forced him to miss two matches but he returned to the side as a striker for a 2-2 draw with Corinthian at Hartsdown on 28.2.89. Mark then had a run of four games as a midfielder / left winger and on 18.3.89 he had the misfortune to score an own goal which gave Gravesend & Northfleet a 2-1 win at Hartsdown. He sliced an attempted clearance past a stranded Joe Radford. After being carried off in a 1-1 draw at Folkestone on 25.3.89 Mark resumed his left-back duties for the last few games of the campaign and played his final match for United in a 5-0 defeat at Sheppey on 1.5.89. It was his 27th appearance (one as sub) without scoring and at the end of the season Mark left the club.

In the summer of 1989 he joined Folkestone and when the club went out of business at the end of 1990 Mark moved on to Folkestone Invicta.

He went on to score 36 goals for Invicta during the 1991/92 season and Mark stayed with the club until October 1994 when he moved on to Whitstable.

He made three reserve team appearances during a short stay with the Oystermen and scored once before leaving the club.

Mark later rejoined Folkestone and played for them during the 1995/96 and 1996/97 seasons.

In 2011 he was working as a Senior Roadworks Engineer at a Deal-based firm of Land Surveyors.

In August 2013 Mark played in a charity match to celebrate former Thanet player John Lineham s 50th birthday and a host of other former Margate / Thanet players were also involved in the game.

name: Phil Warner
other clubs: Aldershot (0), Hastings United, Basingstoke Town and Bracknell Town
bio:
Versatile Woking-born player who joined Aldershot as a 15 year-old on 22.7.63 but never made the first team there. Phil left the club at the end of the 1965/66 season and joined Margate in August 1966.

He made his debut on 5.9.66 in a Southern League Cup tie against Hastings at Hartsdown Park and went on to make a total of 43 appearances (five as a substitute) without scoring during the 1966/67 campaign as Margate won promotion from the Southern League Division One by finishing as runners-up. Phil featured in both full-back positions and after a shaky start to his Margate career he turned in a string of solid performances during the second half of the season.

Phil found himself in the reserves for the majority of the 1967/68 campaign and he made just 12 first team appearances (one as substitute). At the end of the season he was released after failing to agree terms.

Phil then joined Hastings where he spent both the 1968/69 and 1969/70 campaigns before being released.

In the summer of 1970 Phil signed for Hampshire League club Basingstoke and he stayed with the club until the end of the 1973/74 season.

In September 1974 Phil linked up with Spartan League outfit Bracknell and soon became their captain.

name: Roger Warner
other clubs: Charlton Athletic (0), Dulwich Hamlet and Croydon
bio:
Bromley-born defender who began his career at Charlton and worked his way through the club's youth ranks. Roger was signed as an associated schoolboy on 4.2.87 and then became a trainee on 4.7.88. He played for Charlton's Colts side from 1987/88 to 1989/90 and also played for the reserves during 1988/89 and 1989/90.

Roger left Charlton early in 1990 and signed for Margate in February of that year aged 18, making his debut at centre-back in a 5-0 defeat at Baldock on 24.2.90. The Thanet Times reported that Roger "created a favourable impression" despite the result. He played in Margate's next three games too, twice as a centre-back and once at left-back. According to the Thanet Times he "impressed" in the number three shirt in a 0-0 draw at Dunstable on 10.3.90. Shortly after playing in Joe Radford's testimonial match against a Charlton X1 on 14.3.90 Roger was released as he had a chance to play in Finland. He'd made four appearances without scoring before his departure.

Roger spent around three months in Finland with a club he identified as FC Vaasa and in 2008 he said "My interest in the game was dwindling by then." The team Roger played for can't have been called FC Vaasa as no such club exists and its actual identity isn't known.

After returning from Finland Roger joined Dulwich in the summer of 1990 and he then moved on to Croydon before retiring from senior football at the end of the 1990/91 season.

Roger played Sunday football until he was 32 and in 2008 he was co-owner of a business offering marketing advice and solutions to technology firms. Roger was living in Lewes, East Sussex at that time and had his own website at http://rogerwarner.net/.

name: Cyril Watkins
other clubs: Ramsgate Athletic, Sittingbourne, Snowdown Colliery Welfare, Dover and Deal Town
bio:
5' 10" tall, versatile left-sided player who played for Ramsgate Colts as a 14 year-old and then progressed into Ramsgate s reserves as a 15 year-old during the 1948/49 season. Cyril made his debut for them in an 11-0 win over Bettsehanger Colliery Welfare Reserves at Southwood on Christmas Day 1948.

Cyril signed professional forms for Ramsgate at the age of 17 and on 21.4.51 he played for the senior side for the first time as they beat Chatham 1-0 in a Kent League game at Southwood. The East Kent Times said that Cyril turned in a hard-working performance at left-half. He eventually stayed at Southwood for almost seven years before being released in September 1955.

Cyril then had a brief spell with Sittingbourne.

In October 1955 he joined Margate and made his debut in a 1-1 draw with Gillingham Reserves at Hartsdown Park on 29.10.55. Cyril impressed with his accurate passing and in his first three appearances he played in three different positions to quickly gain a reputation as being a utility man. In total Cyril made 16 first team appearances and scored twice during the 1955/56 campaign. His first goal came in a 4-2 win at Sittingbourne in the Kent League Cup on 2.5.56 and the other came in the Final of the same competition on 10.5.56 as Margate went down 2-1 to Gillingham Reserves. Cyril also played regularly for the reserves in between his stints in the senior side and towards the end of the season Coventry watched him. Unfortunately, Cyril had an 'off' day and they didn't pursue their interest.

During the 1956/57 season he was in and out of the first team but made a total of 31 appearances without scoring. On 17.11.56 Cyril was part of the Margate side that beat Dunstable 3-1 at Hartsdown Park in the FA Cup 1st Round and he had several extended spells in the first team but only really established himself in the last couple of months of the season.

The 1957/58 campaign saw Cyril make a total of 34 appearances and it was an eventful season for him. On 31.8.57 he played the last few minutes of a match against Ramsgate in goal after Peter Peters was carried off and then on 7.9.57 Cyril was sent off in a 1-1 draw at Faversham. He clashed with former Margate legend Peter Vandepeer (who scored the Faversham goal) and was dismissed at a time when such events were still very unusual. However the Kent FA let Cyril off with a severe caution due to his previous good conduct.

A week later Cyril got married and then on 16.11.57 he played as Margate lost 3-2 to visitors Crystal Palace in the FA Cup 1st Round. On 14.12.57 Cyril had to play an entire match for the reserves in goal when Peter Peters was taken ill shortly before kick off. The game was against Dover Reserves and Margate won 4-2. On Boxing Day 1957 Cyril scored his only goal of the season with a 25 yard strike into the top corner in a 6-1 home win over Sheppey.

The 1958/59 campaign turned out to be Cyril's last at Margate and he spent most of the season in the reserves, only making ten first team appearances. On 27.12.58 he had another stint in goal after Stan Earl was injured during a 5-1 Kent League defeat at Bexleyheath & Welling but it was only for half an hour or so as Earl returned after treatment. On 13.4.59 Cyril played the first ten minutes of a game against Ashford at Hartsdown in goal as Earl was late arriving.

However at the end of the season Cyril left the club and joined Snowdown.

He then joined Dover for the 1960/61 campaign and went on to spend several seasons at Crabble. On 1.9.62 he was stretchered off with concussion after seven minutes of a game against Margate at Hartsdown.

Cyril joined Deal for the 1963/64 season and he was still playing for their reserves during the 1967/68 campaign.

He later turned out for Christchurch in the Thanet Premier Sunday League, playing alongside his old Margate team-mate Joe Haywood during the 1969/70 season.

Cyril owned a central heating installation company for many years and lived at Pegwell. He was living in Ramsgate during 2013.

As a youngster, Cyril was also a very successful amateur boxer.

name: Barry Watkiss
other clubs: St.Peter s Old Boys
bio:
Keeper born in Stoke On Trent who moved to Kent in the late 1960's / early 1970's and played for local club St.Peter's Old Boys for many years, first appearing for them in the Kent Amateur League during the 1972/73 campaign.

Barry was still turning out locally for Margate Athletic when he joined Margate for the 1980/81 season. He played for the reserves during the early part of the campaign and then got an unexpected chance in the first team in April 1981. Barry was called into action as a stop-gap replacement for Paul Thomas during a drastic player shortage and made his debut in a 1-1 draw at Fareham on 8.4.81. He also played in the following match, a 4-2 defeat at Poole on 11.4.81. Barry then dropped back into local football at the end of the season but returned to Hartsdown Park to play a few games for Thanet United's reserves during the 1981/82 campaign.

He then became Thanet's trainer during the 1982/83 season, working alongside caretaker manager Peter Donnelly.

Barry played the last football of his career during the 1990's when he turned out for Thanet League club Margate Athletic Old Boys whose squad of veterans also included a host of other former Margate / Thanet players.

In 2012 he was living in France.

name: Darren Watson
other clubs: Mullingar Town (Eire), Oxford United (0), Grimsby Town (0), Bristol Rovers (0), Hendon, Kingsbury Town, Chipstead, Whyteleafe and Lingfield
bio:
6' 3" tall, unorthodox striker who went to school in Redcar, Yorkshire but later moved to the London area.

As a teenager Darren spent time at the London Soccer Academy and in 2001 numerous trainees from the academy moved to Ireland to play for Mullingar after London-based building contractor Jim Moore invested £100,000 in the club. His aim was to get his hometown team into the League of Ireland and Darren and the young players from London were given accommodation as well as some 'pocket money'. They had to train twice a day and in September 2001 Darren scored Mullingar's first goal in the Ireland Under-21 League as they beat Drogheda 1-0. The club only played in the Under-21 League and their squad were all youngsters - Darren was 19 at the time.

He had a spell playing in France after leaving Mullingar and in September 2003 Darren started a trial at Oxford United. He had a few outings in the reserves and scored twice after coming on as a substitute in a match against Wycombe Reserves. His two late strikes gave Oxford a 3-1 win and the U's website described his first goal as "a magnificent diving header".

At the start of October 2003 Darren signed for Margate and coach Kevin Hales described him as being "Full of youth, stature and pure rawness." Darren made his debut in a 1-1 draw at Telford in the Conference on 4.10.03 and the Thanet Times said he seemed "to be lacking match fitness". He started Margate's next game too - a 4-0 defeat at Dagenham & Redbridge on 7.10.03 - and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Darren "worked hard despite often being forced wide". He then spent almost two months as a substitute and made six appearances from the bench in the next nine matches. On 25.10.03 Darren headed his first goal after coming on in an FA Cup tie at Grays. His goal helped Margate pull back from 3-1 down to draw 3-3 and the Thanet Times said Darren's "height made him a handful".

On 1.11.03 he came on as a sub after 13 minutes of a Conference game at Morecambe and Darren went on to score a hat-trick as Margate drew 3-3. He was injured scoring his third goal and had to go off with 11 minutes left. It was only the second time a substitute had scored a hat-trick for Margate, matching Colin Clewlow's effort in an 8-0 win over Tunbridge Wells on 19.1.74 - almost 30 years earlier.

Despite his heroics at Morecambe Darren didn't start a match again until he played in a 1-1 draw at Farnborough on 6.12.03 but he then started four of Margate's next five games. In a report on a 2-0 win at Aldershot on 20.12.03 The Times said Darren "made life so uncomfortable for Bradley Thomas, the 21-year-old on loan from Peterborough, that the defender was substituted just past the half-hour".

On 27.12.03 Darren got his fifth goal of the season in a 3-1 defeat against Gravesend & Northfleet at Dover and his run in the starting line-up ended after a 2-0 win over Forest Green at Dover on 4.1.04. He made three more sub appearances during the next month before starting a 2-0 win over Halifax at Dover on 8.2.04. The Thanet Times said Darren's "strength caused no end of problems". His next outing was as a sub in a game against Northwich at Witton Albion on 14.2.04 and Darren scored three minutes after making his entrance as Margate won 3-0.

He was in and out of the side again for the next few weeks after that and scored after coming on in a game at Leigh on 28.2.04 that Margate lost 4-2. Darren then started a Kent Senior Cup tie against Welling at Ramsgate on 2.3.04 and made it back-to-back goals when he fired home a spectacular effort in a 2-0 win. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said his "neat turn and cracking 25-yard shot...left keeper Gavin Kelly with no chance". Darren kept his place for a 3-3 draw with Dagenham & Redbridge at Dover on 6.3.04 but that was his last start of the campaign. He made five more sub appearances in Margate's last 11 games of the season but didn't add to his tally of eight goals, six of which had been scored when Darren came off the bench. In all he made 27 appearances, 16 of them as a sub. Remarkably Darren didn't manage to play any full games, being substituted every time he started a match. In its round-up of the 2003/04 campaign the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Darren had "surprised many pundits and caused defences problems".

In the summer of 2004 he had a trial with Grimsby and Darren scored in a friendly against Doncaster played behind closed doors that ended in a 5-5 draw. His trial extended past the start of the 2004/05 season and Darren played in some reserve team games before Grimsby decided not to offer him a contract after he picked up an injury. Shortly before Grimsby let him go Margate's assistant manager Kevin Raine had told the KM Extra newspaper "If they don't offer him anything, then he will come back to us, and it will be pretty good for us in terms of his fitness. Darren's a bit of an enigma, but has a lot of ability and skill, and he is quick for a big lad. He is still only young, and there is plenty to work with. He has had a few trials at other clubs, but I think what he needs now is a bit of stability."

Darren rejoined Margate at the start of October 2004 and having recovered from injury he made his first appearance of the 2004/05 campaign when he came on as a substitute in a 2-0 defeat at Sutton in the Conference South on 26.10.04. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said "his appearance added leadership as well as height to the attack" and Darren also came off the bench in Margate's next game against Weston-Super-Mare at their adopted home in Ashford on 30.10.04. He scored in a 2-0 win and the Thanet Times' match report was headlined "Elementary For Watson". Darren made two more sub appearances in Margate's next three matches and in the second of them - a 5-1 win over Havant & Waterlooville at Ashford on 13.11.04 - he scored again.

Darren then joined Bristol Rovers on trial and missed Margate's next two games as a result. He scored for Rovers' reserve side in a 4-0 win over Swindon Reserves on 17.11.04 but wasn't signed by the club.

On 29.11.04 Darren returned to the Margate side when he came on as a substitute in a 2-1 win at Thurrock in the Conference Cup and on 7.12.04 he got his third goal of the season in a 1-1 draw with Lewes at Ashford, again after coming on as a substitute. Margate manager Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "Darren scored and he's done well, but he's not 100 per cent fit, so he can only come on as sub. It's just a matter of slowly building up fitness."

Darren finally made his first start of the season in a 1-0 defeat at Hayes on 11.12.04 and played the whole game. It was the first time he'd completed a full 90 minutes since originally joining Margate in October 2003 and it was Darren's 35th outing in a Margate shirt. He then started three of the next four matches but after a 1-0 defeat at Welling on 1.1.05 Darren missed three games altogether due to a toe injury.

He returned as a substitute in a 2-1 win over Basingstoke at Ashford on 5.2.05 and the Thanet Times said Darren's "presence turned the game in Margate's favour" as when he came on with 20 minutes to go Basingstoke were 1-0 up. The paper said "fitness has restricted the striker's appearances this season, but his pace and power struck fear into Basingstoke hearts". Darren then featured as a sub in Margate's next eight matches and on 19.2.05 he headed a late equaliser to level the scores at 1-1 after coming on in a Conference South game against Sutton at Ashford. The Thanet Times said he had "considerable aerial presence".

On 1.3.05 Darren scored his fifth and sixth goals of the season after coming on in a Kent Senior Cup tie against Cray played at Ramsgate and his two extra time strikes secured a 4-3 win. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "tore the Cray defence apart". In its report on Margate's next match - a 1-0 defeat at Hornchurch on 12.3.05 - the Thanet Times noted that Darren came on as sub "surprisingly sporting a pair of full-length tights, much to the delight of the Hornchurch fans" and after a 1-0 defeat against Carshalton at Ashford on 19.3.05 the paper wrote "it is apparently Watson's fitness that is keeping him from starting matches, but his appearance from the subs' bench again seemed to cause the Carshalton defence most worries". The Times also said Darren "imposed himself well".

On 25.3.05 he started his first game for almost three months as Margate lost 5-0 at Grays but Darren was back amongst the substitutes for a 2-0 defeat against Cambridge City at Ashford on 28.3.05. He then made two more starts before dropping back to the bench after a 3-2 defeat against St Albans at Ashford on 5.4.05. Darren made four sub appearances in the last five matches of the campaign as Margate were relegated to the Isthmian League Premier Division and he finished the season having scored six times in 29 outings, 22 of which were as a substitute. All of Darren's goals were scored as a substitute.

In August 2005 Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette that Darren had "Great potential, but maybe not had the right direction in the past." and added "Hopefully he can fulfill his potential here." Darren started the new campaign in the starting line-up and in its report on a 1-0 home win over Maldon in an Isthmian League Premier Division game on 20.8.05 the Thanet Times said he was an "all-action player fans love" and "worked so hard, he could barely stand towards the end". Chris Kinnear agreed and said "Darren worked very hard." It had been Margate's first match back at Hartsdown Park following three seasons of groundsharing.

On 29.8.05 Darren started his fifth game in a row as Margate entertained Redbridge and the Thanet Times said his "confidence must be good as he was trying all sorts of tricks". The match finished 0-0 and Darren then found himself on the substitutes bench for a trip to Worthing on 3.9.05. He came on early in the second half but looked short of fitness and barely lasted 30 minutes before being taken off as Margate drew 1-1.

Darren missed the next game altogether but returned to the starting line-up on 10.9.05 as Margate took on Cowes in an FA Cup tie at Hartsdown Park. He opened the scoring in a 4-0 win and the Thanet Times said he "may have missed a few (chances) this season" but "emphatically" fired home a bouncing ball to open his account for the campaign. The paper said Darren was "a player to divide a crowd if ever there was one" but felt he "did his utmost to win people over" and Chris Kinnear said "Darren's still not fit. Mind you, I don't know when he will be ! He's got ability, his problem is he's such a quiet guy and so laid back and he's like that on the pitch. I've spoken to him, players have spoken to him, everyone's spoken to him, but it's hard to get him going."

Despite his goal Darren found himself back on the bench for Margate's next match on 17.9.05, coming on in a 2-2 home draw with Slough, and he then only made one sub appearance in the next four games. On 8.10.05 he had another outing from the bench as Margate lost 3-0 at home to Cray in the FA Cup and that turned out to be Darren's last game for the club. He was released shortly afterwards having scored once from ten appearances (four as sub) and Chris Kinnear told the Thanet Times "We're disappointed at letting Darren go because he's been with us a while but never really fulfilled his potential. He is a nice guy - there's no two ways about it - and while there's nothing wrong with that, we need players with that drive and ambition and desperation to win."

After a few months out of football Darren resurfaced in February 2006 when he joined Isthmian League Premier Division club Hendon where he was reunited with his old Mullingar striking partner Blaise O'Brien. Darren scored on his debut as Hendon beat Redbridge 2-0 on 4.2.06 before being substituted after 63 minutes and he made nine more appearances without scoring before being loaned to Isthmian League Division 2 outfit Kingsbury at the end of March 2006.

Darren didn't play for Kingsbury's first team although he finished the season there.

In the summer of 2006 he scored in one of Hendon's friendlies but Darren then dropped out of football before the 2006/07 campaign began.

After two years out of the game he resurfaced at Isthmian League Division 1 South club Chipstead at the start of the 2008/09 season and Darren scored in his first two outings there. On 25.8.08 he scored twice in the first half of a home game against Leatherhead to take his goal tally to four from four outings but Darren then picked up a serious knee injury and had to go off before half-time. The game finished 3-3 and Darren didn't feature again for Chipstead until December 2008. He continued to be hampered by injuries during the remainder of the campaign and Darren finished the season having scored four times in a total of ten league appearances (two as sub).

In the summer of 2009 he signed for Whyteleafe and Darren scored on his debut as they lost 2-1 at Sittingbourne in the Isthmian League Division 1 South on 15.8.09. He got two more goals before the end of August but then spent some time away from football before returning to Whyteleafe in December 2009. Darren enjoyed a good second half of the season and ended up with a tally of 14 goals from 26 league outings (eight as sub).

He stayed with Whyteleafe for the 2010/11 campaign but again struggled with various injuries and in November 2010 the Leafe manager Nicky English said "If he made an effort to get himself even 50 or 60 per cent fit he would be a match-winner every single week. He's a lovely guy, a gentle giant - he just doesn't seem to have that push to get himself fit. He is hard to get fit but he makes a big difference." Darren scored once from 11 league appearances (four as sub) before joining Sussex County League club Lingfield on a dual registration basis early in 2011.

He made eight appearances (three as sub) for Lingfield without scoring and at the end of the 2010/11 season Darren dropped out of senior football once more aged 29.
