name: Micky Wells
other clubs: Maidstone United, Canterbury City, Chatham Town, Folkestone, Sittingbourne, Tonbridge, Whitstable Town, Sheppey United and Snodland
bio:
6' 4" tall defender born in Chatham who started his career with Maidstone. During the early part of the 1985/86 campaign Micky had a loan spell at Canterbury and towards the end of the year he was loaned to Chatham. On 7.12.85 he scored for them in a 3-1 defeat at Thanet United.

In the summer of 1986 Micky joined Chatham on a permanent basis and spent 1986/87 and 1987/88 there before moving on to Folkestone.

He spent two seasons at Folkestone and on 1.1.90 Micky scored in a 1-1 home draw with Margate.

He joined Sittingbourne for the 1990/91 campaign and on 1.4.91 Micky was sent off in a 2-1 win at Sheppey after a clash with future Margate player Matt Stock who was also dismissed. Micky stayed with the Brickies for 1991/92 and in March 1992 he was sent off in a 0-0 draw at Canterbury.

He linked up with Tonbridge for the start of 1992/93 and scored eight goals in 33 appearances (three as sub) as the Angels won the Kent League title. He was sent off twice - at Chatham in December 1992 and at Alma Swanley in January 1993.

In the summer of 1993 Micky signed for Margate and made his debut at centre-back in a 3-0 defeat at Sudbury on 24.8.93. He then featured in each of the next 14 games and played as a left-back, centre-back, midfielder and striker at various times. The Thanet Times said he was "ineffectual" in midfield during a 1-0 win at Havant on 4.9.93 and after wearing the number three shirt in a 2-1 win over Sudbury at Hartsdown Park on 26.10.93 Micky was loaned to Whitstable. He scored in a 6-0 win over Greenwich during his time with the Oystermen and at the end of November 1993 Micky returned to Margate.

On 30.11.93 he played at centre-back in a 1-0 defeat at Ashford and on 4.12.93 Micky featured in a 2-2 home draw with Bury, again as a central defender. A few days later he left Margate having made 17 appearances without scoring and joined Whitstable on a permanent basis.

In the summer of 1994 Micky rejoined Chatham and he stayed there until moving to Sheppey in the summer of 1997.

He left the Islanders to join Kent County League club Snodland for the 1998/99 campaign and then rejoined Whitstable in the summer of 1999.

Towards the end of 1999 Micky returned to Sheppey and he finished 1999/00 back at Snodland.

Micky was still playing for Snodland during the 2003/04 campaign by which time he was in his late 30's.

name: Ted Wells
other clubs: Ashford Town, Ramsgate Athletic and Betteshanger Colliery Welfare
bio:
Aggressive Fulham-born centre-forward who later moved to Thanet and joined the Navy as a teenager. Ted was stationed at Holbrook and then Shotley in Suffolk and during World War II he served on Arctic convoys to Russia as well as spending time in the Mediterranean. He ended up in Hiroshima at the end of the conflict.

After returning home to Thanet in 1947 Ted joined Margate and he quickly proved himself as prolific goalscorer for the reserves during the early part of the 1947/48 season. On 1.11.47 Ted made his first team debut in a Kent League game at Snowdown and he got the Margate goal in a 6-1 defeat before returning to the reserves. He made another senior appearance in a 1-1 draw with Canterbury at Hartsdown Park on Christmas Day 1947.

On 27.3.48 Ted was given another first team chance having found the net over 40 times for the reserves and he scored twice as Margate won 4-3 at Maidstone in a Kent League Cup tie. From then on he was a regular in the side until the end of the season and he finished with a total of 12 goals from only 16 appearances. Ted's goals included two in a 4-1 win over Gravesend & Northfleet in the Kent Senior Shield Final on 8.5.48.

Ted began the 1948/49 season with two first team appearances but failed to find the net and soon found himself back in the reserves. On 25.9.48 he was sent off playing for them in a game at Ramsgate.

In October 1948 Ted asked to be released by the club and he joined Ashford. By chance, Ted's debut was a home game against Margate on 30.10.48 and he scored in a 5-2 win. He went on to score over 35 goals for the Nuts & Bolts during the remainder of the season.

Ted stayed with Ashford for the 1949/50 campaign and on 4.3.50 he scored twice in a 3-1 win at Margate. He was still with Ashford during 1950/51 and on 2.9.50 Ted was sensationally sent off just 13 minutes into an FA Cup tie at Margate. He clashed with centre-half Ron Wilson who fell to the floor and after Ted was initially cautioned, the referee then decided to dismiss him from the field. The Thanet local press reported that Ted left the pitch amid a storm of boos but Ashford still managed to win the tie 2-1.

Ted enjoyed a prolific goalscoring start to the 1951/52 campaign with Ashford but his season ended up being blighted by injury. He broke two toes which sidelined him for several months and then on 2.2.52, shortly after returning to first team duty, Ted suffered a broken leg in a Kent League Cup tie against Snowdown. He recovered to play for Ashford again during 1952/53 and on 10.1.53 Ted was conspicuous in a 2-2 home draw with Margate. First he was involved in an altercation with George Dover that saw the Margate man sent off after 22 minutes and Ted then scored both of the Ashford goals. The East Kent Times said of the Dover dismissal None of the officials saw the Wells action which grassed the Margate player, but a linesman observed Dover retaliate . Ted ended 1952/53 with a total of 19 goals.

In the summer of 1953, after almost five years at Ashford, Ted joined Ramsgate and on 16.1.54 he scored as they won 2-0 at Margate in the Kent League. Ted went to spend a total of four seasons with the Rams, mostly playing in their reserves. After a long absence from the senior side, he was restored to the Rams first team for a game at Betteshanger on 24.11.56 and marked his return with a hat-trick in a 6-1 win.

On 26.1.57 Ted had an eventful afternoon as Ramsgate Reserves took on Margate Reserves at Hartsdown Park. He opened the scoring during the first half but was then sent off in the 67th minute after an altercation with Margate keeper Peter Peters. The match finished 1-1. Later in the season, on 13.4.57, Ted scored for the first team in the opening minute of a home game against Margate. Ramsgate went on to win 2-0.

In October 1957 Ted moved on to Betteshanger and on 30.8.58 he scored a hat-trick as Betteshanger beat visitors Margate 5-2. He was still with the club during the 1959/60 campaign aged 37.

During the 1963/64 season Ted was playing local Sunday football for Westgate USC aged 41 and on 12.1.64 he was sent off in a game against Minnis Bay.

He was the older brother of 1950's Margate star Derek Wells and another of Ted's brothers, Gerry, also played once for Margate.

His nephew Steve Wells had a lengthy stint as Margate's Press Officer that ended in 2013 and in that year Ted was still living in the Thanet area.

In July 2013 the Isle of Thanet Gazette published a story about Ted after he received an Arctic Star medal 70 years after earning it by serving in the Navy. It was awarded to servicemen who worked on Arctic convoys to Russia during World War II. Many of his former colleagues were presented with their medals by Prime Minister David Cameron but Ted's arrived by post and he told the Gazette "It was a terrible disappointment to be presented it by the postman after the others met the Prime Minister. I hope something can be arranged so I can receive a proper presentation." The full article can be seen by clicking on '**Click here for more photos**' link beneath Ted's photo at the top of this page.

Ted died in Thanet on 30.12.17 aged 95.

name: Steve West
other clubs: Arsenal (0), West Ham United (0), Purfleet, Tilbury, Aveley, East Thurrock United, Concord Rangers, Enfield, Woking, Dagenham & Redbridge, Hornchurch, Grays Athletic, Fisher Athletic, Leyton and Sutton United
bio:
Burly centre-forward born in Tilbury, Essex who had spells on the books of Arsenal and then West Ham as a youth.

Steve later played for Purfleet and in the summer of 1991 he moved on to Tilbury where he spent the 1991/92 season.

He then had a stint with Aveley before his travels in Essex took him to East Thurrock and later Concord Rangers of the Essex Senior League.

Steve left Concord to join Isthmian League Premier Division outfit Enfield during the 1995/96 campaign and he stayed there until September 1997 when Conference club Woking paid £35,000 for his services.

Steve scored on his debut as Woking beat visitors Dover 4-0 on 30.9.97 and on 10.1.98 he was in the side that lost 1-0 to visitors Margate in the FA Trophy.

As his Woking career progressed Steve had spells when he played as a centre-back and by 1999/00 he was Woking s captain. During 2000/01 he was selected for the England Semi-Professional side and made his debut in a match against Wales. In November 2001 Steve played for an FA X1 against a Southern League side in a representative game at Crawley and he d made around 200 appearances for Woking and scored in the region of 50 goals when he joined Dagenham & Redbridge for a nominal fee in February 2002.

Steve was part of the Daggers side that reached the 4th Round of the FA Cup during 2002/03 where they lost to Norwich and on 8.3.03 he scored after coming on as a substitute in a Conference match against visitors Margate. The Daggers won 3-0 and Steve ended up with 16 league goals for the season.

In June 2003 he was sold to Hornchurch for £10,000 and Steve scored five goals from 20 Isthmian League Premier Division outings for the Urchins during 2003/04 as well as finding the net three times in cup ties.

He joined Conference South outfit Grays for the 2004/05 campaign and on 25.3.05 he came on as a late substitute as they beat Margate 5-0 at Ashford. Manager Chris Kinnear told the Thanet Times "Steve West came on as a sub for them, and he's probably on more money than five of our players put together."

Steve started 2005/06 with East Thurrock - his second spell there - and scored nine goals from 21 Isthmian League Premier Division outings (one as sub) for the Rocks. His tally included one in a 3-1 home win over Margate on 3.12.05.

In January 2006 Steve moved on to Fisher and he scored twice from 14 Premier Division appearances (four as sub) during the remainder of the season.

In the summer of 2006 he signed for Leyton and Steve scored four goals for the Premier Division outfit during the first few weeks of the 2006/07 campaign before leaving the club in September 2006 and dropping out of senior football for the rest of the season.

He resumed his career with a third stint at East Thurrock during 2007/08 and Steve became club captain. He scored in his first outing as the Rocks drew 2-2 at Boreham Wood and Steve went on to make 32 Premier Division appearances (one as sub) during the campaign. He scored 12 league goals and another two in cup ties.

He became player assistant-manager at Sutton for 2008/09 and Steve scored five goals from 38 outings (16 as sub) for the Premier Division club during the season.

In August 2009 he signed for Margate on a non-contract basis aged 36 and made his debut in a 2-1 home win over Boreham Wood in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 22.8.09. The Thanet Times described Steve as a veteran" and he had to go off injured at half time. After missing two games with a back problem he returned to action in a 1-0 defeat against Cray at Hartsdown Park on 31.8.09 and the Isle of Thanet Gazette wrote he looks a victim of Blues 3-5-2 system. The big man was more or less surplus to requirements because I don t reckon Margate put a cross into Cray s box all day. He got a bit of stick but he s been a good player down the years and if Blues had wingers who put the ball on his head, he d still do a job."

On 5.9.09 Steve scored with a header in the aftermath of a long Aaron Lacy throw-in as Margate drew 2-2 at Ashford (Middlesex) and the Thanet Times said he looked dangerous in the air". The Isle of Thanet Gazette then said Steve gave the Hendon defence a going-over" in a 2-1 win over them at Wembley FC on 22.9.09 and added all that was missing was a goal but he had his chances".

Steve made his final appearance in a 0-0 draw with visitors AFC Hornchurch on 26.9.09 and he bore the brunt of the Hartsdown Park crowd s frustrations. It was his fifth game without scoring and a few days later Steve was released with Margate director Keith Piper telling the Thanet Times He isn t what we re looking for." Steve had scored once from eight outings before his departure and shortly afterwards caretaker manager Neville Southall told the Isle of Thanet Gazette I was really disappointed when I heard Westy booed last week. Whatever people s opinion, he tried as hard as anyone and was great in the dressing room."

After leaving Margate Steve went back to East Thurrock as player-coach and scored in the first game of his fourth spell with the club as they beat visitors Wingate & Finchley 3-0 in the Isthmian League Division 1 North on 10.10.09. He scored six times in 12 league outings before leaving East Thurrock at the end of 2009 and retiring.

name: Les Weston
other clubs: Tottenham Hotspur (0), Chelsea (0), Faversham Town, Whitstable Town and Sheppey United
bio:
Left winger born in Shoreditch, London who was on Tottenham s books as an amateur but never featured in Spurs' 1st, 2nd or 3rd teams.

Les joined Chelsea for 1947/48 and went on to feature in their junior sides for three seasons. He made his debut for their Eastern Counties League side on 12.2.49, scoring in a 6-0 win at West Ham. During 1949/50 Les made eight appearances in the Eastern Counties League, scoring once. He also played for Chelsea Reserves in friendlies including one at Ramsgate on 7.1.50.

Les dropped into the Kent League to join Faversham in December 1950 and the Faversham News said that he was undoubtedly a coming star .

In the summer of 1951 Les moved on to Whitstable of the Kent League.

In November 1952 he signed for Margate and the local press mistakenly stated that his first name was Tommy . Les made his senior debut when he wore the number eleven shirt in a 3-1 defeat at Snowdown in the Kent League on 8.11.52. It turned out to be his only first team appearance. Les then played four times for the reserves, scoring twice, before leaving the club in December 1952.

In the summer of 1953 he signed for Sheppey.

name: Luke Wheatley
other clubs: Ramsgate
bio:
Locally born defender whose father Steve played as a goalkeeper for Gillingham and later for Ramsgate. Luke attended Hartsdown Technology College and progressed through Margate s youth ranks. Having started out in the Under-12 s during the 2002/03 season he graduated to the reserves for the start of 2007/08 whilst also playing for his school side, sometimes as a goalkeeper.

On 28.10.08 Luke made his first team debut at centre-back in a 2-0 defeat against Maidstone in the Isthmian League Premier Division at Hartsdown Park and he was only 17 at the time. He also started Margate s next five games and on 11.11.08 Luke scored in a 2-1 win at Boreham Wood, heading home a Wayne Wilson free-kick to level the scores at 1-1. His run in the side ended after a 2-1 win at Hendon on 22.11.08 and Luke then returned to the reserves for the next two months.

He made his comeback in the senior side on 31.1.09 when he came on as a substitute in a 1-0 defeat at Tonbridge and Luke started Margate s next match - a game against Tooting & Mitcham at Hartsdown Park on 7.2.09. The Thanet Times said he was "impressive" in a 2-0 win and Luke was a regular again after that.

On 14.2.09 he scored his second goal, again with a header from a Wayne Wilson free-kick, in a 1-1 draw at Hastings and Luke was also on target in a 3-2 defeat at Harrow on 4.4.09. A few days later he was given a contract for the 2009/10 season and manager Terry Yorath told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "I could have given Luke a contract before now but he s a young lad and you don t know how they re going to react after getting in the team. He s done well and is the kind of player I want to keep at the club." Luke finished the season having scored three times in 19 outings (two as sub) as Margate ended up in the relegation zone of the Isthmian League Premier Division.

He only featured in one friendly ahead of the 2009/10 campaign and on the eve of the season Terry Yorath told the Isle of Thanet Gazette He s a young boy and he ll have to grow up if he wants to be a big-league player."

On 28.7.09 Luke made his first appearance of the new campaign as a substitute in a 1-0 home win over Ramsgate in the first leg of a tie played for the Isle of Thanet Gazette Cup and he then started the second leg at Southwood on 1.8.09 which finished in a 1-1 draw. In the weeks that followed Luke played at centre-back in three of Margate s next six games but after he d worn the number five shirt in a 1-0 defeat against visitors Cray in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 31.8.09 he fell out of favour. Luke made two more sub appearances and then joined Division 1 South club Ramsgate on loan in October 2009.

The Rams manager Jimmy Ward told the Isle of Thanet Gazette He wants to play football, we ve got him in for a month, so let s see what happens. He s one of the best local players around."

Luke returned to Hartsdown Park in November 2009 and on 10.11.09 he made his first start for over two months in a 1-0 win at VCD in the Isthmian League Cup. Luke then kept his place at centre-back for Margate s next two matches but after a 3-2 defeat against Cray at Bromley on 29.11.09 he only made two starts and three sub appearances in the next ten games.

On 9.2.10 Luke played as Margate drew 1-1 with Wealdstone at Hartsdown Park and it turned out to be his last outing for the club. He d made a total of 18 appearances (seven as sub) without scoring during 2009/10 when he rejoined Ramsgate for an undisclosed fee early in March 2010.

By the end of the season Luke had made 12 appearances (two as sub) without scoring for the Rams during his two spells at Southwood. He was a regular in the Ramsgate side during 2010/11 and Luke made another 34 Division 1 South appearances but didn t open his goalscoring account for the club.

He stayed with the Rams for the 2011/12 campaign too and on 13.8.11 Luke played in goal for the last half hour of a Division 1 South match against Corinthian Casuals at Southwood after keeper Daren Hawkes went off injured. Ramsgate lost the game 1-0 and Luke went on to score twice from a total of 37 Division 1 South outings during 2011/12.

He started the 2012/13 season as a fixture in the Rams defence but on 3.11.12 Luke broke his leg in a 4-1 home win over Crawley Down Gatwick and wasn t fit again until the closing weeks of the campaign. In all he made 14 appearances without scoring during the season.

Luke stayed with the Rams for 2013/14 too but on 14.9.13 disaster struck when he suffered another leg break in a match at Tooting & Mitcham. He told the Isle of Thanet Gazette I can t believe I didn t even make it to November this time. It is gutting, to be honest. I went to make the tackle, my leg got caught in the turf and their attacker came a split-second later and bang, game over. It was only my ninth or tenth game back after my last break and I had forced my way back into the team. Luke also spoke about his future and said It s a bit early to say but I really have to think about my future and my career in football. If the recovery goes well then we ll see but I have to think of my future in general life and could that mean giving up the game ? I don t know, it might.

name: Jack Whibley
other clubs: Sittingbourne, Crystal Palace (90,15)
bio:
John Whibley but known as Jack
5' 11" born Sittingbourne. Known as  Shuff  Whibley to family. Attended Borden Grammar School near Sittingbourne 
Working as a drapers assistant in a Sittingbourne High Street shop in 1911. Owned by his father, also John
Started with Sittingbourne Wednesday
Joined Sittingbourne for 1911/12 left winger then. 
7.10.11 played whole game in goal as Sitt lost 3-1 at Crystal Palace Res
Played for Kent 27.3.12   beat Surrey 7-1 in game played at Kingston 
East Kent Gazette - Saturday 24 August 1912  If he be careful, high honours in the amateur world await Jack Whibley.  
August 1912 played for Sittingbourne side that reached final of 6-a-side competition at Chatham, lost to Bromley in final
Started 1912/13 with Sittingbourne but then signed for Leicester Fosse of Div 2 start of October 1912. Harry Sparrow was at Leicester at same time. Very briefly with Leicester as in November 1912 he signed as amateur for Crystal Palace of the Southern League. Newspaper report said he d  obtained his transfer from Leicester Fosse 
First CP outing 20.11.12   London League game v Croydon Common Reserves that finished 2-2
Combined CP appearances with playing for Sitt
26.2.13 played for Kent again v Surrey at Chatham, listed as being Sittingbourne & Crystal Palace
Signed pro forms for Crystal Palace before 13/14 began
November 1914 enlisted with 24th (County of London) Battalion (The Queen's) served in France, Salonika, Egypt and Palestine
Told Kent Messenger 1926  I was lucky enough to escape with nothing worse than being gassed 
Played football for regiment during war, was sergeant when he was demobilized
At CP he initially deputised for Welsh International Bill Davies before the 1st World War so not regular till after WWI 57 apps 12 goals up to 19/20 inclusive when Palace in Southern League. Palace founder members of Division Three South for 20/21 - won it. 
 
Croydon Advertiser 1921  "Of slight physique, he does not appear cut out for the hurly-burly of strenuous football, but ability and pace enabled him to hold his own with most opponents."
"Can cut in and score goals, while his accurate centres provide openings for his colleagues."
 "Quiet and unassuming, he is the best type of professional." 
Scored in Everton (1st Div) 0 CP (3rd Div) 6 on 7.1.22 FA Cup 1st Round 
stayed CP till end of 22/23 making 90, 15 in Football League (150 apps, 27 goals in all comps). Toured Scandinavia with CP. Awarded a benefit for services to club.
May 1923 went back to Sittingbourne 
Sittingbourne 24/25 too . Joined Margate on month's trial which was then made permanent.
13.11.26 fainted on field during Royal Marines Chatham 1 Margate 3   intensely cold and one of six players (three from each side) who went off
March 1930 joined Sittingbourne Wednesday aged 38, had started with them 20ish years earlier
Played cricket for Sittingbourne-based  Gore Court for over 20 years 1000+ runs summer 1912
Died 5.6.72  aged 80  in Bridge, near Canterbury
http://www.cpfc.org/forums/archive/index.php/t-115766.html
Son, also John (born 1917), played for Sheppey during 1949/50

name: Jake Whincup
other clubs: Norwich City (0), Brentford (0), Chalfont St.Peter, Hornchurch, Slough, Redbridge, Long Melford, Cambridge City, Chelmsford City, Crawley Town, Mildenhall Town, Haverhill Rovers, AFC Hornchurch, Ashford Town, Great Wakering Rovers, Arlesey, Grays Athletic, Cheshunt, Ware, Kingstonian, Waltham Abbey and Maldon & Tiptree
bio:
Nomadic keeper who was born in the Barking & Dagenham district of Essex and started out as youth with Norwich where he played for the Under-13 s during the 1997/98 season.

Jake later had a spell on Brentford s books and he started the 2003/04 campaign there before joining Chalfont St.Peter midway through the season.

Jake made 22 Isthmian League Division 2 appearances for Chalfont before the end of 2003/04 and then moved on to Hornchurch of the Conference South in July 2004.

He signed a one-year contract with the Urchins and their goalkeeping coach Jim Stannard had previously worked with Jake during his spell with Brentford.

In August 2004 Hornchurch loaned Jake to Isthmian League Premier Division outfit Slough and he made his debut for them in a 3-1 defeat at Dover on 14.8.04. Jake went on to make 17 appearances in all competitions before going back to Hornchurch in November 2004.

When a financial crisis engulfed Hornchurch Jake moved on to Redbridge in January 2005 and he played twice for them before the end of the 2004/05 season. He was sent off in one of those appearances. Jake also started 2005/06 with Redbridge but only featured once in the first team before joining Eastern Counties league club Long Melford early in September 2005.

Around the same time Jake also had a brief stint with Cambridge City and before the end of September 2005 he moved on to Chelmsford.

He followed a few weeks at Chelmsford with a short spell at Crawley and towards the end of 2005 Jake rejoined Long Melford.

In February 2006 he signed for Mildenhall and Jake played regularly for them in the Eastern Counties League Premier Division during the remainder of the 2005/06 campaign.

Early in July 2006 he featured in friendlies for Fisher before linking up with Haverhill towards the end of the month. Jake played once for the Eastern Counties League outfit and then had a spell with AFC Hornchurch which lasted until December 2006 when he joined Ashford.

Jake went on to make 27 Isthmian League Division 1 South appearances for the Nuts & Bolts during 2006/07 and then featured seven times in league games early in the 2007/08 season before leaving the club to join Great Wakering.

After making one Isthmian League Division 1 North appearance for Great Wakering Jake was on the move again in December 2007 and joined Arlesey.

He made 15 Division 1 North appearances there before linking up with Grays in March 2008.

Jake featured as a substitute in one Conference match for Grays but in June 2008 he was released by the club.

He started the 2008/09 campaign with Division 1 North outfit Cheshunt and Jake played in four league games there.

In October 2008 he rejoined Redbridge and Jake s second stint with the club saw him make a total of 16 appearances before the end of the 2008/09 season.

He couldn t find a club at the start of 2009/10 and after playing in a friendly for Kingstonian in September 2009 Jake signed for Margate in October 2009 as a free agent.

He made his debut in a 3-1 defeat at Wealdstone in the FA Trophy on 17.10.09 and after sitting out Margate s next game - an Isthmian League Premier Division match against Hastings on 7.11.09 - Jake returned to the side for a 1-0 win at VCD in the Isthmian League Cup on 10.11.09. It was his last outing and in December 2009 he was released.

After leaving Margate Jake joined Ware of Division 1 North but he didn t feature in their senior side and early in 2010 he left the club and dropped out of senior football.

Jake resurfaced in the summer of 2011 when he signed for Kingstonian and on 18.10.11 he was part of the K s side that lost 3-1 at Margate in an Isthmian League Cup tie. He only played twice for Kingstonian in the Premier Division during 2011/12.

In the summer of 2012 Jake featured in some friendlies for Walton & Hersham and was expected to sign for the club but in the end he started the 2012/13 campaign at Kingstonian once more.

In October 2012 he signed for Division 1 North outfit Waltham Abbey and Kingstonian s manager Alan Dowson told the K s official website "Jake played his part in the squad last season, but it's only fair that he has a shot at some first team football and I wish him well."

Jake went on to make 31 league appearances for Waltham Abbey before the end of the 2012/13 season.

At the end of January 2014 he left Waltham Abbey and signed for Maldon & Tiptree, also of Division 1 North.

name: Conrad Whitby
other clubs: Almondsbury, Mangotsfield United, Bitton, Keynsham Town, Motor Action (Zimbabwe), Eagles (Zimbabwe), Kiglon (Zimbabwe) and Caps United (Zimbabwe)
bio:
Zimbabwean midfielder who spent time in Thanet as a child due to having relatives in the area.

Conrad played for Margate as a trialist in a 4-2 win at Ramsgate in a friendly played on 31.7.03 and the Thanet Times said he "impressed early in the game". He also played in a friendly at Herne Bay in August 2003. At the time Conrad was based in London.

In January 2004 he signed officially for Margate after a lengthy wait for international clearance and by then Conrad was living in Ramsgate and had a British passport.

His first involvement with the senior team came on 10.1.04 when he was an unused substitute for an FA Trophy tie at Dorchester and Conrad eventually made his debut in a 2-0 win over Welling in a Kent Senior Cup tie played at Ramsgate on 2.3.04. He filled an attacking midfield role and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said he "showed plenty of pace but evidently needs more match practice". Margate manager Chris Kinnear told the paper "I thought he did very well for a young lad - I only wish he had scored when he had his chance at the end. He's going to be a good player for us."

Conrad then came on as a sub as Margate drew 3-3 with Dagenham & Redbridge in a Conference game played at Dover on 6.3.04 and he was in the starting line-up for a 3-1 win at Dover in the Kent Senior Cup semi-final on 23.3.04. He didn't feature again after that and sat out the last seven games of the 2003/04 season. In its round-up of the campaign the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Conrad was "promising" but had "plenty to learn".

In the summer of 2004 he moved on to Ramsgate but Conrad only made one appearance for the Rams early in the 2004/05 season before moving to the Gloucestershire area.

Later in the 2004/05 campaign he had a spell with Western League Division 1 club Almondsbury and Conrad then joined Mangotsfield of the Southern Premier League in the summer of 2005.

His next move took him to Western League Premier Division outfit Bitton in February 2006 and Conrad finished the 2005/06 season there.

He returned to Mangotsfield for the start of 2006/07 and then in December 2006 Conrad linked up with Keynsham of the Western League Premier Division. They were his last English club.

In 2008 Conrad went back to his native Zimbabwe and started playing in the Zimbabwe Premier Soccer League. He initially joined Motor Action before moving on to Eagles in 2010. They were based in Chitungwiza.

In February 2011 Conrad signed for Kiglon, another Chitungwiza club, and he then rejoined Motor Action in July 2011.

At the start of January 2012 Conrad moved to Caps United and a few days later he made his international debut for Zimbabwe as a substitute in a 0-0 draw in Botswana on 7.1.12.

name: Charlie Whitchurch
other clubs: Ford Motors, Portsmouth (0), Charlton Athletic (0), West Ham United (0), Tottenham Hotspur (8,2), Southend United (18,5), Folkestone Town and Betteshanger Colliery Welfare
bio:
Winger born in Grays, Essex who attended Landsdowne Road School in Tilbury and became prominent in local youth football. On 22.4.35 Charlie played for England s schoolboy side in a 3-0 win over Ireland at Liverpool s Anfield stadium, a crowd of 13,000 watched the game. He played twice more for England during May 1935.

After leaving school, Charlie was employed at the Ford Motor Company in Dagenham and played for Ford Motors before being signed as an amateur by Portsmouth.

During the early months of the 1944/45 season, Charlie made a one-off appearance as a guest player for Charlton in a wartime game.

In January 1945 he joined West Ham as an amateur and Charlie went on to become a regular in West Ham's side after making his debut on 13.1.45 in a 5-4 home win over Brighton & Hove Albion. He scored 11 goals in 34 appearances, most of which were made in the Football League South. That was a competition played before the resumption of the Football League proper the following season. In May 1945 Charlie was signed as professional.

In January 1946 he was signed by Tottenham for what was described as a considerable sum and Charlie made eight first team appearances for Spurs.

In July 1947 he joined Southend and Charlie had previously scored once in two appearances as a guest player for the Shrimpers during the 1945/46 season. After scoring five goals in 18 senior appearances for Southend during 1947/48, Charlie dropped into non-league football in July 1948.

He joined Folkestone for 1948/49 and also spent the 1949/50 campaign with them. On 8.10.49, Charlie scored twice and had a penalty saved by Des Cross as Folkestone beat visitors Margate 3-0 in a Kent League game.

In the summer of 1950, Charlie moved on to Betteshanger and spent the 1950/51 season there.

In August 1951 Charlie signed for Margate and made his debut on the opening day of the 1951/52 campaign, playing on the left wing in a 0-0 draw with Whitstable at Hartsdown Park on 18.8.51. He made four more appearances during the early part of the season but then lost his first team place and spent the remainder of the campaign in the reserves. Charlie left the club at the end of the season.

After his departure from Hartsdown Park, Charlie played for Ford Motors again as he was still employed by the company and then emigrated to Canada. He later relocated to the USA where he worked for General Motors.

Charlie died in Michigan, USA in July 1977.

name: Andy White
other clubs: Reading (0), Croydon Athletic, Basingstoke, Havant & Waterlooville, Kingstonian, Staines Town, Gillingham (0+2,0), Bishop s Stortford, Eastleigh, Dorchester Town and Winchester City
bio:
6' 0" tall striker born in Epsom, Surrey who started his career with Reading. Andy played for the Royals youth and reserve teams during an apprenticeship with the club and also had several loan spells with non-league sides.

In February 2009 he spent some time with Isthmian League Division 1 outfit Croydon Athletic where he played once without scoring and at the end of October 2009 Andy had a stint with Basingstoke of the Conference South where he again played once - in a 1-0 defeat at Newport County on 31.10.10 - before going back to Reading.

In January 2010 he was loaned to Conference South club Havant & Waterlooville but Andy didn't make any first team appearances there and in February 2010 he was farmed out to Kingstonian. Andy scored on his debut for the K s as they drew 3-3 with visitors Wealdstone in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 25.2.10 and played once more for the club.

He had two more loan spells before the end of the 2009/10 campaign. Firstly Andy linked up with Conference South club Staines in March 2010 and scored on his debut as they won 3-0 at home against Woking on 13.3.10. He played once more and then briefly returned to Reading. Then in April 2010 Andy had a short second stint with Croydon Athletic where he played just once. At the end of the 2009/10 season he was released by Reading.

In June 2010 Andy signed a one-year deal with League Two club Gillingham and he made his first team debut in a 4-1 defeat at Norwich in the League Cup on 10.8.10, coming on as an 83rd minute substitute. He then played for the Gills reserves and had scored once from four outings for them when he joined Margate on a month s loan in October 2010 to cover for injured striker Shaun Welford.

Andy made his debut in a 0-0 draw at Concord Rangers in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 26.10.10 and became only the second Margate player ever to be sent off on his debut when he picked up two yellow cards. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said his first booking was a mystery" and also felt that Andy s second caution with 15 minutes left was harsh. The paper said he never really had the service to show the talent that earned him a Gills debut in the Carling Cup at Norwich back in August".

Andy kept his place for Margate s next game - a 2-1 defeat against AFC Hornchurch in an FA Trophy tie at Hartsdown Park on 30.10.10 - and the Thanet Times said he didn t have the experience" to be an adequate stand-in for Shaun Welford. Andy then played in a 2-0 home defeat against Bromley in the Kent Senior Cup on 2.11.10 before serving a three match ban. He returned to feature as a substitute in a 5-3 defeat at Croydon Athletic on 17.11.10 but that was Andy s last outing for Margate and he returned to Gillingham having failed to score from four appearances (one as sub).

In January 2011 the Gills loaned Andy to Conference South club Bishop s Stortford and he made six league appearances there without scoring before returning to Priestfield.

In February 2011 Andy scored twice as a Gills X1 won 5-1 in a friendly at Deal and future Margate player Andrew Miller was also on target for Gillingham.

On 23.4.11 Andy made his second and final senior appearance for the Gills when he came on after 76 minutes of a 4-2 home defeat against Barnet in League Two and at the end of the 2010/11 season he was released.

In July 2011 Andy signed for Conference South club Eastleigh and he scored four goals from 18 league outings before being loaned to Dorchester in December 2011.

He scored once from four Conference South appearances for the Dorset club in what was intended to be a three month loan but in January 2012 the deal was terminated and Eastleigh then cancelled Andy s contract shortly afterwards.

He finished the 2011/12 campaign with Winchester of the Southern League Division One South & West and scored six goals from 13 league appearances before the end of the season.

Andy also spent the 2012/13 campaign with Winchester.

name: Dick White
other clubs: Deal Town, Herne Bay, Canterbury City and Folkestone & Shepway
bio:
5' 7" tall defender born in Folkestone who began his career with Deal during the 1970/71 campaign and went on to spend several seasons there before joining Herne Bay.

In the summer of 1976 Dick moved on to Canterbury and made 32 Southern League appearances without scoring for City during the 1976/77 campaign. He then had a very brief spell with Folkestone & Shepway before joining Margate in the summer of 1977.

Dick made his Margate debut at left-back in a 2-1 win over Dorchester at Hartsdown on 3.9.77. He went on to make four further appearances before departing.

Dick later returned to Folkestone & Shepway and played for them during the 1978/79 and 1979/80 seasons.

He then moved on to Deal and was a member of their side that knocked Thanet United out of the FA Cup during the 1981/82 season.

During his time at Margate Dick worked as a plumber and he was also an accomplished sailor.

name: John White

then joined Hearts for  2,700 in May 1922.

top scorer at Hearts for five consecutive seasons, scoring one hundred and two goals, including four goals a game in three successive matches in 1925-26 
Scotland s top scorer in 1922-23 with thirty goals. 
John scored over 100 goals for Hearts before moving to Leeds for  5,600 in February 1927. One of biggest ever fees at time 
Sheffield United put in a  6,000 bid in November 1927 but Leeds rejected.

Left us and went back to Edinburgh and in January 1936 signed for Leith Athletic
played for the Scottish League four times 
one of four brothers who played professional football, including Willie White, who played for Hearts and the Scottish League.

name: Marc Whiteman
other clubs: Manchester United (0), Bury (0), Altrincham, Weymouth, Lewes, Eastbourne Borough, Worthing, Horsham, Maidenhead United, Hastings United, Ringmer, Croydon and Whitehawk
bio:
5' 9" tall striker born in St.Hellier, Jersey who came to the attention of numerous scouts whilst playing football on the island for junior clubs Star Trophy and Rozel Rovers.

At the age of 14 Marc had the option of signing for Glasgow Rangers, Leeds or Manchester United but choose to go to Old Trafford as he was a United supporter.

Marc signed a five-year contract and progressed through the Red Devils youth ranks in the years that followed. During the 1998/99 season he scored twice from eight outings (three as sub) for United's Under-17's side and by the end of the 2000/01 campaign Marc had scored 16 goals from a total of 44 outings at Under-17 and Under-19 levels. He was released at the end of the season aged 18 without making it as far as United's reserves.

In June 2001 Marc signed for Division 2 (later League One) club Bury and in July 2001 he spoke to the Lancashire Evening Telegraph about his time with Manchester United. He told the paper "I was sad to leave United and when you go from a £14.3 million training ground to Bury's facilities, with all due respect, it is difficult. But I want first team football, everyone does, and when you see the likes of Joe Cole making a name for himself at his age you know it can be done." Bury's manager Andy Preece said "He works hard, has a nice touch and good movement."

In August 2001 Marc suffered a badly broken nose in an Under-19's match for Bury which hampered his chances of breaking into the first team but he recovered and played regularly for the Shakers' reserves before being loaned to Northern League Premier Division outfit Altrincham in March 2002.

Marc played six times (three as sub) for Alty without scoring before going back to Bury at the end of the 2001/02 campaign. He was then released having never made a senior appearance.

In the summer of 2002 Marc played in some friendlies for Woking but the Cards decided they couldn't afford to sign him and he left the club before the start of the 2002/03 season proper.

In September 2002 Marc signed for Southern League Premier Division club Weymouth and said "I am desperate to play first team football and am grateful that Weymouth have given me this opportunity. I want to play back in the Football League and consider Weymouth Football Club a good shop window." Looking back again on his time at Old Trafford Marc recalled "The only time Sir Alex Ferguson called me by my name was the day I signed and the day he let me go. Apart from that, it was 'All right, son?'"

Marc stayed with Weymouth until the end of the 2002/03 campaign and in May 2003 he was released.

In August 2003 he joined Lewes of the Conference South and Marc scored 22 goals for the Rooks during 2003/04. His tally included a hat-trick in a 4-0 win at Tooting & Mitcham on 6.9.03.

He stayed at Lewes for the start of the 2004/05 season but in September 2004 Marc was loaned to the Rooks Conference South rivals Eastbourne Borough for a month.

In March 2005 Lewes loaned Marc to Isthmian League Premier Division club Worthing and he scored twice in four league outings there before the end of the 2004/05 campaign.

In the summer of 2005 Marc played in two friendlies for Margate and on 13.8.05 he made his competitive debut in a 2-0 defeat at Ramsgate in a match played for the Kent Messenger Cup. The Thanet Times said he was the player that "threatened most in front of goal" but it was Marc's only appearance and he then moved on to Horsham.

He scored once from four Isthmian League Premier Division outings for the Sussex club (two as sub) before joining Conference South outfit Maidenhead in October 2005.

In March 2006 Maidenhead allowed Marc to join Isthmian League Division 1 club Hastings on a dual registration agreement and he made four league appearances there without scoring before the end of the 2005/06 season.

His move to Hastings was made permanent in August 2006 and Marc went on to score four goals from 14 league outings before being released at the end of October 2006.

In November 2006 he signed for Sussex County League side Ringmer and Marc scored on his debut in a 2-2 draw at Rye n 11.11.06.

Early in December 2006 he linked up with Croydon who were playing in the Kent League at the time and Marc spent the rest of 2006/07 there.

In the summer of 2007 he went back to Ringmer and Marc managed a remarkable 49 goals during the 2007/08 campaign which made him the leading goalscorer in Sussex for the season.

He rejoined Hastings in the summer of 2008 and at that time Marc was working as a sports coach. He scored three times in 30 Isthmian League Premier Division outings (16 as sub) for Hastings during 2008/09 and one of Marc's goals was a dramatic last-minute winner to seal a 3-2 triumph at Margate on 4.10.08.

He spent the 2009/10 campaign with Sussex County League side Whitehawk and in August 2009 Marc scored all three goals in a 3-2 home win over Arundel. Whitehawk reached the FA Vase semi-finals and won promotion to the Isthmian League.

Marc returned to Ringmer again in the summer of 2010 - his third spell with the club - and scored over 20 goals during the 2010/11 season. He stayed with the club for 2011/12 too and on 22.10.11 he scored a hat-trick in a 5-0 win over Woodstock Sports in the FA Vase. Marc finished the campaign as Ringmer's top scorer.

name: Tommy Whitnell
other clubs: Millwall (0), Cray Wanderers, Welling United, Maidstone United, Croydon Athletic, Thamesmead Town, Dulwich Hamlet and Tonbridge Angels
bio:
Striker who started his career in Millwall's Academy. Tommy played in the Lions Under-16's side during the 2004/05 campaign and spent three seasons with the club before being released at the end of 2006/07.

In the summer of 2007 he joined Cray of the Isthmian League Division 1 South and Tommy scored four goals from 13 league outings (eight as sub) during the 2007/08 campaign. He also found the net twice in cup ties.

Tommy stayed with Cray for 2008/09 and scored 11 goals from 27 Division 1 South appearances (six as sub) as they won promotion via the play-offs. His tally included a hat-trick in a 5-2 home win over Croydon Athletic on 20.9.08.

In July 2009 Tommy featured as a substitute for Dover as they took on Tilbury in a friendly and he scored in an 8-0 win before joining Welling for the 2009/10 season.

Tommy went on to score 15 goals from 27 Conference South starts for the Wings during the campaign but he struggled to get regular games at the start of 2010/11 and in September 2010 he was released.

Tommy immediately linked up with Maidstone where he scored three times in 22 Isthmian League Premier Division outings (seven as sub) before moving on to Croydon Athletic in March 2011.

He made eight Premier Division appearances for Croydon and scored four goals before the end of the 2010/11 season as the club were relegated.

In the summer of 2011 Tommy returned to Cray and he scored 25 goals from 48 outings in all competitions during 2011/12. His tally included a strike in a 2-1 defeat at Margate in the Kent Senior Cup on 11.10.11 and a hat-trick in a 4-1 home win over Tooting & Mitcham in February 2012. Tommy also scored twice in a 3-1 win at Margate in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 9.4.12 - his last goals for Cray.

In June 2012 Tommy signed a one-year contract with Margate and the club s Chief Executive Officer Cliff Egan told the Isle of Thanet Gazette Tommy is a proven goal scorer at this level and that is why we have brought him in. Getting a goal scorer at this level is absolutely vital and they can be very difficult to find."

Tommy scored twice in friendlies ahead of the 2012/13 campaign and made his competitive debut in a 2-0 win over Hendon at Hartsdown Park in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 18.8.12. On 25.8.12 he got his first goals for Margate with a double in a 3-3 draw at Kingstonian and the Thanet Times said one of Tommy s efforts was an expertly dispatched" header from a Dan Stubbs cross. He then scored in his next outing as Margate lost 2-1 to visitors Lowestoft on 27.8.11 and manager Chris Kinnear told the Isle of Thanet Gazette Tommy is starting to rattle them in now."

He d started the first eight games of the season before being injured in the pre-match warm-up ahead of an FA Cup tie at Aveley on 22.9.12. Tommy had to sit out the match but returned in a 2-1 home defeat against Maidstone in the FA Trophy on 29.9.12. On 10.11.12 he ended a run of 11 starts without a goal by finding the net in a 2-0 win at Harrow and the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Tommy wonderfully volleyed home" with his left foot after a long Laurence Ball free-kick sent him clear of the home defence. He then made it back-to-back goals by heading home his fifth of the season in a 3-1 win over visitors Bury on 17.11.12.

In its report on a 0-0 draw at East Thurrock on 4.12.12 the Isle of Thanet Gazette said Tommy really put in a shift up front" and he continued to be a fixture in Margate s attack for the next few months. Tommy s long run of starts ended after a 2-1 home win over Hampton & Richmond on 23.2.13 marked his 11th game without a goal and he only featured as a substitute in the next two matches.

Tommy was back in the side for a home game against Bognor Regis on 9.3.13 and scored twice in a 3-0 win. His first goal was hooked over his shoulder from a tight angle and after the match Tommy told Margate s website It has been a while so it s a bit of a relief for them (the goals) to come finally. First one; the ball s come to my chest. I ve just popped it up in the air and thought why not and had a crack." Tommy then described his second goal and said There was no one around me; I beat the offside trap. I had to take my time; I saw the gap so I thought why not and just put it in there and I was glad to see it go in."

During the closing weeks of the season Tommy sometimes found himself playing as a wide midfielder but he found some goalscoring form when featuring in his favoured role up front. On 26.3.13 he was on target in a 4-2 defeat against Wealdstone at Hartsdown Park and Tommy also scored in his next outing on 29.3.13 as Margate beat visitors Thurrock 3-1. He then endured another barren run of five games without a goal up to and including a 2-1 home defeat against Metropolitan Police on 13.4.13. Tommy was dropped to the bench for Margate s next match - against Kingstonian at Hartsdown Park on 16.4.13 - but came on to score his tenth goal of the campaign in a 2-1 defeat.

After one more outing as a substitute he was back in the starting line-up for a Kent Senior Cup tie against visitors Ebbsfleet on 23.4.13 and Tommy scored in a 4-2 defeat. He then played in a 0-0 draw with Harrow at Hartsdown Park on 27.4.13 - the final day of the season - and that turned out to be Tommy s last appearance for Margate. His 11 goals from 46 outings (five as sub) had made him the club s top goalscorer but in June 2013 Tommy rejoined Cray.

He left Cray at the start of January 2014 and joined their fellow Isthmian League Premier Division club Thamesmead.

In March 2014 Tommy was on the move again, this time signing for Premier Division promotion-chasers Dulwich. He scored on his debut - a 4-3 defeat at Maidstone on 15.3.14 - but didn t find the net again from a total of six appearances (one as sub).

Early in June 2014 Tommy moved on to Tonbridge, newly-relegated to the Isthmian League Premier Division.

name: Bob Wickens
other clubs: Ramsgate Athletic, Herne Bay, Canterbury City and Dover
bio:
5' 9" tall, tough-tackling defender who was born in Lichfield, Staffordshire.

Bob started his career with Ramsgate, making his debut for them during the 1967/68 season, and captained the Rams' reserve side before moving to Herne Bay.

He joined Margate in December 1970 and immediately became captain of the reserves. On 13.1.71 Bob made his first team debut in a 1-1 draw at Dartford and went on to make 19 appearances (one as sub) before the end of the 1970/71 campaign. The local press described Bob as having "an over-awing physical presence" and he scored one goal - a 20 yard effort in a 5-4 win over Dartford on 10.3.71.

Bob was in and out of the side during the early part of the 1971/72 season but on 20.11.71 he featured in Margate s infamous 11-0 defeat at Bournemouth & Boscombe in the FA Cup 1st Round. He d made 27 appearances before undergoing a cartilage operation in February 1972 and by the end of March 1972 he d recovered. Bob then played in a few reserve team games before the end of the campaign. Earlier in the season he d been described as "a resolute destroyer" by the local press. At the end of the 1971/72 campaign he was released.

Bob joined Canterbury for the 1972/73 season and went on to stay at Kingsmead for over four years. He made 105 Southern League appearances for City (five as sub) without scoring.

Bob joined Dover for the 1976/77 campaign but retired due to injury during that season.

During the 1984/85 campaign Bob was manager of Thanet United's Under-14 side and he later ran the club's Under-16's too.

In the summer of 1988 he became manager of Ramsgate's Under-18 side before joining Herne Bay as reserve team manager for the 1989/90 season. Bob made three substitute appearances for the reserves aged 39 during the early part of the campaign.

Towards the end of 1989 he took over as manager of Ramsgate and held the position until resigning in October 1991.

In the summer of 1992 Bob returned to Margate to assist with the first and reserve teams for the 1992/93 season.

His brother John played alongside him at Herne Bay, Margate, Canterbury and Dover whilst Bob's sons Brian and Gary later played for Thanet clubs. Brian had a spell at Margate and Gary spent several seasons at Ramsgate.

In 2011 Bob was working as a builder in Margate and in 2015 he emigrated to Thailand.

He died on 16.3.24 at the age of 74.

name: Brian Wickens
other clubs: Ramsgate, Canterbury City and St.Margaret's
bio:
Thanet-born son of 1970's Margate player Bob Wickens who played for Thanet United's Under-12 side during the 1985/86 campaign and progressed through the club's older youth teams before moving to Ramsgate in the summer of 1990.

Brian played for the Rams' Under-18's and reserve sides during the 1990/91 season and in October 1991 he made one reserve team appearance for Margate during a short trial spell before going back to Southwood. Brian made his first team debut for the Rams later in the 1991/92 campaign and then joined Margate in the summer of 1992.

He featured in some of the first team's pre-season friendlies and then played regularly for the Under-18's throughout 1992/93. Brian was sent off twice for them - in a 2-1 defeat at Sittingbourne on 1.11.92 and a 2-0 defeat at Folkestone on 6.1.93. He scored nine goals in 27 Under-18 appearances and also played nine times for the reserves in the Kent Midweek League in addition to being an unused sub for a first team game.

Brian went back to Ramsgate early in the 1993/94 campaign and then rejoined Margate in the summer of 1995.

On 19.8.95 he finally made his first team debut when he came on as a substitute in a 3-1 defeat at Trowbridge and Brian also appeared as a sub in Margate's next three games. On 9.9.95 he made his first start when he played at right-back in a 5-2 win at Corinthian Casuals in the FA Cup and Brian had the distinction of scoring one of the goals. He then featured in Margate's next nine matches, starting eight of them, and showed his versatility by appearing in midfield, at right-back and at left-back before losing his place after wearing the number three shirt in a 2-1 home defeat against Bashley on 17.10.95. Brian didn't make another start until 16.12.95 when he played at right-back in a 4-1 win at Clevedon and he then featured in three of the next four games. On 1.1.96 Brian scored an own goal in a 2-1 win at Tonbridge and on 11.2.96 he played as a striker in a 3-1 defeat at Cinderford. He made a few more sporadic appearances after that, the last of them in a 2-0 win over Fareham at Hartsdown Park on 21.4.96, and finished the season having scored once in 27 first team outings (11 as sub).

Brian stayed at Margate for the 1996/97 campaign but only made one first team appearance, coming off the subs bench to score from distance in a 3-2 defeat at St.Leonards Stamcroft on 11.12.96. The Isle of Thanet Gazette said it was "a superb goal" and "a 25-yard blaster" which dipped over future Charlton keeper Sasa Ilic. Brian left the club at the end of the season.

Brian rejoined Ramsgate for 1997/98 and later had a spell with Canterbury that included the 1999/00 campaign before joining St.Margaret's of the Kent County League. Brian spent several seasons there up to and including 2004/05.

During the 2005/06 campaign he was playing local amateur football in Thanet and in December 2005 Brian was sent off for violent conduct whilst playing for The Dolphin in a match against The Hussar. He was involved in an altercation with the Hussar's goalkeeper that resulted in the match being abandoned and in February 2006 the Isle of Thanet Gazette reported that Brian had been given a 112 day ban by the Kent County Football Association.

He was still living locally in 2012 and was a member of the Westgate and Birchington Golf Club.

name: John Wickens
other clubs: Manchester United (0), Bexley United, Herne Bay, Canterbury City, Dover, Deal Town, Slade Green and Crockenhill
bio:
Hard-working player with a stocky build who was born in Lichfield, Staffordshire. John started his career as a junior at Manchester United and then played for Bexley during the 1963/64 and 1964/65 seasons.

In the summer of 1965 John joined Herne Bay and spent five seasons with them up to and including 1969/70. He was their captain for much of that time and played for Kent. John also played for Minnis Bay in the Thanet Premier Sunday League.

During the 1969/70 season John made three appearances (one as sub) for Margate in Kent Floodlight Cup ties, making his debut in a game at Sheppey on 8.10.69, although he continued to play for Herne Bay in the Kent League too.

However in the summer of 1970 he officially signed for Margate and he went on to make 43 appearances (four as sub) during the 1970/71 season. John scored two goals, one of which was a 25 yard effort in a Southern League Cup tie at Ashford on 26.8.70. On 21.11.70 he played as Margate lost 2-0 at Dagenham in the FA Cup 1st Round.

During the 1971/72 season he made a further 32 appearances (six as sub), playing either in midfield or as a striker. On 20.11.71 John featured in Margate s infamous 11-0 defeat at Bournemouth & Boscombe in the FA Cup 1st Round. He scored twice in a 3-2 defeat at Dover on 12.1.72 and one of John s goals was a cracking 20 yard effort. He scored four goals in total during the season but in May 1972 he was released by the club.

John joined Canterbury for the 1972/73 campaign and led City's scoring charts with 17 Southern League goals in 38 appearances (one as sub) during the season. He also scored a hat-trick as Canterbury beat Margate 3-2 in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Kingsmead on 23.1.73. John went on to spend three more seasons with City and by the time he left the club in the summer of 1976 he'd made a total of 144 Southern League appearances and scored 45 goals. He was City's top scorer for a second time during his last season there.

John joined Dover for the 1976/77 season and scored twice before moving on to Deal for the 1977/78 campaign.

He later had short spells with Slade Green and Crockenhill before returning to Herne Bay during 1978/79.

John became the Bay's player-manager on 8.3.80 aged 35 and during the 1982/83 season his assistant was former Margate player Graham Sawyer. At the end of that campaign John was sacked and by then he'd made over 300 appearances as a player for Herne Bay.

John started 1983/84 in charge of Thanet Premier Sunday League side Dalby and in November 1983 he became Thanet United's manager, taking over from Alan Fagan. Graham Sawyer again linked up with John to assist with training.

After generally improving Thanet's fortunes John was sacked in March 1987 after a bad run of results. Just before his dismissal John's old Margate team-mate Dai Yorath had told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "I would advise him to instill the same dedication and effort he always showed on the field into his own players."

John returned to Herne Bay for a second stint as manager a few months after leaving Thanet and was in charge there until March 1988 before moving to Portugal where he sadly died on 8.10.93 aged only 48. A minutes' silence was held for him before Margate's home game with Erith & Belvedere on 23.10.93.

John was a builder by trade and his brother Bob played alongside him at Herne Bay, Margate, Canterbury and Dover.

name: Chris Wild
other clubs: Leyton Orient (0), Farnborough Town, Hayes, Bristol Rovers (0), Cheltenham Town (0), Cambridge United (0), Harlow Town, Grays Athletic, Redbridge, Heybridge Swifts, St Albans City, Braintree Town, Maidenhead United, Chelmsford City, Hemel Hempstead Town, Barton Rovers, Enfield Town, Slough Town and Billericay Town
bio:
6' 5" tall defender who started his career as a trainee with Leyton Orient. Chris made his first appearances in the O's youth team during the 2000/01 season and often played alongside future Margate centre-back Mark Goodfellow. Chris continued to progress through Orient's youth ranks and he was a regular in the Under-19 side during the 2002/03 campaign as well as playing for the reserves, he also had a loan spell at Farnborough.

At the start of March 2003 he was loaned to Isthmian League Premier Division club Hayes and Chris made three appearances there before returning to Brisbane Road.

Later in March he had a trial at Bristol Rovers where he played for the reserves and scored an own goal as they lost 2-0 to Wycombe. Chris also played for Cheltenham's reserves before the end of the month as he knew he was going to be released by Orient at the end of the season. In April 2003 he played for Cambridge United's reserves but none of Chris' trials came to anything.

After leaving Orient he played in some of Farnborough's friendlies ahead of the 2003/04 campaign but Chris ended up joining Isthmian League Division 1 club Harlow for the start of the season proper.

He made 18 league appearances for the Essex club (one as sub) before moving on to Grays in December 2003.

Chris scored once from five Isthmian League Premier Division outings (one as sub) for Grays before the end of the 2003/04 campaign and stayed with the club for the start of 2004/05 as they joined the new Conference South. Chris made four more appearances (one as sub) and then signed for Redbridge in November 2004.

He scored on his Conference South debut as Redbridge won 3-2 at Newport on 20.11.04 and on 18.12.04 Chris was sent off in a 5-4 defeat at Lewes.

In January 2005 he moved on to Heybridge and Chris scored once from 10 Isthmian League Premier Division outings there before joining Conference South outfit St Albans at the end of March 2005.

He made his debut for St Albans in a 2-1 home defeat against Sutton on 2.4.05 and Chris then played in a 3-2 over Margate at Ashford on 5.4.05 before being sent off in the last minute of a 3-2 defeat at Hayes on 9.4.05. In all he made five appearances (one as sub) before the end of the 2004/05 season.

In the summer of 2005 Chris featured in a friendly for Basingstoke and he then signed for Conference South club Braintree where he started the 2005/06 campaign.

In January 2006 Chris linked up with Maidenhead, also of the Conference South, and spent the rest of the season there.

In August 2006 Chris signed for Margate and made his debut as a substitute in a 5-2 win at Worthing in the Isthmian League Premier Division on 19.8.06. He didn't feature in Margate's next three games but on 2.9.06 Chris made his first start in a 3-0 win over Chelmsford at Hartsdown Park. He then played at centre-back in each of the next nine matches. Chris' last outing came in a 1-0 defeat at his old club Heybridge on 7.10.06 and towards the end of October 2006 he was released. Margate's player-manager Robin Trott told the Isle of Thanet Gazette "Wildy's all right and he'll fit in another team. He did quite well for us at the start, then was bit patchy before I dropped him. The thing is, I don't want OK players in my team. I can't have fringe players starting matches."

Chris joined Isthmian League Premier Division club Chelmsford at the start of November 2006 but only played once - in a 3-0 defeat at Braintree in the Essex Senior Cup on 7.11.06 - before moving on to Hemel Hempstead.

He made his debut for Hemel as they won 3-0 at Northwood in the Southern League Premier Division on 13.11.06 and Chris spent almost a year with the club before joining Barton Rovers in October 2007.

He spent the remainder of the 2007/08 campaign with the Southern League Division 1 Midlands outfit.

In the summer of 2008 Chris returned to the Isthmian League when he signed for Division 1 North club Enfield Town and he captained the Essex club for much of 2008/09, scoring once from 24 appearances.

In April 2009 he joined Southern Football League Division 1 South & West outfit Slough on a dual-registration basis and finished the season there.

Chris stayed with Enfield for the start of the 2009/10 campaign and scored twice from 19 appearances before moving on to Isthmian League Premier Division club Billericay in November 2009.

He settled down at Ricay and by the end of the 2010/11 season Chris had made over 70 appearances for the club. On 13.8.11 he had a lucky escape when he fell two floors from the balcony of a Folkestone hotel room after the concrete he was standing on gave way. Chris only suffered severe bruising and a broken nose but it could easily have been much worse. Billericay were staying in the area following a pre-season friendly at Folkestone and ahead of another game at Sittingbourne which was called off due to Chris' accident.

He made a rapid recovery from his injuries and on 24.9.11 Chris returned to action when he came on as a substitute 60 minutes into a game at East Thurrock. Within four minutes he'd headed what turned out to be the winning goal as Billericay won 2-1 and it was a remarkable comeback for him. At the end of the 2011/12 season Ricay were crowned as Isthmian League Premier Division champions and Chris finished the campaign having scored four times in 28 league outings (two as sub).

He left Billericay in June 2013 after they d been relegated from the Conference South and Chris then rejoined Enfield Town. The Premier Division club s manager Steve Newing said Chris is an Enfield lad and has always wanted to come back to the club. Now that we are playing at the same level as Billericay it gave me an opportunity to speak on a level playing field in terms of football at least. I am delighted that Wildy has signed for us and I am sure he will improve us as a team with both his leadership qualities and ability. He is a winner and that will rub off on others around him. We beat off some stiff competition from others who were able to offer more in terms of finance, so getting his signature is even more satisfying.

Chris left Enfield early in December 2013 and didn t play elsewhere during the remainder of the 2013/14 season.

In May 2014 he rejoined Billericay and manager Craig Edwards said "We let him go year before last because I thought he had got too comfortable. He went to Enfield and it didn't work out there for whatever reason and he left there before Christmas. He hasn't played since then and the break from football has probably been good for him as he's got a real hunger to get back. We had a discussion towards the end of the season and then had a follow-up chat. He says he's in better shape than he has been for the last ten years. He's been boxing and is very fit. He said all the right things when I met him and he assures me he will be in the top three for fitness in the squad, which is some statement as we've got some really fit boys. He's dangerous in both boxes and he's one of the best defenders in this division. We're delighted to have him back."

In July 2014 Chris left Billericay again, citing personal reasons. Craig Edwards said It is a real shame that Wildy has had to leave. He runs his own business and has a young family, so he felt that he wasn't able to commit fully to the club. With training on Tuesday and Thursday, matches on Saturdays and other midweek fixtures, it is all just a little bit too much for him. He has to put his business and family first, which is something that I completely understand. I am gutted and so was he. He looked in great shape and we were delighted to have him with us. Unfortunately it hasn't worked out but we completely respect his decision and he is as devastated as we are.

name: Bill Williams
other clubs: Manchester United (0), Bury (1,0), Rochdale (8,3), Aldershot (8,4), Ramsgate Athletic, Betteshanger Colliery Welfare and Snowdown Colliery Welfare
bio:
Strong centre-forward who started his career with a two year stint at Manchester United without making a senior appearance before moving on to Division Two club Bury.

Bill played once for Bury s first team during the 1946/47 season.

Bill later had a spell with Rochdale of Division Three (North) where he scored three times in eight Football League appearances during 1949/50.

His next move took him to Division Three (South) outfit Aldershot and Bill scored four times in eight Football League appearances for them during the 1950/51 season.

In the summer of 1951 Bill dropped into non-league football to join Kent League club Ramsgate and he then linked up with Betteshanger, also in the Kent League, in the summer of 1952.

During 1952/53 Bill scored 38 goals for Betteshanger and his tally included six in a remarkable 13-2 home win over Chatham on 14.2.53. He then scored 17 times during the 1953/54 campaign before signing for Margate in March 1954.

Bill moved to Hartsdown Park in exchange for Jock Flannigan and made his debut in a 4-2 win at Sheppey in the Kent League on 6.3.54. It turned out to be his only appearance because of an irregularity with the transfer deal. It took place after the Kent League's official deadline and as a result both Bill and Flannigan were barred from playing competitively for their new clubs again during the remainder of 1953/54.

Bill stayed at Margate for the start of the 1954/55 season but only made a handful of reserve team appearances, scoring four times, before leaving the club to join Snowdown in September 1954.

He scored on his debut for Snowdown as they lost 2-1 in an FA Cup tie at Sittingbourne on 9.10.54. Bill then returned to Betteshanger for a short spell before the end of 1954/55.

In August 1955 he rejoined Ramsgate for a second stint, Bill was 30 by then.

He sadly died in the Salford area aged only 48 in the fourth quarter of 1973.

name: Colin Williams
other clubs: Herne Bay
bio:
Local defender born in Garlinge who played for Thanet Schoolboys during his time as a pupil at King Ethelbert's School in Birchington.

Colin went on to play for Margate Colts and Minnis Bay in local amateur football. He also played for the Thanet Youth cricket team and whilst undertaking his National Service from 1954 to 1956 Colin turned out for the Home Counties Brigade.

After being demobbed, Colin joined Margate and he played exclusively for the reserves during the 1956/57 season.

He stayed with the club for the 1957/58 campaign and on 28.8.57 Colin made his first team debut, playing at left-back as Margate drew 1-1 in a Kent League Cup tie at Sittingbourne. He made three further first team appearances deputising for Terry Joyce during the early part of the season and then spent the remainder of the campaign in the reserves.

Colin left the club in the summer of 1958 and joined Herne Bay, shortly before that he'd been approached by Tottenham but opted for a career with the Post Office instead. Colin also turned out for Thanet-based Sunday League club Minnis Bay during 1958/59 and on 1.2.59 he scored seven times as they hammered Nomads 16-0.

He became the father of quads during 1959 and stayed with the Post Office for many years until being forced to retire due to heart disease.

Colin died in Margate on 8.8.04 aged 68.
