bio:
Local attacker who played for Hugin Vikings as a youth and scored all six goals as their Under-16 s side beat Dynamo United 6-4 on 19.9.04.

Anthony then moved into Margate s youth setup and on 8.11.06 he was an unused substitute as the first team lost 1-0 at VCD in a Kent Senior Cup tie.

Over the course of the next few seasons he featured regularly in Margate s reserve team as well as having spells in local amateur football and on 12.10.10 Anthony made his senior debut when he wore the number ten shirt in a 5-2 home defeat against Thamesmead in the Isthmian League Cup. He also came on as a substitute in 2-0 defeat against Bromley in a Kent Senior Cup tie at Hartsdown Park on 2.11.10 before spending the remainder of 2010/11 back in the reserves.

Anthony won the reserve team s Player of the Year award for the season but in the summer of 2011 he joined Ramsgate.

He spent most of the 2011/12 campaign in the Rams reserves but Anthony also played once in the Isthmian League Division 1 South before joining Sittingbourne in the summer of 2012.

After featuring once in the Brickies first team in Division 1 South Anthony returned to Margate in September 2012 and played in some reserve team games before finishing the 2012/13 season back at Ramsgate, once again playing in the reserves there.

At the start of June 2013 he signed for Kent League club Canterbury but before the end of 2013 Anthony was playing in the Thanet Sunday Football League.

name: Brian Woolfe
other clubs: Hoo Institute, Chatham Town, Faversham Town, Gravesend & Northfleet, Folkestone & Shepway, Sheppey United, Welling United and Corinthian
bio:
Cultured left winger born in Highgate, London who started his career with Kent Amateur League club Hoo Institute who hailed from the Chatham area.

Brian linked up with Chatham in the summer of 1968 and spent the 1968/69 and 1969/70 seasons there.

Brian joined Kent League outfit Faversham for the 1970/71 campaign and marked his debut for the club by scoring both goals in a 2-2 draw with visitors Sheppey on 15.8.70.

Towards the end of 1970/71 Brian rejoined Hoo Institute and finished the season there.

In July 1971 Brian joined Southern League club Gravesend & Northfleet as an amateur and after impressing in his first few months with the Fleet, he signed professional forms on 27.11.71. Brian celebrated by setting up the winning goal in a 1-0 victory at Margate on that day. Later in the 1971/72 season Brian was frequently watched by Football League scouts.

He went on to spend eight years with Gravesend and was rated as one of the club's best ever players by their fans of the era. In total Brian made 327 appearances for the Fleet and scored 102 goals, including a hat-trick in a 5-0 win over Margate on 3.12.77. He was granted a benefit during the 1976/77 season.

After leaving Stonebridge Road in the summer of 1979 Brian played for various clubs, starting with Folkestone & Shepway during 1979/80, a season in which he scored ten goals. He then moved to Sheppey for the 1980/81 campaign.

Brian joined Welling for the 1981/82 season and scored for them in a 3-1 win at Thanet on 28.12.81.

In December 1982 Brian joined Thanet, shortly before his 35th birthday. He turned out to be manager Terry Morris' last signing for the club. Brian made his debut in a 6-1 defeat at Salisbury on 20.11.82, Morris' last match in charge of United, and showed some clever touches. He scored his first goal for the club when playing as a striker in a 2-1 defeat at Canterbury on 4.12.82. The Thanet Times said that Brian was "far and away the pick of a disappointing front line" during a 3-1 defeat at Crawley on 11.12.82 but later that month he suffered a knee injury that was expected to rule him out for the rest of the season. However Brian battled back to fitness and returned to the side for the final three games of the 1982/83 campaign, scoring in a 2-2 home draw with Canterbury on 7.5.83. In total he made nine appearances and scored three goals during the season.

During the pre-season friendlies prior to the 1983/84 campaign Brian looked sharp and the Thanet Times said "he will trouble the best in the months to come". However after playing on the left wing in Thanet's first two games of the new season Brian suffered a recurrence of his knee injury and left the club. At the time he considered retiring but decided against that course of action.

Brian later had a second spell at Sheppey and then returned to Chatham before finally retiring from senior football after a stint with Corinthian during the 1985/86 season.

During the 1988/89 campaign, he played for Grain Power Sports in the Rochester League and Brian was 41 by then.

Brian worked as a joiner and was a keen golfer, winning a Champion of Champions event at the Deangate Ridge club in Medway in 1987. He also played rugby for the Medway club and represented Hoo in the Medway Snooker League during the 1980 s.

name: Andy Woolford
other clubs: Gillingham (0), Tonbridge, Chatham Town, Canterbury City, Ramsgate, Dartford, Faversham Town, Medway, Sheppey United and Sittingbourne
bio:
5' 7" tall midfielder born in Murrayshire, Scotland who began his career with Gillingham. Andy played for the Gills' junior teams during the 1969/70 and 1970/71 seasons but never made a senior appearance. He scored six goals for the youth team during 1969/70 and also scored once in four reserve team appearances. Andy then made eight reserve team appearances during 1970/71 as well as continuing to play for the youth side.

Although born in Scotland, Andy was part of the England Youth squad which won the 'Little' World Cup in 1971 under manager Gordon Milne.

In June 1972 Andy joined Margate aged 18 and manager Les Riggs said Andy Nelson has only let the youngster leave Gillingham because he has seven defenders on a stringent financial budget. I persuaded Woolford, who has got potential, to come to Margate instead of spending a trial period with Stoke City. But I have promised that if, after six months or so, any league clubs are interested, I will let him go. Andy was made captain of the reserves and played exclusively for them during the early part of the 1972/73 season, never making a first team appearance. He was unhappy about that and in October 1972 he left the club by mutual consent. Les Riggs told the East Kent Times He is eager to gain a first team place in a Southern League team and became very unsettled with Kent League football recently when it became apparent that he was unlikely to slot into the first team during their impressive run. I had to tell him frankly that I could not guarantee a Southern League place and agreed to cancel his contract and put him on the transfer list.

Immediately after leaving Hartsdown Park, Andy had a trial with Tonbridge and played for them in a Kent Floodlight Cup tie at Ramsgate on 21.11.72. He quickly moved on to Chatham where he spent the remainder of the 1972/73 season.

Andy joined Canterbury for the 1973/74 campaign and made 67 Southern League appearances for City, scoring seven goals, before moving to Ramsgate in the summer of 1975.

Andy became the Rams' captain and on 26.12.75 he was sent off in a 2-2 draw at Ashford. In January 1976 he left the club due to a financial crisis.

He immediately linked up with Dartford and made 11 appearances for them before the end of the 1975/76 season.

Andy's next move took him to Faversham for the 1976/77 season and he then joined Medway for 1978/79. The club changed their name back to Chatham in the summer of 1979 and Andy also spent the 1979/80 and 1980/81 seasons there.

He joined Sheppey for the 1981/82 campaign and by the 1984/85 season Andy was their player-coach.

In the summer of 1985 Andy returned to Hartsdown Park almost 13 years after leaving Margate and he made his debut for Thanet United when he came on as a substitute in a 2-2 home draw with Bromley on 7.9.85. The match was an FA Cup 1st Qualifying Round tie and Andy made his first start for United in the replay at Bromley on 10.9.85. Thanet went down 2-1 but he had the distinction of scoring United's consolation goal. The Isle of Thanet Gazette described it as a "tremendous strike" from fully 25 yards. Andy then enjoyed a run in the side, he initially played in midfield but was then switched to right-back. However in November 1985 he was released having made 14 appearances (two as sub) and Andy then joined Sittingbourne.

He retired as a player at the end of the 1985/86 season due to being troubled by a knee injury.

At the start of December 1986 Andy returned to Faversham, taking over as their manager after former Margate player David McFall had resigned. He came out of retirement to play in a match at Whitstable in May 1987 when Faversham had a shortage of players. Andy continued as manager until the start of 1989 when he resigned and joined Sittingbourne as first team coach.

Andy stayed with the Brickies until early 1992 and had a spell as the club's caretaker manager shortly before his departure.

At the start of the 1992/93 campaign Andy was Tonbridge's coach and in February 1993 he returned to Margate to work as the club's joint manager alongside Mark Weatherly. Andy stepped down as joint manager at the end of the 1993/94 season but initially stayed on as club coach before finally leaving Margate in February 1995 due to work commitments.

name: Eric Worthington
other clubs: Golders Green, Willesden Town, Queens Park Rangers (0), Watford (30,4), Bradford City (2,1) and Dover
bio:
Tall, talented player born in Sheffield who started his career with amateur club Golders Green (later known as Hendon). Eric made his debut for them in November 1943, shortly before his 18th birthday, and went on to score three goals in 17 wartime matches. His older brother Roy (born in 1924) was also on Golders Green's books at the time.

In the summer of 1945, Eric moved on to Willesden before being signed by Queens Park Rangers in September 1947, Roy also joined QPR around the same time. Eric never made the R's first team and as a result he joined Watford in August 1949.

He played 30 senior games for the Hornets during the 1949/50 and 1950/51 seasons.

Eric then dropped out of league football and joined Dover for the 1951/52 campaign where he quickly gained a reputation for being one of the best centre-forwards in the Kent League. During the 1951/52 season, Eric scored 37 goals as Dover won the league title and his tally included five hat-tricks. Three of them came in the space of four matches during January and February 1952. He added another 32 goals during 1952/53 and scored four further hat-tricks. They included four goals as Dover beat Ramsgate 5-3 in an FA Cup tie at Crabble on 11.10.52. Eric was also sent off for striking an opponent in a 4-1 win at Chatham on 6.9.52.

Eric stayed at Dover for the start of the 1953/54 campaign but in September 1953 he moved back into league football and joined Bradford City. He made two first team appearances there and scored once before making a swift return to Kent, signing for Margate in November 1953.

Initially Eric's appearances were restricted as they had to be fitted around a teacher training course that he was undertaking. He made his debut for Margate in an away game at his old club Dover on 19.12.53 and scored the only goal of the match to make an instant impact. Eric then marked his home debut with a first minute goal as Margate beat Ashford 3-2 in a Kent League game at Hartsdown Park on 2.1.54.

On 16.1.54, Eric was injured during the first half as Margate took on visitors Ramsgate, it was only his fourth game for the club. He was knocked out in an aerial challenge and after regaining consciousness he was helped off the pitch. Eric returned for the second half, switching from centre-forward to the left wing, but according to the East Kent Times he was still bemused and had no knowledge of recent events resulting in him being a virtual passenger as Margate lost 2-0. The extent of Eric s concussion was revealed after the match when he couldn t recall any events since Christmas Day some two weeks earlier. In that time Eric had become a father for the first time but had no recollection of that. Further medical checks revealed that Eric had also suffered a fractured jaw and his injuries, combined with his studies meant that he didn't appear again until April 1954. Eric finished the 1953/54 season having made a total of nine appearances, scoring twice.

Eric was made first team captain (Vic Pilcher was club captain) for the 1954/55 season and really established himself. He hardly missed a game and scored 12 times in 42 appearances. He also proved to be very versatile, playing up front and in midfield.

Eric retained the captaincy for the 1955/56 campaign and was virtually ever-present once more, making 42 appearances and scoring 11 times. On 19.11.55 he was in the Margate side that drew 2-2 with Walsall at Hartsdown Park in the FA Cup 1st Round and Eric also played in the replay at Walsall on 24.11.55 that the home side won 6-1. He was the only Kent League player who wore contact lenses and they caused Eric problems during a snowy spell.

During the 1956/57 season Eric played his 100th game for the club and he made a total of 30 appearances during the campaign. On 17.11.56 he played as Margate beat Dunstable 3-1 at Hartsdown Park in the FA Cup 1st Round and Eric also featured in a 4-0 defeat at Millwall in the 2nd Round on 8.12.56. However he suffered a slipped disc early in 1957 and was out for ten weeks. Eric managed six goals during the season and the best of them was a solo effort in a 4-2 home win over Chatham on 20.4.57, a match in which he scored twice.

The 1957/58 season saw Eric's work as a schoolmaster at Bexley Grammar School (he taught games) often causing him to miss midweek matches. However he still played 38 times although he only managed a single goal. Eric operated almost exclusively in midfield during the campaign and continued to display boundless energy, popping up all over the field. On 16.11.57 he was part of the Margate side that lost 3-2 to visitors Crystal Palace in the FA Cup 1st Round and a match report for Margate's 2-2 home draw with Sittingbourne on 26.4.58 singled him out for praise, saying that Eric "stood out like a giant amongst 21 dwarfs".

The 1958/59 season was his sixth at Margate and Eric made 37 appearances. On 15.11.58 he was in the side that lost 3-2 at Headington in the FA Cup 1st Round. He scored twice during a campaign disrupted by a hip injury and the second of his goals was a tremendous solo effort in an 8-0 win over Canterbury at Hartsdown Park on 28.3.59. Eric beat four players before firing home and the strike was described as "a great goal by a great player" in the local paper.

During the 1959/60 season Eric made 26 appearances to go past 200 for the club. He was a regular during the first half of the season and on 14.11.59 he played in a 1-1 draw at Kettering in the FA Cup 1st Round. Eric also featured in the replay at Hartsdown Park on 19.11.59 that Margate won 3-2. He was then in the side that drew 0-0 with visitors Crystal Palace in the 2nd Round on 5.12.59 and took part in the replay at Selhurst Park on 9.12.59 that the Eagles won 3-0.

In January 1960 Eric suffered a ruptured stomach muscle which - apart from a single appearance for the reserves on 30.3.60 - kept him out for the remainder of the campaign. He d managed one goal during the season - a 40 yard effort in a 3-3 draw at Trowbridge in the Southern League on 9.1.60. During his injury lay-off Eric kept himself busy by doing some scouting on behalf of Margate boss Almer Hall and in its end of season review the East Kent Times said that Eric had "found that Southern League soccer suited his cultured style admirably".

The 1960/61 season was Eric's last at Margate and it was a campaign that was disrupted by injury once more. He was only able to make 19 appearances and scored just once - in a 1-1 draw away to Cambridge United on 10.12.60. Eric played in various positions during the season and still displayed all his old class but in May 1961 he decided to retire. Eric had had persistent stomach trouble and as he was also about to take up a position as a PE teacher at Loughborough College he opted to end his football career.

In later years he became the first manager of the England Women's team and was in charge for their first match, against Scotland, in 1972.

In April 1973 Eric emigrated to Melbourne, Australia and became a university lecturer there. He also took up a position as Director of Coaching for the Australian Soccer Federation and his brief was to upgrade the standard of coaching at all levels of the game. Eric initially spent 12 months making a comprehensive study of coaching in each state and in 1974 he travelled with the Australia squad to the World Cup Finals in West Germany. He then laid down a national coaching scheme which got off the ground in January 1975.

Later in 1975 Eric had a spell as caretaker coach of Australia's national team, taking charge of the side for four internationals following the sudden departure of Rale Rasic.

In 1999 he was inducted into the Australian 'Football Hall of Fame'.

Eric had at least one book about football coaching published and he was also an accomplished artist who had his paintings exhibited.

He died in Sydney, Australia on 16.11.06 aged 80 and an article about Eric's life in The Australian newspaper fittingly called him an "outstanding servant to Australian soccer". The piece concluded with "Worthington pioneered the first Australia-wide coaching structure and his influence is still felt today".

name: Alfred Wraight
bio:
Alfred Leonard Wraight born Thanet 
Said to be 17 during early games for club in 24/25 - played for Margate Thursday early that season. But would actually have been 21 at start of 24/25 
Write-up in Thanet Advertiser - Saturday 09 May 1925
24.10.24 found what the East Kent Times and Mail said was  helplessly drunk  on the pavement in Marine Terrace. Case went before Borough magistrates on 25.10.24 (next morning), policeman told court Alfred was  a very respectable young chap  and case dismissed with costs of 4 shillings. Living at 19 Victoria Avenue at the time.
 Was amateur 24/25 and then signed as professional a few weeks into 25/26. Started 26/27 with Margate Amateurs after Margate signed Bailey as keeper, 15.1.27 played in goal for them in 6-1 friendly defeat v Margate at Dreamland and Bailey injured wrist for Margate in match. Then took over in goal for Margate for rest of 26/27.
7.6.30 punched policeman in the face in Market place, Margate. Case went before Borough Police Court on 10.6.30 and Alfred told court he was drunk at the time of the incident. Magistrates imposed 40 shillings fine, rather than prison, as it was a first offence. Alfred was living in Victoria Avenue, Margate at the time and was unemployed.
Article saved in unused  folder Alfred Wraight assault Thanet Advertiser - Friday 13 June 1930
June 1940   was working in a garden trench talking to soldier Richard Ruffell who was in the garden when the soldier was shot and killed by another soldier John Peck.  Death by misadventure  was verdict   the other soldier had been cleaning a machine gun and hadn t realised magazine attached when pulled trigger.
6.9.41 entered neighbours house by back door when drunk and entered her bedroom. Then immediately went to police station and gave himself up. Charged with assault with intent to commit a serious offence but reduced to common assault. By then Alfred was a gardener and was married with 5 children but had been separated for 3 years. Given two years probation. Article Alfred Wraight assault East Kent Times and Mail - Wednesday 10 September 1941
September 1941 appeared at Sandwich matrimonial court for failing to pay maintenance to his estranged wife   arrears of over  54. Agreed to pay  1 per week.
Later in WWII years he was sentenced to two years hard labour for manslaughter at a field general court martial. 
20.11.46 attacked partner with iron bar at home in Victoria Avenue, fracturing her skull. Trial in Maidstone in March 1947   charged with wounding and sentenced to 3 years prison. Medical officer of Maidstone prison told court he believed Alfred was of unsound mind.
Died in Canterbury area Q1 1981 aged 77

name: Nicky Wren
other clubs: Gillingham (0), Gravesend & Northfleet, Dover Athletic, Sittingbourne, Faversham Town, Dartford, Herne Bay, Canterbury City, Maidstone United, Sheppey United, Bly Spartans and Hollands and Blair
bio:
Chatham-born player who started his career as a trainee at Gillingham, joining the club for the 1990/91 campaign. Nicky became a regular in the Gills' youth team for the next couple of seasons and on 28.7.92 he was a substitute for a 0-0 draw at Margate. The match was a Kent Midweek League semi-final held over from the 1991/92 campaign.

He left Gillingham later in 1992/93 and had short spells with Gravesend & Northfleet and Dover before finishing the season at Sittingbourne.

In the summer of 1993 Nicky signed for Margate but after struggling to break into the first team in the opening weeks of the 1993/94 campaign he was loaned to Faversham in September 1993. Nicky stayed there until the end of March 1994. On 2.4.94 he finally made his first appearance for Margate when he came on as a substitute in a 2-0 win at Canterbury but Nicky then went back to Faversham for a few weeks. On 26.4.94 he scored twice for them in a 10-1 win over Margate's reserves at Hartsdown Park in the Kent Midweek League and Nicky was then recalled once more. He made his first start for Margate in a Southern League game at Buckingham on 30.4.94 and scored with a shot from the edge of the penalty area in a 2-0 win. Nicky didn't play again and he was released at the end of the season.

He joined Dartford in the summer of 1994 and then moved on to Herne Bay later in 1994/95.

Nicky returned to Faversham for 1995/96 before signing for Canterbury at the end of the campaign.

He spent two seasons with City and worked in printing during his time with the club.

In the summer of 1998 Nicky joined Maidstone and played regularly for them in the Kent County League before rejoining Sittingbourne in March 1999.

He spent the 1999/00 campaign with Sheppey and then went back to Sittingbourne again for 2000/01.

Nicky later spent several seasons with Bly Spartans in the Kent County League, featuring for them during the 2003/04, 2004/05 and 2005/06 campaigns.

He then moved on to Hollands and Blair, another Kent County League club, where he made 92 appearances and scored 13 goals.

Nicky's father Steve spent many years on the backroom staff at Sittingbourne during the 1990's and early 2000's, having spells as reserve team manager and first team assistant manager amongst other roles.

name: George Wright
other clubs: Ramsgate Athletic, West Ham United (170,0), Leyton Orient (88,1) and Gillingham (4,0)
bio:
5' 9" tall, Ramsgate-born, fair-haired defender who played locally for Thanet Press before being signed by Ramsgate a few weeks into the 1948/49 campaign. George spent most of the season in the Rams reserves but also made a single first team appearance, featuring in a 2-1 win over Royal Marines Chatham in a Kent League Cup tie at Southwood on 2.12.48. Later in the campaign he played for Kent.

In the summer of 1950 George signed for Margate and before making his move, he d been offered a trial at Arsenal but turned the opportunity down. He made his debut in a 3-0 defeat at Snowdown in the Kent League on 23.8.50 - the first match of the legendary Almer Hall s reign as Margate manager - and played in the unfamiliar role of inside forward. George went on to make 22 appearances as a right-back or centre-back during the first half of the 1950/51 season.

In February 1951 he was transferred to West Ham, just a month after team-mate Doug Bing had joined the Hammers. George went on to spend over seven years with West Ham and made 170 first team appearances for them. He also played twice for the FA X1. In addition George played for London in the 2nd leg of the first ever Inter-Cities Fairs Cup away to Barcelona. He and Doug Bing were known as 'the Margate blondes' by the national press whilst at Upton Park.

In February 1957 there were rumours of George returning to Margate as he was transfer-listed and watched a Margate game from the bench with Almer Hall but there was no substance in the stories.

In June 1958 he moved to Leyton Orient and was a regular in their side from 1958/59 to 1961/62.

In July 1962 George joined Gillingham and made a handful of first team appearances for them during the early part of the 1962/63 season.

In September 1962 he dropped back into non-league football to rejoin Ramsgate and made his first appearance in a 2-0 defeat at Tonbridge in the Southern League on 29.9.62. The Rams released George at the end of the 1962/63 campaign and he then retired.

George was the son of a local fishmonger and at one stage was in business in both the confectionery and carpentry trades. He later moved into cabinet-making and ran a second-hand car dealership.

George died in Ramsgate aged 70 during September 2000.

bio:

Played for England in 1906 international against Wales   so first ex MFC player to be international ? See http://www.englandstats.com/players.php?pid=1093 //

During and after which he assisted numerous clubs, including the Corinthians club from 1905-07, Portsmouth FC from September 1905-06. Wright accepted a mastership at Hymers College, and accepted a role at Hull City AFC in April 1906 until 1913, completing 152 league appearances and becoming club captain. Assisted Leyton FC in 1909-10, as well as helping Worthing FC and Reigate Priory FC along the way
England Amateur (twenty appearances), FA XI Tour South Africa in 1910, until he was injured; 
Played in one game for Great Britain at 1912 Stockholm Olympics - got gold medal although didn't feature in final
Hull info - https://www.oncloudseven.com/32-gordon-wright/
and died 5.6.47 in Johannesburg aged 62

name: Vince Wright
other clubs: Bury (0), Derby County (0), Mansfield Town (2,0), Shirebrook Miners Welfare, Tonbridge, Tunbridge Wells United, Canterbury City, Chatham Town and Tenterden
bio:
Winger born in Bradford who started his career in Bury s junior ranks. Whilst on the club s books, Vince made a one-off appearance for England s youth team. He was part of the side that lost 3-1 to Scotland at Aberdeen on 30.10.48 and a crowd of 8,000 watched the match.

In September 1951 Vince was signed by Derby, initially on a month s trial, shortly after completing his National Service. After impressing in his early reserve team outings, he was given a professional contract but Vince didn t feature in Derby s senior side before being released at the end of the 1951/52 season.

In the summer of 1952, he joined Mansfield and Vince played twice for Mansfield s first team in the 3rd Division before being released by the club at the end of the 1952/53 campaign.

He spent the 1953/54 season with Shirebrook Miners Welfare before leaving the club at the end of the campaign.

Vince moved south and signed for Southern League club Tonbridge in the summer of 1954. He scored four goals from 12 appearances for the Angels before leaving the club in December 1954.

Vince signed for Margate as a replacement for the tragically deceased Len Dolding and made his debut in a 4-0 win at Folkestone on 4.12.54. He made an instant impression on Margate's left wing and the local press reported that one spectator claimed Vince had "all the makings of a second Stanley Matthews". By the end of the 1954/55 season he'd made 26 appearances, scoring five times.

In May 1955 Vince was transfer-listed by Margate and signed for Tunbridge Wells ahead of the 1955/56 campaign. When they played at Margate during the season, the programme for the game noted that Vince "always enlivens a game" with his "circus-like antics". On 28.1.56 he scored in a 4-1 home defeat against Margate and Vince then scored all three goals as Tunbridge Wells Reserves beat visitors Margate Reserves on 18.2.56.

In December 1956 Vince moved onto Canterbury.

In 1960 he was working as a chauffeur for a wealthy Tonbridge resident called Herbert Simmonds and during the 1960/61 season Vince played for Chatham.

He spent the 1963/64 campaign with East Sussex League club Tenterden and on 25.1.64 Vince scored eight goals in a 9-2 win over Peasmarsh.

He also played cricket for Tenterden and on 31.7.66 Vince scored 104 not out in a game for them.

In later years, Vince continued to live in Tenterden and helped out with coaching their junior football teams in the early 1970 s.

He died in Canterbury during June 2004 aged 73.

name: Billy Yenson
other clubs: Thames Ironworks, West Ham United, Bolton Wanderers (28,8), Queens Park Rangers, Croydon Common, Crystal Palace, Brentford
bio:
5' 10" Born Kingston Bagpuize, Oxfordshire Q1 1883 as Phillip Owen Yenson.   
Played for Russell Road School, Ferndale and Stanley as a junior and then joined Thames Ironworks in May 1900 - they were wound up and reformed as West Ham in July 1900 
Spent two seasons - 01/02 and 02/03 - with West Ham in their Southern League days (24,0 there) before joining Bolton Wanderers in May 1903 
was centre forward in the Bolton side that lost by a single goal to Manchester City in the 1904 FA Cup Final at Crystal Palace.  Billy Meredith inspired City and got winner 
Bolton to QPR in July 1905 - e-p for Rangers 05/06 (capt) and QPR won 07/08 S League title.  Made 90 S.League apps in total, 4 goals 
Rejoined West Ham June 1908 (26,0 SL 08/09) and then signed for Croydon Common in June 1909. 
 He was soon made club captain and spent 6 seasons at The Nest up to and including 14/15 - cracked shin 19.9.14 C1 Cry Pal 1 ended Croydon career. 
12/13 played in C's two FA Cup ties v First Division Woolwich Arsenal, lost replay 2-1 there. 
Won Southern Football Alliance 12/13 //  Southern League Second Division title 13/14 254 games in total  
Throughout his time at Croydon, he also owned a local tobacconist shop which advertised in the club's handbooks. 
Brother George on Croydon's books too for some of time and another brother 'H' too - probably actually John 
played for Crystal Palace (16/17 from Croy C - folded) and Brentford (16/17)   briefly during WW1 before us.  
Died 20.1.44 in Ilford, Essex aged 61   
Margate 19/20 - captain,   
Croydon Common had benefit fund for him during 1914/15 (injured almost all that season - only 4 apps) and 3.4.15 club donated proceeds from reserves match with Cardiff City Reserves to fund 
Also 'yensoncard.jpg' uploaded - cig card showing him at Croydon. 
Leyton had Billy's son Ken Yenson as capt 51/53 - centre back, played in Bromley FAC win 1949 with Fright and 8.1.49 may have been in Bromley side that lost 3-2 at Margate in KSC - TA report listed him in side, EKT one didn't.  
Apparently of Swedish extraction - Jensen original family name ? - summer 1913 toured Sweden with Croydon and in one match brother scored for Swedish opponents

name: Clive Yeo
other clubs: Ramsgate, Canterbury City, Herne Bay and Phoenix Rovers
bio:
Sidcup-born forward who began his career with Ramsgate during the 1981/82 season. Clive stayed with the Rams until the summer of 1985 when he moved to Canterbury.

He joined Thanet United for the 1985/86 campaign and became a prominent player in the reserves. Clive's form led to a first team call up and he made his senior debut when he came on as a substitute in an Eastern Floodlight Cup tie against Sittingbourne at Hartsdown on 26.11.85. Thanet won 4-0 and Clive scored soon after coming on, he also set up a goal for Norman Fusco to cap a memorable debut. Clive featured as a substitute in United's next four games but then found himself back in the reserves for a lengthy spell. On 29.4.86 he returned to the first team for Thanet's penultimate game of the season, making his first start for the club in a 2-0 defeat at Sheppey. Clive didn't feature in Thanet's final game so finished the campaign having made six appearances (five as sub).

During the 1986/87 season Clive made four more appearances for the first team, the first of them as a substitute in a 1-1 draw at home to Tonbridge in the Eastern Floodlight Cup on 9.9.86. His first start of the campaign came on 1.11.86 in a 3-0 win over Dunstable at Hartsdown, Thanet manager John Wickens said that Clive's "pace up front was handy" and he started in United's next game too. After a long spell back in the reserves Clive returned to the senior side on 21.3.87, making his last appearance of the season as Thanet drew 1-1 with Gravesend & Northfleet at Hartsdown. He was chosen as the reserve team's 'Player of the Year' for the campaign.

In the summer of 1987 Clive left Thanet to join Herne Bay under manager John Wickens and at the end of the 1987/88 season he rejoined Ramsgate.

Clive returned to Hartsdown Park for the 1989/90 season and became a fixture in Margate's reserve team. He was ever-present for them, making 38 appearances (one as sub) and scoring 12 goals as they won the Kent League Division 2. Clive also made two substitute appearances for the first team, featuring in a 2-0 defeat at Canterbury in the Kent Senior Cup on 22.11.89 and a 2-1 defeat at home to Salisbury on 9.12.89. They were his last appearances for the senior side.

Clive stayed at Margate for the 1990/91 campaign and played exclusively for the reserves during the season although towards the end of 1990 he very briefly left the club to join Phoenix Rovers of the Kent County League. He top scored with 15 goals from 25 appearances and his tally included a hat-trick in a 5-1 win over Sheppey Reserves at Hartsdown on 27.10.90. Clive was joint winner of the reserves' 'Clubman of the Year' award, sharing the honour with Steve Winch.

He returned to Phoenix Rovers for the start of the 1991/92 season.

Clive rejoined Ramsgate for 1992/93 and played regularly for them for many years. By 1994/95 he was part of the Rams reserves' management team and Clive still played for them during the 1996/97 season.

He was still turning out for Active Lesters in the Thanet Works League during 2003/04 and Clive then joined Thanet League club AFC Margate where he spent the 2004/05 and 2005/06 seasons before hanging up his boots.

Clive worked as a postman during his time with Thanet / Margate and for many years afterwards. In 2006 he was still living locally and occasionally visited Hartsdown Park to watch Margate games.

name: Dennis Yeomans
other clubs: Southend United (0), Clacton Town and Holbeach United
bio:
Opportunist goalscorer born in Rochford, Essex who started his career with Southend where he played for the reserves during the early part of the 1952/53 season.

A couple of months into 1952/53, Dennis signed for Clacton and during the 1953/54 season he helped them to second place in the Eastern Counties League. Dennis stayed with Clacton until the end of the 1954/55 campaign.

In November 1955 after a few months out of senior football, Dennis joined Holbeach United of the Eastern Counties League, initially on trial. He d recently started his National Service and was based in the Holbeach area. He stayed with Holbeach for the rest of the 1955/56 season before being released at the end of the campaign.

Dennis then had a spell out of senior football while he completed his National Service but on 26.12.56 he turned out for Margate s reserves as they beat Sittingbourne 4-2 at Hartsdown Park. In March 1957 Dennis was demobbed from the army and was free to resume his football career.

Dennis immediately signed for Margate and spent the remainder of the 1956/57 campaign in the reserves, scoring three goals from nine appearances to help them win the Kent League Division 2 title and two cup competitions.

The 1957/58 season was an excellent one for Dennis. He made his first team debut against Ramsgate in a Kent League game at Hartsdown Park on 31.8.57 and scored the winner in a 1-0 victory. He went on to score 32 goals in just 38 appearances during the campaign, making him the club's top scorer. Dennis was rated as one of the best youngsters in the Kent League during the season and he was watched by Tottenham scouts on four separate occasions. On 19.9.57 Dennis bagged four goals in a 5-0 home win over Dover in the Kent Senior Shield and on 5.10.57 he was concussed during a game at Deal. Dennis stayed on the field and after the match he had no idea that Margate had won 5-1 or that he d scored two of the goals. He suffered concussion again later in the campaign.

On 16.11.57 Dennis played as Margate lost 3-2 to visitors Crystal Palace in the FA Cup 1st Round and on 4.1.58 he once again scored four goals as Margate beat Faversham 8-2 at Hartsdown Park. Dennis then notched a hat-trick in a 4-1 win at Snowdown in the Kent Senior Cup on 15.2.58 but on 29.3.58 he was sent off after 35 minutes as Margate drew 0-0 with visitors Canterbury. Dennis had been repeatedly fouled by City s left-back Bob Morley and after another challenge saw both players fall to the ground, Morley threw a punch and Dennis retaliated with one of his own. He was immediately ordered from the field but Morley escaped unpunished. Dennis added two further hat-tricks before the end of the season - in a 6-2 win at Folkestone on 4.4.58 and in a 3-1 home win over Bexleyheath & Welling on 21.4.58.

The 1958/59 campaign wasn't such a good one for Dennis, he scored 17 times in 29 appearances, including both goals in a 3-2 defeat at Headington in the FA Cup 1st Round on 15.11.58, but never really recaptured his electric form of the previous season. He was dropped to the reserves several times and the local press described Dennis as being "out of touch" and "a dull replica of the man that once attracted Crystal Palace". However his goalscoring record was hardly unimpressive and it included another hat-trick - in a 9-5 Kent League win over Chatham at Hartsdown Park on 4.10.58. Dennis also scored with a stunning diving header in a 5-1 win at Ramsgate on 11.10.58 His last goal of the season came in the Kent League Cup Final on 7.5.59 as Margate went down 3-2 to Sittingbourne.

During the 1959/60 campaign Dennis rarely played for the first team and only made six appearances, scoring twice. One of his outings in the senior side was in an FA Cup 2nd Round replay at Crystal Palace on 9.12.59 that Margate lost 3-0. However Dennis was a leading light in the reserves and scored more than 20 goals for them. At the end of the season he was released.

He dropped into amateur football in the Southend area for the 1960/61 campaign.

Dennis worked as a mechanic during his time with Margate.
